options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A neighbor is chased home because he can't pay his debts unexpectedly. Discuss whether personal bankruptcy protection should be strict or broad.

scene: 社区想搞理性消费宣传，有人欢迎，有人觉得政府别教人怎么花钱。

options.t: 我支持引导，少点冲动债更好。
options.t_en: I support guidance, less impulsive debt is better.

options.t: 我反对，怎么花是个人的事。
options.t_en: I object. How to spend it is a personal matter.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: The community wants to engage in rational consumption propaganda, and some people welcome it. Some people think that the government does not teach people how to spend money.

scene: 要在你家门口建一座新电站供全市用，选址方说安全达标，邻居们却没人愿意它挨着自己。

options.t: 我反对建在我这，别来我家旁。
options.t_en: I object to being built here, don't come near my house.

options.t: 我接受，全市用电总得有地方。
options.t_en: I accept that there must be a place for electricity in the city.

options.t: 我支持但要求透明环评和补偿。
options.t_en: I support but demand transparency and reimbursement.

options.t: 我主张分布式小站代替大站。
options.t_en: I advocate distributed small stations instead of large stations.

options.t: 我要求周边居民投票定址。
options.t_en: I asked the surrounding residents to vote on the address.

options.t: 我支持远程供电少建本地站。
options.t_en: I support remote power supply with fewer local stations.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: To build a new power station in front of your house for the whole city, the site selection party said that it was safe and up to standard, but no one in the neighborhood wanted it to be next to them.

scene: 居民电费拟设阶梯补贴，用得少的少交、用得多的多交。大户说不公平，节能家庭说该奖。

options.t: 我支持补贴，鼓励省电。
options.t_en: I support subsidies and encourage saving electricity.

options.t: 我反对，用电多交税是惩罚。
options.t_en: I object that paying more taxes on electricity is a penalty.

options.t: 我支持只保基本额度免费。
options.t_en: I support free basic limits only.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Residents' electricity bills are planned to be subsidized by stairs, and those that use less are underpaid and much more overpaid. The big family said it was unfair, and the energy-saving family said it was the prize.

scene: 智能电网要收集每家用电习惯来调峰，称省电省钱。你想到自家作息被摸得一清二楚。

options.t: 我支持共享，整体省电利大家。
options.t_en: I support sharing, saving electricity for everyone.

options.t: 我反对共享，用电细节是隐私。
options.t_en: I am against sharing, electricity details are private.

options.t: 我支持匿名汇总不关联个人。
options.t_en: I support anonymous aggregation that does not associate individuals.

options.t: 我主张本地储能少依赖电网。
options.t_en: I advocate less reliance on the grid for local energy storage.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: The smart grid should collect each household's electricity habits to adjust the peak, saying that it saves energy and saves money. When you think of your own life, you are clearly touched.

scene: 河边低洼区年年泡水，政府想整体搬迁住户到高地，给补偿但要离祖辈根。居民去留两难。

options.t: 我支持强制搬，命比老屋重要。
options.t_en: I support forced relocation, life is more important than the old house.

options.t: 我反对强搬，根在这里不愿离。
options.t_en: I am opposed to forced relocation, and Root is reluctant to leave here.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The low-lying areas along the river are soaking in water every year, and the government wants to relocate residents to the highlands as a whole, compensating them but leaving their ancestors. Residents went to stay in the dilemma.

scene: 气象推出灾害预警小程序，会按定位推送。有人觉得安心，有人嫌天天弹窗烦。

options.t: 我开着推送，关键时刻能保命。
options.t_en: I drive and push, and I can save my life at critical moments.

options.t: 我关掉，太吵自己看天就行。
options.t_en: I turn it off, it's okay if I make too much noise and look at the sky.

options.t: 我只开严重级别提醒。
options.t_en: I only want severity level reminders.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: Weather launched a disaster warning applet, which will be pushed by location. Some people felt at ease, and some people were annoyed by the popping of windows every day.

scene: 为减缓极端天气，有人提议对高排放行为征税，返给受影响的弱者。支持者说长远划算，反对者说又添税。

options.t: 我支持碳税，谁排多谁多出。
options.t_en: I support a carbon tax, who gets more and who gets more.

options.t: 我反对，税只会越加越多。
options.t_en: I object, taxes will only increase.

options.t: 我支持税但全额返弱势群体。
options.t_en: I support taxes but return the full amount to the vulnerable.

options.t: 我主张用奖励减排代替收税。
options.t_en: I advocate for incentive emission reductions instead of taxes.

options.t: 我支持先试点看效果。
options.t_en: I support piloting the results first.

options.t: 我认为该大企业先担，不先压个人。
options.t_en: I think that the big company should shoulder the responsibility first, and not press the individual first.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: To mitigate extreme weather, it has been proposed to tax high-emission behaviour and return it to the vulnerable affected. Supporters say it's a long-term deal, opponents say it's a tax.

scene: 你常用的内容平台按算法推测你喜欢的一直推，越看越窄。你能关推荐，但默认是开着。

options.t: 我关掉推荐，自己搜才踏实。
options.t_en: I turned off the recommendation and searched on my own.

options.t: 我留着推荐，省得自己找。
options.t_en: I keep the recommendations, so I don't have to look for them myself.

options.t: 我支持默认关、需主动开。
options.t_en: I support default off and active on.

options.t: 我主张可调控频宽而非全关。
options.t_en: I advocate adjustable bandwidth instead of full off.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The content platform you commonly use presumes that you like to push all the time according to the algorithm, and the more you look at it, the narrower it is. You can turn off the recommendation, but the default is on.

scene: 你发现注册过的平台把你的浏览习惯卖给了广告商。你此前从没注意过那行小字条款。

options.t: 我找平台维权，要求停止并删除。
options.t_en: I looked for the platform to defend my rights and demanded that it be stopped and deleted.

options.t: 我默默卸载，懒得纠缠。
options.t_en: I unloaded in silence and was too lazy to entangle.

options.t: 我支持立法重罚这类转卖。
options.t_en: I support legislation imposing heavy fines on this kind of resale.

options.t: 我认了，免费就用数据换。
options.t_en: I accept the trade-off: a free service means paying with my data.

options.t: 我改成只用不注册的服务。
options.t_en: I'd switch to services I can use without signing up.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: You find that a registered platform sells your browsing habits to advertisers. You've never noticed that line before.

scene: 一家平台占了你大半网络生活，小竞争者难活。有人呼吁拆分之，有人说它好用就该让它大。

options.t: 我支持拆分，垄断伤选择和活力。
options.t_en: I support splitting, monopolizing wound selection and vitality.

options.t: 我反对拆分，好用是用户用脚投的。
options.t_en: I am opposed to splitting, easy to use is thrown by the user with his feet.

options.t: 我支持设互通规则而非拆实体。
options.t_en: I support having interoperability rules rather than disassembling entities.

options.t: 我主张扶持小平台平衡。
options.t_en: I advocate supporting the balance of small platforms.

options.t: 我主张用户数据可携带。
options.t_en: I advocate for the portability of user data.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A platform accounts for most of your online life, and small competitors are hard to live. Some people call for splitting, some people say that if it works well, it should be made big.

scene: 论坛拟全面实名制，称能压住水军。你习惯匿名吐槽，也烦那些带节奏的号。

options.t: 我支持实名，干净环境值得。
options.t_en: I support real name, clean environment is worth it.

options.t: 我反对实名，匿名才有真话。
options.t_en: I oppose real names, anonymity is the truth.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: The forum intends to use a comprehensive real-name system, saying that it can suppress the water army. You're used to spitting anonymously and bothering with rhythmic numbers.

scene: 老楼要加装坡道和扶手方便坐轮椅的邻居，费用摊到各户。有人觉得用的人少不值。

options.t: 我支持投入，无障碍是底线公平。
options.t_en: I support engagement, and accessibility is fairness at the bottom line.

options.t: 我勉强同意但希望少摊点。
options.t_en: I reluctantly agree but hope to stall less.

options.t: 我支持政府出钱不由住户摊。
options.t_en: I support the government's contribution that is not shared by households.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: The old building should be equipped with ramps and armrests for wheelchair-accessible neighbors, and the cost should be shared among all households. Some people feel that the number of people who use it is not worth it.

scene: 一家店招聘时为某类常被忽视的求职者留了专门名额，其他应聘者觉得挤占了本属于自己的机会。

options.t: 我支持留名额，结构要主动纠偏。
options.t_en: I support quotas, and the structure should take the initiative to correct deviations.

options.t: 我反对名额，机会该纯粹看能力。
options.t_en: I am against the quota, the opportunity should be purely based on ability.

options.t: 我支持培训衔接而非直接保岗。
options.t_en: I support training bridging rather than direct job protection.

options.t: 我主张公开评审过程接受监督。
options.t_en: I advocate that the public review process be supervised.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: One store hired a special place for a category of often overlooked job seekers, and other candidates felt they were squeezing their own opportunities.

scene: 社区倡议大家使用更中性的称呼来指代不同处境的邻居，避免旧词带来的误会。有人觉得温馨，有人觉得矫情。

options.t: 我主动改用新称呼，少让人不舒服。
options.t_en: I took the initiative to use a new name, which was less uncomfortable.

options.t: 我顺其自然，不强制就好。
options.t_en: I leave it to nature, just don't force it.

options.t: 我反对规范用语，怎么叫是自由。
options.t_en: I am opposed to normative language, how to call it freedom.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: Community initiatives People use more neutral terms to refer to neighbors in different situations, avoiding misunderstandings caused by old words. Some people feel warm, some people feel sentimental.

scene: 住在楼上的邻居每晚十点后练习打击乐器，楼下住着一位准备升学考试的高中生。家长在业主群里抱怨了两次，楼上回应说自己白天上班只能晚上练。双方都觉得对方不体谅。

options.t: 我会直接上门找他谈，约一个双方都能接受的练习时段，邻里的事先自己解决。
options.t_en: I will go directly to him and talk to him about a practice period that is acceptable to both parties, and the neighborhood will solve it by itself in advance.

options.t: 我会把情况反映给物业，让管理方出面制定统一的作息规定并执行。
options.t_en: I will reflect the situation to the property and let the management come forward to formulate uniform working and rest regulations and implement them.

options.t: 我会自己买隔音耳塞和窗帘，别人在自己家里做什么本来就是他的自由。
options.t_en: I buy my own soundproof earplugs and curtains, and what others do in their own homes is his freedom.

options.t: 我会在自家墙边放一台分贝记录仪连续取证，超标就走正式投诉流程。
options.t_en: I will put a decibel recorder next to my wall to continuously collect evidence, and if it exceeds the standard, I will go through the formal complaint process.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The neighbor who lives upstairs practices percussion after ten o'clock every night, and downstairs lives a high school student who is preparing for his entrance exams. Parents complained twice in the owner group, and the upstairs responded that they could only practice at night during the day. Both parties felt that the other was uncomfortable.

scene: 小区门口有一块闲置空地。一部分居民想把它改成共享菜园，轮流种菜轮流照看；另一部分居民想改成收费停车位，收入归业主大会。两种方案都需要动用同一笔公共维修金。

options.t: 我支持做共享菜园，大家排班维护，公共空地应该先服务共同生活而不是先赚钱。
options.t_en: I support sharing vegetable gardens, everyone schedules and maintains, and the public open space should serve co-living first rather than earning money first.

options.t: 我支持改成收费停车位，停车的人付费、不停车的人不掏钱，谁受益谁承担最清楚。
options.t_en: I support switching to paid parking spaces. Those who park pay, those who don't park don't pay, and those who benefit are the clearest.

options.t: 我会提议全体业主投票表决，无论哪个方案都要公开账目和后续维护责任人。
options.t_en: I will propose that all owners vote, no matter which option, to open the accounts and the person responsible for follow-up maintenance.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: There is a vacant lot at the entrance of the community. Some residents want to change it to a shared vegetable garden, taking turns to take care of the vegetables; others want to change it to a paid parking space, and the income will go to the owners' meeting. Both options require access to the same public maintenance fund.

scene: 同楼有位独居老人已经好几天没露面。社区想建立定期敲门探访制度，需要登记独居住户的门牌、联系方式和大致作息。有人觉得这是保命的措施，也有人觉得这是被建档。

options.t: 我会报名做探访志愿者，邻居之间本来就该互相照应，不能等出事才想起来。
options.t_en: I would sign up as a visiting volunteer, the neighbors should have taken care of each other, and I couldn't wait for something to happen before I remembered.

options.t: 我认为应由社区统一建立台账并定期核查，靠自愿排班迟早会断档。
options.t_en: I think that the community should establish a unified account and check it regularly, and the voluntary scheduling will be disconnected sooner or later.

options.t: 我觉得必须先征得老人本人书面同意，不愿意被登记的就不该被登记。
options.t_en: I feel that it is necessary to obtain the written consent of the elderly first, and those who do not want to be registered should not be registered.

options.t: 我会建议引入收费的专业上门服务，责任和质量都比志愿者更稳定。
options.t_en: I would recommend the introduction of paid professional onsite service, with more consistent responsibilities and quality than volunteers.

options.t: 我会请社区里的信仰互助小组承担探访，他们有组织也更有耐心。
options.t_en: I ask for visits from faith-based support groups in my community, who are more organized and patient.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: An elderly man who lived alone in the same building hadn't been seen for days. If the community wants to establish a regular knocking visit system, they need to register the door number, contact information, and general information of the solitary resident. Some people think that this is a life-saving measure, and some people think that this is archived.

scene: 业主群里有人提议给小区所有出入口加装人脸识别门禁，理由是近期有陌生人尾随进楼。费用从公共收益里出，需要采集全体住户的面部信息。

options.t: 我会投赞成票，识别快、外来人员进不来，安全排在便利和顾虑前面。
options.t_en: I will vote yes to identify fast, outsiders can't get in, and safety is ahead of convenience and concerns.

options.t: 我会投反对票，刷卡加访客登记已经够用，面部数据一旦流出就永远收不回来。
options.t_en: I will vote no. Swiping the card and registering visitors is enough. Once the facial data flows out, it will never be collected again.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: There is a proposal in the owner group to install facial recognition access gates to all entrances and exits of the community, on the grounds that strangers have recently followed them into the building. Expenses come from public revenue, which requires collecting facial information from all residents.

scene: 公司通知在所有办公电脑上安装行为管理软件，会记录屏幕截图、键盘活跃度和软件使用时长，数据保存期限没有说明。部分同事觉得无所谓，部分同事觉得被冒犯。

options.t: 我会照常安装，设备是公司的、时间也是买来的，被记录属于合理范围。
options.t_en: I will install it as usual. The equipment is company-owned, the time is purchased, and the records are within a reasonable range.

options.t: 我会和几位同事一起要求公司书面说明采集范围、用途和删除时间。
options.t_en: Together with several colleagues, I will ask the company to state in writing the scope of the collection, the purpose and the time of deletion.

options.t: 我会把私人事务全部挪到自己的手机上，公私分开就不必和公司较劲。
options.t_en: I will move all my private affairs to my mobile phone, and there is no need to compete with the company by separating public and private.

options.t: 我会去劳动权益咨询窗口问清楚这种监控是否越界，必要时走正式渠道。
options.t_en: I will go to the labor rights inquiry window to ask if this monitoring is beyond the boundaries, and if necessary, go to the formal channel.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: The company has notified that the behavior management software will be installed on all office computers, and screenshots, keyboard activity, and software usage time will be recorded, and the data retention period is not explained. Some colleagues feel indifferent, some colleagues feel offended.

scene: 一个六人小组年底只有两个优秀名额。其中一位同事产出明显偏低，但态度诚恳、经常帮别人收尾杂活。组长让大家私下给意见。

options.t: 我会建议按可量化的绩效数据排序，谁产出高谁拿，模糊标准最伤人。
options.t_en: I would recommend sorting by quantifiable performance data, who produces the highest output and who takes it, and fuzzy standards are the most hurtful.

options.t: 我会建议把奖金平摊，项目成果本来就分不清是谁一个人的功劳。
options.t_en: I would recommend splitting the prize money evenly, because the results of the project could not be attributed to anyone else.

options.t: 我会建议先给他一段带辅导的改进期，评价之前得先给成长的机会。
options.t_en: I would recommend that he be given a period of improvement with coaching, and that he be given the opportunity to grow before commenting.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: There are only two outstanding places at the end of the year for a group of six. One of the co-workers had a significantly lower output, but was sincere and often helped others with their chores. The team leader asked everyone to give their opinion in private.

scene: 一家中型公司在讨论要不要长期保留远程办公。管理层担心协作效率和纪律，年轻员工则算过通勤时间账，坚决不想回到每天坐班。

options.t: 我支持全面远程，只考核交付结果，怎么安排一天由每个人自己决定。
options.t_en: I support full remote, only reviewing the delivery results, and how to arrange the day is up to everyone.

options.t: 我支持混合制，每周固定两天到岗做需要面对面的事，其余远程。
options.t_en: I support the hybrid system, coming to work two days a week to do things that need to be face-to-face, and the rest are remote.

options.t: 我支持恢复统一坐班并严格打卡，纪律是协作效率的前提。
options.t_en: I support the restoration of unified shift attendance and strict clocking, and discipline is a prerequisite for collaborative efficiency.

options.t: 我支持上线在线时长与活跃度统计，用数据来判断远程到底有没有效。
options.t_en: I support online time and activity statistics, and use data to determine whether the remote is effective.

options.t: 我支持让每个小组按自己的业务节奏定规则，总部不该一刀切。
options.t_en: I support having each group set the rules at their own pace of business, and headquarters should not be one-size-fits-all.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: A medium-sized company is discussing whether to keep telecommuting for a long time. Management is concerned about collaborative efficiency and discipline, and young employees are counting their commute times and definitely don't want to go back to work every day.

scene: 本地配送骑手们想成立一个自治小组，就单价、恶劣天气补贴和申诉流程与平台谈判。平台方表示接单完全自愿，不接受集体议价。

options.t: 我支持成立自治小组，一方单独定价、另一方只能接受，本身就不对等。
options.t_en: I support the establishment of autonomous groups, where one party sets the price separately and the other party can only accept it, which is not equivalent in itself.

options.t: 我认为接单是自愿的，觉得价钱低可以换平台或换行当，这就是选择。
options.t_en: I think that accepting orders is voluntary, and I think that the price is low enough to change the platform or change the line, this is the choice.

options.t: 我认为应该由行业统一规则划定最低单价和连续工作时长上限。
options.t_en: I believe that the minimum unit price and the maximum continuous working hours should be set by the uniform rules of the industry.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: Local delivery riders want to set up an autonomous group to negotiate with the platform on unit prices, bad weather subsidies, and the appeals process. The platform party indicates that accepting orders is completely voluntary and does not accept collective bargaining.

scene: 一个兴趣论坛里有位老用户长期发表让部分成员感到被冒犯的看法，内容不违法也不涉及威胁。有人要求管理员封号，有人认为封了反而证明说不过他。

options.t: 我会在帖子下逐条公开反驳他，沉默会被当成默认。
options.t_en: I will publicly contradict him one by one under the post, and silence will be taken as a default.

options.t: 我会举报要求平台删帖封号，平台有义务维护社区氛围。
options.t_en: I will report that I asked the platform to remove the ban, and the platform is obligated to maintain the atmosphere of the community.

options.t: 我会直接拉黑不看，别人说什么是他的事，我没义务被打扰也没权力让他闭嘴。
options.t_en: I will directly black out, what others say is his business, I am not obligated to be disturbed and have no right to shut him up.

options.t: 我会推动论坛成员自己起草发言公约，由用户投票通过后再执行。
options.t_en: I will push Forum members to draft their own speaking conventions, which will be voted on by users before implementation.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: There is an old user in an interest forum who has long expressed opinions that make some members feel offended, and the content is not illegal or threatening. Someone asked the administrator for a seal, and someone thought that it would prove that he could not be said.

scene: 某学院社团邀请了一位观点争议很大的研究者做讲座。一部分学生联署要求取消，另一部分学生认为取消就是替所有人做决定。

options.t: 我认为应照常举办，听见不同意见并学会拆解它，本来就是教育的一部分。
options.t_en: I think it should be held as usual, hearing different opinions and learning to dismantle it is part of education.

options.t: 我认为应取消，讲台是稀缺资源，不该分配给撕裂性的观点。
options.t_en: I think it should be canceled, the podium is a scarce resource and should not be allocated to tearful perspectives.

options.t: 我会争取同场安排一位持相反立场的对谈人和开放提问，让争议在现场被检验。
options.t_en: I will try to arrange for an opposing interlocutor and open questions for the dispute to be examined on site.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: A college community invited a researcher with a very controversial viewpoint to give a lecture. One group of students signed a petition to cancel, while another argued that to cancel was to make a decision for everyone.

scene: 一位同事在几十人的工作群里转发了一条未经核实的行业传闻，已经有人开始跟着转。你恰好知道原始出处并不可靠。

options.t: 我会在群里直接指出问题并附上核实方法，错误信息传开的代价更大。
options.t_en: I will point out the problem directly in the group and attach the verification method, and the misinformation will be more expensive to spread.

options.t: 我会私聊提醒他自己撤回，当众纠错会让人下不来台。
options.t_en: I will privately remind him to withdraw, and correcting mistakes in public will make people unable to come down to the stage.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: A colleague forwarded an unverified industry rumor in a work group of dozens of people, and someone has begun to follow. You happen to know that the original provenance is not reliable.

scene: 城市中心广场周边既有商铺也有住宅。管理方在讨论：是否允许任何人不经登记就在广场发表公开演讲，以及能否使用扩音设备。

options.t: 我支持完全开放，公共广场天然就该是谁都能站上去说话的地方。
options.t_en: I support keeping it fully open. A public square is by its nature a place where anyone can stand up and speak.

options.t: 我支持登记备案制，提前报时段便于安排秩序，也便于出事时找到人。
options.t_en: I support a registration system: sign up for a time slot in advance, which makes it easier to keep order and easier to find the right person if something goes wrong.

options.t: 我支持划定固定的演讲区和时段，其余区域保持安静。
options.t_en: I support designating a fixed speaking area and fixed hours, and keeping the rest of the square quiet.

options.t: 我认为该由周边居民和商户共同投票决定要不要设演讲区。
options.t_en: I think the residents and shopkeepers around the square should vote together on whether there should be a speaking area at all.

options.t: 我支持一律禁用扩音设备，说话的自由不该压过别人安静生活的自由。
options.t_en: I support banning amplification equipment outright. The freedom to speak should not outweigh other people's freedom to live quietly.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: The central city square sits among both shops and apartment buildings. The management authority is debating two linked questions: whether anyone should be allowed to stand up and give a public speech in the square without registering beforehand, and whether amplification equipment should be permitted at all. Some people treat the square as a place where anyone can speak; others point to the shops and the residents living around it, and ask who carries the cost of an open microphone in a shared space.

scene: 一座虚构城市准备试点：向所有成年常住居民每月无条件发放一笔基本生活补贴，资金来自新增的财产税。支持者说这能让人有底气拒绝糟糕的工作，反对者说这会养懒人。

options.t: 我赞成无条件发放，有了托底人才敢辞掉压榨自己的工作。
options.t_en: I'm in favor of unconditional payments, because having a floor under you is what makes it possible to quit a job that's grinding you down.

options.t: 我反对，无条件发钱削弱劳动意愿，要发也该改成与就业挂钩的补贴。
options.t_en: I'm against it. Unconditional cash weakens the will to work; if we're going to pay anything at all, it should be tied to employment instead.

options.t: 我赞成，但主张只发给收入低于某条线的人，钱要用在刀刃上。
options.t_en: I'm in favor, but only for people below a certain income line. The money needs to go where it actually makes a difference.

options.t: 我认为应由各社区自行筹资、自行决定发多少，而不是全城一个标准。
options.t_en: I think each neighborhood should raise its own funds and decide how much to pay out, rather than having one standard for the whole city.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: A fictional city is preparing a pilot program: every adult long-term resident would receive an unconditional monthly basic living allowance, funded by a newly introduced property tax. Supporters say this gives people the confidence to walk away from bad jobs. Opponents say it will simply breed laziness. The scheme would apply to everyone regardless of income or employment status, and the debate has split the city along lines that do not match the usual political ones.

scene: 某虚构城邦讨论对超过一定规模的遗产征收高比例税，税款专用于公共教育。一些家族企业主表示这等于对同一笔钱征两次税。

options.t: 我支持高比例征收并全额投入公共教育，出身不该决定一个人的起点。
options.t_en: I support the high rate and putting every cent into public education. Where you start in life should not be decided by whose family you were born into.

options.t: 我反对，财产在赚取时已经完税，怎么传给子女是家庭内部的事。
options.t_en: I oppose it. The money was already taxed when it was earned, and how a family passes it on to its children is the family's own business.

options.t: 我支持征收但把起征点定得极高，只影响极少数人。
options.t_en: I support a tax, but with the threshold set very high, so that it only touches a very small number of people.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A fictional city-state is debating a steep tax on inheritances above a certain size, with all the revenue earmarked for public education. Some owners of family businesses say this amounts to taxing the same money twice.

scene: 一家公司的创始人年薪是普通员工中位数的数百倍。员工代表提议在公司章程里写入最高薪酬与最低薪酬的倍数上限。

options.t: 我支持设倍数上限，差距大到一定程度，协作关系会先垮掉。
options.t_en: I support a ratio cap. Once the gap gets wide enough, the working relationship is the first thing to collapse.

options.t: 我反对设限，薪酬由市场稀缺度和实际贡献决定，行政划线只会赶走人。
options.t_en: I oppose a cap. Pay is set by how scarce a skill is in the market and by what someone actually contributes; drawing an administrative line will only drive people away.

options.t: 我支持强制公开完整薪酬结构，透明本身就会产生约束。
options.t_en: I support requiring the full pay structure to be published. Transparency by itself creates pressure to justify itself.

options.t: 我支持把超出上限的部分强制转成全员持股。
options.t_en: I support converting anything above the cap into shares held by all employees.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: At one company, the founder's annual pay is several hundred times the median salary of an ordinary employee. Employee representatives have proposed writing a cap into the company charter, setting a maximum ratio between the highest and the lowest pay in the firm. Management says pay reflects how scarce a skill is in the market and what each person actually delivers; staff say that once the gap grows this wide, the first thing to break down is how people work together.

scene: 一条老街的商铺租金连续几年上涨，开了二十年的修鞋铺和面馆陆续搬走，取而代之的是连锁店。居民既怀念老店，也承认新店更干净。

options.t: 我支持给这类街区设定租金涨幅上限，保住小店和它们带来的生活便利。
options.t_en: I support capping rent increases in neighborhoods like this, to keep the small shops and the everyday convenience they bring.

options.t: 我认为房东有权自由定价，租不起说明这个位置该换更有效率的用途。
options.t_en: I think landlords have the right to set their own prices. If you can't afford the rent, that's a sign this location should go to a more efficient use.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: Rents on an old street have climbed for several years running. A shoe repair shop and a noodle restaurant that had been there for twenty years have gradually moved out, replaced by chain stores. Residents miss the old places and at the same time admit the new shops are cleaner. The street is busier than ever, but the people who actually live there say it no longer feels like somewhere they can afford to linger.

scene: 本地几家手工木器作坊被外地机械化生产的同类商品冲击，价格差近一半。街区居民在讨论要不要发起优先购买本地货的倡议。

options.t: 我会优先买本地作坊的东西，保住的是街区的手艺和熟人的饭碗。
options.t_en: I would buy from the local workshops first. What I am keeping alive is the street's craft and my neighbours' livelihoods.

options.t: 我会买更便宜的那个，普通人省下来的钱同样是实实在在的价值。
options.t_en: I would buy whichever is cheaper. The money an ordinary family saves is real value too.

options.t: 我支持用公共资金补贴作坊做设计和转型，而不是去限制外地商品进来。
options.t_en: I support using public money to help the workshops with design and retooling, rather than blocking goods from elsewhere from coming in.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Several local hand-carved woodworking shops are being undercut by machine-made goods from elsewhere at roughly half the price. Residents on the street are debating whether to launch a buy-local-first campaign.

scene: 一个虚构岛屿社区八成粮食靠外部输入。议事会讨论是否对进口食品加征关税，用税收扶持本地农场，代价是短期内食品价格上涨。

options.t: 我支持加征关税，粮食能不能自己种出来是安全底线，不能全押在外部。
options.t_en: I support the tariff. Whether we can grow our own food is a basic security line, and we cannot stake all of it on the outside.

options.t: 我反对加税，涨价最终由收入最低的家庭承担，代价分摊得极不公平。
options.t_en: I oppose the tax. The price increase will end up on the lowest-income households, and the burden is spread deeply unfairly.

options.t: 我支持零关税，并与邻近岛屿签订长期互供协定，把风险分散出去。
options.t_en: I support a zero tariff, together with long-term mutual supply agreements with neighbouring islands, so the risk is spread rather than concentrated.

options.t: 我支持税率随季节浮动，本地收获季保护农场，淡季完全放开。
options.t_en: I support a rate that moves with the seasons: protect the farms during the local harvest, and open up completely in the off season.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: In a fictional island community, about eighty percent of the food comes in from outside. The island council is debating whether to place a tariff on imported food and use the revenue to support local farms, knowing that the cost will land as higher food prices in the short term. Those in favour talk about what happens if the ships stop coming; those against talk about which households will feel the price rise first.

scene: 一家老工厂排放全部达标，但单位能耗远高于同行。关停它可以腾出配额给新产业，但会让几百名年纪偏大的工人失业。

options.t: 我支持限期关停，高能耗的代价其实一直在由所有人替它承担。
options.t_en: I support shutting it down on a set timeline. The cost of that high energy use has been carried by everyone else all along.

options.t: 我支持继续运营，先保住这几百个家庭的收入，转型可以慢慢来。
options.t_en: I support keeping it running. Protect the income of those few hundred families first; the transition can take its time.

options.t: 我支持设立转型基金，边逐步减产边免费培训工人转岗。
options.t_en: I support setting up a transition fund: wind production down gradually while retraining workers for new jobs at no cost to them.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: An old factory is fully within emissions limits, but its energy consumption per unit of output is far above what its competitors use. Shutting it down would free up quota for newer industries, but it would put several hundred older workers out of a job. Most of them are close to retirement and have skills that transfer poorly elsewhere. The factory's managers argue that compliance is compliance, while the workers ask why they should pay for a number they never chose.

scene: 城市规划把一条通勤快速路的走线画在一片有百年老树的林地上。通勤族测算这条路每天能省下四十分钟，环保团体则指出这片林地无法重建。

options.t: 我反对修路，几十年长成的林子毁掉就没了，时间成本可以用别的方式省。
options.t_en: I oppose the road. A grove that took decades to grow is gone once it is destroyed, and the time can be saved in other ways.

options.t: 我支持修路，每天堵在路上的四十分钟也是普通人真实的生命成本。
options.t_en: I support the road. Those forty minutes stuck in traffic every day are a real cost in ordinary people's lives too.

options.t: 我支持改走绕行方案并同步加建轨道交通，多花钱但两头都保住。
options.t_en: I support the detour option with rail transit built alongside. It costs more, but both are preserved.

options.t: 我认为应由沿线居民公投决定，承受后果的人才有资格拍板。
options.t_en: I think it should be decided by a referendum of the residents along the route. Only the people who bear the consequences should have the final say.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: The city's plan routes a new commuter expressway through a grove of century-old trees. Commuters estimate the road would save them forty minutes a day; environmental groups point out that the grove cannot be recreated once it is gone.

scene: 社区准备推行强制垃圾分类，并按专用垃圾袋数量计费，扔得越多交得越多。有居民担心这对人口多、收入低的家庭不公平。

options.t: 我支持强制分类加计量收费，谁产生的垃圾多谁多付，这才叫责任对等。
options.t_en: I support mandatory sorting with charges by volume. Whoever produces more waste pays more; that is what matching responsibility to cost looks like.

options.t: 我支持以宣传引导为主，罚款和计费会先压到最扛不住的家庭头上。
options.t_en: I support leading with information and encouragement. Fines and per-bag charges will land first on the households least able to absorb them.

options.t: 我认为应先由管理方把回收点和处理链建好，再谈对居民的处罚。
options.t_en: I think the management should build the collection points and the processing chain first, and only then talk about penalising residents.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The neighbourhood is about to bring in mandatory waste sorting, charged by the number of official rubbish bags a household uses: the more you throw away, the more you pay. Some residents say that is fair, because whoever produces the waste should cover the cost. Others point out that a family with more people and less income will end up paying more for something it cannot avoid, and that the scheme asks most of the people with the least room to change.

scene: 城郊有一片湿地，既可以开发成产业园区带来长期税收和岗位，也可以整体划为保护区。它同时是下游三个城镇的蓄水与净水缓冲带。

options.t: 我支持整体保留为保护区，它的价值本来就不该用税收来衡量。
options.t_en: I support keeping the whole thing as a protected area. Its value was never something that should be measured in tax revenue.

options.t: 我支持开发园区，就业和税收能实实在在改善本地人的生活水平。
options.t_en: I support developing the industrial park. Jobs and tax revenue can make a real difference to local people's standard of living.

options.t: 我支持只开发边缘一小块，并从收益中固定提取生态补偿基金。
options.t_en: I support developing only a small strip at the edge, and earmarking a fixed share of the proceeds for an ecological compensation fund.

options.t: 我支持交给跨区域生态委员会评估，湿地的水不只属于一个城市。
options.t_en: I support handing the assessment to a cross-regional ecological committee. The wetland's water does not belong to one city alone.

options.t: 我支持把湿地交给民间信托长期托管，避免每换一届规划就变一次。
options.t_en: I support placing the wetland under a civic trust for the long term, so the plans do not flip every time a new administration comes in.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: On the edge of the city there is a wetland. It could be developed into an industrial park that would bring long-term tax revenue and jobs, or it could be designated as a protected area in its entirety. It also happens to be the water storage and filtration buffer for three towns downstream. The land is currently held by the city, and a decision is expected within the year.

scene: 楼里一位住户在阳台密集种植开花植物，引来蜜蜂和小虫，隔壁两户抱怨不敢开窗。种植者说自己在做城市生态的小实验。

options.t: 我觉得阳台是私人空间，怎么用是他的自由，介意的人可以装纱窗。
options.t_en: I think a balcony is private space and how it is used is his own business. Anyone bothered can fit insect screens.

options.t: 我会推动整栋楼一起定个绿植公约，紧挨着的空间总得有点共识。
options.t_en: I would push for the whole building to agree a greening code. When spaces are this close together, there has to be some common understanding.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: One resident in our building has densely planted flowering plants on the balcony, which draws bees and small insects, and the two neighbouring flats complain that they no longer dare open their windows. The grower says it is a small experiment in urban ecology.

scene: 一所中学在讨论是否按考试成绩把学生分成不同进度的班级。老师认为分层教学更高效，一些家长担心孩子被贴上标签后就再也翻不了身。

options.t: 我支持分班，因材施教效率最高，把差距大的学生放一起谁都吃不好。
options.t_en: I support streaming. Teaching to the level of the class is the most efficient approach; put students of very different levels in one room and nobody gets a good lesson.

options.t: 我反对分班，标签会内化成孩子对自己的判断，代价比效率损失大得多。
options.t_en: I oppose streaming. The label turns into how a child judges themselves, and that costs far more than any loss of efficiency.

options.t: 我支持按科目走班分层，允许随时升降，分的是进度不是人。
options.t_en: I support setting by subject, with movement up and down at any time. What is being divided is the pace, not the person.

options.t: 我支持把方案交给全体家长和学生代表投票决定。
options.t_en: I support putting the decision to a vote of all parents and student representatives.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A secondary school is debating whether to split students into classes that move at different paces, based on exam results. Teachers argue that teaching to the level of the group is simply more effective, and that a wide spread of ability in one room helps nobody. Some parents worry that a child placed in the slower stream will be labelled, and that the label will outlast the exam results that produced it.

scene: 一所学校打算在教室安装带行为分析功能的摄像头，自动统计每个学生的抬头率与专注时长，生成周报发给老师和家长。

options.t: 我支持装，客观数据能帮老师看清哪一段课讲砸了。
options.t_en: I support installing them. Objective data helps teachers see which stretch of a lesson went badly.

options.t: 我反对装，教室里被持续打分的人会不敢走神，也会不敢提蠢问题。
options.t_en: I'm against it. When you're being scored continuously in a classroom, you stop letting your mind wander, and you stop asking stupid questions.

options.t: 我支持只做全班匿名统计，不识别也不记录到具体某个学生。
options.t_en: I support keeping only anonymous class-wide statistics, with no identification and nothing recorded against an individual student.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A school plans to install cameras in classrooms that use behavior analysis to automatically tally each student's head-up rate and time spent focused, then generate a weekly report for teachers and parents. The vendor says the system is accurate and unobtrusive. Some teachers are curious to see which stretch of a lesson is losing the room. Some students have already started asking whether they can see their own scores. The school has not yet said whether taking part would be optional.

scene: 小学在讨论午餐制度：是全校统一供餐，还是允许学生自带便当。统一供餐意味着口味单一但没人被看出家境差别，自带则更灵活。

options.t: 我支持统一供餐并全部免费，让每个孩子中午吃到的东西看起来一样。
options.t_en: I support one school meal, free for everyone, so that what every child eats at noon looks the same.

options.t: 我支持自带或自费选餐，每个家庭的口味、体质和预算本来就不同。
options.t_en: I support packed lunches or paying for what you choose. Every family's taste, health needs and budget are different to begin with.

options.t: 我支持统一供餐但按家庭收入分档收费，困难家庭全免。
options.t_en: I support one school meal but with fees scaled to household income, and free for families in difficulty.

options.t: 我支持成立学生和家长共同参与的膳食委员会，菜单由他们定。
options.t_en: I support setting up a meals committee with pupils and parents, and letting them set the menu.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A primary school is debating its lunch system: one meal served to everyone, or letting pupils bring their own boxes. A single school meal means monotonous food, but no child is marked out by how well off the family is; packed lunches are more flexible.

scene: 一所学校的通识阅读课要定书目。校方想给出统一清单以保证质量，几位老师希望按自己班级的兴趣自主选书。

options.t: 我支持统一指定书目，标准一致才谈得上公平和质量把关。
options.t_en: I support one set list. Fairness and quality control only become real once the standard is the same for everyone.

options.t: 我支持老师自主选书，读得杂一点才练得出自己的判断力。
options.t_en: I support letting teachers choose. Reading widely and unevenly is how students develop their own judgement.

options.t: 我支持学校给出核心书目，再留出一半篇幅由师生共同挑选。
options.t_en: I support the school setting a core list and leaving the other half to be chosen by teachers and students together.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: A school is drawing up the reading list for its general reading course. The administration wants one common list for every class, on the grounds that a single standard is the only way to guarantee quality and to keep things fair between classes. Several teachers would rather choose books for their own classes, matching what their students are actually interested in. The question is whether consistency or responsiveness matters more here.

scene: 一座虚构城市近年涌入大量外来务工家庭，其子女入学需求让公立学位极度紧张。本地家庭担心自己孩子被挤掉，外来家庭担心孩子失学。

options.t: 我支持按在本地居住年限排序录取，先来后到是最不容易被操纵的规则。
options.t_en: I support sorting admissions by how long a family has lived here. First come, first served is the rule least easy to manipulate.

options.t: 我支持一视同仁公开摇号，孩子不该替父母的迁移决定买单。
options.t_en: I support one open lottery with everyone treated the same. Children should not have to pay for their parents' decision to move.

options.t: 我支持立刻扩建学校并由全市财政承担，问题出在供给不足而不是谁该让位。
options.t_en: I support building schools right away and funding them out of the whole city's budget. The problem is a shortage of places, not a question of who should step aside.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: A fictional city has taken in a large number of migrant worker families in recent years, and the demand for their children's schooling has stretched public school places to the limit. Local families worry their own children will be squeezed out; migrant families worry their children will be left with nothing. The district has to settle on an admissions rule before the next school year, and every option on the table makes somebody feel they are being pushed to the back of the line.

scene: 一批新搬来的居民在社区里保持着自己的饮食习惯和节庆方式，有时在公共院子里办活动。老住户中有人觉得热闹有趣，有人觉得被打扰。

options.t: 我会去参加他们的节庆，社区里多几种过日子的方式是好事。
options.t_en: I would join their festival. A neighbourhood with several ways of living is a good thing.

options.t: 我觉得应该入乡随俗，公共场合的活动还是按原有习惯来更省事。
options.t_en: I think incomers should follow local custom. Events in shared spaces are less troublesome if they stick to the existing habits.

options.t: 我觉得各过各的就行，只要不影响我，谁怎么生活都不关我的事。
options.t_en: I think everyone should just get on with their own life. As long as it does not affect me, how others live is none of my business.

options.t: 我会张罗一次两边一起做饭的邻里聚餐，先认识人再谈规矩。
options.t_en: I would organise a neighbourhood dinner where both sides cook together. Get to know people first, then talk about rules.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A group of newly arrived residents keep their own food habits and festivals, and sometimes hold events in the shared courtyard. Some long-time residents find it lively and interesting; others feel intruded upon.

scene: 城市交通系统在讨论公共标识是否加注第二种常用语言。加注能方便相当一部分居住者，但会增加成本，也有人担心削弱共同语言的地位。

options.t: 我支持加注，标识存在的意义就是让所有真实生活在这里的人看懂。
options.t_en: I support adding it. The whole point of a sign is that everyone who really lives here can read it.

options.t: 我反对加注，统一的公共语言是共同体最基础的黏合剂。
options.t_en: I oppose adding it. One shared public language is the most basic thing holding a community together.

options.t: 我支持只在实际使用人口比例高的片区加注，按需求决定而不是一刀切。
options.t_en: I support adding it only in districts where a high share of residents actually use that language, decided by need rather than by one blanket rule.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: The city's transport system is debating whether public signs should carry a second, widely spoken language alongside the main one. Adding it would make the network far easier to use for a substantial share of the people who actually live here, and it costs money to print, replace and maintain. Some argue that the extra line would gradually weaken the standing of the common language that holds the city together.

scene: 城市计划在所有主干道加装带实时人脸比对功能的摄像头，宣称可以显著提高找回失踪人口和破获盗窃案的效率。系统由一家外包公司运维。

options.t: 我支持装，能更快找到失踪的人、抓到惯偷，这个交换我愿意做。
options.t_en: I support installing them. Finding missing people faster and catching repeat thieves is a trade I'm willing to make.

options.t: 我反对装，知道自己随时被认出来，人在街上的行为就会变形。
options.t_en: I'm against it. Knowing you could be recognized at any moment changes how people behave in public.

options.t: 我支持装，但每次调阅都必须经第三方审批并全程留痕、定期公开次数。
options.t_en: I support installing them, but every query should need third-party approval, be logged end to end, and the number of queries published regularly.

options.t: 我支持只保留录像供案发后回溯，坚决不开实时比对功能。
options.t_en: I support keeping only the recordings for review after an incident has been reported, and firmly oppose switching on real-time matching at all.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The city plans to install cameras with real-time facial matching on all its main roads, claiming it would sharply improve the speed of finding missing persons and solving theft cases. The system would be operated and maintained by an outside contractor. Officials have not published how long the footage is kept or the rules under which the contractor's staff may query it, and the contract itself is not public.

scene: 一家连锁超市用摄像头分析顾客在货架前的停留路径，结合会员卡推送个性化优惠券，据说能让常客每月省下不少钱。

options.t: 我会注销会员卡、结账走现金，我不想让自己的动线被拿去做模型。
options.t_en: I would cancel the loyalty card and pay in cash. I do not want my route through the shop turned into a model.

options.t: 我会继续用，换来的折扣是真金白银，我不介意被分析买菜习惯。
options.t_en: I would keep using it. The discounts are real money, and I do not mind my grocery habits being analysed.

options.t: 我认为应强制商家在门口显著告知，并提供一键退出且不影响价格的选项。
options.t_en: I think shops should be required to post a prominent notice at the door and offer a one-click opt-out that does not affect prices.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A supermarket chain uses cameras to analyse how customers linger in front of shelves, then pushes personalised coupons through its loyalty card. Regulars are said to save a fair amount each month.

scene: 一位家长犹豫要不要在读初中的孩子手机上装管理软件，可以实时定位、查看聊天记录和限制应用。孩子明确表示反对。

options.t: 我会装，未成年阶段安全排在隐私前面，等成年了自然放手。
options.t_en: I would install it. While they are a minor, safety comes before privacy; once they are an adult I will let go.

options.t: 我不会装，在监视里长大的人学不会自己判断风险。
options.t_en: I would not install it. Someone who grows up under surveillance never learns to judge risk for themselves.

options.t: 我会和孩子谈好只开定位、不看聊天内容，规则由两个人一起定。
options.t_en: I would agree with my child to switch on location only and not read their messages, with the rules set by both of us.

options.t: 我什么都不装，平时保持信任，真出问题再说。
options.t_en: I would install nothing. Trust them day to day, and deal with a real problem only if one actually appears.

options.t: 我会希望学校统一提供一套安全管理方案，家长各干各的反而混乱。
options.t_en: I would want the school to provide one common safety scheme; parents each doing their own thing only creates confusion.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: A parent is torn over whether to install monitoring software on their middle-school child's phone. The app would show the child's location in real time, let the parent read chat histories and block selected apps. The child has said plainly that they do not want it. The parent is thinking about safety, and about the fact that the phone was bought so the child could be reached; the child is thinking about being watched by the person they live with.

scene: 小区新换的快递柜默认要求刷脸取件，输入取件码需要额外多点三步。物业说刷脸能减少冒领。

options.t: 我会坚持用取件码，多点几下无所谓，生物特征我不愿意随便留。
options.t_en: I'll stick with the pickup code. A few extra taps are fine; I'm not handing over biometric data just because it's convenient.

options.t: 我会直接刷脸，快、准、不容易被别人拿走，没必要为此较劲。
options.t_en: I'll just use the face scan. It's fast, accurate, and hard for someone else to take, and it's not worth picking a fight over.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: The parcel lockers newly installed in my compound default to unlocking by face scan. Entering a pickup code takes three extra taps. Building management says the face scan cuts down on parcels being collected by the wrong person, and that nearly everyone has switched over. My own face is now something I have to hand to a locker in order to collect a parcel I already paid to have delivered.

scene: 一种新疗法对某类罕见病效果显著，但单个疗程费用极高。公共医保基金总额固定，纳入它意味着另外几个受益人数更多的项目要削减额度。

options.t: 我支持全额纳入，一个人的命不该因为得的病太罕见就被算不划算。
options.t_en: I support covering it in full. A person's life should not be written off as a poor buy because the disease is too rare.

options.t: 我反对纳入，公共资金有限，应该优先覆盖受益人数最多的项目。
options.t_en: I oppose covering it. Public money is limited and should go first to the programmes that reach the most people.

options.t: 我支持纳入但按家庭收入分档自付，越富的家庭自付比例越高。
options.t_en: I support covering it, but with co-payments scaled to household income, so that richer families pay a larger share.

options.t: 我支持由患者互助基金加商业保险来兜这一块，公共医保只保基础。
options.t_en: I support funding this through patient mutual-aid funds and private insurance, with public insurance covering only the basics.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A new therapy works remarkably well for one rare disease, but a single course costs an enormous amount. The public health insurance fund has a fixed total: covering it would mean trimming several other programmes that reach far more people.

scene: 一座虚构城市进入呼吸道疾病高发季，医院走廊排满了人。管理方在讨论是否在室内公共场所强制佩戴口罩，违者罚款。

options.t: 我支持强制并配套处罚，人挤人的空间里，个人选择会直接落到别人身上。
options.t_en: I support a mandate with penalties attached. In a packed room, a personal choice lands directly on other people.

options.t: 我反对强制，把风险和信息讲清楚，戴不戴由成年人自己判断。
options.t_en: I oppose a mandate. Set out the risk and the information clearly, and let adults decide for themselves whether to wear one.

options.t: 我支持只在医院和养老机构强制，其余场所自愿。
options.t_en: I support requiring masks only in hospitals and care homes, and leaving every other setting voluntary.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A fictional city has entered its high season for respiratory illness, and the corridors of its hospitals are packed. The authorities are debating whether to require masks in indoor public spaces, with a fine for anyone who does not comply. Supporters point out that in a crowded room one person's choice lands directly on the people standing next to them. Critics say adults can weigh the risk themselves, provided the information is clear and the rules are stated plainly.

scene: 一家研究机构希望汇集大量匿名化的就诊记录训练疾病预测模型。参与者可以获得少量补贴，但数据一旦汇入就难以单独撤回。

options.t: 我愿意匿名捐出自己的记录，研究成果最终会回到每个人身上。
options.t_en: I'd be willing to donate my records anonymously. The results of the research eventually come back to everyone.

options.t: 我不愿意，健康记录是最私密的东西，匿名化也未必真的匿不掉。
options.t_en: I wouldn't. Health records are the most private thing there is, and anonymization may not really make them anonymous.

options.t: 我愿意，但要求每一次调用都单独征求我的授权并可随时终止。
options.t_en: I would, but I'd want to be asked for consent separately each time the data is used, and to be able to stop it at any point.

options.t: 我认为这类数据应由公共机构统一托管，并彻底禁止转售给商业公司。
options.t_en: I think this kind of data should be held by a public body, with resale to commercial companies banned outright.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A research institute wants to pool a large number of anonymized medical records to train a disease prediction model. Participants get a small payment, but once the data has been merged it is hard to withdraw any single record. The institute says the anonymization is thorough and that the model could catch diseases earlier for everyone. Some patients have started asking what happens if they change their mind a year from now, and nobody has given them a clear answer.

scene: 城市讨论对高糖饮料按含糖量征税，税收专项用于补贴学校和社区的健康餐。饮料店主认为这是在替消费者做决定。

options.t: 我支持征税并把钱投回健康餐，价格信号比劝说管用得多。
options.t_en: I support the tax and putting the money back into healthy meals. Prices change behaviour far better than advice.

options.t: 我反对，成年人喝什么是自己的事，不该被价格惩罚。
options.t_en: I oppose it. What an adult drinks is their own business and should not be punished through price.

options.t: 我支持改为强制在包装正面标注含糖量，让人看得见再自己选。
options.t_en: I support mandatory sugar labelling on the front of the pack instead, so people can see it and then choose.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: The city is debating a tax on sugary drinks scaled to sugar content, with the revenue earmarked to subsidise healthy meals in schools and community kitchens. Shop owners who sell the drinks say this is deciding on consumers' behalf.

scene: 一家公司管理层中某一性别占比长期不足两成。有人提议在章程中写入最低比例，有人认为这会让被提拔者背上非议。

options.t: 我支持设最低比例，不设硬指标，这个数字十年也不会动。
options.t_en: I support a minimum share. Without a hard target, that number will not move in ten years either.

options.t: 我反对配额，晋升只该看能力，人为设比例对谁都不公平。
options.t_en: I oppose quotas. Promotion should turn on ability alone, and a set ratio is unfair to everyone.

options.t: 我支持改造招聘与晋升流程本身，比如匿名初筛和结构化面试，而不是定比例。
options.t_en: I support rebuilding the hiring and promotion process itself, with anonymous first-round screening and structured interviews, rather than setting a ratio.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: At one company, one gender has long made up less than a fifth of management. Some people have proposed writing a minimum share into the company charter. Others say that would put a permanent asterisk next to anyone promoted under it, as if the position had been owed rather than earned. Both sides agree the number has not moved on its own for years; they disagree about what should now be done about it.

scene: 一项提案要求育儿假在父母双方之间等长发放且必须休完，不休作废。企业担心成本，一些家庭说自己更愿意灵活分配。

options.t: 我支持等长且强制休，不强制的话大多数家庭还是会落回原来的分工。
options.t_en: I support equal and mandatory. Without the requirement, most families will just fall back into the same division as before.

options.t: 我反对强制，谁休多久应该由每个家庭按自己的实际情况商量。
options.t_en: I'm against making it mandatory. Who takes how much leave should be worked out by each family according to their own situation.

options.t: 我支持假期等长但完全自愿，先把权利给足再谈观念。
options.t_en: I support leave of equal length that is entirely voluntary. Give people the full right first, and let attitudes catch up.

options.t: 我支持由公共基金承担育儿假的全部成本，否则企业只会绕开可能要休假的人。
options.t_en: I support having a public fund cover the whole cost of parental leave. Otherwise employers will simply find ways around hiring anyone who might take it.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A proposal would require parental leave to be granted in equal length to both parents, and to be taken in full or forfeited. Employers say the cost and the scheduling disruption would be heavy, especially for small firms. Some families say they would rather divide the leave flexibly according to what actually works for them. The proposal's supporters argue that without a hard rule, most households will simply fall back into the old division of labor.

scene: 社区羽毛球联赛报名时，有人提议取消传统的性别分组，改为按积分水平分级；也有人觉得沿用旧分组更省事。

options.t: 我支持改成按水平分级，同水平打起来才好看，分组依据应该是能力。
options.t_en: I support moving to tiers by rating. Matches are better when the levels are even, and ability should be the basis for grouping.

options.t: 我支持沿用原来的分组，规则简单、大家熟悉，改动会让不少人不来了。
options.t_en: I support keeping the existing divisions. The rules are simple and familiar, and changing them would put a lot of people off coming.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: At sign-up for the community badminton league, someone proposed dropping the traditional gender divisions in favour of tiers based on rating points; others think keeping the old divisions is simply less trouble.

scene: 一家公司启用算法自动筛选简历，通过率明显下降但招聘周期缩短。有候选人反映自己连人都没见到就被刷掉了。

options.t: 我支持继续用，算法至少不会因为照片和口音产生个人偏见。
options.t_en: I support keeping it. An algorithm at least does not form a personal bias from a photo or an accent.

options.t: 我反对，历史数据里的偏见会被算法学走并放大成规则。
options.t_en: I oppose it. The biases buried in historical data get learned by the algorithm and then applied as rules.

options.t: 我支持用，但必须允许任何被拒者申请人工复核并给出理由。
options.t_en: I support using it, but anyone rejected must be able to request a human review, with reasons given.

options.t: 我支持用，同时公开评分维度和权重，让候选人知道自己被怎么衡量。
options.t_en: I support using it and publishing the scoring dimensions and their weights, so candidates know how they are being measured.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: A company has started using an algorithm to screen CVs automatically. The share of applicants getting through has fallen noticeably, while the hiring cycle has become much shorter. Some candidates say they were filtered out without ever speaking to a human being, and cannot tell what they were rejected for. The company says the system is faster and applies exactly the same standard to every applicant.

scene: 一款助手可以模仿你的语气自动回复日常消息，回复质量已经难以分辨。同事群里有人开始用它应付寒暄。

options.t: 我会用，寒暄本来就消耗时间，省下来的精力可以放在真正的事上。
options.t_en: I'd use it. Small talk eats up time anyway, and the energy I save can go into things that actually matter.

options.t: 我不会用，人跟人说话的价值就在于是本人在说。
options.t_en: I wouldn't. The whole value of one person talking to another is that it's actually them talking.

options.t: 我会用，但每条自动回复都会标明是助手代回。
options.t_en: I'd use it, but every automatic reply would be marked as sent by an assistant.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: An assistant can mimic your tone of voice well enough to reply to everyday messages on your behalf, and the quality is now hard to tell apart from your own. In the colleagues' group chat, some people have started using it to handle the small talk. Nobody has announced that they are doing it. I noticed because a reply to me arrived in wording that was slightly too polished, and then I started wondering how many of the conversations I'd had that week were actually with the person I thought.

scene: 一辆自动驾驶车在复杂路况下发生剐蹭。车主说自己没碰方向盘，厂商说驾驶员应保持接管准备，保险公司拒绝先行赔付。

options.t: 我认为责任应归厂商，系统是谁设计的谁就得为它的判断负责。
options.t_en: I think liability should fall on the manufacturer. Whoever designed the system should answer for its judgments.

options.t: 我认为责任归车主，选择开启这个功能就等于接受它的风险。
options.t_en: I think liability falls on the owner. Choosing to switch the function on means accepting its risks.

options.t: 我主张由全行业出资建立共同赔付基金，先赔人再慢慢分责任。
options.t_en: I argue for an industry-wide compensation fund. Pay the injured first, then sort out liability slowly.

options.t: 我主张强制全程记录行车数据并接受监管调取，否则永远说不清。
options.t_en: I argue for mandatory recording of all driving data, open to regulators on request. Otherwise it can never be settled.

options.t: 我主张在责任规则明确之前，这类功能就不该放上公共道路。
options.t_en: I argue that until liability rules are clear, this kind of function should not be allowed on public roads at all.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: A self-driving car scraped another vehicle in complicated traffic. The owner says his hands never touched the wheel; the manufacturer says the driver should have stayed ready to take over; the insurer refuses to pay out up front.

scene: 学校发现越来越多作业由生成工具完成，文笔整齐但看不出思考过程。老师之间对是禁还是教产生分歧。

options.t: 我支持允许并专门教怎么用，这类工具早晚会成为基本功。
options.t_en: I support allowing them and teaching explicitly how to use them. These tools will be basic literacy sooner or later.

options.t: 我支持全面禁止，基础的读写和推理必须自己一遍遍练出来。
options.t_en: I support a full ban. Basic reading, writing and reasoning have to be built up by doing them yourself, over and over.

options.t: 我支持允许，但必须一并提交思路草稿和修改记录。
options.t_en: I support allowing them, but a draft of the thinking and the revision history must be submitted alongside the final work.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: The school has noticed that more and more assignments are being produced with generation tools. The prose comes back tidy and well organised, but there is no visible trace of anyone actually thinking the problem through. Some teachers want the tools banned outright in coursework. Others argue that students will use them anyway once they leave school, and that the school's job is to teach them how to use the tools honestly rather than pretend they do not exist.

scene: 一名初次犯事的年轻人偷了一辆自行车，金额不大但情节清楚。社区、失主和处理人员对怎么办法产生分歧。

options.t: 我支持用社区服务替代关押，第一次就把人推进去，出来更难回头。
options.t_en: I support community service instead of detention. Push someone inside on their first offense and it's harder for them to come back afterwards.

options.t: 我支持严格照规定处理，例外开多了规则就没人当真了。
options.t_en: I support handling it strictly according to the rules. Make too many exceptions and nobody takes the rules seriously anymore.

options.t: 我支持先足额赔偿失主，再由双方当面调解达成谅解。
options.t_en: I support full compensation to the owner first, and then a face-to-face mediation between the two sides to reach an understanding.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A young person with no prior record stole a bicycle. The amount is small and the facts are clear. The community, the owner and the people handling the case disagree about what should happen: the owner wants to be made whole, some neighbors want the young person to face the full consequence, and the case worker thinks the first offense is the one that decides which way a life goes. Everyone agrees the bicycle should go back to its owner.

scene: 某地考虑把全部裁判文书上网公开，任何人可检索。支持者说这是最好的监督，反对者说当事人的姓名会被搜索引擎永久绑定。

options.t: 我支持全部公开，公开审判的记录能被查阅，本身就是对裁判者的约束。
options.t_en: I support full publication. The record of an open trial being searchable is itself a constraint on the courts.

options.t: 我反对公开，一次纠纷会跟着一个人一辈子，代价过重。
options.t_en: I oppose publication. One dispute follows a person for life, and the cost is too heavy.

options.t: 我支持公开但彻底隐去当事人身份信息，只留事实与说理。
options.t_en: I support publication with the parties' identifying details removed entirely, leaving only the facts and the reasoning.

options.t: 我支持只向经审核的研究者和律师开放，不面向全网。
options.t_en: I support access only for vetted researchers and lawyers, not the whole internet.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A jurisdiction is considering posting every court judgment online, searchable by anyone. Supporters call it the best oversight there is; opponents say the parties' names would be permanently bound to the case by search engines.

scene: 某地试行让随机抽选的普通居民参与部分案件的评议，与专业人员共同讨论事实认定。有人认为这能防止小圈子自说自话，有人担心外行添乱。

options.t: 我支持推广，让普通人真正参与进去，专业共同体才不会越走越封闭。
options.t_en: I support extending it. Once ordinary people are genuinely in the room, a professional circle stops drifting into talking only to itself.

options.t: 我反对，涉及技术判断的事情就该交给受过训练的人。
options.t_en: I oppose it. Anything that turns on technical judgement should be left to people who have been trained for it.

options.t: 我支持先在事实争议较简单的案件类型里试行，看效果再扩大。
options.t_en: I support piloting it first in types of case where the factual disputes are relatively simple, and widening it once the results are in.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: One jurisdiction is piloting a scheme in which randomly selected ordinary residents sit in on the review of certain cases, discussing the findings of fact alongside trained professionals. Supporters say it stops a small professional circle from settling everything among themselves. Critics worry that people with no training will slow the process down or introduce errors into decisions that turn on technical judgement.

scene: 一所公立学校收到申请，希望在教学楼里设一间供祈祷或静坐使用的房间。校方担心一旦开口，各方需求都会找上门。

options.t: 我支持设一间完全中性的静思室，有信仰的和没信仰的人都能用。
options.t_en: I support setting up a completely neutral quiet room that people with faith and people without faith can both use.

options.t: 我支持按校内实际人数较多的信仰群体的需求安排专门场所。
options.t_en: I support arranging dedicated space according to the needs of the faith group with the largest actual numbers in the school.

options.t: 我反对在公立校园设任何这类空间，公共教育场所应保持中立。
options.t_en: I oppose setting up any space of this kind on a public school campus. Public education should stay neutral.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: A public school has received a request to set aside a room in the main teaching building for prayer or quiet sitting. The school administration worries that once the door is open, every group with a need will come asking, and that whatever it decides will be read as taking a side. The students who made the request say they only want somewhere quiet. Parents have begun writing in, and the letters do not agree with each other.

scene: 一家由信仰团体创办的养老照护机构申请公共补贴。它服务口碑很好，但内部日常有固定的仪式环节。

options.t: 我支持给补贴，把老人照顾好是实打实的贡献，谁办的不重要。
options.t_en: I support the subsidy. Caring for elderly people well is a real contribution, and who runs it does not matter.

options.t: 我反对给补贴，公共资金不该流向带有信仰门槛的组织。
options.t_en: I oppose the subsidy. Public money should not flow to organisations with a faith requirement.

options.t: 我支持给补贴，但必须写明服务对象不得被要求参与任何仪式。
options.t_en: I support the subsidy, but it must be written in that service users cannot be required to take part in any ritual.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: A care home founded by a religious group has applied for a public subsidy. Its reputation for care is excellent, but its daily routine includes fixed devotional rituals.

scene: 一位员工因信仰习惯希望每周固定时段调休，团队排班因此需要重新安排，几位同事表示这样对其他人不公平。

options.t: 我支持公司灵活安排，尊重个人的重要日子成本并不高。
options.t_en: I support the company arranging it flexibly. Respecting the days that matter to someone costs very little.

options.t: 我认为应统一规则、谁都不开例外，否则理由会越来越多。
options.t_en: I think there should be one rule with no exceptions for anyone, otherwise the number of reasons will only grow.

options.t: 我认为可以调休，但必须由他自己与同事换班解决，不增加别人的负担。
options.t_en: I think the time off can be granted, but he has to arrange the swaps with colleagues himself and not shift the burden onto anyone else.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: An employee has asked for a fixed block of time off each week because of a religious practice. Honouring it means rebuilding the team's shift schedule, which moves other people's hours around. Several colleagues say that is unfair to everyone else, and that a personal commitment should not be charged to the whole team. Others point out that the request is predictable and modest, and that scheduling around it is a cost the team could easily absorb.

scene: 一片老城区房屋结构老化、管线陈旧。方案一是原样修缮加固，成本高、户型仍不便利；方案二是整体拆除新建，居民可分到更大更安全的房子。

options.t: 我支持保护性修缮，街巷的样子和记忆一旦推平就再也长不回来。
options.t_en: I support protective renovation. Once the look and the memory of those lanes are bulldozed, they never grow back.

options.t: 我支持拆除新建，先让人住上安全宽敞的房子，情怀不能当墙用。
options.t_en: I support demolition and rebuilding. Get people into safe, roomy housing first; nostalgia is not something you can build a wall out of.

options.t: 我支持由原住户投票决定，并写死回迁比例和时限。
options.t_en: I support letting the original residents vote on it, with the proportion of returning units and the deadline written in and fixed.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: In an old part of the city, the buildings are structurally worn and the pipes are outdated. Option one is to repair and reinforce them as they are: costly, and the floor plans stay inconvenient. Option two is to demolish and rebuild entirely, in which case residents would get larger and safer homes. The neighborhood lanes would not survive the second option, and the people who have lived there longest are the ones least sure they want to trade the streets they know for more square meters.

scene: 住宅楼里越来越多房子被改成按天出租的民宿，游客进出频繁。房东说这是自己的房子，长住居民抱怨门禁形同虚设、租金还被抬高。

options.t: 我支持允许，房子是私产，怎么用、租给谁由所有者决定。
options.t_en: I support allowing it. A flat is private property, and the owner decides how it is used and to whom it is let.

options.t: 我支持全面禁止，短租既推高租金又把住宅楼变成半个旅馆。
options.t_en: I support a full ban. Short lets both push up rents and turn a residential block into half a hotel.

options.t: 我支持允许但需同层邻居书面同意，并限制每年出租天数。
options.t_en: I support allowing it only with written consent from neighbours on the same floor, and a cap on days let per year.

options.t: 我支持允许但征收高额附加税，用来补贴长租房源。
options.t_en: I support allowing it with a steep surcharge, used to subsidise long-term rental supply.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: More and more flats in our block are being converted into short-term holiday lets, with tourists coming and going at all hours. The owners say it is their own property; long-term residents complain that the door security now means nothing and that rents have been pushed up.

scene: 城市考虑把中心几条街划为全天无机动车区，只留步行与自行车。周边商户担心客流下降，居民则期待更安静的街道。

options.t: 我支持划为无车区，街道本来就该先属于走路的人。
options.t_en: I support making them car-free. A street should belong first of all to the people walking on it.

options.t: 我反对，通勤和小商户的进货会一起变难，代价落在最扛不住的人身上。
options.t_en: I oppose it. Commuting and small shops' deliveries both get harder, and the cost lands on the people least able to carry it.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: The city is considering turning several central streets into car-free zones around the clock, keeping them open only to pedestrians and bicycles. Shopkeepers nearby worry that passing trade will fall once people can no longer drive up and park outside. Residents, on the other hand, have been waiting years for streets that are quieter, cleaner, and safe to walk along in the evening.

scene: 关于某类经过基因改良的作物是否必须在包装上显著标注，出现两派意见。一派说消费者有权知道，一派说标注等于暗示危险。

options.t: 我支持强制标注，知情权和结论无关，人有权知道自己吃的是什么。
options.t_en: I support mandatory labeling. The right to know has nothing to do with what the conclusion turns out to be; people are entitled to know what they're eating.

options.t: 我反对强制标注，在没有证据的情况下加标签只会制造恐慌和溢价。
options.t_en: I oppose mandatory labeling. Adding a label when there is no evidence only manufactures fear and a price premium.

options.t: 我支持自愿标注加上统一的科普说明，让市场和信息一起起作用。
options.t_en: I support voluntary labeling together with a standard public explanation, so that markets and information both do their work.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: There are two camps on whether a certain kind of genetically modified crop must be prominently labeled on packaging. One side says consumers have a right to know what they are eating. The other says a label amounts to implying danger, and that in the absence of evidence it works as a warning rather than as information. The crops in question have been on the market for years, and the packaging debate has become a proxy for an older argument about who gets to decide what counts as safe.

scene: 一个农业区面临选择：继续支持大型规模化农场以压低粮价，还是把补贴转向数量众多的小农户以保持作物多样性。两条路都需要长期投入。

options.t: 我支持规模化，效率高、价格低，受益最大的其实是买菜的普通家庭。
options.t_en: I support scale. It is efficient and keeps prices low, and the biggest beneficiaries are ordinary families buying food.

options.t: 我支持扶持小农户，品种多、地块散，遇到病害和天灾时反而更扛得住。
options.t_en: I support backing smallholders. With more varieties and scattered plots, they actually hold up better against disease and bad weather.

options.t: 我支持推动小农户组成合作社，联合起来采购和议价。
options.t_en: I support helping smallholders form cooperatives so they can buy and negotiate together.

options.t: 我认为交给市场就好，谁能活下来说明谁更适合这块地。
options.t_en: I think it should be left to the market. Whoever survives shows they are better suited to that land.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: A farming region faces a choice: keep backing large-scale farms so as to hold food prices down, or redirect subsidies to the many smallholders so that crop diversity survives. Both paths need long-term investment.

scene: 一座城市每天有大量餐厅临期食品被直接丢弃。有人提议立规矩要求餐厅必须把可食用剩余交给回收网络，餐厅担心一旦出事责任说不清。

options.t: 我支持强制捐赠给统一的回收网络，扔掉能吃的东西本身就是浪费公共资源。
options.t_en: I support mandatory donation to one common collection network. Throwing away food that can still be eaten is itself a waste of shared resources.

options.t: 我反对强制，吃出问题算谁的说不清楚，强推只会让餐厅提前销毁。
options.t_en: I oppose a mandate. If someone falls ill, nobody can say whose fault it is, and forcing it will only make restaurants destroy the food earlier.

options.t: 我支持用税收减免鼓励自愿捐赠，并统一制定免责规则。
options.t_en: I support encouraging voluntary donation through tax relief, together with one clear set of liability exemptions.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: Every day a city throws away large amounts of food that restaurants can no longer sell but that is still perfectly edible. Some people want a rule obliging restaurants to hand their safe leftovers to a collection network that distributes them. Restaurant owners say that the moment something goes wrong nobody can say clearly who is responsible, and that a mandatory scheme will simply push them to bin food earlier so that there is nothing left to donate.

scene: 某内容平台准备给流传较广的消息加上真实性核查标签，标签由外部机构给出。有人认为这能减少谣言，有人认为判断真假本身就是一种权力。

options.t: 我支持加标签，交给多家独立机构交叉核查，总比什么都不做强。
options.t_en: I support the labels, provided several independent organizations cross-check each other. That is still better than doing nothing.

options.t: 我反对加标签，谁有资格给别人的话盖章，这个位置本身就危险。
options.t_en: I oppose the labels. Who is qualified to stamp someone else's words as false? The position itself is the danger.

options.t: 我支持只展示信息来源、发布时间和修改记录，判断留给读者自己做。
options.t_en: I support showing only the source, the time of publication and the edit history, and leaving the judgment to readers.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A content platform is preparing to attach fact-check labels to widely circulated claims, with the labels supplied by outside organizations. Some people think this will cut down on rumors. Others think that deciding what is true and what is false is itself a form of power, and that whoever holds it will eventually use it for something other than accuracy. The platform has not yet said how an organization gets approved, or whether a labeled post can be appealed.

scene: 一座城市讨论要不要用公共资金供养一家不以盈利为目标的新闻机构。反对者说这会造出一个不接受市场检验的机构，支持者说不赚钱的调查报道正在消失。

options.t: 我支持公共资助，纯市场化的媒体一定会先放弃那些没人买单的选题。
options.t_en: I support public funding. A purely market-driven media will always abandon, first, the stories nobody will pay for.

options.t: 我反对，读者愿不愿意订阅就是最直接的检验，养不活说明没人真的需要。
options.t_en: I oppose it. Whether readers subscribe is the most direct test; if it cannot survive, nobody really needed it.

options.t: 我支持资助，但必须设立独立编辑委员会并公开全部资金流向。
options.t_en: I support funding, but only with an independent editorial board and full public disclosure of where the money goes.

options.t: 我支持改由读者共同出资成立合作社性质的媒体，钱从谁那来对谁负责。
options.t_en: I support a reader-funded cooperative instead, so that the outlet answers to the people who pay for it.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.
