scene_en: A city is debating whether to fund a non-profit newsroom from the public purse. Opponents say it would create an outlet that never faces a market test; supporters say investigative reporting that does not turn a profit is disappearing.

scene: 一个公共议题讨论区收到大量匿名爆料，其中确实揭出了一些问题，也出现过恶意捏造。平台在考虑是否取消匿名。

options.t: 我支持保护匿名，很多话只有在不用报上名字时才说得出口。
options.t_en: I support protecting anonymity. A great many things only get said when there is no name attached to them.

options.t: 我支持全面实名，说话要有人负责，捏造才有代价。
options.t_en: I support full real-name registration. Speech has to have someone behind it, or fabrication costs nothing.

options.t: 我支持对公众匿名、向平台留存身份，出事能追溯但日常不暴露。
options.t_en: I support staying anonymous to the public while identity is kept on file with the platform: traceable if something goes wrong, not exposed in ordinary use.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A public discussion board has received a flood of anonymous tip-offs. Some of them turned out to expose real problems that nobody would have raised under their own name; others turned out to be deliberate fabrications aimed at particular people. The platform is now weighing whether to remove anonymity altogether, and everyone involved can see that whichever way it goes, something real gets lost.

scene: 一个片区夜间小偷小摸增多。有人提议组织居民志愿巡逻队，有人认为应该要求专业力量增派夜班，还有人主张先把路灯和监控补齐。

options.t: 我支持居民自己组队巡逻，熟人最清楚哪里不对劲，也最上心。
options.t_en: I support residents organizing their own patrols. Locals know best what looks off, and they care the most.

options.t: 我支持要求专业力量加派，业余的人上手管事容易把小事闹大。
options.t_en: I support demanding more officers from the professional force. Amateurs stepping in to handle things tend to turn small problems into big ones.

options.t: 我支持把照明和监控补齐，用设备替代靠人熬夜盯着。
options.t_en: I support filling in the lighting and camera coverage, and using equipment instead of people staying up all night watching.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Petty theft at night has increased in one neighborhood. Some residents want to organize a volunteer patrol. Others say the right move is to demand that the professional force put more officers on the night shift. Still others argue that the first thing to fix is the streetlights and the missing camera coverage, and that everything else is a distraction from a straightforward infrastructure problem.

scene: 一场关于刑罚目的的公开讨论中，四种主张相持不下：改造、威慑、赔偿受害者、按罪行分类对待。

options.t: 我认为核心是改造，出来以后能正常生活的人才不会再犯。
options.t_en: I think the core is rehabilitation. Someone who can live normally after release will not reoffend.

options.t: 我认为核心是惩罚与威慑，代价足够清楚，很多事才不会发生。
options.t_en: I think the core is punishment and deterrence. When the cost is clear enough, a lot of things simply do not happen.

options.t: 我认为核心是让受害者获得实际赔偿和道歉，而不是单纯关人。
options.t_en: I think the core is that victims get real compensation and an apology, not just that someone is locked up.

options.t: 我认为应按罪行类型分开处理，暴力与非暴力根本不该套同一套逻辑。
options.t_en: I think offences should be handled by type. Violence and non-violence should never be run through the same logic.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: In a public debate on what punishment is for, four positions are deadlocked: rehabilitation, deterrence, compensation for victims, and treating offences differently by type.

scene: 有过前科的人在求职时被系统自动筛出。有人认为雇主有权知道，有人认为这等于终身处罚。

options.t: 我支持设定年限，期满自动封存记录，人应该有把过去翻篇的可能。
options.t_en: I support setting a time limit, after which the record is sealed automatically. People should have the chance to turn the page on their past.

options.t: 我支持永久可查，雇主拿自己的钱和名声冒险，有权知道全部信息。
options.t_en: I support permanent access. An employer is staking their own money and reputation, and has the right to know everything.

options.t: 我支持只对直接相关的岗位开放查询，其他岗位一律不得调取。
options.t_en: I support opening the record only for roles where it is directly relevant, and barring every other employer from requesting it.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: People with a criminal record are being filtered out automatically when they apply for jobs. Some argue that an employer is entitled to know, particularly where the role carries responsibility for money or for other people's safety. Others say an automatic screen turns a sentence that has already been served into a punishment that never ends, and that it quietly removes whole groups of people from the labour market.

scene: 两个相邻的虚构城邦共用一条河。上游城邦提出签订长期取水与治污协定，并互设监督人员；下游城邦内部对是否让外人进来查有分歧。

options.t: 我支持签长期协定并接受互相监督，共用的东西就得一起管。
options.t_en: I support signing a long-term agreement and accepting mutual oversight. Something we share has to be managed together.

options.t: 我反对让外部人员进来核查，关系到生存的资源必须自己完全掌握。
options.t_en: I oppose letting outside personnel in to inspect. A resource that decides whether we survive must stay entirely in our own hands.

options.t: 我支持先签一年期的试行版，跑一轮看对方守不守规矩再谈长期。
options.t_en: I support signing a one-year trial version first. Run one cycle, see whether the other side follows the rules, then talk about the long term.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: Two neighboring fictional city-states share a single river. The upstream city-state has proposed a long-term water intake and pollution treatment agreement, with each side stationing inspectors in the other's territory. Within the downstream city-state there is sharp disagreement about whether to let outsiders in to inspect: some see it as the only way to get an honest accounting, others see it as handing control of a survival resource to a neighbor whose interests differ from theirs.

scene: 若干城邦组成的区域论坛提议制定统一的排放与废弃物标准，达标进度慢的成员需接受外部核查。发展程度较低的成员认为标准是按富裕成员的条件定的。

options.t: 我支持加入并接受核查，共同的空气和水没办法各管一段。
options.t_en: I support joining and accepting inspection. Shared air and water cannot be managed one stretch at a time.

options.t: 我反对统一标准，每个地方处在不同发展阶段，节奏应该自己定。
options.t_en: I oppose common standards. Every place is at a different stage of development and should set its own pace.

options.t: 我支持统一标准，但要求富裕成员出资帮助落后成员改造设备。
options.t_en: I support common standards, but rich members must pay to help the lagging ones upgrade their equipment.

options.t: 我支持先设为自愿目标，几年后再转为强制。
options.t_en: I support setting them as voluntary targets first, then making them mandatory after a few years.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: A regional forum of several city-states has proposed common emission and waste standards, with slower members subject to outside inspection. The less developed members argue that the standards were written to suit the rich ones.

scene: 邻近地区遭遇长期干旱，大量居民想迁入本地。本地住房和学位本就紧张，但拒之门外也意味着这些家庭无处可去。

options.t: 我支持尽力接收并提供过渡安置，换成我们遇到灾也希望别人开门。
options.t_en: I support taking in as many as we can and providing transitional housing. If disaster came to us, we would want someone to open the door.

options.t: 我支持按本地承载力设定上限，超出部分不再接收。
options.t_en: I support setting a ceiling based on what this area can actually absorb, and taking in no one beyond it.

options.t: 我支持把钱投到当地去帮他们打井修渠，而不是把人接过来。
options.t_en: I support putting the money into their own area instead, helping them sink wells and build channels, rather than moving people here.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A neighbouring region has been in drought for a long stretch, and a great many of its residents want to move here. Local housing and school places are already stretched thin, and everyone can see the pressure that would follow. But turning these families away means sending them back to a place with no water and no way to make a living, and that is not a decision anyone takes lightly.

scene: 失业救济金的领取条件正在修订。一种意见是无条件按月发放，另一种是必须定期提交求职记录并参加培训，否则停发。

options.t: 我支持无条件发放，附加一堆证明只会把最需要的人挡在门外。
options.t_en: I support unconditional payments. Piling on paperwork just shuts out the people who need it most.

options.t: 我支持附带求职与培训义务，公共资金要有对应的努力。
options.t_en: I support attaching job search and training obligations. Public money should come with a corresponding effort.

options.t: 我支持基础部分无条件发，额外部分由社区互助基金按实际困难追加。
options.t_en: I support paying the basic part unconditionally, with a community mutual-aid fund topping it up according to actual hardship.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: The conditions for receiving unemployment benefits are being revised. One view is that payments should go out monthly with no strings attached. The other is that recipients must regularly submit a record of job applications and attend training, or the payments stop. Officials point out that the current system already requires paperwork many people fail to complete, and that the people most likely to be cut off are those who find the forms hardest to navigate.

scene: 养老金制度改革方案争论不下：是严格按缴费多少领取，还是设置保底并压缩差距，抑或更多依靠家庭和个人账户。

options.t: 我支持多缴多得，缴得多的人拿得多才谈得上公平。
options.t_en: I support getting out what you paid in. It is only fair that those who contribute more receive more.

options.t: 我支持设保底并压缩上下差距，老年阶段的体面不该差出几十倍。
options.t_en: I support a floor and a narrower gap. Dignity in old age should not differ by a factor of tens.

options.t: 我认为应以家庭赡养为主、公共资金只兜最底层，这样负担才可持续。
options.t_en: I think family support should be the mainstay and public money should cover only the very bottom. That is what makes the burden sustainable.

options.t: 我支持完全个人账户自主投资，盈亏自己承担，也别指望别人。
options.t_en: I support fully individual accounts with self-directed investment. You bear your own gains and losses, and expect nothing from anyone else.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The pension reform is stuck: pay out strictly in proportion to contributions, set a floor and compress the gap, or lean more on families and individual accounts.

scene: 一栋老商务楼没有无障碍通道，改造需要一笔不小的费用。业主说租户里没人需要，需要的人则说正因为进不去所以才没人来。

options.t: 我支持由公共财政统一出资改造，通行权不该由是否有人提出来决定。
options.t_en: I support public funds covering the retrofit. Whether people can get in should not depend on whether someone happens to have asked for it.

options.t: 我支持强制业主限期达标并自行承担费用，这本来就是建筑的基本条件。
options.t_en: I support obliging the owner to meet the standard by a deadline and pay for it. Step-free access is a basic condition of a building, not an optional upgrade.

options.t: 我支持由业主与使用者协商分担，公共资金补贴一部分。
options.t_en: I support the owner and the users agreeing how to split the cost, with public funds covering part of it.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: An old office building has no step-free access at all. Retrofitting a ramp or a lift would cost a substantial sum, and the owner says none of the current tenants need one, so there is no case for spending it. The answer comes back that nobody in a wheelchair has ever moved in precisely because the building cannot be entered, and that the absence of demand is being used as proof that demand does not exist.

scene: 关于成年子女对父母的赡养责任，有人主张写成明确的法定义务，有人认为这类事一旦变成义务就变了味。

options.t: 我支持写成明确义务，不然总有人心安理得地把父母甩给别人。
options.t_en: I support writing it in as an explicit obligation. Otherwise there will always be someone who comfortably dumps their parents on somebody else.

options.t: 我认为应完全出于自愿，被强制的照料对两边都是折磨。
options.t_en: I think it should be entirely voluntary. Care that is forced is misery for both sides.

options.t: 我认为应以公共养老体系为主、家庭为辅，别把全部重量压在子女身上。
options.t_en: I think a public elder-care system should carry the main weight, with the family as a supplement. Don't put the whole load on the children.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: There is a debate over whether adult children's duty to support their parents should be written into law as an explicit obligation. Some argue that leaving it vague means the burden falls unpredictably on whoever happens to live nearby or whoever feels guilty enough. Others say that once care becomes a legal duty it changes character, and that a relationship conducted under threat of enforcement is not the same thing as one conducted out of affection.

scene: 一对准备结婚的人在犹豫要不要签婚前财产约定。一方觉得先说清楚更踏实，另一方觉得还没开始就先算账。

options.t: 我会签，把话讲在前面反而让关系更稳定，不必靠猜。
options.t_en: I would sign it. Saying things out loud up front makes the relationship steadier, instead of relying on guesswork.

options.t: 我不会签，一上来就分你我，感情基础会被这份文件先削掉一层。
options.t_en: I would not sign it. Starting by dividing mine and yours takes a layer off the emotional foundation before you have begun.

options.t: 我会签，但只约定各自婚前的资产，婚后所得仍算共同的。
options.t_en: I would sign, but cover only what each of us brings in before marriage. What we earn afterwards stays joint.

options.t: 我认为登记机构应提供免费的标准模板，让普通人不必花大钱请人拟。
options.t_en: I think the registry should provide a free standard template so that ordinary people need not pay a fortune to have one drafted.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: A couple about to marry are hesitating over a prenuptial property agreement. One finds it reassuring to have things spelled out first; the other feels they are settling accounts before they have even begun.

scene: 一个双职工家庭在争论家务怎么分。一方收入明显更高、工作时间更长，主张按收入比例折算；另一方认为家务时间不能被收入买断。

options.t: 我主张按收入和工时比例折算，谁在外面扛得多，家里就该少担一点。
options.t_en: I argue for splitting it in proportion to income and hours. Whoever carries more outside the home should carry a little less inside it.

options.t: 我主张一律对半分，家务是共同生活的成本，不是能用钱抵掉的项目。
options.t_en: I argue for a straight fifty-fifty split. Housework is a cost of living together, not an item you can pay your way out of.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: A two-income household is arguing over how to divide the housework. One partner earns noticeably more and works longer hours, and argues that the split should follow that ratio, since the time bought in from outside is worth more. The other says housework is not something money can buy its way out of, and that an hour of washing up is an hour regardless of who earns the higher salary.

scene: 小区里流浪猫数量增加，有居民固定投喂，也有居民抱怨叫声和卫生。管理方要在几种方案中选一个。

options.t: 我支持绝育后放归，由志愿者管理固定投喂点，人和猫都能有个规矩。
options.t_en: I support trap-neuter-return, with volunteers running fixed feeding points. That way people and cats can both live by some rules.

options.t: 我支持全部送去收容并禁止街头投喂，社区不该变成半个动物园。
options.t_en: I support sending them all to a shelter and banning feeding on the street. A residential compound shouldn't turn into half a zoo.

options.t: 我认为想管的人自己领养回家就好，不该动用公共资源和公共空间。
options.t_en: I think anyone who wants to look after them should just adopt them and take them home. Public resources and public space shouldn't be spent on this.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The number of stray cats in the residential compound has grown. Some residents feed them at fixed times and places; others complain about the noise at night and the mess. Management has to pick one of several options, and whatever it picks will be resented by somebody. The cats, for their part, have already worked out which stairwells are warm in winter and which doorsteps get fed.

scene: 一家研究机构的部分项目仍依赖动物实验。替代技术已经出现但成本更高、成熟度不足，机构内部对是否设定退出时间表存在分歧。

options.t: 我支持设定时间表逐步退出，并把省下的争论精力投到替代技术上。
options.t_en: I support setting a timetable and phasing out, putting the energy saved from arguing into alternatives.

options.t: 我认为在确有必要时可以进行，但必须把使用量压到最低。
options.t_en: I think it can be done where genuinely necessary, but the volume must be pushed to the minimum.

options.t: 我支持由独立伦理委员会逐项审批，谁都不能自己给自己开绿灯。
options.t_en: I support case-by-case approval by an independent ethics committee. Nobody should be able to green-light their own work.

options.t: 我认为由资助方和研究者自律就够了，外部干预会拖慢一切。
options.t_en: I think self-regulation by funders and researchers is enough; outside interference just slows everything down.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: Some projects at a research institute still depend on animal testing. Alternatives exist but cost more and are not yet mature, and the institute is split over whether to set a timetable for phasing the practice out.

scene: 有人提议对肉类按生产环节的资源消耗征收附加税，收入用于补贴植物蛋白研发。反对者认为这是在用价格教育别人怎么吃饭。

options.t: 我支持征税，价格本来就应该反映真实的资源和环境成本。
options.t_en: I support the tax. A price should reflect the real resource and environmental cost behind it.

options.t: 我反对，吃什么是最基本的个人选择，不该被额外收费。
options.t_en: I oppose it. What you eat is among the most basic personal choices, and it should not carry an extra charge.

options.t: 我支持改成补贴替代蛋白让它自己变便宜，而不是把现有的东西弄贵。
options.t_en: I support subsidising alternative proteins so they become cheap on their own, instead of making what already exists more expensive.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: There is a proposal to put a surcharge on meat, scaled to the resources consumed in producing it, with the revenue going to subsidise research into plant protein. Supporters say the price of meat currently leaves out most of what producing it actually costs. Opponents say this amounts to using the price tag to teach people what they should be eating, and that the lesson will be paid for by whoever can least afford it.

scene: 广场上一件公共雕塑引发争议，一部分人觉得难看且冒犯，一部分人觉得它恰恰提出了值得讨论的问题。管理方收到了拆除申请。

options.t: 我支持保留并加一块说明牌，让争论本身成为公共教育的一部分。
options.t_en: I support keeping it and adding an explanatory plaque, so that the argument itself becomes part of the public education.

options.t: 我支持移走，公共空间首先应该让大多数人待着舒服。
options.t_en: I support removing it. Public space should first of all be comfortable for most people to be in.

options.t: 我支持由周边居民投票决定去留，谁天天看见谁说了算。
options.t_en: I support letting the surrounding residents vote on whether it stays. Whoever has to look at it every day should decide.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A public sculpture in the square has become controversial. Some people find it ugly and offensive; others think it raises exactly the kind of question worth arguing about. The management has received a request to remove it. Petitions have been circulating in both directions, and the square is where most of the people who signed them walk every day.

scene: 公共文化基金总额有限，申请者包括几乎没有观众的实验剧团、快要失传的手工技艺班，以及一个已经能卖票盈利的音乐节。

options.t: 我支持优先资助没有观众的实验剧团，市场养不活的未必没有价值。
options.t_en: I support funding the audience-less experimental theatre first. What the market cannot sustain is not necessarily worthless.

options.t: 我认为都不该资助，观众用票投票就是最诚实的评价。
options.t_en: I think none of them should be funded. Audiences voting with tickets are the most honest assessment.

options.t: 我支持把资助名单交给公众投票产生，花的是大家的钱。
options.t_en: I support letting the public vote on the shortlist. It is everyone's money being spent.

options.t: 我支持优先资助濒临失传的传统技艺，断了就真的接不上了。
options.t_en: I support prioritising the craft that is on the verge of being lost. Once it breaks, it truly cannot be reconnected.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: The public culture fund is limited, and the applicants include an experimental theatre troupe with almost no audience, a workshop teaching a craft that is nearly lost, and a music festival that already sells tickets at a profit.

scene: 一座老建筑修好后如何使用引起讨论：改成商铺和咖啡馆能自负盈亏，做成免费展馆则需要长期贴钱维护。

options.t: 我支持部分商业化经营，有稳定收入建筑才能被长期养下去。
options.t_en: I support partial commercial operation. Only with a steady income can the building be looked after over the long term.

options.t: 我支持做免费公共展馆，它的意义就在于所有人都能进去。
options.t_en: I support making it a free public exhibition hall. Its whole point is that anybody can walk in.

options.t: 我支持一楼商业、其余楼层公共开放，用赚的钱养不赚钱的部分。
options.t_en: I support shops on the ground floor and the other floors open to the public, with the profit from one paying for the part that earns nothing.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A restored old building has set off a debate about what it should now be used for. Turned into shops and a cafe, it could cover its own running costs. Run as a free exhibition hall, it would need money poured in year after year, with nothing coming back. Nobody in the room is against the building being used well; the argument is over whether it has to earn its keep.

scene: 少年组联赛要不要公布排名和个人数据引起争论。教练认为排名能激发训练动力，一些家长认为这会让水平一般的孩子早早退出。

options.t: 我支持公布排名，竞争和面对落后本身就是训练的一部分。
options.t_en: I support publishing the rankings. Competition, and facing the fact that you are behind, is part of training.

options.t: 我支持淡化排名，这个年龄先让人喜欢上运动比分出高低重要。
options.t_en: I support playing the rankings down. At this age, getting kids to enjoy the sport matters more than sorting them into levels.

options.t: 我支持同时设竞技组和兴趣组，让孩子自己选进哪一边。
options.t_en: I support setting up a competitive group and a recreational group at the same time, and letting the kids choose which side to join.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: There is an argument over whether a youth league should publish rankings and individual statistics. Coaches say rankings motivate training. Some parents say they will push kids who are only average to quit early. Nobody disagrees that the league needs some way of recording results; the question is how much of it becomes public, and in what form.

scene: 俱乐部要求所有队员佩戴设备，全天采集心率、睡眠和恢复数据用于训练安排。数据存在俱乐部服务器，转会时归属不明。

options.t: 我支持全面采集，科学安排负荷能实实在在减少伤病。
options.t_en: I support full collection. Scientific load management genuinely reduces injuries.

options.t: 我反对，身体数据一旦掌握在俱乐部手里，续约谈判就不对等了。
options.t_en: I oppose it. Once the club holds your body data, contract negotiations are no longer between equals.

options.t: 我支持采集，但数据所有权必须归运动员本人，走的时候能带走。
options.t_en: I support collection, but ownership must stay with the athlete, who can take the data along when leaving.

options.t: 我支持由队医统一保管并对俱乐部管理层保密，只输出训练建议。
options.t_en: I support the team doctor holding the data confidentially, kept from club management, releasing only training advice.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: The club requires every player to wear a device that logs heart rate, sleep and recovery around the clock for planning training. The data sits on club servers, and who owns it if a player transfers is unclear.

scene: 公园里几片球场长期被固定的几伙人占用，新来的人排不上。管理方在考虑收费预约、继续免费还是交给使用者自治。

options.t: 我支持继续免费开放，运动场地是公共品，一收费就把一部分人挡在外面。
options.t_en: I support keeping it free. Sports facilities are a public good, and the moment you charge, a section of the public is shut out.

options.t: 我支持低价收费预约，有价格才有秩序，也能覆盖维护成本。
options.t_en: I support low-cost booking. A price is what creates order, and it also covers the cost of upkeep.

options.t: 我支持成立使用者自治小组排班并自筹维护费，用的人自己管。
options.t_en: I support setting up a users' committee to draw up the rota and raise the maintenance money itself. The people who use it should run it.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Several courts in the park have long been taken over by the same groups of regulars, and newcomers never get a turn. The management is weighing three options: charging for bookings, keeping it free, or handing it over to the users to govern themselves. Everyone agrees the courts are heavily used; what they disagree about is who gets to decide, and what a fair share of a scarce facility actually looks like.

scene: 养老金支付压力上升，有人提议整体推迟领取年龄。办公室岗位的人多数表示可以接受，体力岗位的人普遍反对。

options.t: 我支持弹性退休，愿意继续干的人多干几年多拿，不愿意的照旧。
options.t_en: I support flexible retirement. People who want to keep working can work a few more years and draw more; those who don't stay on the old terms.

options.t: 我反对整体推迟，很多体力岗位的人根本撑不到那个年纪。
options.t_en: I oppose raising it across the board. A lot of people in physical jobs simply cannot last to that age.

options.t: 我支持按工种和劳动强度差异化设定，不该用一个数字盖住所有人。
options.t_en: I support setting it differently by type of work and how physically demanding it is. One number should not cover everybody.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: Pressure on pension payments is rising, and someone has proposed raising the claiming age across the board. Most people in office jobs say they could accept it. People in physically demanding jobs are broadly opposed: many say their bodies will not last that long. The proposal's authors say the alternative is a cut in benefits for everyone, and that doing nothing simply shifts the cost onto the next generation.

scene: 医院挂号、缴费和取药全面转为线上后，不少老年人卡在第一步。有人说这是时代必然，有人说这是把人排除在外。

options.t: 我支持强制所有公共服务保留人工窗口，不会用不该等于办不了。
options.t_en: I support requiring every public service to keep a staffed counter. Not knowing how to use an app should not mean being unable to get anything done.

options.t: 我认为子女或邻居帮一把就够了，这本来就是家里人的事。
options.t_en: I think help from children or neighbours is enough. This is what families are for.

options.t: 我支持大力办培训班教会他们用，长期看学会了才最自由。
options.t_en: I support running classes to teach them, because in the long run knowing how is the real freedom.

options.t: 我支持由社区设代办点统一帮办，把这件事变成公共服务的一部分。
options.t_en: I support setting up community counters that handle it for them, making this part of the public service.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Since registration, payment and prescription pickup at the hospital all moved online, plenty of older people get stuck at the very first step. Some say this is simply where the times are heading; others say it shuts people out.

scene: 一家养老机构提议在所有房间安装摄像头，家属可远程查看。机构说这能防止照护不当，部分老人表示不愿意住在镜头下。

options.t: 我支持全覆盖，说不出话的老人只能靠镜头替他们作证。
options.t_en: I support full coverage. Old people who cannot speak up have only the camera to testify for them.

options.t: 我反对装进房间，年纪大了也仍然有不想被看见的时刻。
options.t_en: I oppose cameras in the rooms. However old you are, there are still moments you do not want to be seen.

options.t: 我支持只装在走廊等公共区域，并由家属委员会共同掌握查看权限。
options.t_en: I support cameras only in corridors and other shared areas, with viewing rights held jointly by a families' committee.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: A care home has proposed installing cameras in every room, with families able to watch remotely. The home says this prevents poor care and gives relatives peace of mind; some residents say plainly that they do not want to live under a lens, and that being old does not mean giving up the wish not to be seen. The question on the table is where safety stops being a reason and starts being an intrusion.

scene: 多个平台向刚工作或还在读书的年轻人推送免息分期，界面只显示每期还多少，年化利率藏在多层页面之后。

options.t: 我认为借不借是个人选择，签了字就要自己承担后果。
options.t_en: I think whether to borrow is a personal choice. If you signed, you carry the consequences yourself.

options.t: 我支持直接禁止向在校学生放贷，这个阶段的判断力和还款能力都撑不住。
options.t_en: I support simply banning lending to students. At that stage neither the judgment nor the repayment capacity is there.

options.t: 我支持强制在首页用同样大的字显示年化利率和总还款额，让人看清再选。
options.t_en: I support requiring the annualized rate and the total repayment amount to appear on the front page in the same size type, so people can see clearly before choosing.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Several platforms push interest-free installment plans at young people who have just started work or are still studying. The interface shows only how much each installment costs; the annualized interest rate sits behind several layers of pages. The plans are advertised as free. Some of the young people using them say they did not realize there was a rate at all until they missed a payment.

scene: 一个人因意外失业无力偿还债务，利息仍在累积，催收电话打到了亲友那里。关于这类情形该怎么处理，出现几种主张。

options.t: 我支持建立个人破产机制，让人在付出代价后能重新开始。
options.t_en: I support a personal bankruptcy mechanism so that after paying a price people can start again.

options.t: 我认为欠债还钱天经地义，轻易免除会让守信的人吃亏。
options.t_en: I think debts must be repaid; that is the natural order. Writing them off easily punishes those who kept their word.

options.t: 我支持由中立机构主持债权人与债务人调解，重新排一份能还得起的分期表。
options.t_en: I support mediation between creditor and debtor led by a neutral body, redrawing an instalment plan the debtor can actually pay.

options.t: 我支持设立公共救助基金为这类突发失业兜底，避免一个人彻底沉下去。
options.t_en: I support a public assistance fund to catch people in this kind of sudden unemployment, so that no one sinks completely.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: Someone lost his job by accident, cannot repay his debts, the interest keeps accruing, and collection calls have started reaching his relatives and friends. Several positions have emerged on how such cases should be handled.

scene: 一家商业机构把用户的消费频次、退货率和缴费记录合成一个分数，分数高的人能拿到更低的贷款利率。

options.t: 我反对，日常消费不该被换算成一个决定我能借多少钱的分数。
options.t_en: I oppose it. Everyday shopping should not be converted into a number that decides how much I can borrow.

options.t: 我接受，行为一贯可靠的人享受更低利率，这是很直接的公平。
options.t_en: I accept it. People whose behaviour is consistently reliable getting a lower rate is a very direct kind of fairness.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: A commercial company combines a user's purchase frequency, return rate and payment record into a single score, and people with high scores are offered lower interest rates on loans. The company calls it behavioural credit. Some customers find it a fair reward for being reliable; others point out that how often you shop is not the same thing as whether you can repay, and that the score is invisible and impossible to appeal.

scene: 一片风力发电场计划建在社区北侧的山脊上。它能让本地电价下降，但会改变天际线，最近的住户距离约一公里。

options.t: 我支持建，想要清洁能源就得有人承担看得见的代价，不能只让别处扛。
options.t_en: I support building it. If we want clean energy, someone has to carry the visible cost; it can't always be dumped on somewhere else.

options.t: 我反对建在这里，同样的项目完全可以放到没人住的地方去。
options.t_en: I oppose building it here. The same project could easily go somewhere nobody lives.

options.t: 我支持建，条件是本地居民长期享受电费折扣和项目分红。
options.t_en: I support building it, on condition that local residents get a long-term discount on their electricity and a share of the project's revenue.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A wind farm is planned for the ridge north of the community. It would bring local electricity prices down, but it would change the skyline, and the nearest homes are about a kilometer away. Supporters point out that the power has to be generated somewhere. Opponents ask why it always seems to be somewhere like this, and the homeowners closest to the ridge have started asking what happens to their property values.

scene: 关于电网该由谁经营出现分歧：公有统一定价、引入多家公司竞争、由社区自建微电网，或者骨干公有加零售市场化。

options.t: 我支持公有并设保底价，电是生活必需品，不该随行情大起大落。
options.t_en: I support public ownership with a guaranteed price. Electricity is a necessity and should not swing wildly with the market.

options.t: 我支持引入竞争，多家公司抢用户，价格和服务才会往上走。
options.t_en: I support introducing competition. When several companies compete for customers, prices and service improve.

options.t: 我支持社区自建微电网自发自用，能源尽量掌握在用电的人手里。
options.t_en: I support community microgrids generating for their own use, keeping energy as far as possible with the people who use it.

options.t: 我支持骨干网公有、零售端放开，两头的好处各取一点。
options.t_en: I support a public backbone with retail opened up, taking some of the benefit from each end.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: There is disagreement over who should run the grid: public ownership with uniform pricing, competition among several companies, community-built microgrids, or a public backbone with a market for retail supply.

scene: 一条跨区域输电线路要穿过若干村庄的农田，沿线农户将获得一次性补偿，但耕作会被永久分割。

options.t: 我支持修建，只要补偿到位，整体的用电稳定比局部不便更重要。
options.t_en: I support building it. As long as the compensation is adequate, stable power for the whole system matters more than local inconvenience.

options.t: 我反对，应该优先发展本地分布式发电，少建这种跨区域的大工程。
options.t_en: I oppose it. Local distributed generation should be developed first, and fewer of these large cross-region projects built.

options.t: 我支持由沿线各村集体共同协商路线走向和补偿方案，方案由他们签字才生效。
options.t_en: I support the villages along the route negotiating the alignment and the compensation together, with the plan taking effect only once they have signed it.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A cross-region transmission line is to cut through farmland in a number of villages. Farmers along the route will receive a one-off payment, but their fields will be permanently divided by the towers and the access roads. The grid company says the line is needed to move power where it is used; the villages point out that the payment is spent once, while the split in the fields lasts for as long as they farm.

scene: 某片低洼区历史上多次进水。有人主张禁止在此新建住宅并逐步搬迁，有人认为世代住在这里的人不该被赶走。

options.t: 我支持禁止新建并有计划搬迁，一次次重建的钱最后还是大家出。
options.t_en: I support banning new construction and planning a relocation. The money for rebuilding over and over ends up coming from everyone anyway.

options.t: 我支持允许继续住和新建，但风险和保费完全自己承担。
options.t_en: I support allowing people to keep living there and to keep building, but with the risk and the insurance premiums entirely on them.

options.t: 我支持用公共资金修好防洪工程，让人能留在自己长大的地方。
options.t_en: I support using public money to finish the flood defenses properly, so people can stay where they grew up.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: A low-lying district has flooded repeatedly over the years. Some people want to ban new housing there and gradually relocate the residents. Others say the people who have lived there for generations should not be pushed out. The district contains a mix of old family homes and newer buildings put up after the last flood, and the insurance companies have already started quietly withdrawing from the area.

scene: 一场风灾之后，重建资金远不够所有需求。是先修学校医院道路，还是先补偿损失最重的家庭，还是交给保险和外部援助，各方争执不下。

options.t: 我支持先重建学校、医院和道路，公共设施恢复了个体才恢复得起来。
options.t_en: I support rebuilding schools, hospitals and roads first. Once public facilities are back, individuals can recover.

options.t: 我支持先足额补偿损失最重的家庭，最惨的人等不起排队。
options.t_en: I support compensating the worst-hit households in full first. The people in the worst state cannot wait in a queue.

options.t: 我认为应主要靠保险赔付，公共资金只处理极端个案。
options.t_en: I think it should rest mainly on insurance payouts, with public money handling only extreme cases.

options.t: 我支持由外部援助机构统一调配资源，本地此时最缺的是组织能力。
options.t_en: I support outside aid agencies coordinating the resources. What is scarcest locally right now is organisational capacity.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: After a windstorm, the reconstruction money falls far short of what is needed. Whether to rebuild schools, hospitals and roads first, to compensate the worst-hit households first, or to leave it to insurers and outside aid, the sides cannot agree.

scene: 极端天气预警发布后，是否强制关闭道路和暂停营业存在分歧。强制会造成经济损失，不强制则可能有人低估风险。

options.t: 我支持在高等级预警下强制停运停业，风险时刻不适合各自判断。
options.t_en: I support mandatory shutdowns of transport and business under a high-level warning. A moment of risk is no time for everyone to judge for themselves.

options.t: 我支持只发预警不作强制，把信息给足，出不出门自己决定自己负责。
options.t_en: I support issuing the warning without compulsion. Give people the full information; whether to go out is their decision and their responsibility.

options.t: 我支持按预警等级分级，用统一系统自动触发不同程度的限制。
options.t_en: I support graduating the response by warning level, with a single system automatically triggering different degrees of restriction.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Once an extreme weather warning is issued, there is disagreement over whether roads should be closed and businesses forced to shut. Compulsion costs money and stops people earning; without it, some will underestimate the risk and go out anyway. The authorities have to decide how much judgement to leave with individuals when the forecast is at its worst, and who answers for the consequences if that judgement is wrong.

scene: 一款内容应用的推荐算法让用户平均使用时长翻倍，也让不少人觉得自己刷得停不下来。平台内部在讨论要不要提供关闭个性化推荐的开关。

options.t: 我支持提供一键关闭的开关，并且默认位置要显眼。
options.t_en: I support offering a one-tap switch, and by default it should sit somewhere obvious.

options.t: 我支持由监管机构对推荐算法进行审核和备案。
options.t_en: I support having the regulator review and register recommendation algorithms.

options.t: 我认为维持现状就好，觉得刷太多的人可以自己少打开。
options.t_en: I think it is fine to leave things as they are. People who feel they scroll too much can just open it less.

options.t: 我支持开放参数让用户自己调，比如多推多久以前的内容、少推什么话题。
options.t_en: I support exposing the parameters so users can tune them, for example how much older content to show and which topics to show less of.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: A content app's recommendation algorithm has doubled average time spent in the app, and plenty of users say they cannot stop scrolling. Inside the platform there is a debate over whether to offer a switch that turns off personalized recommendations. The growth team says the switch would cost engagement. The trust team says the absence of one will eventually show up in a regulator's report.

scene: 一个用户量很大的平台上出现了侵害他人权益的内容。平台称自己只是管道，受害者认为平台从流量里赚了钱就该负责。

options.t: 我认为平台应主动审核并承担连带责任，赚了流量的钱就得管事。
options.t_en: I think the platform should actively review content and bear joint liability. If it takes money from the traffic, it should manage what flows.

options.t: 我认为平台只是管道，责任应完全落在发布内容的人身上。
options.t_en: I think the platform is only a conduit and responsibility rests entirely with whoever posted the content.

options.t: 我认为应交由用户社区自治，由志愿版主按公约处理。
options.t_en: I think it should be left to the user community, with volunteer moderators handling it under a code of conduct.

options.t: 我认为应设立独立申诉机构，复核平台的删除与封禁决定。
options.t_en: I think there should be an independent appeals body reviewing the platform's takedowns and bans.

options.t: 我认为应按平台规模分级要求，小平台从宽、超大平台从严。
options.t_en: I think requirements should scale with platform size: lenient for small ones, strict for the very large.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Content that harms people's rights has appeared on a platform with a huge user base. The platform says it is only a conduit; the victims say a platform that earns money from the traffic should be answerable for it.

scene: 用户想把自己多年积累的评价、收藏和作品从一个平台迁到另一个平台，平台以数据由其加工生成为由拒绝导出。

options.t: 我支持强制平台提供一键导出和迁移，不然所谓选择自由只是空话。
options.t_en: I support requiring platforms to provide one-click export and migration. Otherwise the freedom to choose is just a phrase.

options.t: 我认为这些数据是平台投入加工出来的资产，不该被无偿搬走。
options.t_en: I think this data is an asset the platform has invested in producing, and should not be carried off for free.

options.t: 我支持用户联合成立数据信托，由信托代表大家和平台谈条件。
options.t_en: I support users forming a data trust together, with the trust negotiating terms with platforms on everyone's behalf.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A user wants to move years of accumulated reviews, saved items and work from one platform to another. The platform refuses to allow export, on the grounds that the data was generated by its own processing and belongs to it. The user says the reviews were written by them and the collection was built by their own choices. Behind the technical question of export formats is a question about who a person's own history on a platform actually belongs to.

scene: 关于网络账号是否必须绑定真实身份，讨论区吵了很久。有人举出恶意骚扰的例子，也有人举出因匿名才敢发声的例子。

options.t: 我支持全面实名，能对上人，很多恶意行为自然会收敛。
options.t_en: I support full real-name registration. When you can be matched to a person, a lot of malicious behavior naturally quiets down.

options.t: 我反对实名，匿名保护的往往是最没有资源承受报复的人。
options.t_en: I oppose real-name registration. Anonymity usually protects the people with the fewest resources to absorb retaliation.

options.t: 我支持后台实名、前台匿名，日常不暴露但出事能追溯。
options.t_en: I support real identity behind the scenes and anonymity in public: not exposed day to day, but traceable when something happens.

options.t: 我认为该由各平台自己定规则，用户用脚投票就好。
options.t_en: I think each platform should set its own rules, and users can vote with their feet.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Whether online accounts must be tied to a real identity has been argued over in the forums for a long time. One side cites cases of malicious harassment. The other cites cases of people who only dared to speak because they were anonymous. Both sides have examples that are hard to dismiss, and the argument tends to stall exactly at the point where the examples start.

scene: 一场社区文化节的节目单基本由人数最多的几个团体占满。几个成员很少的小团体提出希望也有展示时段，组织者担心时间不够。

options.t: 我支持主动给小团体预留固定时段，不留就永远轮不到他们。
options.t_en: I support reserving fixed slots for the small groups. Without a reservation they will never get their turn.

options.t: 我认为应一视同仁按报名先后排，不做任何特别安排。
options.t_en: I think everyone should be treated alike, in order of registration, with no special arrangements.

options.t: 我支持用公共文化基金支持他们自己另办一场，规模小但完全由他们做主。
options.t_en: I support using the public culture fund to help them put on their own separate event, smaller but entirely their own.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The programme of a community culture festival is almost entirely taken up by the largest groups. A few groups with only a handful of members have asked for a slot of their own, and the organisers worry there is not enough time.

scene: 为极少数使用者提供的特殊服务，比如手语翻译或特定格式的资料，单次成本很高。预算会议上有人质疑投入产出比。

options.t: 我认为应无条件提供，权利不能按受益人数打折。
options.t_en: I think it should be provided unconditionally. A right cannot be discounted according to how few people benefit from it.

options.t: 我认为应按成本效益排序，有限的钱要先花在覆盖面最广的地方。
options.t_en: I think it should be ranked by cost-effectiveness. Money that is limited has to go first to where it reaches the most people.

options.t: 我支持由该群体自己的组织与公共部门合办，他们最清楚怎么做才有用。
options.t_en: I support the group's own organisations running it jointly with the public authorities. They are the ones who know best what actually works.

options.t: 我支持用自动转写和语音识别等技术把成本压下来，再谈覆盖范围。
options.t_en: I support using automatic transcription, speech recognition and similar technology to bring the cost down first, and then talking about how far coverage can go.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: Some services exist for a very small number of users: sign language interpretation, or documents produced in a specific accessible format. Each time one of them is used, the cost per person reached is high. At the budget meeting someone asks whether the money would do more good elsewhere, and points to the ratio between what is spent and how many people benefit. Nobody in the room disputes the numbers; what they dispute is whether numbers of that kind are the right test here.

scene: 社区活动室只有一间。一个只有七八人的小众爱好团体申请每周固定使用一个晚上，其他居民认为按人数算太浪费，应该让给广场舞队或读书会。

options.t: 我支持按申请先后和实际到场率轮换，谁真的在用谁继续用。
options.t_en: I support rotating by order of application and actual attendance. Whoever is really using it keeps using it.

options.t: 我支持优先满足人数多的团体，公共资源本来就该按人头算。
options.t_en: I support giving priority to the larger groups. Public resources should be allocated per head.

options.t: 我支持按小时收取象征性费用，愿意付钱的自然是真需要。
options.t_en: I support charging a token hourly fee. Whoever is willing to pay is presumably the one who really needs it.

options.t: 我支持给小众团体保留固定时段，事事按多数决，小群体会被慢慢挤没。
options.t_en: I support reserving a fixed slot for small groups. Decide everything by majority and small groups slowly get squeezed out.

options.t: 我支持把方案交给全体居民投票，规则由用它的人一起定。
options.t_en: I support putting the decision to a vote of all residents, so the rules are set by the people who use it.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: The community has only one activity room. A small hobby group of seven or eight people has applied to use it for one fixed evening a week. Other residents think that is a waste given the group's size, and that the time should go to the square dance team or the book club. The room is booked through a paper form by the door, which is part of why the same groups keep getting it.

scene: 你所在的城市有一家百年历史的传统纺织厂，雇佣了约2000名本地工人，但近年因无法与低成本进口产品竞争而濒临倒闭。市政府正在讨论是否对进口纺织品加征高额关税以保护本土产业，但经济学家警告这会导致消费品价格上涨，并可能引发贸易伙伴的报复性关税。你作为市民代表参与了这场公开听证会。

options.t: 我会支持加征关税，优先保护本地工人的就业和家庭的生计，产业安全比短期物价波动更重要。
options.t_en: I would support the tariff, putting local workers' jobs and families' livelihoods first. Industrial security matters more than short-term price swings.

options.t: 我会反对关税壁垒，支持开放竞争，让消费者享受更低价格，同时相信市场会引导工人向更有竞争力的行业转型。
options.t_en: I would oppose tariff barriers and support open competition, letting consumers enjoy lower prices and trusting the market to guide workers into more competitive industries.

options.t: 我会建议用税收补贴帮助企业技术升级，而非直接限制贸易，既保护产业又避免贸易战。
options.t_en: I would propose tax-funded subsidies to help the company upgrade its technology rather than restricting trade outright, protecting the industry while avoiding a trade war.

options.t: 我会主张什么都不做，让市场竞争自然淘汰低效企业，这是经济进化的必然过程。
options.t_en: I would argue for doing nothing and letting competition naturally eliminate inefficient firms. That is the inevitable process of economic evolution.

options.t: 我会提议与贸易伙伴谈判建立公平贸易协定，要求对方提高劳工标准，而非单方面征收关税。
options.t_en: I would propose negotiating a fair trade agreement with trading partners that requires them to raise labour standards, rather than imposing tariffs unilaterally.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Your city has a century-old traditional textile mill employing about two thousand local workers, and it is close to collapse because it cannot compete with low-cost imports. The municipal government is debating whether to impose a high tariff on imported textiles to protect local industry, while economists warn that consumer prices would rise and trading partners might retaliate. You are a citizen representative at the public hearing.

scene: 你居住的城市近五年接纳了大量来自不同文化背景的移民。市政府计划在市中心建立一座多元文化博物馆，展示各族裔的历史与贡献，但一部分长期居民认为公共资源应首先服务于本土文化，担心这会稀释城市的传统身份认同。社区论坛上双方争论激烈，主持人邀请你发言。

options.t: 我会全力支持博物馆项目，文化多样性是城市的财富，了解不同背景能促进社会包容与和谐。
options.t_en: I will back the museum wholeheartedly. Cultural diversity is a city's wealth, and understanding different backgrounds is what builds tolerance and social harmony.

options.t: 我会反对这个项目，认为城市应该先修缮本土历史博物馆，移民应主动融入而非被特别展示。
options.t_en: I will oppose the project. The city should restore its own history museum first; immigrants should take the initiative to fit in, not be put on special display.

options.t: 我会建议博物馆采用对比叙事，同时展示本土文化与移民文化的互动历程，强调共同而非差异。
options.t_en: I will propose that the museum tell the story through contrast, showing how the native culture and immigrant cultures have shaped each other, stressing what is shared rather than what is different.

options.t: 我会主张把资金用于语言融合课程和职业培训，让移民真正融入社会，而不是建象征性建筑。
options.t_en: I will argue that the money should go to language integration courses and vocational training so that immigrants actually settle into society, rather than to a symbolic building.

options.t: 我认为这应由民间筹款而非政府出资，文化表达不应占用纳税人资金。
options.t_en: I think this should be funded by private donation rather than by government. Cultural expression should not be paid for out of taxpayers' money.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: Over the past five years your city has taken in a large number of immigrants from very different cultural backgrounds. The city government plans to build a museum of cultural diversity in the centre of town, presenting the history and the contribution of each community. Some long-standing residents think public money should serve the native culture first, and worry that the museum will dilute the city's traditional identity. At a packed community forum the two sides are going at each other, and the chair invites you to speak.

scene: 你任职的科技公司正在推行一项高级管理岗位性别配额计划，要求未来三年内女性高管比例达到40%。公司目前有15%的女性高管，许多男性员工认为这可能导致能力被忽视，而女性员工则认为这是打破玻璃天花板的必要手段。人力资源部向你这位资深员工征求意见。

options.t: 我会支持配额计划，历史上系统性歧视需要强制性矫正措施，没有外部压力改变不会自然发生。
options.t_en: I would support the quota. Historical systemic discrimination needs mandatory corrective measures. Without outside pressure, nothing changes on its own.

options.t: 我会反对硬性配额，认为应该只根据能力和业绩提拔，任何身份标准都是对优秀者的不公。
options.t_en: I would oppose a hard quota. Promotion should be based on ability and results alone. Any identity criterion is unfair to the people who are excellent.

options.t: 我会建议改为设定透明的晋升标准和匿名评估机制，消除隐性偏见，而非直接设定性别比例。
options.t_en: I would suggest transparent promotion criteria and anonymous evaluation instead, to remove implicit bias rather than directly setting a gender ratio.

options.t: 我会提议从基层培养做起，增加女性技术岗位的比例，而非只在高管层做表面文章。
options.t_en: I would propose starting from the ground up, increasing the share of women in technical roles, rather than doing cosmetic work only at the executive level.

options.t: 我认为公司应该公开所有岗位的薪酬和晋升数据，让市场和社会监督来自然推动公平。
options.t_en: I think the company should publish pay and promotion data for every role, and let market and public scrutiny push fairness along naturally.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The tech company you work for is rolling out a gender quota for senior management, requiring women to make up 40 percent of executives within three years. Women currently hold 15 percent of those roles. Many male employees say ability will end up being overlooked; many women say this is the necessary way to break the glass ceiling. HR has asked you, as a senior employee, for your view.

scene: 你所在地区正在改革刑事审判制度，讨论是否引入公民陪审团参与重大刑事案件的裁决。支持者认为陪审团能带入社会常识和道德感，防止司法精英主义；反对者则担心普通民众缺乏法律知识，容易受情绪和舆论影响，导致裁决不稳定。你是法律委员会的成员。

options.t: 我会坚决支持引入陪审团，司法不能脱离社会良知，普通人集体判断比个别法官更不容易被权力腐蚀。
options.t_en: I would firmly support juries. Justice cannot be cut off from the community's conscience, and the collective judgment of ordinary people is harder to corrupt than that of an individual judge.

options.t: 我会反对陪审团制度，审判是专业领域，应该由训练有素的法官依据法律条文作出理性裁决。
options.t_en: I would oppose juries. A trial is a professional field, and verdicts should be reached rationally by trained judges applying the letter of the law.

options.t: 我会建议采用混合模式，由专业法官和陪审员共同评议，既保留专业性又纳入公众视角。
options.t_en: I would propose a mixed model in which professional judges and jurors deliberate together, keeping expertise while bringing in the public perspective.

options.t: 我认为陪审员应经过基本法律培训并签署责任书，而非随机抽取，以提高裁决质量。
options.t_en: I think jurors should receive basic legal training and sign a statement of responsibility rather than being picked at random, to raise the quality of verdicts.

options.t: 我会主张陪审团只参与事实认定，法律适用仍由法官负责，各司其职以减少错误。
options.t_en: I would argue that juries decide only the facts, while the application of law stays with the judge, each doing their part to reduce error.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: Your region is reforming its criminal trial system and debating whether to bring citizen juries into serious criminal cases. Supporters say juries carry the community's moral sense into the courtroom and guard against judicial elitism; opponents worry that laypeople lack legal knowledge, are easily swayed by emotion and publicity, and produce unpredictable verdicts. You sit on the law reform committee.

scene: 你孩子就读的公立学校正在修订德育课程大纲，有家长团体建议在课程中增加世界主要宗教的伦理教义内容，认为这有助于道德教育；但另一些家长强烈反对，认为公立学校应保持彻底世俗，任何宗教内容都不应进入课堂。学校家委会邀请你参与表决。

options.t: 我会支持纳入宗教伦理内容，宗教是文明的核心组成部分，学生应当了解这些思想遗产。
options.t_en: I will support including religious ethics. Religion is a central part of civilisation, and students should know about this intellectual inheritance.

options.t: 我会坚决反对，公立学校必须保持世俗中立，宗教教育应在家庭和宗教场所进行，不应占用公共教育资源。
options.t_en: I will firmly oppose it. A public school has to stay secular and neutral; religious education belongs in the home and in places of worship, not in public classrooms.

options.t: 我会建议只讲授宗教作为历史和文化现象，而非伦理教义，保持学术距离和客观性。
options.t_en: I will propose teaching religion only as a historical and cultural phenomenon rather than as ethical doctrine, keeping an academic distance and staying objective.

options.t: 我认为应该让学生选择是否参加这类课程，由家长签字同意，尊重不同家庭的信仰自由。
options.t_en: I think students should choose whether to attend such classes, with parents signing consent, so that each family's freedom of belief is respected.

options.t: 我会提议用哲学伦理课程替代宗教内容，用理性讨论代替传统教义，培养批判性思维。
options.t_en: I will propose replacing religious content with a course in philosophical ethics, substituting reasoned discussion for traditional doctrine and training critical thinking.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The public school your child attends is revising its ethics curriculum. One group of parents has proposed adding the ethical teachings of the world's major religions, arguing that this would strengthen moral education and give children a sense of the traditions that shaped their civilisation. Another group of parents objects strongly: a public school must stay strictly secular, and no religious content belongs in a classroom at all. The parent council has asked you to vote.

scene: 你居住的老城区有一片建于上世纪五十年代的低矮居民区，建筑老化但社区氛围浓厚，许多三代同堂的家庭在此生活。城市规划局提出整体拆迁方案，将在此建设高密度商业综合体和现代住宅，声称能提升城市形象和土地效率。原居民将被安置到远郊的新建小区。社区召开居民大会，你被推选为居民代表。

options.t: 我会反对拆迁，社区的社会纽带和集体记忆无法用金钱衡量，城市不应该只为效率牺牲人的生活。
options.t_en: I would oppose the demolition. The social ties and collective memory of a community cannot be measured in money, and a city shouldn't sacrifice people's lives just for efficiency.

options.t: 我会支持改造，老旧建筑存在安全隐患，城市更新能带来更好的基础设施和经济发展机会。
options.t_en: I would support redevelopment. Old buildings carry real safety risks, and urban renewal can bring better infrastructure and economic opportunities.

options.t: 我会要求在原址进行微改造而非整体拆除，保留建筑外观和街巷格局，同时改善内部设施。
options.t_en: I would demand micro-renovation in place instead of wholesale demolition: keep the building facades and the street layout, while improving the interiors.

options.t: 我认为补偿标准必须包括未来房价差异和搬迁成本，不能让居民为城市升级承担代价。
options.t_en: I think the compensation standard must cover the future difference in property values and the cost of moving. Residents shouldn't bear the price of the city's upgrade.

options.t: 我会提议引入社区规划师和居民共同设计更新方案，让受影响的居民参与决策而非被动接受。
options.t_en: I would propose bringing in community planners to design the renewal together with residents, so the people affected take part in the decision instead of just accepting it.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: In the old part of the city where you live there is a low-rise neighborhood built in the 1950s. The buildings are aging but the community is close, and many families have three generations living there. The planning bureau has proposed demolishing the whole area for a high-density commercial complex and modern housing, arguing it would improve the city's image and land efficiency. The original residents would be relocated to new developments on the far outskirts. A residents' meeting has been called, and you have been chosen to represent them.

scene: 你所在地区是传统的农业区，近年来大型农业企业推广转基因作物和集约化养殖，产量大幅提升但引发了关于食品质量和环境影响的争议。一群本地小农发起了"食用传统"运动，倡导有机耕作和本地直销，但产品价格比工业化食品高出30%以上。你被邀请在一场食品政策论坛上表态。

options.t: 我会支持小农有机运动，食品不仅是营养，还关乎文化和环境，我们应该为质量而非产量付费。
options.t_en: I would support the smallholders' organic movement. Food is not only nutrition; it is also culture and environment, and we should pay for quality rather than quantity.

options.t: 我会支持工业化农业，技术进步和规模经济是喂饱不断增长人口的唯一现实途径，不能浪漫化传统。
options.t_en: I would support industrial agriculture. Technological progress and economies of scale are the only realistic way to feed a growing population; tradition should not be romanticised.

options.t: 我会主张强制转基因食品标注，让消费者自主选择，市场应该提供信息透明而非替人决定。
options.t_en: I would argue for mandatory labelling of GM food so that consumers can choose for themselves. The market should provide transparency, not decide on people's behalf.

options.t: 我认为政府应该补贴有机农业研发，降低环保食品的成本，让好选择不仅是有钱人的特权。
options.t_en: I think the government should subsidise research into organic farming and lower the cost of environmentally sound food, so that the good choice is not a privilege of the wealthy.

options.t: 我会支持两种体系并存，工业化食品保障基本供应，有机食品满足差异化需求，不必互相排斥。
options.t_en: I would support the two systems coexisting: industrial food secures basic supply, organic food meets differentiated demand, and they need not exclude each other.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Your region is traditionally agricultural. In recent years large agribusiness has promoted genetically modified crops and intensive livestock farming: yields have risen sharply, but food quality and environmental impact are disputed. A group of local smallholders has started an eat-traditional movement promoting organic farming and direct local sales, though their produce costs more than thirty percent more than industrial food. You have been invited to state your position at a food policy forum.

scene: 你经常使用的新闻平台最近全面改用算法推荐系统，根据你的点击历史推送内容。你发现信息流越来越同质化，难以接触到不同观点。平台负责人解释这是为了提升用户体验，但公共传播学者警告算法正在制造"信息茧房"，削弱公共讨论的基础。作为用户代表，你被邀请参加平台治理听证会。

options.t: 我会要求平台强制加入一定比例的对立观点和公共事务内容，打破茧房，媒体有社会责任。
options.t_en: I will require the platform to include a fixed proportion of opposing views and public affairs reporting, to break the cocoon. Media carry a social responsibility.

options.t: 我认为用户完全自主，平台只是响应需求，如果我不想被局限，我自己会去主动搜索不同内容。
options.t_en: I think users are entirely free to choose and the platform is only responding to demand. If I do not want to be boxed in, I will go and search for other content myself.

options.t: 我会支持用编辑推荐和算法推荐结合，恢复专业编辑的把关角色，不完全由数据驱动。
options.t_en: I will support combining editorial curation with algorithmic recommendation, restoring the gatekeeping role of professional editors so that it is not driven purely by data.

options.t: 我要求平台公开推荐算法的基本逻辑，让用户理解为何看到某些内容，透明度是信任的前提。
options.t_en: I want the platform to publish the basic logic of its recommendation algorithm, so users understand why they are seeing certain things. Transparency is the precondition of trust.

options.t: 我会提议建立公共资助的独立新闻聚合平台，不以点击率为目标，专门提供多元视角。
options.t_en: I will propose a publicly funded independent news aggregator, not aimed at click-through rates, dedicated to offering a plurality of perspectives.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The news platform you use most has switched entirely to algorithmic recommendations, feeding you stories based on what you have clicked on before. You have noticed your feed growing more and more uniform, and it is now hard to come across a view you do not already hold. The platform's head explains that this is simply about improving the user experience. Public communication scholars warn that the algorithm is building an information cocoon that erodes the ground public debate stands on. As a user representative you have been invited to a platform governance hearing.

scene: 你所在城市发生了一系列公共场所暴力事件，警方通过数据分析锁定了一群有犯罪前科的人员，认为他们"高风险"。政府提议对这群人实施预防性监控和宵禁，无需新的犯罪证据即可限制其行动自由。民权组织强烈反对，认为这是"先定罪后审判"；安全部门则认为这是保护公众的必要手段。你是独立审查委员会成员。

options.t: 我会支持预防性措施，在确定威胁面前，个人自由必须让位于公共安全，监管好过后悔。
options.t_en: I would support the preventive measures. Against a clear threat, individual freedom has to give way to public safety; oversight is better than regret.

options.t: 我会坚决反对，没有犯罪就不能惩罚，预防性监控是对法治原则的破坏，人人可能沦为嫌疑人。
options.t_en: I would firmly oppose it. Without a crime there can be no punishment. Preventive monitoring destroys the rule of law, and anyone could become a suspect.

options.t: 我会建议增加警力巡逻和社区干预，而非针对特定人群，用在场预防代替事后监控。
options.t_en: I would recommend more police patrols and community intervention instead of targeting a specific group: prevention through presence rather than monitoring afterwards.

options.t: 我认为应该严格限定预防性措施的期限和申诉渠道，作为临时手段而非长期制度。
options.t_en: I think the duration and the appeal channels for preventive measures must be strictly limited, as a temporary tool rather than a permanent institution.

options.t: 我会主张投资于社会根源解决——教育、就业和心理援助，从源头减少犯罪动机。
options.t_en: I would argue for investing in the social roots of the problem, education, employment and mental health support, to reduce the motive for crime at its source.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A series of violent incidents in public places has hit your city. Using data analysis, the police have identified a group of people with criminal records and labeled them high risk. The government proposes preventive monitoring and a curfew for this group, restricting their freedom of movement without any new evidence of a crime. Civil rights organizations are strongly opposed, calling it conviction before trial. The security services call it a necessary measure to protect the public. You sit on the independent review committee.

scene: 邻国发生了严重的人道主义危机，政府军被指控对平民使用暴力，数十万人流离失所。国际社会讨论是否进行军事干预以保护平民。支持者援引"保护责任"原则，认为主权不应成为屠杀的盾牌；反对者警告干预往往造成更大灾难，且容易被强国用作扩张工具。你是本国议会外交委员会顾问。

options.t: 我会支持授权军事干预，国家主权不应高于人权，国际社会有道德义务制止大规模暴行。
options.t_en: I would support authorising military intervention. National sovereignty should not outrank human rights, and the international community has a moral duty to stop mass atrocities.

options.t: 我会反对军事干预，外国干预很少带来和平，尊重主权是国际秩序的基石，应通过外交施压。
options.t_en: I would oppose military intervention. Foreign intervention rarely brings peace, respect for sovereignty is the cornerstone of international order, and pressure should come through diplomacy.

options.t: 我会建议仅提供人道主义走廊和难民援助，不派战斗部队，军事干预的代价不可控。
options.t_en: I would propose providing only humanitarian corridors and refugee assistance, without sending combat units, since the costs of military intervention are uncontrollable.

options.t: 我认为干预必须经过多边机构授权，且由多国共同执行，防止任何单一国家借此谋取私利。
options.t_en: I think any intervention must be authorised by a multilateral body and carried out jointly by several countries, so that no single state can use it for its own ends.

options.t: 我会主张优先接纳难民并提供庇护，而非在海外用兵，保护具体的人比抽象的主权更重要。
options.t_en: I would argue for prioritising the admission of refugees and offering asylum rather than deploying troops abroad. Protecting actual people matters more than abstract sovereignty.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A severe humanitarian crisis has broken out in a neighbouring country. Government forces are accused of using violence against civilians, and hundreds of thousands have been displaced. The international community is debating military intervention to protect civilians. Supporters invoke the responsibility to protect and argue that sovereignty must not become a shield for massacre; opponents warn that interventions usually cause greater disaster and are easily used by powerful states as a tool of expansion. You are an adviser to your parliament's foreign affairs committee.

scene: 你所在的城市正在试点改革：原本「全民普发、人人有份」的月度现金补贴，将被改为「只有收入低于门槛的家庭才能申领」的定向补助。支持者称这样能省下预算、把钱集中给最需要的人；反对者认为门槛审查会羞辱领取者、制造「贫困陷阱」，而且行政成本不低。你是社区服务站的工作人员，需要在居民说明会上解释这项改革并收集意见。
scene_en: Your city is piloting a reform: a monthly cash benefit that was once universal—paid to everyone equally—is being converted into a targeted subsidy that only households below an income threshold can apply for. Supporters say this saves budget and concentrates money on those who need it most; opponents argue that means-testing humiliates recipients, creates a 'poverty trap,' and carries high administrative costs. You are a community service worker who must explain the reform and collect opinions at a residents' meeting.

options.t: 我会支持定向补助：有限的公共资金应当精准流向最困难的家庭，而不是给高收入家庭发同样多的钱，普发其实是在变相补贴富人。
options.t_en: I will support the targeted subsidy: limited public funds should flow precisely to the households in greatest need, rather than paying the same amount to high-income families—universal payments effectively subsidize the rich.

options.t: 我会反对取消普发：全民平等领取是社会保障的尊严底线，任何审查都会把人分成三六九等，还可能因为标准设定不当而漏掉真正困难的人。
options.t_en: I will oppose scrapping the universal benefit: everyone receiving it equally is the baseline of dignity in social security. Any means-testing sorts people into tiers and may miss the truly needy when the criteria are poorly set.

options.t: 我会建议保留普发、但提高高收入者的累进税来补足成本，既保住「人人有份」的象征意义，又用税收实现再分配。
options.t_en: I will suggest keeping the universal benefit but raising progressive taxes on high earners to cover the cost—preserving the symbolic value of 'everyone has a share' while redistributing through taxation.

options.t: 我认为应当干脆取消现金补贴、减少公共支出，把资源交还给市场和个人自行安排，靠促进就业而非救济来改善贫困。
options.t_en: I think we should simply cancel the cash benefit and cut public spending, returning resources to the market and individuals to manage on their own, improving poverty through employment rather than relief.

options.t: 我会推动用数据和自动化简化审查流程、降低行政成本，在「精准帮扶」与「体面领取」之间找平衡，而不是在普发与定向之间非此即彼。
options.t_en: I will push to simplify the review process with data and automation to cut administrative costs, finding a balance between targeted help and dignified receipt instead of treating universal and targeted as an either-or.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene: 你所在的城市动物园因财政紧张决定缩减开支，管理层提出两项方案：一是把大型动物（如大象、熊）转移给其他设施、缩小展示规模；二是提高票价并引入动物表演以增加收入。有人提醒，动物表演涉及长期训练，可能损害动物福利；也有人指出，动物园承担着濒危物种繁育和科普教育的公共职能，不能只算经济账。你是动物园的理事会成员，需要投票表态。
scene_en: Your city's zoo is cutting expenses due to a tight budget, and management proposes two options: one, transfer large animals such as elephants and bears to other facilities and shrink the exhibition; two, raise ticket prices and introduce animal performances to increase revenue. Some point out that animal shows involve long-term training that may harm animal welfare; others note that the zoo bears the public duty of breeding endangered species and science education, so it cannot be judged by money alone. You are a zoo board member and must vote.

options.t: 我会投票反对动物表演：把动物逼着做出违反天性的动作来取悦观众，是对其生命价值的利用和伤害，动物园宁可缩减规模也不能靠表演牟利。
options.t_en: I will vote against animal performances: forcing animals into acts against their nature to entertain audiences exploits and harms their lives; the zoo should shrink rather than profit from shows.

options.t: 我会支持涨价和表演：动物园需要可持续的收入才能维持繁育和科普，若因资金枯竭而倒闭，动物同样无处可去，两害相权取其轻。
options.t_en: I will support raising prices and holding shows: the zoo needs sustainable revenue to sustain breeding and education; if it collapses from lack of funds, the animals have nowhere to go either—choosing the lesser of two evils.

options.t: 我会主张优先压缩运营成本、向政府申请更多公共拨款，而不是把负担转嫁给游客或牺牲动物福利，公共文化设施本就该由财政保障。
options.t_en: I will advocate first cutting operating costs and seeking more public funding from the government, rather than shifting the burden to visitors or sacrificing animal welfare—public cultural facilities should be funded by the treasury.

options.t: 我会推动把动物园转型为更注重栖息地保护和野化放归的保育中心，逐步减少圈养展示，让动物福利成为核心而非次要考量。
options.t_en: I will push to transform the zoo into a conservation center focused on habitat protection and rewilding, gradually reducing captive display so animal welfare becomes the core, not an afterthought.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene: 你所在的城市准备用一笔公共文化基金支持艺术项目，评审委员会收到两份申请：一份是先锋实验剧团的作品，主题尖锐、形式前卫，可能引发争议甚至被部分公众反感；另一份是民俗博物馆的传统展陈升级，稳妥但有固定受众。委员会内部意见分裂：有人认为公共资金应扶持敢于冒犯和创新的艺术，有人则认为应服务于大多数人的文化需求。你是评审委员，需要表达你的立场。
scene_en: Your city is about to use a public cultural fund to support art projects, and the review committee receives two applications: one is an avant-garde experimental theater work with a sharp theme and cutting-edge form that may provoke controversy or even offend some of the public; the other is a conventional exhibition upgrade for a folk museum—safe but with a fixed audience. The committee is split: some believe public money should support art that dares to offend and innovate, while others believe it should serve the cultural needs of the majority. You are a reviewer and must state your position.

options.t: 我会把资金投给先锋剧团：艺术的公共价值恰恰在于突破常规、挑战既有认知，若只资助「稳妥不出错」的作品，文化就会失去生命力。
options.t_en: I will fund the avant-garde troupe: the public value of art lies precisely in breaking conventions and challenging settled ideas. If we only fund 'safe' works, culture loses its vitality.

options.t: 我会把钱投给民俗博物馆升级：公共资金来自所有纳税人，理应服务于多数人的文化认同与传统传承，而不是少数人的实验趣味。
options.t_en: I will fund the folk museum upgrade: public money comes from all taxpayers and should serve the majority's cultural identity and heritage, not the experimental tastes of a few.

options.t: 我会主张把基金分成两档、同时资助两者，但要求先锋项目同步开展公众导览与讨论，让创新与普及并行而非互斥。
options.t_en: I will advocate splitting the fund to support both, but require the avant-garde project to also run public tours and discussions, so innovation and popular access advance together rather than exclude each other.

options.t: 我会建议公共基金原则上不直接资助艺术内容，而是补助观众和基础设施，把「什么值得支持」的判断权交给市场与公众的消费选择。
options.t_en: I will suggest that public funds generally not subsidize artistic content directly, but instead subsidize audiences and infrastructure, leaving the judgment of 'what is worth supporting' to the market and the public's consumption choices.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene: 你所在的国家体育协会正在讨论是否允许运动员在重大赛事中使用能够提升成绩的新一代训练科技（如基因层面的体能优化或外骨骼辅助）。支持者认为这是体育进步、人类极限的延伸；反对者担心这会破坏公平竞争，把体育变成「谁的资金和科技更强」的军备竞赛。你是协会的规则制定委员会成员，需要提出立场。
scene_en: Your national sports association is debating whether to allow athletes to use a new generation of performance-enhancing training technology (such as gene-level physical optimization or exoskeleton assistance) in major competitions. Supporters see this as sporting progress and an extension of human limits; opponents worry it will destroy fair competition and turn sport into an arms race of 'who has more money and better technology.' You are a member of the rules committee and must take a position.

options.t: 我会支持有条件开放新科技：体育本就见证人类极限的突破，只要技术对所有人开放、信息公开，就不必固守旧的身体观。
options.t_en: I will support conditionally allowing the new technology: sport has always witnessed the extension of human limits. As long as the technology is open to all with transparent information, there is no need to cling to an old view of the body.

options.t: 我会坚决反对：竞技体育的核心是公平起点下的技艺与意志较量，任何超出自然训练范畴的增强都会让胜负失真、也让观众失去信任。
options.t_en: I will firmly oppose it: the core of competitive sport is a contest of skill and will on a level starting point. Any enhancement beyond natural training distorts the result and destroys the audience's trust.

options.t: 我会建议单独设立「增强组」和「传统组」两条赛道分开比赛，让追求极限者与崇尚纯粹者各得其所，互不干扰。
options.t_en: I will suggest setting up separate 'enhanced' and 'traditional' categories so that those seeking limits and those valuing purity each get their place, without interfering with each other.

options.t: 我会推动先做长期健康与安全研究，再谈公平问题——如果技术会伤害运动员身体，那么无论成绩多惊人都不该被允许。
options.t_en: I will push for long-term health and safety research first, before the fairness question—if the technology harms athletes' bodies, it should not be allowed no matter how impressive the results.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene: 你所在的小区老年人比例越来越高，有居民提议把一处闲置商铺改造成社区助老食堂，经费由全体业主分摊；也有年轻住户反对，认为自己暂时用不上、不该为别人的养老买单，主张交给市场或子女自行解决。社区居委会想征集一个能平衡代际利益、长期可持续的方案。你是一名业主代表，需要在业主大会上发言。
scene_en: The proportion of elderly residents in your neighborhood is rising. Some residents propose converting a vacant shop into a community canteen for seniors, with the cost shared by all homeowners; younger residents object, arguing they don't need it yet and shouldn't pay for others' elderly care, preferring to leave it to the market or adult children. The community committee wants a plan that balances intergenerational interests and is sustainable in the long run. You are a homeowners' representative and must speak at the general meeting.

options.t: 我会支持由全体分摊：养老是全社会共同的责任，今天你为老人买单，未来你老了也会被照顾，这是代际互助而非单向付出。
options.t_en: I will support shared funding by everyone: elderly care is a collective social responsibility. Today you pay for the elderly, and tomorrow you will be cared for when you age—this is intergenerational mutual aid, not a one-way contribution.

options.t: 我会反对强制分摊：养老首先是家庭和个人自己的事，谁受益谁付费，让市场提供多样化的助餐服务，比强制集体出资更公平。
options.t_en: I will oppose mandatory cost-sharing: elderly care is first and foremost a family and individual matter; those who benefit should pay. Letting the market provide diverse meal services is fairer than forced collective funding.

options.t: 我会建议采用「使用者付费 + 政府补贴」的混合模式，社区提供场地、政府兜底困难老人，让有能力的自付、困难的受助。
options.t_en: I will suggest a mixed model of 'user pays + government subsidy': the community provides the venue, the government covers needy seniors, so those who can afford it pay and those in hardship receive help.

options.t: 我会推动先做需求调研和自愿认捐，而非立刻向全体业主强制摊派，充分尊重不同家庭的实际情况，避免一刀切激化代际矛盾。
options.t_en: I will push for a needs survey and voluntary pledges first, rather than an immediate across-the-board levy, respecting each family's actual situation to avoid a one-size-fits-all approach that fuels generational conflict.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene: 你注意到身边不少年轻人通过「先买后付」和分期消费平台透支购物，有的已经背上多笔循环债务、月供超过收入的一半。有人呼吁政府出台更严格的信贷监管，限制放贷额度与诱导性营销；也有人认为这是成年人自己的选择，过度监管会剥夺自由、扼杀金融创新。你正在参加一场关于「消费信贷该管多严」的公共讨论。
scene_en: You notice that many young people around you are overspending through 'buy now, pay later' and installment platforms, some already carrying multiple revolving debts with monthly payments exceeding half their income. Some call for stricter credit regulation to cap lending amounts and curb inducement marketing; others argue this is adults' own choice, and over-regulation would strip freedom and stifle financial innovation. You are taking part in a public discussion on 'how strictly consumer credit should be regulated.'

options.t: 我会支持严格监管：诱导性的分期营销和过度授信正在系统性地把缺乏经验的年轻人拖入债务陷阱，国家有责任设置护栏、限制高息和放贷额度。
options.t_en: I will support strict regulation: inducement marketing and over-extension of credit are systematically dragging inexperienced young people into debt traps. The state has a duty to set guardrails, cap high interest rates and lending limits.

options.t: 我会反对过多监管：借钱消费是成年人自主决定的自由，平台提供了便利，个人理应为自己的财务选择负责，与其限制不如加强金融教育。
options.t_en: I will oppose excessive regulation: borrowing to consume is an adult's free choice, platforms provide convenience, and individuals should be responsible for their own financial decisions—better financial education than restriction.

options.t: 我会建议监管聚焦「信息披露」而非「限额」：强制平台明示真实年化利率和违约后果，让消费者在充分知情下自行决策。
options.t_en: I will suggest that regulation focus on disclosure rather than caps: require platforms to clearly show the true annual rate and default consequences, letting consumers decide with full information.

options.t: 我会推动建立个人债务预警与免费咨询机制，由公共资源帮助负债者重组还款、走出困境，而不是只在事后惩罚或事前禁止。
options.t_en: I will push to build a personal debt early-warning and free counseling mechanism, using public resources to help debtors restructure repayments and recover, rather than only punishing after the fact or banning beforehand.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene: 你所在的地区计划新建一座大型能源设施以满足快速增长的用电需求，候选方案是「建设周期短、成本低、但碳排放较高的燃气电厂」，或「清洁但前期投入巨大、周期更长的光伏与储能基地」。当地有就业与电价敏感的居民支持前者，也有环保组织和年轻居民坚持后者。你是规划听证会上的公众代表，需要表态。
scene_en: Your region plans to build a large energy facility to meet fast-growing electricity demand. The candidates are a gas-fired plant—quick to build, cheap, but with higher carbon emissions—or a clean but hugely expensive and slower solar-plus-storage base. Local residents sensitive to jobs and electricity prices support the former, while environmental groups and younger residents insist on the latter. You are a public representative at the planning hearing and must take a position.

options.t: 我会支持燃气电厂：在电价和就业压力面前，先把稳定便宜的电力供上最重要，清洁转型可以等技术和成本成熟后逐步推进。
options.t_en: I will support the gas plant: with electricity prices and jobs at stake, ensuring stable and cheap power first matters most; the clean transition can proceed gradually as technology and costs mature.

options.t: 我会坚持光伏储能方案：即便前期更贵，也不能再为短期成本锁定几十年的高碳资产，气候账迟早要还，早转型成本更低。
