options.t_en: I will insist on the solar-storage plan: even if it costs more upfront, we must not lock in decades of high-carbon assets for short-term cost; the climate bill comes due eventually, and early transition is cheaper.

options.t: 我会建议走中间路线：以燃气电厂作为过渡备用，同时配套投资储能与可再生能源，在保供与减排之间分期平衡。
options.t_en: I will suggest a middle path: use the gas plant as transitional backup while investing in storage and renewables alongside, balancing supply security and emission cuts in phases.

options.t: 我会推动优先挖掘需求侧的节能潜力与电网智能化改造，而不是一味新建大型发电设施，用更少的能源满足同样多的需求。
options.t_en: I will push to first tap demand-side efficiency and grid upgrades rather than simply building large new facilities, meeting the same needs with less energy.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene: 你所在的城市近年来极端降雨频繁，内涝日益严重。市政府提出一项「气候韧性改造」计划：搬迁低洼易涝区的部分居民、修筑大型防洪设施，这需要大幅提高市政税或发行长期债券。部分商户和居民担心成本与动迁损失而反对；也有居民认为拖延下去损失只会更大。你是一名受影响的社区代表，需要表达立场。
scene_en: Your city has seen increasingly frequent extreme rainfall and worsening flooding. The government proposes a 'climate resilience' plan: relocating some residents from low-lying flood-prone areas and building large flood-control facilities, which requires sharply raising municipal taxes or issuing long-term bonds. Some merchants and residents oppose it over costs and relocation losses; others argue that delaying only makes losses worse. You are an affected community representative and must state your position.

options.t: 我会支持提前投入：气候风险只会越来越大，现在花大钱防灾，比未来一次次受灾的损失和生命代价要划算得多，政府该果断负债上马。
options.t_en: I will support investing early: climate risk is only growing. Spending heavily now on prevention is far cheaper than the repeated losses and lives at stake later; the government should borrow decisively and get started.

options.t: 我会反对大幅加税和强制动迁：改造应量力而行，不能以「未来风险」为由让当下的人承担沉重负担，应优先做低成本的预警和疏导。
options.t_en: I will oppose sharp tax hikes and forced relocation: improvements should be within our means, not impose heavy burdens on present people in the name of 'future risk'; low-cost early warning and drainage should come first.

options.t: 我会主张让受益更多、风险更高的区域和产业多承担成本，而不是全民平均分摊，谁更暴露于洪水、谁就更该为防护付费。
options.t_en: I will argue that areas and industries with higher exposure and greater benefit should bear more of the cost, rather than spreading it evenly—those more exposed to flooding should pay more for protection.

options.t: 我会推动把防灾与城市更新、绿色基建结合，让搬迁居民获得体面安置和就业机会，把一次性的救灾变成系统性的升级。
options.t_en: I will push to combine disaster prevention with urban renewal and green infrastructure, giving relocated residents dignified resettlement and jobs, turning one-off relief into systematic upgrading.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene: 你所在的公司正在修订招聘与晋升政策，人力资源部提议引入「隐性偏见培训」和「代表性目标」，以改善长期存在的少数群体占比偏低问题。部分员工担心这会变成「按身份而非能力」的录用标准、反而制造新的不公；也有人认为不主动干预，既有失衡永远不会自行消失。你被邀请在员工大会上发言。
scene_en: Your company is revising its hiring and promotion policies, and HR proposes introducing 'implicit bias training' and 'representation targets' to address the long-standing underrepresentation of minority groups. Some employees worry this will become a criterion of 'identity rather than merit' and create new injustice; others argue that without proactive intervention, the existing imbalance will never disappear on its own. You are invited to speak at the all-hands meeting.

options.t: 我会支持这些措施：结构性失衡不会自动消除，设定代表目标和消除隐性偏见是必要的纠偏，让机会真正对所有人开放。
options.t_en: I will support these measures: structural imbalance will not disappear on its own. Setting representation targets and removing implicit bias are necessary corrections to genuinely open opportunity to all.

options.t: 我会反对按身份设目标：录用和晋升应当只看能力与表现，任何配额或目标都是对「择优」原则的侵蚀，也会让被照顾者背上「靠身份」的污名。
options.t_en: I will oppose identity-based targets: hiring and promotion should look only at ability and performance. Any quota or target erodes the merit principle and stigmatizes beneficiaries as 'hired for identity.'

options.t: 我会建议把重点放在「消除门槛」而非「设定目标」：审查招聘流程中的隐性筛选、扩大候选池、提供托儿与灵活用工等配套，让竞争本身更公平。
options.t_en: I will suggest focusing on 'removing barriers' rather than 'setting targets': audit hidden filters in hiring, widen the candidate pool, and provide childcare and flexible work support so the competition itself is fairer.

options.t: 我会推动用数据透明来取代争议：公开各环节的录用数据、定期审计，若确实存在系统性偏见再针对性纠偏，用证据而非口号推进。
options.t_en: I will push to replace controversy with data transparency: publish hiring data at each stage and audit regularly, correcting specifically when systematic bias is proven—advancing by evidence rather than slogans.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene: 你所在的国家正在讨论是否允许「直接面向消费者的基因检测」自由售卖，人们可以自行检测患病风险、药物反应和体质特征。支持者认为这是个人健康自主和信息自由的体现；反对者担心隐私泄露、误读结果引发焦虑，以及保险公司可能据此歧视性地定价或拒保。你受邀参加一场公共听证，需要表达立场。
scene_en: Your country is debating whether to allow 'direct-to-consumer genetic testing' to be sold freely, letting people test their own disease risk, drug response, and physical traits. Supporters see it as personal health autonomy and information freedom; opponents worry about privacy leaks, anxiety from misreading results, and insurers using the data for discriminatory pricing or denial of coverage. You are invited to a public hearing and must state your position.

options.t: 我会支持自由售卖：自己的基因信息属于自己，成年人有权了解并自主决策，限制它才是对个人健康自主权的剥夺。
options.t_en: I will support free sale: one's genetic information belongs to oneself, adults have the right to know and decide autonomously, and restricting it would strip personal health autonomy.

options.t: 我会反对自由售卖：基因数据是高度敏感、不可更改的隐私，一旦泄露或被保险公司利用，代价无法挽回，应当严格监管甚至禁止。
options.t_en: I will oppose free sale: genetic data is highly sensitive, immutable privacy; once leaked or exploited by insurers, the cost is irreversible. It should be strictly regulated or even prohibited.

options.t: 我会建议有条件开放：要求提供遗传咨询、禁止保险公司使用检测结果定价或拒保，并立法保护基因隐私，在自主与安全间设好边界。
options.t_en: I will suggest conditional access: require genetic counseling, prohibit insurers from using results for pricing or denial, and legislate genetic privacy—drawing a boundary between autonomy and safety.

options.t: 我会推动由公共医疗机构提供可负担、带专业解读的检测，而不是放任商业公司逐利销售，让技术进步服务于健康而非焦虑。
options.t_en: I will push for affordable testing with professional interpretation through public medical institutions, rather than leaving sales to profit-driven companies, so the technology serves health rather than anxiety.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene: 你经营一家小型电子零件制造厂，主要生产精密连接器。最近，你收到一份来自某发展中国家大型代工厂的订单，对方希望以低于市场价30%的价格长期采购，承诺每年翻倍增长。若接下订单，你需临时扩招工人、加班赶工，利润空间被压缩到极限；若拒绝，工厂产能将闲置40%，已有老员工可能面临降薪或裁员。同时，你听说同行业的竞争对手已经接了类似低价订单，靠走量勉强维持。

options.t: 我会接下这个订单，走量保本、保住现有员工岗位，市场经济下现金流比利润率更重要，先活下来再谈转型。
options.t_en: I will take the order. Volume keeps us at break-even and keeps the existing jobs, and in a market economy cash flow matters more than margin: survive first, then talk about moving up the value chain.

options.t: 我会拒绝这种压榨性定价，宁可减产转型做高端定制，靠技术和品质溢价而不是靠低价竞争，卷价格没有出路。
options.t_en: I will refuse this kind of predatory pricing. I would rather cut output and move into high-end custom work, earning a premium on technology and quality instead of competing on price. A race to the bottom on price leads nowhere.

options.t: 我会要求政府或行业协会介入，对这种明显压低本土制造业利润空间的订单设定最低价格保护或反不正当竞争审查，不能让企业单打独斗。
options.t_en: I will ask the government or the industry association to step in, setting a floor price or an unfair-competition review for orders that so obviously squeeze the margin of domestic manufacturing. A single firm should not have to fight this alone.

options.t: 我会与对方重新谈判，要求逐步提升价格或共同分摊模具开发成本，同时寻找其他海外客户分散风险，不把鸡蛋放一个篮子。
options.t_en: I will go back and renegotiate, asking for prices to rise step by step or for the tooling development cost to be shared, while looking for other overseas customers to spread the risk. You do not put all your eggs in one basket.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: You run a small factory making precision electronic components, mainly connectors. A large contract manufacturer in a developing country has offered you a long-term order at thirty percent below the market price, promising to double the volume every year. Taking it means hiring temporary workers and running overtime, with your margin squeezed to almost nothing. Refusing it means leaving forty percent of your capacity idle, and possibly cutting pay or laying off workers who have been with you for years. You also hear that a competitor has already taken a similar low-price order and is surviving on volume alone.

scene: 你居住的城市近五年涌入大量外来务工者，他们聚集在城郊一片旧工业区，逐渐形成了一条充满异乡风味的街道——餐馆、杂货店、宗教场所林立。本地居民中有人抱怨治安变差、公共服务压力增大，要求限制外来人口；也有人认为这条街道给城市带来了活力和消费，应该包容多元。市政府正在征集意见，决定是否将这片区域纳入正式的社区规划。

options.t: 我会支持把这片区域纳入正式规划，给他们合法的社区地位，文化多样性是城市的财富，排外只会让我们更封闭。
options.t_en: I would support bringing the area into the formal plan and giving it legal community status. Cultural diversity is an asset to a city; excluding outsiders only makes us more closed.

options.t: 我认为应该先评估公共服务承载力，再设定准入门槛，不能让城市资源被无限稀释，有序接纳比完全开放更负责任。
options.t_en: I think we should first assess how much public service capacity there is, then set admission thresholds. City resources can't be diluted indefinitely; orderly intake is more responsible than full openness.

options.t: 我倾向于尊重他们自发的社区自治，由移民群体自己推选代表与市政府协商，减少自上而下的强制规划，保留多元并存的空间。
options.t_en: I lean toward respecting the self-organized community they have built, letting the migrant groups elect their own representatives to negotiate with the city, reducing top-down planning and keeping room for diversity to coexist.

options.t: 我觉得这条街的存在本身就是对本地文化的侵蚀，我会主张恢复原有社区风貌，限制异域商业招牌和宗教标识的过度扩张。
options.t_en: I think the existence of this street is itself an erosion of local culture. I would argue for restoring the original character of the neighborhood and limiting the spread of foreign shop signs and religious symbols.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: In the past five years a large number of migrant workers have moved into the city where you live, gathering in an old industrial district on the outskirts. A street has grown up there full of flavors from elsewhere: restaurants, grocery stores and places of worship side by side. Some local residents complain that safety has worsened and public services are strained, and want migration restricted. Others say the street has brought energy and spending to the city and that diversity should be embraced. The city government is collecting opinions on whether to bring the area into the formal community plan.

scene: 你是一家科技公司的中层管理者，部门里男女比例约为7:1。最近人力资源部推行了一项新政策：同等条件下优先晋升女性员工，以纠正长期性别失衡。部门里一位业绩确实突出的男同事连续三年落选晋升，而一位资历稍浅但表现合格的女同事获得了晋升名额。男同事私下向你抱怨，认为这是反向歧视，影响了团队士气。

options.t: 我会支持这项政策，结构性不平等需要矫枉过正，短期的配额制是为了打破长期的性别天花板，整体公平需要过程性补偿。
options.t_en: I would support the policy. Structural inequality needs overcorrection, and a short-term quota is meant to break a long-standing glass ceiling; overall fairness requires transitional compensation.

options.t: 我认为晋升应该只看能力和业绩，不管性别。如果因为性别而优先或延后，就是对个人努力的不尊重，我会在内部反馈中反对这种配额。
options.t_en: I think promotion should look only at ability and results, regardless of gender. Prioritising or deferring someone because of gender disrespects individual effort, and I would oppose such a quota in my internal feedback.

options.t: 我理解纠正性别失衡的意图，但 quotas 会让被晋升的女性也被质疑是靠政策而非实力，我会建议改为隐名评审和结构化面试，减少偏见而非强制比例。
options.t_en: I understand the intent to correct the imbalance, but quotas mean the women promoted will also be suspected of getting there through policy rather than ability. I would propose anonymised review and structured interviews instead, reducing bias rather than mandating proportions.

options.t: 我会主张对部门所有女性员工进行系统性的培训和 mentorship，提升她们的真实竞争力，而不是用配额制造虚假的平等，实力平等才是真的平等。
options.t_en: I would argue for systematic training and mentorship for all the women in the department, raising their real competitiveness instead of manufacturing false equality through quotas. Equality of ability is the real equality.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: You are a mid-level manager at a tech company where your department runs about seven men to one woman. HR has just introduced a policy: all else being equal, women are promoted first, to correct a long-standing imbalance. A male colleague with genuinely strong results has missed promotion three years running, while a slightly less senior but competent female colleague got the slot. He complains to you privately that this is reverse discrimination and that team morale is suffering.

scene: 你是一名普通市民，在社交媒体上看到一段视频：一位街头小贩被多名执法人员按倒在地，原因是他在禁止摆摊的路段贩卖水果。视频引发了大量讨论，有人认为执法人员暴力执法、程序不当；也有人认为小贩明知故犯、阻碍执法在先。几天后，官方通报称小贩被处以行政拘留，而发布视频的网友被传唤调查。

options.t: 我会持续关注此事，要求公开完整的执法记录仪影像，程序正义和透明是法治的底线，任何一方都不该在信息不全时被定罪。
options.t_en: I will keep following this and demand that the full body-camera footage be released. Procedural fairness and transparency are the floor of the rule of law, and neither side should be convicted on incomplete information.

options.t: 我认为街头秩序需要维护，执法人员在劝阻无效后采取强制措施是履行职责，不能因为是弱势群体就豁免违法，法律面前人人平等。
options.t_en: I think street order has to be maintained. Once persuasion has failed, taking coercive measures is the officers doing their job. Being poor does not exempt anyone from the law, and everyone is equal before it.

options.t: 我会质疑对视频发布者的传唤，公民监督公权力是基本权利，不应被视为制造事端，除非能证明视频经过恶意剪辑且意图煽动。
options.t_en: I will question the summoning of the person who posted the video. Citizens supervising public power is a basic right and should not be treated as stirring up trouble, unless it can be shown the clip was maliciously edited to incite.

options.t: 我觉得底层谋生和城市管理之间应该有缓冲空间，我会建议政府设立更多合法便民摊位，用疏导替代围堵，而非单纯处罚。
options.t_en: I think there should be some room between people scraping a living at the bottom and how the city is managed. I will propose more legal, convenient stall sites, guiding people instead of cordoning them off, rather than simply punishing them.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: You are an ordinary resident, and a video has come up on social media: a street vendor is pinned to the ground by several enforcement officers, because he was selling fruit on a stretch of road where stalls are banned. The clip has set off a great deal of argument. Some say the officers used excessive force and skipped proper procedure; others say the vendor knew the rule perfectly well and obstructed enforcement first. A few days later the official notice says the vendor has been given an administrative detention, and that the user who posted the video has been summoned for questioning.

scene: 你所在的大学最近在讨论是否应该在校园内设立一个多信仰祈祷/冥想空间，供不同宗教背景的学生使用。支持者认为这有助于少数信仰群体的精神需求和校园包容性；反对者担心这会引发宗教之间的竞争、占用有限的公共空间，并且大学作为公立机构应保持世俗中立。校方正在征集师生意见。

options.t: 我会支持设立多信仰空间，大学应该尊重每个人的精神需求，包容性不是中立性的对立面，而是对不同信仰的平等尊重。
options.t_en: I would support setting up the multi-faith space. A university should respect everyone's spiritual needs. Inclusiveness is not the opposite of neutrality; it is equal respect for different beliefs.

options.t: 我认为公立大学应该保持严格的世俗性，宗教活动属于私人领域，不应占用公共资源或获得制度化的认可，防止宗教对公共空间的渗透。
options.t_en: I think a public university should remain strictly secular. Religious practice belongs to the private sphere, and it should not take up public resources or receive institutional recognition, which would let religion seep into public space.

options.t: 我会建议把空间定位为「安静冥想室」而非「祈祷室」，不明确归属任何宗教，让有精神需求的人都可以用，但不赋予任何宗教官方地位。
options.t_en: I would suggest framing the space as a quiet meditation room rather than a prayer room, belonging to no religion in particular, open to anyone with a spiritual need, without granting any religion official standing.

options.t: 我觉得只要学生自发组织、不占用学校预算和正式建筑，在校园角落找一个临时空间没问题，不该过度管制学生的私下信仰活动。
options.t_en: I think as long as students organize it themselves and it uses no school budget and no official building, finding a temporary corner on campus is fine. Private religious practice among students shouldn't be over-regulated.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The university you are at is discussing whether to set up a multi-faith prayer and meditation space on campus for students of different religious backgrounds. Supporters say it would serve the spiritual needs of minority faith groups and make the campus more inclusive. Opponents worry it would set off competition between religions, take up limited public space, and that a public institution should stay secular and neutral. The administration is collecting views from staff and students.

scene: 你住在一栋上世纪八十年代建成的老小区，六层无电梯。楼里半数住户是行动不便的老人，爬楼梯日益艰难。加装电梯的提案已讨论多年，但一楼和二楼的住户坚决反对，理由是电梯会影响他们的采光、产生噪音，而且他们用不上却要分摊费用。高层住户则认为低层在阻碍改善性需求，双方僵持不下。

options.t: 我会支持高层老人，加装电梯是基本的适老化改造，低层应该顾全大局，对采光和噪音的影响可以通过技术方案缓解，不应让少数人利益阻碍整体改善。
options.t_en: I would side with the elderly upstairs. Installing a lift is basic age-friendly adaptation and the lower floors should consider the bigger picture; the effects on light and noise can be mitigated with technical solutions, and a minority's interests should not block an overall improvement.

options.t: 我尊重低层住户的产权和利益，加装电梯确实改变了他们购房时的预期，应该给予合理补偿，或者让高层多分摊费用，不能强制推行。
options.t_en: I respect the lower-floor households' property rights and interests. Installing a lift does change what they expected when they bought, so they deserve reasonable compensation, or the upper floors should carry more of the cost. It should not be forced through.

options.t: 我认为需要政府补贴和统筹方案，老旧小区改造不能全靠业主扯皮，公权力应该介入协调并提供资金支持，让电梯加装变成公共工程而非私人纠纷。
options.t_en: I think government subsidy and overall planning are needed. Redeveloping old compounds cannot rest on owners arguing it out; public authority should step in to coordinate and provide funding, turning lift installation into a public works project rather than a private dispute.

options.t: 我会提议装外置式小型电梯，只停靠奇数层或每隔一层停靠，减少对低层的影响，同时让费用分摊更灵活，尽量找折中方案。
options.t_en: I would propose an external compact lift serving only odd floors or every second floor, reducing the impact on the lower floors and making cost-sharing more flexible, looking for a compromise wherever possible.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: You live in a 1980s six-storey walk-up with no lift. Half the residents are elderly and find the stairs harder every year. Adding a lift has been discussed for years, but households on the first and second floors firmly oppose it: it would block their light, make noise, and they would pay a share for something they cannot use. Those on the upper floors say the lower floors are blocking a needed improvement, and neither side will move.

scene: 你所在的城市爆发了一起食品安全事件：某大型连锁超市销售的预制菜被检出防腐剂超标，涉及多家供应商。调查发现，这些问题产品大多来自一家使用低成本进口原料的加工厂。事件引发公众对预制菜和食品工业化的广泛担忧。市政府迅速出台了更严格的预制菜标签和添加剂限制法规，但这也导致许多中小预制菜企业成本骤增、面临关停。

options.t: 我会支持严格监管，食品安全是底线，哪怕中小企业因此倒闭也是市场出清，消费者健康比企业生存更重要，监管不严的代价由全民承担。
options.t_en: I will support strict regulation. Food safety is the floor, and even if small firms go under as a result, that is the market clearing out. Consumers' health matters more than any firm's survival, and the cost of weak enforcement is paid by everyone.

options.t: 我认为监管应该分步推进，给中小企业缓冲期和转型支持，一刀切会导致大量失业和供应链断裂，政府不该只堵不疏。
options.t_en: I think regulation should be phased in, with a transition period and support for small and medium firms. A blanket rule will cost a lot of jobs and break supply chains; the government should not only block the way without opening one.

options.t: 我倾向于让消费者自己选，用更透明的标签和溯源系统取代硬性禁令，相信市场机制会让消费者用脚投票淘汰劣质企业。
options.t_en: I lean towards letting consumers decide, replacing outright bans with more transparent labelling and traceability. I trust the market: consumers will vote with their feet and drive out the bad producers.

options.t: 我觉得应该限制进口低价原料，保护本土农业和食品加工企业，食品安全问题背后是全球化供应链失控，适度贸易保护有助于重建可控的食品体系。
options.t_en: I think cheap imported ingredients should be restricted, to protect domestic farming and food processing. Behind the food safety problem is a global supply chain out of control, and moderate trade protection would help rebuild a food system we can actually oversee.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: A food safety scandal has broken in your city: pre-prepared dishes sold by a large supermarket chain were found to contain preservatives above the permitted limit, and several suppliers are involved. The investigation traces most of the problem products to one processing plant that uses cheap imported ingredients. The public is now broadly uneasy about pre-prepared food and about industrialised food production in general. The city government moves quickly to bring in stricter labelling rules and tighter limits on additives, but the new rules sharply raise costs for many small and medium producers, some of which now face closure.

scene: 你是一名内容创作者，经营着一个有十万订阅者的频道，主要讨论社会议题。最近，你注意到平台算法明显倾向于推送情绪化、标题夸张的内容，而理性分析的长视频流量持续下滑。一位同行建议你调整风格：缩短时长、增加争议性话题、使用更耸动的标题，否则很难维持收入。与此同时，你看到平台正在试点「信息可信度评分」系统，由算法和第三方事实核查机构共同评定内容。

options.t: 我会坚持原有风格，不向算法妥协，内容创作者的职责是提供有价值的思考，而不是制造情绪垃圾，短期的流量损失换长期的信誉积累。
options.t_en: I would stick to my existing style and not compromise with the algorithm. A creator's job is to offer thinking worth something, not to manufacture emotional garbage. A short-term loss in reach buys a long-term accumulation of credibility.

options.t: 我会适度调整表达方式，在保持核心观点的前提下优化标题和节奏，这是适应媒介环境的生存策略，清高不能当饭吃。
options.t_en: I would adjust how I express things moderately, improving titles and pacing while keeping the core argument. That is a survival strategy for the media environment; you can't eat integrity.

options.t: 我支持平台的信息可信度评分系统，但必须由多元独立的事实核查机构组成，而非单一平台垄断判定权，算法辅助但人工终审。
options.t_en: I support the platform's credibility scoring, but it has to be made up of multiple independent fact-checking bodies rather than one platform holding a monopoly on judgment: algorithm-assisted, with humans making the final call.

options.t: 我不赞成平台给信息打可信度评分：由平台来判定「真实」等于让它握有筛选内容的权力，我倾向让用户自行辨别、保持开放竞争，而不是用算法预先干预。
options.t_en: I don't support the platform scoring information for credibility. A platform deciding what is true amounts to giving it the power to filter content. I would rather let users judge for themselves and keep the competition open than have an algorithm intervene in advance.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: You are a content creator running a channel with a hundred thousand subscribers, mostly on social issues. Lately you have noticed that the platform's algorithm clearly favors emotional, heavily hyped content, while your long, carefully reasoned videos keep losing reach. A fellow creator suggests you change style: shorter, more controversial topics, more sensational titles, or you will struggle to keep the income. At the same time, you see the platform piloting a credibility score for content, rated jointly by an algorithm and third-party fact-checkers.

scene: 你所在的城市发生了一起震惊公众的抢劫伤人案：一名有多次前科的惯犯在出狱后半年内再次作案，导致一名路人重伤。媒体披露此人此前多次犯罪但量刑较轻，因为法律对某些情节的认定存在弹性空间。事件引发激烈讨论：有人呼吁加重累犯处罚，甚至推动「三振出局」式的终身监禁；也有人指出此人出狱后缺乏社会支持、就业困难，是系统性 Rehabilitation 失败，而非单纯个人之恶。

options.t: 我会支持加重累犯处罚，对反复危害社会的惯犯必须大幅提高刑期，法律保护守法者而不是给惯犯反复试错的机会，公共安全优先。
options.t_en: I would support heavier penalties for repeat offenders. Habitual criminals who keep harming society must face substantially longer sentences; the law protects the law-abiding rather than giving recidivists repeated chances to try again. Public safety comes first.

options.t: 我认为问题出在出狱后的社会支持缺失，应该推动更生保护、就业培训和心理辅导，让人有路可走才不会重蹈覆辙，惩罚不是唯一答案。
options.t_en: I think the problem is the lack of support after release. We should push for rehabilitation protection, job training and counselling, so that people have a path and do not repeat the offence. Punishment is not the only answer.

options.t: 我主张对暴力累犯设立更严格的假释和监控条件，但不必一刀切终身监禁，用电子监控和社区矫正平衡安全与权利，让数据决定风险。
options.t_en: I argue for stricter parole and monitoring conditions for violent repeat offenders without going straight to life sentences. Electronic monitoring and community correction can balance safety and rights, and the data can decide the risk.

options.t: 我认为司法裁量权应该收紧，对类似情节的累犯设定更明确的最低刑期标准，减少法官主观弹性，让判决更可预期、更有威慑力。
options.t_en: I think judicial discretion should be tightened by setting clearer minimum sentences for repeat offenders in similar circumstances, reducing judges' subjective latitude and making sentences more predictable and more deterrent.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A robbery and stabbing that shocked the public has happened in your city: a repeat offender attacked again within six months of release, leaving a passer-by seriously injured. The media reported that he had offended several times before but received relatively light sentences, because the law leaves discretion in how certain circumstances are assessed. The case has set off a fierce argument: some call for much heavier penalties for repeat offenders, even three-strikes-style life sentences; others point out that after release he had no social support and could not find work, and that this is a systemic failure of rehabilitation rather than simple individual wickedness.

scene: 你是一名国际贸易顾问，正为客户评估是否进入一个政局不稳但市场增长迅速的国家。该国最近发生政变，新政府冻结了部分外国资产，但承诺保护新进入的投资者。你的客户是一家制造业企业，如果现在进入可以用极低价格收购破产的本地工厂，但风险是资产随时可能被没收或因为国际制裁而无法交易。与此同时，你的母国政府正在考虑是否对该新政权实施经济制裁。

options.t: 我会建议客户暂缓进入，等企业社会责任和商业利益以外，支持一个未经民主程序上台的政权等于间接认可其合法性，道德风险太高。
options.t_en: I will advise the client to hold off. Beyond corporate responsibility and commercial interest, backing a regime that came to power without any democratic process amounts to recognising its legitimacy by the back door, and the moral risk is too high.

options.t: 我会建议客户抓住窗口期进入市场，商业决策应基于风险和回报计算，不应被政治表态绑架，投资者没有义务替政府执行外交政策。
options.t_en: I will advise the client to seize the window and enter. Business decisions should rest on a calculation of risk and return, and should not be taken hostage by political gestures; investors have no duty to carry out their government's foreign policy for it.

options.t: 我会建议客户与母国政府协调，等待制裁政策明朗后再做决定，外交一致性对跨国企业很重要，单独行动可能面临法律和声誉双重风险。
options.t_en: I will advise the client to coordinate with our own government and wait until the sanctions position is clear. Foreign policy consistency matters a great deal for multinationals, and going it alone risks both legal and reputational exposure.

options.t: 我会建议客户以人道主义投资的名义进入，帮助重建当地民生和就业设施，既获取市场先机又积累国际 goodwill，把商业行为包装成发展援助。
options.t_en: I will advise the client to enter under the label of humanitarian investment, helping rebuild local livelihoods and employment. It secures a market position early and builds international goodwill at the same time, dressing a commercial move up as development assistance.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: You are an international trade consultant, assessing for a client whether to enter a country where politics is unstable but the market is growing fast. A coup took place there recently; the new government has frozen some foreign assets, while promising to protect investors who come in now. Your client is a manufacturer that could buy up bankrupt local plants at a very low price, at the risk of those assets being seized at any moment, or becoming impossible to trade because of international sanctions. Meanwhile your own government is deciding whether to impose economic sanctions on the new regime.

scene: 你所在的城市近期失业率攀升，政府财政紧张。市议会提出两套方案：一套是削减失业救济金发放时长，认为过长的补助会降低人们找工作的动力；另一套是维持甚至小幅提高救济标准，理由是经济下行期失业者并非不愿工作，而是岗位确实稀缺，削减救济会让更多家庭陷入贫困。你作为市民代表被邀请在听证会上发表意见。

options.t: 我会支持削减救济时长并附加严格的求职证明要求——福利不该成为懒散的温床，只有让人感受到不工作的代价，才能真正激励大家重返职场。
options.t_en: I would support shortening the benefit period and attaching strict proof-of-job-search requirements. Welfare shouldn't be a breeding ground for idleness; only when people feel the cost of not working will they really be pushed back into the workforce.

options.t: 我会主张维持现有救济标准，同时政府应投入资金创造公共就业岗位，让人有尊严地获得收入，而不是在饥饿边缘被迫接受低薪压榨。
options.t_en: I would argue for keeping the current benefit level, while the government invests in creating public jobs, so people can earn with dignity instead of being forced to accept low-paid exploitation on the edge of hunger.

options.t: 我觉得救济可以发，但必须引入社区互助审核机制，由本地志愿者评估申请者是否真的在努力找工作，避免资源被滥用。
options.t_en: I think benefits can be paid, but a community mutual-review mechanism has to be brought in, with local volunteers assessing whether applicants are genuinely trying to find work, so that resources aren't abused.

options.t: 我倾向于用负所得税替代现行救济，收入越低补贴比例越高，但绝不取消——这样既保留激励，也守住底线。
options.t_en: I lean toward replacing the current benefits with a negative income tax, where the lower your income the higher the subsidy rate, but never abolishing it. That keeps the incentive and holds the floor.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Unemployment in your city has risen and the government's finances are tight. The city council has proposed two options. One is to shorten how long unemployment benefits are paid, on the theory that overly long support reduces the incentive to look for work. The other is to keep the current level, or raise it slightly, on the grounds that in a downturn the unemployed are not unwilling to work but that jobs are genuinely scarce, and cutting benefits would push more families into poverty. As a citizen representative you have been invited to speak at the hearing.

scene: 你公司的一位女同事生完孩子三个月后就被HR暗示「该回来上班了」，她本想休满法定产假并申请延长无薪育儿假，但部门主管直言项目人手紧张、她的岗位已经有人临时顶替，再拖下去可能「影响考评」。她向你倾诉，说她既不想放弃事业，又觉得对不起孩子。

options.t: 我会建议她先回来上班，孩子可以请保姆或让老人带——职业黄金期一旦断档，再追上来很难，经济独立才是女性最大的底气。
options.t_en: I would advise her to come back first and arrange a nanny or help from grandparents for the child. Once the prime career years are broken, catching up is very hard, and financial independence is a woman's strongest footing.

options.t: 我觉得公司这是在变相逼退，我会鼓励她向劳动监察部门投诉，同时联合其他同事向管理层施压，要求落实法定产假和反歧视保护。
options.t_en: I think the company is quietly pushing her out. I would encourage her to complain to the labour inspectorate and to join with other colleagues in pressing management to honour statutory maternity leave and anti-discrimination protection.

options.t: 我会劝她别太焦虑，三个月其实够了，很多妈妈都是这么过来的，家庭和事业总要有所取舍，先把眼前的工作稳住再说。
options.t_en: I would tell her not to worry so much. Three months is actually enough, and plenty of mothers get through it this way; family and career always require trade-offs, so steady the job in front of her first.

options.t: 我主张推动公司实行男女同长的带薪育儿假，这样她丈夫也能休，压力就不会全压在她一个人身上，职场性别歧视也会减少。
options.t_en: I argue for pushing the company to offer paid parental leave of equal length to men and women, so that her husband can take it too. The pressure would not fall entirely on her, and workplace gender discrimination would ease.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: A female colleague at your company was hinted by HR three months after giving birth that it was time to come back. She had wanted to take her full statutory maternity leave and then apply for extended unpaid parental leave, but her department head said flatly that the project was short-staffed, her post had already been covered temporarily, and dragging it out might affect her review. She confides in you that she does not want to give up her career, yet feels she is failing her child.

scene: 你所在大学的生物实验室正在招募志愿者参与一项新药测试，实验需要使用大量小白鼠，部分实验过程会让老鼠承受疼痛。抗议者在校园门口举牌，要求停止使用动物实验，认为可以改用计算机模拟和细胞培养替代。而实验室负责人回应说，目前的技术手段还无法完全模拟活体免疫反应，停止动物实验会拖慢救人性命的药物研发进度。

options.t: 我会加入抗议队伍，要求学校设立动物实验伦理审查委员会，严格限制动物使用数量，并强制要求研究团队先穷尽所有替代方案。
options.t_en: I will join the protest line and demand that the university set up an animal ethics review committee, strictly cap the number of animals used, and require every research team to exhaust all alternatives first.

options.t: 我理解抗议者的心情，但如果因此延误癌症新药的上市，那些本可以被救的病人怎么办？我会支持在监管下继续实验，但要求尽量减少动物痛苦。
options.t_en: I understand how the protesters feel, but if a new cancer drug is delayed because of this, what happens to the patients who could have been saved? I will support the experiments continuing under supervision, with a requirement to minimise the animals' suffering.

options.t: 我会提议学校增加科研拨款，加速开发器官芯片和AI模拟技术，目标是五年内将动物实验减少一半，而不是简单一刀切地禁止。
options.t_en: I will propose that the university increase research funding to speed up organ-on-chip and AI simulation work, with the aim of halving animal experiments within five years, rather than simply banning them outright.

options.t: 我觉得这取决于实验的价值——如果是治疗罕见病的突破性研究，动物牺牲可以接受；但如果是化妆品毒性测试，那就完全不该用动物。
options.t_en: I think it depends on the value of the experiment. If it is breakthrough research on a rare disease, the sacrifice of animals is acceptable; if it is cosmetics toxicity testing, animals should not be used at all.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A biology lab at your university is recruiting volunteers for trials of a new drug. The work requires large numbers of mice, and parts of the procedure cause the animals pain. Protesters are outside the campus gate with placards, calling for an end to animal experiments and arguing that computer simulation and cell culture can take their place. The head of the lab answers that current techniques still cannot fully reproduce a living immune response, and that stopping animal work would slow down drug development that saves human lives.

scene: 你居住的城市有一座百年老剧院，因年久失修和观众流失，市政府考虑将其拆除改建为商业综合体，预计能带来大量税收和就业岗位。一群本地艺术家和历史保护人士发起请愿，认为老剧院是城市文化记忆的象征，应当修缮并继续作为公共文化空间使用。两边各有支持者，市议会即将投票决定。

options.t: 我会投票支持拆除改建——城市要发展，不能总抱着老建筑 sentimental，商业综合体带来的就业和税收才是实打实的民生利益。
options.t_en: I would vote for demolition and redevelopment. A city has to develop; you can't keep clinging to old buildings out of sentiment. The jobs and tax revenue from a commercial complex are solid, real benefits for ordinary people.

options.t: 我会坚决支持保留并修缮老剧院，可以申请文化遗产保护基金，同时引入当代演出吸引年轻观众，文化地标一旦消失就再也回不来了。
options.t_en: I would firmly support keeping and restoring the old theater. We can apply to heritage preservation funds and bring in contemporary performances to attract younger audiences. Once a cultural landmark is gone, it never comes back.

options.t: 我觉得可以折中：保留剧院外观和核心结构，内部改造为兼具商业和文化功能的复合空间，比如底层餐饮、上层演出厅。
options.t_en: I think there is a middle path: keep the theater's facade and core structure, and convert the interior into a mixed space with both commercial and cultural functions, say restaurants on the ground floor and a performance hall above.

options.t: 我主张把决定权交给社区投票，让附近居民和常去剧院的市民来决定，而不是由市议会或开发商单方面拍板。
options.t_en: I would argue for putting the decision to a community vote, letting nearby residents and the people who actually go to the theater decide, rather than the city council or a developer deciding unilaterally.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: Your city has a century-old theater. Because of long neglect and a shrinking audience, the city government is considering demolishing it and building a commercial complex, which is expected to bring substantial tax revenue and jobs. A group of local artists and heritage preservationists has started a petition, arguing the theater is a symbol of the city's cultural memory and should be repaired and kept in use as a public cultural space. Both sides have supporters, and the council is about to vote.

scene: 国际奥委会正在讨论是否允许接受过青春期前激素抑制治疗的跨性别女性参加女子组比赛。支持者认为这是包容与平等的权利，反对者则认为即便抑制了激素，青春期前男性发育的骨骼和肌肉优势仍会在成年后显现，对顺性别女性运动员不公平。你是一名体育评论员，被邀请在公开论坛上就此发表看法。

options.t: 我会主张按出生时的生理性别分组比赛，同时设立一个开放的「不限性别」组别——这样既保护女子组的公平，也给跨性别运动员参赛通道。
options.t_en: I would argue for competition by birth sex, with an open category not divided by gender. That protects fairness in the women's event while still giving transgender athletes a route to compete.

options.t: 我会支持允许符合条件的跨性别女性参赛，体育的本质是参与和突破自我，用医学标准筛选后，她们的优势已被控制在合理范围内。
options.t_en: I would support allowing eligible transgender women to compete. Sport is about participation and pushing your own limits, and once medical criteria have filtered applicants, their advantage has been kept within a reasonable range.

options.t: 我觉得这个问题太复杂，应该由运动医学专家和生物伦理委员会制定统一标准，而不是由舆论或政治压力决定谁可以参赛。
options.t_en: I think the question is too complex and should be settled by sports medicine experts and a bioethics committee setting a common standard, not by public opinion or political pressure deciding who may compete.

options.t: 我会提议干脆取消男女分组，全部按体重、肌肉量等生理指标进行分级比赛——这样无论性别如何，都在公平的生理层级上竞技。
options.t_en: I would propose abolishing the men's and women's divisions altogether and classifying competition by physiological indicators such as body weight and muscle mass, so that regardless of gender everyone competes at a fair physiological level.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The International Olympic Committee is debating whether to let transgender women who underwent puberty-suppressing hormone treatment compete in the women's category. Supporters frame it as a matter of inclusion and equal rights; opponents argue that even with suppressed hormones, the bone and muscle advantages of male puberty persist into adulthood, which is unfair to cisgender women athletes. You are a sports commentator invited to give a view at a public forum.

scene: 你父母年过七旬，父亲确诊早期阿尔茨海默症，母亲独自照顾日益吃力。你工作繁忙且住在另一座城市。现在有几个选择：把父母送进专业养老院，但费用高昂且父亲抗拒陌生环境；请住家护工，但靠谱的护工难找且家里空间不够；或者你辞职搬回去照顾，但意味着放弃刚有起色的职业生涯。你彻夜难眠。

options.t: 我会选择把父亲送进有认知症专区的养老院，专业护理比家人更科学，我定期去探望——情感上难受，但理性上这是对父亲最好的选择。
options.t_en: I will move my father into a care home with a dementia unit. Professional care is more systematic than what family can manage, and I will visit regularly. It feels terrible, but on the whole it is the best choice for him.

options.t: 我会申请远程办公并搬回父母所在城市，工作可以再找，父母只有一个，我不想在未来后悔没陪伴他们最后的清醒时光。
options.t_en: I will ask to work remotely and move back to my parents' city. A job can be found again; there is only one set of parents, and I do not want to regret not being there for the last of their clear years.

options.t: 我会推动社区建立「日间照料中心」，白天送父亲去，晚上接回家，既减轻母亲负担，又不用完全脱离家庭环境，费用也比全托低。
options.t_en: I will push for the community to set up a day care centre: my father goes during the day and comes home in the evening, which eases the load on my mother without taking him out of the family home, and costs less than full residential care.

options.t: 我会游说政府增加长期护理保险的覆盖范围和补贴，养老不该完全压给家庭个人，这是全社会共同面对的结构性问题。
options.t_en: I will lobby the government to widen long-term care insurance and raise the subsidies. Eldercare should not fall entirely on individual families; this is a structural problem the whole society faces.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: Your parents are over seventy. Your father has just been diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer's, and your mother is finding it harder and harder to care for him alone. Your job is demanding and you live in another city. The options are these: a specialist care home, which is expensive and which your father resists because the place is unfamiliar; a live-in carer, though reliable ones are hard to find and there is no room at home; or you quit and move back, giving up a career that has only just started to take off. You lie awake all night over it.

scene: 你的一位远房表弟刚大学毕业，月收入不高，却沉迷网购和手游氪金，已经在三家网贷平台累计欠下八万元，利息越滚越高。他父母想帮他还清，但家里也不富裕；有亲戚建议让他自己承担后果，「吃一堑长一智」；也有人提议报警或找媒体曝光那些高利贷平台。表弟本人又羞愧又绝望，向你求助。

options.t: 我会帮他联系专业的债务重组咨询，制定还款计划，同时强烈建议他戒掉网贷和过度消费的习惯——成年人要为自己的选择负责。
options.t_en: I would help him get in touch with professional debt restructuring advice and work out a repayment plan, and strongly urge him to break the online borrowing and overspending habits. An adult is responsible for his own choices.

options.t: 我会支持他父母先帮他还清本金，然后立字据让他分期还给父母，但利息部分要去和平台协商减免——家人之间该帮，但也要有规矩。
options.t_en: I would support his parents paying off the principal first, with a written agreement for him to repay them in installments, while the interest portion gets negotiated down with the platforms. Family should help, but there have to be rules.

options.t: 我会建议他向金融监管部门举报这些平台，如果利率超过法定上限就是非法放贷，不该还；同时呼吁政府加强网贷监管，不能放任平台收割年轻人。
options.t_en: I would suggest he report the platforms to the financial regulator. If the rate exceeds the legal ceiling it is illegal lending and should not be repaid. At the same time, the government should tighten oversight of online lending rather than letting platforms harvest young people.

options.t: 我觉得最该做的是让学校和工作单位加强财商教育，年轻人缺乏对复利和信用的认知才容易陷进去，预防比补救更重要。
options.t_en: I think the most important thing is for schools and employers to strengthen financial literacy education. Young people fall in because they don't understand compound interest and credit. Prevention matters more than remedy.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: A distant cousin of yours has just graduated from university. His income is modest, but he is hooked on online shopping and in-app purchases in mobile games, and he has borrowed from three online lending platforms to a total of eighty thousand, with the interest compounding. His parents want to clear it for him, but the family is not well off. One relative says let him carry the consequences and learn the hard way. Another suggests calling the police or going to the media to expose the predatory platforms. The cousin himself is ashamed and desperate and has come to you for help.

scene: 你家乡的山区计划修建一座大型抽水蓄能电站，可以为周边城市提供稳定的清洁能源，减少对煤电的依赖。但电站需要淹没一个有着三百多年历史的古村落，村里还有几十户居民不愿搬迁，他们世代居住在此，祖坟和祠堂都将被水淹没。项目支持者说这是迈向碳中和的必经之路，反对者则认为「发展」不该以抹去文化根脉为代价。

options.t: 我会支持电站建设，同时要求开发商和政府对村民给予足额补偿，并将祠堂和有价值的老建筑整体迁建——发展总要付出代价，关键是怎么减损。
options.t_en: I would support building the station while requiring the developer and the government to compensate the villagers fully and relocate the lineage hall and valuable old buildings as whole structures. Development always has a cost; the question is how to reduce the loss.

options.t: 我会坚决反对这个项目，古村落是不可再生的文化遗产，能源方案有很多，但三百年的社区一旦拆散就再也回不来了。
options.t_en: I would firmly oppose the project. An ancient village is cultural heritage that cannot be regenerated, and there are many energy options, but once a three-hundred-year community is broken up it never comes back.

options.t: 我会主张重新选址，哪怕工程成本增加也要避开古村落，清洁能源和文化遗产不应该是零和博弈，技术上总有替代方案。
options.t_en: I would argue for choosing another site, even at higher engineering cost. Clean energy and cultural heritage should not be a zero-sum game; technically there are always alternatives.

options.t: 我觉得应该让全村公投决定，如果多数村民愿意接受补偿搬迁，那就推进；如果多数人反对，就暂停项目——外人没资格替他们决定。
options.t_en: I think the whole village should decide by referendum: if most villagers accept compensation and relocation, proceed; if most oppose, pause the project. Outsiders have no right to decide for them.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The mountains where you grew up are slated for a large pumped-storage hydropower station that would give nearby cities steady clean electricity and cut dependence on coal. But the reservoir would drown a village more than three hundred years old, and dozens of households refuse to move: they have lived there for generations, and their ancestral graves and lineage hall would go under water. Supporters call it a necessary step towards carbon neutrality; opponents say development should not be paid for by erasing a cultural root.

scene: 你所在的海滨城市遭遇五十年一遇的飓风，沿海低洼区的数千户居民房屋被淹。市政府宣布启动「气候移民」计划，提议将高风险区的居民整体迁往内陆新城，并补偿房产损失；但许多受灾者拒绝离开，他们世代住在这里，对土地有深厚感情，也担心补偿款不够在新城买房。同时，气象学家警告说未来这类极端天气会越来越频繁。

options.t: 我会支持强制搬迁，人命比房产重要，政府应该提供足够的安置住房和就业支持，对抗自然规律只会造成更大伤亡。
options.t_en: I will support compulsory relocation. Human lives matter more than property, and the government should provide enough replacement housing and employment support. Fighting the laws of nature only produces a higher death toll.

options.t: 我尊重不愿离开的居民，但我会建议政府在原址加高堤防、改善排水系统，让他们有选择留下的技术条件，而不是简单把人赶走。
options.t_en: I respect the residents who do not want to leave, but I will propose that the government raise the sea defences in place and improve drainage, so that they have the technical conditions to choose to stay, rather than simply driving people out.

options.t: 我觉得应该让居民自己决定，政府提供搬迁补偿和留下加固两个方案，各选各的，但以后如果再次受灾，留下者不能要求额外救济。
options.t_en: I think the residents should decide for themselves, with the government offering two schemes: compensated relocation, or help to strengthen their homes. Each household picks, but if disaster strikes again, those who stayed cannot ask for extra relief.

options.t: 我会主张把省下的救灾资金投给减排和全球气候谈判，飓风频率上升是气候变化的后果，不解决根源，今天迁这批人，明天还有下一批。
options.t_en: I will argue that the disaster money saved should go into emissions cuts and global climate negotiations. More frequent hurricanes are a consequence of climate change; if the root cause is not addressed, we move these people today and there will be another group tomorrow.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: The coastal city you live in has been hit by the worst hurricane in fifty years, and thousands of homes in the low-lying districts along the shore are underwater. The city government announces a climate migration programme: whole communities in the high-risk zone would move inland to a new town, with compensation for lost property. Many of the people affected refuse to go. Their families have lived here for generations, they are attached to the land, and they doubt the compensation will buy anything in the new town. Meteorologists warn that extreme weather of this kind will only become more frequent.

scene: 你公司的人力资源部推出一项「多元化招聘计划」，规定技术岗位下一批录用中至少30%要给来自欠发达地区的候选人，即便他们的技术测试平均分略低于其他竞争者。部门里有人支持，认为这能纠正历史上教育资源分配不公造成的结构性劣势；也有人反对，觉得这是对个人能力的不公评价，「出身」不该凌驾于「实力」之上。你是技术组长，团队成员就此争论不休。

options.t: 我会支持这个计划，技术能力不是天生的，而是教育机会堆出来的，给弱势群体补偿性的机会是对历史不公的矫正。
options.t_en: I would support the plan. Technical ability isn't innate; it's built out of educational opportunity. Giving disadvantaged groups compensatory chances is a correction of historical injustice.

options.t: 我会反对硬性配额，招聘应该只看能力和岗位匹配度，用出身标签决定录用本身就是歧视，最终会损害团队整体水平。
options.t_en: I would oppose a hard quota. Hiring should look only at ability and fit for the role. Deciding a hire by a label about someone's origins is itself discrimination, and in the end it lowers the whole team's level.

options.t: 我觉得问题出在评估标准太单一，我会建议增加「潜力评估」和「项目模拟」环节，让不同背景的候选人有更多维度展示自己，而不是简单降分录取。
options.t_en: I think the problem is that the assessment criteria are too narrow. I would suggest adding a potential assessment and a project simulation, so candidates from different backgrounds have more dimensions in which to show themselves, rather than simply lowering the bar.

options.t: 我主张公司先投资欠发达地区的编程教育和实习项目，从源头提升候选池质量，而不是在终点强行调整录取比例。
options.t_en: I would argue the company should first invest in programming education and internship programs in less developed regions, raising the quality of the candidate pool at the source, rather than forcibly adjusting the hiring ratio at the finish line.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: Your company's HR department has launched a diversity hiring plan: at least 30 percent of the next round of technical hires must go to candidates from less developed regions, even if their average technical test scores are somewhat below those of other applicants. Some in the department support it, saying it corrects the structural disadvantage left by unequal distribution of educational resources. Others oppose it, saying it judges individual ability unfairly and that where someone comes from should not outweigh what they can do. You are the technical team lead, and the team is arguing about it endlessly.

scene: 你住的老旧小区最近准备加装电梯，但一楼的住户坚决反对，认为电梯会遮挡采光、增加噪音，还可能让自家房产贬值。高层住户则说老人上下楼太困难，这是多数人的需求。居委会组织了几次协商都没达成一致，现在准备投票决定是否推进。你是住在三楼的中年业主，家里没有老人，但楼上有几位八十多岁的邻居每天爬楼梯气喘吁吁。

options.t: 我支持投票少数服从多数，电梯装了对整栋楼都好，一楼个别住户的反对不能阻挡大家改善生活的权利，补偿可以后续再谈。
options.t_en: I support a vote and majority rule. The lift benefits the whole building, and the objection of a few ground-floor households cannot block everyone else's right to a better life; compensation can be discussed afterwards.

options.t: 我反对强行推进，一楼的采光和权益是真实的损失，不能为了多数人的方便就牺牲少数人的利益，除非达成让所有楼层都满意的补偿方案。
options.t_en: I oppose forcing it through. The ground floor's light and interests are real losses, and the convenience of the majority should not come at the cost of the minority unless a compensation plan satisfies every floor.

options.t: 我倾向于装电梯，但建议先由物业或政府出一笔专项补贴补偿一楼住户，用经济补偿平衡利益冲突，而不是单纯靠投票压过去。
options.t_en: I lean towards installing the lift, but I suggest the property management or the government first provide a special subsidy to compensate the ground-floor household, balancing the conflict through money rather than simply outvoting them.

options.t: 我觉得这件事不该政府或居委会包办，业主们应该自己协商出一个市场化的方案，比如由高层住户集资给一楼合理补偿，自由交易比投票更公平。
options.t_en: I think this should not be run by the government or the residents' committee. Owners should negotiate a market-based solution among themselves, for example upper-floor households pooling money to compensate the ground floor properly. Free exchange is fairer than a vote.

options.t: 我无所谓装不装，反正我住三楼影响不大，不想卷入邻居们的纷争，谁赢了我都接受。
options.t_en: I do not mind either way. I live on the third floor and it barely affects me, and I do not want to be drawn into the neighbours' dispute. I will accept whoever wins.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Your old block is preparing to install a lift, and the ground-floor household is firmly against it: the lift would block their light, add noise and might cut the value of their flat. Upper-floor residents say the elderly can barely manage the stairs and that this is what most people need. The residents' committee has held several rounds of talks without agreement and is now preparing a vote. You are a middle-aged owner on the third floor with no elderly relatives at home, but several neighbours upstairs are over eighty and arrive breathless at every landing.

scene: 你是一家科技公司的中层管理者，公司近期推行996工作制（早九点到晚九点、每周六天），声称是为了赶在竞争对手前发布新产品。部分员工私下抱怨身心俱疲，有人已经偷偷在更新简历准备跳槽；但也有人表示理解，认为初创公司就是这样，熬过去就是元老。CEO暗示年度绩效和晋升会向更投入的人倾斜。你手下有刚结婚打算要孩子的员工，也有单身愿意拼的年轻人。

options.t: 我会严格执行公司制度，职场就是竞技场，想要高回报就得高付出，受不了的人可以离开，留下来的人自然会更优秀。
options.t_en: I will enforce the company's policy to the letter. The workplace is a competitive arena, and if you want the high reward you have to make the high commitment. People who cannot take it can leave, and those who stay will naturally be stronger.

options.t: 我会向上级反映员工的疲惫状况，建议至少保证每周一天完全休息，长期来看过劳反而降低效率、增加离职率，对公司和员工都得不偿失。
options.t_en: I will report the exhaustion upwards and argue for at least one full day off a week. Over the long run, burnout lowers output and raises turnover, so the company loses as much as the staff do.

options.t: 我会在团队内部尽量灵活处理，把不紧急的任务挪到正常工时，尽量不安排手下人加班，上面问起来我自己顶一部分。
options.t_en: I will handle it as flexibly as I can inside the team: push non-urgent tasks back into normal hours and avoid putting my people on overtime wherever possible, and cover part of it myself when the question comes down from above.

options.t: 我认为政府应该立法限制过度加班，不能全靠企业自觉，劳动者议价能力太弱，需要外部力量介入保护基本权益。
options.t_en: I think the government should legislate against excessive overtime rather than leaving it to companies' good faith. Workers have far too little bargaining power, and outside pressure is needed to protect basic rights.

options.t: 我支持多劳多得，但应该是自愿的公司可以设高额加班费吸引愿意加班的人，不愿意的按正常工时走，让市场来匹配不同人的选择。
options.t_en: I support rewarding effort, but it should be voluntary: the company can offer generous overtime pay to attract people who want it, and let others work normal hours, leaving the market to match different people's choices.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: You are a middle manager at a technology company that has just brought in 996 working: nine in the morning to nine at night, six days a week, on the argument that it is the only way to ship the new product before a competitor does. Some staff complain privately about being worn out, and a few are quietly updating their CVs. Others say they understand, that this is what a start-up is like and that those who last will be the old guard of the next stage. The CEO has hinted that annual ratings and promotion will tilt towards whoever puts in more. On your team you have people who have just married and are thinking about children, and single young people who are happy to grind.

scene: 你是一所大学的教授，最近学校在讨论是否应该邀请一位在社交媒体上频繁发表争议性政治观点的知名学者来校做公开讲座。这位学者的学术成就很高，但部分学生团体认为他的某些言论冒犯了弱势群体，联名要求学校取消邀请，并威胁如果学校不答应就会组织抗议、甚至可能中断讲座。校长征求你的意见。

options.t: 我坚决反对取消邀请，大学的使命就是思想碰撞，哪怕观点令人不适也应该在辩论中反驳，而不是用抗议堵别人的嘴。
options.t_en: I would firmly oppose canceling the invitation. A university exists for the clash of ideas. Even views that make people uncomfortable should be answered in debate, not silenced by protest.

options.t: 我支持学校审慎评估，如果这位学者的言论可能引发现场冲突甚至安全风险，学校有责任保护校园秩序，可以改为小范围闭门研讨。
options.t_en: I would support the school assessing it carefully. If the scholar's remarks could trigger confrontation on site or even a safety risk, the school has a duty to protect campus order, and could switch to a small closed-door seminar.

options.t: 我认为应该让师生投票决定，如果多数人反对就不请，毕竟公开讲座花的是学校的钱、占用的是公共资源，应该反映社区的主流意愿。
options.t_en: I think staff and students should vote on it. If the majority are against, don't invite him. A public lecture spends the school's money and occupies public resources, so it should reflect the community's prevailing wish.

options.t: 我会建议正常邀请，但同时组织一场对谈或辩论，让不同观点的人在同一个平台上交锋，用更多的言论来平衡争议言论，而不是禁言。
options.t_en: I would suggest inviting him as normal but also organizing a dialogue or debate, so that different views meet on the same platform. Answer controversial speech with more speech, not by shutting it down.

options.t: 我倾向于取消，校园应该是一个让人感到安全的空间，如果某些言论会对特定群体造成实质性伤害，学术自由不应该凌驾于学生的福祉之上。
options.t_en: I lean toward canceling. A campus should be a place where people feel safe. If certain statements cause real harm to a specific group, academic freedom should not take precedence over students' wellbeing.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: You are a university professor. The school is discussing whether to invite a well-known scholar who frequently posts controversial political views on social media to give a public lecture on campus. The scholar's academic record is strong, but some student groups say certain of his statements are offensive to vulnerable groups. They have submitted a joint petition demanding the invitation be withdrawn, and threatened to organize protests, possibly disrupting the lecture, if the school refuses. The president has asked for your opinion.

scene: 你所在的城市正在讨论是否对空置房屋征收惩罚性税收，以抑制投机炒房、增加住房供给。数据显示全市约有12%的住宅长期空置，而很多年轻人买不起房只能租房。房产业主协会强烈反对，称这是侵犯财产权、政府过度干预市场；支持者则认为住房是基本需求，不应该被当作投机工具，空置税的收入还可以用于建设保障性住房。你的家庭有两套住房，其中一套是父母留下的老房，目前无人居住。

options.t: 我支持征收空置税，房子是用来住的、不是用来炒的，用税收手段把闲置房源逼入市场，既能平抑租金也能增加政府收入建保障房，对多数人有利。
options.t_en: I support the vacancy tax. Housing is for living, not for speculation; using tax to push idle homes onto the market both steadies rents and raises revenue to build social housing, which benefits most people.

options.t: 我反对，这是我的合法财产，空不空是我自己的事，政府凭什么惩罚我？今天能征空置税，明天就能征其他税，财产权没有保障谁还敢投资？
options.t_en: I oppose it. This is my lawful property and whether it is empty is my own affair, so what right does the government have to punish me? If it can tax vacancy today it can tax something else tomorrow; with no security of property, who would invest?

options.t: 我觉得可以收，但标准要合理比如只针对拥有三套及以上住房的人，或者空置超过五年的，我这种继承的老房应该豁免，避免误伤普通中产。
options.t_en: I think it can be levied, but the criteria must be reasonable, for example only for owners of three or more homes or vacancies over five years. An inherited old flat like mine should be exempt, so that ordinary middle-class families are not caught.

options.t: 与其征税，不如放松土地供应和建筑限制，让市场自己增加供给，需求多了价格自然下来，政府干预往往是越管越乱。
options.t_en: Rather than taxing, loosen land supply and building restrictions and let the market add supply. With more supply prices will come down naturally; government intervention usually makes things messier.

options.t: 我认为应该把空置税和租金管制结合起来，强制空置房要么出租要么交税，政府用这笔钱大规模建设公共住房，逐步实现住房去商品化。
options.t_en: I think the vacancy tax should be combined with rent control: idle homes must either be let or taxed, and the government should use the money to build public housing on a large scale, gradually decommodifying housing.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Your city is debating a punitive tax on vacant homes to curb speculation and increase supply. Data shows about twelve percent of dwellings sit empty long term, while many young people cannot afford to buy and can only rent. The property owners' association is strongly opposed, calling it an attack on property rights and excessive state meddling in the market; supporters argue that housing is a basic need and should not be treated as a speculative instrument, and that the revenue could fund social housing. Your family owns two homes, one of them an old flat left by your parents that currently stands empty.

scene: 你是一家出口制造企业的负责人，主要生产电子元件。最近本国政府为了保护本土产业，对进口的关键原材料加征高额关税，宣称要把产业链留在国内。结果你企业的生产成本上涨了约25%，而主要竞争对手在邻国设厂、不受影响。你的大客户已经开始询价替代供应商。同时，政府推出了一些补贴本土企业的政策，但审批流程复杂、到位缓慢。

options.t: 我支持政府的保护主义政策，产业链安全比短期利润重要，哪怕现在苦一点，也要把关键产能留在国内，不能依赖外国。
options.t_en: I support the government's protectionist policy. Supply chain security matters more than short-term profit, and even if it hurts now, key capacity has to stay at home rather than depend on other countries.

options.t: 我反对关税保护，成本上升会让我们在国际市场上失去竞争力，客户跑了就很难回来；政府应该减税降本而不是加税。
options.t_en: I oppose tariff protection. Rising costs will cost us our competitiveness in international markets, and once customers leave they rarely come back. The government should be cutting taxes and costs, not adding to them.

options.t: 我理解保护本土产业的初衷，但政策应该更精准比如只补贴真正关键的战略产业，而不是一刀切加关税伤害下游制造企业。
options.t_en: I understand the intention of protecting domestic industry, but the policy should be far more precise, for example subsidising only the genuinely strategic sectors, instead of a blanket tariff that damages downstream manufacturers.

options.t: 我会考虑把部分产能转移到邻国去规避关税，企业首先要活下来，全球化分工是效率最优的选择，逆流而动只会被淘汰。
options.t_en: I will consider moving part of my capacity to a neighbouring country to get around the tariff. A company has to survive first, and the global division of labour is the most efficient arrangement; going against that only gets you eliminated.

options.t: 我认为政府应该在加关税的同时加快补贴落地，并且帮助企业做技术升级转型，而不是让企业独自承担政策成本。
options.t_en: I think the government should speed up delivery of the subsidies at the same time as imposing the tariff, and help firms upgrade their technology and restructure, instead of leaving them to carry the cost of the policy on their own.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: You run an export manufacturer making electronic components. To protect domestic industry, the government has just put a heavy tariff on imported key raw materials, saying it wants the supply chain kept inside the country. The result is that your production costs have risen by about twenty-five percent, while your main competitor, with a plant in a neighbouring country, is unaffected. Your biggest customer has already started asking other suppliers for quotes. The government has announced subsidies for domestic firms, but the approval process is complicated and the money arrives slowly.

scene: 你住的城郊区域发现了一种濒危鸟类的繁殖栖息地，环保组织要求政府将该区域划为自然保护区，禁止开发。但当地已经规划了大型物流中心，预计能创造两千多个就业岗位，附近很多居民指望着这个项目改善生计。政府组织了听证会，你是住在附近的一名普通上班族，平时周末会去那片湿地散步。

options.t: 我支持划为保护区，生物多样性是不可再生的，一旦破坏了多少钱都换不回来，就业问题可以通过发展生态旅游等绿色产业来解决。
options.t_en: I support designating it a reserve. Biodiversity is not renewable; once it is destroyed, no amount of money buys it back. The employment problem can be solved through green industries such as eco-tourism.

options.t: 我反对禁止开发，当地人要吃饭、孩子要上学，不能因为几只鸟就让两千人失去工作机会，人类的发展需求应该优先。
options.t_en: I oppose banning development. Local people need to eat and their children need to go to school. You can't cost two thousand people their jobs over a few birds. Human development needs should come first.

options.t: 我觉得可以折中缩小保护区范围，在边缘地带做严格环评的前提下允许物流中心建设，同时要求企业出资做生态补偿和修复。
options.t_en: I think there is a middle path: shrink the reserve, allow the logistics center at the edge subject to a strict environmental review, and require the company to fund ecological compensation and restoration.

options.t: 我认为应该让当地社区投票决定，这片地关系到大家的生计，环保人士可以游说但不能替本地人做决定。
options.t_en: I think the local community should vote on it. This land is tied to everyone's livelihood. Environmentalists can campaign, but they can't make the decision for the people who live here.

options.t: 我建议政府出钱把这块地买下来做保护区，同时给当地开发商在别处置换土地并给予税收优惠，用市场手段平衡保护和开发。
options.t_en: I would suggest the government buy the land for a reserve, and in exchange give the developer land elsewhere plus tax breaks, balancing protection and development through market means.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: A breeding habitat for an endangered bird species has been found in the suburban area where you live, and environmental groups are demanding that the government designate it a nature reserve and ban development. But a large logistics center has already been planned for the area, expected to create more than two thousand jobs, and many nearby residents are counting on the project to improve their livelihoods. The government has organized a hearing. You are an ordinary office worker living nearby who walks in that wetland on weekends.

scene: 你是一所公立高中的家长代表，学校正在讨论是否在课程中增加批判性思维与多元价值观选修课，内容包括分析不同政治体制的优缺点、讨论社会争议话题。部分家长热情支持，认为现在的孩子太缺乏独立思考能力；但也有家长强烈反对，担心孩子被洗脑或接触到不适合年龄的内容，要求学校只教正确的知识。校方很为难，想听听家长代表的意见。

options.t: 我强烈支持开设这门课，教育的目的是培养会思考的公民，不是制造听话的复读机，越不让孩子接触不同观点，他们长大后越容易盲从。
options.t_en: I strongly support the course. Education is meant to produce citizens who can think, not compliant repeaters. The less children encounter different views, the more likely they are to follow blindly as adults.

options.t: 我反对引入：高中生正处在形成判断力的阶段，我认为学校应先聚焦基础学科和稳定的价值引导，把争议性议题留到他们知识储备更充足之后再讨论。
options.t_en: I oppose introducing it. High school students are still forming their judgment, and I think schools should focus first on foundational subjects and stable value guidance, leaving contested issues until their knowledge base is fuller.

options.t: 我支持开设，但应该有年龄分级和内容审核，老师要接受专门培训，确保课堂是理性讨论而不是灌输特定立场。
options.t_en: I support it, but with age grading and content review, and teachers must be specially trained to ensure the classroom is rational discussion rather than instilling a particular position.

options.t: 我觉得这应该是家长的选择权学校可以开，但必须是选修，家长有权决定自己的孩子上不上的课，不能一刀切强制。
options.t_en: I think this should be the parents' choice. The school may offer it, but it must be elective, and parents have the right to decide whether their child takes it; it cannot be made compulsory across the board.

options.t: 我建议把这类课程放到大学再开，高中阶段还是以知识积累和考试准备为主，到了大学学生有更强的辨别能力再接触多元价值观更合适。
options.t_en: I suggest such courses be offered at university instead. The high school stage should focus on accumulating knowledge and preparing for exams; by university students have better discernment and are more ready for value pluralism.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: You are a parent representative at a public high school that is debating an elective on critical thinking and value pluralism, covering the strengths and weaknesses of different political systems and discussion of contested social issues. Some parents are enthusiastic, saying children today cannot think for themselves; others are strongly opposed, fearing indoctrination or age-inappropriate material, and want the school to teach only the correct knowledge. The school is torn and wants the parent representatives' views.

scene: 你所在的城市近年来接收了一批来自战乱地区的难民，政府为他们提供了临时住房和基础福利。现在两年过去了，部分难民已经找到工作融入社区，但也有一些因语言障碍和文化差异难以就业，靠福利生活。本地一些居民开始在社交媒体上抱怨我们的税收养外国人，要求政府停止接收新难民并缩减现有福利。而你所在社区恰好有几户难民家庭，他们的孩子和你孩子在同一所学校。

options.t: 我支持继续接收难民并加大融入支持，这些人逃离了战争，我们有道德义务帮助他们，长远来看多元文化也能让社会更丰富，不能因短期的经济成本就关闭大门。
options.t_en: I support continuing to take in refugees and increasing integration support. These people fled a war, and we have a moral duty to help. In the long run a mix of cultures makes a society richer too, and we should not shut the door because of a short-term economic cost.

options.t: 我反对继续接收，政府的职责是先保障本国公民的福利，资源有限的情况下应该优先帮助本地人，而不是把负担转嫁给纳税人。
options.t_en: I oppose taking in any more. The government's duty is to look after its own citizens first, and with limited resources local people should come first, rather than having the burden passed to taxpayers.

options.t: 我觉得可以接收，但要有条件难民必须参加语言培训和就业辅导，福利限期发放，逐步从救济转向自立，授人以渔比单纯发钱好。
options.t_en: I think we can take them, but with conditions: refugees must attend language training and job coaching, benefits are time-limited, and support gradually shifts from relief to self-reliance. Teaching someone to fish beats simply handing out money.

options.t: 我认为应该让民间慈善机构和宗教团体来承担主要的救助工作，政府只做最基本的协调，而不是用强制税收来支持，让愿意帮助的人自愿出力。
options.t_en: I think charities and religious groups should carry most of the relief work, with government doing only the basic coordination, rather than funding it through compulsory taxation. Let those who want to help give their help voluntarily.

options.t: 我主张更严格的筛选机制，只接收那些有技能、能快速就业的难民，同时把家庭团聚和技术移民名额向本地劳动力市场需求挂钩。
options.t_en: I argue for a stricter screening system: take only refugees with skills who can find work quickly, and tie family reunification and skilled migration places to what the local labour market actually needs.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Over the past two years your city has taken in a group of refugees from a war zone, and the government has provided temporary housing and basic benefits. Two years on, some have found work and settled into the community, while others remain unemployed because of language barriers and cultural differences and are living on benefits. Some local residents have started complaining on social media that our taxes are supporting foreigners, and are calling on the government to stop taking new arrivals and to cut the benefits that already exist. A few refugee families happen to live on your street, and their children go to the same school as yours.

scene: 你所在的城市最近宣布将在所有公共交通工具上安装AI人脸识别摄像头，理由是打击犯罪和提高反恐效率。官方承诺只用于抓捕通缉犯，数据会严格保密。但隐私倡导者担心这会变成大规模监控，普通人的行踪会被记录和分析；也有市民说我没做坏事就不怕拍。你是一名每天乘地铁通勤的律师，对严格保密的承诺持保留态度。

options.t: 我坚决反对在公共交通上安装人脸识别，隐私是基本权利，严格保密的承诺不可信，技术一旦部署就会被滥用，今天抓通缉犯明天就能追踪异见者。
options.t_en: I firmly oppose facial recognition on public transport. Privacy is a basic right, and a promise of strict confidentiality is not credible. Once the technology is deployed it will be abused: today it catches fugitives, tomorrow it can track dissidents.

options.t: 我支持安装，公共安全高于个人隐私，地铁人流密集是恐怖袭击和犯罪的高风险场所，AI监控能大大提高破案效率，保护的是所有人的安全。
options.t_en: I support installing it. Public safety outweighs individual privacy. Crowded subways are high-risk places for terrorism and crime, and AI monitoring can sharply improve the rate at which cases are solved, which protects everyone's safety.

options.t: 我支持安装，但要求独立机构监督数据使用，设置严格的调取审批程序，并且定期公布使用报告，让权力在阳光下运行。
options.t_en: I support installing it, but with independent bodies overseeing how the data is used, strict approval procedures for access, and regular public reports on usage, so that power operates in the open.

options.t: 我觉得与其全面监控，不如加强地铁的人工安检和巡逻，技术手段应该作为辅助而不是替代人力，减少对隐私的系统性侵犯。
options.t_en: I think that instead of blanket monitoring, we should strengthen human security checks and patrols in the subway. Technology should assist rather than replace people, and that reduces the systematic intrusion on privacy.

options.t: 我认为应该由市民公投决定，这种涉及所有人隐私的重大措施不应该由政府单方面推行，公众应该有知情权和决定权。
options.t_en: I think this should be decided by a public referendum. A measure that affects everyone's privacy should not be pushed through by the government unilaterally; the public has a right to know and a right to decide.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: Your city has announced that AI facial recognition cameras will be installed on all public transport, on the grounds of fighting crime and improving counterterrorism. Officials promise the system will only be used to catch wanted fugitives and that the data will be kept strictly confidential. Privacy advocates worry it amounts to mass surveillance, with ordinary people's movements recorded and analyzed. Some residents say they have nothing to hide if they have done nothing wrong. You are a lawyer who takes the subway to work every day, and you have your doubts about that promise of strict confidentiality.

scene: 你是一位有罕见病孩子的家长，这种病只有一种特效药，由一家跨国药企垄断生产，年治疗费用高达两百万元，不在医保报销范围内。你们家庭已经卖房举债坚持治疗了两年，现在债台高筑。最近你看到新闻，有国家通过强制许可让本土药企仿制该药，把价格压到原来的十分之一，但原研药企威胁要退出该国市场并停止新药研发投入。你正在考虑是否加入患者群体向政府施压的请愿行动。

options.t: 我会坚决加入请愿，要求政府启动强制许可，人命关天，药企的利润不能凌驾于患者的生存权之上，知识产权保护应该让位于基本人权。
options.t_en: I would join the petition firmly and demand that the government issue a compulsory licence. Lives are at stake; company profits cannot outrank patients' right to survive, and intellectual property protection should give way to basic human rights.

options.t: 我理解患者的困境，但强制许可会打击药企研发积极性，长远来看更少人愿意投资罕见病药物，最终伤害的是未来的患者，应该通过慈善和医保谈判解决。
options.t_en: I understand the patients' plight, but compulsory licensing would discourage pharmaceutical research, and in the long run fewer people would invest in rare disease drugs, hurting future patients. It should be solved through charity and insurance negotiation.

options.t: 我会支持请愿，但主张的诉求不是强制许可而是把该药纳入医保并提高报销比例，由政府医保基金和药企谈判定价，在保护创新和保障可及性之间找平衡。
options.t_en: I would support the petition, but the demand should not be a compulsory licence. It should be including the drug in insurance at a higher reimbursement rate, with the public insurer negotiating the price with the company, balancing protection of innovation against access.

options.t: 我认为应该允许个人通过正规渠道从已经实施强制许可的国家合法进口仿制药，政府睁一只眼闭一只眼，让患者有钱的活路、药企也有名义上的专利保护。
options.t_en: I think individuals should be allowed to legally import generics through proper channels from countries that have already issued compulsory licences, with the government turning a blind eye, leaving patients a way to live and companies a nominal patent.

options.t: 我会发起众筹并呼吁社会捐赠，同时推动罕见病专项基金的建立，用社会力量补充医保不足，而不是直接否定知识产权制度。
options.t_en: I would launch a crowdfunding campaign and call for public donations, while pushing for a dedicated rare disease fund, using social resources to fill the gaps in insurance rather than rejecting the intellectual property system outright.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: You are the parent of a child with a rare disease. There is only one effective drug, produced under monopoly by a multinational company, costing two million a year and outside insurance coverage. Your family has already sold a flat and borrowed heavily to keep the treatment going for two years, and is now deeply in debt. You have just read that another country issued a compulsory licence allowing local firms to make a generic version at a tenth of the price, and that the originator has threatened to leave that market and stop investing in new drugs. You are deciding whether to join a patients' petition pressing the government.

scene: 你所在公司的员工医疗保险方案面临续约，保险公司提出按性别分别定价：女性因生育相关医疗支出统计上更高，需多缴约15%；男性则在某些慢性病风险上保费略高。人力资源部对此分为两派：一方认为精算定价是数据驱动的公平，把真实成本摊到每个人头上反而让整体更便宜；另一方认为按性别收不同保费本身就是歧视，保险的意义就是把风险放到一个池子里共担。你必须给出立场。

options.t: 我会坚持统一保费，不分性别——保险的本质就是池化风险，按性别拆分等于让个人为自己无法改变的生理特征额外付费，这正是保险要消除的不确定性。
options.t_en: I will hold out for one premium regardless of sex. Insurance is by its nature the pooling of risk; splitting it by sex means charging people extra for a physical characteristic they cannot change, which is exactly the uncertainty insurance exists to remove.

options.t: 我会接受差异化定价，只要它基于真实精算数据——让所有人付一样的钱，其实是在用一方的钱补贴另一方，只是把差别藏起来了，透明比假装公平更诚实。
options.t_en: I will accept differentiated pricing, provided it rests on real actuarial data. Making everyone pay the same is in fact one group subsidising another, only with the difference hidden. Being transparent is more honest than pretending to be fair.

options.t: 我会提议由公司承担性别造成的保费差额，让员工自付部分完全一致——既尊重精算现实，又不让任何员工因为性别多掏腰包。
options.t_en: I will propose that the company absorb the difference created by sex, so that what employees pay out of pocket is exactly the same. It respects the actuarial reality without making any employee pay more because of their sex.

options.t: 我认为这是保险公司和企业之间的商业合同，市场自然会找到最优方案，不该用意识形态去干预定价逻辑。
options.t_en: I see this as a commercial contract between the insurer and the company, and the market will find the best arrangement on its own; ideology should not be used to override the logic of pricing.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: Your company's employee health insurance is up for renewal, and the insurer has proposed pricing by sex: women would pay about fifteen percent more, because medical spending related to childbirth is statistically higher, while men would pay slightly more for certain chronic disease risks. Human resources has split in two. One side says actuarial pricing is data-driven fairness, and that spreading the true cost across everyone actually makes the whole scheme cheaper. The other says charging different premiums by sex is discrimination in itself, and that the entire point of insurance is to put risk into one pool and share it. You have to take a position.

scene: 一家心理健康创业公司上线了AI情感陪伴聊天机器人，可提供全天候的认知行为疗法式对话，价格只有人类咨询师的十分之一，随叫随到。但它没有临床执照，不能做诊断，偶尔会给出令人不安的建议。一位付不起人类咨询师的大学生觉得它真的帮到了自己；一位持证心理学家警告它可能误导脆弱群体。是否需要监管成了焦点。

options.t: 我会支持要求任何提供心理健康建议的AI工具必须获得临床许可——不能让无照机器在脆弱人群身上练手，哪怕它便宜也不是借口。
options.t_en: I would support requiring any AI tool that offers mental health advice to hold a clinical license. Vulnerable people should not be where unlicensed machines practice, and being cheap is no excuse.

options.t: 我会允许它自由运营，但要求明确标注「非专业护理」——可负担的帮助总比没有帮助好，质量交给市场淘汰。
options.t_en: I would let it operate freely, but require it to be clearly labeled as not professional care. Affordable help is better than no help, and the market can sort out quality.

options.t: 我会支持分级制度：基础情感陪伴AI可以运行，但诊断和治疗计划必须有人类持证专家参与，哪怕远程接入也行。
options.t_en: I would support a tiered system: basic emotional companionship AI can operate, but diagnosis and treatment plans must involve a licensed human expert, even if only remotely.

options.t: 我对AI涉足心理健康整体持谨慎态度——对处于危机中的人来说误导的代价太高了，与其放任AI，不如把精力放在让人类护理变得可负担上。
options.t_en: I am cautious about AI in mental health overall. For someone in crisis, the cost of misleading advice is far too high. Rather than letting AI run loose, put the effort into making human care affordable.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: A mental health startup has launched an AI companion chatbot that offers round-the-clock cognitive behavioral therapy style conversation at a tenth of the price of a human counselor, available whenever you need it. But it holds no clinical license, cannot make a diagnosis, and occasionally gives disturbing advice. A university student who cannot afford a human counselor says it has genuinely helped. A licensed psychologist warns that it could mislead vulnerable people. Whether it needs regulation has become the focus of the argument.

scene: 一名政府分析师将机密文件泄露给记者，揭露了一项未经批准的秘密监控计划，该计划一直在系统性地收集公民通信数据。泄露证实了许多人长期怀疑的事情，但同时也暴露了正在进行的情报行动。分析师面临间谍罪起诉。公众舆论分裂：一派称其为揭露权力越界的英雄，另一派称其为违背保密誓言、危害国家安全行动的罪犯。

options.t: 我会视这位吹哨人为英雄——揭露未经授权的公民监控是公共服务，任何保密协议都不应覆盖违宪项目，该追究的是监控计划本身。
options.t_en: I would see the whistleblower as a hero. Exposing unauthorised surveillance of citizens is a public service, no confidentiality agreement should cover an unconstitutional programme, and what should be prosecuted is the surveillance itself.

options.t: 我会支持起诉——他签署了保密协议并违反了法律，动机不论多么高尚都不能凌驾于法律之上，合法的关切应通过监督渠道反映而非公开泄露。
options.t_en: I would support prosecution. He signed a confidentiality agreement and broke the law; however noble the motive, it cannot outrank the law, and lawful concerns should go through oversight channels rather than public leaks.

options.t: 我会支持在法律中设立公共利益辩护条款，允许吹哨人在独立法庭上为自己的行为辩护，由法庭权衡公共收益与安全损害。
options.t_en: I would support writing a public interest defence into the law, allowing whistleblowers to justify their actions before an independent court, which would weigh public benefit against security harm.

options.t: 我会把焦点放在修复监控计划本身，而不是追惩泄露者——真正的丑闻是未经授权的数据收集，起诉传信人只是转移视线。
options.t_en: I would focus on fixing the surveillance programme rather than punishing the leaker. The real scandal is unauthorised data collection; prosecuting the messenger only distracts attention.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: A government analyst leaked classified documents to a journalist, exposing an unauthorised secret surveillance programme that had been systematically collecting citizens' communications data. The leak confirmed what many had long suspected, but it also compromised ongoing intelligence operations. The analyst now faces espionage charges. Public opinion is split: one camp calls him a hero who exposed power overstepping its bounds, the other a criminal who broke a confidentiality oath and endangered national security work.

scene: 一位居民在申请官方身份证件时佩戴遮盖部分面部的宗教头饰，办证机关以「面部须完全可见以便识别」为由拒绝受理。该居民认为这一要求侵犯了宗教信仰自由，且存在替代验证手段（如额外照片、生物特征录入）。案件进入公开听证，行政统一性与宗教便利之间的张力摆在台面上。

options.t: 我会支持这位居民——信仰自由应通过替代验证来适应，而不是逼人违背信仰去拿一张塑料卡片。
options.t_en: I will side with the resident. Freedom of belief should be accommodated through alternative verification, not by forcing someone to act against their faith to obtain a piece of plastic.

options.t: 我会支持办证机关——身份证件必须显示面部，没有例外。给一个群体开口子，后面会涌来无穷的特殊要求，证件的公信力就没了。
