options.t_en: I will side with the issuing office. An identity document has to show the face, with no exceptions. Open a gap for one group and an endless stream of special requests follows, and the credibility of the document is gone.

options.t: 我会提议折中方案：允许佩戴头饰，但在数据库中存一张露脸照片供官方核验，卡片上印的可以是本人满意的照片。
options.t_en: I will propose a compromise: the head covering is allowed, but a photograph with the face uncovered is kept in the database for official verification, while the card itself can carry a photo the person is comfortable with.

options.t: 我认为国家根本不该要求公民随身携带带照片的身份证件，或者至少应把它设为自愿——强制身份识别本身就是一种控制手段。
options.t_en: I do not think the state should require citizens to carry photo identification at all, or at the very least it should be voluntary. Compulsory identification is itself a means of control.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A resident applies for an official identity document while wearing a religious head covering that conceals part of the face. The issuing office refuses the application on the grounds that the face must be fully visible for identification. The resident says the requirement infringes freedom of religion, and that alternative means of verification exist, such as additional photographs or biometric enrolment. The case goes to a public hearing, and the tension between administrative uniformity and religious accommodation is laid out on the table.

scene: 市政府宣布在一个中上收入街区建设200套保障性住房，以减少居住隔离、让低收入家庭能进入更好的学区和交通圈。当地居民迅速组织抗议，理由是房价会跌、学校会挤、街区氛围会被改变。规划局面临决定：按原方案推进、缩减规模、还是把项目移到地价更低的区域。

options.t: 我会坚决支持建设——居住融合是打破贫困循环的关键，富裕街区不应靠排挤保障房来独占好学校和好交通。
options.t_en: I would firmly support building it. Residential integration is the key to breaking the cycle of poverty, and wealthy neighborhoods should not monopolize good schools and good transit by shutting social housing out.

options.t: 我会支持当地居民——街区有权维护自己的居住品质和房价，政府不该用社会实验去覆盖本地居民的真实意愿。
options.t_en: I would side with the local residents. A neighborhood has a right to protect its living quality and its property values, and the government should not override the real wishes of the people who live there with a social experiment.

options.t: 我会支持缩减规模版本，同时要求开发商同步出资扩建学校和基础设施，让现有居民不承担改造成本。
options.t_en: I would support the scaled-down version, while requiring the developer to fund the expansion of schools and infrastructure at the same time, so that existing residents do not carry the cost of the change.

options.t: 我认为真正该做的是在所有片区按比例配建保障房，而不是硬塞进一个街区——分散建设才公平，也更容易被接受。
options.t_en: I think what should really be done is to require a proportional share of social housing in every district, rather than forcing it into one neighborhood. Dispersed building is fairer and easier to accept.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: The city government has announced two hundred units of social housing in an upper-middle-income neighborhood, to reduce residential segregation and let low-income families reach better schools and transit. Local residents quickly organized protests on the grounds that property values will fall, schools will be crowded and the character of the neighborhood will change. The planning bureau faces a decision: push ahead with the original plan, scale it down, or move the project to an area where land is cheaper.

scene: 食品安全监管机构正在审查是否批准实验室培养肉上市销售。生产商称其占用土地和水资源远少于传统畜牧、不产生动物粪便、无需屠宰，是食品生产的重大突破。传统畜牧户担心被颠覆，质疑「罐子里长出来的肉」是否安全、甚至算不算「食物」。消费者团体也分成了两派。

options.t: 我会支持全面批准——培养肉在动物福利和环境方面是巨大进步，拖延它只是保护既得利益者，代价是地球的。
options.t_en: I would support full approval. Cultivated meat is a huge advance for animal welfare and the environment, and delaying it only protects incumbents, at the planet's expense.

options.t: 我会反对批准，直到长期独立安全研究完成——我们还不知道吃几十年培养肉对健康的影响，把它匆忙推向市场是鲁莽的。
options.t_en: I would oppose approval until long-term independent safety studies are done. We do not yet know the health effects of eating cultivated meat for decades, and rushing it to market is reckless.

options.t: 我会支持批准但要求清晰标注，让消费者自主选择——市场在信息透明的前提下自然会区分出好产品和差产品。
options.t_en: I would support approval with clear labelling, letting consumers choose for themselves. Given transparency, the market will sort good products from bad.

options.t: 我会支持批准，但配套转型援助给将被淘汰的传统畜牧户——进步不应以牺牲农村生计为代价。
options.t_en: I would support approval, paired with transition assistance for livestock farmers who will be displaced. Progress should not come at the cost of rural livelihoods.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The food safety regulator is reviewing whether to approve cultivated meat for sale. Producers say it uses far less land and water than conventional livestock, produces no manure and requires no slaughter, a major breakthrough in food production. Livestock farmers fear being displaced and question whether meat grown in a tank is safe, or even counts as food. Consumer groups are split too.

scene: 一家已拥有本市最大报纸、三家电视台和主流新闻网站的传媒集团，提议收购最后一家独立本地电台。合并后该集团将控制本地约80%的新闻生产。反垄断监管机构必须决定：为维护媒体多元化而否决、为效率而批准、还是有条件批准。

options.t: 我会直接否决——当一个声音控制了一座城市80%的信息渠道，民主本身就处于危险之中，任何效率收益都不值得这个代价。
options.t_en: I will block it outright. When one voice controls eighty percent of a city's information channels, democracy itself is in danger, and no efficiency gain is worth that price.

options.t: 我会批准——消费者想要多元声音，互联网提供了无穷的替代选择。阻止合并只是用监管保护低效的在位者免受市场力量冲击。
options.t_en: I will clear it. Consumers who want a plurality of voices have an endless range of alternatives online. Blocking the merger is just using regulation to protect inefficient incumbents from market forces.

options.t: 我会附条件批准：要求集团剥离至少一家主要媒体 outlet，并为电台设立独立编辑委员会。
options.t_en: I will approve it with conditions: require the group to divest at least one major media outlet, and set up an independent editorial board for the radio station.

options.t: 我支持用公共资金扶持新的独立本地媒体来参与竞争，而不只是堵住合并——真正的问题是本地新闻在商业上活不下去。
options.t_en: I support using public money to help new independent local outlets compete, rather than only blocking the merger. The real problem is that local news cannot survive commercially.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A media group that already owns the city's largest newspaper, three television stations and the leading news website has proposed buying the last independent local radio station. After the merger the group would control roughly eighty percent of local news production. The antitrust regulator has to decide: block it to protect media pluralism, clear it on efficiency grounds, or approve it with conditions.

scene: 市政府提议在所有主要路口、交通枢纽和公共广场安装人脸识别摄像头，实时比对在逃人员数据库。警察局长说这将帮助抓捕暴力罪犯和寻找失踪儿童。隐私倡导者警告这等同于对所有人行动轨迹的永久监控，可能被滥用于政治追踪，且该技术在识别某些族群时存在偏差。市议会必须投票。

options.t: 我会投赞成——在公共场所不做亏心事就没什么好怕的，抓捕罪犯和寻找失踪者的安全收益值得付出代价。
options.t_en: I would vote yes. In public places, if you have done nothing wrong there is nothing to fear, and the safety gains of catching criminals and finding missing people are worth the cost.

options.t: 我会投反对——对每个人行动轨迹的持续生物识别跟踪是对自由的根本威胁，技术的偏差和滥用潜力都不可接受。
options.t_en: I would vote no. Continuous biometric tracking of everyone's movements is a fundamental threat to freedom, and the technology's bias and its potential for misuse are both unacceptable.

options.t: 我支持安装，但前提是严格设限：数据30天内删除除非关联到案件、接受独立审计、禁止用于匹配在逃人员以外的任何用途。
options.t_en: I support installing it, but only with strict limits: data deleted within thirty days unless tied to a case, independent audits, and a ban on any use other than matching wanted persons.

options.t: 我认为应该把资源投到社区警务和犯罪根源治理上，而不是建一套把每个公民当潜在嫌疑人的监控基础设施。
options.t_en: I think the resources should go into community policing and addressing the root causes of crime, not into building surveillance infrastructure that treats every citizen as a potential suspect.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: The city government proposes installing facial recognition cameras at all major intersections, transit hubs and public squares, matching them in real time against a database of wanted persons. The police chief says it will help catch violent criminals and find missing children. Privacy advocates warn it amounts to permanent surveillance of everyone's movements, could be misused for political tracking, and that the technology is biased in recognizing certain ethnic groups. The city council has to vote.

scene: 你所在国家的政府正在考虑是否批准一项大宗武器出口，买方是一个正处于边境冲突中的国家。该国称武器用于自卫，因为邻国已在边境集结军队。但人权组织提供了证据，证明该国曾将此前购买的武器用于针对平民。这笔出口将支撑国内数千个制造业岗位，但会助长一场域外冲突。议会必须做出决定。

options.t: 我会批准出口——它支撑国内产业和就业，我们对另一个主权国家如何使用设备不承担责任，拒绝只会把合同拱手让给竞争对手。
options.t_en: I would approve the export. It supports domestic industry and jobs, we are not responsible for how another sovereign state uses the equipment, and refusing would simply hand the contract to a competitor.

options.t: 我会否决出口——从可能被用于针对平民的武器中获利使我们成为共犯，不论经济效益如何，向活跃冲突区出口武器都应被禁止。
options.t_en: I would block the export. Profiting from weapons that may be used against civilians makes us complicit, and whatever the economic benefit, arms exports to an active conflict zone should be banned.

options.t: 我支持附条件批准：仅在配备最终用途监测、且保留在设备被用于针对平民时切断供应的权利时才能推进。
options.t_en: I support conditional approval: proceed only with end-use monitoring in place and the right to cut off supply if the equipment is used against civilians.

options.t: 我认为只应出口防御性装备——不卖进攻性武器——同时把国内制造产能转向民用技术。
options.t_en: I think only defensive equipment should be exported, no offensive weapons, while domestic manufacturing capacity shifts towards civilian technology.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: Your country's government is considering whether to approve a large arms export to a state in the middle of a border conflict. That state says the weapons are for self-defence, since its neighbour has massed troops on the frontier. But human rights groups have evidence that it used earlier purchases against civilians. The deal would support thousands of manufacturing jobs at home while fuelling a conflict abroad. Parliament must decide.

scene: 一种新型基因疗法可以治愈一种罕见遗传病，但每次治疗费用相当于一年平均工资。公共卫生系统必须决定：是否对全部约500名患者实行全民报销、只报销付不起的患者、还是留给商业保险和个人储蓄。全民覆盖将显著挤压现有医疗预算，但拒绝意味着有患者将因经济原因无法获得治愈。

options.t: 我会支持全民公费报销——任何人都不该因为价签而被拒绝治愈，集体医疗保障的意义恰恰在于为这种情况池化资源。
options.t_en: I will support full public coverage. Nobody should be denied a cure because of the price tag, and pooling resources for exactly this kind of case is what collective health cover is for.

options.t: 我会反对全民报销——这笔开支会挤占影响远多人群的常见病经费，艰难的预算取舍无法回避，不能为了500人牺牲数十万人的基本保障。
options.t_en: I will oppose universal coverage. This spending would take money away from common conditions that affect far more people, and hard budget trade-offs cannot be avoided. We cannot sacrifice the basic cover of hundreds of thousands for five hundred.

options.t: 我会支持按经济能力报销：公费系统为付不起的人买单，能支付的人走商业保险，把公共资金用到最需要的人身上。
options.t_en: I will support covering according to means: the public system pays for those who cannot afford it, those who can go through private insurance, so public money reaches the people who need it most.

options.t: 我会推动厂商谈判批量折扣，并探索国际联合采购把价格降下来，然后再谈覆盖方案——在定价合理之前不应仓促决定。
options.t_en: I will push for negotiating volume discounts with the manufacturer and exploring joint international procurement to bring the price down, and then talk about coverage. Nothing should be rushed before the price is reasonable.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A new gene therapy can cure a rare inherited disease, but each treatment costs the equivalent of an average year's salary. The public health system has to decide whether to cover all of the roughly five hundred patients, cover only those who cannot afford it, or leave it to private insurance and personal savings. Universal coverage would visibly squeeze the existing health budget; refusing means some patients will go without a cure for reasons of money alone.

scene: 米娅和丹尼尔订婚半年后，在一次家宴上，丹尼尔的父母把期望挑明了：按照家族传统，长子夫妇将来要住在父母附近，并成为他们晚年主要的照护者。丹尼尔表示认同，并提醒米娅：他的学费是父母付的，两人公寓的首付里也有父母的积蓄。而米娅在自己热爱的城市里打拼出了一番事业，她想象中的婚姻是两个平等的人自由协商彼此的义务，而不是原封不动地继承一份旧契约。婚期临近，两人必须决定这段婚姻究竟是什么：是一个把整个家族的诉求都吸纳进来的共同体，还是两个个体之间的约定——帮助亲人，凭的是选择与协商，而非默认条款。
scene_en: Mia and Daniel have been engaged for six months when, at a family dinner, Daniel's parents make their expectation explicit: following family tradition, the eldest son and his wife will live near them and eventually become their primary caregivers. Daniel agrees, reminding Mia that his parents paid his tuition and helped with the down payment on the couple's apartment. Mia has built a career she loves in a city two hundred kilometers away, and she imagined a marriage between two equals who renegotiate obligations freely rather than inherit them. As the wedding approaches, the couple must decide what their marriage will be: a union that absorbs the claims of the wider family, or a pact between two individuals who help relatives by choice and negotiation rather than by default.

options.t: 我会对米娅说：婚姻从来不只是两个人的契约，它联结的是两个家庭。父母用二十年的心血和积蓄供儿子读书、帮他付首付，晚年换回子女在身边是天经地义。接受这段婚姻，就意味着接受这份亲情带来的义务。搬过去不是妥协，而是守护家庭运转千百年来的方式。
options.t_en: I would tell Mia that marriage has never been a contract between two people alone; it joins families. Parents who spent twenty years and their savings on their son have earned proximity and care in return, and a spouse who accepts the marriage accepts its debts of gratitude. Moving is not surrender — it is keeping faith with how families have always worked.

options.t: 我会对丹尼尔说：没有人一出生就欠下一份既定的人生剧本。对父母的感恩是真的，但如果感恩必须按默认条款履行，那就成了绑架而不是爱。住多近、照顾谁、付出多少，应该由两个人自由商量，而且可以随时重新商量。一段以继承来的剧本开场的婚姻，只会在往后的岁月里积攒无声的怨恨。
options.t_en: I would tell Daniel that no one is born owing a life plan. Gratitude to parents is real, but gratitude expressed under threat of default is extortion, not love. Every couple must be free to decide — together, and revisably — how close to live, whom to care for, and at what cost. A marriage that begins with an inherited script will breed quiet resentment for decades.

options.t: 我会寻找中间路线：留在我们自己的城市和事业里，但承诺一份具体、不可讨价还价的支持计划——每月固定一笔钱、每晚视频、每月一个周末回去陪伴。义务可以用钱、用陪伴、用规划来履行，不一定非得靠住在一起。重要的是老人真正被照顾到，而不是租约上写着哪个地址。
options.t_en: I would look for the middle path: stay in our own city and careers, but commit to a concrete, non-negotiable schedule of support — a fixed monthly sum, video calls every evening, and one weekend a month in the parents' home. Duty can be honored in money, presence and planning, not only in proximity. What matters is that the elders are genuinely cared for, not which address appears on the lease.

options.t: 我会把问题上移一层：这种撕裂不该由小夫妻独自承受，体面的社会本该分担。我会去推动公共长期照护体系——居家护理员、日间照料中心、喘息服务——让成年子女不必在爱父母和成为全职护工之间二选一，让伴侣之间不必因为养老默认条款而牺牲彼此。
options.t_en: I would push the question upstream: couples should not be tearing each other apart over care that a decent society would fund. I would campaign for a public long-term-care system — home aides, day centers, respite care — so that adult children can love their parents without having to become their full-time nurses, and spouses can choose each other without defaulting into caregiving.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene: 奥卡福博士在研究所动物实验伦理委员会握有决定性一票。一个团队申请用约四千只小鼠和六十只灵长类动物，测试一种针对儿童脑癌的新疗法——这种癌的五年存活率不足两成。该化合物已在类器官和计算机模型中表现良好，但监管机构要求在任何患儿用药之前必须经过活体试验。动物保护人士指出，实验将造成长期痛苦，而现代替代方法已足够可靠。研究人员则反驳说，任何模型都还无法预测一个完整的活体，推迟就意味着本可获救的孩子死去。她必须在数千个有感知的生命与「拯救其中一些孩子的机会」之间做出权衡——那是一个机会，不是确定。
scene_en: Dr. Okafor holds the deciding vote on her institute's animal research board. A team is asking to run experiments on roughly 4,000 mice and 60 primates to test a promising therapy for a childhood brain cancer whose five-year survival rate is below twenty percent. The compound has already performed well in organoids and computer models, but regulators require live trials before any child can receive it. Animal advocates argue the experiments involve prolonged suffering and that modern alternatives are reliable enough to spare the animals. The researchers counter that no model yet predicts a whole living body, and that delaying means children who could have been treated will die. She must weigh thousands of sentient lives against a chance — not a certainty — of saving some of them.

options.t: 我会怀着沉重的心情批准这项研究。在模型还无法完全模拟一个活生生的孩子之前，残酷的算术就摆在那里：几千只小鼠和几十只灵长类，对面是五年存活率不到两成的孩子。我们明知故为地制造痛苦，这应该让我们寝食难安——而正因如此，我们更欠这些动物最高标准的福利保障。
options.t_en: I would approve the research with a heavy heart. Until our models can faithfully mimic a living child, the brutal arithmetic holds: thousands of mice and dozens of primates set against children with a one-in-five chance of seeing their tenth birthday. Suffering we cause deliberately should haunt us, and it is precisely because it haunts us that we owe the animals the strictest humane standards available.

options.t: 我会投反对票。有感知的生命不是实验器材，而「有机会，但不确定」恰恰是科学史上每一次过界行为所用的说辞。类器官、器官芯片和 AI 筛选技术每年都在进步；只要堵死旧捷径，资金和聪明才智就会更快流向替代方案。也许会有孩子在等待中离世——这场悲剧并不能授权我们去折磨其他生灵。
options.t_en: I would vote no. Sentient beings are not laboratory equipment, and 'a chance, not a certainty' is exactly the reasoning that has justified every excess in the history of science. Organoids, organ-on-chip systems and AI screening keep improving; if we forbid the old shortcut, money and ingenuity will flow into alternatives faster. Some children may die waiting — and that tragedy still does not license us to torture other creatures.

options.t: 我只批准一个大幅缩减的方案：用能得出统计学有效结论的最少动物数量、强制麻醉与人道终点、不打招呼的突击检查，以及一个有权中途叫停研究的独立监督委员会。科学之所以还能保有使用动物的权利，前提是把每只动物都当作需要逐案重新论证其痛苦是否正当的生命，而不是账面上一笔常设的开支。
options.t_en: I would approve only a sharply reduced protocol: the minimum number of animals that can yield a statistically meaningful answer, mandatory anesthesia and humane endpoints, unannounced inspections, and an independent review empowered to halt the study mid-course. Science keeps its license to use animals only by treating each one as a being whose suffering must be justified anew, case by case — not as a standing budget line.

options.t: 我会先问委员会一个不一样的问题：为什么一种如此罕见的儿童癌症会缺钱缺到要在这里争论四千只动物和六十只灵长类的地步？我会把票和条件绑定：要求设立一个国家资助的替代方法攻关计划，让十年后的委员会不必再面对这种表决。每一只动物都算数，改变制造这种困境的体制同样算数。
options.t_en: I would ask the board a different question first: why is a childhood cancer this rare so underfunded that 4,000 mice and 60 primates are even being debated? I would tie my vote to demanding a funded national program in alternative methods, so that in ten years no one faces this vote again. Each individual animal counts; so does changing the system that produces the dilemma.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene: 作为国家博物馆的理事，你要就馆里最负盛名的展馆投票表决：132 件青铜雕塑与饰板，是十九世纪一次殖民远征中劫掠而来。原属国的代表团已正式提出归还请求，称这些器物是从被焚毁的王宫里撕走的神圣祖先。馆长警告，归还可能让旗舰展厅空置、门票收入下滑，并为数千件其他藏品开启追索先例。桌面上的折中方案提议五年一续的借展、联合修复实验室，以及全部藏品的开放数字档案。你敬重的一位策展人低声说：博物馆的普世使命是真的，可入藏账册上的血也是真的。表决就在明天。
scene_en: As a trustee of the national museum, you must vote on the fate of its most celebrated gallery: 132 bronze sculptures and plaques seized during a nineteenth-century colonial expedition. A delegation from the country of origin has formally requested their return, describing the objects as sacred ancestors ripped from a burned palace. The museum director warns that repatriation could empty the flagship gallery, cut ticket revenue, and open claims on thousands of other objects. A compromise on the table proposes five-year renewable loans, joint conservation labs, and an open digital archive of every object. A curator you respect says quietly that the museum's universal mission is real — but so is the blood on the acquisition ledger. The vote is tomorrow.

options.t: 我会投无条件归还一票。博物馆的合法性建立在权属的清白之上，任何文物保护的理由都洗不干净一场焚城掠夺。这些东西从来不是收藏家意义上的「艺术品」，它们是一个族谱的载体，故乡社群的声索权不会因为过了一个世纪就过期。哪怕让展厅空上一年也无妨——就让那份空旷告诉大家帝国拿走了什么。
options.t_en: I would vote for full, unconditional return. A museum's legitimacy rests on the honesty of its ownership, and no conservation argument can launder a burned palace. These were never 'artworks' in the collectors' sense; they are records of a lineage, and their community's claim does not expire because a century has passed. Keep the gallery empty for a year if needed — let the emptiness teach what empire took.

options.t: 我主张藏品留在原地。无论当年获取的原罪是什么，如今它们属于一座全球性机构：每年六百万观众——其中不少正来自原属国——能在安保完备、恒温恒湿、免费开放的展厅里看到它们。世界性博物馆不是帝国的战利品，而是人类最接近共享殿堂的东西。若按国界把收藏瓜分殆尽，每一块碎片能对话的人只会更少。
options.t_en: I would vote to keep the collection where it is. Whatever the original sin of acquisition, the objects are now part of a global institution where six million people a year — many from the origin country itself — see them in a secure, climate-controlled, free-to-visit hall. Universal museums are not trophies of empire; they are the closest thing humanity has to shared civic temples. Divide the collection among national borders, and each fragment speaks to fewer people.

options.t: 我会支持「借展+数字档案」的折中方案，并把它做得更实：轮换展出让两地公众都能看到，资助原属国的学生来参与策展与修复，并用两种语言把那段暴力的获取史写在展厅墙上。过去无法被「取消偷窃」，但未来的守护权可以真正共享——这比单方面扣留或单方面归还都走得更远。
options.t_en: I would back the loan-and-archive compromise, and improve it: rotate the objects so both publics see them, fund students from the origin country to curate and conserve, and write the violent acquisition history onto the gallery wall in both languages. The past cannot be un-stolen, but the future custody can be genuinely shared — which is more than either unilateral keeping or unilateral returning achieves.

options.t: 我会按功能拆分处理：代表团指认为祖先之物的——宫廷饰板、纪念头像——立即归还；有据可查、当年确实经交易购得的器物留下。归还是修复，不是一场一刀切的仪式。每件文物离开故土的经过各有各的故事，假装它们共用同一个故事，本身就是另一种轻慢。
options.t_en: I would split the collection by function: the objects the delegation identifies as ancestral — court plaques, commemorative heads — go home now; documented trade goods purchased at the time stay. Restitution should be repair, not a blanket ritual. Each object has its own story of how it left, and pretending they all share one story is its own kind of disrespect.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene: 在国际田径联合会年度大会上，代表们就一项动议展开辩论：禁止昂贵的表现提升科技进入精英赛事——冷冻治疗舱、高原模拟帐篷、个性化碳纤维假肢，以及带能量回弹板的跑鞋。富国的体育项目主张：这些装备合法、安全，只是认真投资运动员的产物；穷国协会则反驳说，领奖台越来越是买来的，而不是拼来的——一个没有赞助商的天才短跑选手，如今正在输掉百分之几秒，也就是整段职业生涯。你握有决定票之一。禁令能让赛场公平，却会冻结创新、惩罚经营有方的项目，且在两百个国家几乎无法执行；放行则保住了对卓越的追求，却把不平等焊死在纪录簿里。
scene_en: At the annual congress of an international athletics federation, delegates debate a motion to ban expensive performance technologies from elite competition — cryotherapy chambers, altitude-simulation tents, personalized carbon-fibre prosthetics, and running shoes with energy-return plates. Wealthy national programs argue the gear is legal, safe and simply the fruit of investing seriously in athletes; poorer federations counter that podiums are increasingly bought rather than earned, and that a sprinter with world-class talent but no sponsor now loses hundredths of a second — entire careers — to equipment budgets. You hold one of the deciding votes. A ban would level the field but freeze innovation, punish well-run programs, and be nearly impossible to enforce across two hundred countries; keeping the technologies open preserves the pursuit of excellence but hardens inequality into the record books.

options.t: 我会投票支持禁令。体育与公众的契约是：成绩衡量的是人——训练、勇气、天赋——而不是采购预算。一旦最有钱的协会可以用钱买下那百分之几秒，起跑线本身就是歪的。执行起来会很麻烦，搞创新的会抱怨，这我承认；但公平从来就不图省事。
options.t_en: I would vote for the ban. Sport's contract with the public is that results measure humans — training, courage, talent — not procurement budgets. Once the richest federation can buy hundredths of a second, the starting line is already crooked. Yes, enforcement will be messy and some innovators will grumble; fairness was never supposed to be convenient.

options.t: 我会投票否决禁令。精英体育从来就没有过公平的赛场——营养、教练、医疗团队样样都要钱，怎么没人提议禁掉这些？装备合法又安全，惩罚那些肯为运动员投入的项目，惩罚的就是卓越本身。穷协会想竞争，出路是拉赞助、建培养体系，而不是把前沿往回拖。
options.t_en: I would vote the ban down. Elite sport has never been a level field — nutrition, coaching and medical teams all cost money, and no one proposes banning those. The gear is legal and safe; punishing programs that invest in their athletes punishes excellence itself. If a poorer federation wants to compete, the answer is sponsorship and development funds, not dragging the frontier backward.

options.t: 我会动议修改提案：技术保持合法，但对最富有的项目征收一笔小额「技术发展费」，汇入共享装备基金，保证每一位打进决赛的运动员都能用上同代装备。让前沿继续前进——也让每一个凭实力站上跑道的选手，穿着同等水平的鞋站上去。
options.t_en: I would amend the motion: keep the technologies legal, but levy a small federation-wide technology fee on the richest programs into a pooled equipment fund that guarantees every qualified finalist access to the same generation of gear. Let the frontier advance — and let everyone who earns a lane stand on it with equivalent shoes.

options.t: 我会提议把赛事一分为二：一个开放的「无限制组」，任何安全的技术都放行；一个传统组，对装备设严格上限——就像方程式赛车与古典车赛并存。观众和运动员可以自己选择敬畏哪一种竞技，我们也用不着再假装一份规则能同时裁判人本主义者与工程师。
options.t_en: I would propose splitting the sport: an open 'unlimited' class where any safe technology goes, and a traditional class with strict equipment caps — like formula racing alongside classic motoring. Fans and athletes can choose which contest deserves their awe, and we stop pretending a single rulebook can referee both the humanists and the engineers.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene: 七十八岁的母亲确诊早期失智症后，三兄妹聚在她家的餐桌旁商量接下来的安排。大哥主张把她送进一家口碑很好的照护机构，全天候有专业人员值守，卖掉老宅支付费用——他称之为「诚实的选择」，因为硬撑着在家照护，迟早以一场危机收场。二姐坚持认为，母亲离开熟悉的一切会衰退得更快，提议兄妹轮流停薪留职在家照护。弟弟建议请住家护理员，让母亲留在自己的房子里，但费用会在四年内耗尽她的养老金和兄妹积蓄的一半。母亲在清醒的时刻只说了一句：她不愿成为负担，也同样不愿消失在「一栋满是陌生人的楼里」。
scene_en: After their 78-year-old mother is diagnosed with early-stage dementia, three siblings gather at her kitchen table to plan what comes next. The eldest wants to move her into a well-reviewed residential facility with round-the-clock staff, selling the family house to cover the fees — 'the honest option,' he calls it, because pretending to manage at home will end in a crisis. The middle sister insists their mother would fade faster among strangers and proposes rotating home care, each sibling taking unpaid leave in shifts. The youngest suggests a live-in aide while keeping their mother in her own house, though the cost would exhaust her pension and half the siblings' combined savings within four years. Their mother, in a lucid moment, says only that she refuses to become a burden — and equally refuses to disappear into 'a building full of strangers.'

options.t: 我会选择机构，而且不粉饰这个决定。训练有素的护理员、夜班有人值守、有康复师，而不是儿子凌晨三点狼狈地独自硬撑——专业照护不等于抛弃，撑不住的业余照护才会出事。我常去看她，带着清醒的头脑和充沛的心力，这比睡不好觉地守在隔壁房间更有价值。
options.t_en: I would choose the facility, and stop dressing it up. Trained staff, awake night shifts, physiotherapists — not a son quietly failing at three in the morning. Professional care is not abandonment; exhausted amateur care is how people get hurt. Visiting often, with a clear head and a full heart, is worth more to her than my poorly slept presence in the next room.

options.t: 我会值我的班。母亲用了三十年送我们上学、陪我们进医院、扶我们熬过失恋——家庭里的照护账本本来就不是用现金结清的。轮班居家照护当然苦，累工作、缺睡眠，但她能守着自己的水壶、自己的花园、窗外熟悉的风景——失智症老人在熟悉的生活里，能把「自己」保持得更久。有些债，只能用陪伴来还。
options.t_en: I would take the shifts. Our mother spent thirty years getting us to school, to hospitals, through heartbreak; the ledger of care in a family is not meant to be settled in cash. Rotating home care is hard on careers and sleep, but she keeps her kettle, her garden, her view — and dementia patients keep their selves longer inside the lives they recognize. Some debts you pay in presence.

options.t: 我会选居家请护理员这条路，因为只有它让母亲继续做自己日子里的主人——她自己的门、自己的钥匙、想看的电视自己选。钱就是为这种时候准备的：一生的积蓄是用来买有尊严的最后一章的，不是留作遗产的。剩下的费用我们兄妹按各自能力分摊，并且每半年随着她的病情变化重新商量一次。
options.t_en: I would back the aide-at-home plan, because it is the only option that keeps her the author of her own days — her door, her keys, her choice of television. The money is for exactly this: a life's savings exist to buy a dignified last chapter, not to bequeath. We siblings share the remaining cost in proportion to what we can each spare, and we revisit the plan every six months as her condition changes.

options.t: 我会对兄姐说：我们在这张餐桌上算的这笔账，才是真正的丑闻。这个国家的每个家庭都在私下里带着同样的悲伤重算同一笔账。我要加入全民长期照护保险的倡导运动——用一个公共资金池支付护理员、日间中心和机构费用——让「父母如何被照顾」不再由这个家庭存款的位数来决定。
options.t_en: I would tell my siblings that our kitchen-table arithmetic is the real scandal. Every family in this country is re-running this same calculation in private grief. I would join the campaign for universal long-term-care insurance — a public pool that pays for aides, day centers and facilities — so that the question of how a parent is cared for stops being decided by the number of digits in the family's savings.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene: 你在一家非营利债务咨询中心做咨询师。一位三十四岁的外卖骑手坐在你对面：负债相当于十一个月的收入，摊在四个「先买后付」应用、三张信用卡和一笔年化三位数的发薪日贷款上。其中一部分付了母亲的医药费，还有一些买了一部手机和一台游戏机——他觉得孩子们辛苦一年后理应得到这些。正式的债务减免项目可以勾销一半欠款，但代价是六年无法获得信贷。个人破产申请几乎能清偿全部债务，却有公开记录、背负沉重污名，房东也已开始旁敲侧击。他抬起头问你该怎么办，还小声问了一句：那个不断借钱给他的系统，是不是才该被指责。
scene_en: You are a counselor at a nonprofit debt-advice center. A 34-year-old delivery driver sits across from you with debts equal to eleven months of his income, spread across four 'buy now, pay later' apps, three credit cards, and a payday loan compounding at triple-digit interest. Some of it covered his mother's hospital bills; some bought a phone and a game console he felt his kids deserved after a hard year. A formal debt-relief program would erase half the balance but freeze his access to credit for six years. A personal-insolvency filing would clear almost everything but is publicly recorded, carries heavy stigma, and his landlord has begun asking questions. He looks up and asks what he should do — and, quietly, whether the system that kept offering him credit is the one that should be blamed.

options.t: 我会建议他申请个人破产。放贷方早就把他违约的风险算进了三位数的利率里——他们放贷时就预期会有人倒下，并且已经提前为这份风险收了钱。破产法存在的意义，正是让人可以破产而不被摧毁。孩子们需要的是一个还能正常生活的父亲，而不是一份漂亮的信用记录；污名褪去的速度，远比债务磨掉的速度快。
options.t_en: I would tell him to take the insolvency. The lenders priced his default into those triple-digit rates; they lent expecting some borrowers to break, and were paid for that risk in advance. Insolvency law exists precisely so that a person can be bankrupt without being destroyed. His children need a father with a functioning life more than a clean credit file; the stigma will fade faster than the debt would.

options.t: 我会先和他一起制定还款计划。协议是他亲手签的，承诺就是承诺，哪怕对面是一台写满掠夺性条款的机器。重组债务、把利率谈下来、卖掉游戏机、用五年还清——因为「从债务面前走开」这个习惯一旦养成，代价高过任何利率。债务减免项目可以做桥，但不能是终点。
options.t_en: I would build him a repayment plan before anything else. He signed those agreements, and a promise is a promise even when the counterparty is a machine with predatory fine print. Restructure, negotiate the interest down, sell the console, and pay it back over five years — because the habit of walking away from debts, once learned, costs more than any interest rate. The relief program can be a bridge, not the destination.

options.t: 我会征得他同意，把他这份档案隐去姓名后送到立法机构。对一个挣最低工资的人放出年化百分之三百的高利贷，不是平等主体之间的合同，而是一台把绝望转化为收益率的机器。他的案子需要的是利率上限、放贷前的偿付能力审查，以及让「先买后付」应用接受和银行同样的监管。一对一的咨询，救不了接下来的一百万份同样的档案。
options.t_en: I would take his file — with his permission, name removed — to the legislature. A payday loan at three hundred percent interest to a man on minimum wage is not a contract between equals; it is a machine for converting desperation into yield. His case calls for an interest-rate cap, affordability checks before credit is extended, and 'buy now, pay later' apps brought under the same rules as banks. One-on-one advice will not stop the next million files like his.

options.t: 我会推荐中间道路：申请债务减免项目，一半勾销、信用冻结六年——并把冻结重新解释为庇护而不是惩罚。六年不能借贷，也就是六年不能再把坑挖深；剩下的一半，他可以有尊严地按还得起的节奏偿还，让孩子亲眼看到他把欠的钱还完。全额偿还会压垮他，全额破产会给他贴上标签。
options.t_en: I would recommend the middle road: the debt-relief program — half erased, credit frozen for six years — with the freeze reframed as shelter, not punishment. Six years without borrowing is six years in which he cannot dig the hole deeper, and the surviving half he can service with dignity at a pace that lets his kids watch him finish what he owes. Full repayment would break him; full insolvency would label him.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene: 一个快速工业化的沿海地区每逢夏季轮流停电，同时背负着十五年内排放减半的国家指标。能源主管机构召集市民咨询委员会为三个方案排序，你是委员之一。方案 A：一批小型模块化核反应堆——近零碳、全天候，但造价高、审批慢，且十年前一场国外核事故的阴影仍在。方案 B：数吉瓦的风光电站加电网级储能——单位电量最便宜、上马最快，但要占用大量农田与荒漠栖息地，且在漫长的无风阴周里电网照样吃紧。方案 C：扩建现有燃气电厂——快速可靠，但等于锁定几十年的排放和对进口燃料的依赖。委员会的排序分量不轻；而四个月后，停电季就会回来。
scene_en: A rapidly industrializing coastal region faces rolling blackouts each summer and a national mandate to cut emissions in half within fifteen years. The energy authority convenes a citizens' advisory panel, on which you serve, to rank three options. Option A: a fleet of small modular nuclear reactors — near-zero carbon and always-on, but expensive, slow to license, and haunted by a foreign reactor accident a decade ago. Option B: several gigawatts of solar and wind farms plus grid-scale batteries — the cheapest power per unit and quick to build, but consuming farmland and desert habitat, and leaving the region exposed during long windless, overcast weeks. Option C: expand the existing gas-fired plant — fast and dependable, but locking in decades of emissions and dependence on imported fuel. The panel's ranking carries real weight; the blackouts return in four months.

options.t: 我会把核反应堆排在第一位。气候的算术不近人情：一个到 2040 年还靠燃气保供的电网，就是一个完不成指标的电网，而电池至今扛不住连绵无风的两周。小型模块化反应堆具有非能动安全性，阻碍它的那种恐惧，本来就是对着上一代电站校准出来的。贵吗？贵。但应对一场紧急状态，哪个严肃的方案不贵？
options.t_en: I would rank the reactors first. Climate arithmetic is unforgiving: a grid still burning gas for dependability in 2040 is a grid that fails its mandate, and batteries still cannot carry a windless fortnight. Small modular designs are passively safe, and the fear that stalls them was calibrated to an older generation of plants. Expensive? Yes. So is every serious response to an emergency.

options.t: 我会把可再生能源排在第一位，不只是因为便宜。屋顶的光伏、归风机脚下的城镇共同持有的风电份额、每个变电站里的电池：一个去中心化的电网就算出事，也是一小块一小块地坏，而不是一瞬间全灭。是的，租用农地必须谨慎，无风的季节也还得让燃气顶一阵——但电池技术每年都在进步，这座桥每年都在变短。
options.t_en: I would rank renewables first, and not only for the price. Solar panels on rooftops, wind shares owned by the towns beneath the turbines, batteries in every substation: a decentralized grid fails gracefully, in pieces, instead of catastrophically all at once. Yes, farmland must be leased carefully, and gas must back up the still weeks — but the battery chemistry improves every year, and every year the bridge gets shorter.

options.t: 我会把扩建燃气排在第一位，并把不便明说的话说出口：医院、水泵和冷链疫苗不是靠意愿运转的。反应堆十年内拿不到许可，可再生能源眼下还扛不住无风的一周，但燃气轮机能在下个停电季到来之前转起来。排放是笔严肃的债——而所有的债，都得先站稳脚跟再还，而不是在轮流停电里还。
options.t_en: I would rank gas expansion first and say the quiet part aloud: hospitals, water pumps and cold-chain vaccines do not run on intentions. The reactors will not be licensed for a decade, the renewables cannot yet carry a windless week, but the gas turbines can be spinning before the next blackout season. Emissions are a serious debt — and like all debts, you service it from a position of stability, not from inside a rolling outage.

options.t: 我会把三个选项都排在没人提的第四个选项后面：少用。工业需求响应合同、严苛到不近人情的建筑能效标准、贵到足以改变行为的晚高峰动态电价，加上节能改造的融资支持。最便宜、最快、最干净的每一兆瓦，都是从未被需求的每一兆瓦。发电方式最终躲不开——但一个不肯动自己用电曲线的地区，吵的这些电站将来一座也省不下。
options.t_en: I would rank all three below the option nobody tabled: use less. Industrial demand-response contracts, brutal efficiency standards for buildings, dynamic pricing that makes the evening peak expensive enough to shift behavior, and financing for retrofits. The cheapest, fastest, cleanest megawatt is the one never demanded. Generation choices are unavoidable in the end — but a region that refuses to touch its consumption curve will need every one of the plants it is arguing about.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene: 河畔小镇哈威克七年里被淹了三次，一次比一次损失惨重，中央政府给了它一次性的选择。方案一：加高堤防并建泵站，可保护大多数住宅约四十年，主要由国家拨款，但每户需终身缴纳维护费，还要把一线河滨花园让给混凝土。方案二：自愿收购——政府按灾前估值买下易涝房屋，并资助家庭迁往高处——小镇因此缩水三分之一，两所学校关闭，哈威克延续两百年的河畔社区认同就此终结。镇民大会上，一批年长的居民干脆两个都拒绝，坚称这条河历来有涨有落，搬走的邻居就是散了的邻居。话筒传到你手里，你有一分钟。
scene_en: The river town of Harwick has flooded three times in seven years, each disaster costlier than the last, and the national government has offered a one-time choice. Plan One: a raised levee and pump system protecting most homes for perhaps forty years, funded largely by a national grant, but requiring every household to pay a lifelong maintenance levy and ceding a strip of riverfront gardens to concrete. Plan Two: a voluntary buyout — the state purchases flood-prone homes at pre-disaster value and helps families relocate uphill — shrinking the town by a third, closing two schools, and ending Harwick's two-hundred-year identity as a river community. At the town hall, an older faction simply refuses both, insisting the river has always risen and always fallen, and that neighbors who leave are neighbors lost. You have one minute at the microphone.

options.t: 我会发言支持修堤。两百年的小镇史不是可有可无的爱好；它是码头、节庆、祖坟和生计的总和，搬不到山上去。加固堤防昂贵而不完美——四十年也不是永远——但与河流谈判，这座镇子历来靠的就是工程。必要时把河滨花园浇上混凝土也认了；一个交出河岸的镇子，其实已经开始溶解了。
options.t_en: I would speak for the levee. Two hundred years of town history is not a hobby; it is an inheritance of docks, festivals, graves and livelihoods that cannot be relocated uphill. Fortifying is expensive and imperfect — forty years is not forever — but engineering has always been how this town negotiated with the river. Pave the gardens if we must; a town that surrenders its riverfront has already begun to dissolve.

options.t: 我会发言支持政府收购，尽管说这话很痛。对抗一条正在上涨的河，等于订购一份按期送达的悲伤：交维护费、失去花园，四十年后水照样赢——只是那时已没有补偿。趁现在按灾前估值成交、整建制地搬上山、还住同几条街，是所有结局里唯一能保住「哈威克人」这个整体的方案。社区的定义是邻居，不是洪泛区；选邻居。
options.t_en: I would speak for the buyout, however much it hurts. Fighting a rising river is a subscription to grief: pay the levy, lose the gardens, and in forty years the water wins anyway — only then without compensation. Taking pre-disaster value now and relocating uphill together — as a town, to the same streets — is the only ending that keeps Harwick's people intact. A community is its neighbors, not its floodplain; choose the neighbors.

options.t: 我会在话筒前把两个方案都拒绝。收购案是拿我们自己的灾难给我们付账；修堤案是抵押我们的花园，买断我们已不再做主的四十年。想卖的人尽管卖；留下的人就像历代农人那样接受这条河——沙袋、诚实的保险、邻居的船。不是每种风险都需要一个国家方案；有些风险，就是住在你祖辈住过的地方的代价。
options.t_en: I would refuse both plans from the microphone. The buyout pays us with our own tragedy, and the levee mortgages our gardens to buy forty years of a life we no longer own. Let those who want to sell, sell; those who stay accept the water as farmers always have — with sandbags, honest insurance, and neighbors' boats. Not every risk needs a state solution; some are simply the terms of living where your people lived.

options.t: 我会用这一分钟换掉问题本身：凭什么像哈威克这样的小镇，要为一堵墙终身交费？制造这些暴雨的排放大多发生在别处、由盈利的产业排出。我会动议：镇里接受修堤——但附带条件，加入洪泛区小镇联盟，要求设立永久的国家级气候补偿基金，资金来自对高碳产业本身征收的附加费。适应的账单，应该寄给造成适应需求的人。
options.t_en: I would use my minute to change the question: why should a town of Harwick's means pay a lifelong levy for a wall at all? The emissions that loaded these storms were mostly released elsewhere, by industries that profited. I would move that the town accept the levee — on condition of joining a coalition of floodplain towns demanding a permanent national climate-compensation fund, financed by a levy of its own on carbon-intensive industry. Adaptation should be billed to those who caused the adapting.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene: 作为政策顾问，你要为部长写一页纸的建议，关于一项法案：要求所有社交平台在开户前用政府颁发的身份证件核验用户年龄，目的是让未成年人远离成瘾式信息流和猎食者。儿童保护组织支持法案，列举了有据可查的伤害。安全研究者则警告：这将废除所有人的匿名权，让举报人、家暴幸存者和不受欢迎的少数群体暴露于报复之下；而把身份与账号关联的中央数据库一旦建立，泄漏只是时间问题——这类数据库从无例外。平台提出折中方案：隐私保护的年龄验证——用密码学证明用户已成年而不记录其身份——对边缘个案不够精准，但什么都不收集，也就无物可失。表决在两周后；部长只信你的判断。
scene_en: As a policy adviser, you must give your minister a one-page recommendation on a bill requiring every social platform to verify users' ages with government-issued ID before accounts can be opened — the aim: keep minors off addictive feeds and out of predators' reach. Child-safety organizations endorse it, citing documented harm. Security researchers warn it abolishes anonymity for everyone, exposing whistleblowers, abuse survivors and unpopular minorities to retaliation, and that a central database linking identities to accounts will eventually leak, as such databases always have. The platforms counter-propose privacy-preserving age verification — cryptography that proves a user is an adult without recording who they are — imperfect for edge cases, but collecting nothing that can be stolen or subpoenaed. The vote is in two weeks; the minister trusts your judgment.

options.t: 我会建议支持该法案。匿名是一种舒适，孩子的安全才是利害攸关。最需要躲在未验证账号后面的那些人——骚扰者、猎食者、敲诈者——恰恰是这块面具最不该保护的人。数据库的风险是待解决的工程问题，而「国家可能滥用」这种论证，一旦同样套用到我们早已信任的其他登记系统上，就不攻自破。
options.t_en: I would recommend supporting the bill. Anonymity is a comfort; a child's safety is a stake. The people who most need to hide behind unverified accounts — harassers, predators, blackmailers — are precisely the ones the mask serves worst to protect us from. The database risks are engineering problems to be managed, and 'the state might misuse it' is an argument that dissolves the moment it is applied to every other registry we already trust with far more.

options.t: 我会建议明确反对。举报人、敌意家庭屋顶下的异见少年、互相辨认的受虐幸存者、暴露即危险的少数群体——对他们而言，匿名不是舒适，而是活命的基础设施。而且把每个公民映射到每个账号的单一数据库，不是可以「缓解」的风险，而是抽屉里上膛的武器，等着一届意图更坏的政府。对孩子的伤害有些是真的；但没有哪一条，足以成为造这个抽屉的理由。
options.t_en: I would recommend opposing it flatly. Whistleblowers, dissident teenagers under hostile roofs, abuse survivors finding each other, minorities for whom visibility means danger — for all of them, anonymity is not comfort but survival infrastructure. And a single database mapping every citizen to every account is not a risk to be mitigated; it is a loaded weapon in a drawer, waiting for a future government with worse intentions. Some harms to children are real; none of them justifies building that drawer.

options.t: 我会建议把平台方的反提案写进法律：强制采用隐私保护的年龄验证——用密码学证明「已成年」而不存储身份——并资助一个独立审计机构为各方案认证。当然会有边缘个案漏网，青少年年龄估计也不完美；那就定好责任、逐步迭代。但设计原则必须守住：国家应当能核实「关于我们的事实」，而不是就此为我们建档。
options.t_en: I would recommend writing the platforms' counter-proposal into law: mandate privacy-preserving age verification — cryptographic proofs that establish adulthood without storing identity — and fund an independent audit body to certify the schemes. Edge cases will slip through, and estimating teenagers' ages is imperfect; set liability and iterate. But the design principle holds: the state should be able to verify facts about us without compiling files on us.

options.t: 我会建议把三种方案全部否掉，把责任移交给平台和家长：法律强制「儿童安全默认设置」——未成年人不得使用算法推荐流、单次使用时长硬性封顶、提供真正可用的家长控制——并让平台为违规担责，就像车企必须为安全带担责那样。查身份证把孩子当成国家的筛查问题；而真正危害他们的成瘾机器是产品设计的选择，产品设计的选择就该在设计环节被监管。
options.t_en: I would reject all three framings and move the duty onto platforms and parents: legally mandated kid-safe defaults — no algorithmic feeds for minors, hard caps on session length, real parental controls — with platforms liable for violations, the way carmakers are liable for seatbelts. ID checks treat children as a state-screening problem; the addiction machinery that endangers them is a product-design choice, and product-design choices should be regulated at the point of design.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene: 在某个山区省份，仍会说维利语的不足八千人，且大多年过五十。地区教育部门提议在本地小学开设可选的双语班：半天国语、半天维利语，由最后一代流利使用者执教，作为试点资助四年。支持者称之为这门千年语言最后的现实机会——连同织在其中的认同、歌谣与亲属称谓。反对者——包括一些说维利语的家长——则认为，课时是稀缺资源，花在维利语上就是从英语和国语里扣走的，那才是改变命运的通行证；文化传承的学费，不该由这个社区的孩子们来交。你是一个一年级孩子的家长，报名会就在今晚。
scene_en: In a mountain province, fewer than eight thousand people still speak Vellish, most of them over fifty. The regional education authority proposes an optional bilingual track at the local primary school: half the day in the national language, half in Vellish, taught by the last generation of fluent teachers, subsidized as a four-year pilot. Supporters call it the last realistic chance for a thousand-year-old language and the identity, songs and kinship terms woven into it. Opponents — including some Vellish-speaking parents — argue that classroom hours are hours not spent on English and the national language, the real currencies of mobility, and that the community's children should not pay the tuition for cultural preservation. You are the parent of a first-grader; the enrollment meeting is tonight.

options.t: 我会给孩子报名，并在会上发言支持。语言不是一门课，而是一种切分世界的方式——亲属称谓、天气、幽默、上千首歌——语言死去时，那座档案馆会一起烧掉。英语孩子任何下午都能从屏幕里学到；维利语却只能从最后一批用它做梦的人身上「接住」。对她未来的孙辈而言，一年用维利语度过的课间，比任何一次考试的分数都值钱。
options.t_en: I would enroll my child and speak for the track. A language is not a school subject; it is a way of parsing the world — kinship, weather, humor, a thousand songs — and when it dies, the archive burns with it. My child can learn English from a screen any afternoon; Vellish can only be caught from the last people who dream in it. A year of playgrounds in Vellish is worth more to her grandchildren than any exam score.

options.t: 我会让孩子留在普通班——怀着敬意，但不道歉。祖母的语言在我心里是爱，歌谣我会在家里传下去——但课时是孩子手里最稀缺的资源，我不会把它花在一种只剩八千位老人使用的语言上。评判她那一代的，将是工作与科学的语言；父母的职责是递给她仍然锋利的工具，而不是让她背负传家宝。
options.t_en: I would keep my child in the standard track — with respect, and without apology. My grandmother's language lives in me as love, and I will pass on the songs at home; but school hours are the scarcest resource my child owns, and I will not spend them on a language with eight thousand aging speakers. Her generation will be judged by the languages of work and science, and a parent's job is to hand her tools that still cut, not heirlooms to carry.

options.t: 我会支持这个双语班，并且推得更远——把它变成常设项目，按其他科目同等标准拨款，并培训年轻流利使用者、付给他们真正的薪水。一个随最后一代教师一同到期的四年试点不是保护，是一场带预算的告别仪式。如果国家把维利语定为区域官方语言，学校、法院和诊所就都必须说它——活下去的关键是被需要，而不是被记得。
options.t_en: I would support the track and push it further — make it permanent, funded like any other subject, with teacher training that pays young fluent speakers a real salary. A four-year pilot that expires with the last teachers is not preservation; it is a farewell ceremony with a budget line. If the state recognized Vellish as an official regional language, schools, courts and clinics would have to speak it too — and survival means being needed, not merely remembered.

options.t: 我会提议改办周末社区学堂：由流利的长辈在周六教歌谣、讲故事、练会话，发一份适度津贴，正常课时则保持不动。文化传承应该由背负文化的人自己选择，由社群与支持者出资，绝不该强加进七岁孩子的课程表。如果孩子们因为快乐而来，这门语言就有机会；如果他们因为被迫而来，它其实已经死了。
options.t_en: I would propose weekend community schools instead: fluent elders teaching songs, storytelling and conversation on Saturdays for a modest stipend, with the school day left intact. Preservation should be chosen by those who carry the culture, funded by the community and its allies, and never imposed through the timetable of seven-year-olds. If the children come because it is joyful, the language has a chance; if they come because it is compulsory, it is already dying.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene: 建于上世纪八十年代的锦华里小区没有电梯，六楼七十多岁的周老先生每周下楼的次数越来越少。楼内十二户中有八户同意加装电梯并平摊费用，一楼两户坚决反对：施工将遮挡采光、产生噪音，且认为电梯主要让高层受益、拉低一层房价。调解会开了三次无果，高层住户开始讨论动用业主大会多数表决强行推进，一楼住户则威胁诉诸法院。作为业委会成员之一，你需要在这场邻里僵局中表明立场。

options.t: 我会支持以三分之二多数表决推进：这是共有楼体的公共改善，不能让两户否决八户的迫切需求。程序合法、补偿合理即可动工，长期拖延对高龄住户是实实在在的伤害。
options.t_en: I would support pushing it through by a two-thirds majority. This is a shared improvement to a jointly owned building, and two households should not be able to veto the urgent needs of eight. With a lawful procedure and reasonable compensation, work can start; dragging it out is doing real harm to the elderly residents.

options.t: 我会反对多数强制：加装电梯不是维修而是改建，实质改变了各户的产权利益格局。除非一楼住户自愿同意并获得充分补偿，否则任何表决都只是被合法化的多数压力。
options.t_en: I would oppose forcing it through by majority. Installing an elevator is not maintenance but reconstruction, and it materially changes the property interests of each household. Unless the ground-floor households agree voluntarily and are fully compensated, any vote is just majority pressure with a legal stamp on it.

options.t: 我会推动一个精细的分摊方案：按楼层递增分摊费用，高层多出、低层少出甚至获得现金补偿，并由公共适老化改造基金补贴一部分，把一楼的实际损失压到最低再谈表决。
options.t_en: I would push for a finely calibrated cost-sharing plan: costs rising by floor, with upper floors paying more and lower floors paying less or even receiving cash compensation, part of it covered by a public fund for age-friendly renovation. Get the ground floor's actual loss down to the minimum first, then talk about a vote.

options.t: 我会建议先请街道牵头做独立评估和听证，把采光、噪音、房价影响的客观数据摆出来，再组织一次正式投票——让决定建立在事实而非情绪对抗上，落败的一方也更容易接受结果。
options.t_en: I would suggest asking the subdistrict office to lead an independent assessment and hearing first, laying out objective data on light, noise and property values, and then hold a formal vote. Let the decision rest on facts rather than emotional confrontation, and the losing side will find the result easier to accept.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: Jinhuali, a residential compound built in the 1980s, has no elevators, and Mr. Zhou, who is over seventy and lives on the sixth floor, goes downstairs less and less often. Eight of the twelve households in the building agree to install an elevator and split the cost. The two households on the ground floor are firmly opposed: the construction will block their light and create noise, and they argue the elevator mainly benefits the upper floors while lowering the value of the first floor. Three mediation meetings have ended without agreement. The upper-floor households are now discussing forcing it through by majority vote at the owners' assembly, and the ground-floor households are threatening to go to court. As a member of the owners' committee, you have to take a position in this neighborhood deadlock.

scene: 河畔社区的绿化带里聚集了四十多只流浪猫，源于多年来的无序繁殖。退休教师林阿姨每天定点投喂，爱猫的居民自发凑钱做了部分绝育；但投诉也在增多：车棚里的抓痕、翻倒的垃圾桶、清晨的叫声，还有观鸟的居民拿出照片，指认流浪猫捕食了社区里仅剩的几窝雏鸟。物业贴出通告要求停止投喂并考虑集中收容处理，喂猫派与投诉派在业主群里激烈对峙。你在群里被点名征求意见。

options.t: 我会主张由公共经费支持「捕捉—绝育—放归」：既承认猫已是社区既成的一部分，也终结无序繁殖，配合登记和定点投喂管理。这是同情心与秩序可以兼得的方案，但需要财政和专业机构介入。
options.t_en: I would argue for publicly funded trap-neuter-return. It acknowledges that the cats are already part of the neighbourhood while ending unchecked breeding, paired with registration and managed feeding points. It is a way to have both compassion and order, though it needs public money and professional agencies.

options.t: 我会支持物业的集中收容处理：城市生态系统容不下这个规模的流浪猫，雏鸟和刺猬的消失不是情绪问题而是生态事实。对猫的善意不该以本地野生动物的消亡为代价，收容后限期领养、无人认领的妥善处置才是负责任。
options.t_en: I would support the property manager's round-up. An urban ecosystem cannot carry stray cats at this scale, and the loss of fledglings and hedgehogs is an ecological fact, not a matter of sentiment. Kindness to cats should not be paid for with the extinction of local wildlife; responsibility means rehoming within a deadline and humane handling of the unclaimed.

options.t: 我会认为这是居民自治的范围，公共资金不应介入：爱猫者自己出钱绝育投喂，厌猫者自行驱赶防护，物业只管公共卫生底线。谁也不必用道德绑架谁，社区问题社区自己消化。
options.t_en: I would treat this as a matter for residents' self-governance, with no public money involved. Cat lovers pay for neutering and feeding themselves, those who dislike cats protect their own property, and the property manager enforces only the public health baseline. No one should morally blackmail anyone else; the community should absorb its own problems.

options.t: 我会提议把它变成社区共建项目：把固定喂食点改造成管理规范的「猫屋」，由志愿者轮值、费用众筹、绝育进度公示，同时给车棚装防护条。让治理顺着已有的热情长出来，而不是靠一纸通告扑灭它。
options.t_en: I would propose turning it into a community co-building project: convert the fixed feeding points into properly managed cat shelters with volunteers on rotation, crowdfunded costs, published neutering progress, and protective strips fitted in the bicycle shed. Let the governance grow out of the enthusiasm that already exists instead of being stamped out by a notice.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: More than forty stray cats have gathered in the green belt of the riverside neighbourhood, the result of years of unchecked breeding. Retired teacher Auntie Lin feeds them at fixed times each day, and cat lovers have pooled money to neuter some of them. But complaints are mounting: scratches in the bicycle shed, overturned bins, dawn yowling, and birdwatchers have produced photographs identifying the cats as the predators of the last few clutches of fledglings. The property manager has posted a notice demanding that feeding stop and is considering rounding the cats up for shelter. The feeders and the complainers are at open war in the owners' group chat, and you have been named and asked for your view.

scene: 恒远科技的创始人宣布引入「271」绩效制度：每季度给全员强制分布打分，末位百分之十进入改进期，两轮垫底即解除合同。他引用行业标杆公司的先例，称「付高薪就要有高标准」。人力资源总监私下统计后发现，被淘汰的大多是入职不满两年的年轻员工和需要接送孩子的中年员工，而几个业绩平庸但资历深的老臣安然无恙。作为管理层会议的一员，你必须表态。

options.t: 我会支持推行：市场竞争不相信温情，强制分布逼出了标杆公司的效率，组织的活力恰恰来自流动。真正的问题是执行要公平——评估标准公开、申诉渠道畅通，让淘汰的是低绩效而不是资历浅。
options.t_en: I will support rolling it out. Market competition has no room for sentiment, and forced distribution is what produced the efficiency at those benchmark firms; an organisation's vitality comes precisely from people moving through it. The real issue is fair execution: publish the criteria, keep appeals open, and make sure it is low performance being weeded out rather than short tenure.

options.t: 我会反对强制排名：团队产出依赖信任与互助，一旦同事变成竞争对手，谁还愿意分享经验、帮人救火？我们高价招来的工程师最后会互相提防。绩效管理应该对事不对排名，协作文化被破坏的代价远高于那百分之十的「活力」。
options.t_en: I will oppose forced ranking. Team output depends on trust and mutual help; once colleagues become rivals, who is going to share what they know or step in when someone is drowning? The engineers we paid so much to hire will end up watching each other. Performance management should be about the work, not about the ranking, and the cost of destroying a collaborative culture is far higher than that ten percent of vitality.

options.t: 我会支持改革绩效体系，但换成另一种：取消强制分布，改为目标透明、频繁反馈，表现持续不达标者进入转岗或退出流程。要的是「没有混日子的角落」，而不是每季度必须找出一批人来垫底。
options.t_en: I will support reforming the performance system, but into something else: drop forced distribution, move to transparent goals and frequent feedback, and put people whose performance stays below standard into a transfer or exit process. What we need is no corner where someone can coast, not a rule that requires a batch of people to be found at the bottom every quarter.

options.t: 我会主张先划清劳动者保护的边界：绩效淘汰会把经营风险转嫁给员工。我会推动与工会协商，要求改进期保留培训、转岗优先权和体面的补偿方案，制度可以有竞争，但底线要写进集体合同。
options.t_en: I will argue for drawing the boundary of worker protection first: performance-based dismissal shifts business risk onto employees. I will push for talks with the union, requiring training during the improvement period, priority in transfers, and a decent severance package. A system can be competitive, but the floor has to be written into the collective agreement.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: The founder of Hengyuan Technology has announced a 271 performance system: every quarter all staff are force-ranked, the bottom ten percent enter an improvement period, and two consecutive bottom placings end the contract. He cites benchmark companies and says that if you pay high salaries you have to set high standards. The HR director runs the numbers privately and finds that most of those pushed out are young employees with less than two years' service and middle-aged staff who have to pick up their children, while a few long-serving veterans with mediocre results are untouched. As a member of the management meeting, you have to take a stand.

scene: 云驰平台的算法上个月把同城订单的每公里单价下调了百分之十四，理由是「提升派单效率、增强竞争力」。三千多名网约车司机中有人发起在某日早高峰集体下线，声浪迅速扩散。平台运营负责人警告：拒单和下线会影响服务分，长期「低活跃」账号可能被永久停止派单；司机群里则流传着一份各家平台的单价对比表。你的表哥开了六年网约车，房贷还剩九年，他问你该怎么办。

options.t: 我会支持司机们组织起来：单个司机对算法毫无议价能力，只有集体行动才构成真正的谈判筹码。应该趁此推动司机工会的合法化，把单价规则、抽成上限、账号封禁程序都摆上谈判桌，这比单日下线重要得多。
options.t_en: I would support the drivers organizing. A single driver has no bargaining power against an algorithm; only collective action is real leverage. This is the moment to push for legal recognition of a drivers' union, and to put the pricing rules, the commission ceiling and the account suspension procedure on the table. That matters far more than one day offline.

options.t: 我会劝他照常出车：平台降价多半是因为竞争加剧和供需变化，价格是市场信号。如果云驰的分成确实不合理，司机会流失到对手平台，算法自会修正；用集体行动对抗价格规律，最后可能两头落空。
options.t_en: I would tell him to keep driving as usual. The price cut is mostly a result of stronger competition and shifting supply and demand; price is a market signal. If Yunchi's cut is genuinely unreasonable, drivers will drift to rival platforms and the algorithm will correct itself. Fighting the law of price with collective action may end up losing on both fronts.

options.t: 我会主张监管介入规则本身：要求平台公开派单与计价算法逻辑、设定抽成上限、封号前须人工申诉复核。司机可以接受市场波动的收入，但不能接受连规则都看不见的黑箱——这是数字时代的劳动保护。
options.t_en: I would argue for regulators to step into the rules themselves: require platforms to disclose the logic of their dispatch and pricing algorithms, set a ceiling on commission, and require human review on appeal before an account is suspended. Drivers can accept income that moves with the market, but not a black box whose rules they cannot even see. This is labor protection for the digital age.

options.t: 我会建议司机们做长线打算：把这次下线当作一次表态，但真正的出路是积累议价数据——行程成本、时薪、事故率——用平台式的工具反向组织信息，让每一轮博弈都建立在证据上，而非情绪上。
options.t_en: I would advise the drivers to think long term. Treat this offline action as a statement, but the real way out is building up bargaining data: trip costs, hourly earnings, accident rates. Use platform-style tools to organize information in reverse, so that every round of negotiation rests on evidence rather than emotion.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Last month the Yunchi platform cut the per-kilometer price of in-city orders by fourteen percent, citing improved dispatch efficiency and competitiveness. Some of its more than three thousand ride-hailing drivers have called for going offline together during one morning rush hour, and the call has spread fast. The platform's operations head warns that refusing orders and going offline will hurt service scores, and that accounts that stay inactive for a long time may be permanently cut off from dispatch. Meanwhile a price comparison table for the various platforms is circulating in the drivers' group chats. Your cousin has driven for six years and has nine years left on his mortgage. He asks you what he should do.

scene: 大学社科院邀请了一位以主张「能力分组教育」闻名的学者来做年度公开讲座，他的研究被批评者指为给阶层歧视提供学术包装。学生会在公告下发起联署，要求校方取消邀请，签名者认为校园不应为伤害性观点提供讲台；另一部分学生和多数教师则联署反对取消，称这是学术自由的原则问题。讲座还有十天，校长办公室请你所在的议事会成员各自提交书面意见。

options.t: 我会写：讲座必须照常举行。大学的意义就在于让最难听的观点也能在阳光下被检验，取消邀请只会把观点赶进回音壁里发酵。同时我会支持学生会申请对谈环节和充分提问时间，用更严格的辩论回应他。
options.t_en: I would write: the lecture must go ahead. The point of a university is that even the most objectionable views can be tested in the open, and cancelling only drives them into an echo chamber to ferment. At the same time I would support the student union's request for a dialogue session and ample question time, answering him with tougher debate.

options.t: 我会写：校方应取消这场讲座。学术自由不等于任何观点都有权占用学校的年度讲台，邀请本身就是一种背书。对他的研究感兴趣的师生完全可以读论文、办内部研讨，公开讲座面向全校，平台的选择应当慎重。
options.t_en: I would write: the university should cancel. Academic freedom does not mean any view has the right to occupy the university's annual lecture, and the invitation itself is an endorsement. Students and staff interested in his work can read the papers and hold internal seminars; a public lecture is open to the whole university, and the choice of platform should be made carefully.

options.t: 我会写：讲座照常，但形式改为注册制学术研讨，听众限相关院系并全程记录。既不向「必须取消」的压力让步，也不把最有争议的观点直接推向大众传播场域——区分学术讨论与公共讲台，是成熟机构应有的分寸。
options.t_en: I would write: the lecture goes ahead, but as a registered academic seminar limited to relevant departments and fully recorded. Neither yield to the pressure to cancel nor push the most contested views straight into mass media; distinguishing academic discussion from a public platform is the tact a mature institution should have.

options.t: 我会写：我反对邀请，但更反对取消。程序正义在于：邀请由学术委员会按既定标准作出，就应由同一程序审查是否撤销；议事会不该因联署人数多少改写规则。这一次忍住不破例，将来才保护得住不受欢迎的少数。
options.t_en: I would write: I oppose the invitation but oppose cancellation more. Procedural justice means that if the invitation was made by the academic committee under established criteria, the same procedure should decide whether to withdraw it; the council should not rewrite the rules according to how many signatures a petition gathers. Restraining ourselves from making an exception now is what protects unpopular minorities later.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: The university's social science faculty has invited a scholar famous for advocating ability-grouped education, whose work critics describe as academic dressing for class discrimination. The student union has started a petition under the announcement demanding that the invitation be withdrawn; signatories argue that the campus should not provide a platform for harmful views. Another group of students and most of the teaching staff have signed a counter-petition, calling it a question of academic freedom. The lecture is in ten days, and the vice-chancellor's office has asked members of your council to submit written opinions.

scene: 小说家程芜花了七年写完一部以某段动荡年代为背景的长篇，虚构了一座小城在运动、饥荒与整肃中的三年。出版社终审提出：涉及历史的段落需整体删除或改为「天灾」，两位主要人物的命运必须改写，否则无法通过重大选题备案。编辑私下表示遗憾，称「能出版的版本」和「你想写的版本」之间隔着一整套流程。程芜在深夜的朋友圈发了一句「删还是不删」，你看到了。

options.t: 我会劝她拒绝删改：文学为无名者保存记忆，正是历史叙述最需要个人视角的时刻。宁可暂不出版，把完整手稿存档、寻求译介到海外，或者等待时机。一个作家一辈子能有一次机会写这样的东西，不该亲手拆掉它。
options.t_en: I will urge her to refuse. Literature keeps the memory of people who were never named, and this is exactly the moment when historical narrative most needs an individual eye. Better not to publish for now: archive the complete manuscript, look for translation abroad, or wait. A writer gets one chance in a lifetime to write something like this, and she should not take it apart with her own hands.

options.t: 我会劝她接受修改后出版：一部删改后仍有力量的小说，好过一部完整却无人能读的手稿。让书以任何形态进入读者的世界，记忆的线索就断不了；完全的诚实可以留在日记和档案里，等后人去拼。
options.t_en: I will urge her to accept the cuts and publish. A novel that still has force after editing is better than a complete manuscript nobody can read. Get the book into readers' hands in whatever form and the thread of memory stays unbroken; complete honesty can wait in diaries and archives for later generations to piece together.

options.t: 我会建议第三条路：这家出版社是唯一选择吗？民营出版、电子书、有声书、连载，传播的形态早已多元化。与其在备案流程里反复自我审查，不如重估作品的出版路径，把「删还是不删」换成「在哪里和读者见面」。
options.t_en: I will suggest a third path: is this publisher the only option? Independent presses, ebooks, audiobooks, serialisation, the forms of publication diversified long ago. Rather than going round and round in self-censorship through a filing process, reassess the route to publication and replace 'cut or not cut' with 'where do I meet my readers'.

options.t: 我会提醒她考虑更现实的层面：作者要生活，编辑要担责，出版社几十号人的生计都压在选题上。她可以坚持完整版另寻出路，但不必把同意修改的同行钉上耻辱柱——表达自由的成本，不该只由最弱的一环承担。
options.t_en: I will remind her to weigh the more practical side: the writer has to live, the editor carries responsibility, and the livelihoods of dozens of people at the publisher rest on which titles get approved. She can insist on finding another route for the complete version, but she need not nail colleagues who agree to revise to a pillar of shame. The cost of free expression should not fall only on the weakest link.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The novelist Cheng Wu spent seven years writing a long novel set in a turbulent era, inventing a small town and following it through three years of campaigns, famine and purge. The publisher's final review comes back with demands: the passages dealing with history must be cut entirely or recast as natural disaster, and the fates of the two main characters must be rewritten, or the book cannot clear the major-title filing process. The editor says privately that they are sorry, that between the version that can be published and the version you wanted to write lies an entire procedure. Late at night Cheng Wu posts one line: cut, or not cut. You see it.

scene: 财政委员会就遗产税改革举行听证。现行制度下，一对企业家夫妇留给独生女的股份与房产，经信托安排后实际税负不足百分之五；而统计显示，最富的十分之一家庭传承的财富，已相当于最穷一半家庭总财富的数倍。反对者强调财富是税后所得的再积累，重复征税惩罚勤俭与创业；支持者则称，起点不平等正在让「出身」重新成为命运的支配变量。听证记录员把话筒递给了你。

options.t: 我会主张大幅提高累进遗产税，并对信托、赠与、离岸架构一揽子堵漏：这笔税源定向投入学前教育与全民医疗，让每一代的起点向中间收拢。遗产税针对的不是奋斗，而是「生在罗马」的世袭优势。
options.t_en: I would argue for a sharply higher progressive inheritance tax, and for closing the loopholes in trusts, gifts and offshore structures in one package. Direct the revenue into preschool education and universal health care, so that each generation's starting point moves toward the middle. The inheritance tax is not aimed at hard work; it is aimed at the inherited advantage of being born at the finish line.

options.t: 我会主张维持低税负：财富已完成一道所得税，身后再征一遍是对财产处分权的二次侵犯；且家族企业的股权被迫出售缴税，往往意味着裁员与产业收缩。一个社会若总在惩罚积累，最后惩罚的是所有人。
options.t_en: I would argue for keeping the burden low. The wealth has already paid income tax once, and taxing it again at death is a second infringement on the right to dispose of one's property. And when family firms are forced to sell shares to pay the tax, it often means layoffs and industrial contraction. A society that keeps punishing accumulation ends up punishing everyone.

options.t: 我会支持调高税率，但对经营性资产设豁免与递延：企业股份只要持续经营、员工不减，可以缓缴甚至抵免；纯金融资产与多套房产从严征收。既打断食利阶层的固化，又不伤及创造就业的实体。
options.t_en: I would support a higher rate, but with an exemption and deferral for operating assets. Shares in a business that keeps operating and keeps its employees can defer or even offset the tax; purely financial assets and multiple properties are taxed strictly. That breaks the entrenchment of a rentier class without wounding the real economy that creates jobs.

options.t: 我会质疑「遗产税能解决起点不平等」的前提：富豪有的是办法规避，税负最终落在中产的专业人士头上。与其在税率上象征性加码，不如把教育、医疗这些真正的起点公共品做扎实，机会平等比税收复仇更实在。
options.t_en: I would question the premise that an inheritance tax can fix inequality at the starting line. The very rich have ways of avoiding it, and the burden ends up on middle-class professionals. Rather than a symbolic increase in the rate, build the things that actually equalize the starting line, education and health care. Equality of opportunity is more real than tax as revenge.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: The finance committee is holding a hearing on inheritance tax reform. Under the current system, the shares and property an entrepreneurial couple leave to their only daughter carry an effective tax burden of under five percent after trust arrangements, while statistics show that the wealth passed down by the richest tenth of households is already several times the total wealth of the poorest half. Opponents stress that wealth is after-tax income accumulated again, and that taxing it twice punishes thrift and enterprise. Supporters say inequality at the starting line is making birth the variable that decides a life. The hearing's recorder hands you the microphone.

scene: 临江镇的经济支柱汉特精工宣布把整条生产线迁往劳动力成本更低的地区，两千一百个岗位将在一年内消失，镇上的餐饮、驾校和两家小学都依赖这家厂。镇长提出用十年期税收减免加免费工业用地换它留下；反对的议员算了一笔账：减免总额折算下来每保留一个岗位要花掉财政近百万元，而厂方从未承诺留下多少年。镇议事会今晚表决，旁听席坐满了穿工装的居民。

options.t: 我会投反对票，但把话说明白：用千万级财政赎买一个去意已决的工厂，是把全镇的未来押在别人的商业计划上。钱应该直接花在人身上——失业保障、技能再培训、吸引新雇主的产业基金，让工人不依赖任何单一雇主。
options.t_en: I would vote against, but say it plainly: buying a factory that has already decided to leave with tens of millions in public money is betting the town's future on someone else's business plan. The money should go directly to people, through unemployment support, retraining and an industrial fund to attract new employers, so that workers do not depend on any single employer.

options.t: 我会投赞成票：两千一百个岗位背后是两千一百个家庭的房贷和学费，镇子撑不过产业空心化。留住工厂哪怕只多留十年，就为转型争取了十年缓冲。财政数字上难看，但社会账不能这么算，稳定的社区本身就是公共品。
options.t_en: I would vote in favour. Behind those twenty-one hundred jobs are twenty-one hundred households' mortgages and school fees, and the town cannot survive deindustrialisation. Keeping the plant, even for another ten years, buys ten years of buffer for the transition. It looks ugly on the fiscal numbers, but the social ledger cannot be kept that way; a stable community is itself a public good.

options.t: 我会投反对票，且一分钱补贴都不给：用纳税人的钱补贴私人企业，只会教会有实力的企业轮番要挟。市场在重新配置资源，镇子该做的是修好基础设施、简化营商手续，让下一个愿意来的人来得容易。
options.t_en: I would vote against, and give not a cent in subsidy. Subsidising private firms with taxpayers' money only teaches capable companies to take turns holding you to ransom. The market is reallocating resources, and what the town should do is fix infrastructure and simplify business procedures so that the next willing investor finds it easy to come.

options.t: 我会提修正案：补贴可以谈，但必须写进有法律效力的对赌协议——留厂年限、最低雇佣人数、违约返还全部减免，并且逐年向镇民公开履约情况。公共的钱换公共的可验证承诺，而不是换一场新闻发布会。
options.t_en: I would move an amendment: subsidy is negotiable, but it must be written into a legally binding performance agreement covering years of operation, minimum headcount and full repayment of relief on breach, with compliance published to residents every year. Public money should buy verifiable public commitments, not a press conference.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Hante Precision, the economic pillar of Linjiang township, has announced that it will move its entire production line to a region with cheaper labour. Twenty-one hundred jobs will disappear within a year, and the town's restaurants, driving school and two primary schools all depend on the plant. The mayor proposes ten years of tax relief plus free industrial land to keep it; an opposing councillor has done the sums: the relief works out at nearly a million in public money per job retained, and the company has never promised how many years it would stay. The town council votes tonight, and the public gallery is full of residents in work overalls.

scene: 进口光伏组件的价格在过去三年下跌了近一半，本地新能源安装量随之大涨，但三家本土组件厂中的两家已宣布停产，剩下的一家申请贸易救济。支持加征关税的产业联盟称关键制造能力是战略资产，不能重蹈「设计留在本地、制造流向海外」的覆辙；安装商和环保组织则警告，涨价将让数百个社区的清洁能源计划推迟数年。贸易政策听证会临近，你在咨询委员会名单上。

options.t: 我会支持加征关税：清洁能源产业链的每个环节都涉及就业、标准与供应安全，等市场教会我们教训时，制造能力和工程师队伍已经散了。短期的装机放缓可以接受，完整的产业生态买不回来。
options.t_en: I will support the tariff. Every link in the clean energy supply chain carries jobs, standards and supply security, and by the time the market has taught us the lesson, the manufacturing capacity and the engineering workforce will already have dispersed. A short-term slowdown in installations is acceptable; a complete industrial ecosystem cannot be bought back.

options.t: 我会反对关税：应对气候变暖的时间窗口不等人，最便宜的组件装上屋顶就是最直接的减排。用关税保护低效产能，等于让所有纳税人替落后产能买单；产业升级的鞭子，恰恰是竞争本身。
options.t_en: I will oppose the tariff. The window for tackling climate change will not wait, and the cheapest module on a roof is the most direct emissions cut there is. Protecting inefficient capacity with a tariff means making every taxpayer pay for the laggards, when competition itself is the whip that drives an industry to upgrade.

options.t: 我会支持有时间表的阶梯关税：首年高、逐年递减，倒逼本土厂在明确期限内把成本降到位；同时把关税收入直接补贴分布式光伏的居民安装。既不让产业猝死，也不让保护变成永久拐杖。
options.t_en: I will support a stepped tariff with a timetable: high in the first year, falling each year after, forcing domestic plants to get their costs down within a fixed deadline, while the tariff revenue goes straight into subsidising rooftop systems for households. It keeps the industry from dying overnight without letting protection become a permanent crutch.

options.t: 我会反对关税，但支持另一种产业政策：放弃在组件组装这种产能过剩环节竞争，把钱投向下一代电池技术的研发和中试。与其在别人的成熟赛道上筑墙，不如在下一赛道上领跑——贸易开放和技术押注并不矛盾。
options.t_en: I will oppose the tariff, but support a different industrial policy: stop competing in module assembly, where there is already too much capacity, and put the money into research and pilot production for the next generation of battery technology. Rather than building a wall on someone else's mature track, lead on the next one. Open trade and a technology bet are not in contradiction.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The price of imported solar modules has fallen by nearly half in three years, and local installations of renewables have surged. But two of the three domestic module plants have announced they are shutting down, and the last one has applied for trade relief. The industry coalition backing a tariff calls critical manufacturing capacity a strategic asset, and says we must not repeat the mistake of keeping design at home while manufacturing drifts overseas. Installers and environmental groups warn that higher prices would push clean energy plans in hundreds of communities back by years. The trade policy hearing is coming up, and your name is on the advisory committee list.

scene: 两国共享的澜沧海渔场，带鱼与鲳鱼资源量已不足历史峰值的四分之一。科研委员会建议两国联合休渔两年并分配可捕配额，但本国船东协会指出：邻国船队的监管松散、禁用网具屡禁不止，单方面守约等于把渔场拱手让人；本地水产市场八成货源和上万个加工岗位也系于此。外交部门在征询各方意见后将于下月谈判，你在渔业政策圆桌上。

options.t: 我会支持联合配额协议，哪怕本国要先吃点亏：渔业崩溃没有赢家，先恢复资源才有分配问题。协议里应加入联合巡航、登船核查和卫星定位共享——把互信建立在互相看得见的基础上，而不是赌对方的善意。
options.t_en: I would support the joint quota agreement, even if my own country takes a loss at first. A fishery collapse has no winners; only once the stock recovers is there anything to divide. The agreement should include joint patrols, boarding inspections and shared satellite tracking. Build trust on the basis of being able to see each other, not on betting on the other side's goodwill.

options.t: 我会主张本国单方面延长休渔并补贴渔民转产，但拒绝把执法权交给任何联合机制：我们管得住自己的船队就行，邻国怎么捕捞是他们的事。把资源恢复的希望寄托在别国守约上，是把自己的饭碗交到别人手里。
options.t_en: I would argue that my country extend its own closed season and subsidize fishermen into other work, but refuse to hand enforcement authority to any joint mechanism. We can manage our own fleet; how the neighbor fishes is their business. Betting the recovery of the resource on another country's compliance is putting your own livelihood in someone else's hands.

options.t: 我会主张强硬护渔：增派海警船伴随本国船队作业，在争议水域先行划设本国执法线，把事实摆在谈判前面。资源分配从来是实力问题，单方面守约只会让守法者出局——先确立存在，再谈共享。
options.t_en: I would argue for hardline fishery protection: send more coast guard vessels to accompany our fleet, draw our own enforcement line in the disputed waters first, and put facts on the table before the negotiations. Allocation of resources has always been a question of strength, and honoring an agreement alone only takes the law-abiding out of the game. Establish presence first, then talk about sharing.

options.t: 我会支持联合管理，但要把渔民请进谈判代表团：配额怎么分、休渔期怎么补、转产基金怎么发，规则制定者里应该有闻得到柴油味的人。没有渔民的协议签得再漂亮，也会在执行的第一夜被撕破。
options.t_en: I would support joint management, but insist that fishermen be brought into the negotiating delegation. How the quota is divided, how the closed season is compensated, how the transition fund is paid out: the people who can smell diesel should be among the rule-makers. A treaty signed without fishermen, however elegant, will be torn up on the first night of enforcement.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: In the Lan Cang Sea fishery shared by two countries, stocks of hairtail and pomfret are below a quarter of their historical peak. A scientific committee recommends that both countries close the fishery for two years and divide a catch quota. But the domestic boat owners' association points out that the neighboring country's fleet is loosely regulated and that banned nets are still in use, so honoring the agreement alone amounts to handing the fishery over. Eighty percent of the supply for the local seafood market and thousands of processing jobs hang on it. The foreign ministry will negotiate next month after consulting all parties, and you are at the fisheries policy roundtable.

scene: 临港湿地是候鸟迁徙路线上仅存的三处停歇地之一，也是城市保障房规划图里最后一块可用的整片土地。规划部门拿出的方案是填埋西半区，建设八千套保障房与配套学校；观鸟会与湿地研究所出示数据称，西半区恰是水鸟的高潮位避难所，填埋后整个湿地的生态功能将退化一半以上。听证会现场，一边是排到明年年底的保障房轮候名单，一边是滩涂上觅食的反嘴鹬。

options.t: 我会支持填埋计划：迁徙的鸟没有户口，轮候名单上的家庭有。当生态完整性与几千个家庭的居住尊严冲突时，人应该优先。配套的补偿湿地和人工滩涂可以建，但八千套房子不能为观鸟望远镜让路。
options.t_en: I would support the reclamation plan. Migratory birds have no household registration; the families on the waiting list do. When ecological integrity conflicts with the housing dignity of thousands of families, people should come first. Compensatory wetlands and artificial mudflats can be built, but eight thousand homes cannot give way to a pair of binoculars.

options.t: 我会要求保障房另选址、湿地整体保留：这块湿地一旦失去就永不再来，而住房可以在任何土地上盖。真正的对立不是「人对鸟」，而是「短期的土地账对不可逆的生态账」——城市化的选项里不该包括烧掉最后一页。
options.t_en: I would demand that the housing be sited elsewhere and the wetland kept whole. Once this wetland is lost it never returns, whereas housing can be built on any land. The real opposition is not people versus birds but a short-term land ledger versus an irreversible ecological one; urbanisation should not include burning the last page.

options.t: 我会推动只填埋四分之一的折中方案：保留高潮位避难所的核心区，边缘低功能区域用于建设，并以立法锁定剩余湿地的永久保护边界。完美的方案不存在，但一半的房子加一个完整的生态骨架，好过全有或全无。
options.t_en: I would push a compromise that fills only a quarter: keep the core high-tide refuge, build on the low-functioning margins, and legislate a permanent protection boundary for the rest. No plan is perfect, but half the homes plus an intact ecological skeleton beats all or nothing.

options.t: 我会建议用市场化手段解决：设立湿地保护信托基金，由开发商购买「生态地役权」抵扣其他地块的开发强度，再把资金用于在更大范围内购买和修复退化湿地——让保护湿地的人得到回报，而不是只有成本。
options.t_en: I would suggest a market approach: set up a wetland conservation trust, let developers buy conservation easements to offset development intensity elsewhere, and use the money to buy and restore degraded wetlands on a larger scale, so that protecting wetlands pays rather than only costs.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: Lingang wetland is one of only three remaining stopover sites on a migratory bird route, and also the last contiguous plot left in the city's social housing plan. The planning department's proposal is to fill the western half, building eight thousand subsidised flats plus schools. The birdwatching society and the wetland institute have produced data showing that the western half is precisely the high-tide refuge for waterbirds, and that filling it would degrade more than half of the wetland's ecological function. At the hearing, on one side is the housing waiting list that runs to the end of next year; on the other, avocets feeding on the mudflats.

scene: 林业部门计划将灰狼重新引入西南山区保护区：狼群曾在此绝迹四十年，鹿群失去天敌后啃秃了山坡植被，森林更新近乎停滞。方案公布后，保护区边缘三个乡的牧民连夜联名反对——去年狼形动物已造成数十起牛羊损失；生态学家则联名支持，称顶级掠食者的回归是生态系统重新闭合的唯一办法。协调会上，一位牧民代表把被咬死的羊羔照片拍在了桌上。

options.t: 我会支持重引入计划，并由公共财政全额兜底：按市场价的一点五倍直补狼害损失、推广防狼灯与牧羊犬项目、为受灾乡设立兽医与保险巡回点。生态恢复是公共利益，就不该让最边远的牧民独自承担它的成本。
