options.t_en: I will support the reintroduction, with the public purse covering all of it: direct compensation for wolf losses at one and a half times market price, predator lights and guard dog programmes, and mobile vets and insurance points for the affected townships. Ecological restoration is a public good, so the herders on the most remote edge should not be left to carry its cost alone.

options.t: 我会主张暂缓引入，先解决人的问题：牧民的生计和恐惧不是「观念落后」，是每天晚上都要面对的现实。在没有建立牧民信任与补偿机制之前强行投放狼群，最后的结果往往是毒饵和盗猎——纸上成功，山里失败。
options.t_en: I will argue for postponing the release and dealing with the human problem first. Herders' livelihoods and their fear are not backward thinking; they are what those families face every single night. Force wolves into the hills before trust and compensation are in place, and the likeliest outcome is poisoned bait and poaching: a success on paper, a failure in the mountains.

options.t: 我会支持引入，且不做例外：鹿群失控正在摧毁整个山体的水土与森林，这是更大的公共灾难。牧业可以转型为生态管护和自然体验向导，狼群带来的客流反而可能是新生计。保护区的归保护区，不能被放牧利益绑架。
options.t_en: I will support the reintroduction with no exceptions. An uncontrolled deer herd is destroying the soil, water and forest of the whole massif, which is a far larger public disaster. Herding can shift towards ecological stewardship and nature guiding, and the visitors that wolves draw could become a new livelihood. A reserve belongs to the reserve, and cannot be taken hostage by grazing interests.

options.t: 我会建议先在封闭围栏内做五年试验种群，配上卫星项圈和实时监测，数据向牧民和公众同步公开：狼到底走多远、吃多少、能不能与人共处，让下一阶段的决定建立在证据上，而不是生态学家的信念或牧民的噩梦上。
options.t_en: I will propose a five-year trial population inside a fenced enclosure, with satellite collars and real-time monitoring, and the data published openly to herders and the public: how far the wolves range, how much they take, whether they can live alongside people. Let the next stage be decided on evidence, rather than on the faith of the ecologists or the nightmares of the herders.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: The forestry department plans to reintroduce grey wolves into a protected area in the southwestern mountains. Wolves were wiped out here forty years ago, and without a predator the deer herd has stripped the hillsides bare, so that forest regeneration has almost stopped. Once the plan was published, herders in the three townships along the edge of the reserve signed a petition overnight: wolf-like animals have already cost them dozens of sheep and cattle over the past year. Ecologists signed a counter-petition, calling the return of a top predator the only way to close the ecosystem again. At the coordination meeting, a herder representative puts photographs of a mauled lamb on the table.

scene: 市第二实验中学的家长会上，校长提出废除运行多年的快慢班制度：过去按入学成绩分班，快班配骨干教师，慢班的学生被贴上标签后成绩和自尊双双下滑。但快班学生的家长当场炸了锅——他们的孩子正受益于现行制度，有家长威胁转学去私立，也有慢班家长私下承认「至少慢班节奏适合我孩子」。教育局的观察员坐在后排，等着看学校怎么选。

options.t: 我会支持彻底废除分班：公立教育的底线是不让十二岁的孩子被一次考试分成两种人生。混编班级里，学得快的解释给学得慢的听，本身就是最好的学习。最好的老师不该只喂给跑在最前面的人。
options.t_en: I would support abolishing it entirely. The floor of public education is that a twelve-year-old should not be split into two kinds of life by one exam. In a mixed class, the faster students explaining things to the slower ones is itself the best learning. The best teachers should not be fed only to the ones out in front.

options.t: 我会支持保留分层教学，但重做规则：按学科而非整体分班，数学快的可以和语文慢的同班；分层名单每学期流动，且慢班获得的辅导课时反而更多。因材施教没错，错的是让分层变成贴上就不撕的标签。
options.t_en: I would keep differentiated teaching, but redo the rules: assign by subject rather than as a whole, so a student who is fast in math can be in the same class as one who is slow in language; move the lists every term; and give the slower group more tutoring hours rather than fewer. Teaching to the level is fine. What is wrong is turning a placement into a label that never comes off.

options.t: 我会主张学校的自由比制度统一更重要：让每所学校按自己的师资和生源决定分不分班，家长用脚投票。教育局该管的是底线标准和信息透明，而不是替两百所学校决定哪种教学组织方式最好。
options.t_en: I would argue that a school's freedom matters more than uniformity. Let each school decide, based on its own teachers and intake, whether to stream at all, and let parents vote with their feet. The education bureau should set the floor standards and require transparency, not decide for two hundred schools which way of organizing teaching is best.

options.t: 我会支持废除，但要求配套跟上来：混编班必须配套助教、课后分层辅导和项目制学习，否则就是拉着快的孩子等、看着慢的孩子沉。废除分班不该是省钱的借口，恰恰应该是投入加大的开始。
options.t_en: I would support abolishing it, but demand that the support come with it: mixed classes need teaching assistants, after-school tutoring at different levels and project-based learning. Otherwise you are dragging the fast kids along while watching the slow ones sink. Ending streaming should not be an excuse to save money; it should be the start of spending more.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: At a parents' meeting at the city's No. 2 Experimental Middle School, the principal proposed abolishing the long-running fast and slow class system. Under the old arrangement, students were assigned by entrance score, the fast classes got the strongest teachers, and students in the slow classes were labeled and saw both their grades and their self-respect slide. Parents of fast-class students erupted on the spot: their children are benefiting from the current system, and some threatened to transfer to a private school. Some slow-class parents admitted privately that at least the slow pace suits their child. An observer from the education bureau sits at the back, waiting to see which way the school goes.

scene: 区青少年图书馆的一本获奖小说被三位家长联合投诉：书中一名十六岁角色的自伤情节和几个粗俗词句，被指「不适合心智未成熟的读者」。馆员按流程调出借阅记录：这本书是近两年青少年借阅量最高的书之一，留言本上有多条写着自己「被这本书接住过」的读者留言。图书馆委员会下周表决，双方都在征集签名，本地论坛已经吵了三轮。

options.t: 我会投票保留：图书馆不是无菌室，一本诚实地写过少年人暗处的书，可能正是某些少年唯一敢碰的求助入口。我可以接受增加内容提示和家长指引，但把借阅量最高的书下架，等于向吵得最大声的人投降。
options.t_en: I would vote to keep it. A library is not a sterile room; a book that honestly describes the dark places of adolescence may be the only way in that some teenager dares to take. I can accept a content note and guidance for parents, but removing the most borrowed book in the library is capitulating to whoever shouts loudest.

options.t: 我会投票支持移入「家长陪同借阅」区：不是禁绝，而是承认十二岁和十六岁的阅读确实需要不同的分寸。公共资源照顾的是所有家庭，包括那些对内容有明确边界的家庭——分级不是审查，是共存。
options.t_en: I would vote to move it to a borrow-with-a-parent section. This is not a ban but an acknowledgment that reading at twelve and at sixteen really do need different measures. Public resources serve all families, including those with clear boundaries about content; grading is not censorship, it is coexistence.

options.t: 我会投票保留，同时把遴选规则晒出来：哪些书进馆、依据什么标准、投诉走什么程序，全部公开并邀请家长代表参与新一轮选书。让争论回到规则层面，而不是每次都在具体某一本书上肉搏。
options.t_en: I would vote to keep it, and publish the selection rules: which books enter, on what criteria, and how complaints are handled, all disclosed, with an invitation to parent representatives to join a new round of selection. Let the argument return to the level of rules instead of hand-to-hand combat over one particular book each time.

options.t: 我会建议把决定权还给借书的人：在借阅系统里给所有争议书加上内容标注，家长可为未成年子女设置个人借阅偏好，图书馆不做统一裁决。一间图书馆服务的是几千个不一样的家庭，不是一个委员会的口味。
options.t_en: I would suggest giving the decision back to borrowers: add content labels to all contested books in the lending system, let parents set individual borrowing preferences for their minor children, and have the library make no collective ruling. A library serves thousands of different families, not the taste of one committee.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Three parents have jointly complained about an award-winning novel in the district youth library: a sixteen-year-old character's self-harm and a few crude phrases are said to be unsuitable for immature readers. Following procedure, the librarian pulled the borrowing records: the book is one of the most borrowed by teenagers in the past two years, and the comment book holds several entries from readers saying this book had caught them when they were falling. The library committee votes next week, both sides are collecting signatures, and the local forum has already been through three rounds of argument.

scene: 果品出口大县连续三年遭遇采摘季用工荒，本地年轻人几乎无人应聘，果园主联合会提议引入季节性外劳计划：六个月工签、不设定居通道、由劳务公司统一管理。人权组织随即指出，此类计划容易催生「绑定雇主」的二等劳工——不敢投诉、不敢受伤、到期必须离境；果农则反问：完整开放定居，本县的教育和医疗容量根本接不住。县里的咨询会议轮到你发言。

options.t: 我会支持季节性计划，但必须写入三项底线：劳动者可自由更换雇主、享有与本地同工同酬的最低工资、投诉渠道独立于劳务公司。没有定居承诺也可以是有尊严的短期劳动，关键是别让「临时」成为克扣的通行证。
options.t_en: I will support the seasonal scheme, but with three bottom lines written into it: workers can change employer freely, they are paid the same minimum wage as local workers for the same job, and complaints go through a channel independent of the contractor. Short-term work without a promise of settlement can still be dignified; the point is not to let temporary become a licence for docking pay.

options.t: 我会支持引入并直接给定居路径：采摘工干满两个季节、无违法记录即可申请长期居留。既要人家的劳动又永远不让人家属于这里，才是问题的根源；一个社区消化不了，可以分年度配额，但不能制度化地生产过客。
options.t_en: I will support bringing them in and giving them a direct route to settlement: two seasons of picking with no record of violations and they can apply for long-term residence. Taking people's labour while never letting them belong is the root of the problem. If one community cannot absorb everyone, use annual quotas, but do not institutionalise the production of people who are only ever passing through.

options.t: 我会反对引入外劳：用工荒的真正原因是工资太低、本地人才不愿意干，抬高工价、投资采摘机械才是正路。用便宜的临时劳动力把结构性问题掩盖起来，果农永远没有动力改进，低薪陷阱也会锁死更多人。
options.t_en: I will oppose bringing in foreign labour. The real cause of the shortage is that wages are too low for local people to want the work; raising pay and investing in picking machinery is the right road. Papering over a structural problem with cheap temporary labour means growers never have a reason to improve, and the low-wage trap locks in even more people.

options.t: 我会主张先把本地的闲置劳动力盘活：邻县山区有大量季节性待业人口，跨境引入之前，应先建立县域间的劳务调度、通勤班车和工资保证金制度。本地的失业者先有活干，缺口再谈外部引入，顺序不能反。
options.t_en: I will argue for mobilising the idle local labour first. There are large seasonal unemployed populations in the mountain townships of the neighbouring county, and before crossing a border we should set up inter-county labour dispatch, commuter buses and a wage guarantee fund. Local unemployed people get work first, and only then do we talk about bringing people in from outside; the order cannot be reversed.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: For three years running, the big fruit-exporting county has faced a labour shortage at harvest. Almost no local young people apply, so the growers' association has proposed a seasonal foreign worker scheme: six-month work visas, no route to settlement, managed centrally by labour contractors. Human rights groups point out that schemes of this kind readily produce bonded second-class labour: afraid to complain, afraid to report an injury, required to leave when the visa expires. The growers answer that fully opening settlement is something the county's schools and clinics simply cannot absorb. The county consultation meeting reaches your turn to speak.

scene: 河东区三十年来形成了讲科尔瓦语的移民聚居区：区里有自己的学校、诊所、超市和两份语报纸，老一代几乎不需要主流语言也能生活无碍。区教育局的督导报告指出，约四成移民子女的通用语水平达不到学龄标准，初中毕业后出路狭窄；而语社区的长者则在座谈会上说，语言是他们「在这座城市没有沉底的最后一块木板」。市里委托你所在的调研组给出方案。

options.t: 我会建议在学前与小学阶段推行通用语强化计划，配套家访和母语衔接课：公共教育的基本职责，是让每个孩子长大后在整座城市都有选择权。母语可以在家、在社区、在周末学堂延续，但学校必须把通用语教会。
options.t_en: I would recommend an intensive common-language program in preschool and primary school, together with home visits and bridging classes in the mother tongue. The basic duty of public education is to give every child real choices across the whole city when they grow up. The mother tongue can continue at home, in the community and in weekend schools, but the school must teach the common language.

options.t: 我会反对一切强制：社区用三十年建起自己的学校、报纸和生活网络，这是自组织的成就，不是问题。要做的反而是支持双语学校升格、把科尔瓦语纳入本市的选修体系——让想学的人有课上，而不是让所有人必须同化。
options.t_en: I would oppose anything mandatory. The community spent thirty years building its own schools, newspapers and networks. That is an achievement of self-organization, not a problem. What should be done is the opposite: support the bilingual schools in upgrading and add Korva to the city's elective curriculum, so that people who want to learn it can, rather than requiring everyone to assimilate.

options.t: 我会主张双向的融合方案：一边给移民子女免费的通用语课程，一边把科尔瓦语和文化史开进本地学校当选修。问题不在谁说哪种语言，而在这座城市始终把「融合」理解为单向的归顺。
options.t_en: I would argue for a two-way integration plan: free common-language classes for migrant children on one side, and Korva language and cultural history as electives in local schools on the other. The problem is not who speaks which language. The problem is that this city has always understood integration as one-way submission.

options.t: 我会建议先解决结构问题：督导报告里的四成数字，和这个区的贫困率、家长工作时长高度重合。语言只是症状——先给夜班家长的孩子提供课后托管和免费辅导，比任何语言政策都更能改变下一代的出路。
options.t_en: I would suggest tackling the structural problem first. That forty percent figure overlaps heavily with the district's poverty rate and with how many hours parents work. Language is only a symptom. Giving the children of night-shift parents after-school care and free tutoring would change the next generation's prospects more than any language policy.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Over thirty years, Hedong District has become a migrant neighborhood of Korva speakers, with its own schools, clinic, supermarket and two newspapers in the language. The older generation can get through life with almost no need for the majority language. A school inspection report found that about forty percent of migrant children fall below grade level in the common language, and that their options after middle school are narrow. Meanwhile, elders in the language community said at a roundtable that the language is the last plank keeping them from sinking in this city. The city has asked the study group you are on for a proposal.

scene: 公安部门提请人大审议「智慧安防条例」草案：在全市公共交通枢纽、商圈和主要路口部署带人脸识别的智能摄像系统，官方测算称可比照相似城市降低约百分之二十的街面犯罪率，失踪人员的寻回时间也将大幅缩短。草案同时规定数据保存九十天、调取须经审批。听证会上，一位律师问了一个让全场安静的问题：「九十天后删除的是数据，还是我们知道自己被看过的记忆？」

options.t: 我会投票支持条例：百分之二十的犯罪率下降，意味着每年少几百起抢劫、少若干条人命，失踪儿童能早回家一天是一天。我的隐私观很朴素——守法的普通人，并没有那么多需要向街角摄像头隐瞒的东西。
options.t_en: I would vote for the ordinance. A twenty percent fall in crime means hundreds fewer muggings a year, several lives saved, and missing children home a day sooner. My view of privacy is simple: an ordinary law-abiding person does not have that much to hide from a camera on the corner.

options.t: 我会投票反对：人脸是改不了密码的生物特征，一旦泄露终身作废。今天为治安收集，明天就可能被用于别的名单——技术从不问自己将来的用途。宁可容忍一部分犯罪率，也要守住不被随手扫描的公共空间。
options.t_en: I would vote against. A face is a biometric you cannot change, and once it leaks it is void for life. Collected for public order today, it can be used for other lists tomorrow; technology never asks what it will be used for later. I would rather tolerate some crime than give up public space where no one is scanned at random.

options.t: 我会提出修正案：批准部署，但人脸识别默认关闭，仅在发生重案时经法官令临时开启；公共区域改用不识别身份的行为分析摄像头，并设立由普通市民抽签组成的数据监督团，每季度公开调取记录。
options.t_en: I would move an amendment: approve deployment but keep facial recognition off by default, switched on temporarily only by judicial order after a serious crime; use behaviour-analysis cameras that do not identify people in public areas; and set up a data oversight panel drawn by lot from ordinary citizens, publishing access logs quarterly.

options.t: 我会支持建设但反对生物特征库：用智能视频做交通治理、人流预警、跌倒检测都可以，一律不做人脸比对。城市需要的是更聪明的眼睛，不是更长久的记性——把「看得见」和「认得出」分开，安全与隐私并非只能二选一。
options.t_en: I would support building the system but oppose any biometric database. Intelligent video for traffic management, crowd warnings and fall detection is fine, but no facial matching of any kind. A city needs sharper eyes, not a longer memory; separate seeing from recognising, and safety and privacy need not be either-or.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: The police department has submitted a draft smart security ordinance to the legislature: intelligent camera systems with facial recognition at public transport hubs, shopping districts and major junctions across the city. Official estimates say street crime could fall by about twenty percent, in line with similar cities, and missing persons would be found much faster. The draft also limits data retention to ninety days and requires approval for access. At the hearing, a lawyer asked a question that silenced the room: after ninety days, what gets deleted, the data or our memory of having been watched?

scene: 一家软件公司在全员远程办公半年后，部署了「生产力分析套件」：随机截屏、键盘鼠标活动记录、应用使用时长报表，管理层可按人查看「专注度曲线」。公告称这是「中性的数据，不是监控」。资深工程师沈薇在全员会上发言：她的「专注度」低谷恰好是她写出最关键架构的时段——那段她在纸上画图。技术总监反问：不衡量，怎么管理？你也是与会者。

options.t: 我会支持公司：办公设备和工时都是公司付的钱，衡量投入天经地义。远程办公模糊了边界，数据反而让评价回归客观——至少它不偏心，不像旧式管理靠谁在老板眼前晃。觉得不被信任的人，可以选回办公室或换个东家。
options.t_en: I will support the company. The equipment and the working hours are both paid for by the company, and measuring input is entirely reasonable. Remote work blurred the boundaries, and the data actually push appraisal back towards objectivity; at least it is not partial, unlike the old style where it came down to who loitered near the boss. Anyone who feels distrusted can come back to the office or find another employer.

options.t: 我会主张立法禁止侵入式监控：截屏与键盘记录的问题不在「是否公开数据」，而在人的尊严——劳动者不该在自家书房里被算法值勤。监管应明确负面清单：可以看结果，不许拍过程。
options.t_en: I will argue for legislation banning intrusive monitoring. The problem with screenshots and keystroke logging is not whether the data are disclosed, but human dignity: a worker should not be clocked by an algorithm in their own study. Regulation should set out a clear negative list: you may look at results, you may not film the process.

options.t: 我会建议公司换掉这套系统，改用产出对齐：每个季度定清交付目标，员工自选工作节奏，评价只看交付质量和协作反馈。沈薇的例子恰好说明，测量过程指标会系统性惩罚深度工作——管理该盯结果，不该盯屏幕。
options.t_en: I will propose the company scrap the system and align on outputs instead: clear delivery goals each quarter, employees choosing their own working rhythm, and appraisal looking only at the quality of what is delivered and the feedback from collaborators. Shen Wei's case shows precisely that measuring process metrics systematically punishes deep work. Management should watch results, not screens.

options.t: 我会主张把监控权交给劳动者自己协商：要不要用、用在哪、数据谁可见，写进集体协议而不是行政公告。同样一套系统，若由员工代表共同治理、数据仅聚合呈现，可以是改进工具；单方面强推，就只是权力的展览。
options.t_en: I will argue that the right to monitor should be negotiated by the workers themselves: whether to use it, where, and who can see the data, written into a collective agreement rather than announced by management. The same system, jointly governed by employee representatives and reporting only aggregated data, could be a tool for improvement; imposed unilaterally, it is nothing but an exhibition of power.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: After half a year of full remote work, a software company has deployed a productivity analytics suite: random screenshots, keyboard and mouse activity logging, reports on time spent in each application, and a focus curve that managers can pull up per person. The announcement calls it neutral data, not surveillance. At the all-hands, a senior engineer named Shen Wei speaks: her lowest point on the focus curve is exactly when she wrote her most important architecture, the stretch she spent drawing diagrams on paper. The engineering director answers: if we do not measure it, how do we manage it? You are in the room too.

scene: 新型呼吸道传染病流行期间，卫生部门每天公布新增确诊者发病前四十八小时的到访场所：「某商场三层餐饮区」「某号线某车厢」。支持者称精准轨迹让市民能自查风险、自愿检测，是低成本高效率的流控手段；反对者指出，已有确诊者被人肉认出住址、遭受电话骚扰——去标识化的轨迹和真实身份之间，往往只隔着一栋楼、一个班次。防疫政策例会上要定下一步规则。

options.t: 我会支持继续公布完整轨迹：在传播速度面前，公民自觉是最后的防线，信息越透明，每个人的自我保护就越精准。骚扰确诊者是治安问题，该用治安手段处理，不能因噎废食地砍掉最有效的公众知情工具。
options.t_en: I would support continuing to publish full trajectories. Against the speed of transmission, public awareness is the last line of defense, and the more transparent the information the more precisely each person can protect themselves. Harassing confirmed patients is a public order offense and should be handled as one. You do not cut off the most effective tool for public awareness out of fear.

options.t: 我会主张改为定向通知：轨迹不再向社会公布，由流调员精确通知同场所、同时段的密接者，配合场所级的消毒公告。公众需要的是「我有没有风险」，不是「谁病了」——精准投递信息，同样能阻断传播，却不必展览患者。
options.t_en: I would switch to targeted notification. Trajectories would no longer be published publicly; instead, investigators would notify precisely the close contacts at the same place and time, alongside venue-level disinfection notices. What the public needs is to know whether I am at risk, not who is sick. Targeted delivery of information can also interrupt transmission without putting patients on display.

options.t: 我会支持公布，但重构粒度：只公布场所与时段，删除一切可拼图细节，模糊化楼层与车厢号，并立法惩处人肉与骚扰行为，确诊者身份信息单独立法保护。透明和隐私各有其界，两条线都该由法律画清楚。
options.t_en: I would support publishing, but redesign the granularity: only the venue and the time window, with every detail that could be pieced together removed, floors and carriage numbers blurred, and legislation to punish doxxing and harassment, with separate legal protection for the identity of confirmed patients. Transparency and privacy each have their limits, and both lines should be drawn by law.

options.t: 我会主张最小化原则并引入日落条款：流调数据只用于防疫，存储加密、疫情解除后三十天内销毁，并由独立的数据保护专员按月审计公布。紧急状态下的每一点让步，都必须带着自动归还的期限，否则临时会变成永远。
options.t_en: I would argue for a minimization principle plus a sunset clause: epidemiological data used only for disease control, stored encrypted, destroyed within thirty days of the outbreak ending, and audited monthly by an independent data protection commissioner whose findings are published. Every concession made in an emergency must come with an automatic expiry, otherwise temporary becomes permanent.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: During an outbreak of a new respiratory disease, the health department publishes every day the places each newly confirmed patient visited in the forty-eight hours before symptoms appeared: a food court on the third floor of a shopping mall, a carriage on a certain subway line. Supporters say precise trajectories let people check their own risk and get tested voluntarily, a low-cost and efficient way to control spread. Opponents point out that confirmed patients have already been identified online, had their addresses exposed and their phones harassed. Between a de-identified trajectory and a real identity there is often only one building and one train's distance. The epidemic policy meeting has to set the next rule.

scene: 立法机关就「医疗协助死亡」法案举行最后一轮听证。法案规定：仅限预期生存期不足六个月的绝症患者，须两名医生评估加十四天冷静期，本人须具备完全决策能力。一位渐冻症患者坐着轮椅到现场，说她的未来是「眼睁睁看着自己的身体一件一件报废」；一位残障组织代表则担忧，社会支持不足时，「可选择死亡」对脆弱者会变成「被期待死亡」。你是听证的委员之一。

options.t: 我会投票支持法案：当医学已经无法提供治愈，把最后的选择权交还给本人，是对其人格最根本的尊重。严格的程序、双重评估和冷静期已经把风险压到最低——我们是把死亡交还给人，不是把人交给死亡。
options.t_en: I would vote for the bill. When medicine can no longer offer a cure, giving the final choice back to the person is the most fundamental respect for their dignity. The strict procedure, double assessment and cooling-off period already press the risk to a minimum; we are handing death back to the person, not handing the person over to death.

options.t: 我会投票反对：这个社会对脆弱者的支持系统远远配不上「自由选择」这个词。当居家护理、疼痛管理、经济保障都不足时，选择死亡的人有多少是自愿，有多少是「不想成为负担」？先把活路铺够，再谈死权。
options.t_en: I would vote against. This society's support for the vulnerable falls far short of the words free choice. When home care, pain management and financial security are all inadequate, how much of the choice of death is voluntary and how much is I do not want to be a burden? Lay the paths for living first, then talk about the right to die.

options.t: 我会支持法案，但把重心放在程序之外：每个申请者必须先经过姑息治疗评估与心理支持，且法案生效与「居家安宁疗护全覆盖」捆绑推进。让协助死亡成为所有退路都试过之后的最后选项，而不是系统缺位时的捷径。
options.t_en: I would support the bill but put the emphasis outside the procedure: every applicant must first have a palliative care assessment and psychological support, and the bill's commencement should be tied to full coverage of home hospice care. Make assisted dying the last option after every other route has been tried, not a shortcut when the system is absent.

options.t: 我会支持一种更克制的版本：不设「协助自杀」，但保障「拒绝延命治疗」的完整权利——可以提前指示、可以撤除呼吸机、可以只做舒缓。让死亡自然到来而不被强行推迟，已经是法律能安全给出的最大自主。
options.t_en: I would support a more restrained version: no assisted suicide, but a full right to refuse life-prolonging treatment, meaning advance directives, withdrawal of ventilation, comfort care only. Letting death arrive naturally rather than being forcibly postponed is already the greatest autonomy the law can safely grant.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: The legislature is holding its final hearing on a medical assistance in dying bill. It would apply only to terminally ill patients with less than six months to live, require assessment by two doctors plus a fourteen-day cooling-off period, and require the person to have full decision-making capacity. A woman with ALS came in a wheelchair and said her future was watching her body be written off, piece by piece. A disability rights representative worried that where social support is thin, the option of dying becomes the expectation of dying for the vulnerable. You are one of the committee members at the hearing.

scene: 上市公司监管新规草案提出：五年内上市公司董事会中任一性别不得低于三分之一，未达标者须公开说明理由，连续两年未达标将被处以罚款。行业协会的测算显示，照现有晋升速度，自然达标还需二十年以上；反对的企业方代表称，配额会把「合格的人」换成「符号性的人」，董事遴选应只看能力。监管机构开放公众意见征询，你所在的机构需要提交正式立场。

options.t: 我会支持强制配额加罚款：等二十年就是再让二十年的人才被漏掉。董事会的「能力标准」本身就没经受过检验——大量董事会里坐着的是圈子、校友和旧部。配额是最粗笨但最有效的扳手，先把门撬开，标准自然会重新定义。
options.t_en: I will support a mandatory quota with fines. Waiting twenty years means losing another twenty years of talent. The merit standard for boards has never actually been tested: a great many boards are filled with the same circle, the same alumni, the same former subordinates. A quota is the crudest and most effective wrench there is: force the door open, and the standard will redefine itself.

options.t: 我会反对配额，支持披露制：强制企业公开董事会构成的性别数据、晋升漏斗和目标，让投资者、员工和公众用脚投票。符号性的任命骗不了市场，也帮不了真正有能力的女性——真实的机会在晋升漏斗的每一层。
options.t_en: I will oppose quotas and support disclosure instead: require companies to publish gender data on board composition, their promotion funnel and their targets, and let investors, employees and the public vote with their feet. Symbolic appointments fool nobody and help no genuinely capable woman; the real opportunity lies at every level of the promotion funnel.

options.t: 我会支持配额，但反对罚款，改为「遵守或解释」：企业要么达标，要么公开解释原因与整改时间表。给企业留出路径差异——有的从内部培养，有的外部引进——比一刀切的罚单更能改变长期的选拔文化。
options.t_en: I will support the quota but oppose the fine, replacing it with comply-or-explain: a company either meets the target or publishes its reasons and a remediation timetable. Leaving room for different paths, some training internally and some recruiting from outside, changes the long-term selection culture more than a one-size-fits-all penalty.

options.t: 我认为真正的问题在董事会产生的方式：提名权集中在董事长和猎头的小圈子里，无论配额与否，选出来的都是「让在位者安心的人」。我会主张董事提名程序强制引入股东和员工代表——程序变了，构成自然会变。
options.t_en: I think the real problem is how boards are produced: nomination rights are concentrated in a small circle around the chair and the headhunters, so with or without a quota, the people chosen are the ones who make the incumbents comfortable. I will argue for mandatory shareholder and employee representation in the nomination process. Change the procedure and the composition will change by itself.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A draft regulation for listed companies proposes that within five years no board may have less than one third of either sex, that companies falling short must publish their reasons, and that two consecutive years of non-compliance brings a fine. Industry association modelling shows that at current promotion rates, natural compliance is more than twenty years away. Business representatives opposed say a quota replaces qualified people with symbolic ones, and that board selection should rest on ability alone. The regulator has opened a public comment period, and your organisation has to file a formal position.

scene: 劳动部门起草「育儿假改革」：方案A是给父亲单独划出不可转让的六个月带薪假，配套国家生育基金全额支付；方案B是给每对父母合计十二个月，家庭自主分配；现行制度则是母亲为主、父亲象征性两周。数据显示方案A在先行地区显著提升了父亲休假率，也有企业私下抱怨招聘成本上升：「反正男员工也要休了，那不如谁都不招。」你所在的咨询会被要求给出建议。

options.t: 我会支持方案A：不设不可转让的配额，育儿假就永远是「母亲的假」——数据已经证明，把分配完全交给家庭，结果就是照旧。国家全额支付则切断了「雇谁谁亏」的算计，性别平等从来是制度设计出来的，不是等来的。
options.t_en: I would support Option A. Without a non-transferable quota, parental leave will always be the mother's leave. The data already shows that leaving the division entirely to families produces the same result as before. Full state funding removes the calculation that whoever you hire is a loss, and gender equality has always been designed into institutions, not waited for.

options.t: 我会支持方案B：国家不该替家庭决定谁带孩子。有的家庭母亲愿意全程照护，有的父亲想休满，都应被尊重——统一的国家方案才是最大的傲慢。配套好就业保护与返岗权利，家庭自会作出适合自己的安排。
options.t_en: I would support Option B. The state should not decide for families who raises the child. Some families have a mother who wants to do the whole period of caregiving, some have a father who wants to take the full leave, and both deserve respect. A single national formula is the greater arrogance. With employment protection and the right to return in place, families will work out what suits them.

options.t: 我会支持方案A并加码执行监督：匿名投诉渠道、「休育儿假影响晋升」由雇主举证自清、把父亲休假率纳入企业年度披露。假写在纸上是容易的，让父亲真的敢休、母亲真的不因此掉队，靠的是执行的牙齿。
options.t_en: I would support Option A and add enforcement oversight: anonymous complaint channels, a rule that an employer claiming leave harmed a promotion must prove it, and fathers' take-up rates included in annual corporate disclosure. Writing a right on paper is easy. Making fathers actually dare to take it, and mothers not fall behind because of it, takes enforcement with teeth.

options.t: 我会主张把假期的支付责任社会化，但假期设计从简：全国统一的育儿金直接发给家庭，金额与休假期数挂钩，让家庭自己谈分工。国家划定经济底线，把生活的形状还给每个家庭——既不惩罚选择，也不强制对称。
options.t_en: I would argue for socializing the cost of the leave, but simplifying its design: a national childcare payment paid directly to families, with the amount tied to the number of months taken, leaving the family to negotiate the division itself. The state sets the economic floor and gives the shape of life back to each household, neither punishing choices nor mandating symmetry.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: The labor department has drafted a parental leave reform. Option A gives fathers six months of paid leave that cannot be transferred, fully funded by a national birth fund. Option B gives each couple twelve months in total to divide as they choose. The current system is centered on the mother, with a symbolic two weeks for the father. Data from early-adopting regions shows Option A significantly raises fathers' take-up. Some employers grumble privately that hiring costs will rise: if male employees will take leave too, better to hire neither. The consultancy you work for has been asked for a recommendation.

scene: 生成式AI让一段以假乱真的「某名人宣布参选」视频在两小时内转发过百万，辟谣的浏览量不到其十分之一。内容监管草案提出两项措施：一是强制所有AI生成内容嵌入不可见水印与元数据标记，二是在重大选举前九十天，平台对政治类AI内容实行「先审后发」。行业代表抗议创新将被审批流程扼杀，选举委员会则称这是「信息免疫系统的最后补丁」。公开听证排在下周。

options.t: 我会支持两项措施全部落地：水印解决「是什么」，先审后发解决「什么时候放」。言论自由保护的是人的表达，不是机器的量产——当一条谣言的制造成本趋近于零而辟谣成本恒定，平台的事前义务就是新的必要成本。
options.t_en: I would support both measures in full. Watermarks answer what this is; pre-approval answers when it may go out. Free speech protects human expression, not machine mass production; when a rumour costs almost nothing to make and debunking costs the same as ever, ex ante obligations on platforms are the new necessary cost.

options.t: 我会支持水印强制，反对事前审查：标记AI内容是技术上可验证的中性义务，任何负责任的厂商都该做；但「先审后发」必然滑向对讽刺、戏仿与合法批评的误伤。用可验证的标记武装受众，而不是用审查员的胆量决定公众能看什么。
options.t_en: I would support mandatory watermarks and oppose pre-publication review. Labelling AI content is a neutral, technically verifiable duty any responsible vendor should meet, but pre-approval inevitably catches satire, parody and legitimate criticism. Arm the audience with verifiable labels instead of letting a reviewer's nerve decide what the public may see.

options.t: 我会两项都反对，走司法与市场路线：水印应由行业标准和采购门槛推动，事前审查则应交给竞争——平台为留住用户自会投资识别与降权，被误导的受害者保留诽谤与欺诈之诉。信息生态的健康，最终靠的是免疫而不是无菌。
options.t_en: I would oppose both and take the judicial and market route: watermarks driven by industry standards and procurement requirements, and pre-publication review left to competition, since platforms will invest in detection and demotion to keep users, and victims of deception keep defamation and fraud claims. A healthy information ecosystem ultimately relies on immunity, not sterility.

options.t: 我会支持水印强制，同时要求公共部门先行：政府自身的公告、新闻稿与政务影像全面存证并公开验证接口，学校开设媒介素养课。监管的对象不该只有平台——一个习惯了随手验证的社会，比一百道审查闸门都坚固。
options.t_en: I would support mandatory watermarks and require the public sector to go first: government announcements, press releases and official imagery fully attested with public verification interfaces, and media literacy taught in schools. Platforms should not be the only object of regulation; a society used to checking things at a glance is sturdier than a hundred review gates.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: A generative AI produced a convincing video of a public figure announcing a run for office, shared a million times in two hours, while the fact-check reached less than a tenth of that. The draft content regulation proposes two measures: mandatory invisible watermarks and metadata on all AI-generated content, and, in the ninety days before a major election, pre-approval before publication for political AI content on platforms. Industry representatives protest that innovation would be strangled by approvals, while the electoral commission calls it the last patch for the information immune system. The public hearing is next week.

scene: 医保局的智能审核系统在新一年度拒赔率上升了三成：系统依据历史数据自动判定「该疗法对六十岁以上患者收益不显著」。一位退休教师申诉后，得到的是系统生成的第二条拒绝理由，格式与第一条相同，落款是「自动审核」。技术方称系统整体准确率百分之九十四、节省的经费扩大了覆盖面；申诉人则说：「我想跟一个能被我说服的东西讲道理。」听证会上双方都在等你的问题。

options.t: 我会先要一条铁律：任何拒赔决定的最终署名必须是人，AI输出只能作为参考意见。算法可以计算概率，但「这个人例外」的判断需要能被恳求、能被说服的主体。百分之九十四的准确率，意味着每年数万个具体的人被统计平均数碾过。
options.t_en: I will start with one hard rule: every denial must be signed by a human being, and AI output can only ever be an opinion for reference. An algorithm can calculate probabilities, but the judgement that this person is an exception needs a subject who can be appealed to and persuaded. Ninety-four percent accuracy means tens of thousands of specific people are being run over by the statistical average every year.

options.t: 我会支持系统继续运行并扩大：百分之九十四的准确率高于人工审核，节省的经费实实在在扩大了覆盖人数——那些因此多报销的患者没有资格上听证会，但他们的账单是真的。要做的是修好坏的百分之六：建申诉快速通道、公开决策规则。
options.t_en: I will support the system carrying on and expanding. Ninety-four percent accuracy is higher than human review, and the savings have genuinely widened the number of people covered. The patients who get reimbursed because of it are not the ones who get to speak at a hearing, but their bills are real. What needs fixing is the bad six percent: fast-track appeals and published decision rules.

options.t: 我会主张公开算法并引入独立审计：训练数据、权重逻辑、每类人群的错误率全部向监管机构和研究者开放，像药品说明书一样发布「适应症与副作用」。公众不需要看懂代码，但必须有权知道规则——黑箱做公共裁决，本身就是程序不正义。
options.t_en: I will argue for publishing the algorithm and bringing in independent audit: training data, weighting logic and error rates for each population group all opened to regulators and researchers, issued like a drug label with indications and side effects. The public does not need to read the code, but it must have the right to know the rules. A black box making public decisions is itself a failure of procedural justice.

options.t: 我会主张敏感决策分级禁入：医保拒赔、低保资格审查、监护权评估这类直接决定个人命运的领域，禁止AI作为决策依据，只允许做材料预处理。效率的归效率，人的归人——有些决定慢一点，是文明的价格。
options.t_en: I will argue for a tiered ban on sensitive decisions: in areas that directly decide a person's fate, such as denial of medical cover, means-testing for welfare, or custody assessment, AI should be barred as a basis for decision and allowed only to pre-process materials. Leave efficiency to efficiency and people to people. Some decisions being slower is the price of being civilised.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The health insurance agency's automated review system has pushed the denial rate up by thirty percent this year: on the basis of historical data, it rules that a given therapy offers no significant benefit to patients over sixty. When a retired teacher appealed, what came back was a second ground for denial generated by the system, in the same format as the first, signed automated review. The technical side says the system is ninety-four percent accurate overall and that the money saved has widened coverage. The appellant says: I want to argue with something that can be persuaded by me. At the hearing, both sides are waiting for your question.

scene: 十七岁的少年参与了一起持械抢劫，作为从犯被判两年少管教养。少管所的心理报告显示他悔改表现突出，出狱后以优异成绩考入技工学校冷作焊接专业，如今二十三岁，正被一家船厂列入录用名单——直到背景审查暴露了他的少年案底。船厂依法可以拒录，法官也依法不能为他出具「无犯罪证明」。司法改革座谈会上，这个案例被编号为「案例九」，讨论是否建立少年犯罪记录封存制度。

options.t: 我会支持建立封存制度：少年司法的全部前提就是「他还没长成」，用十八岁前的一段错处追杀二十三岁的人生，等于宣告教育矫正从头就是谎言。封存不等于销毁——司法机关依然可查，只是不再跟着他进每一次面试。
options.t_en: I would support a sealing system. The whole premise of juvenile justice is that he has not finished growing up. Hunting a twenty-three-year-old life with a mistake made before eighteen declares that correction and education were a lie from the start. Sealing is not destruction: judicial bodies can still look, but the record no longer follows him into every interview.

options.t: 我会反对自动封存，支持个案申请制：有的少年罪案轻如打架，有的重如夺命，一刀切的封存对被害人是不公平的。让法官在刑满若干年后，按罪行轻重、悔改实证与被害人意见逐案裁定，宽恕应该是被论证的，不是被批量发放的。
options.t_en: I would oppose automatic sealing and support case-by-case petition. Some juvenile offenses are as light as a brawl, others as grave as taking a life, and blanket sealing is unfair to victims. Let a judge decide case by case, years after the sentence is served, according to the gravity of the offense, the evidence of reform and the victim's view. Forgiveness should be argued for, not handed out in bulk.

options.t: 我会支持封存，但配套被害人一环：封存生效前，应向被害人履行完赔偿与道歉的全部义务，并把被害人陈述纳入裁定考量。一个制度的正当性，不能建立在让一方沉默的基础上——宽恕的天平上，两边都要有砝码。
options.t_en: I would support sealing, with the victim built in. Before sealing takes effect, all compensation and apology owed to the victim must be completed, and the victim's statement must be part of the ruling. The legitimacy of an institution cannot rest on one party's silence. On the scales of forgiveness, both sides need a weight.

options.t: 我会把矛头指向背景审查制度本身：问题不是案底的存在，而是雇主可以无限索取它。我会主张立法限定——只有与岗位直接相关的犯罪方可询问，其余一律禁止。修复人生的方式，是收窄窥探的范围。
options.t_en: I would aim at the background check system itself. The problem is not that the record exists but that employers can demand it without limit. I would argue for legislation restricting it: only offenses directly relevant to the job may be asked about, and everything else is off limits. The way to repair a life is to narrow the scope of prying.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: At seventeen, a boy took part in an armed robbery and was sentenced as an accomplice to two years in a juvenile correction facility. The psychological report from the facility noted outstanding remorse. After release he tested into a technical school's metal welding program with excellent results. He is now twenty-three and on a shipyard's hiring list, until the background check turned up his juvenile record. The shipyard may lawfully refuse to hire him, and the judge may lawfully not issue him a certificate of no criminal record. At a judicial reform roundtable the case is filed as Case Nine, and the discussion is whether to create a system for sealing juvenile criminal records.

scene: 某中级法院法官对一起引发全网关注的量刑案作出轻判，法理依据充分但与汹涌的舆论期待相去甚远。网络发酵后，有人发起联署要求「罢免不接地气的法官」，一周内签名破百万；法律界则连发声明，称此例一开，今后所有判决都将向流量低头，因为这届法官将学会「先看热搜再翻法条」。司法委员会邀请各方提交意见书，评估是否引入法官民选罢免机制。

options.t: 我会反对引入罢免机制：法官的职责恰恰是在民意的洪水中按住法律这块礁石。今天的百万签名是义愤，明天的百万签名可能是被组织出来的声浪——机制一旦建立，两种情况都会冲击法槌。司法独立不是法官的特权，是少数者的保险柜。
options.t_en: I would oppose introducing recall. A judge's job is precisely to hold the rock of law against the flood of popular feeling. Today's million signatures are righteous anger; tomorrow's million signatures may be an organised roar, and once the mechanism exists both will batter the gavel. Judicial independence is not a judge's privilege; it is the safe deposit box of minorities.

options.t: 我会支持引入罢免，但设高门槛：须超过三分之一登记选民联署、经司法伦理委员会初核、再交付公决。法官不能只向上负责而不向任何人负责——终身制保护的是好的少数，也可能是傲慢的、远离生活的人。
options.t_en: I would support recall with a high threshold: over a third of registered voters signing, a preliminary review by a judicial ethics committee, then a referendum. Judges cannot answer only upwards and to no one; life tenure protects a good minority, and it can also protect the arrogant and the out of touch.

options.t: 我会主张不动罢免这把刀，改用透明的程序修复信任：判决书强制说理并公布合议庭不同意见、庭审全程直播、设立由前法官与随机公民组成的职业操守委员会。让公众看懂判决是怎么作出的，比让公众有能力撤掉判决者更治本。
options.t_en: I would leave the knife of recall alone and repair trust through transparency instead: mandatory reasoning in judgments with dissenting opinions published, full live streaming of hearings, and a professional conduct committee of former judges and randomly selected citizens. Helping the public understand how a judgment was reached is more fundamental than giving them the power to remove the judge.

options.t: 我会支持保留现状但增加一个出口：对明显失范（而非「不合民意」）的法官，由同级人大启动弹劾程序，标准限于贪腐、程序违法与重大失职，量刑轻重永远不属于弹劾理由。问责的扳机要存在，但钥匙必须很难拿到。
options.t_en: I would keep the status quo but add one exit: for judges who clearly misconduct themselves, rather than merely displeasing public opinion, the same-level legislature may start impeachment, limited to corruption, procedural violations and gross dereliction, with the severity of a sentence never a ground. The trigger should exist, but the key must be hard to obtain.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: A judge at an intermediate court gave a lenient sentence in a case that gripped the whole internet. The legal reasoning was sound but far from the surging public expectation. After the outrage spread, someone launched a petition to remove judges who are out of touch, passing a million signatures within a week. The legal profession issued statement after statement: once this precedent exists, every future ruling will bow to traffic, because this generation of judges will learn to check the trending list before turning to the statute book. The judicial committee has invited submissions on whether to introduce a mechanism for recalling judges by popular vote.

scene: 市第三中学新学期开学，高二学生阿依玛按其信仰传统佩戴头巾到校，被教导主任依据《校园着装规范》中「校园内不得佩戴显著宗教标识」的条款劝离。她的父亲到校申诉称这是信仰义务而非装饰；规范的支持者则坚持公立学校应是所有背景学生平等相处的世俗空间，一视同仁的着装规则本身就是对每个人的尊重。区教育局要求学校在一周内给出处理意见并报备。

options.t: 我会建议修改规范、准许佩戴：一个女孩的头巾没有妨碍任何人，倒是禁止的规则在用世俗的名义做宗教才做的事——规定别人如何表达信仰。真正的世俗中立，是学校对信仰既不推广也不清除。
options.t_en: I will propose amending the rule to permit it. One girl's headscarf harms nobody, whereas the ban does, in the name of secularism, exactly what religion does: prescribing how others should express their faith. Genuine secular neutrality means the school neither promotes religion nor erases it.

options.t: 我会支持学校执行现行规范：公立学校不是任何信仰的展示空间，每个走进校门的人都暂时把宗教符号留在门外，这恰恰是对所有信仰的一视同仁。例外一旦开口子，学校将永远在裁定哪个标志「够宗教」、哪个不够。
options.t_en: I will support the school enforcing the current rule. A public school is not a display space for any faith, and everyone who walks through the gate leaves religious symbols outside for the time being; that is precisely what treats all faiths alike. Once you open one exception, the school will be ruling forever on which symbol is religious enough and which is not.

options.t: 我会建议允许佩戴、但保留安全例外的底线：宗教自由与校园管理并不冲突——涉及身份核验、体育课安全装备等具体场景可以有具体规则。用场景化的细则替代符号化的禁令，既尊重信仰也不牺牲管理。
options.t_en: I will propose allowing it while keeping a floor of safety exceptions. Freedom of religion and school management do not actually conflict: identity checks, safety equipment in PE and similar specific situations can have specific rules. Replace a symbolic ban with detailed, situation-based rules, and you respect faith without sacrificing management.

options.t: 我会建议把决定权下放给每个学校的校务委员会，由家长、教师与学生代表共同议定细则，区里只划法律底线。让穿着规范成为社区协商的结果而非上级的统一号令——这样产生的规则，无论松紧，各方都更能接受。
options.t_en: I will propose devolving the decision to each school's council, with parents, teachers and student representatives agreeing the detailed rules together and the district setting only the legal floor. Let the dress code be the product of community negotiation rather than a uniform order from above. Rules made that way, tight or loose, are far easier for everyone to accept.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: On the first day of the new term at the city's third middle school, a second-year student named Aima arrives wearing a headscarf in keeping with her faith, and the discipline director turns her away under the clause in the school dress code stating that conspicuous religious symbols may not be worn on campus. Her father comes in to appeal, saying it is a religious obligation rather than an accessory. Supporters of the rule insist that a public school should be a secular space where students of every background meet as equals, and that one dress rule applied to all is itself a mark of respect for each of them. The district education bureau has asked the school for a decision and a report within a week.

scene: 市民政局开放「社区养老服务补贴」申请，一家教会基金会提交方案：利用现有教堂附属空间改建社区老年食堂与日间照料点，报价仅为商业机构的六成，唯一争议是其将保留饭前的自愿谢恩环节，并计划在活动室悬挂少量宗教艺术品。世俗派团体抗议公共资金不该流向宗教组织；而该基金会已在本区运营免费助餐八年，口碑良好。评审委员会需要给出原则性的裁决标准。

options.t: 我会支持拨款，并把「服务开放、参与自愿」写成合同条款：床位与餐位不得以信仰为条件，宗教环节设在服务时间之外、参与完全自愿，接受年度审计。公益成果不该因提供者的信仰背景被拒——老人吃上热饭，比评审团的哲学立场重要。
options.t_en: I would support the grant, and write open service and voluntary participation into the contract: no one may be denied a place or a meal on grounds of belief, the religious element sits outside service hours, participation is entirely voluntary, and the foundation accepts an annual audit. Public benefit should not be rejected because of who provides it. Old people getting a hot meal matters more than the review panel's philosophical position.

options.t: 我会反对拨款：公共资金进入宗教组织，等于用纳税人的钱为传教的基础设施买单——哪怕服务本身无可挑剔，「挂着圣像的公共食堂」也在为特定世界观背书。同等服务完全可以通过世俗机构购买，没必要冒这个边界风险。
options.t_en: I would oppose the grant. Public money entering a religious organization amounts to paying, with taxpayers' money, for the infrastructure of evangelism. Even if the service itself is beyond reproach, a public canteen with an icon on the wall is endorsing a particular worldview. The same service can perfectly well be purchased from a secular provider; there is no need to take this risk at the boundary.

options.t: 我会支持拨款并扩大这类合作：信仰团体是社区里最后一批还在义务做饭、探视、送终的人，他们的人手、场地与信任是任何官僚系统都买不到的资产。该做的是让所有宗教与世俗组织在同一标准下竞争服务合同——以效果论英雄。
options.t_en: I would support the grant and expand this kind of cooperation. Faith groups are among the last people in a community still cooking, visiting and sitting with the dying, for free. Their hands, their space and their trust are assets no bureaucracy can buy. What should be done is to let every religious and secular organization compete for service contracts under the same standard, with results deciding.

options.t: 我会反对直接拨款，支持税收抵免：不把钱拨给宗教组织，而是允许向任何合规助餐机构（含宗教背景）捐款的个人与企业税前抵扣，把「要不要支持」的选择留给纳税人自己。国家的角色是搭台与核验，不是替所有人掏钱。
options.t_en: I would oppose a direct grant and support a tax credit instead. Do not give the money to a religious organization; instead let individuals and companies deduct donations to any compliant meal provider, including religious ones, from their taxable income, and leave the choice of whether to support it to the taxpayers themselves. The state's role is to set the stage and verify, not to spend on everyone's behalf.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: The civil affairs bureau has opened applications for community elder care subsidies, and a church foundation has submitted a proposal: convert existing space attached to the church into a community canteen for the elderly and a day care point, at sixty percent of the price quoted by commercial operators. The only controversy is that it will keep a voluntary moment of grace before meals and plans to hang a few religious artworks in the activity room. Secular groups are protesting that public money should not flow to religious organizations. The foundation has run free meal service in this district for eight years with a good reputation. The review committee has to set the principled standard for deciding.

scene: 老城「三坊七巷」片区的限高令已执行四十年，青瓦坡顶的天际线保存完好，但核心区一套五十平米老屋住着三代人、无独立厨卫的现象也保存完好。市规划院的新方案提议：片区东侧三分之一放开限高，建设高密度可负担住宅，以十年时间将轮候家庭迁入；建筑遗产学界则警告，天际线一旦破口，整个片区的历史叙事就断了。规划展上留言簿两边都写满了。

options.t: 我会支持放开限高：遗产保护不能以几代人的居住尊严为代价。历史街区的「原真性」如果只剩屋顶轮廓，而住进去的人换了一茬又一茬的有钱人，那保护下来的不过是布景。老城首先得是一座活着的、普通人住得起的城。
options.t_en: I would support lifting the limit. Heritage protection cannot be paid for with the housing dignity of several generations. If the authenticity of a historic district is reduced to a roofline while the people living inside are replaced by successive waves of the wealthy, what is preserved is only a stage set. An old town must first be a living town that ordinary people can afford.

options.t: 我会反对放开限高，主张在别处建新城：天际线是四百年才长成的一件整体作品，破口就是毁灭，且不会再有第二次机会。可负担住房可以也应该建在交通便利的新区——用地铁和配套解决，而不是拆解唯一的老城。
options.t_en: I would oppose lifting the limit and argue for building a new town elsewhere. The skyline is a single work that took four hundred years to grow; a breach is destruction, and there is no second chance. Affordable housing can and should be built in well-connected new districts, solved with metro lines and services rather than by dismembering the only old town.

options.t: 我会支持一个受严格约束的折中：放开区域再砍半、限高从四十米压到二十米、新建筑必须采用传统材料与退台设计，并以法定图则永久锁定其余轮廓。承认要动，但把动的幅度交给最严格的图纸。
options.t_en: I would support a strictly constrained compromise: halve the released area again, cut the height limit from forty metres to twenty, require traditional materials and setback terraces for new buildings, and lock the remaining outline permanently in the statutory plan. Accept that change will happen, but let the strictest drawings set its extent.

options.t: 我会主张先动另一块蛋糕：把全市分散的存量空置房、停工楼盘和机关大院闲置用地清出来改建可负担住房，再回头看老城究竟还剩多少真实缺口。老城的压力，不该是土地惰性的替罪羊。
options.t_en: I would argue for cutting a different cake first: clear the city's scattered vacant homes, stalled projects and idle institutional land for conversion into affordable housing, then come back and see how much real shortfall is left in the old town. The old town's pressure should not be the scapegoat for inertia over land.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The height limit in the old town's Sanfang Qixiang quarter has held for forty years. The grey-tiled pitched roofline is intact, and so is the fact that a fifty-square-metre flat in the core area houses three generations with no kitchen or bathroom of its own. The planning institute's new proposal would lift the limit on the eastern third of the quarter to build high-density affordable housing and move waiting families in over ten years. Architectural heritage scholars warn that once the skyline is breached, the whole district's historical narrative breaks. Both sides have filled the comment book at the planning exhibition.

scene: 云栖巷是大学城旁的老社区，三年间近四分之一的住房被改成了短租民宿，房租涨了六成，长租的陪读家庭和退休教师陆续搬离。楼道里拖着行李箱的游客深夜喧哗，房东们则组建了「房东权益群」，认为自己的房子如何使用是产权范围内的自由。街道拟出台「短租牌照限额+每年出租上限九十天」的新规，听证会前夜，两边的群里都在动员发言。

options.t: 我会支持严格限额：住宅社区的存在靠的是住民之间的稳定预期，当邻居变成每周更换的陌生人，社区的治安、噪音、学校生源就一起塌了。产权从来不是绝对的——你的房子在社区里，就继承了社区的义务。
options.t_en: I will support strict caps. A residential community exists on the stable expectations neighbours have of one another; when neighbours become strangers who change every week, safety, noise and school enrolment all collapse together. Ownership was never absolute: your house sits inside a community, and it inherits the community's obligations.

options.t: 我会反对限额：房子是我的，租给谁、租多久是我的自由。短租让普通房主第一次分享到了旅游经济，而限额会压缩房主的收益空间、同时保住酒店和长租中介的既有份额。我倾向管噪音和扰民行为本身——对行为执法，别对用途设禁。
options.t_en: I will oppose the cap. The house is mine, and who I rent it to and for how long is my freedom. Short-term letting is the first time ordinary owners have had a share of the tourism economy, and a cap squeezes owners' returns while protecting the existing share of hotels and letting agents. I would rather regulate the noise and the nuisance itself: enforce against behaviour, do not ban a use.

options.t: 我会支持限额，但配套市场机制：牌照通过拍卖发放，收益全部注入本社区的可负担长租改造；对把唯一自住房做短租的房东减免限制。让短租的利润反哺被它挤出的长租市场——疏导比堵截有效，钱要回到社区。
options.t_en: I will support a cap, with a market mechanism attached: licences issued by auction, with all proceeds going into converting homes in this neighbourhood into affordable long-term rentals, and relief for owners who are letting out their only home. Let the profit from short-term letting feed the long-term market it has squeezed out. Channelling works better than blocking, and the money should come back to the community.

options.t: 我会建议先做数据、再做规则：短租占比、租金涨幅、投诉记录按楼栋公开，同时给社区自治的工具——业委会可经三分之二表决为本楼设定更严的公约。城市的规则不必一刀切，让每一栋楼在底线上长出自己的规矩。
options.t_en: I will propose doing the data first and the rules second: publish short-term rental share, rent increases and complaint records building by building, and give the community the tools to govern itself, with owners' committees able to set stricter rules for their own building by a two-thirds vote. City rules do not have to be uniform; let each building grow its own rules on top of the floor.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: Yunqi Lane is an old neighbourhood next to the university district. In three years nearly a quarter of its homes have been converted into short-term rentals, rents have risen by sixty percent, and the families who rented long term to be near their children's school, along with retired teachers, have been moving out one by one. Tourists drag their suitcases through the stairwells late at night, making noise. The landlords, meanwhile, have set up a landlords' rights group, arguing that how they use their own property is a matter of ownership. The subdistrict plans a new rule: a cap on short-term rental licences and a maximum of ninety days' letting a year. The night before the hearing, both groups are mobilising speakers.

scene: 农科院育成了一种基因编辑抗病小麦，田间试验中可减少一半的杀菌剂用量、增产约一成，恰好赶上一个多雨的病害流行季。审批进入冲刺阶段：支持方称减少农药与稳产是环境和粮食安全的双重利好；有机农业协会则要求按老式转基因作物的严格标准走十年的环境与食用安全评估。麦收在即，主产区的合作社联名催批，你的意见被收入最终评估卷宗。

options.t: 我会主张加速审批：靶点明确、编辑痕迹可追踪的新育种技术不同于老式转基因，按旧流程再走十年，等于让病害年份的减产和农药滥用再持续十年。监管的强度应与风险相称——用二十年前的尺子量今天的科学，本身就是失职。
options.t_en: I would argue for faster approval. A new breeding technique with a defined target and traceable edits is not the same as older transgenic crops. Running the old process for another ten years means another ten years of lost yield in disease years and of pesticide overuse. The intensity of regulation should match the risk. Measuring today's science with a twenty-year-old ruler is itself a failure of duty.

options.t: 我会支持按最严格标准评估：把基因编辑「和转基因区分开」的说辞，历史上每一次都是产业在争取更宽松的入场券。生态影响是慢变量，十年评估不是官僚主义，是最后的安全冗余——快一年省下的钱，赔不起一次不可逆。
options.t_en: I would support assessing it by the strictest standard. The argument that gene editing should be treated differently from transgenic crops has, every time in history, been industry asking for a looser entry ticket. Ecological effects are slow variables. A ten-year assessment is not bureaucracy, it is the last safety margin. The money saved by going a year faster cannot pay for one irreversible mistake.

options.t: 我会主张批准，但配上两个条件：一是种子专利不得限制农户自留种，编辑技术如涉及公共科研投入须开放给小规模育种者使用；二是产品入市可自主标识。技术可以快，但收益的分配结构必须在批准时就锁定。
options.t_en: I would argue for approval with two conditions. First, the seed patent must not restrict farmers from saving their own seed, and any edit involving public research funding must be open to small breeders. Second, products may label voluntarily on entering the market. The technology can move fast, but the distribution of its benefits has to be locked in at the moment of approval.

options.t: 我会主张批准与否交给分层决定：科学上安全性评估通过即批准上市，但每袋种子与面粉标注「基因编辑来源」，把最终选择权放进超市货架。监管者管安全，市场管偏好——有机消费者和想省钱的农户各得其所。
options.t_en: I would argue that approval be split into layers. If the scientific safety assessment passes, it goes on the market, but every bag of seed and every bag of flour is labeled as gene-edited, putting the final choice on the supermarket shelf. Regulators handle safety, the market handles preference, and organic consumers and farmers who want to save money each get what they want.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: The agricultural academy has bred a gene-edited disease-resistant wheat that cuts fungicide use by half in field trials and raises yields by about ten percent, arriving just in time for a rainy, disease-heavy season. Approval is in its final stretch. Supporters say less pesticide and stable yields are a double win for the environment and for food security. The organic farming association wants the ten-year environmental and food safety assessment required for older transgenic crops. Harvest is imminent, cooperatives in the main growing regions have jointly petitioned for fast approval, and your opinion is going into the final assessment file.

scene: 平原农业县近五年耕地向种粮大户与农业公司集中，流转率已过六成：规模化让亩均成本下降、大型机械与数字监测普及，粮食产量创新高；但三百多个村庄的年轻家庭退出耕作，部分村落只剩老人，一些公司的「托管」合同被指压价、口头约定、单方变更。省里拟出台《耕地流转与规模经营条例》，你所在的农村政策小组负责起草争议条款。

options.t: 我会主张效率优先、集中继续：小农经济养活不了未来，规模化是粮食安全和农民增收的路径。条例要做的是规范合同文本、建立流转价格指导与纠纷仲裁——把集中过程中最坏的毛病治掉，而不是把集中本身治掉。
options.t_en: I would argue for efficiency first and continued concentration. Smallholder farming cannot feed the future; scale is the route to food security and higher farm incomes. The regulation's job is to standardise contract templates, set transfer price guidance and establish dispute arbitration, curing the worst ills of concentration rather than concentration itself.

options.t: 我会主张给规模设上限、给小农设保护：限制单一主体流转面积，恢复村集体对土地流转的民主议定程序，小农户享受单独的补贴与技术通道。乡村不只是粮食的车间，还是几千万人的家园——账不能只算亩产。
options.t_en: I would argue for capping scale and protecting smallholders: limit the area any single entity may take over, restore democratic decision-making by the village collective over land transfers, and give smallholders their own subsidy and technical support channels. The countryside is not just a grain workshop; it is home to tens of millions of people, and the ledger cannot be kept in mu of yield alone.

options.t: 我会主张第三种主体：优先培育农民专业合作社与村集体股份公司来承接规模经营，让土地流转的收益以分红形式留在农户手里。规模经济的好处是真的，问题在于现在这份好处几乎全部流向了外部资本。
options.t_en: I would argue for a third kind of entity: prioritise farmer cooperatives and village collective share companies to take on scaled operation, so that the returns from land transfer stay with farming households as dividends. The benefits of scale are real; the problem is that right now almost all of them flow to outside capital.

options.t: 我会主张中性规则加严格执法：不限制谁种地、种多少，但严查合同欺诈与变相强制，开放农户的诉讼通道与法律援助，流转价格由公开竞价平台形成。谁更有效率谁种，规则只要保证每次进出的自愿与知情。
options.t_en: I would argue for neutral rules strictly enforced: no limit on who farms or how much, but rigorous checks on contract fraud and disguised coercion, open litigation channels and legal aid for farmers, and transfer prices set by a public bidding platform. Whoever is more efficient farms, so long as the rules guarantee that every entry and exit is voluntary and informed.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: In this flat agricultural county, cropland has concentrated into the hands of large grain growers and agribusiness over five years, with more than sixty percent now transferred. Scale has cut per-mu costs and spread large machinery and digital monitoring, and grain output is at a record high. But young families in more than three hundred villages have left farming, some villages are down to the elderly, and some companies' management contracts are accused of lowball pricing, verbal agreements and unilateral changes. The province is drafting a regulation on farmland transfer and scaled operation, and your rural policy group is drafting the contested clauses.

scene: 公共广播机构的年度预算审议又成焦点：它每天覆盖数千万听众，深度调查报道屡屡推动政策修正；但在流量平台上被商业媒体与自媒体的算法推荐打得节节败退，年轻受众流失严重。财政部方案拟削减其预算三成，「让市场检验内容价值」；编辑部则回击称，碎片化时代恰恰更需要一个不靠流量喂养的新闻底座。预算听证上，各方都在等你这一票。

options.t: 我会投票反对削减、反而增加预算：商业媒体的天性是喂给受众想听的，而公共讨论的运转依赖一个所有人共享的事实底座。公共媒体的价值恰恰体现在它「无聊」的地方——没人想看的听证会、不带货的调查报道。
options.t_en: I will vote against the cut and for an increase. Commercial media are built to feed audiences what they want to hear, and the functioning of public debate depends on one shared foundation of facts. A public broadcaster's value shows precisely where it is boring: the hearings nobody wants to watch, the investigations that sell nothing.

options.t: 我会投票支持削减：用全体纳税人的钱供养一个受众越来越少的机构，本身就是问题。新闻的价值由读者用注意力投票，公共媒体若真有价值，靠会员、赞助与付费订阅同样可以活——不少地方的公共台已在这么做。
options.t_en: I will vote for the cut. Keeping an institution with a shrinking audience alive on the taxes of everyone is a problem in itself. The value of news is decided by readers spending their attention; if public media are genuinely valuable, they can survive on membership, sponsorship and subscriptions, as public stations in many places already do.

options.t: 我会投票反对削减，但附带改革条件：理事会改由跨党派的公民提名委员会产生、总编辑任期与政治周期错开、季度报告全部公开。问题不是公共媒体这个制度，而是任何机构垄断了「公共」的解释权——先把治理修好。
options.t_en: I will vote against the cut, but with reform conditions attached: the board chosen by a cross-party citizens' nomination committee, the editor-in-chief's term offset from the political cycle, and quarterly reports fully published. The problem is not the institution of public media, but any body monopolising the right to interpret what public means. Fix the governance first.

options.t: 我会主张把钱换一种花法：预算的三分之一下沉为地方与社区媒体的公共基金，任何编辑独立的非营利媒体——包括小型网络电台和县域调查团队——都可申请。要保卫的是公共性，不是某个特定的机构。
options.t_en: I will argue for spending the money differently: move a third of the budget down into a public fund for local and community media, open to any editorially independent non-profit outlet, including small online stations and county-level investigative teams. What needs defending is publicness, not one particular institution.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: The public broadcaster's annual budget review is the focus again. It reaches tens of millions of listeners every day, and its investigative reporting has repeatedly pushed policy corrections. Yet on the platform giants it is being beaten back by the algorithms of commercial and independent media, and it is losing younger audiences badly. The finance ministry proposes cutting its budget by thirty percent, to let the market test the value of content. The newsroom answers that in a fragmentary age, what is needed is precisely a news foundation that is not fed by traffic. At the budget hearing, everyone is waiting for your vote.

scene: 一段深度伪造的视频让某企业家「亲口承认」了从未发生的行贿，两小时内冲上热搜，其公司市值蒸发数十亿；虽在一天内被多家鉴定机构证伪并全网撤下，但一个月后抽样显示仍有近三成受访者「记得看过那段视频」。平台方称其已尽「通知—删除」义务；受害者则主张平台应在传播前拦截。立法研讨会上，法学家们把这称为「真实感的地基正在被抽走」。

options.t: 我会主张平台事前拦截义务：对高度仿真的人物视频，平台在推流放大前必须核验来源与合成标记，「事后删除」在传播速度面前等于不作为。你既然靠算法赚取了传播的收益，就要承担算法踩油门前的查验责任。
options.t_en: I would argue for a duty to intercept in advance. For highly realistic videos of real people, platforms must verify the source and any synthetic markers before amplifying them. Takedown after the fact, against the speed of distribution, is doing nothing. If you profit from distribution through your algorithm, you carry the duty to check before the algorithm steps on the gas.

options.t: 我会主张以受害者救济为核心的司法路线：伪造视频的本质是诽谤与欺诈，应强化快速禁令、举证责任倒置、平台信息披露义务和惩罚性赔偿。把「造假的成本」抬到高于「造假的收益」，比要求平台当全知裁判更可执行。
options.t_en: I would argue for a judicial route centered on relief for the victim. A forged video is essentially defamation and fraud, so strengthen fast injunctions, reversal of the burden of proof, platform disclosure duties and punitive damages. Making the cost of forgery higher than its reward is more workable than asking platforms to be all-knowing judges.

options.t: 我会主张公共投资建设「真实性基础设施」：统一的出处签名标准、开放的检测工具、给每条官方影像加盖可验证的时间戳。与其在事后追杀假视频，不如让真视频自带证明——防伪的成本公共化，是数字时代的基础工程。
options.t_en: I would argue for public investment in truth infrastructure: a common provenance and signing standard, open detection tools, and verifiable timestamps on every official image. Rather than hunting fake videos after the fact, let real videos carry their own proof. Socializing the cost of authentication is basic infrastructure for the digital age.

options.t: 我会主张最小干预：平台自愿标注、媒介素养教育进课堂、让专业鉴定机构在市场竞争中建立信誉。历史上每一次「伪照恐慌」最后都靠社会的免疫系统消化——立法者跑不过技术，但一个怀疑而多源的读者跑得过谣言。
options.t_en: I would argue for minimal intervention: voluntary labeling by platforms, media literacy in schools, and professional forensic bodies building reputations through market competition. Every past panic over forged photographs was eventually digested by society's immune system. Legislators cannot outrun technology, but a skeptical reader with multiple sources can outrun a rumor.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A deepfaked video had an entrepreneur confessing, in his own apparent voice, to bribery that never happened. It trended within two hours and wiped billions off his company's market value. Within a day several forensic firms had debunked it and it was taken down across the platforms, yet a month later a sample survey found that nearly thirty percent of respondents still remembered seeing the video. The platform says it fulfilled its notice-and-takedown duty. The victim argues that platforms should intercept before distribution. At the legislative seminar, legal scholars call this the ground under our sense of reality being pulled away.

scene: 司法统计显示，本地区监狱已超员三成，其中近四成服刑人员所犯是盗窃、轻伤害、小额诈骗等非暴力轻罪，再犯率不降反升。改革方案提出：对初犯、非暴力的轻罪大幅适用社区矫正、电子监管与强制劳动赔偿，监狱留给暴力犯罪与再犯高危者。被害人协会抗议「正义打折」；矫正官工会则担忧社区监管会沦为无人负责的形式。立法听证进入最后一轮。

options.t: 我会支持方案：把盗窃犯和暴力犯关在同一屋檐下，等于开办犯罪进修学校。监禁摧毁工作、家庭与社会关系——恰恰是防止再犯的全部要素。社区矫正附带强制就业与赔偿，让被害人直接得到补偿，比单纯的岁月折抵更接近正义。
options.t_en: I would support the plan. Putting thieves and violent offenders under the same roof is running a school for crime. Prison destroys work, family and social ties, which are exactly the things that prevent reoffending. Community correction with compulsory employment and compensation gives victims direct recompense, which is closer to justice than simply time served.

options.t: 我会反对方案：量刑的意义一半在震慑，一半在于向社会与被害人宣告罪与罚的等式。把监狱从轻罪者的账单上划掉，等于告诉潜在的违法者门槛降了。被害人的痛感不是「落后的报应观」，是正义直觉本身。
options.t_en: I would oppose the plan. Half the point of a sentence is deterrence, and half is declaring to society and to victims the equation between crime and punishment. Taking petty offenders off the prison ledger tells potential offenders that the bar has been lowered. Victims' pain is not a backward notion of retribution; it is the moral intuition of justice itself.

options.t: 我会支持方案，但先回答钱从哪来：社区矫正需要矫正官、心理服务、就业衔接和电子监管，人均成本并不便宜。若预算不同步到位，非监禁化就只是把监狱的拥挤转移到无人看守的街道上——改革的诚意写在人头上。
options.t_en: I would support the plan, but first answer where the money comes from. Community correction needs officers, psychological services, job placement and electronic monitoring, and the per-head cost is not cheap. If the budget does not arrive alongside, decarceration merely shifts prison overcrowding onto unguarded streets; the sincerity of a reform is written in its headcount.

options.t: 我会支持方向但改变工具：对轻罪者优先适用罚金、周末拘禁与劳动赔偿这类「可感但不断人生」的刑罚，慎用电子脚环——公开可见的监控标记等于把审判搬进社区，服完刑的人背上仍是终身烙印。
options.t_en: I would support the direction but change the instruments: for petty offenders, prefer fines, weekend detention and work-based compensation, punishments you can feel but that do not wreck a life, and use electronic tags sparingly. A visible monitoring mark moves the trial into the neighbourhood, and the person who has served their sentence still carries a brand for life.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: Judicial statistics show that the region's prisons are thirty percent over capacity, and that nearly forty percent of inmates are serving time for non-violent petty offences such as theft, minor assault and small-scale fraud, while recidivism is rising rather than falling. The reform proposal would route first-time, non-violent petty offenders into community correction, electronic monitoring and compulsory work-based compensation, reserving prison for violent and high-risk repeat offenders. The victims' association protests that justice is being discounted; the correction officers' union fears community supervision will become a formality nobody owns. The legislative hearing is in its final round.

scene: 货运行业协会游说立法：让所有雇主都能无偿查询求职者的犯罪记录，「安全岗位之外的也该查，方向盘后面坐的是谁总得让人知道」。反方是更生保护团体：他们的回访显示，出狱者最集中的失业期正是出狱后第一年，而就业是再犯率最强的抑制变量。折中提案是「岗位分级查询」——涉及财务、儿童、驾驶的岗位可查，其余岗位禁止询问。你是立法助理，要为表决者写备忘录。

options.t: 我会建议采纳岗位分级查询：查什么、查到什么程度，取决于岗位本身的风险敞口，而不是雇主的好奇心。孩子的事查侵害前科，钱柜的事查经济前科，方向盘后面的事查危险驾驶——其余岗位，让人重新开始。
options.t_en: I will recommend adopting tiered checks by role. What is checked, and how far back, should depend on the risk exposure of the job itself rather than the curiosity of the employer. A history of offences against children for work with children, financial offences for the cash box, dangerous driving for behind the wheel. For every other role, let people start again.

options.t: 我会建议维持雇主的充分知情权：企业为自己的用人风险负责，信息越充分，判断越准确。一刀切禁止询问，等于强迫雇主闭着眼睛雇人——中小雇主赔不起一次错信，他们宁可少招，反而堵死了更多人的出路。
options.t_en: I will recommend preserving the employer's full right to know. A business carries its own hiring risk, and the fuller the information, the better the judgement. A blanket ban on asking forces employers to hire blind, and small employers cannot afford one bad hire: they will simply hire fewer people, which shuts more people out.

options.t: 我会建议在分级查询之外加一个更生保障：对完成矫正、连续三年无再犯者，记录自动对雇主屏蔽；同时由公共部门和国企带头设定更生者雇佣比例。光给雇主设限不够，得有人先开那扇门。
options.t_en: I will recommend adding a rehabilitation guarantee on top of tiered checks: for anyone who has completed their sentence with no reoffending for three consecutive years, the record is automatically hidden from employers. At the same time, public bodies and state-owned firms should lead by setting hiring ratios for former offenders. Limiting employers is not enough; someone has to open that door first.

options.t: 我会建议把重心放在信息的准确性上：现行数据库错录、漏更、旧案滞留的问题比比皆是，多少人被根本不属于自己的记录拦在门外。先立法保证记录的准确、纠错时限与申诉机制——在谈谁能看之前，先保证看到的是真的。
options.t_en: I will recommend putting the emphasis on the accuracy of the information. Current databases are riddled with mistaken entries, records that were never updated and cases that should have been expunged, and plenty of people are shut out by records that are not even theirs. Legislate first for accuracy, deadlines for correction and an appeal mechanism. Before arguing about who may look, make sure what they see is true.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The freight industry association is lobbying for legislation that would let every employer check an applicant's criminal record free of charge, arguing that checks should not stop at safety-critical roles: people are entitled to know who is sitting behind the wheel. Against them are rehabilitation groups, whose follow-up data show that the period of heaviest unemployment for former prisoners is the first year after release, and that employment is the strongest single factor in reducing reoffending. The compromise on the table is tiered checks by role: permitted for roles involving money, children or driving, prohibited elsewhere. You are a legislative assistant, writing the memo for those who will vote.

scene: 一项重要的司法协助与引渡条约进入议会审议：对方法律体系在羁押期限、辩护权保障上与本国标准存在差距。支持方称，没有条约，逃亡的贪腐与诈骗嫌犯将永远逍遥；反对方指出，条约文本中「政治犯罪不引渡」的定义模糊，且对方法院近年拒绝过独立观察员旁听关键庭审。外交部提醒：若否决，同类谈判将全线停滞。你的选区选民意见几乎对半分裂。

options.t: 我会投票批准，但附上三项保留：羁押与审判标准不符人权公约时得拒绝引渡、死刑罪名一律不引渡、本国法院对「政治犯罪」作最终认定。条约是合作的骨架，保留条款是人权的防火墙——两者可以同时要。
options.t_en: I would vote to ratify, with three reservations attached: extradition may be refused where detention and trial standards fall below the human rights covenant, no extradition on capital charges, and domestic courts have the final word on what counts as a political offense. The treaty is the skeleton of cooperation and the reservations are the firewall for rights; you can have both.

options.t: 我会投票否决：引渡是把本国居民交给他国权力处置，一旦出错没有任何回头路。当对方法庭连独立旁听都拒绝时，任何书面承诺的分量都要打折——司法合作的门永远可以再谈，交出去的人要不回来。
options.t_en: I would vote against. Extradition hands a resident over to another state's power, and if it goes wrong there is no way back. When the other side's courts refuse even independent observers, the weight of any written promise has to be discounted. The door to judicial cooperation can always be reopened; a person handed over cannot be returned.

options.t: 我会投票批准并推动更深的司法合作：不仅签引渡，还要参与联合侦查、证人互认与跨境资产追缴的常设机制。跨境犯罪早已全球化，正义却还停在国境线——让渡部分司法主权，买回的是对本国受害者的保护。
options.t_en: I would vote to ratify and push for deeper judicial cooperation: not just extradition but joint investigations, mutual recognition of witnesses and a standing mechanism for cross-border asset recovery. Cross-border crime went global long ago while justice is still stuck at the border. Giving up some judicial sovereignty buys protection for our own victims.

options.t: 我会投票反对，但理由是时机而非原则：先把对方法律体系的独立评估、既往引渡案例的实际遭遇摸清楚，让议会看到一份尽调报告再表决。国际合作值得做，但值得做的条约，不差这六个月的审慎。
options.t_en: I would vote against, but on grounds of timing rather than principle. First commission an independent assessment of the other side's legal system and find out what actually happened to people extradited under past arrangements, and let parliament see a due diligence report before voting. International cooperation is worth doing, but a treaty worth doing can wait six months for prudence.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: An important mutual legal assistance and extradition treaty is before parliament. The other side's legal system falls short of domestic standards on the length of detention and the protection of the right to counsel. Supporters say that without a treaty, fugitive corruption and fraud suspects will remain free forever. Opponents point out that the treaty's definition of a political offense is vague, and that the other side's courts have in recent years refused to let independent observers into key trials. The foreign ministry warns that a rejection will stall all similar negotiations. Your constituents are split almost exactly in half.

scene: 一个接收本国长期援助的地区爆发了严重的人道危机，同时其当局通过了一系列压缩结社与出版自由的法律。内阁分裂为两派：一派主张立即冻结援助以表明立场；另一派指出，援助的粮食与医疗直接经手民间机构，冻结首先饿到的是最弱势的人群，而当局精英根本不依赖这些钱。反对党要求表态，国际舆论也在观望本国的选择。

options.t: 我会主张维持援助、换轨发放：钱和物资继续，但全部绕开当局，直接经手独立的民间机构与国际组织，并公开每一笔流向。既不让病人为压迫埋单，也不让表态的愤怒落在最轻的那只秤盘上。
options.t_en: I would argue for keeping aid but changing the channel: money and supplies continue, but all of it bypasses the authorities and goes directly through independent civil organisations and international bodies, with every flow published. Neither let patients pay for oppression nor let the anger of a statement fall on the lighter pan of the scale.

options.t: 我会主张冻结并追加针对性限制措施：援助在这个体制里就是合法性燃料——危机的责任在制造危机的制度，不在拒绝供血的国际社会。半心半意的援助只会延长一切，包括苦难本身。
options.t_en: I would argue for freezing aid and adding targeted restrictions. In this system aid is legitimacy fuel; responsibility for the crisis lies with the system that created it, not with the international community that refuses to keep feeding it. Half-hearted aid only prolongs everything, including the suffering.

options.t: 我会主张完全脱钩处理：人道是人道，人权是人权，两笔账分开算。人道援助按人道标准持续评估，人权问题走外交、国际组织与多边声明的轨道。用病人的口粮当外交筹码，无论用得多正当，最后输掉的是道义本身。
options.t_en: I would argue for complete decoupling: humanitarian is humanitarian, human rights is human rights, two separate ledgers. Humanitarian aid is continuously assessed by humanitarian standards; human rights issues go through diplomacy, international organisations and multilateral statements. Using patients' rations as a diplomatic bargaining chip, however justified it looks, ultimately loses the moral ground itself.

options.t: 我会主张把关系整体重估：这个地区的战略位置让援助变成了不能撤的赎金，年复一年。真正该谈的是本国在那里的全部利益——安全、经济、人道——重新排一个顺序，而不是在每一轮危机里重复表态的仪式。
options.t_en: I would argue for reassessing the relationship as a whole. The region's strategic position has turned aid into a ransom that cannot be withdrawn, year after year. What really needs discussing is the full set of our interests there, security, economic and humanitarian, reordered, rather than repeating the ritual of a statement in every round of crisis.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: A region that has received your country's long-standing aid is in a severe humanitarian crisis, and its authorities have just passed a set of laws curtailing freedom of association and the press. The cabinet is split: one side wants aid frozen immediately as a statement; the other points out that the food and medicine go through civil organisations and that freezing it starves the weakest first, while the elite depend on none of it. The opposition demands a position, and international opinion is watching what your country chooses.

scene: 一个工业转型城市的试验区获得授权，对辖区内全体成年居民发放无条件基本收入试点：每月固定金额、不审核、不要求求职，为期三年。支持者称自动化正在掏空传统岗位，社会安全网必须前置；反对者警告它将侵蚀工作伦理、引爆财政赤字，且「给富人发钱」在道义上说不过去。试点的评估委员会向社会公开招募成员，你提交的申请里要写清自己的立场。

options.t: 我会支持全面铺开：无条件性正是力量所在——有审核就有羞辱、有漏掉的人、有吓退的申请者。自动化时代的就业是幸存者偏差，社会分红的逻辑应当像空气一样不问出身。至于财政，那是税制要回答的问题，不是穷人的饭碗要回答的。
options.t_en: I will support rolling it out fully. Its unconditionality is exactly where the strength lies: any test brings humiliation, people who fall through the gaps, and applicants scared off. Employment in the age of automation is survivorship bias, and a social dividend should be as unconditional as the air. As for the fiscal question, that is for the tax system to answer, not for poor people's dinners.

options.t: 我会支持，但理由是自由而非分配：现有的救济体系是一台由官僚、表格和盘查组成的机器，受助者被训练成永远自证清白的嫌疑人。一笔无条件的钱，同时废掉乞求的伦理和管制的成本——这是最体面的福利，也是最便宜的国家。
options.t_en: I will support it, but on grounds of freedom rather than distribution. The existing relief system is a machine of bureaucrats, forms and interrogations, and it trains recipients to be suspects forever proving their innocence.
