An unconditional sum abolishes both the ethics of begging and the cost of policing. It is the most dignified form of welfare and the cheapest kind of state.

options.t: 我会反对铺开、支持严格试点：先搞清楚它对劳动供给、家庭结构、社区互助的真实影响，三年数据出来再谈。把整个社会保障体系押在一个思想实验上，无论左右，都是用穷人当赌注。
options.t_en: I will oppose rolling it out and support a strict pilot. First establish what it actually does to labour supply, household structure and mutual help in the community, and talk again when three years of data are in. Staking the whole social security system on a thought experiment, from left or right, is gambling with poor people's lives as the stake.

options.t: 我会反对，主张资源应定向：同样的预算，花在最穷的三分之一身上可以是翻倍的收入、免费的教育和托育。全民均发是政治上讨喜的对称美，伦理上却是给不需要的人递烟、给快饿死的人递杯水。
options.t_en: I will oppose it and argue that resources should be targeted. The same budget spent on the poorest third could mean double their income, plus free education and childcare. Paying everyone the same is a symmetrical beauty that is politically appealing and ethically hollow: a cigarette for the person who does not need one, a glass of water for the person who is starving.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A pilot zone in an industrial city that is restructuring has been authorised to run an unconditional basic income for every adult resident in its area: a fixed monthly sum, no means test, no job-seeking requirement, for three years. Supporters say automation is hollowing out traditional jobs and the social safety net has to be put in place in advance. Opponents warn that it will erode the work ethic and blow up the deficit, and that handing money to rich people is indefensible morally. The pilot's evaluation committee is recruiting members from the public, and your application has to state your position clearly.

scene: 灵活就业者已占城市劳动人口的近五分之一：外卖骑手、设计接单者、网约司机与零工写手。他们不缴失业保险，也没有雇主替缴——收入中断时，社保体系的回答是「没有记录，无法认定」。新草案提出两个方向：强制平台按流水代扣代缴纳入统一失业保险；或建立自愿参保、财政补贴一半的开放账户。平台方对两者都反对，骑手代表则在座谈会上问：「我们到底是员工还是空气？」

options.t: 我会支持强制平台代缴：劳动就是劳动，不因合同叫「合作」而消失。平台从每一单里抽成，就该为每一单的社会成本买单——按流水比例计入失业、工伤与职业伤害保险，这是平台经济该付的成人票价。
options.t_en: I would support mandatory withholding by platforms. Work is work, and it does not disappear because the contract calls it a partnership. A platform takes a cut of every order, so it should pay the social cost of every order: contribute a share of turnover to unemployment, work injury and occupational injury insurance. That is the adult ticket price of the platform economy.

options.t: 我会支持自愿参保加补贴：零工群体的收入形态千差万别，有以此为生的骑手，也有贴补家用的退休教师——统一强制只会伤其一端。开放账户、可携带、财政补贴一半，把选择权还给劳动者自己。
options.t_en: I would support voluntary enrollment with a subsidy. The income situations of gig workers vary enormously: there are riders who live on it and retired teachers topping up a pension, and one mandated model only hurts one end. An open, portable account with half the cost subsidized by the state gives the choice back to the worker.

options.t: 我会支持强制，但换个主体：不是平台代扣，而是把平台缴费义务并入按单计提的职业伤害与社会保险基金，由中立的公共机构管理、跨平台累计。骑手不该因为换个平台接单就清零——保障跟人走，不跟合同走。
options.t_en: I would support compulsion, but with a different payer. Not platform withholding, but folding the platform's contribution obligation into a per-order occupational injury and social insurance fund, managed by a neutral public body and accumulated across platforms. A rider should not be reset to zero because he switches to another platform. Protection should follow the person, not the contract.

options.t: 我会主张先回答那个更根本的问题：他们到底是员工还是空气？我会推动「第三类劳动者」的法定身份——介于雇员与个体户之间，享有最低安全标准、集体谈判权与按比例的社会保障。保险只是症状，身份才是病灶。
options.t_en: I would argue for answering the more fundamental question first: are they employees or thin air? I would push for a legal status of third-category worker, between employee and self-employed, with minimum safety standards, collective bargaining rights and proportional social protection. Insurance is the symptom. Status is the disease.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: Flexible workers now make up nearly a fifth of the city's labor force: food delivery riders, freelance designers, ride-hailing drivers, gig writers. They pay no unemployment insurance and have no employer paying on their behalf, so when their income stops the social insurance system answers that there is no record and no way to determine eligibility. A new draft proposes two directions: require platforms to withhold and pay contributions based on turnover into a unified unemployment scheme, or create an open account with voluntary enrollment and half the cost subsidized by the state. Platforms oppose both. At the roundtable a riders' representative asks whether they are employees or thin air.

scene: 七十二岁的沈伯在老伴去世三年后，与照顾他两年的护工林姨领了证。子女得知时婚已结完，反应剧烈：长子翻出母亲的旧照质问「对得起我妈吗」，女儿则连夜咨询律师，担心父亲名下两套房产未来的归属——其中一套原本口头承诺留给孙子当婚房。林姨主动提出签婚前协议，沈伯却拒绝：「我剩下的日子，不想再算账了。」家庭会议约在周末，你是被请来「评理」的老友。

options.t: 我会先对子女说：婚姻自主是人格尊严的一部分，不因七十岁而过期。你们真正担心的是房产，那就让担心回到法律轨道——遗嘱、协议、公证都是工具。但别把财产焦虑包装成对亡母的忠诚，那对谁都不诚实。
options.t_en: I would say to the children first: freedom to marry is part of human dignity and does not expire at seventy. What you are really worried about is the property, so let that worry return to the legal track, where a will, an agreement and notarisation are all tools. But do not dress property anxiety up as loyalty to your late mother; that is dishonest to everyone.

options.t: 我会对沈伯说：结不结、和谁结是你的自由，但「不想算账」恰恰是对所有人不负责。把两套房产的归属、林姨的居住权和孙子的那份，趁头脑清明白纸黑字写清楚——把账算在前面，感情才不用替钱背锅，这也是对林姨的保护。
options.t_en: I would say to Uncle Shen: whether you marry and whom is your freedom, but not wanting to settle accounts is precisely irresponsible towards everyone. While your mind is clear, write down in black and white where the two flats go, Auntie Lin's right to live there, and the grandson's share. Settle the accounts up front so that affection need not carry the blame for money, and that protects Auntie Lin too.

options.t: 我会把矛头指向制度：这场家庭战争之所以惨烈，是因为老人的再婚、照护与继承全都压在「家庭内部解决」上。真正的出路是完善的意定监护、遗嘱信托与公共照护——让沈伯的晚年幸福不必以子女的财产预期为赌注。
options.t_en: I would point at the system: this family war is so brutal because elderly remarriage, care and inheritance are all left to be solved inside the family. The real way out is proper advance directives for guardianship, testamentary trusts and public care, so that Uncle Shen's happiness in old age need not be staked against his children's property expectations.

options.t: 我会对子女说：你们的反对里有多少是钱、多少是感情，自己先分清楚。父亲找的不是财产继承人，是深夜能递一杯水的人——这份需要若由你们来满足，他本不必外求。先恢复探望和陪伴，再谈你们的委屈。
options.t_en: I would say to the children: work out for yourselves how much of your opposition is money and how much is feeling. What your father has found is not an heir but someone who can hand him a glass of water in the night; if you had been able to meet that need, he would not have had to look outside. Restore visits and company first, then talk about your grievances.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: Three years after his wife died, seventy-two-year-old Uncle Shen married Auntie Lin, the caregiver who had looked after him for two years. His children only learned after the fact and reacted hard: the eldest son pulled out old photographs of their mother and demanded to know whether this was fair to her, while the daughter consulted a lawyer overnight, worried about the two flats in their father's name, one of which had been verbally promised to a grandson as a wedding home. Auntie Lin offered to sign a prenuptial agreement; Uncle Shen refused, saying he did not want to spend what time he had left settling accounts. The family meeting is this weekend, and you are the old friend invited in to adjudicate.

scene: 「海洋梦幻馆」是本市的纳税大户与孩子们的童年记忆：虎鲸表演、海豚共游与白鲸合影每年带来百万客流，也养活着两百多名员工。动物福利组织公布的调查影像显示，表演动物的刻板行为（反复绕圈、撞击池壁）已相当严重，并援引多地同类场馆的关闭先例。市议会收到的立法提案是十年内全面禁止鲸豚表演；馆方提出的替代方案是改建「自然行为展示」并逐步退役。听证持续了一整天。

options.t: 我会支持十年禁令：让高智商的群游动物在混凝土池子里为掌声表演，无论场馆多干净、饲料多讲究，本质都是囚禁取乐。禁令的缓冲期足够员工转型、场馆改造——社会不是第一次为文明进步消化成本，也不会是最后一次。
options.t_en: I will support the ten-year ban. Making highly intelligent, socially travelling animals perform for applause in concrete pools, however clean the venue and however good the feed, is at bottom captivity for entertainment. The transition period is enough for staff to retrain and the site to be rebuilt; society has absorbed the cost of civilising itself before, and will again.

options.t: 我会支持馆方的转型方案：全面禁止是道德表演，渐进退役才是动物福利。训练转向觅食展示、医疗行为配合与真实社交群体，退役个体转入海边保育湾——用十年的善意设计，替代一刀切的经济处决。
options.t_en: I will support the venue's transition plan. An outright ban is moral theatre; gradual retirement is what animal welfare looks like. Training shifts to foraging displays, cooperation with medical procedures and genuine social groups, and retired individuals move to a coastal sanctuary. Ten years of well-designed goodwill instead of an economic execution by decree.

options.t: 我会主张立法设定硬性福利指标而非指定形式：池体容积、环境丰容标准、刻板行为发生率、兽医独立评估——达标可继续，不达标立刻停演。禁令管的是「表演」这个名词，指标管的才是动物的每一天。
options.t_en: I will argue for legislating hard welfare indicators rather than a prescribed format: pool volume, enrichment standards, rates of stereotyped behaviour, independent veterinary assessment. Meet them and you may continue; fail them and the show stops at once. A ban regulates the noun, performance; indicators regulate the animal's every day.

options.t: 我会反对干预：两百万游客里大多数是普通家庭，他们的孩子看到海豚的那声惊呼，可能就是一生环保意识的起点。场馆有专业兽医与福利标准，比许多打着保护旗号的「庇护地」做得更好——让市场与游客的偏好决定它的未来。
options.t_en: I will oppose intervention. Most of those million visitors are ordinary families, and the gasp of a child seeing a dolphin may be where a lifetime of environmental awareness begins. The venue has professional vets and welfare standards, and does better than many sanctuaries that fly the flag of protection. Let the market and visitors' preferences decide what it becomes.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Ocean Dreamland is the city's biggest taxpayer and part of a generation's childhood: the orca show, swimming with dolphins and photographs with belugas bring in a million visitors a year and support more than two hundred staff. Footage released by an animal welfare group shows that the performing animals' stereotyped behaviours, circling repeatedly and striking the pool walls, are now severe, and cites other cities where similar venues have closed. The bill before the city council would ban cetacean performances outright within ten years; the venue's counter-proposal is to rebuild as a natural behaviour exhibit and phase the animals out. The hearing has run all day.

scene: 市文化基金资助的当代艺术双年展上，一件作品引发轩然大波：艺术家把一批从旧货市场收集的宗教圣像与家用电器组装在一起，命名为「日常祷告」。多个信教团体到市政府抗议，称其「亵渎且用公共资金羞辱信众」；策展方回应作品本意是探讨消费主义与神圣性的关系，批评者「只看了标题没走进作品」。要求撤展与撤资的联名信已送进文化局，你的职位是文化基金评审委员。

options.t: 我会投票维持展出与资助：公共艺术基金资助的是探索，不是赞助让所有人都舒服的装饰。作品冒犯与否，恰恰是它进入公共讨论的方式——文化局的门如果只为不冒犯任何人的作品打开，那扇门后只剩花鸟和静物。
options.t_en: I would vote to keep both the exhibition and the funding. A public art fund pays for exploration, not for decoration that makes everyone comfortable. Whether a work offends is precisely how it enters public discussion. If the bureau's door opens only to work that offends no one, all that is left behind it is flowers and still life.

options.t: 我会投票撤下作品、保留资助机制：公共资金的特殊性在于它来自所有人，包括被冒犯的信众。艺术家完全可以用私人赞助做这件作品，商业与市场的空间都会欢迎它——但把纳税人的钱变成单方面的挑衅，性质就变了。
options.t_en: I would vote to take the work down and keep the funding mechanism. What is special about public money is that it comes from everyone, including the believers who are offended. The artist is perfectly free to make this work with private sponsorship, and commercial and market space will welcome it. Turning taxpayers' money into a one-sided provocation changes the nature of the thing.

options.t: 我会投票维持展出，但把评审程序公开：这次冲突暴露的真问题是——谁决定了这件作品拿公共资金？我会推动评审标准、评委构成与异议程序的全面透明，让下一件争议作品面对的是看得见的规则，而不是几个委员的品味。
options.t_en: I would vote to keep the exhibition, but make the review process public. The real question this conflict exposes is who decided that this work gets public money. I would push for full transparency in the review criteria, the composition of the panel and the objection procedure, so that the next controversial work faces visible rules rather than the taste of a few committee members.

options.t: 我会提议一件更好的事：不撤展，在作品旁同时展出抗议信原文与艺术家的完整陈述，并组织一场公开辩论。冒犯发生的地方，正是讨论开始的地方——把冲突本身做成展览的一部分，比任何一方的胜利都更配得上公共空间。
options.t_en: I would propose something better: do not withdraw the work, but display the full text of the protest letters and the artist's complete statement alongside it, and organize a public debate. Where offense happens is where discussion begins. Making the conflict part of the exhibition itself is more worthy of public space than a victory for either side.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: At a contemporary art biennale funded by the city's cultural fund, one work has caused an uproar. The artist assembled a batch of religious icons collected from flea markets together with household appliances and titled it Daily Prayer. Several religious groups protested at city hall, calling it blasphemous and an insult to believers paid for with public money. The curators respond that the work is about the relationship between consumerism and the sacred, and that its critics looked at the title and never walked into the piece. A joint letter demanding that the work be withdrawn and the funding cut has reached the cultural bureau, where you sit on the fund's review panel.

scene: 省运动会报名系统里出现一个前所未有的案例：一位完成了完整医学过渡与法律性别变更的跨性别女运动员申请参加女子组举重比赛。现行省规沿用旧标准（相关医学证明加两年激素等待期），她全部符合；但多位对手教练联署质疑，称力量型项目的既有优势并未完全消失。国际体育组织的最新框架则建议各项目自订标准。省体育总局只有一周时间决定她能否上场。

options.t: 我会让她上场：规则在她报名时是明确的，她满足了全部既有条件——事后再改规则针对某个具体的人，是对程序正义最坏的示范。如果标准需要更新，那就从下一个赛季开始，光明正大地改。
options.t_en: I would let her compete. The rules were clear when she entered and she met every existing condition; changing them afterwards to target one specific person is the worst possible demonstration of procedural justice. If the standard needs updating, do it openly from next season.

options.t: 我会建议按新的科学框架先行修订分级标准：不是针对她个人，而是趁这个案例把标准现代化——按项目分别评估肌肉量、血红蛋白与既有发育阶段的实际影响，设公开的量化门槛。争议的根源是规则停在旧科学上，裁判不该替规则背锅。
options.t_en: I would propose revising the classification standard under the new scientific framework first: not aimed at her, but using this case to modernise the standard by assessing, sport by sport, muscle mass, haemoglobin and the actual effect of developmental stage, with public quantitative thresholds. The root of the dispute is that the rules stopped at old science; referees should not carry the blame for the rules.

options.t: 我会建议她暂不参加女子组、并推动增设公开组：以开放注册为原则的第三类别，让各类运动员在同等待遇保障下竞技。女子组作为为生理女性设立的保障类别，其边界应当从严——这不是针对谁，是类别本身的定义问题。
options.t_en: I would suggest she not compete in the women's event for now, and push for an added open category: a third class with open registration where all kinds of athletes compete with equal safeguards. The women's category is a protected class created for biological females and its boundary should be drawn strictly; this is not aimed at anyone, it is a question of what the category means.

options.t: 我会建议让运动员们自己参与定规则：成立由现役女运动员、跨性别运动员、运动医学专家组成的常设委员会，标准按项目滚动修订并公示数据。体育的规则从来归参与这项运动的人所有，行政的单方裁定只会让所有人都不服。
options.t_en: I would suggest letting the athletes take part in making the rules: a standing committee of active female athletes, transgender athletes and sports medicine experts, with standards revised sport by sport and data published. The rules of a sport have always belonged to the people who play it; one-sided administrative rulings only leave everyone aggrieved.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The provincial games registration system has thrown up an unprecedented case: a transgender woman athlete who has completed full medical transition and legal gender change has applied to compete in the women's weightlifting event. Current provincial rules follow the old standard of medical documentation plus a two-year hormone waiting period, and she meets all of it. But the coaches of several rivals have signed a challenge, saying that the strength advantage has not fully disappeared. The latest framework from the international federation suggests each sport set its own standard. The provincial sports bureau has one week to decide whether she can compete.

scene: 独居的八十一岁陈婆婆半年内跌倒两次，第二次在地板上躺了六个小时才被送饭的儿子发现。民政部门推广的「安心屋」计划提供全套智能监护：毫米波跌倒雷达、睡眠监测、离床感应，异常自动通知子女与社区站。她的女儿想立刻签约，陈婆婆却抗拒：「我还没死，就已经被机器看着了。」社区调解会上，医生、女儿和老人各自坐着，你被请来协调。

options.t: 我会支持安装，但把控制权交给陈婆婆：雷达只检测跌倒不上传画面、通知名单她自己定、随时可以自己关掉。监护的目标不是「知道老人一切」，是「摔倒后有人来」——让技术服务于她的安全，而不是子女的安心。
options.t_en: I will support installing it, but with control handed to Mrs Chen: the radar detects falls only and uploads no images, she decides who is on the alert list, and she can switch it off herself at any time. The aim of monitoring is not to know everything about an old person, but to make sure somebody comes when she falls. Let the technology serve her safety rather than her children's peace of mind.

options.t: 我会反对整套技术方案，主张人回来：跌倒的风险根源是独居，答案不是更密的传感器而是更近的人。与其每月付设备费，不如资助社区送餐、日间照料中心和「多户合住」的养老互助——机器能报警，但不能扶起，更不能说话。
options.t_en: I will oppose the whole technological package and argue for bringing people back. The root cause of the fall risk is living alone, and the answer is not denser sensors but closer human beings. Rather than paying equipment fees every month, fund community meal delivery, day care centres and shared housing arrangements for mutual support in old age. A machine can raise an alarm, but it cannot lift you up, and it certainly cannot talk to you.

options.t: 我会支持技术，但主张公共承接而非家庭绑架：由社区站统一签约、统一值守，子女只收「已处理」的结果，不收全天候的监控画面。让监护从「子女的孝心责任」变成「公共服务的应答责任」——技术的伦理问题，常常是制度问题的外衣。
options.t_en: I will support the technology, but argue that it should be publicly provided rather than loaded onto the family: the community station signs the contract and runs the monitoring, and the children receive only the result that something has been dealt with, not round-the-clock footage. Turn monitoring from a duty of filial piety into a duty of public service to respond. Ethical problems with technology are often institutional problems wearing a coat.

options.t: 我会尊重陈婆婆本人的最终决定权，哪怕这意味着风险：成年人有权选择自己承担的风险，八十一岁不注销这个权利。我能做的是把选项摆全——陪她试住一周、见见用过的老人、听听社区的上门频次——然后让她自己做决定。
options.t_en: I will respect Mrs Chen's own final decision, even when that means accepting the risk. An adult has the right to choose which risks to carry, and turning eighty-one does not cancel that right. What I can do is lay the options out in full: sit with her through a week's trial, let her meet other people who have used it, tell her how often the community station would visit, and then let her decide.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: Eighty-one-year-old Mrs Chen, who lives alone, has fallen twice in six months; the second time she lay on the floor for six hours before her son, bringing food, found her. The civil affairs department's Safe Home programme offers a full smart monitoring package: millimetre-wave fall radar, sleep monitoring, bed-exit sensors, with alerts sent automatically to her children and the community station. Her daughter wants to sign immediately. Mrs Chen resists: I am not dead yet, and a machine is already watching me. At the community mediation meeting, the doctor, the daughter and the old woman are each seated, and you have been asked to coordinate.

scene: 「先享后付」服务在大学生中的渗透率一年翻倍：四期免息、一键开通、三十秒审批。校园周边的奶茶店、球鞋店与美妆柜台处处是它的标志。学生处统计，已有数百名学生同时使用三四个平台拆东墙补西墙，有人靠生活费周转，有人瞒着家里打零工还账。金融监管闭门会上，平台方强调「我们只是把大人的支付方式给了年轻人」；消费保护组织要求重拳整治。

options.t: 我会主张最严的一档：禁止向无稳定收入的学生开通信用类支付，全部平台强制共享借款人负债数据、统一设置总授信上限。分期的便利是真的，但把信贷的获客逻辑对准还没有收入的人，等于把风险包装成礼物送给最接不住的人。
options.t_en: I would argue for the strictest tier: ban credit-based payment for students without stable income, require all platforms to share borrower debt data, and set a unified total credit ceiling. The convenience of installments is real, but aiming the customer acquisition logic of credit at people who have no income yet is dressing risk up as a gift and handing it to those least able to catch it.

options.t: 我会主张管披露、不管产品：年轻人不是不谙世事，管理自己的债务也是成年人必修的课。要做的是把真实年化、违约后果、多头借贷风险做成显著提示，学校开金融素养课。把十八岁的人当孩子保护，只会培养出二十八岁还不会算账的人。
options.t_en: I would regulate disclosure, not the product. Young people are not naive, and managing your own debt is a required course in adulthood. What is needed is prominent warnings about the real annualized rate, the consequences of default and the risks of borrowing from multiple lenders, plus financial literacy courses in schools. Treating an eighteen-year-old as a child to be protected only produces a twenty-eight-year-old who still cannot do the arithmetic.

options.t: 我会主张抓平台责任而非抓用户：谁放贷谁担风险——分期平台须对用户坏账承担连带责任，自然就会认真核验偿付能力；同时禁止以「免息」名义向商家转嫁费用、诱导分期。让放贷的知道疼，比让借钱的长记性有效。
options.t_en: I would target platform responsibility rather than users. Whoever lends carries the risk: installment platforms should bear joint liability for bad debt, and then they will check repayment capacity seriously. At the same time, ban passing costs to merchants under the name of interest-free offers and ban inducing people into installments. Making the lender feel pain works better than making the borrower remember a lesson.

options.t: 我会主张冷静期加硬熔断：开通后首月额度封顶、单笔超过月生活费的分期需二十四小时冷静期、累计逾期立即全平台冻结新增。目标是让人在深夜的购物车里多一次醒来的机会——规则不阻止消费，只阻止来不及思考的消费。
options.t_en: I would argue for a cooling-off period and a hard circuit breaker: a capped limit in the first month after activation, a twenty-four-hour cooling-off period for any installment larger than a month's living costs, and immediate freezing of new credit across all platforms once someone falls into arrears. The goal is to give people one more chance to wake up while the shopping cart is still open at midnight. Rules do not stop spending; they stop spending that has no time to think.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The penetration of buy-now-pay-later services among university students doubled in a year: four interest-free installments, one-tap activation, approval in thirty seconds. The bubble tea shops, sneaker stores and cosmetics counters around campus all carry its logo. The student affairs office counts several hundred students juggling three or four platforms at once, robbing Peter to pay Paul. Some are scraping by on their living allowance; some are secretly working part-time jobs to pay the debt back. At a closed-door financial regulation meeting, the platforms stress that they are simply giving young people the payment methods adults already have, while consumer groups demand a crackdown.

scene: 启明核电站的两台机组将在八年后到达原设计寿命。电网规划面临抉择：延寿二十年，可为城市的脱碳目标提供近三成的稳定基荷电力，但抗震等级需按新标准补强，废料的中期存储也已接近饱和；提前退役则意味着以燃气调峰补位，碳目标倒退五年，数万人的产业社区将空心化。附近居民在两轮听证里态度分裂，反核的年轻人和电厂的职工家属各自带着标语。

options.t: 我会支持延寿：在储能技术真正成熟之前，可调度的低碳基荷没有替代品。用燃气补位换来的「安全」，是用确定的碳排放和倒退五年的气候目标支付的——风险要量化，不能只靠恐惧定价。废料问题同步启动永久处置库选址，别再拖给下一代。
options.t_en: I would support the extension. Until storage technology truly matures there is no substitute for dispatchable low-carbon baseload. The safety bought by filling the gap with gas is paid for in certain emissions and a climate target set back five years; risk must be quantified, not priced by fear alone. In parallel, start siting a permanent waste repository rather than deferring it to the next generation.

options.t: 我会主张按期退役：核电的风险不在日常运行，在于那条一旦出错就不可逆的尾部——以及留给几百年的废料。气候目标可以追，被污染的土壤和水追不回来。把延寿的钱全部投进电网、储能与需求侧管理，十年后的电网不需要赌。
options.t_en: I would argue for retirement on schedule. The risk of nuclear power is not day-to-day operation but the tail that cannot be reversed once it goes wrong, and the waste left for centuries. Climate targets can be caught up; contaminated soil and water cannot. Put all the extension money into the grid, storage and demand-side management, and the grid of ten years from now will not need a gamble.

options.t: 我会支持延寿，但把条件写死：延寿收益的固定比例注入本地的能源转型基金，用于受影响社区的就业转换与屋顶光伏；永久处置库选址落定前，延寿许可每年复核。让为全城供电的社区，也从电里拿到自己的那份未来。
options.t_en: I would support the extension, but with the conditions written in hard: a fixed share of the extension's returns goes into a local energy transition fund for job conversion in affected communities and rooftop solar, and until a permanent repository site is settled the extension licence is reviewed annually. Let the community that powers the whole city also take its own share of the future from the electricity.

options.t: 我会把决定权还给受影响的居民：在专业机构的安全评估全部公开后，由电站周边三个县市与全市居民分别公决，多数决决定延寿与否，法定补偿方案随票同步公布。电是公共品，风险却落在具体的经纬度上——让承担风险的人签字，是能源决策的底线。
options.t_en: I would give the decision back to the people affected: after the safety assessments by the professional bodies are fully published, hold separate referendums among the three counties around the plant and among the city's residents, with the majority deciding extension or not and the statutory compensation plan published alongside the ballot. Electricity is a public good, but the risk lands on specific coordinates; having those who bear the risk sign off is the floor for energy decisions.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: The two units at Qiming nuclear plant reach the end of their design life in eight years. The grid plan faces a choice: a twenty-year extension would supply nearly thirty percent of the city's steady baseload for decarbonisation, but seismic reinforcement to the new standard would be needed, and interim waste storage is near saturation. Early retirement means filling the gap with gas peaking plants, setting the carbon target back five years and hollowing out an industrial community of tens of thousands. Nearby residents are split across two hearings, the young anti-nuclear group and the plant workers' families each with their own placards.

scene: 气象部门的新模型将东湾海堤后的三个街区划入「五十年一遇」洪水区——模型显示，海堤再加高也只能买到二十年。市政府提出「有序后退」方案：以高于市价三成的价格征收易淹房屋，居民迁往高地的安置社区；老住户们组成「守土会」，第三代渔民的会长说：「你们买得走房子，买不走祖坟和滩涂上的路。」公开征求意见的最后一天，你在留言栏前停了很久。

options.t: 我会支持征收与迁置：气候模型不会谈判，二十年后的决堤不会按补偿标准出牌。三成溢价、整体社区搬迁、原址改为湿地公园与缓冲带——用今天的硬决定，换明天没有人被从屋顶上救走。悲伤是真的，但账也是真的。
options.t_en: I will support the buyout and resettlement. Climate models do not negotiate, and the seawall giving way in twenty years will not follow the compensation schedule. A thirty percent premium, a whole community moved together, and the old site turned into wetland park and buffer zone: a hard decision today so that nobody is lifted off a roof tomorrow. The grief is real, but so is the arithmetic.

options.t: 我会反对强制征收，改为自愿加退出：愿走的以溢价收购，愿留的自担风险——政府不再为高风险区修建和维护海堤，洪水保险按真实风险定价。纳税人没有义务为有人想住在滩涂上的诗意无限买单，居民也没有义务为规划的历史欠账搬家。
options.t_en: I will oppose compulsory purchase and replace it with voluntary exit: those who want to go are bought out at a premium, those who want to stay carry the risk themselves. The government stops building and maintaining the seawall in the high-risk zone, and flood insurance is priced at true risk. Taxpayers have no duty to underwrite the poetry of living on a tidal flat, and residents have no duty to move because of a planning debt run up decades ago.

options.t: 我会主张把钱花在硬防御上：加高海堤、建设排洪泵站与可渗透街区，二十年就是一代人的安居。城市化的历史就是与水争地的历史，「后退」一旦开始就没有终点——今天东湾退了，明天轮到哪个街区？
options.t_en: I will argue for putting the money into hard defences instead: raise the seawall, build stormwater pumping stations and permeable streets. Twenty years is a generation of settled life. The history of cities is the history of taking land from water, and once retreat begins there is no end to it: East Bay pulls back today, which block is next tomorrow?

options.t: 我会支持方向，但反对现在的方案：搬迁社区必须先建好——学校、渔港的替代泊位、祖坟的整体迁置和每年的祭扫交通，都要写进有法律效力的时间表。否则「有序后退」就只是「无序抛弃」的行政用语。买得走房子，就也要容得下滩涂上的路。
options.t_en: I will support the direction but oppose the plan as it stands: the resettlement community must be built first, with schools, a replacement berth for the fishing port, the collective relocation of the graves and annual transport for tomb-sweeping all written into a legally binding timetable. Otherwise orderly retreat is just the administrative term for disorderly abandonment. If you can buy the houses, you can also make room for the paths on the tidal flats.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: The weather service's new model puts three blocks behind the East Bay seawall inside a one-in-fifty-year flood zone, and shows that raising the wall higher buys only another twenty years. The city proposes an orderly retreat: buy out the flood-prone houses at thirty percent above market price and move residents to a resettlement community on higher ground. The old residents have formed a keep-the-land association, and its chairman, a third-generation fisherman, says: you can buy the houses, but you cannot buy the ancestral graves or the paths across the tidal flats. On the last day of public comment, you stand a long time in front of the comment box.

scene: 月活九亿的聊天平台「信巢」再次拒绝开放互操作：其他地区的监管已要求大型通讯服务相互打通，本地用户组织也提交了请愿——换平台不该意味着失联。平台方回应称，强制互通将削弱端到端加密、放大垃圾信息，且小平台可以免费搭乘它二十年建成的网络。技术委员会的听证记录里，工程师们承认：互通在技术上可行，真正的分歧是「谁有权决定网络的边界」。

options.t: 我会支持强制互操作：九亿月活不是平台的私产，是基础设施的既成事实。锁定效应让「用户用脚投票」沦为神话——离开的成本是失联，这不是自由选择。监管该管的就是这种结构性权力：协议互通、数据可携带，把网络还给用户。
options.t_en: I would support mandatory interoperability. Nine hundred million monthly users is not a platform's private property; it is an established fact of infrastructure. Lock-in turns voting with your feet into a myth, because the cost of leaving is losing touch, and that is not a free choice. This structural power is exactly what regulation should address: interoperable protocols, portable data, and the network given back to users.

options.t: 我会反对强制互通：平台是企业家与工程师承担全部风险建成的，互联互通意味着任何人都能搭便车——包括不需要遵守任何规则的人。用户真想离开随时可以，绑定他们的不是技术，是关系网络的惯性，那不该由监管来拆。
options.t_en: I would oppose mandatory interoperability. The platform was built by entrepreneurs and engineers who carried all the risk, and interoperability means anyone can ride free, including people who follow no rules at all. Users who really want to leave can leave at any time. What binds them is not technology but the inertia of their social network, and that is not something regulation should take apart.

options.t: 我会支持互通，但按层级设计：强制的只是消息基础协议——文本、语音、转账请求在不同平台间可互达；加密标准、群功能、商业接口留给各平台自建。像电话号码互通一样管「通」，不管「好用的程度」，竞争就还在，锁定就没了。
options.t_en: I would support interoperability, but designed in layers. Only the basic messaging protocol would be mandatory: text, voice and payment requests crossing between platforms. Encryption standards, group features and commercial interfaces stay with each platform. Regulate connectivity the way telephone numbers are regulated, not the quality of the experience. Competition survives and lock-in disappears.

options.t: 我会主张协议层公共化：由公共机构或开放标准组织维护一套中立的通讯协议，平台自愿接入、接入者获得政府采购与公共服务的入口。让互通成为公共品而非监管惩罚——重要的不是拆掉信巢，是让信巢以外的世界不再需要它点头。
options.t_en: I would argue for making the protocol layer public. Have a public body or an open standards organization maintain a neutral messaging protocol, with platforms joining voluntarily and those that join getting access to public procurement and public services. Make interoperability a public good rather than a regulatory penalty. What matters is not breaking up Xin Nest but making the world outside it no longer need its permission.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: Xin Nest, a chat platform with nine hundred million monthly users, has again refused to open up interoperability. Regulators elsewhere already require large messaging services to connect with one another, and a local users' group has filed a petition: switching platforms should not mean losing touch with everyone. The platform responds that forced interoperability would weaken end-to-end encryption, amplify spam, and let smaller platforms ride free on a network it spent twenty years building. In the technology committee's hearing record, engineers admit that interoperability is technically feasible and that the real disagreement is who has the right to decide where the network's boundaries lie.

scene: 市残联的抽样显示，具备劳动能力的残障人士实际就业率不足四成，而雇主侧的调查更扎心：多数企业承认招聘时「看见轮椅就跳过」，理由从安全隐患到保险成本不等。三种政策方案摆在桌面上：法定雇佣配额（企业须有百分之二残障员工，未达标缴差额金）；纯反歧视诉讼路线；以及税收抵免激励。三方都有各地的成败案例，市里的试点只能选一条先走。

options.t: 我会选配额加差额金：偏见是几十年长成的，不会因为一部反歧视法就融化。配额的粗暴恰恰是它的效率——企业为了让差额金不白交，会自己找到能干的人。再把差额金全部注入职业重建与无障碍改造，形成闭环。
options.t_en: I would choose the quota plus levy. Prejudice took decades to grow and will not melt because of one anti-discrimination law. The crudeness of a quota is exactly its efficiency, because to avoid paying the levy for nothing firms will find capable people themselves. Then channel the whole levy into vocational rehabilitation and accessibility upgrades, closing the loop.

options.t: 我会选反歧视诉讼路线：配额制最大的代价由残障者自己支付——从此每个岗位上的残障员工都要背着「配额来的」的标签。让每位求职者拥有追究歧视性拒录的权利，把正义建立在权利上，而不是配额的账本上。
options.t_en: I would choose the anti-discrimination litigation route. The biggest cost of a quota is paid by disabled people themselves, because from then on every disabled employee in a post carries the label of having been a quota hire. Give every jobseeker the right to challenge discriminatory rejection, and build justice on rights rather than on a quota ledger.

options.t: 我会选税收抵免：按实际雇佣人数与岗位适配成本抵免企业税收，无障碍改造全额退税。让雇用残障者从「道德要求」变成「划算的事」——市场不响应说教，但永远响应价格。补贴跟着人走，不跟着名单走。
options.t_en: I would choose tax credits: credit firms against tax according to actual numbers employed and the cost of adapting the workplace, with full refunds for accessibility works. Make employing disabled people go from a moral requirement to a good deal, because the market does not respond to sermons but always responds to prices. Let the subsidy follow the person, not the list.

options.t: 我会主张公共部门先走配额、私部门走激励：政府和国企按百分之三强制达标并公示进度，把差额金用于私企的抵免资金池。公共机构本就是社会价值的示范单位——要求市场做到的，先让自己的账本说话。
options.t_en: I would argue that the public sector should go first with a quota and the private sector with incentives: government and state-owned enterprises required to meet three percent and publish progress, with the levy funding a credit pool for private firms. Public bodies are supposed to model social values, so before demanding it of the market, let your own ledger speak.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A sample survey by the municipal disabled persons' federation shows that fewer than forty percent of disabled people who are able to work are actually employed, and the employer-side survey is blunter still: most firms admit they skip the application when they see a wheelchair, citing anything from safety liability to insurance costs. Three policy options are on the table: a statutory quota requiring firms to have two percent disabled staff or pay a levy, a pure anti-discrimination litigation route, and tax credits as an incentive. Each has success and failure stories elsewhere, and the city's pilot can only start with one.

scene: 你与同性伴侣共同生活十二年，在法院登记伴侣关系。一对同性朋友意外离世，留下七岁的女儿；孩子祖父母年迈体弱且多年未联系。学校老师多次家访，希望为孩子安排一个稳定的家。朋友临终前口头说过「希望你们能照顾她」，但未立遗嘱；社会福利机构评估认为你们是孩子目前最合适的监护候选人。你和孩子已相处两年，感情深厚。祖父母得知后沉默数日，提出愿接手但需要孩子每周在你们家过周末。

options.t: 我会正式申请共同监护：十二年的家庭关系是事实上的家庭，孩子也需要连续性。法律应当承认这种关系——若承认不了，至少要给这个孩子一个稳定的家，我们愿用其他法律工具（事实监护、特别许可）补位。
options.t_en: I will formally apply for joint guardianship. Twelve years of family life is a family in fact, and the child needs continuity. The law ought to recognise that relationship; if it cannot, then at the very least this child should be given a stable home, and we will fill the gap with whatever other legal instruments exist, de facto guardianship or a special licence.

options.t: 我会先走完法律程序再决定：在法庭裁定前不擅自介入孩子的抚养。监护资格要按法律走完评估、听证、上诉全流程——无论结果是否对我们有利。如果法律不让同性伴侣共同监护，我会作为个人申请人单独评估。
options.t_en: I will go through the legal process first and decide afterwards: no stepping into the child's upbringing before the court rules. Guardianship has to run the full course of assessment, hearing and appeal, whichever way it comes out for us. If the law will not let same-sex partners hold joint guardianship, I will apply individually and be assessed on my own.

options.t: 我会主动向孩子的祖父母让出监护主导权：血缘与亲情不是可以被「更合适」取代的。我们承诺做孩子成长里的稳定支持者——课后托管、长假同住——但日常监护与法律签字权留给祖父母。
options.t_en: I will offer the grandparents the leading role in guardianship. Blood and family feeling are not things a more suitable candidate can replace. We will commit to being steady supporters in the child's life, after-school care, long holidays at our home, but day-to-day custody and the right to sign legally stay with the grandparents.

options.t: 我会主张制度应主动修订：同性伴侣的共同监护权需要立法明确——不是每次让个案去争。把「事实家庭」概念写进民法，让无数个十二年不靠法官的自由裁量就被看见。
options.t_en: I will argue that the system should be amended of its own accord: joint guardianship for same-sex partners needs to be written into law, rather than fought for case by case. Put the concept of the family in fact into the civil code, so that countless twelve-year relationships are seen without depending on a judge's discretion.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: You have lived with your same-sex partner for twelve years, and your partnership is registered with the court. A same-sex couple who were friends of yours have died, leaving a seven-year-old daughter; the child's grandparents are old and frail and have not been in contact for years. The school's teachers have visited several times, wanting a stable home arranged for the girl. Before dying, your friends said orally that they hoped you would look after her, but left no will; the welfare agency's assessment finds that you are currently the most suitable guardianship candidates. You have known the child for two years and are deeply attached. The grandparents, after days of silence, say they are willing to take her, but ask that she spend every weekend at your home.

scene: 本地一家化妆品公司宣称，2024 年起所有新产品的人体安全性测试改用「器官芯片」——一种由人类干细胞培养的微型组织芯片，模拟皮肤、角膜、肝脏对刺激的反应。动物保护协会认为是历史性突破；但也有科学家指出，芯片无法模拟完整的免疫系统与代谢反馈，长期安全性仍有盲区。监管局草案分两派：全面认可芯片替代动物测试（设五年过渡期）vs 仍要求动物测试作最终验证手段。

options.t: 我会支持全面认可芯片替代：动物测试对人类的预测率本就有限，伦理成本由无辜生命承担。器官芯片是科学进步，监管要跟上——明确禁止同期再做动物重复验证，五年过渡期内逐年淘汰。
options.t_en: I would support full recognition of chips as the replacement. Animal tests were never very predictive for humans, and the ethical cost was carried by innocent lives. Organ chips are scientific progress and regulation should keep up: explicitly ban duplicate animal verification in the same period, and phase it out year by year across the five-year transition.

options.t: 我会支持但保留并行的「兜底验证」：芯片是首选，但涉及长期毒性、跨器官效应、生物累积的产品，必须保留有限的动物测试作最终验证。进步不能建立在「我们百分百猜对」上——错一次的代价太高。
options.t_en: I would support it but keep a parallel fallback verification. Chips first, but for products involving long-term toxicity, cross-organ effects or bioaccumulation, a limited number of animal tests must stay as the final check. Progress cannot rest on assuming we will get it a hundred percent right; the cost of one error is too high.

options.t: 我会主张让市场做主：哪家公司最先把产品卖出去、并被消费者起诉赔偿，就说明哪种测试方法靠谱。监管不需要偏好任何一种科学路线，只需要保证「出了事有人负责」。
options.t_en: I would argue for letting the market decide. Whichever company puts a product on the market first and then gets sued for damages shows which test method actually works. Regulation does not need to prefer any scientific route; it only needs to guarantee that when something goes wrong, someone is liable.

options.t: 我会主张建立公共的器官芯片测试平台：把芯片做成公共基础设施——任何企业、任何科研机构都可申请使用，测试结果全国统一数据库。这是一项关乎生命伦理的科学，不该让商业公司各自闭门造车。
options.t_en: I would argue for a public organ chip testing platform, making the chips public infrastructure that any company or research institute can apply to use, with results going into one national database. This is science that touches the ethics of life, and it should not be left to commercial firms each working behind closed doors.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: A local cosmetics company says that from 2024 all its new products will be tested for human safety using organ chips: thumbnail-sized tissue cultures grown from human stem cells that mimic how skin, cornea and liver react to an irritant. Animal welfare groups call it a historic breakthrough. Some scientists point out that chips cannot reproduce a full immune system or metabolic feedback, so long-term safety still has blind spots. The regulator's draft has two camps: full recognition of chips as a replacement for animal testing with a five-year transition, or keeping animal tests as the final verification step.

scene: 博物馆收到一幅清代宫廷画家佚作，画面三分之一的颜料层已脱落、霉斑覆盖。多位修复专家的意见分歧：传统派主张「修旧如旧」——用矿物颜料填补缺口但保留所有历史痕迹；现代派主张「可识别修补」——用当代工艺补全画面但留下视觉区隔；激进派建议用 AI 复原原作可能的样貌、用 AR 让观众「看到原作」。馆方将在下月公开展出最终方案。

options.t: 我会选传统修旧如旧：原作的历史是它的一部分——每一处霉斑都是它被那个时代对待过的证据。观众的情感连接建立在「我看到的是真实物件」上，任何 AI 复原都是赝品。
options.t_en: I would choose the traditional repair as of old. The work's history is part of it, and every patch of mould is evidence of how an era treated it. Visitors' emotional connection rests on knowing they are seeing the real object, and any AI reconstruction is a forgery.

options.t: 我会选可识别修补：让观众能看清原作完整构图，也清楚知道哪部分是现代补全。这是博物馆的伦理——既不假装历史是完整的，也不让残缺掩盖原作的精彩。修补处用淡淡的「补色」而非纯白。
options.t_en: I would choose detectable retouching: let visitors see the complete composition clearly and also know exactly which parts are modern infill. That is museum ethics, neither pretending history is whole nor letting the damage hide the painting's brilliance. Use a faint toned infill rather than pure white at the repairs.

options.t: 我会选 AI 复原加 AR：让观众戴设备看到「原作可能的样貌」，旁边有完整图录说明复原依据。修复史本身就是艺术史的一章——不掩盖、不假装，让观众获得两层的理解。
options.t_en: I would choose AI reconstruction plus AR: let visitors wear a device to see what the original probably looked like, with a full catalogue note beside it explaining the basis for the reconstruction. The history of restoration is itself a chapter of art history, so conceal nothing, pretend nothing, and give visitors two layers of understanding.

options.t: 我会主张公开展出所有方案 + 观众票选：修复不是专家的私事。让三种方案在展厅并列展示三个月，让每位观众投票、留下意见——艺术属于公众，修复权也应分享。
options.t_en: I would argue for exhibiting all the options publicly and letting visitors vote. Restoration is not a private matter for experts. Show the three approaches side by side in the gallery for three months and let every visitor vote and leave comments; art belongs to the public, and so should the right to restore it.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: The museum has acquired a lost work by a Qing court painter; a third of the pigment layer has flaked away and mould covers much of the surface. The conservators are divided. The traditionalists want repair as of old, filling the losses with mineral pigments while keeping every trace of history. The modernists want detectable retouching, completing the picture with contemporary methods but leaving a visible distinction. The radicals suggest using AI to reconstruct what the original probably looked like and AR so visitors can see the original. The museum will publish its final plan next month.

scene: 本地大学游泳队一位出生时被指定为男性的跨性别运动员，在完成两年激素治疗后，希望参加本年度女子组 100 米自由泳比赛。生理学论文显示，激素治疗显著降低肌肉量与血红蛋白水平，但骨骼结构与肌腱长度难以逆转。队伍里其他女生的反应两极：有人说「她也是女性，凭什么不让参赛」，有人要求组委会出具「运动公平的生理指标证明」。赛前一周，校方尚未给出最终决定。

options.t: 我会支持她参赛：性别认同是基本权利，体育精神是参与而非比较。运动场上不应有「生理公平的生理指标证明」的设定——那是把人按身体打分。运动员的身份就是身份证上的身份。
options.t_en: I will support her competing. Gender identity is a basic right, and the spirit of sport is taking part rather than comparison. There should be no such requirement as physiological proof of fairness on the field; that is scoring people by their bodies. An athlete's status is the status on her identity document.

options.t: 我会反对她参赛：女子组存在的全部意义是公平竞争。激素治疗不能完全逆转的骨骼与肌腱优势是生理事实——让一位身体不属于女子组生理范围的运动员参赛，对其他女生不公平。
options.t_en: I will oppose her competing. The entire reason a women's category exists is fair competition. The skeletal and tendon advantage that hormone therapy cannot fully reverse is a physiological fact, and letting an athlete whose body falls outside the physiological range of the women's category compete is unfair to the other women.

options.t: 我会主张设立过渡组或按睾酮上限分组：现行二元分组太粗。运动生理学已经有按睾酮水平等指标的细分组方案。问题不是「她能不能进女子组」，而是分组方式该重新设计——让每类身体条件都有自己的竞技舞台。
options.t_en: I will argue for a transition category, or categories set by a testosterone ceiling. The current binary split is too crude, and sports physiology already has finer groupings based on testosterone and other measures. The question is not whether she can enter the women's event but how the categories should be redesigned, so that every kind of body has a stage to compete on.

options.t: 我会主张由运动员自行决定报名哪个组：取消强制性别组，改为按身体指标自愿申报。规则透明、指标公开、运动员承担选择后果。这是科学问题不是道德问题——让生理学和选择权各自归位。
options.t_en: I will argue that athletes decide for themselves which category to enter: drop compulsory sex categories and let people declare voluntarily according to physical indicators. Rules transparent, indicators published, the athlete carrying the consequences of the choice. This is a scientific question, not a moral one; let physiology and the right to choose each go back where they belong.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A swimmer on the local university team, assigned male at birth, has completed two years of hormone therapy and wants to compete in the women's 100 metres freestyle this season. Physiology papers show that hormone therapy markedly reduces muscle mass and haemoglobin levels, but that skeletal structure and tendon length are difficult to reverse. Reaction within the squad has been sharply divided: some say she is a woman too, so on what grounds should she be excluded; others want the organisers to produce physiological proof of sporting fairness. A week before the meet, the university has not issued a final decision.

scene: 你所在社区的「老年食堂」运营五年，去年开始出现十二名失独或孤寡老人每天独自来吃饭，饭后再独自离开。社工统计，这些老人家中无人，子女或已离世或长期不联系。志愿者协会提出三套方案：上门送餐（每餐十二元）、社区集体午餐（每餐八元）、加装远程健康监测设备（每月八十元）。街道办说预算只够做其中一项，必须排序。

options.t: 我会先做社区集体午餐：人不是只需要吃饭——独居最致命的是孤独。集体午餐每天都能见面，让食堂变成社交场所，再配两名社工关注异常。送餐虽暖，但把人关在家里反而更糟。
options.t_en: I would do the communal lunch first. People do not only need food; loneliness is the deadliest part of living alone. A communal lunch means seeing each other every day and turns the canteen into a place to socialize, with two social workers watching for anything unusual. Delivering meals is kind, but keeping people shut in their homes is worse.

options.t: 我会先做上门送餐：十二位老人很多已行动不便，再小的距离也是距离。让他们来食堂是单方面的「省事」——应该把服务送上门。每次送餐也是社工上门评估安全的机会。
options.t_en: I would do home-delivered meals first. Many of these twelve already have limited mobility, and even a short distance is still a distance. Making them come to the canteen is convenience for the provider, one-sided. The service should go to them. Each delivery is also a chance for a social worker to check on them in person.

options.t: 我会先做远程健康监测：独居死亡事件的最大特征是「几天没人知道」。监测设备可以一发现异常就报警——这是成本最低、效益最高的生命守护。社交和送餐可以在装好监测后逐项叠加。
options.t_en: I would do remote health monitoring first. The defining feature of deaths among people living alone is that nobody knows for days. Monitoring equipment can raise an alarm the moment something is wrong. That is the cheapest and most effective protection of life. Social contact and meal delivery can be layered on once the monitoring is in place.

options.t: 我会主张预算本来就不够——应向街道办申请追加，并联动医院与志愿组织分担成本：把「老年人最后的日子」当成系统工程，而非一道预算选择题。
options.t_en: I would argue that the budget is simply not enough. We should ask the subdistrict office for more and bring in hospitals and volunteer groups to share the cost: treat the last days of old people's lives as a system-wide problem, not as a multiple-choice question about a budget.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: The community canteen for the elderly has been running for five years. Since last year, twelve elders who lost their only child or live alone have come to eat by themselves every day and gone home by themselves afterwards. Social workers' records show that no one lives with them; their children have either died or have not been in touch for years. The volunteers' association has put forward three options: home-delivered meals at twelve yuan each, a communal lunch at the canteen at eight yuan each, or remote health monitoring equipment at eighty yuan a month. The subdistrict office says the budget covers only one, and they must be ranked.

scene: 你在金融调解委员会做志愿者，一位六十五岁退休老人向你哭诉：她被短视频里的「投资老师」带着做「高息理财」亏损了三十六万养老金，账户里只剩不到一万。她不明白那些「老师」是骗子，平台上的广告是合规的（持牌机构投放），她签过电子合同。子女在海外，她不想让家人担心。调解委员会只能建议她民事诉讼，但她既没钱请律师，也承受不起漫长诉讼。

options.t: 我会帮她对接法律援助并代为提起诉讼：合法权利不容平台用合规广告逃避。调解委员会可申请免费律师代理、协助电子证据固定——让平台为「诈骗广告」承担连带责任，倒逼平台整改广告审核。
options.t_en: I would help her get legal aid and file the suit on her behalf. Her lawful rights cannot be evaded by a platform hiding behind compliant advertising. The mediation committee can apply for free representation and help secure the electronic evidence, making the platform jointly liable for fraudulent advertising and forcing it to tighten ad review.

options.t: 我会帮她联系平台的客户关怀通道申请部分退款，并签署不再追诉：诉讼对她是二次伤害、跨代影响。平台愿意赔多少就多少，让她拿到能安稳度日的钱。制度问题归制度，个人损失归个人。
options.t_en: I would help her contact the platform's customer care channel to request a partial refund and sign away further claims. Litigation is a second injury for her, with knock-on effects across generations. Whatever the platform will pay, take it, so that she has money to live on in peace. Systemic problems are for the system; individual losses are for the individual.

options.t: 我会劝她报警并联系金融监管局举报：这是诈骗，不是投资亏损。监管局收到投诉才有动力查处这家平台——一个老人追不回来三十六万，但能让千万老人不再被骗。先公后私。
options.t_en: I would advise her to report it to the police and to the financial regulator. This is fraud, not an investment loss. Only when the regulator receives complaints does it have an incentive to investigate the platform; one elderly person may never recover 360,000, but millions of others can be spared. Public first, private second.

options.t: 我会主张平台应为「无投资经验」用户强制限制高风险产品：六十五岁、零投资经验、不读合同——任何一个属性都该触发「不可购买」的熔断。让平台用算法保护弱势用户。
options.t_en: I would argue that platforms must restrict high-risk products for users with no investment experience. Sixty-five years old, zero experience, does not read contracts: any one of those should trigger a circuit breaker. Let platforms use algorithms to protect vulnerable users.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: You volunteer on a financial mediation committee. A sixty-five-year-old retiree tells you, in tears, that an investment teacher in short videos led her into high-yield wealth products and she lost 360,000 of her pension, leaving under ten thousand in her account. She did not understand that the teachers were fraudsters: the ads on the platform were compliant, placed by licensed firms, and she signed an electronic contract. Her children are overseas and she does not want to worry them. The committee can only advise civil litigation, but she cannot afford a lawyer and cannot bear a long lawsuit.

scene: 市政府推「光伏屋顶全覆盖」计划——所有三层以上新建住宅强制配套光伏，未配套的不予验收。但老城区的居民反对意见尖锐：屋顶产权属整栋楼共有，单户无权决定；老房子承重不够；西晒面电费收益归谁不清楚。街道办在两轮协调会上仍僵持不下，最后决定「先从别墅区与新建小区试点，暂不强制老城区」。环保组织批评这是「嫌贫爱富」。

options.t: 我会支持原方案，老城区也应强制：气候不等人。先给老城区三年改造补贴，三年后仍未配套的征收碳排放补偿金。把光伏屋顶当成二十一世纪的电表基础——和接电、接水一样是公共服务。
options.t_en: I will support the original plan, with the old town included. The climate will not wait. Give the old town a three-year retrofit subsidy, and charge a carbon compensation fee on anyone still without panels after that. Treat a solar roof as the electricity meter of the twenty-first century: a public service like a water or power connection.

options.t: 我会同意分层推进但反对「老城区豁免」：老城区的问题是产权和补贴方案没设计好，不是不该做。街道办应协调出「屋顶共有+收益分账」的可执行方案；老房子承重不足可走光伏外墙或社区集中式。
options.t_en: I will agree to a phased approach but oppose an old-town exemption. The problem in the old town is that ownership and subsidy design were never worked out, not that it should not be done. The subdistrict should broker a workable shared-roof and revenue-split scheme, and where the structure cannot bear the load, use solar facades or community shared arrays.

options.t: 我会支持试点，但应让市场来推：补贴取消，改为电费收益的稳定预期。老城区不强制，靠邻居示范与电费账单上的收益数字慢慢说服人。环境问题最终靠经济激励解决。
options.t_en: I will support the pilot but argue the market should drive it: drop the subsidy and offer a stable expectation of electricity income instead. No compulsion in the old town; let neighbours' examples and the numbers on their bills do the persuading. Environmental problems are ultimately solved with economic incentives.

options.t: 我会主张先立法解决屋顶产权共有问题：屋顶产权归整栋业主共有，配套光伏需全体业主过半数同意。把「装光伏」和「修电梯」放同一法律框架——业主自治是基础，强制只是兜底。
options.t_en: I will argue for legislating the shared roof ownership question first: the roof belongs to all the owners in the building, and installing solar requires a majority of them to agree. Put installing panels in the same legal framework as installing a lift. Owners' self-government is the foundation, and compulsion is only the fallback.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: The city is pushing a rooftop solar for all programme: every new residential building of three storeys or more must be fitted with solar panels, and buildings without them will not pass completion inspection. Residents in the old town object sharply. The roof belongs to the whole building as shared property, and no single household can decide; the old structures cannot carry the weight; and it is unclear who would receive the income from the panels on a west-facing roof. Two rounds of coordination meetings have ended in deadlock, and the subdistrict has finally decided to start with the villa districts and new developments and leave the old town voluntary for now. Environmental groups call it favouring the rich and ignoring the poor.

scene: 连续三周四十度高温，市政避暑中心每天开放但入夜后空无一人——老人们怕回家路上中暑，宁可整夜睡在地铁站、商场楼梯间。一位政协委员提议「高温期间全市地铁二十四小时开放，露宿人员可在指定车厢过夜」，运营公司反对：清洁、安保、设备损耗成本每年预估三千万，且「鼓励露宿」有损城市形象。街道办说「先小范围试行」。

options.t: 我会支持全市地铁二十四小时开放：高温是公共卫生紧急事件——死人是真问题，「城市形象」是伪问题。三千万摊到全市人均不到三十元，省下的医保和殡葬费远超此数。先救人，再谈优化。
options.t_en: I would support opening the whole subway system around the clock. A heat wave is a public health emergency. People dying is a real problem; the city's image is a fake one. Thirty million spread across the city is under thirty yuan per person, and the savings in medical and funeral costs far exceed that. Save lives first, then talk about optimizing.

options.t: 我会反对全市全开，主张精准开放：高需求站点夜间开放，需求小的维持现状。地铁不是廉价旅馆——清洁、噪音、其他乘客权益都要管。开放的同时配套社工对接、医疗巡诊，才能解决「露宿」本身。
options.t_en: I would oppose opening everything and argue for opening precisely: stations with high demand open at night, the rest stay as they are. The subway is not a cheap hotel. Cleaning, noise and the rights of other passengers all have to be managed. Alongside opening, provide social work outreach and medical patrols, or the rough sleeping itself never gets solved.

options.t: 我会反对开放，主张加强社区级避暑中心与上门服务：地铁是出行设施，让地铁承担避难所功能是本末倒置。钱应该花在二十四小时值班的社区避暑中心、志愿上门送水和健康监测——把服务送到老人身边。
options.t_en: I would oppose opening the subway and argue for strengthening community cooling centers and home visits instead. The subway is a transport facility, and making it serve as a shelter is putting the cart before the horse. The money should go to community cooling centers staffed around the clock and volunteers delivering water and health checks, bringing the service to where the old people are.

options.t: 我会主张长期看，城市基础设施设计就要为极端高温重做预算：地铁、图书馆、社区中心都应预设「高温开放」模式。新建公共建筑强制配独立通风避暑层；老城区分批改造。把应急变成日常。
options.t_en: I would argue that in the long run, the city's infrastructure design has to budget for extreme heat. Subways, libraries and community centers should all have a built-in heat wave mode. New public buildings should be required to include a dedicated ventilated cooling floor; old districts should be retrofitted in phases. Turn the emergency into the everyday.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: For three weeks running the temperature has hit forty degrees. The city's cooling centers open every day but are empty after nightfall. Old people are afraid of heatstroke on the walk home and would rather sleep all night in subway stations and shopping mall stairwells. A political advisor proposes keeping the whole subway system open around the clock during heat waves, with people sleeping rough allowed to stay overnight in designated carriages. The operator objects: cleaning, security and equipment wear are estimated at thirty million a year, and encouraging rough sleeping damages the city's image. The subdistrict office says try it on a small scale first.

scene: 某短视频平台算法调研报告披露：每日使用超过四小时的用户中，十三至十八岁青少年占比百分之三十八；推荐算法会基于「完播率」自动投放越来越极端的内容以提升粘性；家长控制工具被设计得「难找、藏得深」。三位受害青少年家长联名起诉平台——其中一个孩子已确诊严重抑郁。教育部门希望平台「用算法保护孩子」——但需要家长签署「知情同意」才能开启青少年模式。

options.t: 我会支持强制全面开启青少年模式：算法不识别年龄就是失职。所有用户默认按年龄分级，十三至十八岁禁用算法推荐、二十二点后强制下线。家长「知情同意」的设计是故意给逃避留口子。
options.t_en: I would support mandatory teen mode for everyone. An algorithm that does not recognise age is failing at its job. All users should be age-graded by default, with recommendation algorithms off for thirteen-to-eighteen-year-olds and forced log-off after ten at night. The parental informed consent design deliberately leaves a gap to slip through.

options.t: 我会支持由家长与学校共同决定：算法强制开启是替家长做决定——但很多家长自己都不会管。应当给学校批量推送家长培训，强制十三至十八岁用户在父母账号下使用，家长可设每日时长上限。
options.t_en: I would support parents and schools deciding together. Forcing teen mode on is deciding for parents, yet plenty of parents cannot manage it themselves. Schools should push parent training out in bulk, require thirteen-to-eighteen-year-olds to use accounts under a parent's, and let parents set daily time limits.

options.t: 我会反对强制，主张让家长自己决定：算法分级应透明可查，家长一键开关。学校有责任教数字素养，家长有责任陪伴。把决定权留给家庭——而不是让平台当保姆。
options.t_en: I would oppose compulsion and let parents decide. Algorithm grading should be transparent and inspectable, with a one-click switch for parents. Schools are responsible for teaching digital literacy, parents for being present. Leave the decision with families rather than making the platform a nanny.

options.t: 我会主张把算法分级透明化、由独立第三方审计：用户可以看到自己被推送了什么类型内容、占比多少、平台如何分类。审计报告公开，让算法接受阳光——不靠强制，靠透明。
options.t_en: I would argue for making algorithm grading transparent and audited by an independent third party: users can see what type of content they are being pushed, in what proportion, and how the platform classifies it. Publish the audits and let the algorithm face the sun, not through compulsion but through transparency.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A research report on a short-video platform's algorithm has been released: among users who spend more than four hours a day, thirteen-to-eighteen-year-olds make up thirty-eight percent; the recommendation algorithm automatically pushes ever more extreme content based on completion rates in order to raise stickiness; and parental controls are designed to be hard to find and buried deep. Three parents of affected teenagers are suing the platform jointly, and one of the children has been diagnosed with severe depression. The education department wants the platform to protect children with algorithms, but teen mode only switches on after a parent signs an informed consent.

scene: 一名华裔混血新生儿在医院出生，母亲是当地人、父亲是华裔，名字「思远」是父亲坚持的中文名（寓思念远方）。登记处说父亲可填族裔或国籍，但姓名一栏不接受非本国字母表字符。父母双方都不愿改名——父亲希望儿子有文化根，母亲希望孩子有个特别的名字。校方未来招生时，「名字+族裔」的搭配可能让他在升学、就业、社交场合被反复询问「你来自哪里」。

options.t: 我会支持原名不改：名字是文化身份的一部分——孩子有权知道自己来自哪。改名是文化同化压力，要从法律上保证姓名自由，让「思远」和任何本国名字一样能在所有证件上显示。
options.t_en: I will support keeping the original name. A name is part of cultural identity, and a child has the right to know where he comes from. Changing it is pressure to assimilate. Name freedom should be protected in law, so that Siyuan can appear on every document just like any national name.

options.t: 我会支持加拼音或英文名双轨登记：日常用「思远+Siyuan」，证件可双轨显示。这不是向同化妥协，是给孩子多个工具——既保留文化根，又减少日常摩擦。族裔不是负担。
options.t_en: I will support dual-track registration with a transliteration or an English name: Siyuan in Chinese characters plus Siyuan in Latin letters in daily use, both shown on documents. This is not a compromise with assimilation but giving the child more tools: the cultural root kept, the daily friction reduced. Ethnicity is not a burden.

options.t: 我会主张从根本上扩大可登记字符集：不是给「思远」加拼音，而是让所有合法字符都能上身份证——这才是真正的姓名自由。一个国家的证件系统不应被自己的字母表限制。
options.t_en: I will argue for widening the registrable character set at the root: not adding a transliteration for Siyuan, but letting every legal character onto an identity document. That is what real name freedom means. A country's document system should not be limited by its own alphabet.

options.t: 我会建议父母现在就把孩子带到族裔混血社群：名字是开始，不是终点。让孩子从小知道「我是华裔混血+本地人」是有故事的群体，而非孤立个体。同伴社群比改名更能让他自信。
options.t_en: I will suggest the parents bring the child into mixed-heritage communities now. A name is the beginning, not the end. Let him grow up knowing that being Chinese-heritage and local is a group with a story, not an isolated individual. A community of peers will do more for his confidence than a change of name.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A mixed-heritage baby is born in hospital: the mother is local, the father of Chinese descent, and the name Siyuan is a Chinese name the father insisted on, meaning a longing for somewhere far away. The registry office says the father can enter an ethnicity or nationality, but the name field does not accept characters outside the national alphabet. Neither parent wants to change it: the father wants his son to have a cultural root, the mother wants the child to have a name that stands out. And later, when schools look at admissions, the combination of that name and that ethnicity may mean being asked again and again where he is from, in exams, in job interviews, in ordinary conversation.

scene: 入夏以来，你们小区地下车库的通风井拐角成了七八只流浪猫的窝。三楼的退休教师每天傍晚定点投喂，还用旧棉衣给它们做了窝，眼下母猫刚生完一窝小猫；底楼两户连着递了四份书面投诉，说跳蚤爬进了屋里、半夜叫春吵得婴儿睡不安稳。物业经理打算请第三方上门捕捉后统一处理，并贴出全小区禁喂的通知。你是业委会里唯一养宠的一票，你的意见会被直接写进决议。

options.t: 我会把「抓走」这一条从方案里划掉，改推 TNR：由愿意投喂的住户出钱出力，统一捕捉、绝育、耳标后再回置，并在远离底楼的位置做固定猫屋。邻里的问题最好由邻里自己消化，而不是把活物交给一个我们看不见的过程。
options.t_en: I would strike the catching and removal clause from the plan and push for trap-neuter-return instead: residents willing to feed pay and do the work, the cats are caught, neutered, ear-tipped and returned, with fixed shelters placed away from the ground floor. Neighbors should sort out their own problems rather than handing living creatures over to a process we cannot see.

options.t: 我会支持物业清走并限期让愿意收养的住户办手续，逾期由专业机构带走。人的居住卫生和婴儿睡眠优先，这不是残忍，是秩序。让两百户人家为一个微小的善意长期让渡生活品质，这份善意就太贵了。
options.t_en: I would support the property manager clearing them out, with a deadline for residents who want to adopt to complete the paperwork, after which a professional organization takes them away. People's hygiene and a baby's sleep come first. This is not cruelty, it is order. Asking two hundred households to give up their quality of life indefinitely for a small kindness makes that kindness far too expensive.

options.t: 我会先要求物业把力气花在投诉本身上：给底楼加装纱窗做除虫、费用由公共维修支出，噪音投诉逐条记录核实。至于猫，它们在的时候老鼠少了一半；真要解决人不舒服，动猫未必是最短的那条路。
options.t_en: I would first demand that the property manager put the effort into the complaints themselves: fit screens and do pest control for the ground floor out of the common maintenance budget, and record and verify each noise complaint one by one. As for the cats, while they are here the rats are down by half. If the real goal is that people stop being uncomfortable, moving the cats may not be the shortest route.

options.t: 我会提议召开全体业主表决，并把三个方案的预算、后续责任和谁喂养写清楚再投。小区公共事务的正当性来自程序，而不是谁声音大、谁更心软，或者谁恰好坐在物业办公室里。
options.t_en: I would propose a vote of all owners, with the budget, the follow-up responsibility and who does the feeding for all three options written out before the vote. The legitimacy of a compound's common affairs comes from procedure, not from who is loudest, who is softest-hearted, or who happens to sit in the property office.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: Since the start of summer, the corner by the ventilation shaft in your compound's underground garage has become home to seven or eight stray cats. A retired teacher on the third floor feeds them at the same time every evening and has made them beds out of old padded coats. A mother cat has just had a litter. Two households on the ground floor have filed four written complaints in a row: fleas have got into their homes, and the mating cries at night keep the baby awake. The property manager plans to bring in a third party to catch them and deal with them, and to post a notice banning feeding throughout the compound. You hold the only pet-owner vote on the owners' committee, and your opinion will go straight into the resolution.

scene: 你在一家医疗器械公司带华东区销售团队。老王一个人扛着全组近四成的营收，几家三甲医院的关系牢得像固定资产；但两年里先后有五名新人从他组里离职，离职面谈记录里反复出现同一个词：羞辱。他没打过人，没违反员工手册任何一条，只是把最难啃的活丢给新人，再当着全组的面嘲笑结果。月底是述职会，总部给的口径是看结果。另外两名组长私下说：再不动他，我们还得接着招人。

options.t: 我会给他一次明确而书面的整改：指出具体行为、配三个月沟通训练、再犯就转到不带人的单兵岗位。业绩是团队这个舞台替他搭出来的，舞台上怎么待人，不能由业绩豁免。
options.t_en: I would give him one clear, written improvement plan: name the specific behaviour, attach three months of communication coaching, and move him to an individual role with no reports if it happens again. His results were built on the stage the team set for him, and how he treats people on that stage cannot be excused by results.

options.t: 我会保他不动。公司付钱买的是结果，不是性格；一个成年新人因为被说两句就走，招聘环节本该问清抗压。换掉最强产出者，损失分摊到全组人的奖金池上，谁替那两名组长补。
options.t_en: I would keep him as he is. The company pays for results, not personality; if a grown adult newcomer leaves because of a couple of remarks, the hiring process should have tested resilience. Replacing the strongest producer spreads the loss across everyone's bonus pool, so who is going to make that up for the two team leads?

options.t: 我会向总部申请把他转成独立的战略客户经理：留住他的关系和收入，同时让他不再站在新人职业入口的那个位置上。管理权是可以没有的，产出不必跟着一起赔进去。
options.t_en: I would ask head office to move him into an independent strategic accounts role: keep his relationships and his revenue while taking him out of the position at the entry gate for newcomers. Line management is something you can do without; output need not be lost along with it.

options.t: 我会先算一笔账摆进述职报告：两年五任新人，招聘费、三个月培训期的沉没成本、客户关系的交接损耗、上一位接手者重新爬坡的时间。说服他的上级不需要讲道理，账单就够。
options.t_en: I would put the numbers into the review report first: five new hires in two years, recruitment costs, the sunk cost of the three-month training period, the loss on handing over client relationships, and the ramp-up time for the last person who took over. Persuading his manager does not need an argument; the bill is enough.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: You lead the east China sales team at a medical device company. Lao Wang alone carries nearly forty percent of the group's revenue, and his relationships with several top-tier hospitals are as fixed as capital assets. Yet five new hires have left his team in two years, and the same word keeps appearing in exit interviews: humiliation. He has never hit anyone and has broken no line of the employee handbook; he simply gives newcomers the hardest work and then mocks the results in front of the whole team. The monthly review is at the end of the month, and head office's line is that results are what count. The other two team leads say privately that if nothing is done about him, they will be hiring again.

scene: 你是一家市级图书馆的馆长。暑期青少年读书会原本邀请了一位本地童书作者，来给孩子们讲图画书是怎么画出来的。海报贴出一周后，一份两百多人签名的信递到馆办公室：这位作者近年公开倡导一种不被多数家庭认可的家庭形态，家长担心他会向孩子传递立场。随即又有另一份联署，称撤邀就是审查。活动在十天后，场地已订，孩子们已经读过他的书。

options.t: 我会照常举办并把主题钉死：这一场只谈分镜、色彩和怎么把一句废稿画成封面，不涉及个人主张；同时邀请一位签名的家长到场旁听。公共图书馆的职责是让孩子接触已被讨论过的世界，而不是替所有家长先筛一遍。
options.t_en: I will hold the event as planned and pin the subject down: this session is only about storyboarding, colour, and how a discarded draft becomes a cover, with nothing about personal convictions, and I will invite one of the signing parents to sit in. A public library's job is to let children meet a world that has already been argued over, not to pre-screen it on every parent's behalf.

options.t: 我会把场次改成面向家长和教育工作者的闭门交流，孩子场取消。两百份签名背后是真实的家庭关切，馆方没有权力让孩子在家长的价值观之外被单独接触。这不是审查，是场地与受众的边界。
options.t_en: I will change the session into a closed discussion for parents and educators and cancel the children's session. Behind two hundred signatures there is real family concern, and the library has no authority to put children in contact with something outside their parents' values. This is not censorship; it is a boundary between venue and audience.

options.t: 我会照办，并加一场配套活动：由两位立场相反的讲者同台，主题是成年人如何体面地谈分歧。真正的把关不是把人挡在门外，而是让孩子看见 disagree 也可以不撕破脸。
options.t_en: I will go ahead, and add a companion event: two speakers on opposite sides on the same stage, on how adults can disagree decently. Real gatekeeping is not shutting people out but letting children see that disagreement does not have to end in a broken relationship.

options.t: 我会先把依据、流程和责权向主管部门报批公开，让决定挂到一条明确的责任链上。馆长不该凭个人偏向在联署压力下做取舍，公共机构要能向所有人解释自己为什么这么选。
options.t_en: I will first report the basis, the process and the allocation of responsibility to the supervising department and make it public, so that the decision hangs on a clear chain of accountability. A director should not be making choices under petition pressure out of personal preference; a public institution has to be able to explain to anyone why it chose as it did.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: You are the director of a city library. The summer reading club for young people had invited a local children's author to talk to the children about how a picture book gets made. A week after the posters went up, a letter with more than two hundred signatures arrives at the library office: the author has in recent years publicly advocated a family form that most families do not accept, and parents are worried he will pass his views on to the children. A counter-petition follows at once, calling any withdrawal of the invitation censorship. The event is in ten days, the room is booked, and the children have already read his book.

scene: 你们村三百多户的集体土地被征收，账上进了一笔九位数的补偿款。村民大会连开三晚没散：外出打工的青壮年主张按人头一次性分到户，说钱在自己手里最稳；几位老人坚持留一部分做厂房或入股冷链库，让后代年年有分红；还有人拍桌子质问，同村的十二户低保和两位正在化疗的人，凭什么不能先重补一份。你是村民推选出的分配小组成员，明天要拿出草案。

options.t: 我会主张一次性分到户。集体的钱最容易在每个环节被稀释，而村民等不起年年分红；让三百多个家庭各自做主——有人还债、有人盖房、有人让孩子上学——比一个村委替他们决定更可靠。
options.t_en: I would argue for a one-off distribution to households. Collective money is most easily diluted at every step, and villagers cannot wait years for a dividend. Let more than three hundred families each decide for themselves: one pays off debt, one builds a house, one sends a child to school. That is more reliable than a village committee deciding for them.

options.t: 我会主张把大半留下来变成集体资产，并写死分红机制，同时给困难户定额补助。一次性分光是最省事的选项，十年后没有地的村庄会回到原点；钱变成资产，才谈得上代际。
options.t_en: I would argue for keeping most of it as collective assets, with the dividend mechanism written in and fixed, plus a fixed allowance for the households in difficulty. Dividing it all up at once is the easiest option, and in ten years a village with no land left will be back where it started. Only when money becomes an asset can anyone talk about generations.

options.t: 我会主张先做困难优先的分层：重病户与低保户加计份额，剩余部分再按人头分。补偿不只是一笔产权清算，也是一个共同体最后一次照顾自己最弱成员的机会，这个顺序不该被票数推翻。
options.t_en: I would argue for a needs-first tier: households with serious illness and those on minimum living support get an additional share, and the remainder is divided per capita. Compensation is not just a settlement of property rights; it is the last chance for a community to look after its weakest members, and that order should not be overturned by a vote count.

options.t: 我会先要求公开全部账目和每亩单价的测算依据，谈清楚总数怎么来的再谈怎么分。分法可以争，但如果连进账都不透明，任何方案都是在替别人签字。
options.t_en: I would first demand that all the accounts and the calculation basis for the per-mu price be made public. Settle how the total was arrived at before talking about how to divide it. The division can be argued over, but if even the intake is not transparent, then any plan is someone signing on another person's behalf.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The collective land of your village, more than three hundred households, has been expropriated and a nine-figure compensation payment has landed in the account. The village assembly has run three nights without breaking up. The young adults who work away from home want a one-off per-capita distribution to each household, saying money in your own hands is safest. Several elders insist on keeping part of it for a workshop or a stake in a cold storage facility, so that their descendants get a dividend every year. Others bang the table and ask why the twelve households on minimum living support and the two people in chemotherapy should not get a larger share first. You are on the distribution group elected by the villagers, and tomorrow you have to produce a draft.

scene: 你是市陶瓷行业协会的秘书长。本地三百多家中小窑口的日用瓷，正被一批到岸价低于你们泥料成本的进口产品挤到墙角——两年关了六十多家，一批能拉出薄胎、会配釉的师傅开始转行送外卖。会员大会给了你三个待选方案：申请为期五年的保障措施（配额或附加税）；用行业基金补贴窑口改做高端文创与非遗体验；或者干脆不动，让效率低的企业出清，资源流向活下来的那批。

options.t: 我会推动保障措施。这不是保护落后，是给转型期定价：一个能拉出薄胎的师傅要十年养出来，散了就再也拼不回来。让价格先替竞争做决定，赔掉的是整整一代人和一座城市的辨识度。
options.t_en: I would push for safeguard measures. This is not protecting backwardness; it is pricing the transition period. A craftsman who can throw an eggshell body takes ten years to train, and once dispersed cannot be reassembled. Let price decide the competition now, and what is lost is a whole generation and a city's distinctiveness.

options.t: 我会反对保护。便宜的碗进来了，直接受益者是每一个要买碗的家庭；用附加税把这份便宜收回去，等于向全体消费者征税去养一批不肯变的窑口。竞争本来就会伤人，这正是它在做的事。
options.t_en: I would oppose protection. Cheap bowls have arrived, and the direct beneficiaries are every household that needs to buy a bowl; clawing that cheapness back with a surcharge is taxing all consumers to keep a batch of kilns that will not change. Competition hurts, and that is precisely what it is doing.

options.t: 我会把钱花在人身上而不是窑口上：给转岗师傅发技能再培训补贴、给学徒付生活津贴，再挑几家有设计能力的窑口扶持做高端与文旅。护住手艺人的饭碗，不必把整条低端产品线一起护住。
options.t_en: I would spend the money on people rather than on kilns: retraining subsidies for craftsmen changing roles, living allowances for apprentices, and support for a few kilns with design capability to go high-end and into cultural tourism. Protect the craftsmen's livelihoods without protecting the entire low-end product line.

options.t: 我会主张行业自组联合体：统一品牌的海外渠道、共享釉料实验室与设计资源，让小窑口抱团够到自己去不了的市场。外力给的护栏会过期，自己长出来的能力不会。
options.t_en: I would argue for the industry forming its own consortium: a shared brand for overseas channels, shared glaze laboratories and design resources, so that small kilns can band together to reach markets they could not reach alone. Guardrails given by others expire; capability grown from within does not.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: You are secretary-general of the city ceramics association. Daily-use porcelain from more than three hundred small and mid-sized local kilns is being squeezed into a corner by imports whose landed price is below the cost of your own clay; over sixty workshops have closed in two years, and the craftsmen who can throw eggshell-thin bodies and mix glazes are starting to deliver food. The members' meeting has given you three options: apply for five-year safeguard measures in the form of quotas or a surcharge, use an industry fund to help kilns move into high-end design and heritage craft experiences, or do nothing and let inefficient firms exit so that resources flow to those that survive.

scene: 你所在的水利单位要在一条断流二十三年的内陆河上做试点：每年四到六月，从上游水库下泄一段生态流量，让老河床重新见水。消息传开，沿岸四个村先坐不住了——干涸的河床早被他们平整成玉米地，多年习惯在河滩上种油葵，有一户还在老河床上盖了看护房和鸡舍。水文专家说，三个汛期的冲刷，这些地就都毁了。协调会下周开，你是派去的协调员。

options.t: 我会把恢复放在第一位，同时拿出真金白银的置换：沿岸另行划出等面积的灌溉地，青苗和迁建按实际投入补偿。一条死掉的河，让下游二十万人失去的是地下水补给和夏天那点降温——这不是乡愁，是资产。
options.t_en: I will put restoration first, but with real money on the table for replacement: irrigated land of equivalent area allocated elsewhere along the bank, and compensation for standing crops and rebuilding at actual cost. A dead river costs the two hundred thousand people downstream their groundwater recharge and what little cooling summer used to bring. That is not nostalgia; it is an asset.

options.t: 我会主张把时间表拉长到五年，逐年增加下泄水量，让农户有时间改种耐旱作物或退种。生态目标我不想降，但「合法种了二十年的地一夜被冲掉」这种执行方式，会把环保变成沿岸人眼中的敌人。
options.t_en: I will argue for stretching the timetable to five years, increasing the release year by year, so that farmers have time to switch to drought-tolerant crops or to stop farming. I do not want to lower the ecological target, but executing it by washing away fields that were legally farmed for twenty years will turn environmental protection into the enemy in the eyes of the people along the bank.

options.t: 我会先反对这次试点。这四个村的口粮账我有明细，一句公共利益抹不掉它。真要做，先打井、先修渠、先把替代生计做到位——顺序错了，再正确的目标也是让别人替我们买单。
options.t_en: I will oppose the pilot as it stands. I have the detailed food and income figures for those four villages, and a phrase about the public interest does not wipe them out. If it is really to be done, drill the wells first, repair the channels first, get the alternative livelihoods in place first. Get the order wrong and even a correct goal means making other people pay for us.

options.t: 我会主张先把收益算成钱：地下水回补、河岸降温、鸟类栖息，折算后和玉米、油葵摆在同一份报告里比。让人争的是同一个账本，而不是各自喊各自牺牲了多少。
options.t_en: I will argue for costing the benefits in money first: groundwater recharge, riverside cooling, bird habitat, converted into figures and put in the same report as the maize and the sunflowers. Then people are arguing over one set of accounts, instead of each side shouting about how much it has sacrificed.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Your water resources unit wants to pilot something on an inland river that has been dry for twenty-three years: from April to June each year, release a stretch of ecological flow from the upstream reservoir and let the old riverbed see water again. Once word got out, the four villages along the bank were up in arms. They have long since levelled the dry bed into maize fields and are used to growing sunflowers on the floodplain, and one household has even built a watch hut and a chicken shed on the old bed.
