Hydrologists say three flood seasons of scour will destroy all of it. The coordination meeting is next week, and you are the coordinator sent to it.

scene: 你是一所县中的校长。去年你顶着压力砍掉全校的晚自习和周末补课，把时间还给自主学习，还给每个班配了答疑导师——半年下来，学生的睡眠时长和体质监测数据都好看了，心理咨询室的预约也降了。但这次月考后，几位尖子生的家长联名要求恢复培优班：别人市的学校没停，乡下孩子本来就输在起跑线，凭什么让我们的孩子只跑到匀速。县里回你一句自己把握好。

options.t: 我会守住改革。教育不是军备竞赛的记账：用孩子的睡眠换十分的排名，十年后会以别的方式被要回去。我会加开面向全体学生的分层答疑，而不是给前二十名单独开小灶。
options.t_en: I would hold the reform. Education is not bookkeeping in an arms race: trading children's sleep for ten places in the rankings will be demanded back in some other form in ten years. I would add tiered question sessions open to all students, rather than setting up a separate track for the top twenty.

options.t: 我会恢复一个自愿的晚间培优班，并严格限制人数与时长。理想我能讲一整晚，但眼前这些具体的孩子只有这一次升学；别人都在跑的时候，让别人单方面停下来的那个人，代价由别人家的孩子付。
options.t_en: I would restore a voluntary evening honors class, with strict limits on numbers and hours. I could talk about ideals all night, but these particular children only get this one shot at the next stage. When everyone else is running, the person who makes only the others stop is spending other people's children to pay for it.

options.t: 我会把争议摆到明面上：开一次全年级家长会，公布这两年的睡眠、体质和成绩分布数据，再让学生自己选择晚自习时段。真正的减负不是减时间，是把选择权还回去一部分。
options.t_en: I would put the dispute out in the open: hold a parents' meeting for the whole year group, publish the last two years of data on sleep, fitness and grade distribution, and then let the students choose their own evening study hours. Real relief is not cutting time; it is giving back part of the choice.

options.t: 我会向县里提议把补课时长做成全县统一的刚性上限并纳入督导。一所学校的单方面自律，只会在升学排名里被惩罚；规则要让所有人一起被约束才有意义。
options.t_en: I would propose to the county that tutoring hours be made a hard, uniform ceiling across the whole county and built into inspection. One school being self-disciplined on its own will only be punished in the rankings. Rules only mean something when they bind everyone at once.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: You are the principal of a county high school. Last year you took the pressure and scrapped evening study sessions and weekend tutoring across the school, giving the time back to independent study and assigning each class a tutor for questions. Half a year on, students' sleep hours and physical fitness data look better, and appointments at the counseling office are down. But after this month's exams, several parents of top students jointly demanded the honors class be restored: schools in other cities never stopped, rural children are already behind at the starting line, so why should our children only ever run at a steady pace. The county told you to use your own judgment.

scene: 你所在的边境小镇十年走了三成人口，中心小学今年只剩四十一名学生，县教育局的撤并函压在镇长桌上——并到六十公里外的寄宿学校，每周五才回家。这时有人提案：接收一批愿意长期务农的外来家庭落户，用闲置公房安顿，孩子入学正好把生源补足。商贸市场的摊主多数支持，几位老人反复问同一句话：人来了之后，镇上的节、山上的老庙、合唱队那首方言歌，还唱吗。你是镇议会成员。

options.t: 我会支持接收。一所四十一个孩子的学校撑不下去，而那批人在等我们答复——这不是一道关于文化的选择题，是两个都真实的困境同时摆在桌上。先让学校活下来，文化靠的是活着的镇。
options.t_en: I would support taking them in. A school with forty-one children cannot stay open, and those people are waiting for our answer. This is not a multiple-choice question about culture; it is two real dilemmas on the table at once. Let the school live first, because culture depends on a living town.

options.t: 我会支持，但条件要先谈死：落户家庭的孩子必须入学本地学校，青壮年入生产合作社，同时由镇里出资把方言和本地节俗做成全校必修的乡土课。文化不是靠把人挡在镇外守住的，是靠把它教给所有孩子守住的。
options.t_en: I would support it, but the conditions must be nailed down first: the children of settling families must enrol in the local school, the adults must join the production cooperative, and the town must fund a local studies course on the dialect and local festivals that is compulsory for the whole school. Culture is not defended by keeping people outside the town; it is defended by teaching it to every child.

options.t: 我会反对这个方案。把人口流失改写成接收方案，回避了真问题：年轻人为什么走、产业为什么留不住。这批人安顿好之后，十年后照样会走——除非我们肯修那条路和那座冷库。
options.t_en: I would oppose this plan. Rewriting population loss as a resettlement plan dodges the real questions: why young people leave and why industry will not stay. Once these people are settled, in ten years they will leave too, unless we are willing to fix that road and that cold store.

options.t: 我会主张先做小规模试点：限定十五户，配一名家校联络员，两年后评议再决定扩不扩。宏大的方案在纸面上总能赢，具体到星期一早晨谁在校门口招呼谁，只能用小规模先试出来。
options.t_en: I would argue for a small pilot first: fifteen households, one home-school liaison officer, a review after two years before deciding whether to expand. Grand plans always win on paper; who greets whom at the school gate on Monday morning can only be worked out at small scale.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Your border township has lost thirty percent of its population in ten years. The central primary school is down to forty-one pupils this year, and the county education bureau's consolidation letter is sitting on the mayor's desk: merge into a boarding school sixty kilometres away, home only on Fridays. Then someone proposes inviting a group of outside families willing to farm long term to settle, housing them in vacant public flats, with their children filling the school roll. Most stallholders in the market support it. A few of the elderly keep asking the same question: once these people come, will the town festival, the old shrine on the hill, and that dialect song the choir sings still be sung? You are a member of the town council.

scene: 最近半年，你们市发生四起老人走失，其中两位是在深夜被找到的。警方正式申请：要求网约车与共享单车平台开放实时行程数据的查询接口，用于紧急定位走失人员，承诺只在报警后启用、逐案留痕。两家平台表示可依法配合，但希望有一部明确授权规范和期限；本地一家数码权益团体则指出，接口一旦建成，它的用途不会由今天承诺它的人决定。你参与起草这部地方规范。

options.t: 我会支持建接口，但把约束写死：限报警后启用、须经一名以上警官审批、事后向被查询人本人发出告知、数据九十天销毁。定位老人的效率是真的；正因为是真的，才更需要一个可被审计的形式。
options.t_en: I will support building the interface, with the constraints nailed down: activated only after a report is filed, requiring approval from at least one officer, a notice sent to the person queried afterwards, and the data destroyed after ninety days. The speed of locating a missing old person is real, and precisely because it is real it needs a form that can be audited.

options.t: 我会反对建立任何常态化接口。每一次只用于紧急情形的承诺，最后都变成了例行查询。四起走失当然沉重，但一个能实时定位全城行踪的系统，一旦被别的目的动用，没有人能替你反对。
options.t_en: I will oppose any standing interface. Every promise that it will be used only in emergencies ends up as routine querying. Four missing people is genuinely grave, but once a system that can locate anyone in the city in real time is used for other purposes, there will be nobody to object on your behalf.

options.t: 我会主张不由平台建常设接口：由警方指挥中心作为唯一窗口，平台只对单个已立案请求作一次性回复。差别不在技术上，而在设施由谁持有——随时能查和逐案申请，完全不是一回事。
options.t_en: I will argue the interface should not be built and held by the platforms: the police command centre should be the single window, and the platforms reply once, case by case, to an individual request that has already been opened as a case. The difference is not technical but about who holds the facility. Being able to look at any time and applying case by case are completely different things.

options.t: 我会先要求做一次公开听证，把四起案例的响应时间线全部还原，看真正的瓶颈是缺数据，还是报警后头两小时没人出动。如果瓶颈不在数据上，建接口只是为了显得在做事。
options.t_en: I will first ask for a public hearing that reconstructs the response timeline of all four cases, to see whether the real bottleneck was a lack of data or the fact that nobody was dispatched in the first two hours after the report. If the bottleneck is not the data, building the interface is only a way of looking busy.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: In the past six months four elderly people have gone missing in your city, and two of them were found late at night. The police have formally applied for ride-hailing and shared-bicycle platforms to open a query interface on real-time trip data, to be used for emergency location of missing people, with a commitment to activate it only after a report is filed and to log every case. Both platforms say they will cooperate in accordance with the law, but want a clear authorisation standard and a time limit. A local digital rights group points out that once the interface exists, its uses will not be decided by the people who promised them today. You are helping draft the local regulation.

scene: 你所在的移植伦理委员会今晚必须给答复。一枚匹配的肝脏刚送来，等待名单排第一位的是一位四十九岁的男性——他的医学评分最高，但三个月前他复饮了，这是戒酒后的第二次复发；排第三位的是一位二十四岁的女性，首次急性发病、从未有过酒精依赖、有一个四岁的孩子。分配规则是按医学评分排的，规则里没写咎由自取这一条，也没写他还年轻这四个字。

options.t: 我会按规则给第一位。评分体系之所以存在，正是为了把此刻我最想推翻的判断，交给一个不含报复心的计算。一旦开始讨论谁值得，下一个被审判的就是抽烟的、不运动的和穷了一辈子的人。
options.t_en: I would follow the rules and give it to the first patient. The scoring system exists precisely so that the judgment I most want to overturn right now is handed to a calculation with no appetite for revenge. Once we start discussing who deserves it, the next to be judged are smokers, people who do not exercise, and people who have been poor all their lives.

options.t: 我会要求给年轻人。医学评分算的是紧迫性，没算她还有六十年，也没算一个四岁的孩子。规则是人写的，写的时候没想过这个场面；在它没想到的场合里，沉默的规则不该替我们说话。
options.t_en: I would argue for the younger woman. The medical score measures urgency; it does not count the sixty years she may still have, and it does not count a four-year-old child. Rules are written by people who did not imagine this scene. Where the rules did not imagine it, a silent rule should not speak for us.

options.t: 我会要求一个程序：两个医疗组各自不记名提交理由，委员会闭门表决，判决理由入档供日后同类情形援引。这类决定躲不开人的判断，那就让它至少不是某一个人的判断。
options.t_en: I would ask for a procedure: the two medical teams each submit their reasons anonymously, the committee votes behind closed doors, and the reasoning goes on record so that similar cases can cite it later. Decisions like this cannot escape human judgment, so at least let it not be one person's judgment.

options.t: 我会把复发当成医学事实处理：要求第一位签署术后戒酒与随访条款，并在移植前由成瘾科再做一次评估。惩罚复发救不了任何人，把它写进治疗条件才有用。
options.t_en: I would treat the relapse as a medical fact: require the first patient to sign post-transplant abstinence and follow-up terms, and have the addiction department do one more assessment before the transplant. Punishing a relapse saves nobody. Writing it into the treatment conditions is what actually works.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: Your transplant ethics committee has to give an answer tonight. A matched liver has just arrived. First on the waiting list is a forty-nine-year-old man with the highest medical score, but he started drinking again three months ago, his second relapse since he stopped. Third on the list is a twenty-four-year-old woman with a first acute onset, no history of alcohol dependence, and a four-year-old child. Allocation follows the medical score. The rules say nothing about bringing it on yourself, and nothing about being young either.

scene: 你在一所医学院的教材委员会里。几十年来，人体解剖与临床医学教材一直以成年男性的身体作为所谓标准人体：肌肉起止点画的是男体，典型症状列的是男体的表现，女性则只在生殖与妊娠章节里出现——后果是一代代医学生学到的是半个人的医学。学生联署要求重编并讲透差异。出版社的报价摆在面前：重编要吃掉你们三年教材预算的一半，工期还要拖两年。

options.t: 我会主张就重编，即便要拖两年。把男体叫做标准人体不是中性表述，它直接写进了几亿人的诊断延迟里——心脏病的胸痛表现男女不同，这件事教出血的代价。这笔钱迟早要出，只是由哪一届学生承担。
options.t_en: I would argue for the rewrite, even with a two-year delay. Calling the male body the standard is not a neutral description; it is written directly into diagnostic delays for hundreds of millions of people. Chest pain in a heart attack presents differently in men and women, and that costs lives when it is taught badly. This money has to be spent eventually; the only question is which cohort of students pays.

options.t: 我会先做最省钱的一步：给现有教材里每处以男体为标准的表述加框标注差异，并增补女性典型表现的独立章节。完美的重编本要两年，九月就上课的这批学生等不起，能救的一步先落地。
options.t_en: I would do the cheapest step first: box a note on every place in the existing textbooks that treats the male body as standard, and add separate sections on typical female presentations. A perfect rewrite takes two years and the students starting in September cannot wait, so land the step that saves lives now.

options.t: 我会反对这次改造。称为标准，是因为教材要先教通例，临床阶段再教变异；把每个章节铺成双份，学生的记忆负担翻倍而通例反而糊了。真正的问题在临床带教的偏见里，不在图上。
options.t_en: I would oppose this overhaul. We call it standard because textbooks must teach the general case first and variants come in clinical training; making every chapter double doubles the memorisation load and blurs the general case. The real problem is bias in clinical teaching, not in the diagrams.

options.t: 我会要求先把成本拆开看：重编的费用里多少是绘图、多少是审稿、多少是出版社的排产损失。若是前者，我们可以组师生自己做；若是后者，就让报价透明到可被反驳为止。
options.t_en: I would ask for the cost to be broken down first: how much of the rewrite is illustration, how much is review, and how much is the publisher's lost print scheduling. If it is the first, we can form a team of staff and students to do it ourselves; if it is the last, make the quote transparent enough to be argued with.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: You sit on a medical school's textbook committee. For decades, anatomy and clinical textbooks have taken the adult male body as the standard human: muscle attachments drawn on male bodies, typical symptoms listed as male presentations, and women appearing only in chapters on reproduction and pregnancy, so that generation after generation of students learn medicine for half the population. Students have petitioned for a rewrite that teaches the differences properly. The publisher's quote is on the table: the rewrite would eat half your three-year textbook budget and delay everything by two years.

scene: 你们医院放射科上线 AI 辅助读片系统满一年，漏诊率明显下降，报告出具时间从四小时缩到四十分钟。代价也摆在台面上：住院医师上手看片的机会被系统挤占，带教老师担心五年后没人会独立读疑难片子；更棘手的是院内复核数据——这套模型在深色皮肤人群上的假阴性率明显偏高，而你们恰恰接诊这样的人群。你是科室主任，明天要在院务会上给建议。

options.t: 我会主张继续用并扩大覆盖，同时把教学用的原始片子单独留给住培医生。诊断效率和漏诊率是我此刻最硬的证据；至于教学是否掉队，那是管理问题，不该让患者的检出率去补这个窟窿。
options.t_en: I will argue for continuing and extending coverage, while setting aside original films for the residents to train on. Diagnostic efficiency and the miss rate are the hardest evidence I have right now; whether teaching falls behind is a management problem, and patients' detection rates should not be used to plug that hole.

options.t: 我会要求暂停扩大，先把偏差查清楚：用院内历史病例按人群分层跑一遍指标，哪家厂商拿不出分层数据就换厂商。工具在我的科室里不能有偏心，否则我签的每一份报告都不干净。
options.t_en: I will ask for expansion to be paused until the bias is properly investigated: run the hospital's historical cases through the metrics stratified by population group, and replace any vendor that cannot produce stratified data. A tool in my department cannot be partial, or every report I sign is tainted.

options.t: 我会把系统降级为第二阅片人：AI 先看，医生独立看完再对答案，不一致处强制双签，同时保留住培医生的原片训练。既拿到效率，也保住会读片子的人和最后那道纠错闸门。
options.t_en: I will demote the system to second reader: the AI reads first, the doctor reads independently and then compares, any disagreement requires two signatures, and residents keep their training on original films. That way we take the efficiency and keep both the people who can read films and the final error-correction gate.

options.t: 我会反对在诊断环节使用黑箱模型，只在随访提醒、结构化归档这类辅助环节保留。医学的责任链必须能追到一个人；当一台机器做出判断而我只在它的结论上签字时，出事那天站上被告席的还是我。
options.t_en: I will oppose using a black box model in the diagnostic step, keeping it only for ancillary work such as follow-up reminders and structured filing. The chain of medical responsibility has to trace back to a person. When a machine makes the judgement and I only sign under its conclusion, the one standing in the dock on the day it goes wrong is still me.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Your hospital's radiology department has had an AI reading-assist system for a year. The miss rate has fallen noticeably and report turnaround has gone from four hours to forty minutes. The costs are also on the table: residents get less chance to read films themselves, and the teaching consultants worry that in five years nobody will be able to read a difficult case unaided. More awkward still is the internal audit data: the model's false negative rate is clearly higher on darker skin, and that is precisely the population you serve. You are the department head, and tomorrow you have to make a recommendation to the hospital board.

scene: 你是值班的法律援助律师，接手的被告是一位七十八岁的老人。他在确诊阿尔茨海默病早期后的第三个月，把上门护理员推倒并抓伤其面部，构成轻伤二级。他的儿子拿出病历请求做刑事责任能力鉴定；被害的护理员本人到医院表示谅解、希望和解，并提出向护理公司索要误工赔偿。公诉机关的量刑建议是八个月到一年。而老人的记忆差到已经说不清那天的经过。

options.t: 我会申请刑事责任能力鉴定并推动刑事和解。刑罚的前提是一个能够理解自己在做什么的人；一个连经过都记不住的人被关进去，惩罚的其实不是他。被害人也选择了谅解，法律不必比她更记仇。
options.t_en: I would apply for the criminal responsibility assessment and push for a criminal settlement. Punishment presupposes a person who can understand what he is doing. Locking up a man who cannot even remember what happened does not actually punish him. The victim has chosen to forgive, and the law does not need to hold a grudge longer than she does.

options.t: 我会主张免予刑事处罚，但附加强制医疗与看护令：责令家属落实看护并由家庭财产承担费用，定期向司法所报告。免刑不等于免责，家人不能把病人推出家门就算完事。
options.t_en: I would argue for exemption from criminal punishment, but attach a mandatory treatment and caregiving order: require the family to put care in place and cover the cost from family assets, with regular reports to the judicial office. Exemption is not exoneration. Families cannot simply push a sick person out the door and consider the matter closed.

options.t: 我会反对轻纵。护理员脸上的伤是真伤，一句有病就抹掉刑事记录，所有做护工的人都会知道自己不在保护之列。判决不只是写给被告的，也是说给下一个可能被推倒的人听的。
options.t_en: I would oppose letting it go lightly. The injury on the care worker's face is a real injury, and wiping a criminal record away with the word illness tells every care worker that they are not among the protected. A judgment is written not only for the defendant but for the next person who might be pushed over.

options.t: 我会要求先把案子部分拉回民事与行政：护理公司有没有针对认知症客户的派工流程与安全规范，如果没有，那是监管缺位在先。把一个病人送上被告席，解决不了下一次类似的事。
options.t_en: I would ask that part of the case be moved back into civil and administrative channels first. Does the care company have a dispatch procedure and safety protocol for clients with dementia? If not, the regulatory gap came first. Putting a sick man in the dock does not prevent the next incident of this kind.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: You are the duty legal aid lawyer, and your client is a seventy-eight-year-old man. Three months after being diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer's, he pushed over a home care worker and scratched her face, causing a level-two minor injury. His son has produced the medical records and asked for an assessment of criminal responsibility. The injured care worker herself came to the hospital to express understanding and asked for a settlement, and wants to claim lost-work compensation from the care company. The prosecution recommends eight months to a year. The old man's memory is so poor that he can no longer describe what happened that day.

scene: 你们医院肿瘤科的安宁疗护病区，十年来一直靠一支本地宗教志愿者队伍提供夜间陪伴：他们给濒死的病人读经、握着手祈祷、帮家属熬过最难的一夜，护士站确实离不开他们。上个月两位家属先后投诉——志愿者在病人意识模糊、止痛泵剂量刚调整过的时段反复劝说其改宗，并把拒绝祈祷描述为一种危险。志愿队否认强迫，说自己只是提供安慰。作为医务社工部主管，你要提交处置意见。

options.t: 我会要求暂停他们的夜间探视资质，改为白天、应家属书面申请后进入。临终病床边的权力失衡是极端的：一个连抬手都困难的病人无从拒绝，而信仰的选择只有在还能说话时才算数。
options.t_en: I would suspend their night visiting credential and allow entry only by day and only on written request from the family. The power imbalance at a dying patient's bedside is extreme: someone who can barely lift a hand cannot refuse, and a choice of faith only counts while you can still speak.

options.t: 我只主张重申并公示规则：不得在非清醒时段传教、不得为治疗配合附加宗教条件、护士有权随时中止探视。这支队伍十年送走了上千人，因为两起投诉就清退这份稀缺的陪伴，代价由谁付。
options.t_en: I would only restate and publish the rules: no proselytising when the patient is not lucid, no religious conditions attached to cooperation with treatment, and nurses empowered to stop a visit at any time. This team has accompanied over a thousand people to the end in ten years, so who pays the price of clearing out this scarce companionship over two complaints?

options.t: 我会主张医院这一步干脆别退：购买专业安宁社工岗位，让陪伴由拿薪酬、可问责、可培训的人来做。把临终关怀外包给志愿者的好意，本来就是财政的偷懒，出问题只是时间。
options.t_en: I would argue that the hospital should not step back at all, but fund professional palliative social work posts, so that companionship is provided by people who are paid, accountable and trainable. Outsourcing end-of-life care to volunteers' goodwill was always the treasury being lazy; trouble was only a matter of time.

options.t: 我会主张让各信仰团体与不信教的人文关怀组织共同入驻，适用同一套行为准则。只卡一支队伍是歧视，而只用一支队伍才是问题所在；中性不是空心，而是能被检查的。
options.t_en: I would argue for admitting all faith groups and non-religious humanist care organisations under one shared code of conduct. Restricting one team is discrimination, while relying on only one team is the actual problem; neutrality is not emptiness, it is being inspectable.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: For ten years the palliative care ward in your hospital's oncology department has relied on a local religious volunteer group for night companionship: they read scripture to the dying, hold their hands in prayer, and help families through the hardest night, and the nurses' station genuinely could not manage without them. Last month two families complained in succession, saying that volunteers repeatedly urged conversion at times when the patient was confused and the pain pump had just been adjusted, and described refusing prayer as dangerous. The volunteer team denies coercion and says it offers only comfort. As head of medical social work, you must submit a recommendation.

scene: 你住的六层老楼经鉴定为局部危房，需要全体业主同意加固，费用按面积分摊。方案、报价和图纸公示了大半年，二十四户里二十二户签了字，卡住的是两户：一户常年旅居海外，电话联系上一次后要求改成只按一半出资；另一户是八十六岁的独居老人，名下只有这套房和每月三千出头的退休金，她签了字就意味着未来四年要靠借钱吃饭。街道给的期限还剩一个月。

options.t: 我会推动申请代建代修：由区属平台先行垫资，房屋出售或继承时清偿。一栋楼的安全不该挂在两户人的现金流上，更不该让一位老人替别人的账单付——既危险又不体面。
options.t_en: I will push for a build-and-repair-on-behalf arrangement: a district-owned platform advances the money, repaid when the flat is sold or inherited. The safety of a building should not hang on the cash flow of two households, and an old woman should certainly not be paying other people's bills. It is dangerous, and it is indecent.

options.t: 我会组织邻居筹措老人的份额，公开认捐到付清为止。这是共同体最初级的样子：谁也没有这个义务，但邻里能让命运的差别不要这么硬，也让老阿姨留在她住了四十年的家里。
options.t_en: I will organise the neighbours to raise the old woman's share, with an open pledge list until it is covered. This is what a community looks like at its most basic: nobody is obliged to do it, but neighbours can make the lottery of fate a little less harsh, and let her stay in the home she has lived in for forty years.

options.t: 我会坚持按原有比例执行，只给海外业主追加一次书面催告并公告到期视为同意。规则既然是大家定的，就不能因为一户不方便而重写。照顾弱者的钱该从税收出，而不是从邻居口袋里出。
options.t_en: I will insist on applying the original proportions, with one further written notice to the overseas owner and a public announcement that expiry counts as consent. If the rules were set by everyone, they cannot be rewritten because one household finds it inconvenient. Money to look after the vulnerable should come from taxation, not from neighbours' pockets.

options.t: 我会先去要求街道列出政策工具清单——公积金提取、维修资金应急通道、公租房临时周转——把合规可行的办法完整摆到两户面前。很多人不是不讲理，是没人告诉他们有哪些路可以走。
options.t_en: I will go and ask the subdistrict for a full list of the policy tools available: housing fund withdrawal, the emergency channel for maintenance funds, temporary public rental housing. Put every lawful, workable option in front of the two households. A lot of people are not being unreasonable; nobody has told them which roads are open.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: The six-storey building you live in has been assessed as partially unsafe, and reinforcing it requires the consent of every owner, with the cost split by floor area. The plan, the quotes and the drawings have been posted for over half a year, and twenty-two of the twenty-four households have signed. Two are holding it up. One owner lives abroad all year and, after a single phone call, wants to pay only half. The other is an eighty-six-year-old woman living alone, whose only assets are this flat and a pension of just over three thousand a month; signing means borrowing to eat for the next four years. The subdistrict's deadline is a month away.

scene: 你们县是养殖大县，上级要求在十年内把畜禽粪污资源化利用率提到九成以上，并推行一套新的养殖环境与抗生素减量标准。规模型养殖场算过账，改造摊销到每头猪不到成本的百分之二；而占比六成的中小养殖户根本摊不起——他们的棚舍不得不大改就得退出，能拿到的补贴只够盖一套漏粪板系统。你是县农业局负责过渡政策的人，六十天内要拿出方案。

options.t: 我会主张分档推进：规模场五年内达标，中小户给十年，配套低息贷款与技术员上门。转型成本不能由最经不起风险的人先掏，否则一纸标准落地就变成了消灭一类人。
options.t_en: I would argue for a phased approach: large farms meet the standard within five years, small and medium ones get ten, with low-interest loans and technicians visiting in person. The cost of transition should not be paid first by those least able to bear risk; otherwise a standard on paper becomes the elimination of a category of people.

options.t: 我会主张按期推进不打折。抗生素残留和粪污直排的账单，向来是二十年后再付的；而恰恰能让边际收益最低的小农户退出、土地与订单向高效率主体集中，本来就是产业升级的路径。
options.t_en: I would argue for sticking to the timetable without discount. The bill for antibiotic residue and manure discharged straight into the water has always been paid twenty years later. And letting the small farms with the lowest marginal returns exit so that land and contracts concentrate in more efficient hands has always been the path of industrial upgrading.

options.t: 我会主张建立以村为单位的集中处理中心：粪污由专业公司统一收运制肥，养殖户按量付费，设施不改也能达到排放要求。与其逼六千户各自建一座污水处理站，不如让专业的人干专业的事。
options.t_en: I would argue for village-level centralized treatment centers: manure collected and processed into fertilizer by a professional company, farms paying by volume, so that emission standards can be met without rebuilding the sheds. Rather than forcing six thousand households to each build a treatment station, let professionals do the professional work.

options.t: 我会把选择拆给农户：愿意改造的给贷款和技术改造服务；愿意退出的给高于市场价的退出补偿和转岗培训；但不许拖着不改也不退。政策最怕把所有人塞进一个模子，结果全部卡在里面。
options.t_en: I would split the choice and hand it to the farmers. Those willing to retrofit get loans and technical renovation services. Those willing to exit get compensation above market price and retraining for other work. But nobody may neither change nor leave. The worst thing a policy can do is force everyone into one mold and leave them all stuck in it.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Your county is a major livestock producer. The province requires that within ten years the resource utilization rate of livestock manure reach ninety percent or more, along with a new standard for farm environment and antibiotic reduction. Large-scale farms have done the arithmetic: the retrofit amortizes to under two percent of cost per pig. But the small and medium farms, which make up sixty percent, cannot absorb it at all. Their sheds would need major rebuilding or they would have to exit, and the subsidy on offer only covers one slatted-floor system. You are the person at the county agriculture bureau responsible for transition policy, and you have sixty days to produce a plan.

scene: 你们城市唯一一家还养着独立市政报道团队的日报，被一家投资集团收购。新东家的方案很直白：裁掉包括市政版在内的二十二名采编，内容转向可规模化的流量选题，并撤回已经排期的两篇本地大型项目环评报道。编辑部提出另一条路：转为读者会员制加新闻信托基金，采编权归理事会。但过渡资金只够撑四个月，而你是这张报的主编。

options.t: 我会推动会员制与信托方案并立刻启动筹资。能够盯住开发者的本地新闻是一种公共品，交给流量逻辑，最先被砍掉的往往是成本最高的调查报道。四个月够吗？不够，但不试就一定没有。
options.t_en: I would push the membership and trust plan and start fundraising immediately. Local journalism that can hold developers to account is a public good, and under the traffic logic the first thing cut is usually the most expensive investigative work. Is four months enough? No, but not trying guarantees nothing.

options.t: 我会接受投资集团的重组，同时尽量把手下的人争取留下。新闻作为一门生意已经撑不住了，与其让整张报纸关门，不如保住一份薪水和可以继续做内容的空间。清高换不到明天的头条。
options.t_en: I would accept the investment group's restructuring while fighting to keep as many of my people as possible. News as a business can no longer hold up, and rather than let the whole paper close it is better to keep a salary and some space to keep making content. High-mindedness does not buy tomorrow's front page.

options.t: 我会先把两篇环评报道做完发出去再谈其他的。由谁出钱来决定哪些事实不发表，这是我们答应读者的反面；如果这会让谈判破裂，那就说明这个价格从来就不只是收购。
options.t_en: I would finish and publish the two environmental review stories first, then talk about everything else. Letting whoever pays decide which facts are not published is the opposite of what we promised readers; if that breaks the negotiation, then the price was never only about an acquisition.

options.t: 我会主张由市政以购买公共服务的方式输血：按常住人口购买一定规模的公共议题报道，报纸保持编辑独立。公共财政买的可以是看门人而不是喉舌，这一条写清楚就能用。
options.t_en: I would argue for the municipality to fund it by purchasing a public service: buy a set amount of public-interest reporting per resident, with the paper keeping editorial independence. Public money can buy a watchdog rather than a mouthpiece, and once that clause is written clearly it works.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: The only daily in your city that still funds an independent municipal affairs desk has been bought by an investment group. The new owner's plan is blunt: cut twenty-two editorial jobs including the municipal desk, pivot to scalable traffic-driven content, and pull two already scheduled investigations into the environmental review of a large local project. The newsroom has proposed another route: convert to reader membership plus a journalism trust, with editorial control vested in a board. But the bridge funding lasts only four months, and you are the editor.

scene: 你是假释委员会的五名成员之一。案卷里的人已服刑十九年，起因是二十三岁时的一次抢劫致人死亡。狱方材料显示他近八年表现稳定：他在监狱扫盲班里教会了数十名囚犯识字，自费給一名受害者家属写过信，车间带出的徒弟出去后没人再犯。而受害者家属每年都寄来一份反对意见，这封信也在卷里。审定会上你要说清楚：什么叫一个人已经变了。

options.t: 我会支持假释。刑罚有期限，这正是它的承诺；二十年后的他不是二十三岁的他，而一个人能在最没有自由的地方教别人识字，这种改变已经用十九年自证。受害者家属的痛苦我应当承受，但它不能决定刑期。
options.t_en: I will support parole. A sentence has a term, and that is precisely its promise; the man at forty-two is not the man at twenty-three, and someone who can teach others to read in the place with the least freedom has proved that change over nineteen years. I should bear the family's pain, but it cannot set the length of the sentence.

options.t: 我会支持附条件假释：先落实就业安置与心理干预，设接触禁令和定期报到。有同情心必须有结构——真放出去还有一个四十七岁的人要生活，而他也需要再一次向社会证明自己。
options.t_en: I will support parole with conditions: employment placement and psychological support in place first, a no-contact order and regular reporting. Compassion has to have structure. If he really goes out, a forty-seven-year-old man still has to live, and he needs to prove himself to society one more time.

options.t: 我会反对。一条命换十九年，这个换算我签不下字。受害者家属年年寄那封信，说明这件事从未结束；法律留给他们的参与权就在这一张纸上，其余一切都是我们在自我原谅。
options.t_en: I will oppose it. One life exchanged for nineteen years is an equation I cannot sign. The family sends that letter every year, which shows this was never over. The right to take part that the law gives them is this one sheet of paper, and everything else is us forgiving ourselves.

options.t: 我会要求先看再犯风险的科学评估，而不是由我们五个人凭直觉投票，并把受害者家属陈述也列入考量。把决定绑在可复核的依据上，比动情更负责任，也更经得起下一次复查。
options.t_en: I will ask to see a scientific assessment of reoffending risk first, rather than the five of us voting on instinct, and to have the family's statement weighed in it. Tying the decision to evidence that can be reviewed is more responsible than being moved, and it will stand up better at the next review.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: You are one of the five members of the parole board. The man in the file has served nineteen years, for a robbery at twenty-three in which someone died. The prison's report shows eight years of stability: he has taught dozens of prisoners to read in the literacy class, written at his own expense to one of the victim's family, and none of the men he trained in the workshop have reoffended after release. The victim's family sends a letter of objection every year, and that letter is in the file too. At the review meeting you have to say clearly what it means for a person to have changed.

scene: 你们与邻国共享一条跨境河流。对方宣布要在上游建一座调蓄大坝，为他们缺水的北部平原供水，条件是向你们提供一部分廉价电力和一项即将到期的过境贸易优惠。你们的水文团队算出三个后果：下游湿地面积减少、旱季入境水量下降、沿岸两座城市的地下水补给变薄。同时另一个大国已提出为他们提供全套融资，条件是港口与铁路使用权。你是谈判团顾问。

options.t: 我会主张把对方从对手变成利益共同体：由我们出资合建、共享调度权与发电收益，总比让他们从别处拿钱更好。大坝要不要建可以由我们一起定，至少能把闸门的钥匙留一部分在自己手里。
options.t_en: I would argue for turning the other side from an adversary into a stakeholder: we co-finance and share dispatch rights and power revenue, which is better than letting them take the money from somewhere else. Whether the dam gets built can be decided by both of us together, and at least we keep a hand on part of the key to the gates.

options.t: 我会主张明确反对并启动国际水道仲裁，同时申请把下游湿地列入国际保护名录。证据我们是有的；跨境水道的规则之所以存在，就是为了让上游在这种时候付出代价。
options.t_en: I would argue for clear opposition and for triggering international watercourse arbitration, while applying to have the downstream wetland listed as an internationally protected site. We have the evidence. The rules on transboundary watercourses exist precisely so that upstream states pay a price at moments like this.

options.t: 我会主张接受这笔交易：用湿地换电力、过境优惠和二十年的旱季保底配水协议，全部写进条约并设联合监测站。强硬听起来解气，但沿岸两座城市的地下水补给本来就在逐年漏水。
options.t_en: I would argue for accepting the deal: the wetland in exchange for electricity, the transit concession, and a twenty-year guaranteed minimum dry-season allocation, all written into a treaty with joint monitoring stations. Being tough sounds satisfying, but the groundwater recharge under those two riverside cities has been leaking away year by year anyway.

options.t: 我会主张先拖住对方至少一个信用周期再谈实质条款，同时用这段时间修好自己的蓄水与再生水设施。真正的弱点在我们这边而不在那座坝上，先把自己的短板补掉再来谈条件。
options.t_en: I would argue for holding the other side off for at least one credit cycle before negotiating substance, and using that time to build our own water storage and reclaimed water facilities. The real weakness is on our side, not at that dam. Fix our own gap first, then talk terms.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: You share a cross-border river with a neighboring country. They have announced plans for a storage dam upstream to supply water to their arid northern plain, offering in exchange a share of cheap electricity and a transit trade concession that is about to expire. Your hydrology team calculates three consequences: the downstream wetland shrinks, dry-season inflow falls, and groundwater recharge thins under two riverside cities. Meanwhile another major power has offered to finance the whole project in return for port and railway access. You are an adviser to the negotiating team.

scene: 你们市的廉租房轮候家庭已排到八年，而财政手上有笔专项资金，只能选一个方向：给轮候家庭发货币补贴让他们自己去市场上租；集中新建一批保障房；还是收购存量二手房改造后配租。房价正在下行，三种做法的单位成本和见效时间差别很大。你是财政局外聘的政策顾问，明天要给意见。

options.t: 我会主张货币补贴，钱直接到家庭手里。八年等待不是因为他们怀念某种户型，而是因为没有支付能力；现金是最尊重他们自己处境的形式，也最不容易在中间环节沉淀损耗。
options.t_en: I would argue for cash allowances, with the money going straight to families. The eight-year wait is not because they miss a particular floor plan but because they cannot pay; cash is the form that most respects their own circumstances and is least likely to silt up in intermediate hands.

options.t: 我会主张收储存量二手房并分散配租：交付最快，学校、菜场和医疗现成，还能把一家人放进已经熟起来的社区。现金涌进租赁市场只会抬高租金，因为房子的总数并没有变。
options.t_en: I would argue for buying existing second-hand flats and allocating them across scattered locations: fastest delivery, schools, markets and clinics already there, and a family placed in a community that is already alive. Cash flooding into the rental market only pushes rents up, because the total number of homes does not change.

options.t: 我会主张集中新建：只有握在政府手里的房子，十年后还服务于同一个群体；货币补贴是年度开支，房价一涨就前功尽弃。队伍已经排到第三代了，总得给后代留下资产。
options.t_en: I would argue for concentrated new build: only housing held in public hands will still serve the same group in ten years, whereas a cash allowance is an annual expense and is wiped out the moment prices rise. The queue already runs to a third generation, so we owe the next generation some assets.

options.t: 我会先要求把准入核验与补贴公式修好再谈形式：核验松散、骗租查处不到位的情形下，任何一种形式都会被人消耗掉一半。工具可以讨论，但当篮子漏了，装什么都一样。
options.t_en: I would first demand that eligibility checks and the subsidy formula be fixed before discussing the form. With loose verification and weak enforcement against fraudulent tenancies, any instrument will be half consumed. The tool can be debated, but when the basket leaks it makes no difference what you put in it.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: Families on your city's waiting list for low-rent housing are now queued eight years deep, and the finance bureau holds a special fund that can go in only one direction: cash allowances so that waiting families rent on the open market, building a batch of new social housing, or buying up existing second-hand flats, renovating them and allocating them. Prices are falling, and the three options differ sharply in unit cost and time to delivery. You are an outside policy adviser to the finance bureau and must give your view tomorrow.

scene: 小区电动车充电桩只有六个车位，晚高峰常常排起长队，物业打算把中央那块闲置绿地改建为带顶棚的充电车棚来解决排队难题。支持者说刚需优先，反对者担心绿化减少、楼间距更挤，这背后是「实用便利」与「公共环境」谁先让步的真实张力，居民意见明显分裂。

options.t: 我支持改建，充电是每天的实际刚需，绿地可以改到边角补种几排灌木，总比大家天天抢桩强，先把问题解决了最重要。
options.t_en: I support the conversion — charging is a daily necessity, and we can replant shrubs in the corners. Solving the queue problem matters more than preserving that one patch of green.

options.t: 我反对占绿地，小区绿化率本来就低，应该保留这片地，让车主去周边商场或错峰充电，不该为图方便牺牲大家的环境。
options.t_en: I oppose taking the green space; our greenery ratio is already low. Owners should charge off-peak or at malls rather than sacrificing the environment for convenience.

options.t: 公共空间怎么用得大伙投票定，我会提议开业主大会表决，少数服从多数，不能让物业自己拍板就直接动工。
options.t_en: How public space is used should be decided by a vote. I'd call an owners' meeting and let the majority decide, not the property manager alone.

options.t: 这种小事该交给街道规划部门统一调配，居民各执一词没结论，专业规划才能兼顾绿地不被砍与充电不难两不误。
options.t_en: This should be left to the district planning office. Residents won't agree, and professional planning can balance greenery and charging.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The compound has only six parking bays with charging points for electric scooters, and at the evening peak the queue runs long. The property manager wants to turn the unused green space in the middle of the compound into a covered charging shelter to clear the backlog. Supporters say a basic need comes first; opponents worry about losing the greenery and about the blocks being squeezed even closer together. Behind it is a real question of whether practical convenience or shared open space gives way first, and residents are clearly split.

scene: 楼上住户总把湿拖把晾在阳台栏杆外，水珠日夜滴到楼下窗台和晾衣杆上，楼下多次上门沟通对方都笑笑说下次注意却照旧。物业说没有明文禁止，双方陷入「我的晾晒自由」与「你的不受打扰」的拉锯，邻里关系越来越僵。，支持和反对的声音都不少，社区内部一时难以形成共识。

options.t: 我自己花点钱装个外伸遮雨棚自保，不跟人红脸起冲突，滴水淋不着我就行，邻里关系能不闹僵就不闹僵。
options.t_en: I'll spend a little on an extending awning to protect myself. As long as the drips don't hit me, I won't argue and strain the relationship.

options.t: 我找物业按管理规约处罚，既然有公约就该执行，不能总让守规矩的人吃亏、晾拖把的钻空子当没看见。
options.t_en: I'll ask the property to penalize per the rules. The covenant should be enforced so rule-followers aren't the ones who suffer.

options.t: 我在业主群里公开@对方，把照片发出来靠邻里舆论施压，让大家评评理，这比私下磨嘴皮子要有用得多。
options.t_en: I'll post the photos in the owners' group and let public opinion pressure them. Peer pressure works better than private nagging.

options.t: 我还是上门好言商量，顺手送对方两个拖把架，邻里情面最要紧，未必非要闹到物业或群里才把事解决。
options.t_en: I'd visit and talk it over kindly, even gifting a mop hanger. Neighborly goodwill matters most; it needn't escalate to the property or group.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: The upstairs neighbor always hangs wet mops outside the balcony railing, and water drips day and night onto the windowsill and drying rack below. The downstairs household has gone up to talk several times; the neighbor smiles and says he will be careful next time, then does exactly the same thing. The property manager says there is no explicit rule against it. The two sides are stuck in a tug of war between my freedom to dry things and your right not to be disturbed, and relations between the neighbors are getting worse and worse. There are plenty of voices on both sides, and the community cannot form a consensus for now.

scene: 老旧小区准备升级门禁，物业推荐装人脸识别闸机，说能拦住外来推销和可疑人员。年轻租户担心人脸数据被留存泄露，老年住户却觉得刷脸省得带卡。这是「出入安全」与「生物隐私」之间的现实权衡，居民态度两极。，各方都拿得出道理，真要落定却谁也说服不了谁。

options.t: 我支持装，小区安全优先，刷脸后陌生人进不来，老年人也不用记卡，住着比现在踏实多了。
options.t_en: I support it — security first. Face recognition keeps strangers out and spares the elderly from carrying cards. Much safer.

options.t: 我反对，人脸是敏感生物信息，门禁用钥匙或密码就够了，不该为了方便让所有人都被采集肖像留底。
options.t_en: I oppose it. Faces are sensitive biometrics; keys or codes suffice. We shouldn't be scanned just for convenience.

options.t: 可以装，但必须经业主大会表决，且数据只存在本地机器、绝不传云端，整个过程要透明可查才行。
options.t_en: It's fine if owners vote for it, the data stays on local devices, never the cloud, and the process is transparent.

options.t: 我建议改用非人脸的智能门禁卡，既能记录谁进出防尾随，又不收集面孔，兼顾安全与隐私两方。
options.t_en: I'd use non-facial smart cards — they log entries to prevent tailgating yet collect no faces, balancing safety and privacy.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: An old residential compound is upgrading its entrance security, and the property manager recommends facial recognition gates, saying they would keep out cold-callers and suspicious strangers. Younger tenants worry that face data will be retained and leaked; older residents think scanning a face is easier than carrying a card. This is the practical trade-off between secure entry and biometric privacy, and residents are split down the middle. Everyone can make a case, yet once it comes to actually deciding, no one can convince anyone else.

scene: 小区宠物狗越来越多，部分狗主遛狗不清理粪便，草坪和步道常有遗留，带孩子玩耍的家长意见很大。物业想管又怕得罪人，居民对「怎么管、谁出钱」分歧明显，这折射出养宠自由与公共洁净之间的持续冲突。，利弊明摆在面前，怎样取舍成了绕不开的现实难题。

options.t: 我主张物业设巡查和罚款，屡教不改就公示名单，公共环境得有人管，不能全靠住户自觉。
options.t_en: I want the property to patrol and fine repeat offenders, even publishing names. Public hygiene needs enforcement, not just good will.

options.t: 我觉得邻里互相提醒最管用，在单元口放免费拾便袋，靠人情和习惯慢慢改，比罚款要温和得多。
options.t_en: I think neighbors reminding each other works best — free poop bags at the entrance. Habit and goodwill beat fines.

options.t: 我建议装监控抓拍不清理的行为并单元屏公示，技术手段最公正，也不用人盯人、伤了邻里和气。
options.t_en: I'd install cameras to catch offenders and display them on the lobby screen — tech is fair and avoids personal friction.

options.t: 我倾向于划一片专用遛狗区并隔离，爱狗的和怕脏的各行其道，自由与整洁可以两全其美。
options.t_en: I'd designate a fenced dog area. Dog lovers and the cleanliness-minded keep to their lanes — freedom and tidiness both win.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: There are more and more dogs in the compound, and some owners do not clean up after them, so droppings are often left on the lawns and the paths, and parents out with small children are angry about it. The property manager wants to act but is afraid of offending people, and residents disagree openly about how to regulate it and who should pay. It reflects the running conflict between the freedom to keep a pet and a shared standard of cleanliness.

scene: 六层老楼住户倡议加装电梯，高层老人上下楼困难、意愿强烈，低层住户却担心采光变差、噪音增加且要摊一笔钱，不愿签字。单元内为此分成两派，牵扯「多数人便利」与「少数人权益」之间的现实博弈。，争论持续发酵，大家都在等一个能服众的收场。

options.t: 我支持政府补贴推动统一加装，这是惠民工程，低层受点影响但整体受益，该顾全小区的大局。
options.t_en: I back government-subsidized unified installation. It's a public good; lower floors bear minor impact but the community gains.

options.t: 我主张高低层私下协商、按楼层阶梯分摊费用，愿装愿摊的自己谈，别搞强制的一刀切。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: I'd have high and low floors privately negotiate staggered costs. Those who want it pay — no blanket mandate.

options.t: 我反对用多数票强制低层，采光噪音是实打实的损失，少数人的财产权不能被多数人绑架。
options.t_en: I oppose forcing lower floors by majority vote. Lost light and noise are real; minorities' property rights shouldn't be overridden.

options.t: 我建议用住宅维修基金加居民自筹，由业委会牵头自治，政府少插手、社区自己把事解决。
options.t_en: I'd use the maintenance fund plus self-raised money, with the owners' committee leading. Less government, more local autonomy.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Residents of an old six-floor building have proposed installing an elevator. The elderly on the upper floors find the stairs hard and want it strongly. The households on the lower floors worry about worse light, more noise and having to put money in, and will not sign. The stairwell has split into two camps, caught in the real contest between convenience for the majority and the rights of a minority. The argument keeps going, and everyone is waiting for an ending that people can accept.

scene: 一家互联网创业公司盛行「996」加班文化，老板在晨会上说年轻人就该拼搏、公司也会发加班费。已婚带娃的员工苦不堪言，单身员工倒觉得能多赚。这关乎「奋斗回报」与「劳工休息权」之间的持续拉扯。，两种诉求都有人撑腰，协调起来格外费劲。

options.t: 我支持适度拼搏，只要公司真给足加班费、不强制，多劳多得、年轻时候多存点钱也挺好。
options.t_en: I support hustling if the overtime pay is real and not coerced. More work, more pay — good for saving young.

options.t: 我反对强制长时间加班，劳动法保障休息权，用加班换产出是透支人，公司该守住底线。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: I oppose forced long hours. Labor law protects rest; trading hours for output burns people out. Firms must hold the line.

options.t: 我主张由工会代表和资方谈工时与报酬，集体议价比个人单挑老板有底气也更有谈判力。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: I want unions to negotiate hours and pay with management. Collective bargaining beats facing the boss alone.

options.t: 我认为政府应立法明确最长周工时并严查违规，光靠员工个人维权实在太弱势了。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: The government should cap weekly hours by law and enforce it. Individual complaints are too weak alone.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: An internet startup runs on a 996 culture of nine to nine, six days a week, and the boss tells the morning meeting that young people should strive and that the company does pay overtime. Employees with spouses and children are miserable; single colleagues rather like the extra money. This is the running tug-of-war between reward for hard work and the right to rest, and each claim has its backers, which is exactly why reconciling them is so hard.

scene: 某零售企业上线算法排班与考核系统，员工每单、每步都被实时打分，排名末位者自动减薪。员工抱怨不知道评分标准、申诉无门，管理层称数据最客观。这触及「效率至上」与「算法透明」的矛盾。，不同居民各有各的难处，最后怎么平衡仍没有标准答案。

options.t: 我支持数据考核，算法不看人情、标准统一，比主管凭印象打分公平，效率也明显更高。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: I support data scoring — algorithms ignore favoritism and apply uniform standards, fairer and more efficient than managers' impressions.

options.t: 我反对黑箱算法，评分逻辑不公开就该有人工复核通道，员工有权知道为什么被扣分。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: I oppose black-box algorithms. If the logic is hidden there must be human review; workers deserve to know why points are docked.

options.t: 我认为员工必须能查看自己的评分并提起申诉，过程透明才能让人服气，不能系统说了算。
options.t_en: Workers must see their scores and appeal. Transparency earns trust; the system alone can't be final.

options.t: 我主张政府把算法纳入监管，要求企业披露考核模型、防歧视，别让机器替人做裁断。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Government should regulate algorithms, forcing firms to disclose models and prevent bias. Machines shouldn't decide fates.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A retail company has brought in algorithmic scheduling and appraisal. Every order an employee handles and every movement they make is scored in real time, and whoever ranks at the bottom takes an automatic pay cut. Staff complain that they do not know what the scoring criteria are and that there is no way to appeal. Management says the data are the most objective thing there is. The clash is between efficiency above all and the demand that an algorithm be transparent.

scene: 一家制造厂因订单季节性波动，想用劳务派遣工替代部分正式工以压低人力成本、灵活调配。正式工担心被边缘化，派遣工则看重能进门工作。这是「用工灵活」与「就业稳定」之间的现实取舍。，支持和反对的声音都不少，社区内部一时难以形成共识。

options.t: 我支持灵活用工，订单淡旺季明显，派遣能降本保竞争力，企业活下来大家才有活干。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: I support flexible staffing. With seasonal orders, dispatch cuts costs and keeps the firm competitive — survival helps everyone.

options.t: 我反对滥用派遣，正式工与派遣工干一样的活却不同权，应保障劳动者稳定的就业。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: I oppose dispatch abuse. Same work, different rights erodes stability; workers deserve secure employment.

options.t: 我主张允许派遣，但立法要求同工同酬、设转正比例，别让它变成廉价用工的漏洞。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Allow dispatch, but mandate equal pay and conversion quotas by law, so it isn't a cheap-labor loophole.

options.t: 我认为用派遣还是正式工是企业自主经营权，市场会自然淘汰那些用工不合理的公司。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Whether to use dispatch is managerial discretion; the market will punish firms with bad labor models.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A manufacturing plant, facing seasonal swings in orders, wants to replace some permanent staff with agency workers in order to cut labor costs and adjust staffing flexibly. The permanent workers worry about being pushed to the margins, while the agency workers value simply getting a foot in the door. This is the real trade-off between flexibility in hiring and stability of employment. There are plenty of voices on both sides, and the community cannot form a consensus for now.

scene: 远程办公普及后，一家公司要求居家员工装上监控软件，实时记录屏幕活动、统计键盘鼠标轨迹，称是为了保证效率。员工觉得家里被安了眼睛，管理层说数据只用于考核。这是「管理效率」与「居家隐私」的张力。，各方都拿得出道理，真要落定却谁也说服不了谁。

options.t: 我支持装监控，居家容易摸鱼，公司付薪水有权知道产出过程，不然远程就是钻空子。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: I support monitoring. Remote work invites slacking; the firm paying wages deserves to see the process.

options.t: 我反对，家是私人空间，屏幕监控侵犯生活隐私，考核看结果就够了，别越界。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: I oppose it. Home is private; screen monitoring invades life. Judge by results, not by surveillance.

options.t: 我倾向只看交付成果、不盯过程，给员工安排和节奏的自主权，效率反而更高。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: I'd judge deliverables, not process, giving staff autonomy over schedule — that lifts productivity.

options.t: 我主张员工代表和公司协商出监控的边界清单，哪些可记、哪些禁区，白纸黑字定下来。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Worker reps and the firm should negotiate a boundary list of what's monitored and what's off-limits, in writing.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Now that remote work is common, one company requires home-based staff to install monitoring software that logs screen activity in real time and counts keyboard and mouse movements, saying it is to guarantee efficiency. Employees feel a camera has been installed in their home; management says the data is used only for appraisal. This is the tension between managerial efficiency and privacy at home. Everyone can make a case, yet once it comes to actually deciding, no one can convince anyone else.

scene: 不少招聘启事写明「35岁以下优先」，中年求职者投简历石沉大海。年轻HR说这是经验与成本的权衡，被拒的求职者觉得是年龄歧视。这关乎「用人自主」与「就业公平」之间的冲突。，利弊明摆在面前，怎样取舍成了绕不开的现实难题。

options.t: 我理解企业自主，35岁以上薪资预期高、家庭牵绊多，用人成本考量其实很现实。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: I get employer discretion. Over-35 candidates expect higher pay and have family ties — cost is a real factor.

options.t: 我反对年龄划线，这是赤裸裸的歧视，应立法禁止、设举报通道保障公平。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: I oppose age caps — outright discrimination. Ban them by law with reporting channels for fairness.

options.t: 我认为市场会自然淘汰偏见，靠年龄筛人的公司留不住人，长远来看会吃亏。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: The market punishes bias; firms filtering by age lose talent and suffer long-term.

options.t: 我主张员工组织起来监督招聘、对明显歧视的岗位发起举报，用集体力量施压。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Workers should organize to monitor hiring and report blatantly discriminatory postings, applying collective pressure.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: Plenty of job adverts say under thirty-fives preferred, and middle-aged applicants send their CVs into silence. Younger recruiters call it a trade-off between experience and cost; the people turned down call it age discrimination. It is a conflict between an employer's freedom to choose whom to hire and fairness in the labour market, and the costs of the two positions fall on very different people.

scene: 某社交平台一条未经证实的实名举报帖冲上热搜，转发几万次，评论区两极分化。平台纠结要不要限流，支持者说防谣言、反对者说捂盖子。这是「信息秩序」与「流通自由」之间的拉锯。，争论持续发酵，大家都在等一个能服众的收场。

options.t: 我支持平台先限流，没核实的爆料疯传会误伤当事人，等查清再放也不迟。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: I support throttling first. Unverified allegations spread fast and harm the accused; release after facts check out.

options.t: 我反对限流，谣言应该让它在公开场域里自净，平台一限流反而像捂盖子、更可疑。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: I oppose throttling. Rumors self-correct in the open; limiting reach looks like a cover-up and fuels suspicion.

options.t: 我主张交给第三方事实核查标注「待核实」，既不删也不放任，让用户自己判断。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: I'd have independent fact-checkers label it 'unverified' — neither deleted nor unchecked, letting users decide.

options.t: 我倾向用户举报加算法降权、社区自治，平台别当裁判，靠众人之力压住水军。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: I'd use user reports plus algorithmic down-ranking — community self-governance, not platform as judge.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: An unverified post accusing a named person shot to the top of the trending list on a social platform, shared tens of thousands of times, with the comments split down the middle. The platform is torn over whether to throttle its reach; supporters say this prevents rumors, opponents say it is covering things up. This is the tug of war between order in information and freedom of circulation. The argument keeps going, and everyone is waiting for an ending that people can accept.

scene: 大学课堂上有老师常借专业课延伸出争议性的社会与政治观点，部分学生认同、部分学生不适，有人偷偷录下视频发到校外账号并举报。校方陷入「学术自由」与「课堂边界」的两难。，两种诉求都有人撑腰，协调起来格外费劲。

options.t: 我支持举报，课堂是公共教学场所，不该夹带偏颇立场，老师也该守职业分寸。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: I support reporting. The classroom is public teaching space; biased views don't belong, and teachers owe professional restraint.

options.t: 我反对举报，大学本该包容异见、激发思辨，把老师送上风口只会寒了学术自由。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: I oppose reporting. Universities should embrace dissent and debate; targeting teachers chills academic freedom.

options.t: 我主张学校设正式申诉渠道，由学术委员会评估是否越界，而不是学生私自外发视频。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: I'd have a formal channel where a faculty committee assesses overreach, not students leaking videos outward.

options.t: 我认为学生有权不选这门课或换班，用脚投票比举报更体面，也保住自己节奏。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Students can simply drop or switch sections — voting with their feet beats reporting and keeps their own peace.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: In university classes, a lecturer often extends the professional material into contested social and political opinions. Some students agree, some are uncomfortable, and someone secretly recorded a video, posted it to an outside account and reported it. The university is caught between academic freedom and the boundaries of the classroom, and each claim has its backers, which is exactly why reconciling them is so hard.

scene: 网络匿名发言常滋生网暴和谣言，监管部门酝酿要求平台对重点板块实行实名发帖。网友分成两派：一方要干净空间，一方怕实名后弱势群体不敢发声。这是「问责」与「匿名保护」的权衡。，不同居民各有各的难处，最后怎么平衡仍没有标准答案。

options.t: 我支持重点区实名，匿名太容易造谣网暴，实名能让人对自己的话负责。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: I support real-name in key zones. Anonymity breeds libel and mobbing; real names make people accountable.

options.t: 我反对强制实名，匿名恰恰是弱势群体、举报者敢说话的护盾，不能因噎废食。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: I oppose mandatory real-names. Anonymity shields the vulnerable and whistleblowers; don't throw it out.

options.t: 我主张分级管理，普通闲聊可匿名，涉及公共投诉举报的板块才要求实名。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: I'd tier it: casual chat stays anonymous, but public complaint sections require real names.

options.t: 我认为实名与否应交由用户自己决定，平台提供开关，个人为选择负责。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Let users decide for themselves; the platform offers a toggle and individuals own their choice.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Anonymous posting online breeds harassment and rumour, and the regulator is drafting a requirement for real-name posting in the platform's key sections. Users have split in two: one side wants a clean space, the other fears that once names are attached, the vulnerable will stop speaking at all. It is a trade-off between accountability and the protection anonymity gives, and neither side thinks the other has understood what is at stake.

scene: 历史教材对某个近代事件的表述引发家长争论，有人觉得不够全面，民间机构想推出补充读物供学生参考。教育部门担心口径不一，民间则强调多元视角。这是「统一叙述」与「多元解读」的碰撞。，支持和反对的声音都不少，社区内部一时难以形成共识。

options.t: 我支持民间出补充读物，历史本就该多视角，学生接触不同叙述才有独立判断。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: I support supplementary readers. History deserves multiple angles; students need varied narratives to judge independently.

options.t: 我反对民间自行编史，教材须由权威统一，口径散了会误导孩子、制造混乱。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: I oppose private histories. Textbooks need one authoritative voice; fragmented accounts mislead children.

options.t: 我建议学校列出多视角书单、在课堂上引导比较，由老师把关而不是直接禁。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Schools should offer a multi-perspective reading list and guide comparison in class, with teachers curating — not banning.

options.t: 我认为家长自己在家补充讲解就行，不必外推读物，家庭教育补位最自然。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Parents can supplement at home; no need for public readers. Family education filling the gap is most natural.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: The way a history textbook describes a modern event has set off an argument among parents. Some feel it is not complete enough, and a civic organization wants to publish supplementary reading for students to consult. The education department worries about inconsistent accounts, while the civic side stresses multiple perspectives. This is a collision between a single unified narrative and plural interpretation. There are plenty of voices on both sides, and the community cannot form a consensus for now.

scene: 城市中心广场是市民集会常去的地方，现行规定所有集会需提前三天向公安报批。维权团体希望放宽、随聚随走，警方则担心人流失控、影响交通。这是「集会自由」与「公共秩序」的张力。，各方都拿得出道理，真要落定却谁也说服不了谁。

options.t: 我主张放宽审批，和平集会自由是基本权利，提前三天报批门槛太高、变相限制。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: Loosen approval. Peaceful assembly is basic; a three-day pre-approval is a hidden barrier that limits it.

options.t: 我支持维持审批，广场在闹市，不报批人流一多就乱，警方得有底才能保安全。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: Keep approval. The square is downtown; without it crowds spiral and police can't plan for safety.

options.t: 我倾向折中：小规模随聚免批、超人数或占道的活动才报批，分档管理。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Compromise: small gatherings skip approval, only large or road-blocking ones file — tiered management.

options.t: 我建议集会场地由社区和警方协商排期，邻里自己协调比一刀切禁令更柔和。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Let communities and police coordinate a schedule; local negotiation is softer than a blanket ban.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: The central city square is where citizens usually gather, and current rules require any assembly to be reported to the police three days in advance. Advocacy groups want the requirement relaxed so that people can gather as they come; the police worry about crowds getting out of control and traffic being disrupted. This is the tension between freedom of assembly and public order. Everyone can make a case, yet once it comes to actually deciding, no one can convince anyone else.

scene: 某大城市研究对多套房产征收持有税，用以补贴保障房和公共服务。有房者担心资产缩水、无房者盼着房价降温，学界对「劫富济贫」还是「伤及社会活力」争论不休。这是再分配与效率的拉锯。，利弊明摆在面前，怎样取舍成了绕不开的现实难题。

options.t: 我支持征房产税，财富多了就该多担税、反哺公共服务，利于缩小贫富差距。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: I support a property tax. More wealth means more tax to fund public goods, narrowing inequality.

options.t: 我反对，加税最终转嫁租金、伤的是中产和租客，也打击持有与改善住房的积极性。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: I oppose it. The tax lands on rents, hurting the middle class and tenants, and dulls the incentive to improve housing.

options.t: 我主张只对第二套以上或豪宅征收、设高免税额，精准调节不误伤普通自住。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Tax only second homes or mansions with a high exemption — targeted, sparing ordinary owner-occupiers.

options.t: 我倾向用增值税、消费税等替代，不动房产存量，靠流量税种调节更平稳。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Use VAT or consumption taxes instead, leaving housing stock alone; flow-based taxes adjust more smoothly.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A large city is studying a holding tax on second and further homes, with the revenue going to subsidised housing and public services. Owners worry about their assets shrinking, people without property are hoping prices cool, and academics argue endlessly over whether it is taking from the rich to help the poor or damaging the vitality of the city. It is a tug of war between redistribution and efficiency, and every number in the proposal lands on someone differently.

scene: 经济下行期，地方政府盘算怎么刺激消费：一种是直接给居民发现金，一种是发限定在本地的消费券。商家盼人来、居民盼到手，财政则盘算杠杆与成本。这是「普惠直补」与「定向拉动」的取舍。，争论持续发酵，大家都在等一个能服众的收场。

options.t: 我支持直接发现金，钱到手居民自己决定怎么花，最实在也最尊重个人选择。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: I support direct cash. People decide how to spend it — most concrete and respectful of choice.

options.t: 我倾向发本地消费券，钱留在街坊商家、杠杆更大，能真救活小店和餐饮。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: I prefer local vouchers; money stays with neighborhood shops, a bigger lever that rescues small businesses.

options.t: 我觉得都不如减税降费、扶持企业，把生产端搞活了就业和收入自然就上来。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Neither beats tax cuts for firms. Revive production and jobs and incomes follow naturally.

options.t: 我主张政府定向补贴受冲击的行业稳就业，钱花在保岗位上比撒给个人更有效。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: I'd have government target aid to hit industries to protect jobs — more effective than spraying cash on individuals.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: In a downturn, the local government is working out how to boost consumption: one option is handing cash directly to residents, the other is issuing vouchers that can only be spent locally. Businesses want people coming through the door, residents want money in hand, and the finance office is weighing leverage and cost. This is the choice between universal direct transfers and targeted stimulus. The argument keeps going, and everyone is waiting for an ending that people can accept.

scene: 多地拟上调最低工资标准，工会欢迎、小商户叫苦。支持者说保底层生活，反对方说会推高用工成本、逼老板少招人。这是「劳工底线」与「市场出清」之间的交锋。，两种诉求都有人撑腰，协调起来格外费劲。，不同居民各有各的难处，最后怎么平衡仍没有标准答案。

options.t: 我支持大幅提高最低工资，劳动者体面生活是底线，企业也该承担相应成本。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: I back a big hike. A dignified life is the floor; firms should shoulder the cost too.

options.t: 我反对猛涨，小本生意利润薄，工资硬抬只会裁员、让最弱的人先失业。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: I oppose sharp hikes. Thin-margin shops will just cut staff, and the weakest lose jobs first.

options.t: 我主张分区域、按生活成本浮动设定，一线城市高、县域低，不搞全国统一数。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Set it regionally by cost of living — higher in metropolises, lower in counties, not one national number.

options.t: 我认为应由劳资双方集体谈判定工资，政府别统一定价，行业差异实在太大。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Wages should be set by collective labor-management bargaining; government pricing ignores huge sector gaps.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: Several places plan to raise the minimum wage; unions welcome it and small shopkeepers complain. Supporters say it protects the living standards of those at the bottom; opponents say it pushes up labour costs and forces owners to hire fewer people. This is the clash between a wage floor and market clearing. Each claim has its backers, which is exactly why reconciling them is so hard, and different residents each have their own difficulty, so there is still no standard answer on how to balance them.

scene: 在一般竞争领域，国企与民企同台竞技，有人主张国企退出让市场更有效率，也有人认为国企保民生稳定、不能退。这关乎「市场主导」与「国有兜底」的路线之争。，不同居民各有各的难处，最后怎么平衡仍没有标准答案。，支持和反对的声音都不少，社区内部一时难以形成共识。

options.t: 我支持国企退出一般竞争领域，民企更讲效率，把市场交还给民营资本。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: SOEs should exit ordinary competition; private firms are more efficient — hand the market back to them.

options.t: 我反对退出，国企在民生、就业波动时是稳定器，不能完全交给逐利的民企。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: Don't exit. SOEs stabilize livelihoods and employment; leaving it all to profit-seeking private firms is risky.

options.t: 我主张分类改革：关键战略领域国有、一般领域混改放开，因业施策。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Reform by category: state-owned in strategic sectors, mixed-ownership opening elsewhere — tailor by industry.

options.t: 我倾向让市场自然选择，谁效率高谁留，政府少定身份、少给输血。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Let the market pick winners by efficiency; government should stop labeling and subsidizing by ownership.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: In ordinary competitive sectors, state-owned and private firms compete on the same ground. Some argue the state firms should withdraw so the market works more efficiently; others say they keep livelihoods stable and must not withdraw. It is a contest over whether the market or the state should be the backstop, and both sides can point to real cases that support them.

scene: 关于是否开征遗产税，主张者说能削贫富代际传递，反对者说会逼资产外流、伤创富动力。富裕家庭筹划移民避险，普通家庭则盼更公平。这是「代际公平」与「私产激励」的对峙。，支持和反对的声音都不少，社区内部一时难以形成共识。

options.t: 我支持开征遗产税，财富代际传递拉大差距，税收能让起点更公平。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: I support an estate tax. Inherited wealth widens gaps; taxation makes the starting line fairer.

options.t: 我反对开征，辛苦创下的家业该由家人继承，重税打击奋斗和储蓄意愿。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: I oppose it. Hard-earned family wealth should pass on; heavy tax kills the drive to build and save.

options.t: 我主张设很高免税额、只对巨额遗产征收，普通家庭不受影响、巨富适当贡献。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Set a high exemption, taxing only huge estates — ordinary families untouched, the ultra-rich contribute.

options.t: 我倾向用慈善抵税来替代，鼓励富人以捐赠换减税，比强制征收更柔和。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Use charity tax credits instead, nudging the rich to donate for deductions — softer than forced collection.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: On whether to introduce an inheritance tax, supporters say it would weaken the transmission of wealth across generations, and opponents say it would drive assets abroad and damage the incentive to create wealth. Wealthy families are planning emigration to protect themselves, while ordinary families hope for something fairer. This is the standoff between fairness across generations and the incentive of private property. There are plenty of voices on both sides, and the community cannot form a consensus for now.

scene: 国产高端芯片遭国外制裁，产业链吃紧。一种声音主张国家全力补贴、搞全产业链自主可控；另一种说融入全球分工更划算。这是「技术自立」与「全球协作」的路线选择。，各方都拿得出道理，真要落定却谁也说服不了谁。，利弊明摆在面前，怎样取舍成了绕不开的现实难题。

options.t: 我支持举国补贴、把设计制造全链条自主搞起来，关键命脉不能捏在别人手里。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: I back national subsidies to build the whole chain domestically — critical lifelines can't sit in others' hands.

options.t: 我反对全自主，全球分工才高效，砸钱重复造轮子不如买来集成更划算。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: I oppose full autonomy. Global division is efficient; rebuilding every wheel wastes money better spent integrating.

options.t: 我主张关键设备与材料自主、周边环节继续开放合作，抓牛鼻子、不闭门。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Keep core equipment and materials domestic, stay open on peripheral links — grip the key, don't shut the door.

options.t: 我认为研发该由企业主导、政府少干预，市场导向比行政指派更出成果。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: R&D should be enterprise-led with less government meddling; market direction beats administrative orders.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Domestic high-end chips have been hit by foreign sanctions and the supply chain is under strain. One voice calls for the state to subsidise at full force and build a self-sufficient chain end to end; another says it is cheaper to stay embedded in the global division of labour. This is the choice of route between technological self-reliance and global cooperation. Everyone can make a case, yet once it comes to actually deciding, no one can convince anyone else, and with the pros and cons laid out plainly, how to weigh them has become an unavoidable practical problem.

scene: 跨境电商的小额包裹长期享受免税额度，冲击了本土实体零售。本土商家呼吁取消免税门槛，消费者则担心涨价、选择变少。这是「保护本土」与「消费红利」之间的拉扯。，利弊明摆在面前，怎样取舍成了绕不开的现实难题。

options.t: 我支持取消小额免税，给本土商家公平环境，不能让进口包裹长期占便宜。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Cancel the small-parcel exemption for a fair field; imported parcels shouldn't get a permanent free ride.

options.t: 我反对取消，免税让消费者买到便宜进口货，好处实打实落在老百姓手里。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: Keep it. The exemption lets consumers buy cheap imports — a real benefit in ordinary people's hands.

options.t: 我主张设一个合理门槛，小额自用保留、批量代购才征税，平衡两边。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Set a sensible threshold: keep small personal use duty-free, tax bulk reselling — balance both sides.

options.t: 我倾向由市场定价、政府不设这个优惠，让内外商品在同一起跑线竞争。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Let the market price it; government should drop the perk so domestic and foreign goods compete evenly.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: Small cross-border e-commerce parcels have long enjoyed a tax-free allowance, and that has hit local bricks-and-mortar retail. Local shopkeepers are calling for the threshold to be scrapped; consumers worry about higher prices and fewer choices. It is a pull between protecting domestic business and preserving the benefits consumers get, and the argument is really about who should absorb the cost of the adjustment.

scene: 城里一家几十年老字号点心铺，被连锁咖啡和网红烘焙品牌抢走客流，老师傅担心手艺失传。有人呼吁政府扶持老字号，也有人认为该让它优胜劣汰。这是「护文化」与「市场法则」的取舍。，争论持续发酵，大家都在等一个能服众的收场。

options.t: 我支持政府扶持老字号，它承载城市记忆和就业，不能眼睁睁被连锁冲垮。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: I support aiding old brands — they carry the city's memory and jobs, not to be crushed by chains.

options.t: 我反对扶持，市场优胜劣汰最公平，不好吃不上进的就该让位给新品牌。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: No aid. Market survival of the fittest is fair; stale brands should yield to new ones.

options.t: 我主张帮老字号做品牌升级、触网出海，用现代手段把传统手艺卖出去。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Help old brands upgrade and go global online — sell traditional craft with modern means.

options.t: 我认为消费者用钞票投票就行，好不好吃大家自己选，不必政府出手。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Let consumers vote with wallets; they choose what's good. No government hand needed.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: An old pastry shop that has been in the city for decades is losing customers to chain coffee shops and trendy bakery brands, and the master baker worries the craft will die with him. Some call for the government to support longstanding local brands; others say let it survive or fail on its merits. This is the choice between protecting culture and the law of the market. The argument keeps going, and everyone is waiting for an ending that people can accept.

scene: 一家本土科技公司估值很高，外资基金想大比例收购股份。支持者欢迎资本、反对者警惕核心技术与数据外流。监管面临「开门引资」与「安全审查」的抉择。，两种诉求都有人撑腰，协调起来格外费劲。，不同居民各有各的难处，最后怎么平衡仍没有标准答案。

options.t: 我支持限制外资收购，核心科技关系国家安全，不能让命脉落到外人手里。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Restrict foreign buys. Core tech touches national security; the lifeline can't fall to outsiders.

options.t: 我欢迎资本自由流动，外资进来带来钱和管理，对企业壮大是好事。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: Welcome free capital flow. Foreign funds bring money and management that help firms grow.

options.t: 我主张对敏感行业做安全审查、一般领域放开，分门别类管。，照这个思路走最省心。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Run security reviews on sensitive sectors, open the rest — manage by category.

options.t: 我倾向以市场为主、只在确涉国防民生的个案上干预，少设普遍门槛。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Mostly market-led, intervening only in clear defense or livelihood cases — few blanket barriers.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A local technology company carries a high valuation, and a foreign fund wants to buy a large stake. Supporters welcome the capital; opponents are wary of core technology and data flowing out. Regulators face the choice between opening the door to investment and security review. Each claim has its backers, which is exactly why reconciling them is so hard, and different residents each have their own difficulty, so there is still no standard answer on how to balance them.

scene: 本国耕地有限，主粮长期部分依赖进口。农业派主张高度自给保安全，贸易派说国际采购更便宜、把地腾给高值作物。这是「粮食自主」与「比较效益」之间的权衡。，不同居民各有各的难处，最后怎么平衡仍没有标准答案。，支持和反对的声音都不少，社区内部一时难以形成共识。

options.t: 我支持主粮高度自给，饭碗端在自己手里才踏实，战时断供就是天大的事。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: Keep staple food self-sufficient. Our bowl in our own hands is safe; supply cuts in crisis are catastrophic.

options.t: 我反对过度自给，国际买粮更便宜，腾出耕地种高价值经济作物更划算。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: Oppose over-self-sufficiency. Importing grain is cheaper; free land for high-value crops pays more.

options.t: 我主张保战略储备、日常适度进口，平时用市场、急时靠库存，两手都有。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Keep strategic reserves, import moderately day-to-day — market normally, stockpiles in emergencies.

options.t: 我倾向由农户合作社自己决定种什么，市场信号比计划指令更灵。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Let farmer co-ops decide what to plant; market signals beat planning orders.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Arable land here is limited, and staple grain has long been partly imported. The agricultural camp argues for a high degree of self-sufficiency as a matter of security; the trade camp says buying abroad is cheaper, and that the land would be better used for higher-value crops. It is a trade-off between food autonomy and comparative advantage, and the two positions rest on different judgements about what the risk of dependence really is.

scene: 一座金属矿位于自然保护区边缘，企业拿到环评批复准备开采，承诺出资修路并带动周边就业。环保组织坚决反对，说会污染水系、惊扰野生动物。这是「资源开发」与「生态保育」的冲突。，支持和反对的声音都不少，社区内部一时难以形成共识。

options.t: 我支持开采，本地就业和税收实在，资源就该为人所用，何况已经过了环评。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: I support mining — local jobs and tax are real, resources should serve people, and it passed review.

options.t: 我坚决反对，保护区边缘也脆弱，一旦水体和物种受损不可逆转，钱换不回来。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: I firmly oppose it. Even the edge is fragile; damaged water and species are irreversible — money can't restore them.

options.t: 我主张严格限采规模并强制提取修复基金，边采边补、把代价先留出来。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Strictly cap output and mandate a restoration fund upfront — mine while repairing, with costs pre-set.

options.t: 我倾向让受影响村民集体协商补偿方案，利益相关者自己谈比上面定更服众。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Let affected villagers collectively negotiate compensation; stakeholders deciding beats top-down orders.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A metal mine sits at the edge of a nature reserve. The company has its environmental approval and is preparing to start mining, promising to fund road construction and create jobs for the surrounding area. Environmental groups are firmly opposed, saying it will pollute the water system and disturb wildlife. This is the conflict between resource development and ecological conservation. There are plenty of voices on both sides, and the community cannot form a consensus for now.

scene: 城市原有的限塑令只管塑料袋，现在环保部门想把一次性餐具、吸管、包装全纳入限制，商家算成本、居民嫌麻烦。这是「源头减塑」与「生活便利」之间的拉锯。，各方都拿得出道理，真要落定却谁也说服不了谁。，利弊明摆在面前，怎样取舍成了绕不开的现实难题。

options.t: 我支持全面限塑，白色污染触目惊心， inconvenience 换干净环境值当。
options.t_en: I support a full ban. Plastic pollution is glaring; minor inconvenience is worth a clean environment.

options.t: 我反对一刀切，做好分类回收就够了，全面禁会增加生活成本、小商家最难。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: Oppose the sweep. Good sorting and recycling suffice; a full ban raises costs, hurting small vendors most.

options.t: 我主张分阶段推进，先难降解的、后易替代的，给商家和居民缓冲期。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Phase it in — hardest-to-degrade first, easy substitutes later — giving businesses and residents a buffer.

options.t: 我倾向鼓励企业研发可降解材料来替代，用技术创新解决而不是靠禁令。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Encourage firms to develop biodegradable alternatives — solve it through innovation, not bans.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: The city's existing plastic bag ban covers only bags, and the environmental department now wants to include single-use cutlery, straws and packaging. Businesses are counting the cost and residents find it a nuisance. This is the tug-of-war between cutting plastic at the source and everyday convenience. Everyone can make a case, yet once it comes to actually deciding, no one can convince anyone else, and with the pros and cons laid out plainly, how to weigh them has become an unavoidable practical problem.

scene: 一条风景峡谷拟建大型水电大坝，支持者说能供清洁电力、调蓄防洪，反对者说会淹没原生河谷、阻断鱼类洄游。沿河村落对淹地补偿期待不一。这是「清洁能源」与「原生生态」的取舍。，利弊明摆在面前，怎样取舍成了绕不开的现实难题。

options.t: 我支持建坝，清洁电力和防洪都是刚需，牺牲一段河谷换来万家灯火值得。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Build it. Clean power and flood control are needs; one valley traded for light in countless homes is worth it.

options.t: 我反对建坝，原生峡谷和洄游鱼道一旦毁掉就再也回不来，生态债还不起。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: No dam. A pristine gorge and fish runs, once gone, never return; the ecological debt is unpayable.

options.t: 我主张用小型分散式风光发电替代，不淹地也能供能，绕开大坝的破坏。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Use small distributed wind and solar instead — power without flooding, avoiding the dam's damage.

options.t: 我倾向让受淹村落公投决定，利害直接相关的人自己表决才公平。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Let the flooded villages vote. Those directly affected should decide — that's fair.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A large hydropower dam is proposed for a scenic gorge. Supporters point to clean electricity and to flood control through storage; opponents say it would drown a pristine river valley and cut off migrating fish. Villages along the river have very different expectations about compensation for the land that would be flooded. It is a choice between clean energy and untouched ecology, and every version of the plan distributes the gains and the losses differently.

scene: 为应对气候变化，学界建议对钢铁、水泥等高耗能企业征收碳税。工业界说会削弱出口竞争力、搬厂去国外，环保界说必须倒逼转型。这是「碳定价」与「产业竞争力」的张力。，争论持续发酵，大家都在等一个能服众的收场。

options.t: 我支持征碳税，让排碳者买单、倒逼企业技改，拖延转型代价更大。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: Tax carbon so emitters pay and retrofit. Delaying transition costs far more.

options.t: 我反对征碳税，高耗能是出口支柱，加税只会把工厂和就业赶到国外。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: Oppose it. Heavy industry is an export pillar; the tax just ships factories and jobs abroad.

options.t: 我主张对出口产品实行碳税返还或边境调节，国内控排又不亏了竞争力。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Rebate or border-adjust carbon tax on exports — cut domestic emissions without losing competitiveness.

options.t: 我倾向靠行业协会自律减排、定标杆，少用税收这种硬杠杆。，这是我更认可的出路。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Let industry associations self-regulate and set benchmarks; avoid the hard lever of taxation.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: To address climate change, researchers recommend a carbon tax on energy-intensive industries such as steel and cement. Industry says it would weaken export competitiveness and push plants overseas; environmentalists say it is the necessary pressure to force a transition.
