This is the tension between carbon pricing and industrial competitiveness. The argument keeps going, and everyone is waiting for an ending that people can accept.

scene: 南方鱼塘近年频遭外来入侵物种泛滥，吃掉本土鱼苗、破坏水质。养殖户想全面消杀保收成，生态学者担心药剂伤及周边原生生物。这是「产业自救」与「生态干预」的权衡。，两种诉求都有人撑腰，协调起来格外费劲。，不同居民各有各的难处，最后怎么平衡仍没有标准答案。

options.t: 我支持全面消杀，养殖户的生计要紧，外来物种不除、塘就废了。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Support full eradication. Livelihoods matter; without removing the invader the ponds are ruined.

options.t: 我反对大范围用药，生态得靠天敌调控、少干预，药剂会连带伤了本土生物。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: Oppose broad pesticides. Let ecology self-regulate with predators; chemicals harm native life too.

options.t: 我主张先科学评估、分区精准处理，重点塘用药、其余物理防控。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Assess scientifically, treat by zone — chemicals in key ponds, physical control elsewhere.

options.t: 我倾向由渔民合作社自治防控，经验在民间、统一行动比上面指挥灵。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Let fisher co-ops self-manage control; local know-how and unified action beat top orders.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: Fish ponds in the south have been overrun repeatedly by invasive species in recent years, which eat native fry and damage water quality. Farmers want a full extermination programme to save the harvest; ecologists worry that the chemicals will harm native organisms nearby. This is the trade-off between an industry saving itself and intervening in an ecosystem. Each claim has its backers, which is exactly why reconciling them is so hard, and different residents each have their own difficulty, so there is still no standard answer on how to balance them.

scene: 某中学拟要求全体学生统一穿校服，校方说能减攀比、增认同，部分学生和家长觉得压抑个性、花钱又不便。这是「集体认同」与「个性表达」之间的校园之争。，不同居民各有各的难处，最后怎么平衡仍没有标准答案。，支持和反对的声音都不少，社区内部一时难以形成共识。

options.t: 我支持统一校服，少比穿戴、多比成绩，也省得家长天天为孩子穿啥操心。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: I support uniforms — compare grades not clothes, and spare parents daily wardrobe worries.

options.t: 我反对强制校服，穿衣是个性表达，整齐划一磨掉孩子的自我和创意。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: Oppose forced uniforms. Dress is self-expression; uniformity grinds down individuality and creativity.

options.t: 我主张校内统一、校外自由，既保集体感也不剥夺孩子校门外的自我。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Uniforms on campus, freedom off it — keep collective feel without stripping self outside school.

options.t: 我认为该由家长投票决定，是否穿、怎么穿，家庭意愿最该被尊重。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Let parents vote on whether and how — family wishes deserve the most respect.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A secondary school plans to require every student to wear the same uniform. The school says it reduces comparison over clothes and builds a sense of belonging; some students and parents find it stifling, and say it is an extra expense and an inconvenience. It is a school-level argument between collective identity and individual expression, and both sides think the other is missing something obvious about what school is for.

scene: 小升初评价方式引发讨论：一派坚持分数最公平、好操作，一派主张看综合素质、兴趣与实践。家长怕素质评价变成拼资源、暗箱。这是「唯分数」与「全人发展」的路线分歧。，支持和反对的声音都不少，社区内部一时难以形成共识。

options.t: 我支持看综合素质，孩子不能只当考试机器，兴趣和实践同样重要。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Support holistic assessment. Kids aren't exam machines; interests and practice matter too.

options.t: 我坚持分数最公平，一把尺子谁都看得见，素质评价太易被关系和钱操纵。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: Stick to scores — one visible ruler for all; holistic review is too easily swayed by connections and money.

options.t: 我主张多元评价加全程监督防作弊，既看能力也堵住操作空间。，照这个思路走最省心。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Multiple metrics plus full oversight against cheating — assess ability yet close manipulation gaps.

options.t: 我倾向让每所学校自定评价标准，因校制宜比全市一刀切合理。，于情于理我都站这边。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: Let each school set its own criteria — fitting local context beats one city-wide rule.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: How students are evaluated for the transition from primary to middle school has set off a debate. One camp insists that scores are the fairest measure and the easiest to administer; the other argues for looking at overall qualities, interests and practice. Parents fear that holistic evaluation will turn into a contest of resources and backroom deals. This is the split between scores as the only measure and educating the whole person. There are plenty of voices on both sides, and the community cannot form a consensus for now.

scene: 城市中产兴起送孩子进私立国际学校，公立学校担心优质生源与资源流失。支持者说多了选择，反对者说加剧教育不公、阶层割裂。这是「教育选择」与「机会公平」的拉锯。，各方都拿得出道理，真要落定却谁也说服不了谁。

options.t: 我支持多元办学，家长有钱有愿就该有选择，国际校也逼公办提升。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: Support diverse schooling. Parents with means and wish deserve choice; international schools push public ones to improve.

options.t: 我反对加剧分流，好资源往贵族校聚、薄弱校更弱，阶层鸿沟从娃娃拉开。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: Oppose deeper tracking. Good resources pool at elite schools, weakening others — class gaps start in childhood.

options.t: 我主张公办为主、私立作补充，并让公办吸纳国际课程长处。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Public as the core, private as supplement, with public schools borrowing international strengths.

options.t: 我认为家长自费自选就行，教育消费和个人选择不该被统一安排。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Let parents pay and choose; education as a personal consumer choice shouldn't be uniformly arranged.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Middle-class city families are rushing to send their children to private international schools, and public schools worry about losing the strongest pupils and resources. Supporters say it widens choice; opponents say it deepens educational inequality and class division. This is the tug-of-war between educational choice and equality of opportunity. Everyone can make a case, yet once it comes to actually deciding, no one can convince anyone else.

scene: 是否把性教育与心理健康课纳入中小学必修，引发家长争论。支持者说科学认知能自我保护，保守家长认为这类内容应在家庭教、学校别越界。这是「科学启蒙」与「家庭边界」的碰撞。，利弊明摆在面前，怎样取舍成了绕不开的现实难题。

options.t: 我支持进课堂，用科学方式讲身体和情绪，孩子早懂才能更好保护自己。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Put it in class — teach bodies and emotions scientifically so kids protect themselves early.

options.t: 我认为这类课该由家庭教，学校只管学科，敏感内容交给父母更妥当。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: These lessons belong at home; school handles academics. Sensitive topics fit parents better.

options.t: 我主张设为家长可自选的选修，愿学的学、顾虑的免，尊重差异。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Make it an opt-in elective — those who want it take it, the reluctant opt out; respect difference.

options.t: 我支持国家统一大纲、全员必修，避免各地各校参差不齐、漏掉弱势孩子。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: A unified national curriculum, mandatory for all, so no region or child is left out unevenly.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: Whether sex education and mental health should be compulsory in primary and secondary schools has set parents arguing. Supporters say scientific knowledge is how children learn to protect themselves; more conservative parents hold that this belongs in the family and the school should not overstep. It is a collision between scientific education and the boundary of the family, and the disagreement is as much about who has authority over a child as about the content itself.

scene: 大量随迁子女进城，其入学是否应与本地户籍生享同城待遇引发讨论。支持者说孩子不应因父母户口被差别对待，反对者担心学位和财政被稀释。这是「同城公平」与「资源边界」的张力。，争论持续发酵，大家都在等一个能服众的收场。

options.t: 我支持同城同待遇，孩子没选户口的权利，教育公平不该卡在户籍上。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: Equal treatment in the city. Kids didn't choose their hukou; fairness shouldn't hinge on it.

options.t: 我反对一步放开，本地学位和财政有限，得按户籍循序渐进，否则两边都受损。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: Oppose opening at once. Local seats and budgets are finite; phase by hukou or both sides lose.

options.t: 我主张上级财政转移支付、扩班增位，用钱跟人走来解决容量问题。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Higher-level fiscal transfers to add seats — let the money follow the children to fix capacity.

options.t: 我倾向家长自费择校、市场补位，政府保底、之上靠家庭选择。，这是我更认可的出路。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Parents pay to choose, market fills gaps; government guarantees a floor, choice above it.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Large numbers of children of migrant workers have moved into the city, and whether they should get the same treatment as local children with household registration is under discussion. Supporters say a child should not be treated differently because of the parents' registration; opponents worry about school places and the public budget being diluted. This is the tension between equal treatment within the city and the limits of resources. The argument keeps going, and everyone is waiting for an ending that people can accept.

scene: 沿海城市外来务工者越来越多，户籍附带的医疗、子女教育等福利是否该全面放开，引发本地与外来群体的激烈讨论。一方要平等，一方怕公共资源被挤占。这是「开放包容」与「本地优先」的拉锯。，两种诉求都有人撑腰，协调起来格外费劲。

options.t: 我支持全面放开，外来者也是城市建设者，该平等享福利，不该分三六九等。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Open it fully. Migrants built the city too; they deserve equal benefits, not a caste system.

options.t: 我主张渐进放开，资源就这么多，一步到位会挤兑本地人，得有序来。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: Open gradually. Resources are limited; all-at-once crowds out locals — it must be orderly.

options.t: 我倾向积分落户，按居住年限和贡献排队，透明可预期、谁都不吃亏。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Points-based hukou by years resided and contribution — transparent, predictable, fair to all.

options.t: 我主张把尺度交给地方自定，各市情况不同，不宜全国一把尺。，于情于理我都站这边。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: Let localities set the scale; cities differ, so one national ruler fits none well.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: Migrant workers keep arriving in the coastal city, and whether the welfare tied to household registration, such as healthcare and children's schooling, should be opened up across the board has set off a fierce argument between locals and newcomers. One side wants equality; the other fears public resources will be overrun. This is the tug-of-war between openness and local priority, and each claim has its backers, which is exactly why reconciling them is so hard.

scene: 社区里清真餐馆和异国风味店越开越多，邻里对气味、宰杀规范和营业时间看法不一。有人呼吁统一管理保卫生，有人主张包容多元、不必多管。这是「规范管理」与「文化包容」的取舍。，不同居民各有各的难处，最后怎么平衡仍没有标准答案。

options.t: 我支持规范管理，餐饮卫生和噪音有统一标准，对谁都公平、也保环境。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: Regulate uniformly — hygiene and noise standards fair to all and protective of the environment.

options.t: 我反对多加管束，多元风味是城市活力，只要合法就不必拿规矩去同化。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: Oppose extra rules. Diverse food is the city's vitality; if legal, don't assimilate it by regulation.

options.t: 我主张由餐饮行业自律定标准、互相监督，比政府硬管更接地气。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Let the food industry self-regulate and monitor itself — more grounded than hard government rules.

options.t: 我倾向邻里坐下来协商营业时间和气味处理，情面商量比通报罚单暖。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Neighbors sit down to agree on hours and odors; talking it over beats notices and fines.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: More and more halal restaurants and foreign-flavour shops are opening in the neighbourhood, and residents disagree about smells, slaughtering practices and opening hours. Some call for unified management to protect hygiene; others say a diverse neighbourhood should be tolerant and not meddle. It is a trade-off between regulation and cultural accommodation, and the practical questions of noise and smell keep getting tangled up with questions of belonging.

scene: 移民后代的子女教育引发讨论：是否应强制他们上母语与祖籍文化课，以保文化根脉；还是让他们自愿融入主流、少加负担。长辈盼传承，孩子嫌额外补课。这是「文化根脉」与「自然融入」的张力。，支持和反对的声音都不少，社区内部一时难以形成共识。

options.t: 我支持强制母语文化课，根不能丢，懂来路的孩子才有稳固的身份认同。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Mandate heritage-language classes. Roots shouldn't be lost; knowing origins grounds identity.

options.t: 我反对强制，孩子生于此地就该自然融入主流，额外补课是负担、易生隔阂。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: Oppose mandates. Born here, they should blend in naturally; extra classes burden and divide.

options.t: 我主张学校开成选修，愿学者学、不愿不强求，尊重每个家庭的节奏。，照这个思路走最省心。
options.t_en: Offer it as an elective at school — learners opt in, none forced; respect each family's pace.

options.t: 我认为学不学由家庭自决，父母最清楚孩子需要什么文化传承。，于情于理我都站这边。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: Let families decide. Parents best know what cultural continuity their child needs.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: The schooling of the children of immigrants is under discussion: should they be required to take classes in the mother tongue and ancestral culture in order to preserve their cultural roots, or should they be left to integrate into the mainstream voluntarily, without an extra burden. The elders want the heritage passed on; the children resent the extra classes. This is the tension between cultural roots and natural integration. There are plenty of voices on both sides, and the community cannot form a consensus for now.

scene: 边境出现无证越境者涌入，警方资源紧张。强硬派要求一律遣返护主权，人道派主张个案评估、给真正受迫者庇护。这是「边境主权」与「人道庇护」之间的冲突。，各方都拿得出道理，真要落定却谁也说服不了谁。，利弊明摆在面前，怎样取舍成了绕不开的现实难题。

options.t: 我支持一律遣返，国境线是主权底线，不该谁想进就进、乱了秩序。，这最贴合我一贯的想法。
options.t_en: Deport all. Borders are sovereign bottom lines; no one enters at will and disrupts order.

options.t: 我反对一刀切，受迫害的该给庇护，个案甄别才有人道，不能全当违法者。，我觉得这样最说得通。
options.t_en: Oppose blanket deportation. The persecuted deserve asylum; case-by-case review is humane.

options.t: 我主张扩合法入境配额与通道，让人有序进来，而不是堵不住再忙着遣。，毕竟现实里只能两害相权。
options.t_en: Expand legal quotas and channels so entry is orderly, instead of plugging leaks then deporting.

options.t: 我倾向边境城市就地设收容、由地方自治安置，中央和地方分担。，这是我更认可的出路。
options.t_en: Border cities set up local shelters with autonomous placement; central and local share the load.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Undocumented border crossers are arriving in numbers and police resources are stretched. The hardliners demand that all be returned to protect sovereignty; the humanitarians argue for case-by-case assessment and protection for those genuinely persecuted. This is the conflict between border sovereignty and humanitarian asylum. Everyone can make a case, yet once it comes to actually deciding, no one can convince anyone else, and with the pros and cons laid out plainly, how to weigh them has become an unavoidable practical problem.

scene: 引进的外语影视剧在播出时，是否该强制译制成当地方言版本引发讨论。支持者说护方言、接地气，反对者说标准语更通用、没必要另搞一套。这是「方言文化」与「通用标准」的取舍。，利弊明摆在面前，怎样取舍成了绕不开的现实难题。

options.t: 我支持方言译制，乡音是文化根，本地人听着亲切，也能帮方言活下去。，权衡之下也只能这么选。
options.t_en: Dialect dubbing — local speech is cultural roots; it feels warm to locals and keeps dialects alive.

options.t: 我反对强制方言，标准语全国通用、沟通成本最低，没必要为剧另起炉灶。，说到底还是更合我的脾气。
options.t_en: Oppose forced dialect. Standard speech is nationwide and lowest-cost; no need to reinvent per show.

options.t: 我倾向平台自己选，市场决定配不配方言，观众用播放量投票。，照这个思路走最省心。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Let platforms choose; the market decides on dialect dubs, viewers vote with view counts.

options.t: 我主张政府补贴方言内容，保全非遗语言，但不强制所有剧都配。，于情于理我都站这边。
options.t_en: Government subsidizes dialect content to preserve intangible heritage, but doesn't force it on every show.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: There is a debate over whether imported foreign-language films and series should be required to have a version dubbed into the local dialect. Supporters say it protects the dialect and feels closer to home; opponents say the standard language is more widely understood and there is no need to produce a separate version. It is a trade-off between dialect culture and a common standard, and the cost of either choice is paid by a different group of viewers.

scene: 你所在的互联网公司宣布要在开敞办公区安装带拾音功能的智能摄像头，说是为了「安全与效率分析」。同事担心私下的闲聊、吐槽甚至就医话题都会被系统转写记录。管理层强调这是合规授权范围内的行为，并出示了员工手册里的同意条款，你怎么看这件事？

options.t: 公司场地装监控是管理方的正当权力，只要提前告知、不对外泄露，用技术提升效率和安全本就无可厚非，员工应当配合并信任制度。
options.t_en: Installing cameras on company premises is the management's legitimate prerogative; as long as staff are informed and data isn't leaked, using tech to boost efficiency and safety is fair, and employees should cooperate and trust the system.

options.t: 我坚决反对，办公区也是私人表达空间，偷偷转写对话侵犯基本隐私，应当立法严格限制雇主的监控边界，不能让同意条款变成空白支票。
options.t_en: I firmly oppose this; the office is also a space for private expression, and covertly transcribing conversations violates basic privacy. Law should tightly limit employers' surveillance powers, not let consent clauses become blank checks.

options.t: 与其一刀切禁止，不如让工会和员工代表跟公司谈判，明确哪些数据可采集、谁能看、保留多久，用集体约定来框住它，比个人硬扛更稳。
options.t_en: Rather than an outright ban, let the union and employee reps negotiate with the company on what data may be collected, who can view it, and for how long—use a collective agreement to bound it, steadier than going alone.

options.t: 我无所谓，自己平时少在工位聊私事就行，靠个人注意避开风险比指望制度保护更现实，懒得为这种事跟公司闹得不愉快伤和气。
options.t_en: I don't mind; I'll just avoid personal talk at my desk. Relying on personal caution to dodge risk is more realistic than counting on institutional protection, and I won't sour relations with the company over it.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The internet company you work for has announced that it will install smart cameras with audio recording in the open-plan office, saying it is for security and efficiency analysis. Colleagues worry that private conversations, complaints, even talk about medical appointments will all be transcribed and recorded by the system. Management stresses that this falls within the scope of lawful authorization and points to the consent clause in the employee handbook. What do you make of it?

scene: 市教委计划在全市中小学试点「情绪识别系统」，通过教室摄像头分析学生上课是否专注、有无焦虑。家长群里有人支持能早发现心理问题，也有人担心孩子从小活在被算法打分的环境里、丧失舒展成长的余地，作为学生家长你的态度是？

options.t: 支持，教育主管部门有权用新技术守护学生心理健康，能早干预总比等问题严重了才发现好，何况数据只在校园内闭环使用又不出门。
options.t_en: I support it; education authorities have the right to use new tech to safeguard students' mental health, and early intervention beats discovering problems only when severe, especially since data stays on-campus.

options.t: 反对，用算法给孩子的情绪贴标签会扼杀天性，校园该保留不被监视的自由成长空间，否则童年都活在被打分的焦虑里太残忍。
options.t_en: I oppose it; labeling children's emotions with algorithms crushes their nature, and schools should preserve a free space to grow without constant surveillance, or childhood becomes anxious score-watching.

options.t: 可以用，但必须由家长委员会共同决定使用范围，并把数据所有权和删除权牢牢握在家庭手里，学校只是受托处理而非随意调阅。
options.t_en: It may be used, but the parents' committee must jointly decide its scope, and data ownership and deletion rights must stay firmly in the family's hands; the school only processes, not browses freely.

options.t: 我无所谓，技术本身中性关键看怎么用，我更愿意相信厂家的隐私设计和本地化处理，只要孩子成绩不掉、情绪不崩，不把它想得太坏。
options.t_en: I don't care; the tech is neutral and it's about use. I'd rather trust the vendor's privacy design and on-device processing; as long as grades hold and mood is fine, I won't assume the worst.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: The municipal education commission plans to pilot an emotion recognition system in primary and secondary schools, using classroom cameras to analyse whether pupils are paying attention and whether they are anxious. Some parents in the class chat support it, saying psychological problems can be caught early; others fear their children will grow up in an environment where an algorithm grades them and there is no room to grow at ease. As a pupil's parent, what is your position?

scene: 小区物业引入「人脸识别门禁+行为轨迹分析」，能自动标记哪些住户深夜频繁出入、是否与可疑人员同行。民警说有助于反诈和防盗，部分老人却觉得每天被系统「盯着」不舒服，连下楼遛弯都像被盘问，你作为住户怎么选？

options.t: 支持，公安与物业联动用科技防盗反诈，是为了全体住户的安全，个人那点不习惯可以克服，毕竟谁都不想自家被盗或被骗走养老钱。
options.t_en: I support it; police and property using tech against theft and fraud serves everyone's safety, and individual discomfort is something one can live with—no one wants to be robbed or scammed.

options.t: 反对，把正常居民的行为轨迹拿去做画像，是把守法公民当嫌疑人，过度安防侵蚀了日常自由，老人遛个弯都要被系统评判太荒唐。
options.t_en: I oppose it; profiling law-abiding residents' movements treats innocent citizens as suspects, and excessive security erodes everyday freedom—absurd that an elder's walk gets judged by a system.

options.t: 安全重要，但轨迹数据必须本地存储、定期销毁，且由业主代表大会监督用途，不能交给第三方随意调阅，更不能拿去给商家做精准推销。
options.t_en: Safety matters, but trajectory data must be stored locally and purged periodically, with the owners' congress overseeing its use—not handed to third parties or used by merchants for targeted ads.

options.t: 我图省事，刷脸进门确实方便不用带卡，隐私的事我懒得深究，只要别出大乱子、别把我的行踪卖给别人就成。
options.t_en: I value convenience; face-entry is handy and card-free, and I can't be bothered to dig into privacy as long as nothing goes wrong and my whereabouts aren't sold.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The property manager has brought in facial recognition at the entrance together with movement-pattern analysis, which can automatically flag which residents come and go late at night and whether they are accompanied by anyone suspicious. The police say it helps prevent fraud and theft. Some older residents find it uncomfortable to be watched by a system every day, as if even a walk downstairs were an interrogation. As a resident, what do you choose?

scene: 一款热门健身App请求永久读取你的GPS定位、通讯录和健康数据，声称用于「个性化推荐和社交匹配」。卸载重装后你会发现它仍在调用后台位置。作为用户，你打算怎么处理这种偷偷摸摸滥用权限的事？，在出行便利与个人行踪暴露之间，你究竟站哪一边？

options.t: 该管的是监管，要求平台默认最小授权、违规重罚，但我自己还是会为了功能便利授权，毕竟方便最重要，天天盯着权限太累心。
options.t_en: Regulators should step in—default to minimal permissions and heavily fine violations—but I'll still grant access for convenience; ease matters most, and policing permissions daily is exhausting.

options.t: 立刻卸载并举报，企业无权在后台偷跑定位，用户主权必须靠拒绝滥用产品的行动来捍卫，否则今天让一步明天就被看得精光。
options.t_en: I'll uninstall and report it immediately; a company has no right to stealthily track location, and user sovereignty must be defended by refusing abusive products—give an inch today and you're fully exposed tomorrow.

options.t: 可以授权但要在社区里推动成立用户联盟，集体向厂商索要数据清单和一键撤回权，用抱团增加议价力，让小用户也有说话的份。
options.t_en: I can grant access, but I'd push to form a user alliance to collectively demand a data inventory and one-click withdrawal, pooling clout so small users also get a voice.

options.t: 我无所谓，反正也没什么见不得人的，大数据描摹我也就图个推荐准些，没空跟它较劲，关了通知眼不见心不烦便是。
options.t_en: I don't care; I've nothing to hide, and if big data profiles me it just makes recommendations more accurate. I've no time to fight it—mute the notifications and move on.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A popular fitness app asks for permanent access to your GPS location, contacts and health data, claiming it is for personalized recommendations and social matching. After you uninstall and reinstall it, you find it is still calling your location in the background. As a user, how do you plan to deal with this kind of quiet abuse of permissions? When it comes down to convenience on the move versus exposing your movements, which side are you actually on?

scene: 地铁拟上线「客流密度预测」系统，用手机信令和闸机数据实时推算每节车厢拥挤度并推送给乘客。支持者说能分散人流、减少踩踏，质疑者担心这等于全民被持续追踪行踪、连常去谁家都暴露，你支持吗？，面对这种既想要方便又怕被盯死的两难，你会怎么表态？

options.t: 支持，公共交通本就是公共空间，用 aggregate 数据疏导客流、保障安全是公用事业的正当职责，总比高峰期挤成照片强得多。
options.t_en: I support it; public transit is a public space, and using aggregate data to route crowds and ensure safety is a proper duty of the public utility—far better than rush-hour crush.

options.t: 反对，信令级追踪能还原个人全天轨迹，这种颗粒度的监控必须限于重大紧急状态，不能常态化，否则通勤自由成了被登记的账本。
options.t_en: I oppose it; signaling-level tracking can reconstruct a person's whole-day path, and such granular monitoring must be reserved for major emergencies, not normalized—or commutes become a logged ledger.

options.t: 可以做，但数据必须匿名聚合、不出站级精度，并由市人大听取专项报告，让公众参与规则制定，别让地铁公司自己说了算。
options.t_en: It can be done, but data must be anonymized and aggregated no finer than station level, with the municipal legislature receiving reports so the public helps set rules, not the metro alone.

options.t: 我盼着它能准点告诉我哪节车厢空，至于背后怎么算的我不关心，好用就行，省得天天挤在门口被门夹还迟到扣钱。
options.t_en: I just hope it tells me accurately which car is empty; I don't care how it computes that behind the scenes—as long as it works and saves me from being crushed and late.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: The metro plans to launch a passenger density forecast system, using mobile signalling and gate data to estimate in real time how crowded each carriage is and push it to passengers. Supporters say it spreads the flow and reduces the risk of a crush; sceptics say it amounts to continuous tracking of everyone's movements, exposing even whose home you visit often. Do you support it? Faced with this dilemma of wanting convenience while dreading being watched, how would you take a stand?

scene: 你母亲查出早期肺癌，医生建议做基因检测以匹配靶向药，费用约三万元且部分不在医保。siblings 中有人主张砸钱做最全检测，有人认为老办法化疗更稳妥实惠。作为主要陪护子女，你怎么权衡这笔钱和这条命？，在花钱买希望和理性省钱之间，你这个当家人的怎么定？

options.t: 听医生的，用最新基因技术选最精准的方案，钱可以再挣，但精准治疗的机会错过了就没有，母亲的病不能省在该花的地方。
options.t_en: I'll follow the doctor and use the latest genetic tech for the most precise plan; money can be earned again, but the chance for targeted treatment won't return, and mom's illness isn't where to save.

options.t: 我更信成熟稳妥的常规疗法，不盲目追新，把省下的钱留给后续康复和生活质量更实在，新检测未必值得三万块去赌。
options.t_en: I trust the proven, steady standard therapy over blindly chasing novelty, and would rather save the money for recovery and quality of life; a new test isn't worth gambling 30k on.

options.t: 治疗选择不能只由家属拍板，应让主治、医保和社会救助多方协商，把个体负担摊进公共保障网，别让一家人被费用压垮。
options.t_en: Treatment choices shouldn't be decided by family alone; the attending doctor, insurer, and social aid should negotiate together, spreading the individual's burden across the public safety net.

options.t: 谁出钱谁说了算，既然主要花我兄弟姐妹的钱，我尊重出资方的意见，不抢这个决定权，免得日后为钱的事全家反目成仇。
options.t_en: Whoever pays calls the shots; since my siblings are footing most of the bill, I respect the funder's view and won't grab the decision, lest the family turn on each other over money.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: Your mother has been diagnosed with early-stage lung cancer, and the doctor recommends genetic testing to match a targeted drug. It costs about thirty thousand, and part of it is not covered. Among the siblings, some want to spend whatever it takes on the most complete panel; others think conventional chemotherapy is steadier and cheaper. As the child doing most of the caring, how do you weigh that sum of money against that one life, and where do you draw the line?

scene: 市里唯一的三甲医院排队半年起，卫健委提出把部分常见病下沉到社区诊所并强制首诊在社区。年轻白领嫌社区设备差，老人却觉得离家近更方便。你作为既要上班又要带父母的夹心层，支持强制首诊分流吗？，夹在排队大半年和被迫去社区之间，你的脚往哪边迈？

options.t: 支持，政府统筹分级诊疗能盘活资源、让大医院攻重症，这是公共医疗该做的全局调度，总比全家排半年队熬黄了脸强。
options.t_en: I support it; government-coordinated tiered care frees up resources and lets big hospitals focus on severe cases—exactly the systemic scheduling public health should do, better than half a year of queues.

options.t: 反对，看病是个人自由，强制首诊等于替患者做主，设备差的社区耽误病情谁负责？我可不敢拿父母的身体去试水。
options.t_en: I oppose it; seeing a doctor is a personal freedom, and mandatory triage decides for the patient—if an under-equipped clinic delays diagnosis, who's accountable? I won't risk my parents' health.

options.t: 分流可以，但得先砸钱把社区设备和医生水平提上来，否则光下命令不补能力是甩锅，病人最终还是得回流大医院白折腾。
options.t_en: Triage is fine, but first pump money into community equipment and doctor quality; otherwise ordering without building capacity is blame-shifting, and patients just flow back to big hospitals.

options.t: 我无所谓去哪看，谁近谁快我就带父母去哪，别让我反复跑腿填表就谢天谢地了，政策怎么定我配合便是。
options.t_en: I don't care where I go; I'll take my parents wherever is closest and fastest, and I'd be grateful if they'd just stop making me run around and fill forms—I'll comply with policy.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: The waiting list at the city's only top-tier hospital starts at six months. The health commission proposes moving some common illnesses down to community clinics and making the first visit mandatory there. Young office workers say the community clinics have poor equipment; older people find them easier because they are close to home. As someone in the sandwich generation, working and caring for aging parents at the same time, do you support mandatory triage to the community level? Between waiting half a year and being pushed to the clinic, which way do your feet move?

scene: 一款AI问诊软件宣称准确率超年轻医生，可24小时免费答疑。有患者拿它当首诊，结果漏诊了阑尾炎。舆论分为「鼓励AI降低医疗门槛」和「严禁替代真人」两派。你站哪边，会让自己家人用它吗？，当省事和稳妥撞车，你还敢把自己家人的身体交给屏幕吗？

options.t: 鼓励，AI能把基础问诊带给偏远缺医地区，降低门槛利大于弊，漏诊是个别案例要改进而非禁掉，总比那里根本没医生看强。
options.t_en: Encourage it; AI brings basic triage to under-served remote areas, and lowering the barrier does more good than harm. Missed diagnoses are outliers to fix, not reasons to ban—better than no doctor at all.

options.t: 严禁，医疗关系人命，算法黑箱不能替代医师负责制，必须由真人签字担责才算数，拿家人身体赌机器的概率我不敢。
options.t_en: Ban it; medicine concerns lives, and an opaque algorithm can't replace physician accountability—only a real doctor's signed responsibility counts. I won't bet my family's health on a machine's odds.

options.t: 可以辅助但必须标注「仅供参考」，且用户要知情同意其局限，把选择权留给自己而非平台替你定，急症还是直奔急诊最稳。
options.t_en: It may assist, but must be labeled 'for reference only,' with users informed of its limits—keep the choice with the individual, not the platform; for emergencies go straight to ER.

options.t: 我先试试看灵不灵，能解决小毛病就省了挂号排队，真不对劲我再去医院，自己掂量着来，不神话它也不一棍子打死。
options.t_en: I'll try it and see if it works; if it handles minor issues I skip the queue, and if something feels off I'll go to the hospital—I'll judge for myself, idolizing nor banning it.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: An AI consultation app claims accuracy above that of young doctors and offers free answers around the clock. A patient used it for a first consultation and appendicitis was missed. Opinion has split into one camp encouraging AI to lower the threshold to care and another insisting it must never replace a real doctor. Which side are you on, and would you let your own family use it? When convenience collides with safety, would you still hand your family's health to a screen?

scene: 你怀孕的妻子被产检机构强力推销一套八千元的「高端全维筛查」，称能查上百项罕见病。你查文献发现多数项目对低风险孕妇意义有限。面对机构的话术和妻子的焦虑，你怎么办？，在机构的话术和妻子的不安之间，你这个丈夫怎么拍板？

options.t: 既然有钱就做最全的，多查一项多份安心，机构提供的选择我愿意为家人买单，宁可错花不能漏查让心里留疙瘩。
options.t_en: Since we can afford it, do the most comprehensive panel; one more check means more peace of mind, and I'll pay for the options the provider offers my family—better overspend than regret a gap.

options.t: 拒绝过度检查，按临床指南做必要项目即可，不被商业化套餐绑架才是理性消费，八千块留着请月嫂比查罕见病实在。
options.t_en: Reject over-testing; do only what clinical guidelines require. Not being hijacked by commercial packages is rational consumption—8k for a maternity helper beats rare-disease screening.

options.t: 应立法规范产检套餐的知情同意和价格透明，让监管挡住机构利用焦虑赚钱的空间，别让每个家庭都自己跟销售斗智斗勇。
options.t_en: Law should mandate informed consent and price transparency for prenatal packages, letting regulation block institutions from profiting off anxiety, instead of each family dueling salespeople.

options.t: 听媳妇的，她焦虑她就做，家人情绪稳定比省那点钱重要，我不替她拿这个主意，免得万一有事怪我心里只有钱。
options.t_en: I'll defer to my wife; if she's anxious, she does it. Her peace of mind matters more than saving money, and I won't make this call for her, lest she blame my penny-pinching if anything goes wrong.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Your pregnant wife is being hard-sold an eight-thousand-yuan premium full-spectrum screening by the antenatal clinic, which claims it checks for more than a hundred rare conditions. You look at the literature and find that most of the items mean very little for a low-risk pregnancy. Faced with the clinic's sales pitch and your wife's anxiety, what do you do, and who do you have to persuade first?

scene: 你父亲中风后需要长期康复，公立机构排不上、民办康复中心月费过万。兄弟姐妹为「该不该卖房凑护理费」吵成一团，你也陷入两难：钱从哪来、谁来陪、尊严怎么保？你怎么处理这笔家庭账？，钱、孝心与长远照顾这三本账，你准备怎么算才不后悔？

options.t: 卖房也要把父亲照护好，孝道和责任在家庭之上，钱没了可以再攒，亲人等不起，住什么房子都不如父亲还在身边踏实。
options.t_en: Even selling the home, I'll care for my father well; filial duty and family come first. Money can be earned back, but a parent can't wait—no house beats having dad around.

options.t: 不应由家庭独自扛，应联合其他家庭向政府施压，把长期照护纳入公共社保而非转嫁子女，凭一家之力扛不起这无底洞。
options.t_en: The family shouldn't bear this alone; we should join other families to pressure government to put long-term care into public social insurance rather than offload it onto children—one family can't fund this pit.

options.t: 理性算账，选性价比最高的方案，不迷信贵就是好，把钱花在刀刃上才对得起全家，盲目砸钱反而拖垮兄弟姐妹各自的小家。
options.t_en: Be rational; pick the most cost-effective plan, don't equate expensive with better, and spend where it counts most to be fair to the whole family—blind spending drags down everyone's household.

options.t: 按出资比例分责任，谁能力强多出、能力弱少出，用市场化的AA制摆平兄弟姐妹的争执，亲兄弟明算账反而少积怨。
options.t_en: Split responsibility by contribution—those with more ability pay more, those with less pay less—using a market-style cost-sharing to settle the siblings' dispute; clear accounts among brothers breed less resentment.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: After his stroke, your father needs long-term rehabilitation. Public facilities have no places available, and private rehabilitation centers cost over ten thousand a month. Your siblings have fallen into a shouting match over whether the house should be sold to cover the cost of care, and you are caught in the middle: where does the money come from, who does the accompanying, and how is his dignity protected? How do you handle this family ledger? With money, filial duty and long-term care all on the table, how do you do the arithmetic so that you do not end up regretting it?

scene: 你们公司招聘研发岗，HR汇报两名候选人实力相当，一位是育龄女工程师、一位是男工程师。有主管暗示「优先男的，免得将来休产假扯后腿」。作为用人部门负责人，在晋升与公平之间你怎么定？，当团队战力和公平原则打架，你这一票往哪边投？

options.t: 按能力录用，任何以生育为由的差别对待都是歧视，企业要带头破除职场性别偏见，我宁可得罪主管也不拿偏见当理由。
options.t_en: Hire on merit; any differential treatment based on childbearing is discrimination, and companies should lead in breaking workplace gender bias. I'd rather offend the supervisor than use bias as excuse.

options.t: 理解主管的顾虑，小微企业讲究现成战力，用人上优先考虑团队即战力也属现实考量，生意场上不能拿情怀对冲交付压力。
options.t_en: I understand the supervisor's concern; small firms value immediate firepower, and prioritizing ready combat strength is a pragmatic call—business can't offset delivery pressure with ideals.

options.t: 应推动制度保障，比如强制男性陪产假、普惠托育，从源头消解「生育惩罚」，而非让企业各算各的、把矛盾甩给面试官。
options.t_en: We should push institutional guarantees—mandatory paternity leave, universal childcare—to remove the 'motherhood penalty' at its root, rather than each firm calculating alone and dumping the conflict on interviewers.

options.t: 我尊重市场信号，若业内多数企业都看重某岗位的连续性，顺着这个惯例选人也是降低风险的正常判断，硬拗着选反而可能影响团队绩效。
options.t_en: I respect market signals; if an industry widely values continuity in a role, following that consensus to choose is a normal risk-reducing judgment—forcing the opposite is unfair to team performance.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Your company is hiring for an R and D post. HR reports two candidates of equal strength: a female engineer of childbearing age and a male engineer. A manager hints that they should prefer the man, so as not to be held back later when she takes maternity leave. As the head of the hiring department, how do you decide between the team's strength and fairness? When team capability and the principle of fairness collide, which way does your vote go?

scene: 学校女儿回家说，体育课男生跑得快能免跑圈、女生慢就被留堂加练。你联系老师，对方说「男女体能差异本就不同对待更科学」。你接受这套说法吗，会怎么跟女儿和学校沟通？，面对老师口中所谓科学的差别对待，你准备怎么替女儿争？

options.t: 不接受，用性别划线区别对待本身就是刻板印象，应当按个人能力而非男女来安排训练，我打算写邮件请老师改成自选强度。
options.t_en: I don't accept it; drawing lines by sex is stereotyping itself—training should follow individual ability, not male vs female. I'll email the teacher to switch to self-selected intensity.

options.t: 接受，男女生理差异客观存在，分档教学更照顾多数人的体验，也算因材施教的务实做法，没必要上纲上线伤了师生和气。
options.t_en: I accept it; sex-based physiological differences are real, and tiered teaching better suits most students—a pragmatic way of teaching to the individual, no need to make a fuss and strain relations.

options.t: 差异可以承认，但规则要透明公平，由家长和学生代表共同制定体测标准，避免老师一人拍板，也让女儿参与定自己该跑多少。
options.t_en: Differences can be acknowledged, but rules must be transparent and fair, with parents and student reps jointly setting fitness standards instead of one teacher deciding, and let my daughter help set her own target.

options.t: 小事一桩，我让孩子自己适应规则、练好体能，别为这种事跟学校硬杠，影响孩子情绪和老师在班的印象反而不划算。
options.t_en: It's minor; I'll have my child adapt to the rules and build fitness, and avoid clashing with the school over this so my kid's mood and the teacher's impression aren't hurt—not worth it.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: Your daughter comes home from school and says that in PE, boys who run fast are let off the extra laps, while girls who are slow are kept back for more training. You ring the teacher, and the answer is that physical differences between boys and girls make different treatment the more scientific approach. Do you accept that explanation, and how do you talk to your daughter and to the school about it?

scene: 社区要推「爸爸育儿假」宣传，鼓励男性休产假带娃。有邻居笑称「大老爷们带什么孩子」，也有人点赞打破男主外传统。你愿意在自己家带头休满陪产假，给女儿做个不一样的榜样吗？，在单位氛围和传统角色之间，你愿意做那个不一样的爸爸吗？

options.t: 当然休满，育儿是父母共同的责任，男性带头打破「赚钱养家」的单一角色才叫真正平等，我想让女儿看见爸爸也能温柔顾家。
options.t_en: Of course I'll take the full leave; childcare is a shared parental duty, and men leading the break from the single 'breadwinner' role is real equality—I want my daughter to see dad can be tender at home.

options.t: 还是以工作为重，家里长辈和妻子能带，我多赚钱养家更实在，角色分工各司其职没啥不好，硬拗反而全家手忙脚乱。
options.t_en: Work comes first; elders and my wife can care for the child, and my earning more is more practical. Each role has its job, and that's fine—forcing it only frazzles the family.

options.t: 休不休假是个人自由，不应被宣传道德绑架，也别用「模范爸爸」的标签来压人，我用多少假是我家和公司之间的事。
options.t_en: Whether to take leave is personal freedom; it shouldn't be morally coerced by campaigns, nor should people be pressured with 'model dad' labels. How much leave I take is between my family and firm.

options.t: 看单位让不让，领导准我就休、不准我也没法，个体拗不过单位氛围，随大流最省心，真想要假不如等项目间隙再休。
options.t_en: It depends on whether my employer allows it; if the boss approves I'll take it, if not there's nothing I can do. The individual can't fight workplace culture, so I go with the flow—better to take it between projects.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The community is running a campaign for paternity leave, encouraging men to take parental leave and look after the baby. One neighbor jokes about grown men minding children; others applaud breaking the old idea that the man is only the breadwinner. Are you willing to set the example in your own home, taking the full paternity leave and giving your daughter a different kind of model? Between the mood at work and the traditional role, are you willing to be that different father?

scene: 热播剧里女主靠自身努力当上CEO却被弹幕骂「不近人情、不像女人」。你女儿问为什么成功女性总被要求「温柔」。你怎样跟她解释这种现象，又怎样教她面对？，当弹幕的恶意撞上女儿的疑惑，你打算怎么给她撑腰？，你又会用什么话替她挡下那些恶意？

options.t: 我告诉她这是旧偏见，成功不该被性别框定，我们要一起质疑那些「女人该怎样」的隐形规矩，你做自己想做的那种厉害的人。
options.t_en: I tell her it's an old bias; success shouldn't be boxed by gender, and we should question those invisible rules about 'how women should be'—be the capable person you want to be.

options.t: 我劝她理解传统，温柔和能干不矛盾，融入主流期待反而走得更顺，没必要刻意对着干，棱角太硬容易在职场撞得头破血流。
options.t_en: I advise her to understand tradition; gentleness and competence aren't contradictory, and fitting mainstream expectations eases the path—no need to confront it; too sharp an edge gets bloodied at work.

options.t: 我带她参与性别教育社群，推动学校和媒体重构榜样叙事，让更多元的成功被看见，也让她知道不是只有一种活法被允许。
options.t_en: I'll involve her in gender-education communities to push schools and media to rebuild role-model narratives so more diverse success becomes visible, and show her there's more than one allowed way to live.

options.t: 弹幕而已别当真，网络情绪过眼就忘，教女儿专注自己目标、别被陌生人的评价牵着走，键盘侠的话哪天就翻篇了。
options.t_en: It's just barrage comments—don't take them seriously; online noise fades fast. Teach my daughter to focus on her own goals and not be led by strangers' opinions; keyboard warriors move on tomorrow.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: In a hit drama the heroine works her way up to CEO, and the comment stream calls her cold and unfeminine. Your daughter asks why successful women are always expected to be gentle. How do you explain this to her, and how do you teach her to face it? When the malice in the comments meets your daughter's confusion, how do you back her up, and what words will you use to shield her from it?

scene: 你们小区业委会改选，参选的两位热心人都很能干，一位是全职妈妈、一位是企业女高管。有业主嘀咕「高管肯定没空管琐事」。你投票看什么，会不会被这些闲话带节奏？，闲话和真本事之间，你这一票到底跟着什么走？，落笔那一刻你心里到底想的是谁？

options.t: 我投能力和公心，不因为她是高管就预设没空，也不因为是妈妈就默认更细心，看方案说话，闲话不该左右我一票。
options.t_en: I vote on competence and public spirit—not assuming the executive lacks time, nor assuming the mom is inherently more attentive. Let the proposals speak; gossip shouldn't sway my vote.

options.t: 我更倾向全职妈妈，小区多是家长里短，时间充裕、同理心强的人处理邻里事更接地气，高管再厉害也怕是空中楼阁。
options.t_en: I lean toward the full-time mom; the neighborhood runs on everyday matters, and someone with ample time and empathy handles local issues more practically—an exec may be lofty but detached.

options.t: 我主张把业委会职责清单化、轮值化，不管谁当选都用制度约束精力投入，别押宝某类人，规则比人靠谱。
options.t_en: I argue for a listed, rotated division of duties so whoever is elected is bound by system to invest effort—don't bet everything on one type of person; rules beat individuals.

options.t: 谁跟我关系近、平时肯帮我忙我就投谁，能力高低不如实惠的人情往来重要，业委会嘛不过是个抬头方便的由头。
options.t_en: I vote for whoever is closer to me and willing to help out; ability matters less than tangible personal favors—the owners' committee is just a convenient title for mutual aid.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Your compound is electing a new owners' committee, and the two keen candidates are both capable: one a full-time mother, the other a female executive. Some owners mutter that an executive will surely have no time for small matters. What do you vote on, and will you let that kind of talk steer you? When you mark the paper, who is actually in your mind?

scene: 你负责的小团队引入自动排班AI，它依据历史数据把夜班更多分给单身员工，理由是「他们没家庭负担」。有同事投诉算法在变相歧视。你作为主管，在效率与公平之间怎么调？，效率与公平掐架时，你准备怎么调顺这盘棋？

options.t: 算法基于效率最优，单身同事确实更灵活，我用技术降管理成本，只要总工时公平、补贴到位，把夜班集中安排也不算亏待。
options.t_en: The algorithm optimizes efficiency; single colleagues are genuinely more flexible, so I use tech to cut management cost as long as total hours stay fair and subsidies are paid—clustering nights isn't mistreatment.

options.t: 立刻叫停这种设定，用婚姻状态排班是歧视，应改成人人轮流、可自主申报偏好的人本规则，效率不能凌驾于人的尊严。
options.t_en: I'd halt that setting at once; scheduling by marital status is discrimination and should become a human-centered rule of equal rotation with self-declared preferences—efficiency can't override dignity.

options.t: 让全员讨论排班原则并写进团队公约，用集体商定的规则约束AI，而不是默认听系统的，谁加班多补贴怎么给大家定。
options.t_en: Let the whole team discuss scheduling principles and write them into a team charter, using a collectively agreed rule to bound the AI rather than defaulting to the system—overtime pay decided by all.

options.t: 我懒得改系统，谁有意见私下找我调，个案灵活处理比推翻算法更省事，团队别为套排班规则内耗得天天开会。
options.t_en: I can't be bothered to change the system; whoever objects can come to me privately and I'll adjust case by case—more convenient than overturning the algorithm and meeting daily over scheduling rules.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The small team you lead has brought in an automatic scheduling AI, and based on historical data it assigns more night shifts to single employees, on the grounds that they have no family obligations. A colleague has complained that the algorithm is discriminating by proxy. As the supervisor, how do you adjust the balance between efficiency and fairness? When efficiency and fairness are at each other's throats, how do you straighten out this board?

scene: 本地图书馆要撤掉半数人工借阅台、改成人脸借书机和AI导览。老年读者抱怨不会用、像被赶走。馆长说这是降本增效的必然。你怎么看用机器替换人工服务这件事？，机器替换人之后，那些被甩在门外的读者谁来管？，被挡在门外的那位你打算管不管？

options.t: 支持，公共服务要跟上数字化，省下的人力可投入到更深的内容服务，落伍的环节该淘汰，总不能为了怀旧拖住整个社会。
options.t_en: I support it; public service must keep up with digitalization, and the saved labor can go into deeper content services—outdated steps should be phased out; we can't halt society for nostalgia.

options.t: 反对，技术不能把一部分人甩在门外，图书馆必须保留人工窗口，数字鸿沟不是淘汰弱者的理由，老人也有进馆看书的的权利。
options.t_en: I oppose it; tech must not shut anyone out. Libraries must keep a human desk—the digital divide is no reason to discard the vulnerable; elders too have the right to enter and read.

options.t: 可以智能化，但保留足够人工岗并配志愿者教老人，用社区互助弥合使用门槛，别让省下的钱变成老人的眼泪。
options.t_en: Digitalization is fine, but keep enough human posts and add volunteers to teach seniors, using community mutual aid to bridge the usage gap—don't let saved money become elders' tears.

options.t: 我反正都用手机借书了，老人跟不上那是他们的事，社会进步总要有人掉队，总不能为几个不习惯的人拖着全馆不升级。
options.t_en: I already borrow by phone; if seniors can't keep up, that's on them. Social progress always leaves some behind; we can't hold the whole library back for a few who won't adapt.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: The local library plans to remove half its staffed lending desks and replace them with face-scan self-service machines and an AI guide. Older readers complain that they cannot use them and feel driven away. The director says this is the inevitable price of cutting costs and raising efficiency. What do you think about replacing human service with machines? Once machines replace people, who takes care of the readers left outside the door, and will you take care of the one you saw turned away?

scene: 你开发的产品被要求接入大模型自动生成用户评论「水军」内容以冲好评。老板说同行都这么干、不跟进就吃亏。你接不接这活，会不会用「大家都在做」说服自己？，当大家都这么干遇上你的底线，这笔活你接不接？，你的良心这道关又怎么过？

options.t: 接，商业竞争讲结果，别人都用AI刷量，我不做就亏了，技术本身没有善恶，工具落在谁手里决定好坏而非工具本身。
options.t_en: I'll do it; business competition is about results. If rivals all use AI to inflate numbers, not doing it loses out—tech itself is amoral; the wielder decides good or bad, not the tool.

options.t: 拒绝，用算法造假误导消费者是欺骗，我宁可丢工作也不写这种坑人的功能，今天帮人刷好评明天也可能骗到我头上。
options.t_en: I refuse; using algorithms to fake and mislead consumers is fraud, and I'd rather lose the job than build such harmful functionality—boost others' reviews today and it may defraud me tomorrow.

options.t: 应推动行业公约和监管，禁止AI生成虚假评论，用规则把劣币赶出市场而非个人硬扛，让守规矩的厂也有活路。
options.t_en: We should push industry covenants and regulation banning AI-generated fake reviews, using rules to drive bad actors out rather than individuals bearing it alone, so compliant firms survive too.

options.t: 我无所谓接不接，按合同和工资办事，伦理问题留给老板和立法者去操心，我不过是颗拧螺丝的齿轮而已。
options.t_en: I don't mind either way; I work per contract and salary, and leave ethical questions to the boss and lawmakers—I'm just a cog turning a screw.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: The product you are building is being asked to plug in a large model that generates fake user reviews to inflate the ratings. The boss says everyone in the trade does it, and that you lose out by not keeping up. Do you take the job, and will you talk yourself into it by telling yourself that everybody is doing it? How do you get past your own conscience on this one?

scene: 学校引入AI批改作文，老师说能秒出分数和润色建议，学生却说「机器读不懂我的真心话」。家长会上两种声音对立：该不该让算法给孩子的文字打分？你作为家长怎么表态？，机器打分和孩子真心之间，你这个家长挺谁？，你这份挺法会不会反而伤了孩子？

options.t: 欢迎，AI批改高效、反馈及时，能解放老师去关注更难的育人工作，是好事，重复劳动交给机器本就是进步的方向。
options.t_en: I welcome it; AI grading is efficient with timely feedback, freeing teachers for harder mentoring work—a good thing, and handing repetitive labor to machines is progress.

options.t: 反对，文字里有情感和独特思考，机器打分会窄化学术标准，孩子的表达权不该交给算法，分数背后该有个人看见的温度。
options.t_en: I oppose it; writing carries emotion and unique thought, and machine scoring narrows academic standards—a child's expressive rights shouldn't be handed to an algorithm; scores deserve a human's warmth.

options.t: 可作辅助，但final分数必须由老师定，AI只给参考，并把使用权交回班级共同约定，别让机器悄悄成了判卷的主宰。
options.t_en: It can assist, but the final score must be the teacher's; AI only advises, and its use should be collectively agreed by the class—don't let the machine quietly become the grader-in-chief.

options.t: 我让孩子自己习惯工具，将来本来就和AI共事，早点适应比抗拒更有用，抵触新东西到社会上反而吃亏的是自己。
options.t_en: I'll have my child get used to the tool; they'll work alongside AI anyway, so adapting early beats resisting—resenting new things only hurts them in the real world.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: The school has brought in AI to grade essays. Teachers say it produces a score and polishing suggestions in seconds; students say the machine does not understand what they really mean. At the parents' meeting two positions face off: should an algorithm be allowed to score a child's writing? As a parent, where do you come down? Between the machine's score and the child's sincerity, which side are you on as a parent? And could the way you take that side end up hurting your child instead?

scene: 城市开放了「算法备案」窗口，要求外卖、打车等平台公开派单逻辑以防大数据杀熟。有公司抱怨商业机密受损。作为天天被平台算计的单车用户，你支持强制公开吗？，平台的秘密和你的钱包之间，你站哪头？，你的那点隐私到底还守不守得住？

options.t: 支持，算法影响千万人的价格和机会，公众有权知道规则，透明胜过黑箱里的任性行为，秘密不能是平台割韭菜的护身符。
options.t_en: I support it; algorithms affect millions' prices and opportunities, the public has a right to know the rules, and transparency beats capricious behavior inside black boxes—secrecy isn't a shield for fleecing users.

options.t: 反对，派单模型是企業核心资产，强制公开等于逼走创新，监管可用抽查代替全透明，把配方交给对手公司太不划算。
options.t_en: I oppose it; dispatch models are a company's core asset, and forced disclosure drives away innovation—regulators can use spot checks instead of full transparency; handing the recipe to rivals is unwise.

options.t: 折中，只公开「不杀熟」的约束性规则和投诉通道，核心技术细节留给监管闭环审查，既给用户交代也护住企业饭碗。
options.t_en: A compromise: disclose only the binding rules against price discrimination and a complaint channel, leaving core technical details to closed-loop regulatory review—accountable to users yet protecting the firm.

options.t: 我不在乎它公开不公开，平台给的优惠券我照领，规则黑不黑跟我日常省钱没关系，真贵了我换一家便是。
options.t_en: I don't care if it's disclosed; I'll still claim the platform's coupons, and whether the rules are opaque doesn't affect my daily savings—if it's pricey I'll switch.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: The city has opened an algorithm filing window, requiring delivery and ride-hailing platforms to disclose how they dispatch orders, in order to prevent algorithmic price gouging of regular customers. Some companies complain that trade secrets would be harmed. As someone who is daily at the mercy of platform pricing, do you support mandatory disclosure? Between the platform's secrets and your wallet, which side are you on, and can what little privacy you have left still be defended?

scene: 你邻居因冲动打了人一拳被刑拘，对方谅解后家属求情「初犯、已赔偿，别留案底毁一生」。检察官说可酌情不起诉。你觉得该不该给司法留这个「宽容」的空间，还是一律依法办？，在法理的温度和一律从严之间，你更信哪一种正义？

options.t: 该宽容，司法要有温度，对真诚悔过、已弥补的初犯给改过机会，比一棍子打死更合人道，也是给社会留个回头路。
options.t_en: There should be leniency; justice needs warmth, and giving a first offender who truly repents and makes amends a chance beats ruining a life outright—also a path back for society.

options.t: 必须依法，法律面前人人平等，谅解和赔偿不能替代定罪，否则富人花钱买自由，规矩就成了给钱让道的后门。
options.t_en: It must follow the law; all are equal before it, and forgiveness or compensation can't replace conviction, or the rich simply buy freedom and rules become a paid side door.

options.t: 应建立公开的酌定标准，由社区评议和司法共同决定，既留温度又防人情泛滥，让宽与不宽都有章可循不靠关系。
options.t_en: We should build published discretion standards, decided jointly by community review and the judiciary—keeping warmth while preventing favoritism, so leniency follows rules not connections.

options.t: 邻里的事能私了就私了，别动不动惊动公权力，关起门来解决最不伤和气，真闹到法庭两家这辈子都结了梁子。
options.t_en: Neighborhood matters should be settled privately when possible; don't invoke state power so readily. Resolving behind closed doors preserves harmony; a court case breeds lifelong feud.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A neighbour was taken into custody after throwing a punch in a moment of temper. The other party has forgiven him, and the family are pleading that he is a first offender who has already paid compensation, and that a criminal record would ruin his whole life. The prosecutor says discretionary non-prosecution is possible. Should the law leave room for that kind of mercy, or should it be applied strictly in every case? Between warmth in the law and uniform severity, which justice do you trust?

scene: 网上热传一段城管暂扣小贩三轮车的视频，评论两极：一边喊「执法必严」，一边说「谋生不易该柔性」。你作为路过的市民，怎么看这次硬核执法？，硬执法和活命的考量撞一起，你给这次扣车打几分？，你心里的那杆秤又悄悄往哪边倾？

options.t: 支持严格执法，规则就是规则，占道经营影响秩序，不处罚只会让守规矩的人吃亏，城市脸面也得有人出来维护。
options.t_en: I support strict enforcement; rules are rules, and vending on the road disrupts order—without penalties, those who comply lose out, and the city's face needs someone to uphold.

options.t: 应柔性执法，生存权优先，先疏导到合法摊位再谈管理，别用硬扣车把人逼上绝路，一碗擀面皮里藏着一家人的柴米油盐。
options.t_en: Enforcement should be flexible; the right to livelihood comes first—channel vendors to legal spots before managing, not crush them with impounded carts; a bowl of noodles feeds a family.

options.t: 关键在制度，政府应划出惠民摊区、降门槛，让执法从「堵」变「疏」，源头化解冲突，而不是每次都靠冲突上热搜。
options.t_en: The key is the system; government should set up affordable vending zones and lower barriers, turning enforcement from 'blocking' to 'channeling' and resolving conflict at its source, not viral clips each time.

options.t: 我路过拍个视频发朋友圈就走，执不执法是政府的事，我一个路人不好多嘴，惹了麻烦还得自己花时间跑派出所做笔录。
options.t_en: I'll film a clip for my feed and move on; enforcing or not is the government's business, and as a passerby I won't meddle—getting involved means time at the station giving statements.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: A video of urban management officers impounding a street vendor's tricycle is spreading online, and the comments split in two: one side says enforcement must be strict, the other says it is hard to make a living and enforcement should be gentler. As a passerby, what do you make of this hardline enforcement? When hard enforcement and the need to make a living collide, what score do you give this impounding? And which way is the scale inside you quietly tipping?

scene: 你公司被竞争对手恶意抹黑，证据确凿但对方在当地有背景。律师说「打官司赢面大但耗时长」，也有人说「找关系施压更快」。你选哪条路，信法律还是信熟人？，信法律还是信关系，这道选择题你打算怎么填？，真到自家企业头上你究竟还信谁？

options.t: 走法律程序，相信司法能给出公正判决，哪怕慢也要守住「规则解决问题」的底线，这次退了下次被欺负的是自己。
options.t_en: Go through the legal process; I trust the courts to deliver justice, and even if slow, I'll hold the line that rules settle disputes—yield now and next time it's me who's bullied.

options.t: 现实点，当地关系也是资源，能用非诉手段快速止损就不必耗在法庭上折磨自己，商机不等人拖黄了官司赢了也白搭。
options.t_en: Be realistic; local connections are also a resource, and if non-litigation means can stop the loss fast, there's no need to torture myself in court—opportunities don't wait and a won case may be moot.

options.t: 联合行业商会共同维权，用集体力量推动公正执法，避免单家企业被背景方各个击破，团结起来才有人听我们说话。
options.t_en: Join the industry chamber to defend rights collectively, using group strength to push for fair enforcement and avoid one firm being picked off by well-connected rivals—united, we're heard.

options.t: 算了，生意场上磕碰难免，不值得为口气把公司拖进泥潭，忍一时风平浪静，留得青山在不怕没柴烧。
options.t_en: Forget it; bumps in business are inevitable, and it's not worth dragging the company into the mud over pride. Endure and the waters calm; keep the mountain green and there's fuel yet.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Your company has been smeared by a competitor. The evidence is solid, but the other side has connections locally. Your lawyer says a lawsuit would probably win but take a long time; others say leaning on connections would be faster. Which road do you take, and do you trust the law or the people you know? When it comes to your own business, whom do you actually still trust?

scene: 你社区发生盗窃，警方为快速破案在业主群发「嫌疑人画像」并号召邻里指认。有人赞效率高，有人忧「未审先判」伤及无辜。你觉得这种群防通报妥当吗，会不会把好人也网进去？，效率与无辜之间，这种群防通报你敢点赞同吗？

options.t: 妥当，警民合作提速破案、震慑犯罪，公布线索是公共安全的合理需要，真凶落网比谁的面子更重要。
options.t_en: It's proper; police-public cooperation speeds up solving cases and deters crime, and publishing leads is a reasonable need for public safety—catching the real thief outweighs anyone's face.

options.t: 不妥，未定罪就发画像指认容易网暴误伤，无辜者的名誉权比破案效率更重要，万一认错人这家人跳进黄河洗不清。
options.t_en: It's improper; identifying suspects before conviction easily triggers online mobbing and wrongful harm—an innocent's reputation matters more than case speed; a mis-ID ruins a family irreparably.

options.t: 可做但须规范，由警方统一发布、隐去可识别细节，并设纠错通道，防民间私刑式指认，让线索归线索、定罪归法庭。
options.t_en: It can be done but must be regulated: police issue uniformly, mask identifiable details, and provide a correction channel to prevent vigilante-style identification—tips stay tips, conviction stays with court.

options.t: 我只在群里围观不转发，真认出人来再私下报官，不掺和公开指认那摊浑水，免得认错还得给人赔礼道歉。
options.t_en: I'll just watch in the group without forwarding; if I recognize someone I'll privately report to police, not wade into public identification—lest I mis-identify and owe someone an apology.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: There has been a burglary in your compound, and to close it quickly the police post a sketch of the suspect in the owners' group chat and call on neighbours to identify him. Some applaud the efficiency; others worry that it convicts someone before trial and may catch innocent people. Is a community alert like this appropriate, or will it sweep decent people into the net? Between speed and innocence, would you give it your approval?

scene: 你未成年表弟打架致人轻伤，按新规可适用「少年司法」转介到社区矫治而非坐牢。舅妈主张「送去管教的学校才长记性」，你倾向哪种，觉得孩子该被罚还是该被教？，罚与教的分岔口上，你觉得表弟该往哪条路走？，你这个当哥的又该递一句什么话？

options.t: 支持社区矫治，少年宜教不宜罚，在熟悉环境里矫正更利回归，监禁反易交叉感染学来更多坏毛病，毁了孩子的前程。
options.t_en: I support community correction; youth should be taught not punished, and rehab in a familiar setting aids reintegration—prison risks cross-infection of bad habits and ruins the child's future.

options.t: 该严格，未成年人也知对错，送管教学校才能立规矩，过软的处置是对受害者的不公，也让别的孩子觉得打了人没代价。
options.t_en: It should be strict; minors know right from wrong, and a discipline school sets boundaries—too-soft handling is unfair to the victim and tells other kids that hitting has no price.

options.t: 应让家庭、社工和司法共同制定个性化方案，按孩子具体情况选路径，而非一刀切，他为什么动手、家里啥情况都得考虑。
options.t_en: Family, social workers, and the judiciary should jointly craft a personalized plan, choosing the path by the child's specific situation rather than one-size-fits-all—why he hit and home context both matter.

options.t: 家里出钱私了赔够，别走司法程序让孩子留记录，家族面子比什么矫治都重要，案底跟一辈子找工作都受影响。
options.t_en: The family will pay enough privately to settle it; keep the child out of the justice system's records—family face matters more than any correction, and a record haunts a career for life.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Your underage cousin got into a fight that left someone with a minor injury. Under the new rules, juvenile justice can refer him to community correction instead of prison. Your aunt insists that only a reform school will teach him a lesson. Which way do you lean: should the boy be punished or taught? At the fork between punishment and education, which road do you think your cousin should take? And what is the one thing you, as his older cousin, ought to say to him?

scene: 你孩子学校组织春游，目的地是一座著名寺庙，老师鼓励顺道「体验祈福文化」。有家长信佛觉得好，无神论家长担心变相传教。作为家委，你怎么安排这次出行的边界？，世俗课堂和一缕香火之间，这趟春游的边界你划在哪？

options.t: 支持去，宗教文化也是传统文化一部分，让孩子开阔眼界、尊重多元没坏处，见见不同信仰本就是种教养。
options.t_en: I support going; religious culture is part of traditional culture, and broadening children's horizons to respect diversity does no harm—seeing different faiths is itself upbringing.

options.t: 反对，公立学校应保持世俗中立，组织祈福活动越界，可改去博物馆讲历史更妥当，别让课堂变成庙会的附庸。
options.t_en: I oppose it; public schools should stay secularly neutral, and organizing blessing activities oversteps—a museum for history would be more fitting; don't make class a temple fair appendage.

options.t: 折中，去可以但只作建筑与历史参观、不参与仪式，由家长投票决定并提前告知，谁想参加谁去、不愿的不勉强。
options.t_en: A compromise: visiting is fine but only as architecture and history, no rituals, with parents voting and being informed in advance—those who want go, those who don't aren't forced.

options.t: 我随大流，别的家长去我就让娃去，宗教不宗教的我不在乎，别耽误春游就行，孩子出去跑跑比闷教室里强。
options.t_en: I go with the flow; if other parents go, my kid goes. I don't care about the religious angle—just don't cancel the spring outing; kids running outside beats sitting in class.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: Your child's school is organising a spring outing to a famous temple, and the teacher encourages the pupils to experience blessing culture along the way. Buddhist parents think it is fine; atheist parents worry it is missionary work by another name. As a member of the parents' committee, where do you draw the boundary for this trip? Between the secular classroom and a wisp of incense, where do you draw the line for this outing?

scene: 小区里一户基督徒邻居常在阳台挂十字架、周日在家唱诗，楼下大爷觉得「怪里怪气」想投诉。物业来问你意见，你觉得这算不算该管的「扰民」？，信仰自由和邻里观感顶牛时，你让不让他挂那十字架？，你这一句准信又打算怎么开口说？

options.t: 信仰自由受保护，只要不扰民就不该管，多元共存是本小区该有的气量，挂个十字架又没碍着谁走路。
options.t_en: Religious freedom is protected; as long as it doesn't disturb others, it shouldn't be regulated—coexisting with diversity is the tolerance this community should have; a cross blocks no one's path.

options.t: 公共空间要顾及多数感受，明显出格的宗教标识和声响可以适当规约，维护社区秩序，毕竟小区是大家共有的不是教堂。
options.t_en: Public spaces should consider the majority's feelings; conspicuously out-of-line religious symbols and noise can be modestly regulated to maintain community order—the compound is shared, not a church.

options.t: 由邻里坐下来议定「互不扰」的共处约定，把界限讲在前头，比事后投诉更和睦，唱诗声关窗、标识收进阳台内便是。
options.t_en: Let neighbors sit down and agree on a 'mutual non-disturbance' coexistence pact, setting boundaries upfront—more harmonious than complaining later; close windows for hymns, keep symbols on the balcony.

options.t: 我关起门来过自己的日子，邻居家信啥、挂啥与我无关，别来问我这种闲事，我连他家养几盆花都懒得记。
options.t_en: I keep to my own life behind closed doors; what my neighbor believes or hangs is none of my business—don't ask me about such trivialities; I don't even recall how many plants they keep.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A Christian neighbour in the compound often hangs a cross on the balcony and sings hymns at home on Sundays. The man downstairs finds it odd and wants to complain. The property manager asks your opinion: does this count as the kind of nuisance that should be regulated? When freedom of belief and the neighbours' sense of comfort push against each other, do you let him keep the cross up, and how do you say so?

scene: 你家老人病重，医院按流程全力抢救，但老人此前口头说过「信佛不想过度医疗」。子女对「该不该尊重遗愿停掉部分治疗」争执不下。你站哪边，孝和意愿哪个更大？，孝心和老人遗愿拔河时，你准备往哪头使劲？，这口气你往哪边咽才睡得踏实？

options.t: 尊重老人信仰与自主，生前明确意愿应被听见，过度抢救反是对其信念的不敬，让他走得有尊严比插满管子更孝。
options.t_en: Respect the elder's faith and autonomy; a clearly stated living wish should be heard, and over-treatment dishonors their belief—letting them go with dignity is more filial than tubes everywhere.

options.t: 生命至上，医疗以挽救为第一原则，信仰选择不能替代专业抢救，家属无权放弃，只要还有一线就該搏一搏。
options.t_en: Life is paramount; medicine's first principle is to save, and faith choices can't replace professional resuscitation—family has no right to give up; fight for every thread of hope.

options.t: 应提前立好合法生前预嘱，让个人信仰以书面形式绑定医疗决策，减少家人事后撕扯，也免得医生两头为难。
options.t_en: A legal advance directive should be made in advance, binding personal faith to medical decisions in writing to reduce family strife afterward and spare doctors being caught in the middle.

options.t: 听大哥的，他是长子也是主要出钱的人，家里这种事历来长兄拍板，我不多嘴，省得担了主意还落不着好。
options.t_en: I'll follow my eldest brother; as the firstborn and main payer, he's always decided such family matters, and I won't chime in—lest I bear the choice yet get no credit.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: An elder in your family is seriously ill. The hospital is doing everything to resuscitate, following procedure, but the elder had said verbally before that as a Buddhist he did not want excessive treatment. The children cannot agree on whether to respect that wish and stop some of the treatment. Which side are you on: does filial duty or the elder's wish weigh more? When filial love and the old person's last wish are in a tug of war, which way will you pull? Which way do you have to swallow this to sleep at night?

scene: 市里想在天主教墓地旁建一座大型骨灰堂，方便无信仰市民。宗教团体担心冲撞、世俗居民嫌「阴气重」。规划听证会上你支持哪个方案，如何安顿两种不安？，教义的安宁和市民的需求打架，你这票投给谁？，你的那票到底先顾教义还是市民？

options.t: 支持建，公共资源应服务全体市民，信仰团体的忌讳不能否决多数人的殡葬需求，生者怎么安顿逝者不该被教义卡住。
options.t_en: I support building it; public resources should serve all citizens, and a religious group's taboos can't veto the majority's funeral needs—how the living settle the dead shouldn't be blocked by doctrine.

options.t: 应尊重在地信仰社群的空间感受，另选址或留出缓冲，强行贴建只会制造对立，信仰的安宁也是公共资源该顾的。
options.t_en: We should respect the local faith community's sense of space—relocate or add a buffer; forcing adjacent construction only breeds conflict, and believers' peace is also public good to mind.

options.t: 由市民代表和宗教团体共同协商选址与规制，把分歧摊在桌上而非各执一词，定下的方案大家都得认、都好过。
options.t_en: Citizen reps and the religious group should jointly negotiate site and rules, putting differences on the table rather than each insisting alone—the settled plan all can accept beats the alternative.

options.t: 我不在乎建哪，只要别建我家旁边、别拉高房价就成，其余随你们定，殡葬用地跟我这活人没半毛钱关系。
options.t_en: I don't care where it's built, as long as not next to my home and not raising property prices—otherwise decide as you like; burial land has nothing to do with me, a living person.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: The city wants to build a large columbarium next to a Catholic cemetery for the convenience of non-religious citizens. Religious groups worry it would be an affront; secular residents find it morbid. At the planning hearing, which option do you support, and how do you settle both kinds of unease? When the peace of a doctrine and the needs of citizens collide, where does your vote go, and do you put doctrine first or citizens first?

scene: 你公司在传统节日的「企业文化」活动里加入了焚香祈福环节，年轻员工觉得迷信、老员工觉得有年味。HR来征求你的意见，职场该不该有这缕香火？，年味和迷信的界线前，你这柱香是留还是撤？，这香火里的分寸你又怎么拿捏？

options.t: 保留，传统仪式承载集体记忆和归属感，只要不强制参与就挺好，别把习俗当迷信一棍子打死，年味本来就是这么来的。
options.t_en: Keep it; traditional rituals carry collective memory and belonging, and as long as participation isn't forced it's fine—don't dismiss custom as superstition; the festive feel comes from exactly this.

options.t: 去掉，职场是理性协作空间，掺入祈福仪式容易让不信的人被边缘，应保世俗中性，年味回家过、公司就谈干活。
options.t_en: Remove it; the workplace is a rational collaborative space, and mixing in blessing rituals marginalizes non-believers—keep it secular and neutral; festive feel belongs at home, work is for work.

options.t: 改成自愿的文化体验角，信不信都行、不强推，用包容设计兼顾不同员工的舒适度，想上香的上香、想喝茶的喝茶。
options.t_en: Turn it into a voluntary cultural-experience corner—believe or not, no pushing—using inclusive design to suit different employees' comfort; those who want incense burn it, others sip tea.

options.t: 公司搞啥我跟着做，反正不费我钱不累我身，有点仪式感烘托气氛也挺热闹，一年就这一回别太较真。
options.t_en: I'll just go along with whatever the company does; it costs me nothing and tires me not, and a bit of ritual livens the mood—once a year, no need to be so serious.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: Your company has added an incense-and-prayer ritual to its corporate culture events for the traditional festival. Younger staff find it superstitious; older staff say it is what gives the day its flavour. HR comes to ask your view: should the workplace have that wisp of incense at all? Faced with the line between festive atmosphere and superstition, do you keep the ritual or drop it, and how do you judge the right amount?

scene: 你所在的老破小小区纳入改造，方案二选一：政府全资翻新外观但回收部分公共空间建车位；或居民自筹加政府补贴保住花园。作为业主你投哪票，是要面子还是要里子？，面子工程和小区的绿荫之间，你这一票卖给谁？，你那点念想又值几斤几两分量？

options.t: 选政府全资，公共设施本就该政府兜，车位缓解停车难更实用，花园可以以后再说，天天抢车位打架比没花看更闹心。
options.t_en: Pick government-funded; public facilities should be covered by the state, and parking eases a real pain—the garden can wait; daily parking fights annoy more than lacking flowers.

options.t: 保花园，居民自筹留绿地对邻里感情和儿童玩耍重要，不能全交给政绩式的外立面，刷红的墙不如孩子脚下有块草。
options.t_en: Keep the garden; resident-funded green space matters for neighborly bonds and kids' play, and we shouldn't hand it all to facade-focused vanity projects—red walls beat no grass under kids' feet.

options.t: 我的房子我做主，若多数要车位我跟着走，个人偏好拗不过小区整体决定，少数服从多数别为片绿地把业委会搅散。
options.t_en: My home, my call—but if the majority wants parking I'll follow; personal preference can't override the community's overall decision; don't let one green patch split the owners' committee.

options.t: 关键看哪项更增值，房产是最大资产，选能抬高房价的方案才算聪明业主，外观新、车位足的房子转手就是硬通货。
options.t_en: What matters is which raises value; property is my biggest asset, so pick the plan that lifts prices—a refreshed facade with parking is hard currency at resale, the smart owner's move.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Your rundown old compound has been included in a renovation program, with two options: the government pays for a full exterior facelift but takes back some of the common space for parking, or the residents contribute with a government subsidy and keep the garden. As an owner, which way do you vote: face or substance? Between the showcase project and the shade in the compound, who do you sell your vote to? And how much is that bit of sentiment of yours actually worth?

scene: 你刚工作三年攒了首付，老家父母劝你回小城买大房子安稳，同事劝你留一线城市租房拼机会。面临「定居何处」你更认同哪种活法，安稳与可能之间怎么选？，安稳的小城和拼搏的一线之间，你的人生落点在哪？，这落点你敢不敢现在就一锤定音？

options.t: 留一线租房，机会和视野是无形资产，年轻时该闯，房子晚几年买不迟，把首付拿去投资自己比困在水泥里值。
options.t_en: Stay in the tier-1 city renting; opportunity and perspective are intangible assets, and youth is for striving—buying a home can wait; spend the down payment on yourself, not trapped in concrete.

options.t: 回小城买房，安稳和可负担的生活更重要，不拿半生给房贷当奴隶才叫清醒，有瓦遮头比虚无缥缈的上升更踏实。
options.t_en: Return to the small city and buy; stability and affordable living matter more, and not enslaving half your life to a mortgage is the clear-headed choice—a roof beats vague upward mobility.

options.t: 城市应多建保障房和租购同权，让年轻人不必二选一，用公共政策托底选择自由，别让房价替每个人安排人生。
options.t_en: Cities should build more affordable housing and equalize renting and buying rights, so youth needn't choose one or the other—let public policy underwrite that freedom, not let prices plan everyone's life.

options.t: 哪赚钱去哪，我跟着工作机会走，房子只是落脚处，别被「安家」的执念绑住，哪天外派哪天抬腿就走才自由。
options.t_en: I go where the money is; I follow job opportunities, and a home is just a foothold—don't let the fixation on 'settling down' tie me down; freedom is packing up when transferred.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: After three years of work you have saved a down payment. Your parents back home urge you to return to a smaller city, buy a big flat and live securely; colleagues urge you to stay in the tier-one city, rent and chase opportunities. Faced with the question of where to settle, which way of living do you identify with more, and how do you choose between security and possibility? Between a steady small town and a striving metropolis, where does your life land, and dare you settle it with one stroke now?

scene: 你们楼要装电梯，低层住户嫌没用还挡光、不愿摊钱，高层老人上下楼困难坚决要装。僵持不下时你作为中层住户怎么斡旋，这台电梯装还是不装？，老人的电梯和底楼的阳光打架，你这个中间层怎么和稀泥？，这碗水你又怎么端才不洒一地？

options.t: 支持装并让高层多出资、低层获补偿，用「谁受益谁多付」的市场化分摊化解矛盾，老人下楼晒太阳的权利也该被算进去。
options.t_en: Support installing it with upper floors paying more and lower floors compensated—resolve the conflict via 'who benefits pays more'; elders' right to go downstairs for sun should count too.

options.t: 反对强制，低层物权应被尊重，不能靠多数投票剥夺少数对共有部分的否决，得自愿达成一致，否则楼里从此结成死仇。
options.t_en: Oppose coercion; lower-floor property rights deserve respect, and a majority vote can't strip a minority's veto over common parts—consensus must be voluntary, or the building turns to feud.

options.t: 政府应给老旧小区电梯补贴并出标准方案，把邻里扯皮转化为公共工程而非内耗，别让一栋楼的私事耗光邻里情。
options.t_en: Government should subsidize elevators in old neighborhoods with a standard plan, turning neighbor bickering into public works instead of internal friction—don't let one building's affair exhaust good will.

options.t: 我中立，装不装都行，只要别让我额外多出钱、别吵得整栋不得安生就谢天谢地，电梯对我上下楼本就无所谓。
options.t_en: I'm neutral; install or not, either way, as long as I'm not asked for extra money and the building isn't torn apart by arguments, I'm grateful—an elevator barely affects my floors anyway.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Your building is installing a lift. The lower floors say it is no use to them and blocks their light, and refuse to contribute; the elderly on the upper floors cannot manage the stairs and insist it goes ahead. With the two sides deadlocked, how do you, living in the middle, broker it? Does the lift get built or not, and how do you hold the balance without spilling it?

scene: 你们市中心一块地政府原计划建保障房，后改规划建商务地标以拉升税收。刚需青年骂「又给富人腾地」，招商方说「产业起来才能养城市」。你支持改规划吗，民生与税基孰先？，税收的天际线和刚需的炕头之间，你偏哪边？

options.t: 反对，保障房是民生底线，为税收牺牲刚需是把公平让位于GDP的短视，年轻人住不起的城市繁华得再好看也是空壳。
options.t_en: I oppose it; affordable housing is a livelihood floor, and sacrificing need-based demand for tax revenue is short-sighted, trading fairness for GDP—a city's glitter is hollow if youth can't live there.

options.t: 支持，产业和商业税基才能反哺公共服务，长远看地标带动的就业惠及所有人，光建保障房没有税连物业都养不起。
options.t_en: I support it; industry and commercial tax base ultimately funds public services, and the jobs a landmark draws benefit everyone in the long run—only affordable housing with no tax can't even fund its upkeep.

options.t: 应要求配建比例，商务地标里强制留足保障房指标，用规制把发展与民生绑在一起，不能只顾天际线不顾人间的炕。
options.t_en: Require a build ratio—mandate enough affordable units within the commercial landmark, binding development and livelihood together by regulation; don't mind the skyline while ignoring people's beds.

options.t: 我反正买不起这片的房，建啥都跟我无关，只盼别因此把周边物价房租再炒高，别让我这租客被赶上更远的郊外。
options.t_en: I can't afford a place here anyway, so what's built is irrelevant to me; I just hope it doesn't further inflate local prices and rents and push this tenant farther to the suburbs.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A plot in the city center was originally planned for affordable housing, but the plan has been changed to a commercial landmark to raise tax revenue. Young people who need a first home say the land is being cleared for the rich again; the investment office says the city can only be sustained once industry takes off. Do you support changing the plan? Between the skyline of tax revenue and a first home of one's own, which side are you on?

scene: 你租的公寓房东突然要卖房、限你一个月搬走，合同里违约金条款模糊。中介建议你「认栽赶紧找房」，你朋友建议你「据理硬刚」。你怎么应对这突如其来的扫地出门？，突然被扫地出门的你，是硬刚到底还是认栽走人？，真到了卷铺盖那天你心里怕不怕？

options.t: 硬刚，依法合同未到期就不能赶人，宁可走仲裁也要守住租客的合法居住权，退一步房东下次更敢随便撵人。
options.t_en: I'll stand firm; by law a lease can't be terminated early, and I'd rather arbitrate than surrender a tenant's legal right to housing—give in and the landlord dares evict at will next time.

options.t: 认栽搬走，和房东耗时间精力不值当，市场里下一个房子总找得到，别因口气误事，拖着不走还得搭上误工费更亏。
options.t_en: I'll take the loss and move; fighting the landlord isn't worth the time and energy, and another place can be found—don't let pride spoil things; staying costs lost wages, worse deal.

options.t: 应推动租客协会集体议价与法律援助，让个体面对房东时不至于孤立无援，一个人的合同糊涂坑的是一片租房人。
options.t_en: We should build a tenants' association for collective bargaining and legal aid, so individuals facing landlords aren't left isolated—one vague contract traps a whole renting class.

options.t: 跟房东谈笔补偿，多给俩月过渡加搬家费就走人，用钱买平事最省心，拿钱找好房比跟中介对骂体面得多。
options.t_en: I'll negotiate compensation—two extra months and a moving fee, then leave; buying peace with money is easiest, and taking cash to find a good place beats cursing the agent.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Your landlord suddenly wants to sell the flat you rent and gives you one month to leave, while the penalty clause in the contract is vague. The agent advises you to accept it and find somewhere fast; your friend advises you to stand your ground on the contract. How do you respond to being thrown out at short notice? Now that you are being pushed out, do you fight it to the end or accept it and go, and are you actually afraid as you pack?

scene: 你老家的村集体想把千亩良田外包给农业公司经营现代化大棚，承诺租金和岗位。老农担心「地被人拿走、子孙不会种田」。作为返乡青年你支持流转吗，效率和根脉谁重？，效率和根脉拔河，这片地被外包你点不点头？，你这一声点头背后又意味着什么？

options.t: 支持流转，规模经营和科技种田能提高产出惠及全村，守着小农模式才真没出路，会种田的手艺不如会算账的脑子金贵。
options.t_en: I support the transfer; scaled operation and tech farming raise output for the whole village, and clinging to smallholder mode is the real dead end—tilling skill is worth less than a calculating mind.

options.t: 反对，耕地是命根子，外包断了村庄与土地的连接，应保住农户自主耕作的权利，地没了村子也就散了魂。
options.t_en: I oppose it; arable land is our lifeline, and outsourcing severs the village's bond with the soil—farmers' right to till autonomously must be kept; lose the land and the village loses its soul.

options.t: 应股份制合作，村民以地入股分红并参与管理，让公司和农民成利益共同体而非租赁关系，赚钱管家两不耽误。
options.t_en: Use shareholding cooperation: villagers invest land for dividends and join management, making company and farmer a community of interest rather than a lease—profit and control both covered.

options.t: 谁给租金高就租给谁，家里老人种不动了，变现比撂荒强，别谈那些虚的情怀，钱到手给孙子交学费最实在。
