options.t_en: Whoever pays more rent gets the land; the elders can't farm it anymore, and cashing in beats letting it lie fallow—skip the sentimental talk; money in hand pays my grandkid's tuition, that's real.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The village collective in your home town wants to lease a thousand mu of good farmland to an agricultural company to run modern greenhouses, promising rent and jobs. Older farmers worry that the land is being taken out of their hands and that their children will never learn to farm. As a young person who has come back, do you support the transfer, and which matters more to you, efficiency or roots? What does your nod actually mean?

scene: 超市同种蔬菜，有机的贵三倍、普通的使用了合规农药。你给孩子做辅食，在「贵但少残留」和「便宜但常规」之间怎么选，这份额外的钱值不值得花？，贵三倍的有机和便宜的常规之间，你给孩子碗里盛什么？，这口饭你又喂得安不安心？

options.t: 选普通菜，合规农药残留安全可控，把省下的钱花在更均衡的食谱上更划算，孩子营养靠搭配不靠那点有机标。
options.t_en: I pick regular produce; compliant pesticide residues are safely controlled, and spending the savings on a more balanced diet is better value—a child's nutrition comes from variety, not the organic label.

options.t: 选有机，孩子身体娇嫩，宁可多花钱也尽量避开销残留，健康溢价我愿意付，宁可信其有不可拿娃的肝去试药。
options.t_en: I choose organic; a child's body is delicate, and I'd rather pay more to avoid residues—I'm willing to pay the health premium; better safe than test my kid's liver with pesticides.

options.t: 应推动补贴让有机平价、加强农残抽检公示，别把「吃得安全」变成有钱人的特权，普通家庭也配给孩子干净一口。
options.t_en: We should subsidize affordable organic and strengthen residue testing and disclosure, so 'eating safe' isn't a privilege of the rich—ordinary families also deserve a clean bite for their kids.

options.t: 我两种混着买，主打一个性价比随缘，不纠结标签，洗干净煮熟都一样，钱花在刀刃上比花在招牌上聪明。
options.t_en: I buy both mixed by mood and value; I don't obsess over labels—washed and cooked, they're all the same to me; spend on the point, not the badge—smarter with money.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: At the supermarket, the same vegetable costs three times as much when it is organic, while the ordinary one was grown with pesticide within the legal limits. You are making baby food for your child: how do you choose between expensive with less residue and cheap but conventional, and is the extra money worth spending? Between organic at three times the price and the cheap conventional one, what do you put in your child's bowl? And does that mouthful go down easily?

scene: 你承包的鱼塘附近食品厂偷排污水，鱼大批死亡、损失惨重。厂方想私下赔点钱了事，环保局说已立案将重罚。你接受私了还是等公法，要眼前钱还是讨公道？，眼前赔偿和长远公道之间，你这鱼塘的亏吃还是不吃了？，这口气你又到底咽不咽得下去？

options.t: 等公法，必须让污染者担责并整改，私了是帮它逃避监管，以后还会祸害别人，我这口鱼塘烂了不能白烂。
options.t_en: Wait for the law; the polluter must be held accountable and forced to fix things. A private settlement helps it dodge regulation and harm others later; my pond ruined shouldn't be in vain.

options.t: 拿赔偿走人，打官司耗不起，真金白银补上损失比虚无缥缈的「正义」实在，鱼塘重买鱼苗还得靠这笔钱续命。
options.t_en: Take the payout and leave; I can't afford the lawsuit, and real money covering my loss beats illusory 'justice'—I need this cash to restock the pond and keep going.

options.t: 联合沿河养殖户集体索赔并督促整改，用抱团让环保执法长出牙齿、护住共同水源，一个人告不如一条河的人一起告。
options.t_en: Join riverside farmers to claim collectively and push remediation, using solidarity to give environmental enforcement teeth and protect our shared water—one suing beats the whole river suing together.

options.t: 私下多要一笔、同时留证备着，两头都不放，进可攻退可守最稳妥，谈不拢我再拿证据找媒体和环保局。
options.t_en: I'll privately demand a bigger sum while keeping evidence in reserve—covering both fronts is safest; if talks fail I'll take the evidence to media and the environment bureau.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: A food factory near the fish ponds you lease has been discharging wastewater on the sly, and the fish are dying in large numbers with heavy losses. The factory wants to settle quietly with a payment; the environmental bureau says a case is opened and a heavy fine will follow. Do you take the private settlement or wait for the public process, the money in hand or the principle? Between immediate compensation and long-term justice, do you swallow the loss at your ponds, and can you actually swallow this?

scene: 县里推广转基因抗虫棉种，产量高、少打药，但部分农民顾虑「种子不能留种、年年得买」。作为农技站你会怎么引导，技术红利和种子主权怎么摆？，技术红利和种子主权之间，你这良种推广员怎么开口？，这良种你推的时候心虚不心虚？

options.t: 大力推广，减药增产利生态也利收入，技术红利要抓住，顾虑多是信息没到位，我下田给大伙算笔明白账就通了。
options.t_en: Promote vigorously; less pesticide and higher yield help both ecology and income, and we should seize the tech dividend—worries stem from poor information; I'll show farmers the math in the field.

options.t: 审慎，农民失去留种权就绑死在种子公司，应保留传统种源以防被单一供应链卡脖子，种子捏别人手里吃饭都不香。
options.t_en: Be cautious; losing seed-saving binds farmers to the seed company, so traditional seed stock should be kept to avoid chokehold by a single supply chain—seeds in others' hands spoil the meal.

options.t: 建农户合作社统一议价和留种储备，用集体力量平衡技术依赖、守住议价权，单家独户跟大公司根本不在一张牌桌上。
options.t_en: Build farmer cooperatives for unified bargaining and seed reserves, using collective strength to balance tech dependence and defend bargaining power—a lone household isn't even at the same table as a big firm.

options.t: 上面让种啥我发啥，增产指标完成了事，农民接不接受慢慢就习惯了，推广任务压下来我不带头谁带头。
options.t_en: I distribute whatever's mandated; once the yield target is met, that's the job done, and farmers will get used to it over time—if the promotion task lands, who leads if not me.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: The county is promoting genetically modified pest-resistant cotton seed: higher yields, fewer sprays. Some farmers worry that the seed cannot be saved and has to be bought again every year. As an agricultural extension officer, how do you guide them, and where do the gains from the technology sit against seed sovereignty? When you promote the seed, is there anything in you that hesitates?

scene: 城市社区兴起「阳台种菜」热潮，物业以「违建和蚊虫」为由要取缔各家的种植箱。爱种菜的业主和物业起冲突。你作为业委会怎么摆平这盆葱蒜引发的战争？，几盆葱蒜引发的战争里，你这业委会站在哪一边？，这盆葱蒜你又到底护不护得住？

options.t: 支持物业，公共环境整洁和防蚊是全体利益，个人乐趣不能损害邻里，该规范就规范，种菜再香也香不过全楼不蚊咬。
options.t_en: I side with property; public cleanliness and mosquito control serve everyone, and personal hobby can't harm neighbors—regulate where needed; veggies smell fine but not as good as a bite-free building.

options.t: 支持业主，自己阳台种点葱蒜是生活自主，城市人 reconnect 土地的权利不该被禁，治理蚊虫有招不该一禁了之。
options.t_en: I side with owners; growing scallions on one's own balcony is personal autonomy, and city dwellers' right to reconnect with the land shouldn't be banned—there are ways to curb mosquitoes besides a blanket ban.

options.t: 定公约，限定容器材质、位置和防蚊措施，让种菜与整洁共存，由业主共同监督执行，规则大家定才服众。
options.t_en: Set a charter: limit container material, placement, and mosquito measures so gardening and tidiness coexist, with owners jointly overseeing it—rules made by all are accepted by all.

options.t: 我没种也不反对别人种，只要别积水招蚊子进我家，物业怎么定我都配合，邻里和睦比几盆草重要得多。
options.t_en: I don't garden and don't object to others doing so, as long as no standing water brings mosquitoes into my home; I'll comply with whatever property decides—harmony beats a few pots of greens.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: Growing vegetables on balconies has become a craze in city communities, and the property management wants to ban everyone's planter boxes on grounds of illegal structures and mosquitoes. Owners who love gardening are in open conflict with management. As a member of the owners' committee, how do you settle this war over a few pots of scallions and garlic? In a war started by a few pots of scallions, which side is your committee on? And can you actually protect those pots at all?

scene: 市里一家地方新闻网报道了某化工企业排污的线索，但未经第三方检测就抢先发布，引发居民连夜抢购矿泉水、相关企业股价也跟着剧烈波动。企业坚称报道不实，要求平台撤稿并公开道歉；平台则犹豫是否该替用户做删留决定。作为该平台的内容审核员，你要在新闻自由、公众知情权与企业名誉受损之间做出艰难的取舍与权衡。

options.t: 我倾向于保留报道并加注「待核实」提示，真相不该被捂住，公众有知情权，平台不该替企业压下可能有价值的线索，沉默只会助长猜测。
options.t_en: I lean toward keeping the report with a 'unverified' note; the truth shouldn't be suppressed, the public has a right to know, and the platform shouldn't bury a possibly valuable lead for the company.

options.t: 我认为平台应主动撤下无检测依据的报道，避免引发恐慌和损害企业名誉，不实信息造成的连锁损失往往比漏报一条新闻更现实也更严重。
options.t_en: I think the platform should proactively remove the report lacking test basis to avoid panic and reputational harm; the damage from false info is more real than a missed story.

options.t: 我支持让企业走法律途径起诉媒体，由法院判定真伪，平台保持中立不预先删稿，让司法程序而非算法来最终决定孰对孰错。
options.t_en: I support letting the company sue the media in court to determine truth; the platform stays neutral and doesn't pre-delete, letting the judiciary rather than algorithms decide.

options.t: 我更愿意用算法把这类未核实报道降权、仅推送给主动关注环保的用户，既保留讨论空间又减少误伤普通大众的可能，把判断权留给人。
options.t_en: I'd rather downrank such unverified reports via algorithm, showing them only to users who actively follow environmental topics—preserving space while reducing collateral harm.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A local news site in the city reported a lead about a chemical firm's discharge, but published before third-party testing, setting off a night-time rush to buy bottled water among residents and sharp swings in the company's share price. The company insists the report is false and demands that the platform retract it and apologise publicly; the platform is torn over whether it should make the keep-or-delete decision for its users. As a content moderator on that platform, you must weigh press freedom and the public's right to know against damage to the company's reputation in a genuinely difficult trade-off.

scene: 一段看起来逼真的深度伪造视频在社交平台疯传，画面中本市市长收受现金并点头示意。技术团队确认是AI合成，但辟谣速度远远赶不上传播。作为平台治理委员会成员，你需要决定对这类已经技术证伪的伪造内容采取什么样的处置姿态与限度，既不能放任也不能滥权。

options.t: 我主张对经技术确认的伪造视频直接下架并标注「AI合成」水印，防止误导选举与公共秩序，平台有责任主动拦截明显的造假与 manipulation。
options.t_en: I advocate taking down technically confirmed fakes and labeling them 'AI-generated' to prevent misleading elections and public order; platforms have a duty to block clear fraud.

options.t: 我认为应以滚动辟谣和降低推荐权重为主、谨慎删除，过度下架会助长「平台封口」的猜疑，反而损害平台与公众之间的长久信任。
options.t_en: I think rolling corrections and lower recommendation weight, with cautious deletion, is better; over-removal fuels 'platform censorship' suspicion and hurts trust.

options.t: 我建议强制所有政治类视频携带可验证的数字来源证书，无证内容不予推荐，从技术源头遏制深度伪造的流通与对民主的侵蚀。
options.t_en: I propose mandating verifiable digital source certificates for all political videos; unverified content won't be recommended, curbing deepfakes at the technical source.

options.t: 我觉得应由独立第三方事实核查机构而非平台内部裁决，政府也不宜直接指令，把判定权交给社会公认的民间组织更让人信服。
options.t_en: I think independent third-party fact-checkers, not internal platform panels or direct government orders, should decide—handing judgment to widely trusted civil groups.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: A convincing deepfake is spreading fast on social platforms, showing the city's mayor taking cash and nodding. The technical team has confirmed it is AI-generated, but the correction travels far more slowly than the clip. As a member of the platform governance committee, you have to decide what posture and what limits to adopt towards forgeries that have already been technically disproved, without either letting them run or overreaching your authority.

scene: 国家广播公司面临经费削减，政府提议把它转为广告驱动的商业化媒体以减轻财政负担。支持者说纳税人不该长期养媒体，反对者担心公共媒体编辑独立性的丧失与多元声音被资本挤压。你是财政与文教联席会的列席市民代表，需要对这条改革明确表态并承担后果。

options.t: 我反对全面商业化，公共媒体应保留国家拨款以维持编辑独立、不被广告主和大资本裹挟，这也是一国文化主权不可或缺的一部分。
options.t_en: I oppose full commercialization; public media should keep state funding to preserve editorial independence from advertisers and big capital—it's part of cultural sovereignty.

options.t: 我支持转商业化，纳税人不必长期供养媒体，让其靠内容和订阅自谋生路，反而更能贴近真实的市场需求与读者偏好。
options.t_en: I support commercialization; taxpayers shouldn't permanently fund media—let it survive on content and subscriptions, which better fits market demand.

options.t: 我主张折中：保留基础公共拨款但引入多元基金会与社会捐助，减少单一政府控制也避免过度依赖广告收入而软化监督。
options.t_en: I favor a middle path: keep basic public funding but add diverse foundations and donations, reducing single-government control yet avoiding over-reliance on ads.

options.t: 我认为应交给市场彻底私有化、出售给民间资本，公共媒体的历史角色可由独立新闻机构自然承接与延续，政府不必亲自办媒体。
options.t_en: I think it should be fully privatized and sold to private capital; independent news outlets can naturally take over the public media's historic role.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: The national broadcaster faces budget cuts, and the government proposes turning it into an advertising-driven commercial media outlet to ease the fiscal burden. Supporters say taxpayers should not be supporting media indefinitely; opponents worry about the loss of editorial independence in public media and about diverse voices being squeezed by capital. You are a citizen representative attending the joint finance and education committee, and you need to take a clear position on this reform and accept the consequences.

scene: 某短视频平台因仇恨言论泛滥遭舆论批评，运营方考虑引入更严格的内容审核规则，但创作者担心「误伤」正常表达与讽刺内容。你作为平台用户顾问，要在社区安全与表达自由之间给出可操作的具体建议，并说明你更看重哪一边。

options.t: 我支持扩大审核并明确禁止煽动性仇恨内容，线上空间也该有底线，受害者群体的安全优先于绝对的、不加约束的发言自由。
options.t_en: I support broader moderation with clear bans on inciteful hate content; online spaces need red lines, and the safety of targeted groups comes before absolute speech freedom.

options.t: 我担心审核越界会变成思想审查，宁可依赖用户举报和透明度报告，也不愿让平台替所有人定义什么话能说、什么话不能。
options.t_en: I worry expanded moderation becomes thought censorship; I'd rather rely on user reports and transparency reports than let the platform define for everyone what can be said.

options.t: 我建议用AI先筛明显违规、人工复核争议内容，并公开审核标准，既提速又保留可被质疑的弹性空间，减少黑箱操作。
options.t_en: I suggest AI pre-filters clear violations with human review of disputed cases and public standards—speeding up while keeping challengeable flexibility.

options.t: 我认为社区应自己制定公约、自管自清，平台只提供工具不替用户裁决，把治理权交还给使用者群体才是长久之道。
options.t_en: I think communities should write their own rules and self-police; the platform only provides tools, handing governance back to user groups.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A short-video platform has been criticised publicly over a flood of hate speech, and its operator is considering stricter content rules, while creators worry that ordinary expression and satire will be caught in the crossfire. As an adviser to the platform on user issues, you must give concrete, workable suggestions on community safety versus freedom of expression, and explain which side you weight more heavily.

scene: 地震灾区通讯中断，官方通报与民间志愿者在社交群里的现场视频互相矛盾，恐慌情绪不断蔓延。你是前方临时信息协调组的成员，要决定对外信息发布究竟以谁为准、如何兼顾时效与可信，不让谣言跑在救援前面。，面对这类没有明确对错的分歧，不同立场各有其道理，最终如何取舍只能由处在其中的人按自身处境与价值排序去认真掂量。

options.t: 我坚持以官方统一通报为准，混乱时期需要权威口径避免谣言误导救援，民间片段难免以偏概全、放大局部的焦虑与误判。
options.t_en: I insist on official unified bulletins; in chaos we need an authoritative voice to avoid rumor-driven rescue mistakes, and civilian clips are inevitably partial.

options.t: 我认为应并行发布民间现场视频并标注时间地点，多渠道互证比单一信源更可信，也倒逼官方更及时、更透明地回应。
options.t_en: I think we should also publish civilian on-site videos with timestamps; multi-source cross-checking beats a single feed and pushes officials to be timely.

options.t: 我主张由独立记者和救援机构组成联合信息发布池，政府提供数据但不垄断解释权，以此提升整体公信力与救援效率。
options.t_en: I propose a joint pool of independent journalists and rescue groups; government supplies data but doesn't monopolize interpretation, boosting credibility.

options.t: 我建议优先用卫星和无人机技术核实关键画面，再对外发布，用技术背书替代立场之争从而降低误传风险与次生灾害。
options.t_en: I suggest verifying key footage first with satellites and drones, then publishing—letting technical evidence replace position-fighting and cut misreporting.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Communications are down in the earthquake zone, official bulletins contradict the videos volunteers are posting in group chats, and panic keeps spreading. You are on the temporary information coordination team in the field, and you have to decide whose word the public releases should rest on, and how to balance speed against credibility so that rumour does not outrun the rescue. On a disagreement with no clear right answer, each position has its reasons, and only the people inside it can weigh the trade-offs by their own circumstances and priorities.

scene: 本市盗窃案频发，市议会讨论是否对第三次盗窃一律判处强制最低刑期、即所谓「三振法案」。支持者说能震慑惯犯，反对者担心监狱人满为患、轻罪者被重判。你是列席的社区代表，需对这条刚性规则明确表态并说明理由。，相关各方的利益与原则在此相互拉扯，并不存在显而易见的标准答案，只能结合具体情境权衡轻重。

options.t: 我支持三振法案，对屡教不改的惯犯必须重罚才能保护守法居民，宽容过度反倒是在纵容犯罪横行、让邻里失去安全感。
options.t_en: I support three-strikes laws; repeat offenders must face harsh penalties to protect law-abiding residents—too much leniency just enables crime.

options.t: 我反对强制最低刑，法官应看具体情节量刑，小偷小摸也被重判既不人道也浪费纳税人的监狱开支，更堵死改过之路。
options.t_en: I oppose mandatory minimums; judges should weigh circumstances—jailing petty thieves harshly is both inhumane and a waste of prison spending.

options.t: 我主张把钱更多投在社区帮扶与就业培训上预防犯罪，比单纯加刑治标更治本，从收入与尊严的源头减少惯犯的产生。
options.t_en: I'd invest more in community support and job training to prevent crime; that addresses roots better than just lengthening sentences.

options.t: 我认为应区分暴力与非暴力累犯，仅对危害人身的三振重判，财产型小案交给缓刑与赔偿更为合适，避免刑罚失衡。
options.t_en: I'd distinguish violent from non-violent recidivists—only strike hard on those harming persons, while property petty crimes fit probation and restitution.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: Theft is frequent in this city, and the council is discussing whether to impose a mandatory minimum sentence on any third theft conviction, the so-called three strikes law. Supporters say it would deter repeat offenders; opponents worry about overcrowded prisons and petty thieves being sentenced harshly. You are a community representative attending the session, and you need to take a clear position on this rigid rule and explain your reasoning. The interests and principles of the parties involved pull against each other here, and there is no obviously correct answer; the weight can only be judged in context.

scene: 警方拟为巡逻警员全面配备随身摄像头，称可规范执法、留存证据；警察工会却担心增加行政负担并侵犯警员隐私。作为市政监督委员会委员，你要对这一笔不小的装备预算投票，并解释你更在意哪类风险。，这场争论没有轻易的胜负，每一种选择都附带代价，关键看你认为哪一端的价值更值得优先守护。

options.t: 我力挺全面配装，摄像头能约束双方行为、减少纠纷误判，对警察和市民都是保护而非单纯的监视工具，利大于弊。
options.t_en: I strongly back full deployment; cameras constrain both sides and cut disputes, protecting officers and citizens alike rather than surveilling them.

options.t: 我支持但要求录像仅用于涉诉调查、严格封存，不能沦为全天候追踪警员行踪的工具，必须防住内部滥用与泄露。
options.t_en: I support it but require footage only for investigations and strict sealing—not a tool for tracking officers around the clock, guarding against abuse.

options.t: 我反对强制配装，执法尊严与现场判断不应被镜头绑架，警员隐私和临场自主同样值得被尊重，信任不能靠监视建立。
options.t_en: I oppose mandating cameras; dignity of policing and on-the-spot judgment shouldn't be held hostage by lenses—officers' privacy and autonomy matter too.

options.t: 我建议先在小片区试点并公开统计数据再推广，用证据而非立场决定摄像头是否真的降低了冲突与投诉。
options.t_en: I suggest piloting in a small district and publishing stats before scaling; let evidence, not stance, decide if cameras truly cut conflicts.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: The police plan to issue body cameras to all patrol officers, saying the devices would discipline law enforcement and preserve evidence; the police union worries about extra administrative burden and officers' own privacy. As a member of the municipal oversight committee, you must vote on this not insignificant equipment budget and explain which kind of risk concerns you more. This argument has no easy winner; every choice carries a cost, and what matters is which value you think deserves protecting first.

scene: 市禁毒委讨论将个人持有少量毒品由刑事罪改为行政违法、侧重医疗戒断。支持者称监禁只会制造累犯，反对者怕释放错误信号助长滥用。你是公共卫生与司法联席会的市民代表，须在两个部门的逻辑间给出立场。，局面里的两难远非一句对错能概括，真正要紧的是厘清自己究竟把哪一方的诉求放在更靠前的位置。

options.t: 我支持去刑化并用公共医疗帮成瘾者戒断，把他们当病人而非罪犯，社会成本更低也更显人道，也更易让其回归家庭。
options.t_en: I support decriminalization with public medical detox; treat addicts as patients not criminals—lower social cost and more humane.

options.t: 我坚决反对去刑化，持有即违法的红线不能松，宽松只会让更多年轻人误以为吸毒毫无后果，进而放纵自己。
options.t_en: I firmly oppose decriminalization; the 'possession is illegal' red line must hold, or youth will think drugs carry no consequence.

options.t: 我主张折中：首犯强制治疗、再犯才入刑，用阶梯式处理既给改过机会也保留必要的法律威慑，避免一棍子打死。
options.t_en: I favor a middle path: mandated treatment for first offenders, prison only for repeat ones—a stepped approach keeping both chance and deterrence.

options.t: 我认为应把禁毒经费大头转向社区教育与就业扶持，惩处只是末端，预防才是真正治本的出路灯，才是可持续之策。
options.t_en: I think the bulk of anti-drug funds should shift to community education and job support; punishment is the tail, prevention the real fix.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: The city's narcotics committee is discussing reclassifying personal possession of small quantities of drugs from a criminal offence to an administrative one, with the emphasis shifting to medical treatment and withdrawal. Supporters say prison only manufactures repeat offenders; opponents fear it sends the wrong signal and encourages use. You are the citizen representative on the joint public health and justice panel, and must take a position between the two departments' logics. The dilemma resists any one-line verdict; what matters is being clear about whose claim you put first.

scene: 两名少年毁坏公物被捕，少年法庭提出让其对受害者道歉、修复损失、参加公益服务的恢复性司法方案，而非送进少管所。受害者家属态度不一。你是方案评审的社区成员，要权衡两种路径的利弊。，面对这类没有明确对错的分歧，不同立场各有其道理，最终如何取舍只能由处在其中的人按自身处境与价值排序去认真掂量。

options.t: 我赞成恢复性司法，让少年直面后果、修复关系比关押更能真正悔改，也减轻司法系统的长期负担与纳税人的开销。
options.t_en: I favor restorative justice; facing consequences and repairing relationships reforms better than confinement and eases the justice system's load.

options.t: 我认为必须依法惩处以儆效尤，太柔和的处理会让肇事者觉得代价低，对受害者来说也不够交代，也难以安抚社区。
options.t_en: I think they must be punished by law as a warning; too-soft handling makes offenders feel the cost is low and fails the victims.

options.t: 我主张由受害者家属与少年及其家庭面对面协商补偿方式，国家不包办，让社区纽带去修复裂痕、重建彼此的信任。
options.t_en: I propose the victim's family and the teen's family meet to negotiate restitution; the state shouldn't run it, letting community bonds mend the rift.

options.t: 我担心恢复性司法缺乏统一标准易因人而异，应保留法官监督底线、防止富人用钱「买」到轻罚，维护法律面前平等。
options.t_en: I worry restorative justice lacks uniform standards and varies by person; judges should guard the floor to stop the rich 'buying' leniency.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: Two juveniles have been arrested for damaging public property. The juvenile court proposes a restorative justice plan instead of reform school: apologizing to the victims, repairing the damage, and doing community service. The victims' families do not agree with one another. You are a community member reviewing the plan, and you have to weigh the pros and cons of the two paths. Faced with a disagreement that has no clear right or wrong, each position has its reasons, and in the end the choice can only be weighed by the people involved, according to their own circumstances and the order of their values.

scene: 高发罪社区拟加装人脸识别闸机与街面监控网络，警方称能快速锁定嫌疑人；居民有的觉得安全、有的怕被全天候盯梢。你是该社区议事会的轮值召集人，须协调两方诉求并拿出方案。，相关各方的利益与原则在此相互拉扯，并不存在显而易见的标准答案，只能结合具体情境权衡轻重。

options.t: 我支持加装监控网络，治安差的片区先把发案率压下来最实在，居民夜里敢出门比隐私顾虑更重要，安全是安居的前提。
options.t_en: I support the surveillance network; in high-crime areas cutting incidents matters most, and residents walking safely at night beats privacy worries.

options.t: 我反对无差别人脸识别，正常居民不该被当嫌疑人扫描，安全感不能靠牺牲所有人的自由来换取，否则人人自危。
options.t_en: I oppose indiscriminate facial recognition; law-abiding residents shouldn't be scanned like suspects—security can't cost everyone their freedom.

options.t: 我主张限定监控只用于重大刑案回溯、数据定期销毁，并设独立监督，在安全与权利之间取得平衡，防止权力悄悄扩张。
options.t_en: I propose limiting surveillance to major-case review with periodic data deletion and independent oversight, balancing security and rights.

options.t: 我认为与其铺监控不如多派社区民警和夜间照明、改善环境，技术监视终究治标而不治本，人与人的联结更能防犯罪。
options.t_en: I think more officers and night lighting beat blanket surveillance; environmental improvement addresses causes, not just symptoms.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: A high-crime neighbourhood plans to install facial recognition gates and a street surveillance network. The police say suspects could be identified quickly; residents are divided between feeling safer and fearing round-the-clock scrutiny. As the rotating convenor of the neighbourhood council, you must reconcile the two sides and produce a plan. The interests and principles at stake pull against each other here, and there is no obviously correct answer, only a weighing of priorities in the specific circumstances.

scene: 邻国对我国主打农产品加征关税，本国农民叫苦连天。经贸部门拟对等反制并扶持国内供应链；出口企业则怕贸易战升级丢了海外订单。你是商务部公众咨询会的代表，要权衡农户与出口商的利益。，这场争论没有轻易的胜负，每一种选择都附带代价，关键看你认为哪一端的价值更值得优先守护。

options.t: 我支持对等反制，主权经济体不能任人拿捏，短期阵痛换长期谈判筹码，也倒逼国内产业真正自立、不再仰人鼻息。
options.t_en: I support reciprocal retaliation; a sovereign economy can't be pushed around—short pain buys leverage and forces domestic industry to stand alone.

options.t: 我反对打关税战，开放互利才是正道，应坐下来谈判降低壁垒，保护消费者与出口企业的利益，别让农民被当筹码。
options.t_en: I oppose tariff wars; open mutual benefit is the right path—sit down, lower barriers, and protect consumers and exporters.

options.t: 我主张一边谈判一边精准扶持受冲击农户，用补贴与转产缓冲，不把农民当贸易筹码硬扛到底，兼顾就业与饭碗。
options.t_en: I favor negotiating while precisely aiding hit farmers with subsidies and crop shifts—not using them as hard bargaining chips.

options.t: 我认为应联合其他受影响国家共同施压、走多边机制，而非单打独斗，把双边摩擦变成规则博弈，才不会被各个击破。
options.t_en: I think we should join other affected nations to pressure via multilateral bodies, not go alone—turning a bilateral spat into rule-based contest.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A neighbouring country has put a tariff on our main agricultural exports, and farmers here are in uproar. The trade ministry plans matching countermeasures and support for domestic supply chains; exporters fear an escalating trade war will cost them their overseas orders. You are a representative at the commerce ministry's public consultation, and have to weigh farmers against exporters. There is no easy winner in this argument, every option carries a cost, and the question is which end you think is more worth defending.

scene: 一艘载有战乱国平民的难民船在公海遇险，邻近几国互相推诿靠岸港。本国民调分裂：有人怜悯有人忧资源。你是移民事务跨部门会议的列席市民，须就接收方案表态并说明理由。，局面里的两难远非一句对错能概括，真正要紧的是厘清自己究竟把哪一方的诉求放在更靠前的位置。

options.t: 我主张履行人道义务立即接收并安置，文明底线高于算计，况且青壮年难民长期看也是可用劳动力，能反哺本地经济。
options.t_en: I say fulfill the humanitarian duty to receive and settle them now; civilization's floor beats calculus, and young refugees become labor too.

options.t: 我反对无上限接收，本国就业与福利已吃紧，应先保障国民再谈援助，先后顺序绝不能乱，否则会引发内部对立。
options.t_en: I oppose unlimited intake; our jobs and welfare are already strained—secure citizens first, then aid; order matters.

options.t: 我建议按配额由多国分担，并配套语言与职业培训，让接收国压力可承受、融入也更具可持续性，避免集中承压。
options.t_en: I suggest quotas across nations with language and job training, keeping host-country pressure bearable and integration sustainable.

options.t: 我认为根源在战乱，应把资源更多投向斡旋停火与就近难民营，而非都运到千里外的富裕国家，治本胜过治标。
options.t_en: I think the root is war; more resources should go to brokering ceasefires and nearby camps, not shipping everyone to distant rich states.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: A boat carrying civilians from a war-torn country is in distress on the high seas, and the neighboring countries are passing the question of a port of landing back and forth. Opinion in this country is split: some feel compassion, others worry about resources. You are a citizen attending the interdepartmental meeting on immigration, and you must take a position on the reception plan and explain your reasons. The dilemma here cannot be summed up by a single word like right or wrong; what matters is clarifying which side's claims you actually put first.

scene: 友邦卷入局部冲突请求军事援助，政府考虑派出工兵与医疗队参与国际维和，也有声音主张直接军售支持。议会将表决。你是外交国防听证会的公众代表，须亮明态度并承担后果。，面对这类没有明确对错的分歧，不同立场各有其道理，最终如何取舍只能由处在其中的人按自身处境与价值排序去认真掂量。

options.t: 我支持派非战斗维和力量，履行国际责任也积累外交信用，但坚决不卷入直接交战与正面战场，守住不参战的底线。
options.t_en: I support non-combat peacekeeping—meeting international duty and building diplomatic credit—but firmly staying out of direct fighting.

options.t: 我反对任何军事介入，远方的仗不关我们事，年轻人不该为别国冲突流血，应专注本土安全与民生而非远征。
options.t_en: I oppose any military involvement; their war isn't ours, our youth shouldn't bleed for foreign conflicts—focus at home.

options.t: 我主张以军售与情报支持盟友，用最小本国风险换取战略伙伴，比派兵更可控也更隐蔽，不把子弟兵推上第一线。
options.t_en: I favor arms sales and intelligence support to allies—securing strategic partners at minimal domestic risk, more controllable than troops.

options.t: 我认为应先推动多边调停与制裁施压，军事选项留作最后手段，外交优先于枪炮与武力，和平才最符合各方利益。
options.t_en: I think we should first push multilateral mediation and sanctions, keeping military options as last resort—diplomacy before guns, peace best serves all sides.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: A friendly state caught up in a local conflict has asked for military assistance. The government is considering sending engineers and medical teams to an international peacekeeping mission, while some voices argue for direct arms sales instead. Parliament will vote. As a public representative at the foreign affairs and defence hearing, you must take a clear position and accept the consequences. On a disagreement with no clear right answer, each stance has its reasons, and those inside the situation can only weigh them against their own circumstances and priorities.

scene: 新一轮全球气候协定要求各国提交减排路线图，国内煤电与制造业担心成本、呼吁推迟；环保团体要求更激进目标。你是能源转型座谈会的市民代表，要平衡产业工人与后代的利益。，相关各方的利益与原则在此相互拉扯，并不存在显而易见的标准答案，只能结合具体情境权衡轻重。

options.t: 我支持按协定积极减排，气候无国界，拖下去代价更大，绿色转型也催生新的产业机会与就业，利在长远。
options.t_en: I support meeting the accord's cuts; climate knows no borders, delay costs more, and the green shift spawns new industries.

options.t: 我反对激进时间表，本国制造竞争力与工人饭碗优先，减排可循序渐进、别让普通人与蓝领为环保单独买单。
options.t_en: I oppose an aggressive timeline; our manufacturing edge and workers' jobs come first—cut emissions gradually, don't bill ordinary people.

options.t: 我主张发达国家先履诺并出资技术转移，发展中国家公平分摊，不能一刀切要求同步减排，否则有失公允。
options.t_en: I say developed nations must first deliver and fund tech transfer; developing countries share fairly—no one-size-fits-all sync.

options.t: 我认为应押注核电与碳捕集等技术突破，用工程方案解减排难题，而非仅靠限产与关停，保住增长与就业。
options.t_en: I think we should bet on nuclear and carbon-capture breakthroughs, solving cuts via engineering rather than just shutdowns.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A new round of global climate agreements requires every country to submit a roadmap for cutting emissions. Domestic coal power and manufacturing worry about the cost and are calling for delay; environmental groups want more aggressive targets. You are a citizen representative at the energy transition forum, and have to balance industrial workers against future generations. The interests and principles of the parties pull against each other, there is no obviously correct answer, and the balance can only be struck in the circumstances of the case.

scene: 财政部拟削减对外援助预算以补国内民生，发展援助机构称此举损害软实力与地区稳定。你是预算听证会的公众列席者，要在内外之间给出判断并说明取舍逻辑。，这场争论没有轻易的胜负，每一种选择都附带代价，关键看你认为哪一端的价值更值得优先守护。

options.t: 我支持削减援外、把钱先花在本国民生上，纳税人缴的税该优先解决自家穷人的温饱问题，远人不及近邻。
options.t_en: I support cutting aid to fund domestic welfare first; taxpayer money should fix our own poor before others abroad.

options.t: 我反对削减，援助换来稳定市场与友邦关系，长远看护的是本国贸易与安全的外部环境，省小钱可能亏大钱。
options.t_en: I oppose cuts; aid buys stable markets and friendly ties, ultimately protecting our trade and security environment.

options.t: 我主张把援助更多转为技术合作与能力建设，而非直接给钱，既省钱又真正帮对方走向自立，避免养出依赖。
options.t_en: I favor shifting aid to tech cooperation and capacity-building over cash—cheaper and truly helping recipients stand alone.

options.t: 我认为援外应公开绩效审计、砍掉无效项目，但不搞一刀切归零，保留关键的人道通道，让每一分钱都花在刀刃上。
options.t_en: I think foreign aid needs public performance audits and trimming ineffective programs—but not a blanket zeroing, keeping key humanitarian channels.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: The finance ministry plans to cut the foreign aid budget to fund domestic welfare, and development agencies say the move damages soft power and regional stability. You are a member of the public attending the budget hearing, and you have to make a judgment between home and abroad and explain the logic of your trade-off. There is no easy winner in this argument, and every choice carries a cost; what matters is which end you think is more worth protecting first.

scene: 市政府试点全民基本收入，每月无条件给每位成年市民发固定金额，财源来自新增的数字服务税。支持者说能托底，反对者忧养懒人、推高物价。你是试点评估市民小组的成员，须给出判断。，局面里的两难远非一句对错能概括，真正要紧的是厘清自己究竟把哪一方的诉求放在更靠前的位置。

options.t: 我支持无条件发钱，给人免遭生存焦虑的底气，也能释放创业与照护等不被市场计价的劳动价值，社会整体更从容。
options.t_en: I support unconditional cash; it gives people freedom from survival anxiety and unleashes unpaid labor like caregiving and startups.

options.t: 我反对养懒人式发钱，福利应绑定就业或培训，否则财政不可持续还会进一步推高通胀，最终伤到普通人。
options.t_en: I oppose lazy-making handouts; welfare should tie to work or training, or it's fiscally unsustainable and inflates prices.

options.t: 我主张负所得税式托底：收入越低补越多，既保基本又不削弱工作动力，比一刀切更精准，也更能服众。
options.t_en: I favor a negative-income-tax floor: more aid the lower the income—protecting basics without killing work incentives, more precise than flat grants.

options.t: 我担心数字税最终转嫁给消费者、小商家吃亏，发钱来源应先算清再谈，别制造新的不公与阶层间的怨气。
options.t_en: I worry the digital tax lands on consumers and hurts small shops; clarify the funding before talking, don't create new unfairness.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The city government is piloting a universal basic income, paying every adult citizen a fixed sum each month unconditionally, funded by a new tax on digital services. Supporters say it provides a floor; opponents fear it breeds idleness and drives up prices. As a member of the citizens' panel evaluating the pilot, you must give a judgment. The dilemma here cannot be reduced to a question of right or wrong; what matters is being clear about whose claim you place further forward.

scene: 医保改革方案二选一：全民公立医疗免费但排队久，或公立保基本、商业险补优质。患者与医院立场不一。你是医改公众咨询团的成员，须权衡公平与效率的两端。，面对这类没有明确对错的分歧，不同立场各有其道理，最终如何取舍只能由处在其中的人按自身处境与价值排序去认真掂量。

options.t: 我支持全民公立免费医疗，健康是基本权利不应看钱，税收统筹比商业保险更显公平，也兜住最脆弱的人。
options.t_en: I support free universal public care; health is a right beyond wealth, and tax-pooling is fairer than commercial insurance.

options.t: 我倾向公立保底、商保提质，用市场竞争提升服务效率，愿意多花钱买更快更好的诊治体验，选择本就该多元。
options.t_en: I prefer public as floor, private for quality; market competition lifts efficiency, and I'll pay more for faster, better care.

options.t: 我主张基本医疗全包、高额费用共保，设封顶线防因病致贫，兼顾公平与制度的可持续，不让家庭被医疗费拖垮。
options.t_en: I propose fully covering basic care with co-insurance on big bills and a cap to prevent poverty from illness—fair and sustainable.

options.t: 我担心公立独大导致资源错配和官僚低效，应保留多元办医、让民众用脚投票选服务，竞争才能逼出好医疗。
options.t_en: I fear a monolithic public system misallocates resources and turns bureaucratic; keep plural providers so people vote with their feet.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: Health reform comes down to two options: free public care for all, with long queues, or public cover for the basics with commercial insurance for the better tier. Patients and hospitals do not line up on the same side. You are a member of the public consultation panel and have to weigh fairness against efficiency. Faced with a disagreement where there is no clear right answer, each position has its reasons, and only those living inside it can decide by their own circumstances and priorities.

scene: 经济下行期失业金申领人数激增，劳动部门考虑把最长领取期从半年延长到一年，企业界担心助长不就业。你是就业政策听证会的市民代表，要给出立场并解释。，相关各方的利益与原则在此相互拉扯，并不存在显而易见的标准答案，只能结合具体情境权衡轻重。

options.t: 我支持延长领取期，找工作需要时间，断保让人走投无路反而更易陷入长期贫困的循环，也加剧社会不稳定。
options.t_en: I support extending benefits; job-hunting takes time, and cutting off aid pushes people into desperate, chronic poverty.

options.t: 我反对久领，应配套强制职业培训与岗位推介，福利是跳板不是躺平的长椅与终点，否则养出依赖难回头。
options.t_en: I oppose long draw-down; pair it with mandatory training and job placement—welfare is a springboard, not a bench to lie on.

options.t: 我主张阶梯式递减发放：初期全额、越往后越少，既托底又保留找工作的经济压力，比一直发或一刀切断更稳。
options.t_en: I favor a declining scale: full early, less later—a floor that still keeps the economic pressure to find work.

options.t: 我认为关键在创造岗位而非调补贴，应减税降费鼓励企业扩招，从源头减少失业总量，让有活干胜过有钱领。
options.t_en: I think the key is creating jobs, not tweaking benefits; cut taxes and fees to spur hiring, reducing unemployment at its source.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: During a downturn the number of people claiming unemployment benefits has surged, and the labor department is considering extending the maximum claim period from six months to a year. Business groups worry it will encourage people not to work. You are a citizen representative at the employment policy hearing, and you have to give a position and explain it. The interests and principles of the parties involved pull against each other here, and there is no obviously correct answer; the weight can only be judged in context.

scene: 人口老龄化加速，养老基金承压，人社部门拟把法定退休年龄逐步延后并拉长缴费年限。体力劳动者叫苦，白领多能接受。你是养老改革座谈会的公众代表，要平衡两类劳动者。，这场争论没有轻易的胜负，每一种选择都附带代价，关键看你认为哪一端的价值更值得优先守护。

options.t: 我支持延退，寿命延长了、基金得平衡，多缴几年也合理，况且许多岗位经验十分可贵，年长者的价值不该被低估。
options.t_en: I support raising the age; lifespans grew and the fund needs balance—paying longer is fair, and experience in many jobs is valuable.

options.t: 我反对一刀切延退，建筑工、护工等重体力者该早退，应按工种分档而非统一的一条年龄线，否则苦了干粗活的人。
options.t_en: I oppose a flat raise; builders and carers do heavy labor and deserve earlier exit—tie it to occupation, not one age line.

options.t: 我主张弹性退休：早退少领、晚退多领，把选择权交个人，国家只设可领的底线年龄，尊重每个人不同的身体与意愿。
options.t_en: I favor flexible retirement: retire early for less, late for more—hand choice to individuals, with the state setting only a floor age.

options.t: 我认为应从国资划转与提高征缴率补缺口，别总让普通职工靠延退来为基金买单，也要动存量而非只压个人。
options.t_en: I think we should fill the gap via state-asset transfers and better collection, not always making ordinary workers pay through delayed retirement.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: With the population ageing fast and the pension fund under pressure, the human resources department plans to raise the statutory retirement age gradually and lengthen the contribution period. Manual workers are crying foul; white-collar workers mostly accept it. As a public representative at the pension reform forum, you must balance the two kinds of workers. This argument has no easy winner; every choice carries a cost, and what matters is which value you think deserves protecting first.

scene: 中心城区房价高企，住建局推出只租不售的保障性住房并优先照顾低收入家庭，开发商抱怨挤压利润、纳税人质疑补贴对象。你是住房保障委员会的市民成员，须表态。，局面里的两难远非一句对错能概括，真正要紧的是厘清自己究竟把哪一方的诉求放在更靠前的位置。

options.t: 我支持扩大保障房，住有所居是底线，市场房价再高也不该让任何人无家可归，安居才能谈得上其他权利。
options.t_en: I support expanding public housing; shelter is a floor, and no one should be homeless no matter how high market prices climb.

options.t: 我反对政府深度介入供房，应靠放宽土地与审批让市场多建租赁房，补贴不如直接松绑，让供需自己把价格压下来。
options.t_en: I oppose deep state involvement in housing; ease land and permitting so the market builds rentals—deregulation beats subsidies.

options.t: 我主张保障房只给本地缴纳社保一定年限者，避免福利被迁入人口挤占，先紧着贡献者，也算对纳税人和老居民公平。
options.t_en: I say public housing only for those who paid local social insurance for years—avoid newcomers crowding out the benefit, prioritizing contributors.

options.t: 我建议以购房补贴券代替新建，让受助家庭在普通小区自主租房，减少集中贫困与标签化，融入社区也更利于稳定。
options.t_en: I suggest housing vouchers instead of new builds, letting aided families rent in normal neighborhoods—reducing concentrated poverty and stigma.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: With prices in the central districts out of reach, the housing bureau has launched rent-only subsidised housing, giving priority to low-income families. Developers complain their margins are being squeezed; taxpayers question who exactly is being subsidised. You are a citizen member of the housing security committee, and have to state a position. The dilemma resists a one-line verdict; what matters is being clear about whose claim you place in front.

scene: 立法机构审议是否承认同性婚姻，民调两极。支持者谈平等与遗嘱监护权，反对者援引传统家庭观。你是该法案公众听证会的列席市民，须明确表态并承担公共讨论的后果。，面对这类没有明确对错的分歧，不同立场各有其道理，最终如何取舍只能由处在其中的人按自身处境与价值排序去认真掂量。

options.t: 我支持承认同性婚姻，婚姻权不该因性向被剥夺，也关乎医疗探视与财产继承的实在保障，平等是底线而非施舍。
options.t_en: I support recognizing same-sex marriage; the right shouldn't be denied by orientation, and it affects real protections like visitation and inheritance.

options.t: 我反对改动婚姻定义，认为应由一男一女组成才符合传统与子女成长需要，可另设民事伴侣以满足其法律诉求。
options.t_en: I oppose redefining marriage as one man and one woman per tradition and children's needs; a separate civil-union status is fine.

options.t: 我主张先扩民事伴侣权到等同婚姻的实质权益，暂缓改名，求同存异稳步推进改革，避免社会为此激烈对立。
options.t_en: I propose first extending civil-union rights to marriage-equivalent substance, deferring the name—advancing by finding common ground.

options.t: 我认为国家本不应垄断婚姻定义，应交由宗教与民间社群各自认定，法律只管共同财产与监护，政教应各归各位。
options.t_en: I think the state shouldn't monopolize marriage's definition; let faiths and communities define it, with law only handling property and guardianship.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The legislature is considering whether to recognize same-sex marriage, and opinion polls are sharply divided. Supporters talk about equality, wills and guardianship rights; opponents invoke the traditional view of the family. You are a citizen attending the public hearing on the bill, and you must state your position clearly and accept the consequences of public debate. Faced with a disagreement that has no clear right or wrong, each position has its reasons, and in the end the choice can only be weighed by the people involved, according to their own circumstances and the order of their values.

scene: 新规拟给父母双方各放带薪育儿假，企业担心用工成本、部分家庭愿由一方全职带娃。你是人社与妇联联席会的市民代表，要协调雇主与家庭两方不同的焦虑。，相关各方的利益与原则在此相互拉扯，并不存在显而易见的标准答案，只能结合具体情境权衡轻重。

options.t: 我支持父母同享带薪育假，促进共同照护也削弱职场性别歧视，孩子两头都有人陪伴，家庭与职场才能都更健康。
options.t_en: I support paid leave for both parents; it aids shared care and weakens workplace gender bias, with the child accompanied by both.

options.t: 我反对强制平分，家庭该自己决定谁休假，国家别替夫妻安排角色，灵活比一刀切更好，也尊重不同的家庭传统。
options.t_en: I oppose forced splitting; families should decide who takes leave—the state shouldn't assign roles; flexibility beats uniformity.

options.t: 我主张育假成本由社保共担而非全压企业，否则中小公司不敢招育龄女性，反伤女性就业，保障反而变成就业的枷锁。
options.t_en: I say leave costs should be shared by social insurance, not dumped on firms—or SMEs fear hiring women of childbearing age, hurting them.

options.t: 我倾向给家庭一笔育婴津贴、假由自用，比规定假期更尊重差异、也减轻企业排班压力，让家庭按自身情况做安排。
options.t_en: I prefer a childcare allowance with leave used as the family sees fit—more respectful of difference and easier on employer scheduling.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: New rules would give both parents paid parental leave. Companies worry about labour costs, while some families would rather one parent stayed at home full time. As a citizen representative on the joint human resources and women's federation panel, you must reconcile the different anxieties of employers and families. The interests and principles at stake pull against each other here, and there is no obviously correct answer, only a weighing of priorities in the specific circumstances.

scene: 离婚冷静期制度实施后，部分遭遇家暴的当事人反映难以及时脱身。妇联呼吁增设家暴豁免通道，司法部谨慎评估滥用风险。你是家事法修订的咨询市民，要权衡。，这场争论没有轻易的胜负，每一种选择都附带代价，关键看你认为哪一端的价值更值得优先守护。

options.t: 我支持为家暴受害者开绿色通道、免冷静期，安全压倒程序，不能让制度把人困在危险里，救命比劝和更紧迫。
options.t_en: I support a fast lane waiving the cooling-off period for abuse victims; safety trumps procedure, the system mustn't trap people in danger.

options.t: 我赞成保留冷静期但细化家暴认定与举证，防滥用也不能因噎废食否定其劝和本意，多数冲动离婚确可被缓冲。
options.t_en: I keep the period but refine abuse criteria and proof; prevent abuse without scrapping its reconciling intent over a few cases.

options.t: 我主张全面取消强制冷静期，成年人有离婚自主权，一个月拖延只增加摩擦与额外成本，也方便施暴者转移财产。
options.t_en: I favor scrapping the mandatory period entirely; adults have autonomy over divorce, and a month's delay only adds friction and cost.

options.t: 我认为应配套强制婚姻辅导与儿童权益评估，冷静期才有意义，别只卡时间不解决矛盾，让缓冲真正起到修复作用。
options.t_en: I think it needs mandatory counseling and child-welfare assessment; only then does the cooling period mean something, not just stalling.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Since the divorce cooling-off period came in, some people experiencing domestic violence say they cannot get out in time. The women's federation is calling for an exemption route for domestic abuse cases; the justice ministry is cautiously assessing the risk of it being abused. You are a citizen adviser on the revision of family law, and have to weigh it. There is no easy winner in this argument, every option carries a cost, and the question is which end you think is more worth defending.

scene: 3岁以下托育缺口大，公办普惠还是民办市场的供给路线之争激烈，年轻父母负担沉重。你是托育政策听证会的市民代表，要在政府与市场之间做出明确取舍。，局面里的两难远非一句对错能概括，真正要紧的是厘清自己究竟把哪一方的诉求放在更靠前的位置。

options.t: 我支持公办普惠托育，照护是公共服务，低价可靠才能真减负，不该全丢给市场去定价，幼有所育是政府的本分。
options.t_en: I support public affordable childcare; care is a public service, and only low-cost reliable options truly ease burdens—not market pricing.

options.t: 我倾向放宽准入让民办多办，竞争提质降价，政府只管安全底线与兜底最弱势的群体，其余交给供需自己调节。
options.t_en: I prefer easing entry for private providers; competition lifts quality and lowers price, with government only on safety and the vulnerable.

options.t: 我主张给家庭发托育券、可自选机构，钱跟人走比政府直办更灵活也便于公众监督，把选择权还到父母手里。
options.t_en: I favor childcare vouchers families can spend at any provider; money follows the child—more flexible than state-run and easier to oversee.

options.t: 我认为应鼓励单位与社区办托、邻里互助托育，恢复社区纽带也降成本，不必全依赖机构，人情味本身也是照护。
options.t_en: I think workplaces and neighborhoods should run care, with mutual-aid childcare—reviving community bonds and cutting cost without full institutional reliance.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: The shortage of childcare places for children under three is severe, and the argument over how to supply them is fierce: publicly run affordable care, or a market of private providers. Young parents are carrying a heavy burden either way. You are a citizen representative at the childcare policy hearing, and you have to make a clear choice between the government and the market. The dilemma here cannot be summed up by a single word like right or wrong; what matters is clarifying which side's claims you actually put first.

scene: 独生子女一代面临四位老人照护，长护险试点推广与否引发讨论：子女该扛还是社会共担？传统孝道与现代保障如何相处。你是老龄政策公众座谈的成员，须表态。，面对这类没有明确对错的分歧，不同立场各有其道理，最终如何取舍只能由处在其中的人按自身处境与价值排序去认真掂量。

options.t: 我认为赡养老人是子女本分，孝道不能外包给机构，家庭照护才有温度与真正的尊严，血脉之情机构替代不了。
options.t_en: I see eldercare as children's duty; filial piety can't be outsourced—family care alone carries warmth and dignity.

options.t: 我支持长护险社会共担，独生子女扛不动，用保险分摊才可持续，也解放女性照料者，让孝心不被体力拖垮。
options.t_en: I support social long-term care insurance; only-children can't bear it alone, and pooled insurance is sustainable and frees women caregivers.

options.t: 我主张家庭照护给抵税与津贴、机构照护补一部分，两条腿走路尊重不同家庭的选择，不让尽孝的人反而吃亏。
options.t_en: I favor tax breaks and allowances for family care plus partial subsidies for facilities—two tracks respecting different choices.

options.t: 我反对强行社会化和集中供养，老人愿居家就助其居家，社区上门服务比养老院更合人意，熟悉的家才是安心的归处。
options.t_en: I oppose forced socialization and group homes; help elders age at home if they wish—community visiting care fits people better than institutions.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: The one-child generation faces caring for four elderly parents, and whether to roll out long-term care insurance nationwide is under debate: should children carry it, or should society share it? How should traditional filial duty coexist with modern social protection? As a member of the public panel on ageing policy, you must take a position. On a disagreement with no clear right answer, each stance has its reasons, and those inside the situation can only weigh them against their own circumstances and priorities.

scene: 城郊大型养殖场被曝臭味与粪污直排，环保组织要求关停、养殖户称是生计所系、本地肉价会涨。你是城乡规划听证会的市民代表，要在环境与生计之间权衡。，相关各方的利益与原则在此相互拉扯，并不存在显而易见的标准答案，只能结合具体情境权衡轻重。

options.t: 我支持严管乃至关停违规养殖，环境与健康优先，污染不该由周边居民默默埋单，守得住清水绿地才有宜居城市。
options.t_en: I support strict control or closure of violators; environment and health come first, and neighbors shouldn't pay for the pollution.

options.t: 我反对一刀切关停，应帮养殖户上治污设备、就地改造，保住生计也减污，别只赶走问题而让污染换个地方出现。
options.t_en: I oppose blanket closure; help farmers install treatment and upgrade in place—preserving livelihoods while cutting pollution, not just moving it.

options.t: 我认为根本在少吃肉、减规模，推广植物蛋白，从源头降养殖环境压力，也善待圈养的牲畜，饮食选择也是环保。
options.t_en: I think the root is eating less meat and shrinking scale, promoting plant protein—easing farming's pressure and treating livestock better.

options.t: 我主张把养殖场迁至远离居民区的集约园区、统一治污，用规划疏解而非封堵矛盾，让生产与生活在空间上各得其所。
options.t_en: I propose moving farms to remote intensive-farming parks with unified treatment; planning eases the conflict rather than blocking it.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: A large livestock farm on the edge of the city has been exposed for its smell and for discharging manure straight into the water. Environmental groups want it shut down; the farmers say it is their livelihood and that local meat prices would rise. You are a citizen representative at the urban and rural planning hearing, weighing environment against livelihood. The interests and principles of the parties pull against each other, there is no obviously correct answer, and the balance can only be struck in context.

scene: 某化妆品集团仍用动物做安全性测试，动保组织抵制其产品，公司称部分毒理尚无替代法。你是消费者倡议平台的投票参与者，要决定自己的消费立场与理由。，这场争论没有轻易的胜负，每一种选择都附带代价，关键看你认为哪一端的价值更值得优先守护。

options.t: 我拒绝购买动物测试品，用钱包表态，cruelty-free才是底线，企业该加速寻找替代方案，消费者的选择能推动改变。
options.t_en: I refuse animal-tested products and vote with my wallet; cruelty-free is the floor, and firms should speed up alternatives.

options.t: 我理解企业审慎，安全数据关系人命，全面禁动物测试若牺牲可靠性也不可取，应渐进推进而非一夜之间叫停。
options.t_en: I understand corporate caution; safety data bear on human life, and banning all animal tests at the cost of reliability is unwise—go gradual.

options.t: 我主张立法强制替代法优先、仅限无替代的重大风险才特批动物实验，用规则逼出创新，不让企业以借口拖延转型。
options.t_en: I favor a law mandating alternatives first, with animal tests only for major risks lacking substitutes—using rules to force innovation.

options.t: 我认为政府应资助替代技术研发与互认，别只道德谴责企业，给出可行出路才有实际用处，技术到位了抵制才不必硬扛。
options.t_en: I think government should fund alternative-tech R&D and mutual recognition, not just morally blame firms—give a viable path.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: A cosmetics group still uses animals for safety testing, animal protection groups are boycotting its products, and the company says that for some toxicology there is no alternative method yet. You are a voting participant on a consumer advocacy platform, and you have to decide where you stand as a consumer, and why. There is no easy winner in this argument, and every choice carries a cost; what matters is which end you think is more worth protecting first.

scene: 老旧动物园设施差、动物刻板行为明显，动保组织要求关闭，园方称承担救护与科普职能、贸然关停更伤动物。你是市政公园评议会的市民成员，要给出判断。，局面里的两难远非一句对错能概括，真正要紧的是厘清自己究竟把哪一方的诉求放在更靠前的位置。

options.t: 我支持限期改造或转型为庇护所，动物福利不过关就不该展演，科普不能以囚禁为代价，活生生的痛苦不该被观赏。
options.t_en: I support a deadline to reform or convert to a sanctuary; failing welfare shouldn't exhibit animals, and education can't cost captivity.

options.t: 我反对简单关闭，许多动物已难野放，动物园的救护与公众教育价值应被承认并加以改进，关停不等于动物就更好。
options.t_en: I oppose simple closure; many animals can't be released, and zoos' rescue and educational value deserve recognition and improvement.

options.t: 我主张逐步淘汰表演性展陈、只保留救护与科研，把娱乐功能让位于动物本身的福祉，让动物园回归保护而非表演。
options.t_en: I favor phasing out performative displays, keeping only rescue and research—letting animal welfare outrank entertainment.

options.t: 我认为应由独立动保专家定期评估认证、不达标取消资质，用专业标准代替情绪化的争论，让决策建立在证据之上。
options.t_en: I think independent animal-welfare experts should periodically certify zoos; revoke licenses if substandard—using expertise over emotion.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: The old city zoo has poor facilities and the animals show clear signs of stereotypy. Animal protection groups want it closed; the zoo says it provides rescue and education functions and that closing it abruptly would harm the animals more. As a citizen member of the municipal parks review board, you must give a judgment. The dilemma here cannot be reduced to a question of right or wrong; what matters is being clear about whose claim you place further forward.

scene: 市教育局拟在中小学食堂试点每周一天纯素餐以推广可持续饮食，部分家长担心孩子营养与选择权。你是家校委员会的家长代表，要表达意见并说明关切。，面对这类没有明确对错的分歧，不同立场各有其道理，最终如何取舍只能由处在其中的人按自身处境与价值排序去认真掂量。

options.t: 我支持校园素食日，从小养成低碳饮食习惯利人利地球，营养可由豆类蛋奶来补足，孩子也该懂食物与环境的关联。
options.t_en: I support a school veg day; building low-carbon habits early helps people and planet, with nutrition met by legumes, eggs and dairy.

options.t: 我反对校方替孩子定饮食，餐盘选择应交家庭，推广可持续请走课外倡导而非强制推行，尊重家长对子女的安排权。
options.t_en: I oppose the school dictating kids' diets; the plate should be the family's call—promote sustainability through extracurricular advocacy, not compulsion.

options.t: 我主张提供素食与荤食双选项、不强制，用教育与透明营养标签引导而非下达命令，让习惯在理解中而非强迫中形成。
options.t_en: I favor offering both veg and meat options without mandate, guiding via education and clear nutrition labels rather than orders.

options.t: 我担心统一采购素食增财政与供应链压力，应先试点偏远校、看反馈再定，别搞一刀切，稳妥好过声势浩大的折腾。
options.t_en: I worry uniform veg procurement strains budgets and supply chains; pilot in remote schools first, read feedback, avoid one-size-fits-all.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: The city education bureau plans to pilot one meat-free day a week in primary and secondary school canteens to promote sustainable eating. Some parents worry about their children's nutrition and about the right to choose. You are a parent representative on the school-family committee, and have to give your view and set out your concerns clearly. On a disagreement with no clear right answer, each position has its reasons, and the weighing up can only be done by those inside it.

scene: 北方林区野猪泛滥毁田伤人，林业部门拟开放限额狩猎调控种群，动保人士呼吁避孕与迁徙替代。你是野生动物管理听证的市民代表，须权衡人与兽的边界。，相关各方的利益与原则在此相互拉扯，并不存在显而易见的标准答案，只能结合具体情境权衡轻重。

options.t: 我支持限额狩猎调控，种群失衡已威胁农户生计安全，数量管理是当下最务实的选择，护人也算护住这片山林。
options.t_en: I support quota hunting; the imbalance now threatens farmers' livelihoods and safety, and population control is the pragmatic pick.

options.t: 我反对猎杀，主张投避孕饵与生态廊道引导迁徙，用非致死手段恢复人兽之间的平衡，生命值得我们用更耐心的办法。
options.t_en: I oppose killing; use contraceptive bait and ecological corridors to steer migration, restoring human-wildlife balance by non-lethal means.

options.t: 我主张由受损农户获生态补偿、同时试验避孕，先赔后治，别让百姓独自扛下损失，经济补偿与种群调控可以并行。
options.t_en: I favor compensating affected farmers while piloting contraception—pay first, then treat; don't let citizens alone bear the loss.

options.t: 我认为关键在栖息地修复减少人兽接触，治标猎杀不如治本规划，让野猪有自己生存的空间，人也守住田与安全的底线。
options.t_en: I think the key is habitat restoration to cut human-wildlife contact; symptomatic hunting pales against planning that gives boar their own space.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: Wild boars have proliferated in the northern forest region, damaging fields and injuring people. The forestry department plans to open a limited quota hunt to control the population, while animal protection advocates call for contraception and relocation instead. You are a citizen representative at the wildlife management hearing, and you have to weigh the boundary between people and animals. The interests and principles of the parties involved pull against each other here, and there is no obviously correct answer; the weight can only be judged in context.

scene: 市美术馆计划展出一组讽喻时政的装置作品，部分议员批评其「冒犯公众」要求撤展，馆长坚持艺术自由。你是文化拨款评审的市民代表，要在拨款与内容之间表态。，这场争论没有轻易的胜负，每一种选择都附带代价，关键看你认为哪一端的价值更值得优先守护。

options.t: 我支持照常展出，公共艺术就该容纳刺耳声音，冒犯本身常是思考的起点，审查才是真冒犯，纳税人的钱也该养自由的脑。
options.t_en: I support showing it; public art should hold uncomfortable voices, and offense often starts thought—censorship is the real insult.

options.t: 我反对用公帑为刻意挑衅的作品背书，纳税人的钱不该资助冒犯多数人的表达方式，公共资源应照顾更宽泛的共识。
options.t_en: I oppose public funds backing deliberately provocative work; taxpayer money shouldn't sponsor expression that offends the majority.

options.t: 我主张设明确标识与年龄分区、不撤展，既保表达自由也尊重观展者的自主选择权，让成年人为自己决定是否走近。
options.t_en: I favor clear labeling and age zoning without removal—protecting free expression while respecting viewers' own choices.

options.t: 我认为公共场馆应多元平衡，可同期办传统展对冲，让不同取向的市民各取所需，文化的活力正来自并存而非独尊。
options.t_en: I think public venues should balance diversity—run a traditional show alongside, so different citizens each find what they need.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The city art museum plans to show a set of installations satirising current politics. Some councillors call them offensive to the public and demand that the show be cancelled; the director insists on artistic freedom. As a citizen representative on the cultural grants panel, you must take a position between funding and content. This argument has no easy winner; every choice carries a cost, and what matters is which value you think deserves protecting first.

scene: 老城区一栋有年头的戏院面临拆除改建商场，文保人士力保、开发商称地块闲置低效。你是城市更新委员会的市民成员，要在记忆与效益之间取舍并说明理由。，局面里的两难远非一句对错能概括，真正要紧的是厘清自己究竟把哪一方的诉求放在更靠前的位置。

options.t: 我支持保留并活化老戏院，记忆与美学不可再生，文旅价值长期胜过一次性的商业开发，城市的灵魂藏在老建筑里。
options.t_en: I support preserving and revitalizing the old theater; memory and aesthetics are non-renewable, and cultural-tourism value outlasts one-off development.

options.t: 我倾向拆除改建，闲置地标不产生效益，新商场带来就业与税收更实在也更能拉动经济，旧的不去新的难以来。
options.t_en: I lean toward demolition and rebuild; an idle landmark yields nothing, while a new mall brings jobs and tax—more concrete.

options.t: 我主张修旧如旧改为文化综合体，既保外壳又注商业造血，让保护本身能够养活自己，不必年年靠财政贴钱维养。
options.t_en: I propose restoring it as a cultural complex—keeping the shell while adding commercial self-funding, letting preservation pay for itself.

options.t: 我认为应由居民投票决定地标去留，街坊的记忆不该由远处的资本与官员代为签下，谁天天路过谁才最有发言权。
options.t_en: I think residents should vote on the landmark's fate; the neighborhood's memory shouldn't be signed away by distant capital and officials.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: An old theatre in the historic district faces demolition to make way for a shopping centre. Heritage campaigners are fighting to keep it; the developer says the site is sitting idle and wasted. You are a citizen member of the urban renewal committee, and have to choose between memory and return, and explain why. The dilemma resists a one-line verdict; what matters is being clear about which claim you put first.

scene: 一部基于真实历史的电影因视角敏感被要求删改后才能上映，导演称剪了就失真，观众则立场分裂。你是影视内容审委会的公众观察员，要给出判断与理由。，面对这类没有明确对错的分歧，不同立场各有其道理，最终如何取舍只能由处在其中的人按自身处境与价值排序去认真掂量。

options.t: 我反对为过关而删改历史，记忆不能按当下舒服度裁剪，观众自有基本的判断力，捂住一段往事并不会让它消失。
options.t_en: I oppose cutting history to pass review; memory can't be trimmed to current comfort, and audiences can judge for themselves.

options.t: 我支持必要的尺度把关，避免过度刺激引发对立，艺术自由也该有社会责任的基本边界，自由不等于毫无顾忌。
options.t_en: I support necessary boundary control to avoid sparking confrontation; artistic freedom still has a social-responsibility limit.

options.t: 我主张分级而非删剪，成人向内容标级上映，把选择权交观众而非替所有人定下调子，成年公民能为自己做主。
options.t_en: I favor rating over cutting; release adult content with a rating, handing choice to viewers rather than setting the tone for all.

options.t: 我认为应附创作谈与史料来源让观众自辨，用透明取代修剪，争议反而成公共讨论，越藏越容易被人当成禁忌。
options.t_en: I think attach a director's note and sources so viewers judge; replace trimming with transparency, turning dispute into public debate.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: A film based on real history has been required to cut and revise before release because its angle is considered sensitive. The director says cutting it destroys its truth, and audiences are split. You are a public observer on the film and television content review committee, and you have to give a judgment and your reasons. Faced with a disagreement that has no clear right or wrong, each position has its reasons, and in the end the choice can only be weighed by the people involved, according to their own circumstances and the order of their values.

scene: 西方博物馆藏有本国流失文物，政府正式提出归还请求，馆方以「全球共享、妥善保管」为由婉拒。你是文化遗产论坛的公众代表，要亮明立场并说明依据。，相关各方的利益与原则在此相互拉扯，并不存在显而易见的标准答案，只能结合具体情境权衡轻重。

options.t: 我主张无条件归还，文物是民族记忆的载体，所有权与解释权本就该回到原属的国家，文化根脉不能长期流落他乡。
options.t_en: I demand unconditional return; artifacts carry a nation's memory, and ownership and interpretation belong to the origin country.

options.t: 我反对简单回流，大馆的保存与全球展会让更多人看见，文化本就该是人类共有财富，孤芳自赏反失了文物的意义。
options.t_en: I oppose simple repatriation; great museums preserve and show them globally, and culture is rightfully humanity's common heritage.

options.t: 我主张长期租借与联合策展、共享研究权，既认归属又保可及，折中方案更切实可行，也让研究不因返还而中断。
options.t_en: I favor long-term loans and joint curation with shared research rights—affirming ownership while keeping access; a workable middle.

options.t: 我认为应建本土一流馆舍与数字存档再谈归还，先有本事接得住，别让国宝回来却因条件差再受损伤，准备比情绪重要。
options.t_en: I think we should build top-tier local facilities and digital archives before repatriation—prove we can safeguard them, not risk damage through poor prep.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene_en: A Western museum holds antiquities that were taken from your country, and the government has formally requested their return. The museum has declined, citing global sharing and proper stewardship. As a public representative at the cultural heritage forum, you must state your position and the grounds for it. The interests and principles at stake pull against each other here, and there is no obviously correct answer, only a weighing of priorities in the specific circumstances.

scene: 流媒体冲击下，本国影视配额法案要求平台本土内容占比，创作者叫好、用户嫌选择变少、外资平台抗议。你是传媒规制听证的市民代表，要权衡保护与自由。，这场争论没有轻易的胜负，每一种选择都附带代价，关键看你认为哪一端的价值更值得优先守护。

options.t: 我支持本土配额，文化多样性需政策托底，本国故事与就业不该被外来资本彻底淹没，屏幕上也该有自己的面孔。
options.t_en: I support local quotas; cultural diversity needs policy backing so domestic stories and jobs aren't drowned by foreign capital.

options.t: 我反对强制比例，观众用脚投票，好内容自然会赢，配额只会养出受保护之下的平庸，市场比文件更懂观众。
options.t_en: I oppose forced ratios; audiences vote with their feet, good content wins, and quotas only breed protected mediocrity.

options.t: 我主张用补贴激励本土创作而非限外，把钱投向编剧与新人，比设门槛更治本也更公平，好作品多了自然有人看。
options.t_en: I favor subsidizing local creation over restricting imports—fund writers and newcomers, which addresses roots better than thresholds.

options.t: 我认为配额可设但需定期复审、随产业成熟退场，别让临时保护变成永久的壁垒，扶持该有退出的一天。
options.t_en: I think quotas are okay but need periodic review and phase-out as the industry matures—don't let temporary protection become a permanent wall.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene_en: Under pressure from streaming, a domestic content quota bill would require platforms to carry a minimum share of local film and television. Creators are cheering; users complain their choices will shrink; foreign platforms are protesting. You are a citizen representative at the media regulation hearing, weighing protection against freedom. There is no easy winner in this argument, every option carries a cost, and the question is which end you think is more worth defending.

scene: 女子组赛事中跨性别女选手参赛资格引争议，体育界在公平与包容间拉扯，各协会规则不一。你是国家奥委会公众咨询的成员，要表达立场并讲清边界。，局面里的两难远非一句对错能概括，真正要紧的是厘清自己究竟把哪一方的诉求放在更靠前的位置。

options.t: 我支持按现行医学阈值审慎准入，包容不应被牺牲，但须有可核验的生理标准防不公，让规则站在科学与公道一边。
options.t_en: I support careful entry by current medical thresholds; inclusion shouldn't be sacrificed, but verifiable physiological standards prevent unfairness.

options.t: 我主张按出生性别分组，生理优势难靠声明抹平，保证生理女性选手的公平竞争权利，公平是竞技不可退的底线。
options.t_en: I favor grouping by birth sex; physiological advantage isn't erased by declaration, protecting cis-female athletes' fair-competition right.

options.t: 我建议设公开组与女性组并行，让所有人有赛道，把争议从『谁该被排除』转为多选项，包容与公平可以都给空间。
options.t_en: I suggest parallel open and women's divisions so everyone has a lane, shifting the debate from 'who to exclude' to more choices.

options.t: 我认为各项目差异大，应交由国际单项联合会按项目定规，国家别抢跑搞一刀切，游泳与举重的生理影响本就不同。
options.t_en: I think sports differ widely; let each international federation set rules per event—the state shouldn't rush a one-size-fits-all.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene_en: The eligibility of transgender women athletes to compete in women's events has caused controversy. The sports world is pulled between fairness and inclusion, and the rules of different federations do not agree. You are a member of the national Olympic committee's public consultation, and you have to state your position and set out where the boundary lies. The dilemma here cannot be summed up by a single word like right or wrong; what matters is clarifying which side's claims you actually put first.

scene: 大学体育联盟讨论是否允许运动员凭姓名肖像权接商业代言并分赛事收入，校方担心冲击学业与业余传统。你是校务听证的学生代表，要给出态度与理由。，面对这类没有明确对错的分歧，不同立场各有其道理，最终如何取舍只能由处在其中的人按自身处境与价值排序去认真掂量。

options.t: 我支持运动员变现自身价值，凭本事赚的钱不该被学校与联盟截留，也是公平的劳动回报，汗水换来的不该归别人。
options.t_en: I support athletes monetizing themselves; money earned by skill shouldn't be skimmed by schools and leagues—fair pay for labor.

options.t: 我反对过度商业化，学生运动员先读书，奖学金已是回报，代言会扭曲校园体育的初心，读书人别先成了商品。
options.t_en: I oppose over-commercialization; student-athletes study first, scholarships are the return, and endorsements distort campus sport's purpose.

options.t: 我主张设收入上限与学业门槛，可变现但防被经纪资本裹挟，保住学生身份的底线，赚钱不能压过求学这条主线。
options.t_en: I favor an income cap and academic bar—monetize but avoid capture by agent capital, keeping the student status intact.

options.t: 我认为应由运动员集体谈判分成、收益反哺球队与设施，比个人散接更可持续，也让没代言的队友间接受益。
options.t_en: I think athletes should collectively bargain a share, with proceeds funding teams and facilities—more sustainable than scattered deals.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene_en: The university sports league is debating whether to let athletes take commercial endorsements on their name and image and share in event revenue; the university worries about the impact on study and the amateur tradition. As a student representative at the campus hearing, you must state your view and your reasons. On a disagreement with no clear right answer, each stance has its reasons, and those inside the situation can only weigh them against their own circumstances and priorities.

scene: 国际赛前，几名运动员以单膝下跪方式就社会不公表达立场，组委会担忧政治化、部分观众要求禁赛。你是赛事纪律委员会的公众观察员，须权衡两端。，相关各方的利益与原则在此相互拉扯，并不存在显而易见的标准答案，只能结合具体情境权衡轻重。

options.t: 我支持运动员在场上有节制地表达立场，体育从不是无菌区，沉默才是真正的反常，让赛场也容得下良知。
options.t_en: I support athletes expressing views on-field with restraint; sport was never aseptic, and silence would be the anomaly.

options.t: 我反对赛场政治化，看比赛就该看比赛，诉求请走场外渠道，别绑架观众与整场赛事，竞技的纯粹值得被守护。
options.t_en: I oppose politicizing the arena; watch sport for sport—take grievances off-field, don't hijack spectators and the event.

options.t: 我主张赛前赛后允许、比赛中止仪式禁烟，划清表达时段保竞技纯粹也留足空间，规矩清楚大家都不委屈。
options.t_en: I favor allowing expression before/after but not during play or anthems—marking times that keep competition pure yet leave room.

options.t: 我认为应由运动员工会与组委会谈成行为准则，行业自管胜过外部的硬性禁令，自己人定的规矩才服众也服管。
options.t_en: I think the players' union and organizers should negotiate a conduct code; self-regulation beats external bans.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene_en: Before an international competition, several athletes take a knee to take a stand on social injustice. The organising committee worries about politicisation, and some spectators want them banned. You are the public observer on the event's disciplinary committee, and have to weigh both ends. The interests and principles of the parties pull against each other, there is no obviously correct answer, and the balance can only be struck by weighing what matters in the specific situation.

scene: 反兴奋剂新规拟对个人无过错也追责的「严格责任」扩围，运动员喊冤说难防被人下套，律所赞其威慑力。你是反兴奋剂听证会的市民代表，要亮明态度。，这场争论没有轻易的胜负，每一种选择都附带代价，关键看你认为哪一端的价值更值得优先守护。

options.t: 我支持严格责任扩围，干净比赛靠强威慑，个人疏忽也该担责才能护住多数诚实的选手，姑息一次就毁掉信任。
options.t_en: I support expanding strict liability; clean sport needs strong deterrence, and personal negligence must answer to protect honest athletes.

options.t: 我反对无过错也重罚，程序正义不能丢，被人构陷就该有自证清白的通道而非一律担罪，无辜者不该陪绑。
options.t_en: I oppose punishing the faultless; procedural justice matters, and the framed must have a path to prove innocence, not blanket guilt.

options.t: 我主张区分故意与过失，故意重罚、过失教育加短期禁赛，分级才显出真正的公平，板子该打在有意作弊者身上。
options.t_en: I favor splitting intent from negligence—harsh for deliberate, education plus short ban for accidental; tiers show fairness.

options.t: 我认为应砸钱升级检测与供应链溯源技术，从源头堵住而非只事后严惩运动员本人，治本比拿选手开刀更负责任。
options.t_en: I think we should fund better testing and supply-chain tracing tech, blocking at the source rather than only punishing athletes after.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene_en: A new anti-doping rule proposes widening strict liability, so that individuals are held responsible even where they were not at fault. Athletes protest that they cannot guard against being set up, while law firms praise the deterrent effect. You are a citizen representative at the anti-doping hearing, and you have to make your stance clear. There is no easy winner in this argument, and every choice carries a cost; what matters is which end you think is more worth protecting first.

scene: 市政府欲出资新建大型专业球场，主办队承诺带火城市，反对者说纳税人钱该投学校医院。你是市政预算听证的市民代表，要在地标与民生之间取舍。，局面里的两难远非一句对错能概括，真正要紧的是厘清自己究竟把哪一方的诉求放在更靠前的位置。

options.t: 我支持建馆，赛事经济与城市名片长远赚得回来，文体活力也是市民幸福感的一部分，生活会因此更有滋味。
options.t_en: I support building it; event economy and city branding pay back long-term, and cultural vitality is part of citizens' wellbeing.

options.t: 我反对用公帑补贴球队老板，学校医院更急，体育场馆请走市场化融资而非纳税人埋单，民生优先于面子工程。
options.t_en: I oppose public cash subsidizing team owners; schools and hospitals are urgent—let stadiums use market financing, not taxpayers.

options.t: 我主张公私合营、限定赛后向公众开放为健身空间，确保全民可用才值得出这笔钱，球场不该赛后大门紧锁。
options.t_en: I favor public-private partnership with mandated post-event public access as fitness space; only then is public spending worth it.

options.t: 我认为应先修缮社区小场馆普惠大众，别总追地标大工程，普通人的运动权更该优先，楼下的球场比远处的馆更亲民。
options.t_en: I think fix neighborhood small venues for the many first; stop chasing landmark mega-projects—ordinary people's right to sport comes first.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene_en: The city government wants to fund a new large purpose-built stadium, and the home team promises to put the city on the map; opponents say taxpayers' money should go to schools and hospitals. As a citizen representative at the municipal budget hearing, you must choose between a landmark and basic services. The dilemma here cannot be reduced to a question of right or wrong; what matters is being clear about whose claim you place further forward.

scene: 你所在街道计划利用一处闲置的二层小楼改建社区嵌入式养老院，方便辖区内失能半失能老人就近照护。公示一出，楼下几户低层住户担心夜间救护车频繁进出、老人活动噪音扰民，联名反对；而不少独居老人子女则强烈支持，认为这是雪中送炭。街道必须在居民生活安宁与养老刚需之间做出艰难取舍，双方都觉得自己有理，矛盾一时难以调和。

options.t: 我认为养老是公共福利，政府应出资把闲置公房改建成普惠性养老院，优先保障低收入失能老人，在这件事上公共责任应当优先于个别住户的安静偏好。
options.t_en: I see elder care as a public good; the government should fund converting idle public buildings into affordable nursing homes, prioritizing low-income disabled seniors—public duty should come before a few residents' quiet preferences.

options.t: 我倾向引入民营养老机构市场化运营，用服务收费覆盖成本，政府只做资质与质量监管，不要把财政补贴拿去挤占其他更紧迫的民生支出。
options.t_en: I prefer market-run private nursing homes funded by service fees, with government only licensing and supervising—don't let subsidies crowd out other urgent welfare spending.

options.t: 长辈养老终究要靠儿女，我更支持以家庭照护为主、社区提供上门辅助，不该把老人集中送去机构，亲情的陪伴比再好的硬件设施都更重要。
options.t_en: Elder care ultimately falls on children; I favor family care with community in-home support rather than warehousing seniors in institutions—family companionship matters more than facilities.

options.t: 我尊重养老需求，但反对在居民楼下强建养老院，涉及房产价值与生活安宁的业主应有否决权，公共利益的需求不能凌驾于既有住户的合法权利之上。
options.t_en: I respect the need for care, but oppose forcing a nursing home below residents' homes; owners whose property and peace are affected deserve a veto—need cannot override existing residents' rights.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Your subdistrict plans to convert an empty two-storey building into a small care home embedded in the neighbourhood, so that frail and semi-frail elderly residents nearby can be looked after close to home. Once the notice went up, several households on the lower floors signed a joint objection, worried about ambulances coming and going at night and about the noise of activities; the children of many people living alone strongly support it as help at exactly the right moment. The subdistrict has to make a hard choice between residents' quiet and the need for care, both sides feel they are right, and the conflict will not be reconciled quickly.

scene: 人社部推进养老保险全国统筹，用结余较多省份的资金调剂填补收不抵支地区。沿海务工大省不少缴费人说自己缴的钱被拿去补了别处，心里不平衡；而人口流出、基金穿底的省份则盼着中央调剂救命。这牵动钱该留给本地人还是全国共济的深层争论，地方利益与全国公平正面碰撞。

options.t: 我支持全国统筹，养老是国民共济，发达地区反哺欠发达地区天经地义，这样能缩小区域鸿沟、守住全体老人底线公平，不能只顾一地一域。
options.t_en: I support national pooling; pension is national solidarity, and prosperous regions repaying less-fortunate ones is right—it narrows regional gaps and upholds baseline fairness for all elders.

options.t: 我反对，谁缴费谁受益，本省结余应先保本地退休人，强行抽调取走等于变相惩罚多缴费地区，会挫伤发达省份参保人的积极性。
options.t_en: I oppose it; those who pay should benefit. A province's surplus should protect its own retirees first—forced transfers effectively punish high-contributing regions and dampen enthusiasm.

options.t: 我主张根本改革，逐步提高退休年龄并做实个人账户，靠制度自身可持续运行，而不是靠东挪西补式的调剂来掩盖结构性缺口。
options.t_en: I favor structural reform: gradually raise retirement age and fully fund individual accounts, making the system self-sustaining rather than robbing Peter to pay Paul.

options.t: 我更看重家庭与社区互助养老，少些集中统筹，多扶持社区日间照料中心，让养老回归就近的共同体，也减轻远距离制度运转的成本。
options.t_en: I value family and community mutual-aid elder care; less central pooling, more support for neighborhood day-care so care returns to local communities and cuts long-distance costs.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene_en: The ministry of human resources is advancing national pooling of pension insurance, using surplus funds from wealthier provinces to fill the gap in regions that cannot cover their payments. Many contributors in the coastal provinces with large migrant workforces say the money they paid in is being taken to subsidize somewhere else, and they feel it is unfair. Provinces with shrinking populations and depleted funds are counting on central transfers to stay afloat. This touches the deeper argument over whether the money should stay with local people or be shared nationwide, and local interests collide head-on with national fairness.

scene: 单位里57岁的老周身体尚可但岗位早已边缘化，新出台的渐进式延迟退休方案要求他再多干三年。年轻同事担心老人占着位子、晋升通道更堵；老周自己则怕收入断档、也怕被当成累赘。如何平衡代际流动与个体生计，成为单位里讳莫如深的争议焦点。

options.t: 我支持延迟退休，人均寿命延长、基金压力大，渐进式延退是国际惯例，而且应当允许弹性自愿选择，让身体好、有意愿的人多干几年。
options.t_en: I support delayed retirement; longer life expectancy and fund pressure make gradual postponement standard practice, and it should allow flexible voluntary choice for willing, healthy workers.

options.t: 我反对一刀切延退，蓝领体力劳动者本就吃不消，应当分工种区别对待，并且保障提前病退通道，不能让干不动的人硬撑到法定年龄。
options.t_en: I oppose one-size-fits-all delay; manual workers can't cope and need job-specific treatment plus a guaranteed early disability-retirement path, not being forced to endure.

options.t: 我主张用市场激励而非强制，给延退者加发养老金、给接纳的企业发补贴，让供需双方自然调节，比行政命令更能被各方接受。
options.t_en: I prefer market incentives over compulsion: extra pension for delaying workers and subsidies for employers, letting supply and demand adjust naturally.

options.t: 我更希望发展银发再就业与志愿服务，让老人以非全职方式贡献经验，既保住尊严又给年轻人腾出晋升空间，自然完成代际交接。
options.t_en: I'd rather develop senior re-employment and volunteering, letting elders contribute experience part-time—preserving dignity while opening mobility for the young.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene_en: Old Zhou at the office is fifty-seven, still in reasonable health, but his post was sidelined long ago. The newly announced phased delay of retirement means he must work three more years. Younger colleagues worry that older staff are holding posts and blocking promotion; Zhou himself fears a gap in income and being seen as a burden. How to balance generational mobility and individual livelihood has become a subject no one at the office will discuss openly.
