The bloc's scale would boost overall exports, but model forecasts show the assembler's domestic market share falling from 40% to 25% as competitors enter, with 30,000 concentrated job losses in one industrial city. Negotiators warn there is no option to join later on the same terms.

options.t: 我会加入该集团：通过再培训和迁岗支持来消化整体收益的成本，对国家而言比留在这个规模的市场之外更划算。
options.t_en: I would join the bloc: spreading the overall gains through retraining and relocation support is cheaper for the country than staying outside a market this size.

options.t: 我会选择不加入：失去这家企业会掏空整座工业城市，任何贸易统计数据都补偿不了一个社区。
options.t_en: I would stay out: losing the assembler would hollow out a whole industrial city, and no trade statistic compensates a community for that.

options.t: 我会以谈成十年保护期让本土企业留在本土市场为前提加入，用一部分集团红利换调整时间。
options.t_en: I would join only with a negotiated ten-year carve-out protecting the assembler's home market, trading some of the bloc's benefits for adjustment time.

options.t: 我会选择加入，并把预计节省的关税转化为直接发给受影响城市居民的公民红利。
options.t_en: I would join and put the projected tariff savings into a citizens' dividend paid to the affected city's residents directly.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene: 某国福利部的资金只够推进一项旗舰改革：要么向每位成年居民发放普惠月度现金，要么把最底层 20% 收入者的定向补助翻倍。精算模型显示，普惠方案能降低 8% 的极端贫困并大幅缓解中产焦虑；定向翻倍能削减 19% 的极端贫困，但会带来污名化和官僚审查。你为部长提供建议。
scene_en: A national welfare ministry has funding for one flagship reform: a universal monthly payment to every adult resident, or a doubling of targeted benefits for the bottom 20% of earners. Actuaries model that the universal payment reduces extreme poverty by 8% and middle-class anxiety substantially; the targeted doubling cuts extreme poverty by 19% but adds stigma and bureaucratic screening. You advise the minister.

options.t: 我会选普惠发放：没有财产审查的机器，没有窗口前的羞辱，每位公民在体系中持有同样的份额。
options.t_en: I would pick the universal payment: no means-testing machinery, no stigma at the counter, and every citizen holds the same stake in the system.

options.t: 我会选定向翻倍：钱是固定的，就要先救最深的贫困，哪怕要填表排队。
options.t_en: I would pick the targeted doubling: with fixed money, the deepest poverty first, even at the cost of forms and queues.

options.t: 我会在两个省做五年随机对照试点，两者并行，让实测结果来决定全国推广。
options.t_en: I would run both as a five-year randomized pilot in two provinces and let the measured outcomes decide the national rollout.

options.t: 我会选普惠发放，但对中位收入以上部分渐进征税回收，既保住底线又不建官僚机器。
options.t_en: I would pick the universal payment but tax it back progressively above the median income, keeping the floor without the bureaucracy.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene: 银行拒绝了两兄妹的房贷申请——他们轮班全职照顾卧床的母亲，因为两人都没有工资收入。目前的立法提案是设立照护工作积分，让无薪的家庭照护在社保体系中计为可累积养老金的应税收入。保险公司警告道德风险与造假，照护者协会则称这是对早已存在的工作的迟到认可。你是立法委员会成员。
scene_en: A bank refuses a mortgage application from two siblings who care for their bedridden mother full-time in shifts, because neither has payroll income. The proposal on the table: legislate care-work credits that make unpaid family caregiving count as pensionable, taxed income for social-insurance purposes. Insurers warn of moral hazard and fraud; caregiver associations call it the overdue recognition of work that already exists. You sit on the legislative committee.

options.t: 我会立法设立积分：养老金体系是围绕工资岗位设计的，把全职照护者排除在外，等于无声地惩罚一种完整的家庭形态。
options.t_en: I would legislate the credits: pension systems were built around payroll jobs, and excluding full-time caregivers quietly punishes an entire form of family.

options.t: 我会反对提案，改为扩大现金照护津贴：用固定津贴承认照护是诚实的，伪造工资类别只会招来造假。
options.t_en: I would oppose it and expand the cash care allowance instead: valuing care through a flat allowance is honest, while fake payroll categories invite fraud.

options.t: 我会立法设积分，但上限按兼职费率封顶并要求定期入户评估，把成本控制在范围内。
options.t_en: I would legislate the credits but cap them at part-time rates and require periodic home assessments, keeping the cost bounded.

options.t: 我会把同样的钱用于资助专业上门照护服务，让家人保住工作、把护理部分委托出去。
options.t_en: I would fund professional home-care services with the same money instead, so families can keep jobs and delegate the nursing part.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene: 某国仅存的三家海豚馆面临一项禁令提案：禁止圈养大型海洋哺乳动物，设十年过渡期——动物迁往海岸庇护所，员工转岗，国家补偿运营方。客流数据显示这些场馆每年让数百万儿童接触海洋生物；兽医团体指出部分物种的圈养寿命短于野外。你为委员会起草建议。
scene_en: A country's last three dolphinaria face a proposed ban on keeping large marine mammals, with a ten-year transition: animals move to coastal sanctuaries, staff retrain, and the state compensates the operators. Attendance data show the parks introduce millions of children to marine biology annually; vet groups note captive lifespans for some species are shorter than in the wild. You draft the committee recommendation.

options.t: 我会支持禁令及过渡安排：为了公众教育而把大范围活动的动物留在水池里，是把新奇感置于福利之上。
options.t_en: I would back the ban with the transition: keeping wide-ranging animals in tanks for the sake of public education prices wonder over welfare.

options.t: 我会反对禁令：教育覆盖面是真实收益，福利可以通过强制执行的池体面积标准来提高。
options.t_en: I would oppose the ban: the educational reach is real, and welfare can be raised through enforced enclosure-size standards instead.

options.t: 我会立即禁止繁育和新捕捞，同时让现有动物在升级后的设施中安度余生，让场馆逐步关闭。
options.t_en: I would ban breeding and new captures immediately while letting existing animals live out their lives in upgraded facilities, closing the parks gradually.

options.t: 我会把补贴转投免费的沿海庇护所和虚拟现实项目，保留教育、终结圈养。
options.t_en: I would redirect the subsidies to free coastal sanctuaries and virtual-reality programs, keeping the education and ending the captivity.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene: 国家艺术委员会的预算是固定的。现行公式把 70% 拨给两家旗舰机构：歌剧院和国家博物馆——票房远不能覆盖成本，但访客量最大。改革提案会把旗舰拨款上限压到 40%，其余以小额资助分发给社区剧团、合唱团和独立艺术家，单笔资助的监管相应减少。
scene_en: The national arts council's budget is fixed. Under the current formula, 70% goes to the two flagship institutions: the opera house and the national museum, whose ticket sales cover little of their costs but whose visitor numbers are the largest. A reform proposal would cap flagship funding at 40% and distribute the rest through small grants to neighborhood troupes, community choirs, and independent artists, with far less oversight per grant.

options.t: 我会维持旗舰份额：承载经典、吸引大众的机构才是公共艺术资助正当性的来源。
options.t_en: I would keep the flagship share: institutions that carry the canon and draw the crowds are what justify public arts funding at all.

options.t: 我会采纳再分配方案：一千个小舞台比两座殿堂培养出更多实践中的艺术家，文化就活在人们创造它的地方。
options.t_en: I would adopt the redistribution: a thousand small stages produce more practicing artists than two temples, and culture lives where people make it.

options.t: 我会把旗舰上限设为 40%，但要求小额资助经过公开的艺术评审，既守住质量标准又不搞中央计划。
options.t_en: I would cap flagships at 40% but require the small grants to pass a published artistic-jury review, keeping quality standards without central planning.

options.t: 我会把整个委员会转为配比资助模式：公共资金只用来放大私人捐款，让市场约束每一笔拨款。
options.t_en: I would move the whole council to matching-grant mode: public money only multiplies private donations, so the market disciplines every grant.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene: 某国际田径联合会须为女子 400 米定规则。其科学小组报告：某一类运动员因一种先天特征，平均保有约 3 秒的优势，任何训练都无法消除。可选方案：保持该组别开放、设定明确的激素或测量阈值，或增设一个所有人皆可参加的公开组。律师警告任何阈值都会引发诉讼，中游运动员则追问这对他们的公平意味着什么。
scene_en: An international athletics federation must set a rule for its women's 400m after its science panel reports that one category of athletes, by a natural trait, holds an average advantage of about 3 seconds that no training removes. The options: leave the category open, require a defined hormone or measurement threshold, or create an additional open category in which everyone may compete. Lawyers warn any threshold will be litigated; athletes from the middle of the pack ask what fairness means for them.

options.t: 我会保持组别开放：身体本就有差异，围绕先天特征画法律界线，等于让体育联合会的业务变成审查女性身体。
options.t_en: I would leave the category open: bodies vary, and drawing legal lines around natural traits puts sports federations in the business of policing women's bodies.

options.t: 我会采纳一个连同底层数据一起公开的明确阈值：组别存在的意义是让竞争成立，透明的界线胜过无边的优势。
options.t_en: I would adopt a defined threshold published with the underlying data: categories exist to keep competition meaningful, and a transparent line beats open-ended advantage.

options.t: 我会增设公开组并保留女子组，让每位运动员都有赛道，也无人被排除在纪录之外。
options.t_en: I would add the open category and keep the women's category as is, giving every athlete a lane without excluding anyone from the record books.

options.t: 我会不改变参赛资格，把联合会资金转投到实测优势最小的项目上，让参与度自行调整。
options.t_en: I would leave eligibility alone and shift the federation's money into the events where measured advantages are smallest, letting participation respond on its own.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene: 某地区 65 岁以上居民占 22%，必须扩大养老服务。方案 A：认证并补贴用于搬抬、监测和陪伴的护理机器人，成本为人工照护时薪的一半。方案 B：用公共资金培训并雇佣 8000 名新增人类照护员。家庭反映的最大问题是孤独感，工会则反驳称老年照护的机器人化会开一个蔓延开来的先例。你负责撰写地区规划。
scene_en: A region with 22% of residents over 65 must scale up elder care. Option A: certify and subsidize care robots for lifting, monitoring, and companionship, at half the cost of human care hours. Option B: train and employ 8,000 additional human caregivers with public funds. Families report loneliness as the top complaint; unions counter that a robot workforce in eldercare sets a precedent that spreads. You write the regional plan.

options.t: 我会推广机器人：一半的成本让覆盖的老人翻倍，持续监测也能发现每日两次家访发现不了的跌倒。
options.t_en: I would scale the robots: half-cost coverage doubles the number of elders reached, and monitoring catches falls a twice-daily visit cannot.

options.t: 我会雇佣照护员：这里最难治疗的状况是孤独，只有愿意留下来聊天的人能治它。
options.t_en: I would hire the caregivers: loneliness is the condition hardest to treat here, and only a person who stays to talk treats it.

options.t: 我会资助机器人做搬抬和监测，但要求饮食与陪伴必须由人来完成，按各自擅长分工。
options.t_en: I would fund robots for lifting and monitoring but require human hours for meals and companionship, splitting the tasks by what each does well.

options.t: 我会把资金直接发给家庭作为照护预算，由每个家庭自己购买机器人、服务和工时的组合。
options.t_en: I would give families the money directly as a care budget and let each household buy the mix of robots, services, and hours it prefers.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene: 某州议会辩论将小额消费贷款利率上限设为年化 12%，而目前市场边缘利率从 30% 到 400% 不等。限利支持者举出每年落入催收的 4 万户家庭；放贷方和一些经济学家回应称，有约束力的上限会恰好切断银行拒贷人群的正规信贷，把他们推向非正规渠道。你握有委员会的决定性一票。
scene_en: A state parliament debates capping interest on small consumer loans at 12% APR, where the current market runs from 30% to 400% at the fringe. The cap's supporters cite the 40,000 households that fall into collections each year; lenders and some economists respond that a binding cap removes credit from exactly the borrowers banks refuse, pushing them to informal lenders. You hold the committee's deciding vote.

options.t: 我会投赞成票：靠借款人失败赚钱的产品不是值得保护的市场结果，非正规放贷的担忧可以用发照和执法来应对。
options.t_en: I would vote for the cap: a product that profits when borrowers fail is not a market outcome to protect, and the informal-lender fear can be met with licensing and enforcement.

options.t: 我会投反对票：成年人应当有为自己的风险定价的自由，取缔合法供给并不会消灭需求。
options.t_en: I would vote against the cap: adults must be free to price their own risk, and banning the legal supply does not delete the demand.

options.t: 我会把上限设在 36% 并配套发照制度，在边缘市场与全面禁止之间取道。
options.t_en: I would set the cap at 36% with a licensing regime, threading between the fringe market and full exclusion.

options.t: 我不设上限，改为出资建立按成本放贷的州立信用社，用竞争而非禁令挤压边缘市场。
options.t_en: I would skip the cap and fund a state credit union offering small loans at cost, competing the fringe down instead of banning it.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene: 河谷建坝提案：一座水电站将为全国提供 9% 的电力，运行零排放、寿命 80 年，但将淹没 60 平方公里森林、两座村庄，以及一条滋养下游渔业的洄游鱼道。建模的替代方案：四倍土地面积的光伏和风电加储能，成本 1.6 倍，建设期多十年。能源部请你给出建议。
scene_en: A river valley proposal: a hydro dam that would supply 9% of the country's electricity with zero operating emissions for 80 years, but submerge 60 square kilometers of forest, two villages, and a fish migration route that feeds downstream fisheries. Alternatives modeled: four times the land covered in solar and wind plus storage, at 1.6 times the cost and a decade longer to build. The energy ministry asks your recommendation.

options.t: 我会支持建坝：80 年稳定的零排放电力重于土地损失，村庄可以通过补偿搬迁解决。
options.t_en: I would build the dam: firm zero-emission power for 80 years outweighs the land loss, and the villages can be relocated with compensation.

options.t: 我会否决大坝并资助光伏-风电-储能路径：被淹没的河谷无法复原，差价就是保住它的真实成本。
options.t_en: I would reject the dam and fund the solar-wind-storage path: a flooded valley cannot be un-flooded, and the price difference is the real cost of keeping it.

options.t: 我会把大坝缩小为无大型水库的径流式设计，接受更低的出力以保住河谷与村庄。
options.t_en: I would downsize the dam to a run-of-river design without a large reservoir, accepting lower output to keep the valley and villages.

options.t: 我会建坝，并从第一天起就把下游渔业和搬迁家庭的补偿作为其收入的永久性 levy（专项税）列支。
options.t_en: I would build the dam and earmark a permanent levy on its revenue for the downstream fisheries and the displaced families, priced in from day one.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene: 某地区 15% 居民的母语是少数民族语言，正辩论一项语言法案：官方双语标识、贯穿十二年级的少数民族语言学校教育，以及面向流利使用者的公务员招录加分。预算部门标出成本，使用者的祖辈还记得学校里曾全面禁用该语言的年代。反对者质问为何他们的税款要为一种自己不会说的语言买单。你为起草委员会提供咨询。
scene_en: A region where 15% of residents speak a minority language as their mother tongue debates a language act: official bilingual signage, minority-language schooling through grade 12, and civil-service hiring preferences for fluent speakers. Budget offices flag the cost; speakers' grandparents recall a period when the language was banned outright in schools. Opponents ask why their taxes fund a language they do not speak. You advise the drafting committee.

options.t: 我会全案通过：一门语言失去学校就失去一代人，事后再补救的成本远高于双语标识。
options.t_en: I would pass the act in full: a language that loses its schools loses a generation, and repairing that later costs far more than signage does.

options.t: 我会资助学校但不设招录加分：语言传承需要的是教育，而招聘配额是按语言而非能力分配岗位。
options.t_en: I would fund the schools but not the hiring preferences: education is what transmission needs, while hiring quotas hand out positions by language rather than merit.

options.t: 我会把法案限定为由使用该语言的市镇自费提供的自愿双语服务，把选择权和账单都留在当地。
options.t_en: I would limit the act to voluntary bilingual services funded by the minority-language municipalities themselves, keeping the choice and the bill local.

options.t: 我会通过法案，并附加年度公开报告跟踪学校注册与公务员录用数据，让政策的真实效果被测出来而非被假设。
options.t_en: I would pass the act and add an annual public report on school enrollment and civil-service uptake, so the policy's real effect is measured, not assumed.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene: 一家 1200 人的会计师事务所收到员工理事会请求：全薪试行四天工作制。合伙人模型的预测两极分化——要么营收下滑 4%，要么生产率提升 10%，完全取决于会议与交接流程如何重构。两家各占营收五分之一的客户已放话：响应变慢就转移账户。你是董事会成员，必须做出决定。
scene_en: A 1,200-person accountancy firm is asked by its staff council to trial a four-day week at full pay. The partners' model predicts either a 4% revenue dip or a 10% productivity gain, depending entirely on how meetings and handovers are redesigned. Two clients, each a fifth of revenue, have already said they will move accounts if response times slip. You sit on the board and must decide.

options.t: 我会批准为期一年的试行并配套流程重构项目：如果生产率机制是真的，数据会证明，而人才争夺的成本已经计入。
options.t_en: I would approve the one-year trial with the redesign program attached: if the productivity mechanism is real, the data will show it, and the war for staff is already priced in.

options.t: 我会婉拒并改提四天压缩 40 小时方案：同样的工时、同样的客户覆盖，不拿公司五分之一的营收做实验。
options.t_en: I would decline and offer a compressed 40-hour four-day option instead: same hours, same client coverage, no revenue experiment with a fifth of the firm at stake.

options.t: 我会只在一家 150 人的办公室试行，按实测结果扩面，让两家锚定客户完全不受实验影响。
options.t_en: I would run the trial in one 150-person office only and expand by measured results, protecting the two anchor clients from any experiment.

options.t: 我会不试验直接永久推行：知识工作者实际的有效工作日本就不足四天，假装不是这样只是让日历虚胖。
options.t_en: I would approve it permanently without a trial: knowledge workers already average fewer than four productive days, and pretending otherwise just pads calendars.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene: 一家拥有 2.5 万名骑手的外卖平台将所有人归为独立承包商。一项法案草案将强制改为雇员身份，配送成本增加 19%：平台模型预测骑手名额减少 4000 个，但余下的人获得最低工资保障、病假和工伤覆盖。骑手自己的调查也分裂：55% 最看重灵活自由，45% 报告扣除车辆成本后收入低于最低工资。你是上议院议员。
scene_en: A delivery platform with 25,000 couriers classifies them all as independent contractors. A draft law would force reclassification as employees, adding 19% to delivery costs: platform modeling predicts 4,000 fewer courier slots but guaranteed minimum pay, sick leave, and injury coverage for the rest. Couriers themselves split in surveys: 55% value the flexibility above all, 45% report earnings below minimum wage after vehicle costs. You sit in the upper house.

options.t: 我会投改籍赞成票：一种把工伤成本留给骑手的利润模式，等于用身体支付的补贴。
options.t_en: I would vote for reclassification: a business model whose margin exists because injury costs sit with the courier is a subsidy paid by bodies.

options.t: 我会投反对票：强制雇员身份会删掉一半骑手为它而来的随叫随到的自由。
options.t_en: I would vote against it: forcing employment status deletes the on-demand schedule that half the couriers chose this work for.

options.t: 我会立法设立第三种身份：按平台工时累积的可携带保障，但不设固定班次、不赋予雇主排班权。
options.t_en: I would legislate a third status: portable benefits accruing per platform hour worked, without fixed shifts or an employer's scheduling power.

options.t: 我会强制规定每单最低收入和工伤保险，但保留承包商身份，修补最坏的后果而不重组整个行业。
options.t_en: I would mandate minimum per-delivery earnings and injury insurance while leaving the contractor status untouched, fixing the worst outcomes without reorganizing the industry.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene: 在某国家庭补习成风，调查显示最高收入十分位家庭在补习上的支出是最低十分位家庭的 9 倍，持续扩大考试分数差距，政府起草法案禁止营利性学科补习。执法难题摆在眼前：在可比司法辖区，家长和补习老师几周内就找到了变通办法。教育部长问：国家是否应当限制家庭的消费选择。
scene_en: A country where private tutoring is a national obsession drafts a law banning for-profit tutoring of the school curriculum, after surveys show top-decile-income families outspend bottom-decile families on tutoring by a ratio of 9 to 1, feeding exam-score gaps. Enforcement questions loom: parents and tutors draft workarounds within weeks in comparable jurisdictions. The education minister asks whether the state should restrict what families buy.

options.t: 我会通过禁令：当财富可以直接兑换成考试排名，考试衡量的就是家庭财力，国家必须保护它赖以运行的信号。
options.t_en: I would pass the ban: when wealth converts directly into exam rank, the exam measures family money, and the state must protect the signal it relies on.

options.t: 我会反对禁令：为孩子购买机会是最古老的家长本能，禁令只会把钱赶进更隐蔽的渠道。
options.t_en: I would oppose the ban: parents purchasing opportunities for their children is the oldest instinct there is, and a ban just reroutes the money to less visible channels.

options.t: 我不设禁令，改为为低收入学生扩免费公立补习，用增加供给而非禁止来缩小差距。
options.t_en: I would skip the ban and expand free state tutoring to low-income students instead, attacking the gap by supply rather than prohibition.

options.t: 我会用登记制度限制每个学生的补习时长而非取缔行业，托高底线的同时不把市场赶入地下。
options.t_en: I would cap tutoring hours per student by registry rather than banning the industry, so the floor rises without driving the market underground.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene: 政府提议为每位居民发放强制数字身份，用于开户、购酒、在线投票和调阅健康档案。试点地区欺诈率大幅下降，原本数周的流程缩短到几分钟。隐私团体指出，该身份会把每一笔交易都汇入国家持有的单一可检索档案。法案进入委员会，你必须给出建议。
scene_en: A government proposes a mandatory digital identity for every resident, required for opening bank accounts, buying alcohol, voting online, and accessing health records. Fraud falls sharply in pilot regions, and services that took weeks move to minutes. Privacy groups note the ID links every transaction into one searchable profile held by the state. The bill reaches committee and you must recommend.

options.t: 我会支持法案：一个经过验证的身份能终结大部分身份欺诈，档案关联的风险可以用数据最小化规则来控制。
options.t_en: I would support the bill: one verified identity ends most identity fraud, and the profile-linking risk can be contained by data-minimization rules.

options.t: 我会反对法案：一把能打开公民全部生活的钥匙正是那种不该存在的架构，无论欺诈数据多好看。
options.t_en: I would oppose the bill: a single key to every citizen's life is the one architecture that should not exist, whatever the fraud numbers.

options.t: 我只支持凭证存于公民自己的设备、不建中央数据库的版本，让验证发生而国家看不到谁做了什么。
options.t_en: I would support it only with the credentials held in citizens' own wallets and zero central database, so verification happens without the state seeing who did what.

options.t: 我会把它设为自愿制并配法律激励：服务保持快捷开放，但不强制任何人注册。
options.t_en: I would make it voluntary with legal incentives: services stay fast and open to all, but no resident is compelled to enroll.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene: 卫生部辩论建立集中式疫苗接种登记系统，整合全部居民的免疫记录，并通过药房系统标记漏种常规疫苗的人。 uptake 模型显示漏种率可下降三分之一。反对者认为国家给每位公民挂健康标记会让健康监控常态化；医学会则支持，指出疫情暴发的死亡本就超过登记系统可能造成的代价。你撰写内阁备忘录。
scene_en: A ministry debates a centralized vaccination registry that merges every resident's immunization records and flags, via pharmacy systems, anyone overdue for routine vaccines. Uptake modeling shows missed-dose rates falling by a third. Opponents object that the state keeping a health flag on every citizen normalizes health surveillance; the medical association supports it, noting outbreaks already cost more lives than the registry could. You write the cabinet note.

options.t: 我会推荐该系统：可预防的死亡是具体的，而监控滑坡是推测，被挽救的生命却是每年可数的。
options.t_en: I would recommend the registry: preventable deaths are concrete and the surveillance slippery-slope is a prediction, while the lives saved are annual and countable.

options.t: 我会建议反对：国家给每位公民的身体挂永久标记，越过了只应属于紧急权力的界线，接种率可以用提醒机制来提升。
options.t_en: I would recommend against it: a permanent state flag on every citizen's body crosses a line that emergency powers were supposed to be for, and uptake can be raised by reminders instead.

options.t: 我会推荐该系统，但记录 24 个月后转为匿名汇总，让标记在设计上就是临时的。
options.t_en: I would recommend the registry with records expiring into anonymized aggregates after 24 months, so the flag is temporary by design.

options.t: 我会推荐默认加入、可登记退出的版本：不提交表格即入册，在覆盖率与拒绝权之间取得平衡。
options.t_en: I would recommend an opt-out registry: everyone is included unless they file a form, balancing coverage against the right to refuse.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene: 某证券交易所监管机构提议：上市公司须在四年内让董事会的弱势性别比例不低于 40%，否则除牌。反对者称董事会应只凭能力就座；支持者引用了十年自愿目标——比例从 9% 升到 17% 后陷入停滞。征求意见期临近截止，你必须提交立场。
scene_en: A stock exchange regulator proposes that listed companies fill at least 40% of board seats with the underrepresented gender within four years, with delisting as the sanction. Opponents argue boards should be seated on competence alone; supporters cite a decade of voluntary targets that moved the ratio from 9% to 17% and stalled. The consultation closes soon and you must file a position.

options.t: 我会提交支持：十年客气地劝说只挪动了 8 个百分点，只有可执行的底线才能改变候选名单本身。
options.t_en: I would file in support: ten years of asking politely moved the needle 8 points, and only an enforceable floor changes who is even considered.

options.t: 我会提交反对：董事席位是所有者的信义抉择，国家规定其构成等于用配额替代判断。
options.t_en: I would file against: a board seat is an owner's fiduciary choice, and the state dictating its composition substitutes quota for judgment.

options.t: 我会提议仅强制披露：每家上市公司逐年公开董事会构成与继任管道，其余交给投资者。
options.t_en: I would propose a disclosure-only rule: every listed firm publishes its board composition and pipeline annually, and investors do the rest.

options.t: 我会支持该底线，但把它绑定在候选人池要求而非结果上，让企业必须公平面试，而国家不替任何人安排席位。
options.t_en: I would support the floor but tie it to candidate-pool requirements rather than outcomes, so firms must interview fairly without the state seating anyone.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene: 某州教育当局必须裁定一所宗教学校网络的拨款申请：其学业成绩位列前 10%，候补名单常年爆满。其章程要求每日集体礼拜，并在两门课程中把本教经典作为史实讲授。督学确认其招生无歧视。世俗运动者要求拒绝拨款；学校方则称家长是自由选择的。裁决之笔在你手中。
scene_en: A state education authority must rule on funding applications from a network of faith schools whose academic results rank in the top decile and whose waiting lists stretch for years. Their charter requires daily collective worship and teaches their scripture as historical fact in two subjects. Inspectors confirm no discrimination in admissions. Secular campaigners want the funding refused; the schools argue parents choose them freely. You hold the ruling pen.

options.t: 我会批准拨款：家长自由排队争取这些成绩，而一个只因学校不认同自身世界观就断供的国家，等于把信仰变成了忠诚测试。
options.t_en: I would approve the funding: parents freely queue for these results, and a state that funds schools only when they share its own worldview has made belief a loyalty test.

options.t: 我会以'经典作为史实'条款为由拒绝拨款：公共资助的教学不能把一种信仰的文本当作事实讲授，无论考试分数多高。
options.t_en: I would refuse funding for the scripture-as-history clauses: publicly funded teaching must not present one faith's text as fact, whatever the exam scores.

options.t: 我会附带条件批准：增设比较宗教模块，并把那些课程改写为传统叙事而非史实。
options.t_en: I would fund the school conditionally on adding a comparative religion module and recasting those lessons as tradition rather than fact.

options.t: 我会把拨款转为可在任何学校使用的按生学费券，宗教与否不限，让家庭而非教育局来裁决这个问题。
options.t_en: I would convert the funding to per-student vouchers usable at any school, religious or not, letting families and not the ministry settle the question.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene: 某市公屋轮候名单长达 12 年，正辩论覆盖全部私人租赁的租金管制：租金冻结在现价加通胀，且取消空置期解冻。房东协会预测维护崩塌、房源撤市；租户工会引用了几十年来管制成功稳住房租的城市案例。该市空置率为 1.1%。议会请你提交分析。
scene_en: A city with a 12-year waiting list for public housing debates rent control covering all private rentals: rents frozen at current levels plus inflation, with vacancy decontrol removed. Landlord associations predict maintenance collapse and listings withdrawn from the market; tenant unions cite cities where controls held rents for decades. Vacancy in the city is 1.1%. The council asks your analysis.

options.t: 我会支持全面管制：1.1% 的空置率下租户毫无市场议价能力，紧急状态足以证成冻结。
options.t_en: I would support full control: at 1.1% vacancy tenants have no market power at all, and the emergency justifies the freeze.

options.t: 我会反对：成本上涨的同时封顶租金，等于把每位房东变成卖家，轮候名单赖以存在的房源只会收缩。
options.t_en: I would oppose it: capping rent while costs rise converts every landlord into a seller, shrinking the stock the waiting list depends on.

options.t: 我会只对 30 年以上楼龄的建筑管制，新建项目豁免，让供给激励得以保留。
options.t_en: I would support control on buildings older than 30 years only, leaving new construction exempt so supply incentives survive.

options.t: 我不搞管制，改为每年以城市预算的 3% 直接兴建公屋，用房子而不是价格规则来消减轮候名单。
options.t_en: I would skip control and build public housing directly at 3% of city budget annually, attacking the waiting list with units rather than price rules.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene: 生物安全监管机构审评首个氮高效小麦品种：经基因编辑，需肥量降低 30%，同时削减农场成本与水域缺氧带。环保团体内部分裂：一派称其为真正的减排工具，另一派要求基因编辑生物先做十年田间试验再谈批准，并引用一次早年的转基因失败案例。种植者希望本季就拿到种植权。你为监管机构起草决定。
scene_en: A biosafety regulator reviews the first nitrogen-efficient wheat variety, gene-edited to need 30% less fertilizer, cutting both farm costs and waterway dead zones. Environmental groups split: some call it a genuine emissions tool, others demand a decade of field trials on gene-edited organisms before any approval, noting one earlier transgenic failure. Growers want planting rights this season. You draft the regulator's decision.

options.t: 我会本季批准：肥料削减 30% 对水域和气候是可测的收益，且这种编辑不留任何可追溯的外源基因。
options.t_en: I would approve this season: a 30% fertilizer cut is a measurable win for waterways and climate, and the edit leaves no foreign genes to trace.

options.t: 我会要求完整试验期：一次生态系统的意外就抵得过一季的收益，土壤生物学上的可逆性并未被证实。
options.t_en: I would require the full trial period: one ecosystem surprise outweighs a season's gains, and reversibility in soil biology is not established.

options.t: 我会限定区域批准，配套强制缓冲区和独立监测，逐季按实测结果扩面。
options.t_en: I would approve for a limited area with mandatory buffer zones and independent monitoring, expanding by measured results each season.

options.t: 我会把决定权交给各省自己的生物安全规则，因为生态条件和公众态度本就因地区而异。
options.t_en: I would leave the decision to each province's own biosafety rules, since ecological conditions and public attitudes differ across regions.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene: 某市警察局提议部署预测警务系统：用十年案件数据每日为街区计算抢劫风险分值，并据此调配巡逻时长。试点显示覆盖区街头抢劫下降 18%。审计团体发现，由于历史上的报案偏差，模型给两个少数族裔聚居区派驻的巡逻密度是其他地区的 2.3 倍。警察委员会必须表决。
scene_en: A metropolitan police force proposes a predictive-policing system that scores city blocks daily by robbery risk from a decade of incident data and shifts patrol hours accordingly. Its pilot cut street robbery 18% in covered zones. Audit groups find the model sends 2.3 times the patrol density to two majority-minority districts, driven by historic over-reporting there. The police board must vote.

options.t: 我会投扩大部署票：抢劫下降 18% 首先保护的正是这些街区的居民，而模型出现之前巡逻分配也从未平等过。
options.t_en: I would vote to expand the system: an 18% robbery cut protects residents of exactly those districts first, and patrol allocation was never equal before the model.

options.t: 我会投取消票：把历史偏差喂给算法等于给它洗成客观，那 18% 是在不公正的基线上量出来的。
options.t_en: I would vote to cancel it: feeding historic bias into an algorithm launders it into apparent objectivity, and the 18% was measured on an unjust baseline.

options.t: 我会投继续运行票，但强制季度偏差审计和公开仪表盘，只在差距指数下降的区域扩面。
options.t_en: I would vote to continue with a mandatory quarterly bias audit and public dashboards, expanding only in zones where the disparity index falls.

options.t: 我会投支持票，但把社区自报的犯罪数据作为并列输入，让模型向居民自己的报告学习，而非只依赖警方文书。
options.t_en: I would vote to fund community-reported crime data as a parallel input, so the model learns from residents' own reports rather than police paperwork alone.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene: 一个 1100 万人口的富裕国家面临年度安置配额决策。联合国难民署的区域请求是 4 万个名额；内政部预测，住房与语言吸纳系统能承受的是 1 万，再多就会在庇护申请者之间引发插队。民意五五开，护理和建筑业的雇主则以劳动力短缺为由游说提高配额。你为内阁提供咨询。
scene_en: A wealthy country of 11 million faces an annual resettlement quota decision. UNHCR's regional ask is 40,000 places; the interior ministry's projection says 10,000 is what housing and language systems absorb without queue-jumping among asylum seekers. Public opinion splits evenly; employers in care and construction lobby for higher quotas citing labor shortages. You advise the cabinet.

options.t: 我会建议按难民署数字执行：需求不会收缩迁就接收系统，而系统建成的速度可以快过危机本身。
options.t_en: I would recommend the UNHCR figure: need does not shrink to fit intake systems, and systems can be built faster than a crisis passes.

options.t: 我会建议按内政部的 1 万执行：超出吸纳能力的承诺只会产出帐篷营地而非融入，那种失败反而喂养关门的政治。
options.t_en: I would recommend the ministry's 10,000: a promise beyond absorption capacity produces tent camps, not integration, and that failure feeds the politics of closure.

options.t: 我会建议 2.5 万并绑定已拨款的住房项目和区域安置规则，用书面答复消化能力问题，取道折中。
options.t_en: I would recommend 25,000 tied to a funded housing program and regional placement rules, meeting the need halfway with the capacity question answered in writing.

options.t: 我会建议担保人模式：由社区团体为个别家庭的住房和语言成本兜底，在不增加中央预算的情况下提高名额。
options.t_en: I would recommend a sponsorship model: community groups underwrite individual families' housing and language costs, raising numbers without central budgets.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene: 养老金部预测：法定退休年龄固定在 65 岁，而 65 岁时预期寿命已提高 7 岁，体系将在 11 年内陷入赤字。可选方案：逐步提高至 68 岁；工资税加征 2 个百分点；或全面削减 9% 的待遇。体力劳动者 65 岁时的预期寿命比办公室职员低 4 岁。你是改革委员会主席。
scene_en: The pensions ministry projects that the state retirement age, fixed at 65 while life expectancy at 65 has risen seven years, will push the system into deficit within 11 years. Options: raise the age to 68 gradually; raise payroll contributions 2 points; or cut benefits 9% across the board. Manual workers' life expectancy at 65 is four years lower than office workers'. You chair the reform commission.

options.t: 我会逐步提高退休年龄：寿命的增益是真实的，多工作两年能让每一代人的待遇原封不动。
options.t_en: I would raise the age gradually: longevity gains are real, and working two more years keeps every cohort's benefit intact.

options.t: 我会加征缴费：削待遇或延工龄，惩罚的是身体早已透支的劳动者，而工资税本就是这个体系的立身之本。
options.t_en: I would raise contributions: cutting benefits or extending work years taxes the workers whose bodies already gave out, and payroll funding is how the system was built.

options.t: 我会提高年龄但按职业设置例外：20 岁前就参加体力工作的劳动者 66 岁退休，办公室职员 68 岁。
options.t_en: I would raise the age with an occupation-based exception: manual workers who started before 20 retire at 66, office workers at 68.

options.t: 我会把退休年龄设为 62 到 70 岁之间按月精算调整的弹性区间，让每个人给自己的取舍定价。
options.t_en: I would make the age flexible between 62 and 70 with actuarial adjustment per month, letting each person price their own trade-off.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene: 一位遗嘱人把全部财产留给慈善机构，剥夺了十年前与他断绝往来的两名成年子女的继承权。法律规定直系血亲享有三分之二的特留份，除非存在'重大事由'。子女援引该条；慈善方以断绝往来抗辩。可比辖区的判例对'断绝往来是否构成重大事由'分裂。你是审查特留份制度的法律改革机构成员。
scene_en: A testator leaves everything to charity, disinheriting his two adult children who had stopped contact with him a decade earlier. The statute reserves a compulsory share of two-thirds for direct descendants unless 'weighty grounds' exist. The children invoke it; the charity cites the estrangement. Courts in comparable jurisdictions split on whether estrangement alone qualifies. You sit on the law-reform body reviewing the compulsory-share rule.

options.t: 我会维持特留份制度：财产经由家庭传递，允许一代人用一个签名斩断下一代，会侵蚀这个制度本身。
options.t_en: I would keep the compulsory share as is: property passes through families, and letting one generation cut the next off with a signature corrodes the institution itself.

options.t: 我会废除特留份：赠与如何安排是所有者的权利，把已断绝关系的子女强行塞回遗产，对谁都不是奖赏。
options.t_en: I would abolish the compulsory share: a gift is the owner's to direct, and forcing severed children onto the estate rewards neither side.

options.t: 我会保留制度，但立法明确'重大事由'的定义，把断绝往来列为法官权衡的因素之一，用公开标准取代判例的不确定性。
options.t_en: I would keep it but define 'weighty grounds' by statute with estrangement as a factor a judge weighs, replacing judge-made uncertainty with published criteria.

options.t: 我会把特留份从三分之二降到三分之一，在保留直系血亲底线的同时给遗嘱人更多自由。
options.t_en: I would cap the compulsory share at one-third rather than two-thirds, leaving the testator freer while keeping a floor for descendants.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene: 食品创新署提议把 2 亿资金从畜牧业营销补贴转投培育肉和精密发酵初创企业，目标是在十年内让成本与绞肉持平。农场工会预测两个农业省将集中流失 1.5 万个岗位；气候模型测算这一转变可减少全国 4% 的排放。消费者测试显示接受度上升但尚不足 40%。你为该署撰写建议。
scene_en: A food-innovation agency proposes redirecting 200 million from livestock marketing subsidies to cultivated-meat and precision-fermentation startups, aiming for cost parity with ground meat within a decade. Farm unions project 15,000 livestock job losses concentrated in two rural provinces; climate models credit the switch with 4% of national emissions. Consumer testing shows acceptance rising but below 40%. You write the agency's recommendation.

options.t: 我会支持转投：一项能削减全国 4% 排放的技术值得资助，哪怕市场到来的速度慢于预测。
options.t_en: I would back the redirection: a technology that cuts 4% of national emissions is worth funding even if the market arrives slower than projected.

options.t: 我会继续资助畜牧业：在接受度不足 40% 时，用一场实验室押注替换运转中的乡村经济，岗位和公款都有风险。
options.t_en: I would keep funding livestock: replacing a functioning rural economy with a laboratory bet, while acceptance sits below 40%, risks both jobs and public money.

options.t: 我会把资金对半：一半给初创企业，一半用于两省的转岗培训与过渡支持，让押注与调整同行。
options.t_en: I would split the fund: half to the startups, half to retraining and transition support for the two provinces, so the bets and the adjustment travel together.

options.t: 我会把资金与消费者接受度里程碑挂钩，实测接受度过 40%、50%、60% 才逐档释放。
options.t_en: I would condition the money on consumer uptake milestones, releasing tranches only as measured acceptance passes 40%, 50%, and 60%.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene: 国家图书馆获得一笔一次性经费，须数字化 5 万件藏品。馆员团队分裂为两派：一派主张数字化经典馆藏——阅览室里借阅量最大的作品，确保世界对遗产核心的最大访问量；另一派主张优先处理濒危的地方档案、方言报纸和口述历史，它们在物理上正在朽坏，且不会有任何其他机构代为复制。你撰写建议书。
scene_en: A national library must digitize 50,000 items with a one-off grant. The curatorial staff split: one proposal digitizes the canonical collection, the most-viewed works in reading rooms, ensuring maximum global access to the heritage core; the other prioritizes endangered regional archives, dialect newspapers, and oral histories, which decay physically and which no other institution will ever copy. You write the recommendation.

options.t: 我会数字化核心馆藏：让全世界访问经典才是图书馆的本职，而 popular（大众熟知的）作品也是这笔经费对公众的交代。
options.t_en: I would digitize the core collection: global access to the canon is the library's actual mission, and popular works justify the grant to the public.

options.t: 我会数字化濒危档案：经典有纸质和其他副本留存，而朽坏中的方言报纸档案是世上仅此一份的存在。
options.t_en: I would digitize the endangered archives: the canon survives in print and in other copies, but a rotting dialect newspaper archive is the only copy that will ever exist.

options.t: 我会按 60-40 倾向濒危档案分配，并对剩余的经典清单开放公众投票，把馆员的判断与公众的参与结合起来。
options.t_en: I would split 60-40 toward the endangered archives but publish a public vote on the remaining core list, mixing curatorial judgment with ownership.

options.t: 我会把选择权拍卖给最高额的私人联合出资方，数字化双倍数量的藏品，接受出资方的优先级影响馆藏。
options.t_en: I would auction the choice to the highest private co-funder and digitize twice as many items, accepting that the donor's priorities shape the collection.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene: 一座 200 万人口的城市入围大陆级运动会的候选主办地。申办要求一座 14 亿的体育场和运动员村；预计运营亏损 1.8 亿，而模型测算的旅游和基建收益，在多数针对同类赛事的学术研究中被证实并未兑现。基层体育俱乐部追问这 14 亿能给他们建多少设施。市长征求你的立场。
scene_en: A city of 2 million is shortlisted to host a continental games. The bid requires a 1.4 billion stadium and athletes' village; the projected operating loss is 180 million, against modeled tourism and infrastructure benefits that most academic studies of comparable events find fail to materialize. Grassroots clubs ask what 1.4 billion would build in their facilities. The mayor asks for your position.

options.t: 我会支持申办：全球舞台对城市轨迹的改变不是单项赛事研究能捕捉的，而且基础设施的寿命长于赛事本身。
options.t_en: I would support the bid: a global stage changes a city's trajectory in ways studies of single events do not capture, and the infrastructure outlives the games.

options.t: 我会反对：遗产收益的证据一贯为负，而 14 亿投进社区设施，触达的运动员远多于两周赛事。
options.t_en: I would oppose it: the evidence on legacy benefits is consistently negative, and 1.4 billion in neighborhood facilities would reach more athletes than two weeks of games ever will.

options.t: 我只支持附带约束性遗产方案的申办：体育场缩至 2.5 万座，闭幕次日即转交俱乐部使用。
options.t_en: I would support the bid only with a binding legacy plan: the stadium downsized to 25,000 seats and converted to club use on day one after closing.

options.t: 我会把决定交给全市公投，并公开两版预算账本，让居民自己决定这 14 亿公款怎么花。
options.t_en: I would put it to a citywide referendum with both budget books published, letting residents choose how 1.4 billion of their money is spent.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene: 某省辩论如何支持 30 万名无薪家庭照护者，有两个方案：直接向照护者发放月度照护津贴；或发放照护积分，让家庭购买专业喘息服务。照护者调查显示 60% 会把现金用于家庭开支；社工警告不与服务挂钩的现金会加深被照护者的孤立。财政部测算两案成本相同。你为省长提供建议。
scene_en: A province debating how to support 300,000 unpaid family caregivers considers two schemes: a monthly care stipend paid to the caregiver directly, or a care credit that lets families purchase professional respite hours instead. Caregiver surveys show 60% would keep the cash for household costs; social workers warn that cash without service ties deepens isolation for the cared-for person. The finance ministry prices the schemes identically. You advise the premier.

options.t: 我会发现金津贴：照护者最清楚自家的缺口，以钱的形式抵达的补贴尊重他们每天都在做的选择。
options.t_en: I would pay the cash stipend: caregivers know their own households' shortfalls, and a subsidy that arrives as money respects the choice they already make daily.

options.t: 我会发服务积分：现金补偿的是照护者，喘息小时触及的才是被照护的人，而孤立才是致命的结局。
options.t_en: I would pay the service credit: cash compensates the caregiver while respite hours reach the person being cared for, and isolation is the outcome that kills.

options.t: 我会两案并行，让每个家庭在同一个额度内自行分配现金与服务小时。
options.t_en: I would offer both and let each family split its allocation between cash and service hours within one envelope.

options.t: 我会发现金津贴，但要求区域护士每年做一次福祉探访，钱留给家庭，监督交给国家。
options.t_en: I would pay the cash stipend but require an annual well-being check by a district nurse, keeping the money with the family and the oversight with the state.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene: 某国毕业生的人均学生贷款是起薪的 130%，还款按中位收入以上部分的 9% 计收，余额 25 年后核销。一项改革提案以相当于一年 GDP 6% 的成本核销所有未偿余额的 50%，但对造成债务的借贷规则不作任何修改。未来的学生仍将以相同条款借款。你是财政委员会成员。
scene_en: A country's graduates carry student loans averaging 130% of starting salary, with repayment rates set at 9% of income above the median and balances written off after 25 years. A reform proposal cancels 50% of all outstanding balances at a cost of 6% of one year's GDP, with no change to the borrowing rules that created them. Future students would borrow on identical terms. You sit on the treasury committee.

options.t: 我会投核销赞成票：那 9% 的扣缴本就是对毕业生的额外征税，减掉一半余额是对一个把教育当消费品定价的体系的修正。
options.t_en: I would vote for the cancellation: the 9% levy already functions as an extra tax on graduates, and clearing half the balance corrects a system that priced education as if it were consumption.

options.t: 我会投反对票：规则不变的核销是把从未上过大学的纳税人的钱转移给这一代毕业生，还会诱使下一届照旧借款、坐等同样待遇。
options.t_en: I would vote against it: a one-time write-off with unchanged rules is a transfer to today's graduates paid by taxpayers who never attended, and it invites the next cohort to borrow expecting the same.

options.t: 我会把核销与面向未来学生的收入挂钩学费资助捆绑，让修法同时覆盖存量债务和补充进来的流量。
options.t_en: I would pair the cancellation with income-contingent tuition funding for future students, so the fix covers both the stock of debt and the flow that replaces it.

options.t: 我会只对中位收入以下的毕业生核销、以上者全额保留，让核销落在实际困难所在的地方。
options.t_en: I would cancel balances only for graduates below the median income and fully repayable ones above it, targeting the write-off where the hardship actually sits.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene: 电网运营商须为一座 800 万人口的地区在两条脱碳路径间做决定。路径一：一座新核电站，全天候稳定电力，建设期 14 年，造价 32 亿。路径二：风电、光伏加储能组合达到同等年发电量，5 年内可部署，造价 26 亿，过渡期的季节性缺口由燃气调峰机组覆盖。两者资金全部来自用电者。你撰写监管机构意见书。
scene_en: A grid operator must decide between two decarbonization paths for a region of 8 million. Path one: one new nuclear plant, firm 24/7 power, 14 years to build, 3.2 billion. Path two: wind, solar, and storage buildout reaching the same annual output, deployable in 5 years, 2.6 billion, with seasonal shortfalls covered by gas peakers during the transition. Both are fully financed by ratepayers. You write the regulator's opinion.

options.t: 我会支持核电路径：六十年的稳定清洁电力值得等待，而路径二里的燃气调峰是比转型活得更久的化石承诺。
options.t_en: I would back the nuclear path: firm clean power for sixty years justifies the wait, and gas peakers in path two are a fossil commitment that outlives the transition.

options.t: 我会支持可再生路径：核电等待期第 5 到 14 年里避免的排放是永久性 avoided（避免）的，造价差正好投给储能研发。
options.t_en: I would back the renewables path: emissions avoided in years 5 through 14 of the nuclear wait are emissions that never return, and the cost gap funds storage research.

options.t: 我会先启动可再生建设，同时保留核电选址许可，到第六年再判断季节缺口数据是否足以支撑建站。
options.t_en: I would start the renewables buildout now and hold the nuclear site license open, deciding year six whether the seasonal-gap data justify the plant.

options.t: 我会让零售用户在账单上自选路径：核电订阅者锁定 20 年合同，可再生订阅者签灵活合同。
options.t_en: I would let retail customers choose their path on their own bill, with nuclear subscribers locked into 20-year contracts and renewables subscribers into flexible ones.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene: 某国 40 万人的公务员队伍，招录考试按人口比例大体选人，但晋升持续存在差距：管理层 82% 来自多数族群。一项法令草案设定内部晋升目标：各部委管理层新增必须在八年内与人口构成匹配，部长担责。反对者称之为制度化的偏袒，支持者称这是唯一真正改变过构成的杠杆。你是公职委员会成员。
scene_en: A national civil service of 400,000, whose recruitment exams select candidates from groups in rough proportion to population, shows a persistent gap in promotion: management grades are 82% from the majority group. A draft decree sets internal promotion targets: each ministry's management intake must match population composition within eight years, with department heads accountable. Opponents call it institutionalized preference; supporters call it the only lever that has ever moved composition. You sit on the public-service commission.

options.t: 我会支持该法令：中立的考试带来中立的新人，晋升却依然聚在 82%，说明过滤器在管道中段，必须在它起作用的地方回应。
options.t_en: I would support the decree: neutral exams got neutral intakes yet the promotions still pooled at 82%, so the filter sits in the middle of the pipeline and must be answered where it acts.

options.t: 我会反对该法令：规定结果颠倒了考试赖以建立的原则，晋升池应当用导师制和轮岗政策来拓宽，而不是规定结果。
options.t_en: I would oppose the decree: mandating outcomes reverses the principle the exams were built on, and promotion pools should be widened by mentoring and posting policy instead.

options.t: 我会附带豁免阀支持：部委可申请两年延期，但须公开晋升标准审计，让目标只为有据可查的障碍让步。
options.t_en: I would support it with an exemption valve: ministries may apply for two-year extensions with published promotion-criteria audits, so the target bends only for documented barriers.

options.t: 我会先强制匿名评审小组和结构化评分，五年后重新测量，再考虑是否设定构成目标。
options.t_en: I would mandate blind promotion panels and structured scoring first, then re-measure in five years before considering any composition target.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene: 你住的老小区一二楼住户习惯在单元门口公共区域拉绳晾被，三楼以上住户嫌挡路且不雅观，物业没有相关规定。你家阳台小，梅雨季被子很难彻底晾干。

options.t: 我会在业主群里提议大家商量一个时段和位置，既照顾低层晾晒的需要，也减少挡路，靠邻里协商定个默契。
options.t_en: I would raise it in the owners' group and suggest we agree on a time slot and spot — meeting the lower floors' need to dry things while reducing the blockage, settling it through neighborly negotiation.

options.t: 我直接找物业要求立规矩，明确公共区域禁止私拉晾绳，违反就清理，规则清楚最省口舌。
options.t_en: I would go straight to the property manager and ask for a rule forbidding private lines in common areas, cleared if violated — a clear rule saves the most arguing.

options.t: 我自己买个折叠烘干架放阳台凑合用，不跟人争这点地方，免得邻里红了脸。
options.t_en: I would just buy a folding dryer rack for the balcony and make do, rather than argue over the space and risk a fight with neighbors.

options.t: 我联名几户向社区居委会反映，请他们协调划出专门的晾晒区，用公共资源解决公共麻烦。
options.t_en: I would gather a few households to ask the neighborhood committee to set aside a designated drying area, using public resources for a shared nuisance.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Residents on the lower floors of your old apartment block habitually string clotheslines in the common area by the entrance to dry quilts, while upper-floor residents find it obstructive and unsightly, and the property manager has no rule about it. Your balcony is small and quilts never fully dry in the rainy season.

scene: 邻居养的中型犬进电梯时常不牵绳，你牵着小孩有点紧张，也担心电梯里的卫生。对方觉得自家狗温顺、不会咬人。

options.t: 我会在电梯里平和地请邻居把狗牵好，说孩子怕、也怕惊到狗，请他体谅，不指责。
options.t_en: I would calmly ask the neighbor to leash the dog in the elevator, saying my child is frightened and I worry about startling it, without blaming.

options.t: 我向物业投诉，要求强制执行电梯牵绳规定，不牵就禁入，靠制度保护住户安全。
options.t_en: I would complain to the property manager and demand enforcement of a leash rule in elevators, banning entry otherwise, to protect residents by regulation.

options.t: 我避开乘梯高峰、抱紧孩子快速进出，尽量不正面冲突，自己多留神。
options.t_en: I would avoid peak elevator times and hold my child close in and out, steering clear of confrontation and staying alert myself.

options.t: 我在业主群发起文明养宠倡议，推动大家签约定电梯牵绳、及时清理，用公约自律。
options.t_en: I would start a civil pet-keeping initiative in the group, pushing everyone to agree on leashing and prompt cleanup, self-regulating through a pact.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The neighbor's medium-sized dog often rides the elevator off-leash; you hold your child and feel uneasy, also worrying about hygiene. The owner thinks the dog is gentle and would never bite.

scene: 你所在团队连续两个月加班到深夜赶项目，主管暗示这是「奋斗期」、不提倡请假。你本人开始失眠，家庭时间也被挤占。

options.t: 我会在一对一里和主管摊开自己的负荷和睡眠问题，提议重新排期或加人手，先把进度谈清楚。
options.t_en: I would lay out my workload and sleep problem in a one-on-one and propose rescheduling or more staff, getting the timeline clear first.

options.t: 我接受这段高强度，但会留存工时记录，若身体出问题就拿证据主张加班补偿，先保住项目再说。
options.t_en: I would accept the intensity but keep timesheets, and if my health breaks I would use the evidence to claim overtime pay — finish the project first.

options.t: 我带头在部门里提议设「无会无加班日」和调休制度，让大家都能喘口气，靠集体约定减压。
options.t_en: I would lead a proposal for a 'no-meeting no-overtime day' and comp-time rules so everyone can breathe, easing pressure by collective agreement.

options.t: 我直接按合同工时上下班，到点就走、必要的事次日处理，把边界守在纸面约定上。
options.t_en: I would simply work the contracted hours and leave on time, handling leftover tasks next day, holding the boundary the contract sets.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Your team has worked late into the night for two straight months on a project, and your supervisor hints this is a 'grind period' where leaves are discouraged. You have started losing sleep and your family time is squeezed.

scene: 公司新来了一位能力很强但沟通风格很冲的同事，常在会议上直接否定别人的方案。你和他要合作一个重要交付，担心摩擦影响结果。

options.t: 我会私下约他聊聊工作习惯，说清楚我看重直说但希望先听完整再判断，把合作方式提前对齐。
options.t_en: I would privately chat with him about working style, saying I value frankness but prefer hearing the full picture first, aligning our approach early.

options.t: 我向主管申请调整分工，让各自负责独立模块、减少正面碰撞，用结构避开性格冲突。
options.t_en: I would ask the supervisor to split responsibilities into independent modules to reduce clashes, using structure to avoid personality conflict.

options.t: 我发起团队内部的「反馈公约」，约定提意见先复述对方要点再给建议，靠规则把沟通过程理顺。
options.t_en: I would launch a team 'feedback pact' — restate the other's point before advising — smoothing communication through rules.

options.t: 我忍住不快、照他的节奏配合把交付做好，个人情绪先放一边，结果比相处重要。
options.t_en: I would swallow my annoyance and match his pace to finish well, setting personal feeling aside — results matter more than rapport.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: A highly capable but blunt new colleague frequently shoots down others' plans in meetings. You must collaborate with him on an important deliverable and worry friction will hurt the result.

scene: 本地一个兴趣论坛里，有人发帖用很刺耳的话骂某个小众爱好者群体，帖子引来不少附和。你平时也在这个圈子，看着心里不舒服。

options.t: 我会在帖下沉稳反驳，摆出事实说明这个群体并不像他描述的那样，就事论事不升级对骂。
options.t_en: I would reply calmly with facts showing the group is not as described, sticking to the issue without escalating into name-calling.

options.t: 我向版主举报该帖违反社区文明公约，请按规则处理人身攻击内容，由平台把关。
options.t_en: I would report the post to moderators as violating the civility rules, letting the platform handle personal attacks.

options.t: 我直接取关那个账号、并建个更友善的小组自己玩，不想把精力耗在争辩上。
options.t_en: I would just mute that account and start a friendlier subgroup, not spending energy on the argument.

options.t: 我发起一份「理性讨论守则」置顶帖，号召大家就事论事、不贴标签，用社区共识改善氛围。
options.t_en: I would pin a 'civil discussion charter' calling for issue-focused talk without labels, improving the climate through community consensus.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: On a local hobby forum, someone posted a harsh rant against a small fan community, drawing plenty of agreement. You are part of that circle and feel uneasy.

scene: 公司内网论坛有人匿名发帖，实名举报某中层挪用小额公款，但拿不出确凿证据，只是「听说的」。HR 正在讨论是否删帖。

options.t: 我认为未经证实的实名指控会毁人清白，支持先隐藏帖子、走内部调查，别让谣言当判罚。
options.t_en: I think unproven named accusations ruin reputations; I support hiding the post and running an internal investigation rather than letting rumor be the verdict.

options.t: 我主张保留帖子并公开调查进展，员工有渠道反映疑虑，透明比捂盖子更能止住猜疑。
options.t_en: I argue for keeping the post and publishing the investigation's progress; staff need a channel for concerns, and transparency curbs suspicion better than a cover-up.

options.t: 我私下把线索整理好直接交给审计，不掺和公开争论，让专业部门按程序查。
options.t_en: I would privately compile the leads and hand them to audit, staying out of the public debate and letting professionals follow procedure.

options.t: 我无所谓删不删，反正不关我事，照常干活，别人的恩怨我不掺和。
options.t_en: I don't care either way; it's not my business, so I just keep working and stay out of others' disputes.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: On the company intranet someone anonymously posted a named allegation that a middle manager embezzled minor funds, with no hard evidence — just 'what I heard.' HR is debating whether to delete it.

scene: 你所在城市准备对高收入群体加征一笔地方附加税，用于补贴低收入家庭的子女托育。听证会上两派争得很凶。

options.t: 我支持这笔税，收入高的人多担一点，能让更多孩子有得起托育，整体更公平。
options.t_en: I support the tax; those earning more shoulder a bit more so more children can afford childcare, which is fairer overall.

options.t: 我反对，钱应该靠刺激就业和经济增长去分，加税只会把人逼走、税基反而缩水。
options.t_en: I oppose it; the money should come from boosting jobs and growth, and the tax only drives people away and shrinks the base.

options.t: 我赞成方向但要求公开每一笔补贴的去向和效果，钱花得明明白白大家才服气。
options.t_en: I like the direction but demand public tracking of every subsidy's flow and effect — clear spending earns public trust.

options.t: 我更愿意自己和企业做定向捐赠、结对帮扶，不靠强制征税，自愿比摊派更可持续。
options.t_en: I would rather give targeted donations and mentorship myself than rely on forced taxation; voluntarism outlasts compulsion.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Your city plans a local surtax on high earners to subsidize childcare for low-income families. The hearing is fiercely contested.

scene: 你们小区旁边的老工业区要改造，政府拿出一笔补偿款，但居民对「按面积补」还是「按人头补」分歧很大。

options.t: 我主张按人头补，家里人口多的本来就挤，补偿该照顾实际居住的人。
options.t_en: I favor per-head compensation; larger households are cramped and the payout should cover actual residents.

options.t: 我认为按面积补最清楚，房产证写多少补多少，少了扯皮、也尊重产权。
options.t_en: I think by-area is clearest — compensate what the deed says, less haggling and more respect for property.

options.t: 我建议两套结合：保底按人、增量按面积，既托住困难户也不亏了大户。
options.t_en: I suggest a blend: a per-head floor plus area-based surplus, protecting the struggling while not shorting larger owners.

options.t: 我懒得掺和怎么分，拿到自己那份就行，别人的账随他们争。
options.t_en: I won't meddle in the split; I'll take my share and let others argue theirs.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: The old industrial zone by your neighborhood is being redeveloped with a compensation fund, but residents split sharply over 'by area' versus 'by headcount.'

scene: 你家乡以出口小商品为主，最近主要买家市场提高了环保和劳工标准，不少厂子因达不到面临退单。镇上讨论要不要集体升级产线。

options.t: 我支持镇上牵头贷款帮厂子升级设备和工时制度，单家扛不动，抱团才能留住房订单。
options.t_en: I support the town leading loans to upgrade equipment and hours; no single shop can bear it, only unity keeps the orders.

options.t: 我认为该让市场淘汰落后的，政府别兜底，逼出来的转型才有效率。
options.t_en: I think the market should weed out laggards; government shouldn't backstop them — only forced transition is efficient.

options.t: 我主张先派人和买家谈过渡期、分批达标，给厂子喘息而不是一刀切断单。
options.t_en: I argue for negotiating a phased grace period with buyers, giving factories room to breathe instead of a hard cut.

options.t: 我担心的就是贷款压垮小厂，不如帮它们转做内销，别全押在外需上。
options.t_en: I fear loans crushing small shops; better help them pivot to domestic sales than bet everything on external demand.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Your hometown exports small goods; the main buyer market just raised environmental and labor standards, and many factories face cancelled orders. The town debates a collective production upgrade.

scene: 本地两家同类企业准备合并以对抗外来大平台的低价冲击，但合并后很可能裁掉一批重复岗位。

options.t: 我支持合并，活下来才保住大多数岗位，零散对抗只会被逐个吃掉。
options.t_en: I support the merger; surviving protects most jobs, and scattered resistance just gets eaten one by one.

options.t: 我反对以裁岗换生存，应该找差异化路子，别用工人的饭碗去填利润。
options.t_en: I oppose trading layoffs for survival; they should find a differentiated path, not fill profits with workers' livelihoods.

options.t: 我同意合并但要求设转岗和培训基金，被裁的人有去处，转型别丢下人。
options.t_en: I accept the merger but demand a reskilling fund so the laid-off land elsewhere — transition shouldn't leave people behind.

options.t: 我作为可能被裁的一员，先悄悄更新简历、看看外部机会，把主动权捏自己手里。
options.t_en: As a possible layoff target, I would quietly update my resume and scout outside options, keeping the initiative in my own hands.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene_en: Two local firms plan to merge to withstand a foreign platform's low-price pressure, but the merger will likely cut overlapping roles.

scene: 城郊一条河近几年水质变差，沿岸居民反映有工厂夜间偷排。环保部门人手有限，巡查难以全覆盖。

options.t_en: I'd propose a shared soundproofing fund co-financed by residents and the shop, splitting costs where the benefits land.

options.t: 我睡得沉不太受影响，两边吵架我懒得掺和，谁也别拿我当票数。
options.t_en: I sleep through it and barely notice; I can't be bothered to pick a side, and neither camp should count me as a vote.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene: 你所在的读书俱乐部里，有位成员持续分享阴谋论书单并组织线下讨论，另有成员要求俱乐部把他除名，会长把决定权交给全体会员。
scene_en: In your book club, one member keeps sharing conspiracy-theory reading lists and hosting meetups. Others demand his removal; the chair puts the decision to a full member vote.

options.t: 我投留任，除非他煽动伤害具体的人，俱乐部没资格给书单划正误。
options.t_en: I'd vote to keep him — unless he incites harm against specific people, a book club has no business ruling reading lists right or wrong.

options.t: 我投除名，俱乐部是小共同体，守住共同底线比收留任何观点都重要。
options.t_en: I'd vote him out — a club is a small community, and keeping a shared bottom line matters more than accommodating every viewpoint.

options.t: 我提议平行办辩论专场，请他和质疑者同台，比投票除名更有意思。
options.t_en: I'd propose a debate night where he faces his critics on stage — more interesting than a removal vote.

options.t: 我建议俱乐部设内容分级标签，他继续办他的专场，不感兴趣的会员可屏蔽推送。
options.t_en: I'd suggest content labels: he keeps his own track, and uninterested members can simply filter it out.

options.t: 这种撕扯太消耗了，我打算退会省心，书去哪儿读不行。
options.t_en: This infighting drains me; I'd rather just quit the club — I can read books anywhere.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene: 你所在城市的老牌纺织厂因海外订单转移而半停产，工会、厂方和市政府开会讨论出路，员工拿到三份差别很大的方案。
scene_en: Your city's legacy textile mill is half-shut after overseas orders moved away. The union, management, and city government meet to chart a way out, and workers hold three very different proposals.

options.t: 我支持政府给转型补贴并强制再培训计划，把工人送进自动化产线是新订单的前提。
options.t_en: I back government transition subsidies with mandatory retraining — moving workers onto automated lines is the precondition for new orders.

options.t: 我反对拿公共财政续命夕阳产能，该关就关，遣散费谈判交给劳资双方。
options.t_en: I oppose public money propping up sunset capacity — if it must close, let it; severance is between labor and management.

options.t: 我想推动工人持股接管，把厂子改成合作社接小批量定制单，自己当家。
options.t_en: I'd push a worker buyout — turn the mill into a cooperative taking small custom orders, with workers as owners.

options.t: 我主张把厂房改造成物流仓储园区出租，租金养人，纺织这块就让它过去。
options.t_en: I'd convert the plant into a leased logistics park — rent sustains the workers, and textiles can be left behind.

options.t: 我年近退休不太在乎方案细节，谁能保证我这几年的工资和社保我就跟谁。
options.t_en: Nearing retirement, I care little for the plans' details — I'll back whoever guarantees my wages and benefits for the years left.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene: 你老家县城要上一个稀土提炼项目，税收和两千个岗位随之而来，但环评显示尾矿库距水源保护区只有八公里，县里正在听证。
scene_en: Your home county is weighing a rare-earth refining project promising tax revenue and two thousand jobs — but the environmental assessment puts its tailings pond just eight kilometers from a water-source protection zone, and a public hearing is underway.

options.t: 我支持项目落地，脱贫机会等不起，环保措施写进合同盯紧执行就行。
options.t_en: I support the project — an escape from poverty can't wait; write the safeguards into the contract and enforce them closely.

options.t: 我反对选址，水源一旦污染没有回头路，这个账怎么算都不划算。
options.t_en: I oppose the site — once the water is contaminated there is no undoing it; by any accounting the deal fails.

options.t: 我建议先补做流域风险模型和第三方监测，数据齐了再投票。
options.t_en: I'd call for a watershed risk model and third-party monitoring first — vote once the data is in.

options.t: 我主张照常上马但提高环境税和押金比例，用钱把潜在治理成本先锁住。
options.t_en: I'd proceed but raise the environmental levy and deposit share, locking in funds for potential cleanup up front.

options.t: 我不在县城住了，就业和水源都不直接轮到我，听证会我就不去了。
options.t_en: I no longer live in the county; neither jobs nor the water table affect me directly, so I'd skip the hearing.

options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。
options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.

scene: 你所在的医院打算引入 AI 分诊系统，初诊准确率略高于值班医生，但系统是黑盒，出错时医生要花额外时间复核并承担签字责任。
scene_en: Your hospital plans to roll out an AI triage system whose initial-assessment accuracy slightly exceeds on-duty doctors' — but the model is a black box, and when it errs, doctors spend extra time reviewing and bear signature liability.

options.t: 我欢迎上线，整体准确率更高就是更少人被误判，黑盒不是理由。
options.t_en: I welcome the rollout — higher overall accuracy means fewer misjudged patients; a black box is no objection.

options.t: 我要求可解释版本或先做影子运行，签字责任落在我头上，我就得看得懂它为什么这么判。
options.t_en: I'd demand an explainable version or a shadow run first — if the liability lands on my signature, I must understand why it decides as it does.

options.t: 我建议人机双轨并行一年，用真实病例对账后再决定谁主导。
options.t_en: I'd run human and AI tracks in parallel for a year, reconciling real cases before deciding who leads.

options.t: 我担心医院借机压缩医生编制，要求合同写明 AI 只辅助不替代。
options.t_en: I suspect the hospital will use this to cut doctor headcount, so I'd require contract language that AI assists but never replaces.

options.t: 轮到谁签字谁操心，反正系统好用我就用，不好用我照样按老办法来。
options.t_en: Whoever signs takes the worry; I'll use the system if it works and fall back on old habits if it doesn't.

options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。
options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.

scene: 你作为陪审团候选人在一桩小额债务案旁听资格筛选中，法官问：如果被告出示了微信转账记录但拒收传票缺席审理，你是否能接受缺席判决。另一位候选人当场表示绝不接受。
scene_en: You are a jury-pool candidate in small-claims screening. The judge asks whether you could accept a default judgment against a defendant who showed WeChat transfer records but refused service and skipped the hearing. Another candidate flatly says he never could.

options.t: 我能接受，程序规则对双方一体适用，逃避传票不该换来无限延期。
options.t_en: I could accept it — procedural rules bind both sides alike, and dodging service shouldn't buy endless delays.

options.t: 我不能接受，缺席裁判容易漏掉关键抗辩，宁可多传唤几次也要人到场。
options.t_en: I couldn't accept it — default rulings can miss key defenses; summons again and again until the person shows up.

options.t: 我建议设定严格前置条件，平台交易记录经公证后缺席判决才生效。
options.t_en: I'd set strict preconditions: a default judgment takes effect only if the platform's transaction records are notarized.

options.t: 我倾向给被告一次线上出庭的补救机会，公平感比效率更影响人守不守法。
options.t_en: I'd give the defendant one chance to appear online — perceived fairness matters more than efficiency for compliance.

options.t: 几千块钱的案子走什么程序我无所谓，别叫我再来陪审就行。
options.t_en: For a case of a few thousand yuan I don't much care about procedure — just don't call me for jury duty again.

options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。
options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.

scene: 你关注的调查记者账号发文指认某供应链存在造假，涉事企业发律师函否认并要求平台下架，文章被限流，粉丝群在争论该信谁。
scene_en: An investigative journalist you follow publishes evidence of fraud in a supply chain. The implicated company sends lawyer letters denying it and demands the platform take the article down; the post's reach is throttled, and your fan group is arguing over whom to believe.

options.t: 我要求平台公开限流和下架的具体依据，暗箱处置比错误报道更伤信任。
options.t_en: I'd demand the platform publish the exact grounds for throttling and takedown — opaque handling corrodes trust more than a mistaken report.

options.t: 我倾向等司法或监管结论再站队，律师函和爆料都只是各自的秤。
options.t_en: I'd wait for a court or regulator's finding before picking sides — lawyer letters and exposés each carry their own weight.

options.t: 我自己动手核查原始单据和报关数据，证据链看得见我才转。
options.t_en: I'd dig into the original documents and customs data myself — I share only what I can trace.

options.t: 我支持平台对未证实的指控加显著标记并限流，谣言跑得比核实快。
options.t_en: I support prominent unverified-claim labels and throttling — rumors outrun fact-checks.

options.t: 我建议读者众筹设独立核查基金，请第三方机构逐条验证双方说法。
options.t_en: I'd pitch a reader-funded independent verification fund, having a third party test each side's claims item by item.

options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。
options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.

scene: 台风季前，你所在的沿海街道要决定是否把一段年久失修的海堤加高两米，工程款需要沿街住户按受益面积分摊三成，地势高的住户质疑自己凭什么掏钱。
scene_en: Before typhoon season, your coastal district must decide whether to raise a crumbling seawall by two meters. Households along the street would cover thirty percent of the cost by benefited floor area, and residents on higher ground question why they should pay at all.

options.t: 我支持按受益面积分摊，堤防是整体，高处的住户也别想搭便车白保护。
options.t_en: I support cost-sharing by benefited area — the seawall works as a whole, and high-ground residents shouldn't ride free on its protection.

options.t: 我反对强制分摊，应由财政全额承担防灾工程，防灾本来就是公共品。
options.t_en: I oppose mandatory cost-sharing — disaster works should be fully publicly funded; protection is a public good by nature.

options.t: 我提议只加高地势低街段的堤段并配挡水板，把钱花在刀刃上。
options.t_en: I'd raise only the low-lying segments and add flood boards — spend the money where it cuts risk most.

options.t: 我想先要一份海平面与风暴潮的十年预测模型，再决定加多高、摊多少。
options.t_en: I'd first request a ten-year sea-level and storm-surge model, then decide how high to build and how to split the cost.

options.t: 我家在三层从没淹过，摊派名单里有我我就投反对。
options.t_en: My third-floor home has never flooded; if the assessment list includes me, I'll vote no.

options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。
options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.

scene: 你常用的短视频平台上线了自动个性化推送总开关，默认开启且藏在四级菜单里，用户组织发起「一键关闭」联署，平台回应说算法推荐提升了大家的使用满意度。
scene_en: Your short-video platform launches a master switch for personalized recommendations — on by default and buried four menus deep. A user group starts a petition for one-tap opt-out; the platform replies that algorithmic feeds raise user satisfaction.

options.t: 我支持立法要求个性化推送默认关闭，想开的人自己去开，选择权不该被菜单深度吃掉。
options.t_en: I back legislation making personalized feeds opt-in — those who want them can turn them on; choice shouldn't die in a menu's depth.

options.t: 我觉得无所谓，推送合我口味我用着挺顺手，深不深菜单不碍事。
options.t_en: I don't mind — the feed suits my taste and works smoothly; menu depth is no trouble.

options.t: 我建议平台提供推荐理由说明功能，看到它为什么推这条，我自己决定关不关。
options.t_en: I'd push for recommendation explanations — once I see why a video was served, I'll decide myself whether to switch off.

options.t: 我担心未成年人被动沉迷，支持对未成年账户强制默认关闭并限制夜间推送。
options.t_en: I worry minors get hooked passively; I support forced opt-out defaults and night-time feed limits for minors' accounts.

options.t: 联署我签了个名，但我不指望平台让步，真嫌烦我早卸载了。
options.t_en: I signed the petition, but I don't expect the platform to budge — had it truly bothered me, I'd have uninstalled already.

options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。
options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.

scene: 你所在的业余足球联赛引入了半自动越位识别系统，判罚精度上升但比赛被频繁打断，队员和观众都抱怨节奏没了，联赛委员会让大家投票决定保留、取消还是限时使用。
scene_en: Your amateur football league has introduced semi-automated offside detection. Calls are more accurate, but matches are interrupted constantly, and players and fans grumble that the rhythm is gone. The league committee puts it to a vote: keep it, scrap it, or use it only in select situations.

options.t: 我投保留，误判引发的争吵比暂停多耗十分钟更毁比赛。
options.t_en: I vote keep — arguments over a bad call ruin a match more than a ten-minute pause does.

options.t: 我投取消，业余联赛图的是流畅和友情，差半米的越位没人真在乎。
options.t_en: I vote scrap — amateur leagues are about flow and camaraderie; nobody truly cares about an offside by half a meter.

options.t: 我投只在进球和争议时段启用，平时让比赛自己呼吸。
options.t_en: I vote to use it only for goals and disputed moments, letting the match breathe the rest of the time.

options.t: 我提议由各队队长协商每场是否启用，把决定权留在场上的人手里。
options.t_en: I'd let the teams' captains negotiate per match whether to use it — leave the call to those on the pitch.

options.t: 我是替补常坐冷板凳，系统在不在都行，能多踢几分钟比什么都强。
options.t_en: I'm a substitute warming the bench — system or not, a few extra minutes on the pitch beat anything else.

options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。
options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.

scene: 你住的老城区这两年搬进了十几户外来移民家庭，孩子在同一所小学读书。社区活动中心原本只在工作日晚间开放，最近这几家人向街道申请周六上午开一场母语读书会，让孩子们别把母语丢了。中心只有一名兼职管理员，周六上午原先是老居民的书法班，占着唯一的多功能厅，两边都改不了时间。
scene_en: Over the past two years a dozen immigrant families have moved into your old downtown block, and their children attend the same primary school. The community center used to open only on weekday evenings; these families have now asked the neighborhood office for Saturday mornings so the children can hold a reading circle in their mother tongue and not lose it. The center has one part-time manager, and Saturday morning is already taken by the long-standing residents' calligraphy class in the only multipurpose room. Neither side can shift its time.

options.t: 我会支持周六上午开放给读书会，书法班挪到同日下午就行，两边都能用上这间厅。读书会一次两小时，书法班下午本来就空着，多跑一趟不算什么。
options.t_en: I'd support opening Saturday morning to the reading circle and moving calligraphy to that afternoon, so both groups keep the room. The circle only needs two hours, and the afternoon slot is free anyway.

options.t: 我倾向先保证老居民用了十年的固定时段，新来的家庭可以排到工作日晚上的空档。书法班十年没断过，排班一乱，老人家很可能就不来了。
options.t_en: I'd rather protect the slot the established residents have used for ten years; the new families could take a free weekday evening. The class has run for ten years without a break; once the schedule shifts, the older members may simply stop coming.

options.t: 我提议两家各出一部分钱合聘第二个管理员，周末延长开放，谁也不用让出时段。我算过，一个管理员一个月的工资，两家均摊到每户不过几十块钱。
options.t_en: I'd suggest both groups chip in to co-fund a second manager so the weekend can extend without either side giving up its slot. By my count, a second manager costs each household only a few dozen yuan a month.

options.t: 我想先问清这几家人打算长期办还是只办几期，再决定要不要动原有的排班表。孩子学母语是长期的事，办两期就停，还不如一开始就别占排班。
options.t_en: I'd first ask whether these families plan a long-running program or just a few sessions before touching the existing schedule. Learning a mother tongue takes years; two sessions and then a stop would waste the schedule change entirely.

options.t: 我觉得中心本来就该优先照顾缴费多年的老会员，新需求可以等下一轮预算再谈。中心的器材和场地都是老会员这几年一点一点凑出来的。
options.t_en: I think the center should prioritize members who have paid dues for years; new requests can wait for the next budget round. The center's equipment and space were built up by the older members piece by piece over the years.

options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。
options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.

scene: 你住的小区物业在每层电梯厅装了带人脸识别的门禁，刷脸才能按键上楼，说是能挡住外卖员和推销员。业主群里有人贴出物业与一家数据公司的合作协议，条款允许对方拿走脱敏后的通行记录做客流分析，还能按季度收费。物业解释这只是「提升运营效率」，但没说明数据存在哪里、保存多久。
scene_en: Your building's property manager has installed facial-recognition access control in every elevator lobby: you must show your face before the buttons work, which the manager says keeps delivery riders and salespeople off residential floors. Someone in the owners' chat posts the manager's contract with a data firm — it lets the firm take de-identified entry records for foot-traffic analysis and charge a quarterly fee. The manager calls this "operational efficiency" but won't say where the data is stored or how long it is kept.

options.t: 我要求物业出示完整的数据流向说明，并主张人脸数据只在本地存储、不得外传，否则我不同意启用。我提议从今晚起在群里公示这台设备存了哪些字段、存在哪台机器上。
options.t_en: I'd demand a full data-flow disclosure and argue facial data must stay on the local device and never leave the building; otherwise I won't consent to it being switched on. I'd propose posting in the chat tonight exactly which fields the device stores and on which machine.

options.t: 我支持保留人脸门禁，安全比通行记录更要紧，但要换掉任何有权外传数据的供应商，并公开存储位置。出事时能查清谁进过楼，这比一份通行记录被谁看见更急。
options.t_en: I support keeping facial access — safety matters more than entry logs — but I'd replace any vendor allowed to export the data and require the storage location to be published. When something happens, knowing who entered the building matters more than who sees an entry log.

options.t: 我提议改成刷卡加临时访客码，挡住陌生人的效果差不多，还不用采集生物信息。刷卡的芯片成本每户几十块，物业装得起，也不必请人运维。
options.t_en: I'd propose switching to keycards plus temporary visitor codes; it stops strangers about as well without collecting biometrics. Card readers cost a few dozen yuan per household, which the manager can afford without hiring anyone to maintain them.

options.t: 我更在意外卖能不能按时送到门口，只要不采集我孩子的脸，物业用什么办法我都接受。楼道里推销的人少了，我母亲晚上回家就敢自己走那段路了。
options.t_en: What matters to me is whether takeout reaches my door on time; as long as my child's face isn't captured, I'll accept whatever method the manager chooses. With fewer salespeople in the corridors, my mother dares to walk that stretch home alone at night.

options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。
options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.

scene: 县医院这个月只分到六支稀缺的靶向药，医保目录只覆盖其中一种适应症。药房同时收到两份申请：一位是本地退休教师，教龄三十年，家属全程陪诊；另一位是从外省转来的年轻工人，独自在这边打工。两人病情分期相近，但年轻工人的基因检测显示更可能从这类药中获益，报告是外院出的，需要复核。
scene_en: The county hospital received only six vials of a scarce targeted cancer drug this month, and the insurance list covers just one indication. The pharmacy gets two applications at once: a retired local teacher with thirty years of service whose family accompanies every visit, and a young migrant worker transferred in from another province, living here alone. Their disease staging is similar, but the worker's genetic test — run at an outside lab and still needing verification — suggests a better chance of responding to this drug.

options.t: 我支持按预期的获益概率分配，把药给更可能见效的那位，理由写在病历里接受复核。报告虽然要复核，但复核只需要三天，病人的治疗窗口等不起更久。
options.t_en: I'd allocate by likelihood of benefit and give the drug to the patient more likely to respond, with the reasoning written into the record for review. The outside report needs checking, but verification takes three days, and the treatment window will not wait longer.

options.t: 我主张按申请先后排队，规则简单透明，不会因为身份、户籍或检测结果产生差别。两个人同时递材料，谁的日期在前就先给谁，公开写在候诊屏上。
options.t_en: I'd go by order of application — simple and transparent, without differentiating by background, household registration, or test results. Both submitted on the same day, so the earlier date goes first — posted openly on the waiting-room screen.

options.t: 我想推动医院把两份病历提交区域伦理委员会集体评议，不由药房单独裁定谁先用。药房没有能力判断基因报告的真伪，让集体评议来担这个责任更妥当。
options.t_en: I'd push the hospital to send both files to a regional ethics committee for a collective review rather than letting the pharmacy decide alone. The pharmacy cannot verify the genetic report itself; a collective review is better placed to carry that responsibility.

options.t: 我倾向优先本地参保多年的居民，外省转入的应回原籍申请，本地人缴的保费得有用。本地医保基金是全市参保人一起缴的，先保本地缴费的人说得过去。
options.t_en: I'd prioritize residents with long-standing local coverage; the out-of-province patient should apply where they are insured, so local premiums count for something. The local insurance pool is funded by all local contributors, so prioritizing them is defensible.

options.t: 我想先问两家的药企能否通过慈善赠药补上缺口，把两个人的治疗都接住。慈善赠药通常有申请窗口，赶在月底前递材料还来得及。
options.t_en: I'd first ask whether either manufacturer's charity program can close the gap so both patients get treated. Charity programs have application windows, and filing before month-end is still feasible.

options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。
options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.

scene: 你所在的行业协会准备发布一份技术岗招聘模板，建议会员企业在简历表里取消性别与婚育状况两栏。几家制造型企业反对，说排夜班和核算产假预算都需要提前知道；另几家则担心，删掉这两栏之后，自己连有没有性别失衡都统计不出来。协会秘书处让你在理事会上表态。
scene_en: Your industry association is preparing a hiring template for technical roles that would remove gender and marital/parental-status fields from application forms. Several manufacturers object, saying they need that information in advance to assign night shifts and budget for parental leave; others worry that without the fields they cannot even measure whether they have a gender imbalance. The secretariat asks you to take a position at the board meeting.

options.t: 我支持删除这两栏，排班和预算可以用入职后收集的信息做，面试之前不该出现。真需要排夜班的，入职后问一句就知道，产假预算也能按实际人数算。
options.t_en: I support removing both fields — shift planning and budgeting can use information gathered after hiring; it should not exist before the interview. For night shifts, one question after hiring settles it, and parental-leave budgets can follow actual headcount.

options.t: 我建议保留字段但改为自愿填写，同时由协会每年发布一份匿名汇总的性别比例报告。匿名汇总能看出结构问题，又不至于让某一份简历在初筛时就被划掉。
