options.t_en: I would combine the specialty court with a published dashboard of outcomes — reoffense rates, treatment completion, store loss reports — so the council reviews the data annually instead of re-litigating the philosophy every election season; the approach matters less than whether anyone actually measures it.
options.t: 我会同时设立专门法庭和公开的结果看板——再犯率、治疗完成率、店铺损失报告——让议会每年看数据，而不是每逢选举季重吵一遍路线之争；路径之争固然重要，但有没有人真的在测量更重要。

options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.
options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。

scene_en: A mid-sized coastal nation discovers illegal fishing fleets from a neighboring state inside its exclusive economic zone, with catches roughly equal to a tenth of its domestic fishing industry's annual output. Its navy has two aging patrol vessels. Options before the cabinet: accept a joint-surveillance offer from a distant power with a naval base nearby, file arbitration and publicize satellite evidence while buying two new patrol boats, or open quiet licensing talks letting foreign vessels fish legally for a fee.
scene: 某中等沿海国家发现邻国的非法渔船队进入其专属经济区，捕捞量约等于本国渔业年产量的十分之一，而海军只有两艘老旧巡逻艇。内阁面前有三个选项：接受附近拥有海军基地的域外大国的联合监控提议；提起仲裁并公开卫星证据，同时采购两艘新巡逻艇；或开启低调谈判，向外国渔船发放有偿合法捕捞许可。

options.t_en: I would take the arbitration route and build the patrol fleet. Publicizing satellite evidence puts the burden on the fleet's owners without renting out our waters, and a nation that polices its own zone keeps its options open with every power instead of leaning on one.
options.t: 我会走仲裁路线并建设巡逻舰队。公开卫星证据把压力放回船队所有者身上，而不必把我们的海域租借出去；自己守得住专属区的国家，对任何大国都保有余地，不必依附某一家。

options.t_en: I would accept the joint-surveillance offer. Two aging hulls cannot cover an EEZ that size, and enforcement that actually happens beats enforcement that is technically sovereign; the base agreement can be limited to maritime domain awareness with sunset clauses reviewed every five years.
options.t: 我会接受联合监控提议。两艘老旧船体覆盖不了那么大的专属区，实际发生的执法胜过主权上成立、现实中落空的执法；基地协议可以限定在海事情报共享，并设五年一审的日落条款。

options.t_en: I would open the licensing talks. Fish that will be taken either way should pay into our budget and our observer program, licensing gives us a registry of every hull and season, and it converts a confrontation we cannot win into an industry we can tax and inspect.
options.t: 我会开启许可谈判。无论如何都会被捞走的鱼，不如让收益进入我们的预算和观察员计划；发许可让我们掌握每条船、每个捕捞季的登记，把一场打不赢的对抗，变成一个可以征税和检查的产业。

options.t_en: I would quietly fund a coalition with three neighboring coastal states to pool patrol assets and satellite data first. Four small navies watching together cover more water than any single deal with a distant power, and the negotiating position of a bloc is one no fishing fleet can wait out.
options.t: 我会先低调与三个邻国沿海伙伴共建联合巡逻资产与卫星数据池。四个小国海军一起守望，覆盖的海域超过任何一份与域外大国的协议；而以集团姿态谈判，是任何渔船队都拖不起的。

options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.
options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。

scene_en: A national football league's newly promoted club shocked everyone by reaching the continental quarterfinals, funded by a billionaire owner whose loans to the club now exceed its annual revenue. League regulators must decide whether the existing financial-fairness rules apply, which currently cap owner debt but grandfather pre-existing loans. Smaller clubs argue the imbalance prices them out of trophies; the promoted club's supporters argue a century of small-market obscurity should not bind a new era; broadcasters worry a points deduction would tank the season.
scene: 某全国足球联赛一支升班马俱乐部一路杀进大陆八强，震动全国——其背后是亿万富翁老板，向俱乐部提供的贷款已超过俱乐部年收入。联赛监管方须决定既有的财务公平规则是否适用：现行规则限制老板债务，但对既有贷款有祖父条款豁免。小球会指责这种失衡让他们与奖杯无缘；升班马球迷则说，一个世纪的小市场沉寂不该束缚新时代；转播商担心扣分会毁掉整个赛季的收视率。

options.t_en: I would apply the cap without grandfathering. Rules that bend for the fashionable newcomer stop being rules, and every club knew the debt ceiling when it planned its spending; a phased two-season schedule softens the landing without making the exemption permanent.
options.t: 我会不留祖父条款、直接适用上限。会为时髦新贵弯折的规则就不再成其为规则，每家俱乐部制定开支时都知道债务上限在哪；设两年过渡期可以缓冲落地，但豁免不能变成永久。

options.t_en: I would keep the grandfather clause and tighten only forward-looking rules. Punishing a club retroactively for spending that made this season historic teaches owners that ambition invites audits, and investment is how a sleepy league grows its audience; the cap should shape tomorrow's budgets, not erase yesterday's.
options.t: 我会保留祖父条款，只收紧面向未来的规则。为一个造就了历史性赛季的开支追溯惩罚，只会让老板们学到「雄心招来审计」；投资正是沉睡联赛扩大观众的方式，上限应当塑造明天的预算，而不是抹掉昨天的。

options.t_en: I would convert owner loans into equity instead of punishing them. Debt that can be called in a bad year is the real danger to a club's survival, and an equity rule protects fans from midnight bankruptcies while leaving ambitious owners free to spend what they truly commit.
options.t: 我会把老板贷款转为股权，而不是惩罚贷款。真正威胁俱乐部存亡的是坏年景里可能被催收的债务；股权规则保护球迷免于深夜破产，同时让有雄心的老板自由投入他们真心承诺的资金。

options.t_en: I would commission an independent review with fan representatives on the panel before touching the rules, and publish every club's debt position meanwhile. Whatever the panel decides, a decision made in the open is one the relegated and the promoted can both live with next season.
options.t: 我会先委托一个有球迷代表参与的独立审查，规则未动期间公开每家俱乐部的债务状况。无论审查得出什么结论，在阳光下做出的决定，降级的和升级的俱乐部下个赛季都还过得下去。

options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.
options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。

scene_en: A provincial grid operator must decide how to replace a retiring coal plant that supplies a quarter of regional peak load. Proposals: a utility-scale battery plus solar and wind buildout spread across four years with a diesel bridge period; a new gas plant delivering firm capacity in two years with a twenty-five-year operating life; or extending the coal plant's retirement five years while transmission upgrades unlock hydropower imports from a neighboring province.
scene: 某省级电网运营商须决定如何替代一座即将退役、承担区域四分之一峰荷的燃煤电厂。提案有三：建设覆盖四年的大型电池加风光项目，其间以柴油机组过渡；新建一座两年内交付稳定容量的燃气电厂，运营期二十五年；或将燃煤电厂退役推迟五年，同时升级输电线路以解锁邻省水电输入。

options.t_en: I would take the renewables buildout even with the diesel bridge. Four years of generator noise is a bounded cost, while a gas plant locks its emissions in for twenty-five; the same transmission work that the battery plan needs is what lets cheap hydropower flood in later anyway.
options.t: 我会选择风光方案，即使有柴油过渡期。四年的机组噪音是有边界的成本，燃气电厂却把排放锁定二十五年；电池方案所需的输电升级，本身就是日后廉价水电大举入网的前提。

options.t_en: I would build the gas plant. Blackouts during a two-diesel bridge winter would hit hospitals and small factories first, and a plant that can throttle up and down is exactly the firm partner a variable renewables buildout still needs; it can convert to hydrogen later if that matures.
options.t: 我会建燃气电厂。柴油过渡的两年里若在冬季停电，最先受冲击的是医院和小工厂；一台可灵活调节出力的机组，正是波动性风光体系仍然需要的稳定搭档——若氢能成熟，日后还可改造。

options.t_en: I would extend the coal plant five years and buy the transmission upgrades. Using an existing asset fully before replacing it is not a betrayal of climate goals, it is sequencing; every imported hydropower megawatt displaces coal immediately, without waiting for a battery supply chain to catch up.
options.t: 我会推迟燃煤电厂五年退役并购买输电升级。在替代品就位前把既有资产用满不是背叛气候目标，而是排序问题；每兆瓦输入的水电都立刻替代燃煤发电，不必等电池供应链追上来。

options.t_en: I would split the province: gas firm capacity for the industrial north, the renewables-and-battery path for the hydro-adjacent south, with an open annual review. Two regions with different load shapes should not share one forced answer, and the review keeps the split honest as costs shift.
options.t: 我会分而治之：工业密集的北部配燃气稳定容量，邻近水电的南部走电池加风光路线，并设公开的年度复核。负荷形态不同的两个地区不该共用一个强行统一的答案，年度复核也让这条分界随成本变化保持诚实。

options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.
options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。

scene: 你在同一家物流仓库的两份工作之间进入终面。合同 A 提供固定月薪，轮班安排提前两周公布；合同 B 底薪更高，但排班与时薪由需求预测算法决定：预测高峰日你能多赚六成，清淡日你可能在岗两小时后就被无偿打发回家。已在 B 合同上的两位同事说，他们的月收入在宽裕和勉强糊口之间来回摆动。
scene_en: You have reached the final round for two jobs at the same logistics warehouse. Contract A offers a fixed monthly wage with rotating shifts announced two weeks ahead. Contract B pays a higher base rate but ties your schedule and hourly pay to a demand-prediction algorithm: on forecast peak days you can earn sixty percent more, on quiet days you are sent home unpaid after two hours. Two coworkers already on Contract B say their monthly income swings between comfortable and barely enough.

options.t_en: I would sign the fixed contract. Knowing what next month pays is what lets me plan rent, loan payments, and family obligations; the peak-hour premium sounds attractive, but the income risk ends up carried by the workers with the least bargaining power.
options.t: 我会签固定合同。能提前知道下个月赚多少钱，我才能安排房租、还款和家里的事；高峰溢价听着诱人，但收入的波动风险最后都压在了最没有议价能力的员工身上。

options.t_en: I would take the algorithm contract and push hard. I am young with no dependents, and a sixty percent premium on peak days is exactly what I need; the volatility is a cost I have priced in and would bear myself.
options.t: 我会选算法合同并全力冲刺。我年轻、没养家，高峰日多赚六成正是我需要的；波动是我自己算过账之后愿意承担的成本，赌输了也由我自己收拾。

options.t_en: I would not sign either contract on paper alone; I would first join coworkers in demanding the company publish its pricing and dispatch rules. Without transparent criteria the promised premium can be redefined at any time; verifiable standards come before choosing.
options.t: 两份合同我都不会只看文字就签，会先联合同事要求公司公开算法定价与派单规则。规则不透明，所谓溢价随时可以改口径；先有可核查的标准，再谈选哪一份。

options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.
options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。

scene: 某县将停用的港口土地出售给开发商，一次性获得的收入相当于全县两年的预算。议会有三个提案：把其中一部分作为等额现金分红发给每一位居民；用于扩建长期欠账的诊所和校车网络；或连续五年削减本县的小微企业税负以吸引雇主。公开听证会人满为患，这笔钱必须在本财政年度内定下用途。
scene_en: A county sells decommissioned port land to a developer and receives a one-time windfall equal to two years of its entire budget. The council faces three proposals: distribute part of it as an equal cash dividend to every resident, spend it on expanding the underfunded clinic and school-bus network, or cut the county's small business levy for five years to attract employers. Public hearings draw overflow crowds, and the money must be committed within this fiscal year.

options.t_en: I support the equal cash dividend. Each person understands their own priorities best — some need to pay down debt, some need a new roof; leaving the money in residents' hands makes fewer assumptions than a committee guessing the county's needs, and it reaches the most hard-pressed directly.
options.t: 我支持等额现金分红。每个人对自己生活的优先级最清楚——有人要还债，有人要修屋顶，把钱交给各家自己支配，比让一个委员会替全县人猜需求更少出错，也最能直接帮到手头最紧的人。

options.t_en: I would vote for the clinic and school buses. A dividend thins out to a month of groceries per person, but a clinic that can handle prenatal visits and buses that run on time are a foundation used every day for the next decade; deferred public services do not repair themselves.
options.t: 我会投给诊所和校车。分红摊到每个人头上只够一个月伙食，但一间能做产检的诊所和能准点的校车，是往后十年每天都会用到的底子；公共服务的欠账不会因为等额发放而自己补上。

options.t_en: I would choose the five-year tax cut. Local small firms employ more people than anyone in the county, and hiring and raises tend to follow once the levy drops; a one-time dividend is spent and gone, while money left in others' pockets keeps producing new jobs.
options.t: 我会选择减税五年。本地小企业雇着全县最多的人，税负降下来之后扩招和加薪会自己发生；一次性分红花完就没了，而留在经营者口袋里的钱能持续生出新岗位。

options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.
options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。

scene: 你所在地区一家雇有四千人的太阳能组件工厂，订单正流向价格低三成的进口产品，工厂宣布若情况不变将裁员。贸易部门正在权衡三种应对：对进口组件征收临时关税；用一般财政资金直接发放工资补贴以维持工厂竞争力；或者不干预——理由是更便宜的组件能加速本国的能源转型。行业协会与安装企业各执一词，都在游说。
scene_en: A domestic solar panel factory employing 4,000 people in your region is losing orders to imports priced thirty percent lower, and the plant has announced layoffs unless conditions change. The trade ministry is weighing three responses: a temporary tariff on imported panels, direct wage subsidies paid from general revenue to keep the factory competitive, or no intervention on the grounds that cheaper panels accelerate the country's own energy transition. Industry groups and installation companies are lobbying on opposite sides.

options.t_en: I support a temporary tariff. Four thousand jobs anchor the livelihoods of a whole surrounding community, and the low prices often rest on looser labor and environmental standards elsewhere; a five-year adjustment window for domestic industry beats letting it bleed out in a subsidy race.
options.t: 我支持临时关税。四千个岗位牵着一整片社区的生计，而低价往往来自别处更宽松的用工与环保标准；给本国产业一个五年的调整窗口，比让它在补贴竞赛里慢慢失血更实在。

options.t_en: I oppose the tariff. Panels thirty percent cheaper mean a third more clean electricity from the same budget, benefiting every electricity consumer and the climate targets; inflating every project to save one plant does not add up, and laid-off workers should be caught by retraining programs.
options.t: 我反对加税。组件便宜三成，意味着同样预算能多装三分之一的清洁电力，受益的是全体用电者和气候目标；为保住一个厂给所有项目加价，账算不过来，被裁的工人应该由再就业培训来接住。

options.t_en: I lean toward wage subsidies rather than tariffs. Tariffs push the cost straight onto downstream installers and users, while subsidies direct the money to the workers themselves and leave the firm's fate to market competition; for similar spending, one path builds a wall, the other props up people.
options.t: 我更倾向工资补贴而不是关税。关税把成本直接推给下游安装商和用户，补贴则把钱定向给工人本人，企业该不该继续存在仍由市场竞争说话；同样花的钱，一条路是筑墙，一条路是扶人。

options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.
options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。

scene: 城市边缘最后一块未开发湿地，是二十年间数量已减半的候鸟种群的栖息地。开发商提出在此建设物流园，可在青年失业率偏高的城区创造三千个岗位，并承诺在二十公里外出资建造一块等面积的人工湿地作为补偿。生态委员会自己的报告也承认，这种人工替代湿地从未被证明能容纳相同的物种。
scene_en: The last undeveloped wetland on the city's edge shelters a migratory bird population that has declined by half in twenty years. A developer proposes a logistics park that would create 3,000 jobs in a district where youth unemployment is high, offering to fund an artificial wetland of equal area twenty kilometers away as compensation. The ecology board's own report concedes the artificial replacement has never been shown to host the same species.

options.t_en: I would veto the project. The artificial wetland has never been shown to support the same birds, so equal area is not equal value; treating a habitat used for decades as an asset that can be rebuilt elsewhere is a premise that does not hold, and the jobs should be sited elsewhere.
options.t: 我会否决项目。人工湿地没被证明能养活同一种候鸟，『等面积』不等于等价值；把一片用了几十年的栖息地当成可以异地重建的资产，这个前提站不住，就业应该另找地块解决。

options.t_en: I would approve the project. Three thousand stable jobs matter enormously to this district, and with the bird population already halved by many pressures, losing this one site may not be the decisive blow; requiring the compensatory wetland to pass inspection before construction begins would limit the risk.
options.t: 我会批准项目。三千个稳定岗位对这个区太重要了，候鸟种群二十年已经减半，说明压力来自多方，缺这一块地未必是压垮它们的最后一根稻草；要求补偿湿地建好并通过验收后再开工，能把风险压低。

options.t_en: I would not vote with this gap in the evidence; I would first run a joint process of independent assessment and resident hearings — how much the birds still depend on this site, how viable the replacement wetland really is — and let the data and technical testimony come before any approval.
options.t: 我不会在证据缺口这么大时直接表决，会先启动独立评估加居民听证的联合程序：候鸟到底还依赖这块地多少、补偿湿地可行性多大，让数据和技术陈述先走完，再谈批不批。

options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.
options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。

scene: 一所成绩差距悬殊的中学，须从下学年起在两种模式中做选择。模式 A 按学科把学生分入快班与慢班，承诺进度更贴合、课堂更易管理；模式 B 保留混合班级，把同等预算转投课堂内的助教和面向全体的课后辅导。在一个年级试点的结果显示：模式 A 提高了尖子生的分数，但成绩末位四分之一学生的差距反而扩大。
scene_en: A middle school with wide achievement gaps must choose between two models from next year. Model A regroups students into faster and slower classes by subject, promising tailored pacing and easier classroom management. Model B keeps mixed-ability classes and redirects the same budget into in-class teaching assistants and after-school tutoring open to everyone. A pilot in one grade showed Model A raised top-student scores but widened the gap for bottom-quartile students.

options.t_en: I support ability grouping. In one classroom some students are lost while others are bored, and that wears on both; after regrouping, the slower classes can rebuild fundamentals at a fitting pace, and with periodic re-placement, landing in a lower group does not mean being stuck there.
options.t: 我支持分层教学。同一个教室里有人听不懂、有人吃不饱，对两边都是消耗；分层后慢班可以用更合适的节奏把基础补牢，配套定期流动机制，分进慢班不等于被固定在那里。

options.t_en: I support the mixed classes with tutors. The pilot already showed what tracking does to the bottom quartile, and a school's job includes the students who are hardest to teach; assistants inside the classroom lift everyone without sorting children by a test score at thirteen.
options.t: 我支持混合班加助教。试点已经展示了分层对末位四分之一学生做了什么，而学校的职责也包括最难教的学生；课堂里的助教能把所有人托起来，不必在十三岁就按一次考试分数给孩子分类。

options.t_en: I would take a third path: keep the mixed classes but open cross-grade electives and project tracks for students who finish early. Grouping solves pacing while mixed classes preserve the peer environment; giving fast learners an outlet has fewer side effects than splitting classes apart.
options.t: 我会选第三条路：保留混合班，但给先学完的学生开放跨年级选修和项目制通道。分层解决的是课堂节奏，混班保留的是同伴生态；给进度快的人一个出口，比把班级切开副作用更少。

options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.
options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。

scene: 一座小镇唯一的学校因入学人数跌破三十人而面临关停，主街一半的铺面空置。安置机构提议在五年内安置两百户新来家庭：学校得以保留、商铺有人接手，条件是镇里提供接待服务和语言课程。镇民大会上，老住户分成两派——一派怀念校园里重新有孩子的日子，另一派担心镇子的公共服务会被改变得比它能消化的更快。
scene_en: A small town's only school was slated for closure after enrollment fell below thirty students, and half the shops on the main street stand empty. A resettlement agency proposes housing 200 newcomer families over five years, which would keep the school open and fill the storefronts, provided the town supplies reception services and language classes. At the town meeting, long-time residents split between those who miss having children in the schoolyard and those who worry the town's services will change faster than it can absorb.

options.t_en: I support receiving them. Once the school closes, only the elderly remain, and in ten years even the supermarket leaves; two hundred families bring students, yes, but also a bakery, construction crews, and street life, and the language classes are an investment the town has owed for a while.
options.t: 我支持接收。学校关了，镇上就只剩老人，十年后连超市都会撤走；两百户家庭带来的不只是学生，还有面包店、工地和人气，配套的语言课是镇子本来就欠的一笔投入。

options.t_en: I support receiving them, but at half the scale and a slower pace. The school survives while the town's reception capacity is not pierced overnight; settle the first hundred families, get jobs and classes running, and only then talk about the next batch — steadier for everyone involved.
options.t: 我支持接收，但规模减半、节奏放慢。学校保住了，镇里的接待能力也不至于被一夜打穿；先来的一百户安顿好、就业和课程跑顺了，再谈下一批，对双方都更稳妥。

options.t_en: I would first ask the town itself. Whether the school stays and what the town becomes is the life of the people who have lived here longest; whether to sign the resettlement agreement should be decided by a vote of local residents, not settled for us by an outside agency and the county.
options.t: 我会先问镇民自己。学校要不要留、镇子要变成什么样，这是长期住在这里的人的生活；安置协议签不签，应该由本镇居民投票决定，而不是由外来的机构和县里替我们定。

options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.
options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。

scene: 你所在的公司宣布将在所有办公电脑上安装监控软件：记录活跃分钟数、应用使用情况，并定期截屏，汇入管理者可以查看的仪表盘。人事部门称其用意是发现过载、平衡工作量，而非追责。部署定在两周后，公司只安排了答疑会，并未征求员工同意。你和一位同事正在商量在员工大会上该持什么立场。
scene_en: Your company announces it will install monitoring software on all laptops: it tracks active minutes, application usage, and takes periodic screenshots, feeding a dashboard managers can view. HR says it is meant to flag overload and balance workloads, not to discipline. The rollout is scheduled in two weeks, and employees have been invited to a Q&A rather than asked to consent. You and a colleague are deciding what position to take at the staff meeting.

options.t_en: I would accept it, but only after three things are published: which fields are recorded, who can view them, and how long they are kept. If the data shows team-level load rather than scoring individuals, it can genuinely speak for overworked departments; boundaries in writing beat verbal reassurances.
options.t: 我会接受，但要求先公开三样东西：记录哪些字段、谁能查看、保留多久。如果数据只看团队整体负载而不是逐人打分，它确实能替忙闲不均的部门说话；写在纸上的边界比口头保证可靠。

options.t_en: I would oppose it outright. Screenshots and minute-level activity measure posture, not output; the most overloaded will not be spotted by it, only taught to perform busyness for the camera. How I work should not become a curve on a manager's dashboard.
options.t: 我会明确反对。截屏和逐分钟记录量度的是坐姿不是产出，过载最重的人不会被它发现，只会学会在镜头前表演忙碌；我自己怎么工作，不该变成管理者仪表盘上的一条曲线。

options.t_en: I would propose the middle path: aggregated anonymous statistics only, with no viewable per-person detail. Workload data is useful for scheduling, but there should be no archive of screenshots traceable to a named person; a solution with both benefits is technically straightforward.
options.t: 我会提议折中方案：只做匿名汇总统计，任何单个人的明细都不可查看。负荷数据对排班有用，但不该存在一份能点名到人的截屏档案；两全的做法在技术上完全做得到。

options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.
options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。

scene: 连环入室盗窃案后，市议会就青少年犯的处置展开辩论。一项提案扩大「恢复性司法」试点：年轻加害人与受害者见面，约定赔偿与社区服务，完成后撤销指控；两年的数据显示其再犯率低于走法院程序。另一项提案则规定无论年龄，第三次犯罪一律强制最低刑期收押。受害者联合会内部对两案也各有支持者。
scene_en: After a series of burglaries, your city council debates two responses to juvenile offenders. One proposal expands a restorative justice pilot where young offenders meet victims, agree on repayment and community service, and have charges dropped on completion; its two-year numbers show lower reoffending than court processing. The other sets mandatory minimum detention for any third offense regardless of age. The victims' association is itself split between the two camps.

options.t_en: I support expanding the restorative justice pilot. The two-year numbers are on the table: young people who complete the meeting-and-repayment process reoffend less. Detaining every third offender saves only present trouble and sends the bill back years later as a higher reoffending rate.
options.t: 我支持扩大恢复性司法试点。两年的数据摆在那里：走完见面赔偿程序的年轻人再犯更少；把第三次犯罪的人直接收押，省下的只是眼前的麻烦，账单会以更高的累犯率在几年后寄回来。

options.t_en: I support mandatory minimum detention. The pilot numbers look good, but they cover hand-picked minor cases; for a third-time burglar the community process has already given two chances. Residents need a clear floor — crossing it carries a certain consequence, and that certainty is itself the deterrent.
options.t: 我支持强制最低刑期。试点数据好看，但那是筛出来的轻案；对第三次入室盗窃的人，社区程序已经给过两次机会了。住户需要一条明确的底线——越线有确定的后果，这种确定性本身就是威慑。

options.t_en: I would first require an independent review of the pilot data for selection bias before voting. Both proposals rest on the same figure; if the case-selection was skewed, expanding the pilot or mandating detention could both be doubling down on a wrong premise. One month for a clean basis is worth it.
options.t: 我会先要求独立复核试点数据的抽样偏差，再回来表决。两边的方案都建立在同一个数字上，如果挑案标准偏了，扩大试点和强制收押都可能是在错误前提下加码；多花一个月换一个干净的依据，值得。

options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.
options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。

scene: 一座中型城市须为紧邻轨道交通的街区更新区划，该街区现以独栋住宅和空地为主。方案 A 允许建中层公寓楼，其中三成单元必须以低于市场的租金出租；方案 B 维持低层区划，但把地块切分成入门级小住宅的开发商可免缴各项费用。六年间全市房租上涨四成，而数十年前在此购房的业主对两个方案都反对。
scene_en: A mid-sized city must update its zoning for a transit-adjacent district currently occupied by single-family homes and empty lots. Plan A allows mid-rise apartment blocks with a mandatory 30% of units rented below market. Plan B keeps the low-rise zoning but waives fees for builders who subdivide lots into affordable starter homes. Rents in the city have risen forty percent in six years, and the district's homeowners, who bought decades ago, oppose both plans.

options.t_en: I support Plan A. Mid-rise buildings at the transit stop with a third of units rent-capped is the only path on the table that actually adds supply; a forty percent rent rise will not be chased back by waiving a few fees, and longtime homeowners' streetscape should not be subsidized by every renter in the city.
options.t: 我支持方案 A。地铁口建六层的楼、其中三成租金受限，是眼下唯一能让供给真正增加的路径；房租涨四成不是靠免几笔费用能追回来的，老业主的街区景观不该由全城的租客补贴。

options.t_en: I support Plan B. The fee waiver buys starter homes that genuinely belong to their occupants, and the neighborhood's street scale and social fabric stay intact; the mid-rise plan would turn the district into a transient corridor for renters, and the shadow of six stories falls on someone else's yard first.
options.t: 我支持方案 B。免费用换来的是真正属于自住者的小住宅，本地的街道尺度和社区结构不被推平；高楼方案会把这个街区变成租客轮换的过渡带，而六层楼的影子先落在别人家院子里。

options.t_en: I find both plans too timid and would propose handing the lots to a community land trust: publicly held land, saleable homes, prices indexed to local median income. It addresses supply and affordability at once, does not depend on a one-time waiver, and benefits residents twenty years out as well.
options.t: 两个方案我都嫌不够，会提议把地块交给社区土地信托：土地公共持有、房屋可售、价格与本地中位收入挂钩。供给和可负担同时解决，也不依赖一次性的费用减免，二十年后的住户同样受益。

options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.
options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。

scene: 一种真菌病害正在全国麦田蔓延，预计下季减产最高可达两成。公共研究机构（而非外国专利持有方）已培育出抗病的基因编辑品种，农业部须做决定：赶在本季快速批准；先进行两季完整的田间公开试验；或批准种植但强制设隔离带与标识，同时持续监测。农民合作社与消费者团体提交了针锋相对的意见。
scene_en: A fungal disease is spreading through the country's wheat fields, with yield losses projected up to a fifth next season. A gene-edited resistant variety exists — developed in a public institute, not a foreign patent holder — and the agriculture ministry must decide: fast-track approval for this season, run two full seasons of open field trials first, or approve with mandatory buffer strips and labeling while monitoring runs. Farmer cooperatives and consumer groups filed opposing comments.

options.t_en: I would fast-track approval. Twenty percent of the harvest is not an abstraction; it is small farms' entire cash flow for a year. The variety comes from a public institute with no patent lock attached, and every season the disease spreads, the cost of waiting lands on those least able to pay it.
options.t: 我会走快速批准。两成收成不是抽象数字，是很多小农一整年的现金流；这个品种出自公共机构、不附带专利锁，病害每多扩散一季，等待的代价就落在最付不起的人头上。

options.t_en: I would insist on two full seasons of open trials. Even a public-institute variety must answer questions about gene flow and long-term soil effects; a year of losses can be buffered from reserves and imports, but once an unverified variety is rolled out at scale, there is no pulling it back.
options.t: 我会坚持先做两季田间试验。公共机构出的品种也要回答基因漂流和长期土壤影响的问题；病害损失可以靠储备和进口缓冲一年，但一个没验证过的品种一旦大面积铺开，出了问题收不回来。

options.t_en: I would take conditional approval: buffer strips, mandatory labeling, season-by-season monitoring published in an annual report. The disease will not wait two years, and consumers' right to know should not be skipped either; planting starts under controlled conditions, the data speaks, and the rules can tighten or loosen at any time.
options.t: 我会选带条件的批准：设隔离带、强制标识、逐季监测并在年报公开。病害等不了两年，消费者的知情权也不该被跳过；让种植在受控条件下开始，数据说话，规则随时可以收紧或放开。

options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.
options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。

scene: 全国最大的地方报业集团被一家同时经营博彩门店和房产门户网站的控股公司悄然收购，编辑人员反映针对这些行业的报道正受到越来越大的软化压力。议会委员会提出三种对策：设立公共利益基金，用平台税收入补贴地方新闻；出台透明度规则，强制报业集团在每篇文章页面公示所有权与收入来源；或者不干预，把并购视为市场事务。
scene_en: The country's largest regional newspaper chain has been quietly acquired by a holding company that also owns betting shops and real-estate portals, and editorial staff report growing pressure to soften coverage of those industries. A parliamentary committee proposes three remedies: a public interest fund that subsidizes local news with money raised from platform levies, a transparency rule forcing chains to publish ownership and revenue sources on every article page, or no intervention, treating consolidation as a market matter.

options.t_en: I support the public interest fund. Council meetings and court coverage by local reporters carry no advertising value, and the market was never going to sustain them; topping them up from a platform levy is simply acknowledging that reality. Money distributed by an independent committee with an editorial-independence clause keeps it from becoming an official mouthpiece.
options.t: 我支持公共利益基金。地方记者跑的市政会和法院新闻没有广告价值，市场本来就养不起，靠平台税输血只是承认这个现实；钱由独立委员会分发、附编辑独立条款，就不会变成官方喉舌。

options.t_en: I support the transparency rule over subsidies. Who owns the paper and where the money comes from, printed under every article, lets readers weigh it themselves; once government starts paying and picking media, however pretty the clauses, the list of subsidized outlets is itself a form of influence.
options.t: 我支持透明度规则而不是补贴。谁拥有这张报、钱从哪来，印在每篇文章下面，读者自己会掂量分量；一旦政府开始发钱挑媒体，无论条款写得多好看，接受补贴的名单本身就是一种影响。

options.t_en: I would choose no intervention. Readers have already voted with subscriptions, and local papers that cannot survive show where demand has moved; government stepping into the media market means deciding for readers what they should see, and consolidation itself has stopped no one from launching a new paper.
options.t: 我会选不干预。读者已经用订阅量投过票，办不下去的本地报说明需求在转移；政府接手媒体市场，等于替读者决定他们该看什么，而并购本身并没有阻止任何人另办一份新报。

options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.
options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。

scene: 养老金精算报告预测十四年后出现缺口：要么退休年龄提高两岁，要么缴费率上调 2.5 个百分点并由雇主与员工均摊，要么把定额普享养老金改为对最高四分之一领取者做资产审查。从事重体力、预期寿命更短的农村劳动者在听证中陈情：延退对他们打击最重。
scene_en: The state pension fund's actuary projects a shortfall in fourteen years: either the retirement age rises by two years, contribution rates rise by 2.5 points split evenly between employers and workers, or the flat universal pension becomes means-tested for the top quartile of retirees. Rural workers with physically heavy jobs and shorter life expectancy have testified that a later retirement age falls hardest on them.

options.t_en: I would raise contribution rates. If the shortfall is a money problem, solve it with money; asking today's workers to chip in a bit more is fairer than making bricklayers haul for ten extra years. Splitting it between employers and workers spreads the pain thinly and avoids a tiered system where the long-lived collect and the short-lived never do.
options.t: 我会选提高缴费率。缺口是钱的问题，就该用钱解决，让现在工作的人多缴一点比让砌砖工多搬十年砖公平；分摊到雇主和员工两头，账面痛苦最小，也不会出现长寿者领得多、短寿者领不到的分层。

options.t_en: I support means-testing. Having affluent pensioners keep full universal benefits amounts to young contributors transfusing people who do not need it; concentrating the savings on those who actually lack money lets the same budget catch twice as many at the bottom.
options.t: 我支持资产审查。让高退休金的富裕老人继续拿全额普享金，等于让年轻缴费者给不需要的人输血；把省下的钱集中给手头真正拮据的人，同样的预算能多兜住一倍的底。

options.t_en: I would raise the retirement age, with an early-retirement track for heavy physical jobs. Life expectancy has grown, and a scheme designed fourteen years ago cannot carry today; the problem is not the later age itself but the one-size-fits-all — tiering by occupation and contribution years is more sustainable than oscillating between rates and benefits.
options.t: 我会支持延退，但给重体力劳动者留提前退休通道。寿命在延长，十四年前定的方案撑不到今天；问题不在延退本身，而在一刀切——按职业和缴费年限分档，比在缴费率和待遇之间反复摇摆更可持续。

options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.
options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。

scene: 一项全国性照护假制度正在设计中，允许员工休带薪假期照料重病的父母或配偶。桌上有三种筹资模式：雇主责任制，由各企业自行承担自家员工的假期待遇；全体雇主共同缴费的社会保险池；以及自愿参与、对提供该假期的企业给予税收抵免的制度。小企业主警告，雇主责任制会让他们在招聘处于照护年龄段的员工时更犹豫。
scene_en: A new national care leave scheme is being designed to let workers take paid weeks to look after a seriously ill parent or spouse. Three financing models are on the table: employer mandates, where each company pays its own employees' leave; a social insurance pool shared by all employers; or a voluntary system with tax credits for companies that offer it. Small businesses warn the mandate model will make them hesitant to hire workers of caregiving age.

options.t_en: I support the social insurance pool. Care is something everyone meets eventually, and pooling it across all employers means no single company is punished for hiring someone with a sick parent; a uniform standard also spares small firms from paying on a different scale than large corporations.
options.t: 我支持社会保险池。照护是每个人迟早会遇到的，成本摊到全体雇主头上，没有哪家企业会因为雇了要照顾父母的人而被单独惩罚；统一标准也让小企业不必和大公司按不同口径掏钱。

options.t_en: I support the voluntary tax-credit model. Whether to offer the benefit should follow each firm's capacity — those who can afford it get the credit, those who cannot face no forced bill; leaving the choice to the market is more workable than drawing a hard line that everyone groans at.
options.t: 我支持税收抵免的自愿模式。要不要给员工这个福利，让企业按自己的承受力决定，给得起的得到减税，给不起的没有被强制的账单；把选择留给市场，比划一条人人叫苦的硬线更实际。

options.t_en: I would choose the employer mandate with state payment on behalf of small businesses. Responsibility belongs with the party in the most direct relationship of benefit — the firm that profits from an employee's stability should pay; with the treasury covering firms under twenty staff, the discrimination small businesses warn of is defused.
options.t: 我会选雇主责任制，但配套中小企业国家代缴。责任就该由受益关系最直接的一方承担——谁的企业享受了员工留下的稳定，谁就该付费；对雇员少于二十人的企业由财政接手，就能把警告中的歧视压下去。

options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.
options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。

scene: 在对大型繁殖场条件的调查曝光后，市议会将就是否禁止零售商业繁殖机构的幼犬幼猫进行表决。宠物店此后只能展示收容所动物；购买者仍可直接向持证繁殖者购买。店主表示该禁令切断了他们的主要收入线，却对无证的网络卖家毫无作用，而收容所的接收量已经翻倍。
scene_en: A city council is voting on banning retail sales of puppies and kittens from commercial breeding facilities, following investigations into conditions at large-scale breeders. Pet stores would be limited to showcasing shelter animals; buyers could still purchase directly from licensed breeders. Store owners say the ban closes their main revenue line while doing nothing about unlicensed online sellers, and shelter intake has already doubled.

options.t_en: I support the ban. A puppy in a shop window is itself a demand engine — the passerby paying at the counter has no idea of the conditions behind it; cutting off the smoothest retail channel redirects demand toward shelters, which is exactly where the doubled intake is waiting.
options.t: 我支持禁令。橱窗里的幼犬本身就是需求引擎——路过付钱的人不知道背后是什么条件；切断零售这条最顺的路，需求才会流向收容所，正好接住已经翻倍的接收量。

options.t_en: I oppose the ban. Licensed breeders lose their only open sales channel and the trade merely moves into harder-to-police private messages online; if the target is breeding mills, the answer is enforcement capacity against unlicensed sellers, not closing the shops that follow the rules — while the extra shelter load lands on the budget and on volunteers.
options.t: 我反对禁令。持证繁殖者失去唯一的公开销售渠道，交易只会转入更难查的网络私信；要解决繁殖场，就该扩编执法去查处无证卖家，而不是把守规矩的店关门——同时多出来的收容压力最后由财政和志愿者买单。

options.t_en: I would back the middle path: no ban, but require stores to display each puppy's breeder registration and inspection records, and give shelter animals equal window space. With the information level, consumer choice means something; a blanket ban only pushes the trade into the shadows.
options.t: 我会支持折中方案：不禁售，但要求宠物店对每只幼犬公示繁殖场编号与实地检查记录，并给收容所动物同样的橱窗位置。信息摆平了，消费者的选择才有意义；一刀切只会把生意推进阴影里。

options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.
options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。

scene: 市中心一座 1920 年代的电影院已空置九年，修缮预算是拆除费用的四倍。议会须在三者中选择：全额修缮并配套十年文化补贴；拆除后建设含八十套住宅的商业住宅综合体；或适应性再利用——保留立面与前厅、在其后建住宅——成本高于拆除但低于全额修缮。遗产团体与住房倡导组织各自动员。
scene_en: A 1920s picture palace in the city center has stood empty for nine years; restoration estimates run to four times the budget of demolishing it. The council must choose: full restoration with a ten-year cultural subsidy, demolition for a mixed housing-and-retail block with 80 apartments, or adaptive reuse — keeping the facade and foyer while building housing behind — which costs more than demolition but less than full restoration. Heritage groups and housing advocates are mobilizing separately.

options.t_en: I support full restoration. A city can grow few things of its own; a domed ceiling built with ninety-year-old craft, once demolished, is gone, while eighty apartments can be built on any plot. The subsidy spread over ten years comes to what a mid-tier road resurfacing costs anyway.
options.t: 我支持全额修缮。一座城市能自己长出来的东西不多，九十年前手艺做的穹顶拆了就是拆了，八十套公寓在哪个地块都能盖；文化补贴十年摊下来，其实只是一条中等道路的养护预算。

options.t_en: I would choose demolition. What a building empty for nine years supports is moss and debt; eighty apartments are the daily lives of eighty households. A city's memory lives in things still in use, not in a facade standing guard for someone's nostalgia.
options.t: 我会选拆除。空了九年的建筑养着的只有苔藓和债务，八十套住宅是八十户人家的生活；城市记忆靠的是还在被使用的东西，不是一堵替谁怀旧站岗的立面。

options.t_en: I support adaptive reuse. With the facade and foyer kept, the block keeps its historic character, and the eighty apartments shrink to sixty-something after the added cost; each camp takes most of what it wanted, and a plan like this is the one most likely to survive both the budget and the vote.
options.t: 我支持适应性再利用。立面和前厅留下，街区的历史感还在，八十套住宅扣掉增量成本后仍能建六十几套；两个阵营各拿走大半想要的东西，这种方案在预算和投票上都最容易活下来。

options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.
options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。

scene: 全区唯一的养老院因无法达到新的人员配置标准即将关停，九十位在住老人大多来自周边村庄。县里提出三种应对：补贴老人入住六十公里外的区域养老院并安排每周班车；发放居家照护包，为照料亲人的家庭成员支付照护者工资；或将关停建筑改造为代际共居住所，学生以免租入住、提供夜间值守换取住宿。
scene_en: The district's only nursing home will close because it cannot meet new staffing standards; its ninety residents come mostly from surrounding villages. The county proposes three responses: subsidized places at a regional facility sixty kilometers away with a weekly shuttle, a home-care package paying family members a caregiver wage, or converting the closing building into an intergenerational residence where students live rent-free alongside elderly residents in exchange for overnight support hours.

options.t_en: I support the regional facility with the shuttle. Professional care belongs in professionally staffed settings — what the new standards demand is not something a village annex can provide; distance can be patched with shuttles and travel subsidies, and care quality is not something to gamble against pressure sores.
options.t: 我支持区域养老院加班车。专业的事交给专业配置——新标准要求的东西，村庄小院给不了；距离可以用班车和探亲补贴补，护理质量不能拿老人的褥疮风险去赌。

options.t_en: I would choose the caregiver wage. Most of the ninety want to stay in their own villages, and spouses and children are already providing the care — it simply has never counted as labor. Paying them costs less than uprooting the elderly sixty kilometers away, and meets far less resistance.
options.t: 我会选居家照护工资。九十位老人里大多数想留在自己村庄，配偶和子女的照料本就在发生，只是从没被算作劳动；把工资给他们，比把老人连根拔到六十公里外便宜，也遇到更少的抵抗。

options.t_en: I would try the intergenerational residence. Students need housing and the elderly need someone to answer the door at night — the two gaps fit together. It will not substitute for heavy-care nursing, but as a low-cost first layer it keeps in town those who can be kept.
options.t: 我会试代际共居。学生要住处，老人要夜里有人应门，两个缺口正好对上；它替代不了重度失能的照护，但作为低成本的第一层，先把能留在镇上的老人留下来。

options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.
options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。

scene: 州议会正就短期贷款机构的利率上限展开辩论。若将年化利率上限设为 36%，州内多数发薪日贷款门店将停业；邻州的研究结论不一——部分显示借款人转向透支和无证网络放贷，部分显示家庭财务状况改善。放贷方主张，该上限会切断被银行拒绝的借款人唯一能获得的正规信贷；消费者组织则反驳称，这类产品从设计上就让借款人陷入反复续借。
scene_en: A state legislature is debating a cap on short-term lenders' interest rates. A 36% APR cap would shut down most payday storefronts in the state; research from neighboring states is split — some shows borrowers shifted to overdrafts and unlicensed online lenders, some shows household finances improved. Lenders argue the cap removes the only formal credit available to borrowers banks refuse; consumer groups counter that the product is engineered to trap borrowers in repeat borrowing.

options.t_en: I support the cap. A product at three to four hundred percent annualized is not lending; it is hunting the people most vulnerable in the days before payday. As for those who shifted to unlicensed lenders in neighboring states, that precisely shows a formal alternative — such as small postal-savings loans — needs to be built alongside.
options.t: 我支持设上限。年化三、四百个百分点的产品不是在放贷，是在围猎发薪日前后最脆弱的一群人；邻州研究里转向无证放贷的那部分人，恰恰说明正规替代渠道——比如邮政储蓄小额贷——需要一起补上。

options.t_en: I oppose the one-size cap. Risk-based pricing is not greed, and people banks refuse also face emergencies; close the storefronts and what they face is offshore online lenders and bounced checks at even higher cost. Better to keep the stores and mandate disclosure of the true annualized rate.
options.t: 我反对一刀切的上限。风险定价不是贪婪，银行不借的人也要有地方应急；把门店关掉，他们面对的就是境外的网络放贷和被退回的支票，成本只会更高。宁可保留门店并强制披露真实年化利率。

options.t_en: I would back a public alternative: small emergency loans from a state bank and credit unions at rates covering cost, then let that real cost benchmark discipline market pricing. No need to pick between banning and tolerating first — put a borrowable option on the table.
options.t: 我会支持公共替代方案：由州立银行和信用社开设小额应急贷，利率覆盖成本即可，再用这个真实成本去约束市场定价。不必先在禁止和放任之间选边，先把借得起的选择摆上桌。

options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.
options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。

scene: 河畔街区八年内三次被淹，新修订的洪泛区地图刚把街区大半划入高风险区，保险费翻倍。县里为居民提供了两项计划的选择：按灾前市值自愿收购、土地退还为湿地；或堤防加房屋抬高的工程方案，保住每一栋房子，但每户成本是收购方案的四倍，且需要发行公债通过全民投票。
scene_en: A riverside neighborhood has flooded three times in eight years, and the floodplain map just redrew most of it into the high-risk zone, doubling insurance premiums. The county offers residents a choice between two programs: voluntary buyouts at pre-flood market value with the land returned to wetland, or a levee-and-elevation program that protects every house but costs four times as much per household and needs a bond referendum to pass.

options.t_en: I would take the buyout and move. After the third flood I no longer have faith in 'this time it's different'; money in hand and a new house on higher ground beats betting again on a levee's approval and construction schedule, and the restored wetland would also hold water for downstream.
options.t: 我会接受收购方案搬走。第三次被淹之后，我对『这次不一样』的说法已经没有信心；钱落袋、新家在坡上，比再赌一轮堤坝的批复和施工期实在，恢复的湿地还能替下游分洪。

options.t_en: I support the levee program and will vote for the bond. The neighborhood took generations to build, and its school, congregation, and neighbor networks do not relocate; per household it costs four times as much, but the ledger on buying out a rooted community has never been only the budget line.
options.t: 我支持堤防方案并会投公债赞成票。街区是几代人攒出来的，学校、教堂和邻居网络搬不走；按户算账贵四倍，但把一个扎了根的社区连根买断，这笔账从来不只写在预算表里。

options.t_en: I would push to merge the two: build the levee to hold a five-year protection window while keeping the voluntary buyout open to those who want out, with proportions set by uptake. A program forcing one answer on everyone is the most fragile kind, both in a flood and at the ballot box.
options.t: 我会推动两案合并：先修堤防保住五年的防护窗口，同时保留自愿收购给想走的人，比例由报名情况决定。强制所有人给同一个答案的方案，在洪水面前和投票箱前都最脆弱。

options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.
options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。

scene: 一项议会法案要求达到用户规模门槛的平台，在安全审查框架下向认证研究者开放数据访问以研究算法对用户的影响，拒绝配合将被处以罚款。平台代表称该强制要求侵犯用户隐私与商业机密，不可接受；研究者则指出平台自身泄露的内部研究显示，其提升使用时长的功能所产生的效应从未被公司公布。你的选区议员下月将对法案投票。
scene_en: A parliamentary bill would require platforms above a user threshold to grant accredited researchers data access to study algorithmic effects on users, under security review, with fines for refusal. Platform representatives call the mandate an unacceptable breach of user privacy and trade secrets; researchers point to the platform's own leaked internal studies showing engagement-optimizing features whose effects the company never published. Your representative will vote on the bill next month.

options.t_en: I support the bill. A platform that ran its own internal studies and withheld them has demonstrated that voluntary transparency does not arrive on its own; security review and researcher accreditation already narrow the avenues for abuse, and the 'privacy' being refused looks more like trade secrets under another name.
options.t: 我支持法案。平台自己做过内部研究又压着不发的行为说明，指望自愿透明等不来；安全审查和研究者认证已经把滥用路径收窄了，被拒绝的这份「隐私」更像商业机密换了个名字。

options.t_en: I oppose the mandated access. User data and recommendation weights are a platform's core assets and security perimeter, and bulk researcher access opens a door no one can fully watch; the same goal is reachable through voluntary agreements and industry standards, while the bill only drives smaller platforms out of the market.
options.t: 我反对强制开放。用户数据和推荐权重是平台最核心的资产与安全边界，给研究者批量访问等于开一道谁也无法全程盯着的门；同样的目标可以用自愿协议加行业标准达到，法案只会把中小平台逼出市场。

options.t_en: I would demand one revision first: access runs inside a third-party escrow environment, outputs are statistics only with no raw records leaving, and platforms bear the cost. Research gets done while personal detail never leaves the room — a version like this outlives the next administration better than the bill's pass-or-veto framing.
options.t: 我会要求先修一版：数据访问在第三方托管环境内进行、输出只给统计结果不给原始记录、费用由平台承担。研究能做，个人明细不落外人手里，这一版比原案「要么过、要么否」的框架更经得起换届。

options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.
options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。

scene: 一个世居语言少数群体约占所在地区人口 8%，向地区政府提交请愿：在其聚居的四个区，市政服务、法庭程序与官方标识应提供其语言版本，费用由地区预算承担。多数语言的媒体担心这会形成平行行政体系，而该群体指出，宪法中的文化权利条款八十年来从未被真正落实。
scene_en: A regional government must rule on a petition from a long-established linguistic minority, about 8% of the region, asking that municipal services, court proceedings, and official signage be available in their language in the four districts where they are concentrated, with costs met by the regional budget. The majority-language press argues this will create parallel administration, while the minority notes the constitutional clause on cultural rights has never been operationalized in eighty years.

options.t_en: I support implementing it in the four districts. A constitutional clause on the books for eighty years should not remain decoration; the language of public services decides whether an elderly person can see a doctor alone and whether a witness can testify accurately in court — these are administrative costs, not favors.
options.t: 我支持在四个聚居区落实。宪法写了八十年的条款不该永远是装饰；公共服务用谁的语言，决定的是老人能不能独自看病、证人能不能在法庭上准确作证——这些是行政成本，不是恩惠。

options.t_en: I support language learning over bilingual administration. Eighty years of shared life has produced one common working language; split services into two tracks and the clearer the border, the smaller both communities' radius of movement. The budget works harder on schools and translation subsidies than on restructuring administration.
options.t: 我支持学习语言而不是双语行政。八十年的共同生活已经形成了一个统一的工作语言；服务分成两套，边界划得越清楚，两个群体各自的移动半径就越小。预算花在语言学校和翻译补贴上，比改行政体系更有效。

options.t_en: I would approve bilingual services and court proceedings, and leave signage to each district. Rights-related procedures must be within everyone's reach, while the street-level language landscape is something local majorities and minorities can negotiate; passing the whole package turns a negotiable matter into wholesale confrontation.
options.t: 我会批准服务与法庭的双语，标识则交由各区自行决定。涉及权利的程序必须人人可达，街头的语言景观则让当地多数与少数协商；一揽子通过只会把可谈的事变成全面对抗。

options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.
options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。

scene_en: The logistics company you work for has rolled out an AI system that scores warehouse staff continuously from scanner logs, camera feeds and task timers. Every Friday the lowest-scoring decile automatically receives warning letters, and the scores feed into promotion and shift assignments. The union demands that the scoring criteria be published and that every worker be able to appeal to a human reviewer within 48 hours. Management replies that the algorithm is more even-handed than supervisor intuition, that exposing the criteria would let some staff game the system, and that a 48-hour appeal right would swamp the floor managers. You have been elected as one of the worker representatives in the negotiation.
scene: 你所在的物流公司上线了一套 AI 系统，通过扫描记录、摄像头画面与任务计时持续为仓库员工打分。每周五得分最低的一成员工会自动收到警告信，分数同时进入晋升与排班决策。工会要求公司公开打分标准，并保证每位员工能在四十八小时内向人工复核员申诉。管理层回应称，算法比主管的个人印象更公平，公开标准会让部分员工钻空子，而四十八小时申诉权会让基层主管不堪重负。你被同事推选为谈判中的员工代表。

options.t_en: I will hold firm on the union's full demand. Workers cannot contest what they cannot see, so the criteria must be published and every score appealable to a human within days. If that slows the system down, that is a cost the company accepted when it chose to rank people automatically.
options.t: 我会坚持工会的完整要求。看不见标准就谈不上申辩，打分依据必须公开，每个分数都要能在几天内找到人工复核。如果这会让系统慢下来，那是公司选择自动给人排名时就该承担的成本。

options.t_en: I will tell the union to accept the system. A transparent rule applied to everyone treats long-timers and newcomers alike, while supervisor discretion in the old days quietly favoured whoever got along with the shift lead. Keeping the exact weights internal is a reasonable trade for that consistency.
options.t: 我会劝工会接受这套系统。对所有人一视同仁的透明规则，反而比过去主管凭交情排班的做法更公平；至于把具体权重留在公司内部，我认为是换取这种一致性的合理代价。

options.t_en: I will push for a middle clause: the company publishes the categories it measures and their rough weights, but not the model itself, and an appeal board with two workers and one manager reviews contested scores monthly. If the board finds repeated errors, the burden shifts to the company to fix the model.
options.t: 我会争取一个折中条款：公司公开它测量的维度和大致权重，但不公开模型本身；同时设立由两名员工和一名主管组成的申诉委员会，按月复核有争议的分数。一旦发现同一类错误反复出现，修正模型的举证责任就转到公司一方。

options.t_en: I don't feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.
options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。

scene_en: Your city has a one-off budget surplus and must choose between two child-focused schemes: a universal child allowance paid to every family with children regardless of income, or housing vouchers restricted to low-income renters, distributed through a means test. The universal scheme's backers argue that means-tested programs shed eligible families through paperwork, stigma and changing circumstances, while everyone pays taxes and everyone's children should benefit. The voucher scheme's backers argue that with a fixed budget, concentrating the money on the families paying more than a third of their income in rent helps the most distressed far more per unit of money. The council will decide next month.
scene: 你所在的城市有一笔一次性预算结余，需要在两个面向儿童的方案之间做出选择：一是全民儿童津贴，凡有孩子的家庭无论收入高低一律发放；二是只面向低收入租房家庭的住房券，须经家计调查才能领取。全民方案的拥护者认为，家计调查会因表格繁琐、 stigma 压力和生活变动把本该受益的家庭筛掉，而人人都纳税，孩子们也都该受益。住房券方案的拥护者则认为，预算固定的情况下，把钱集中给那些房租超过收入三分之一的家庭，每一块钱能帮到最困难的人更多。议会将于下月表决。

options.t_en: I will vote for the universal allowance. Every screening process has leaks at its edges, and the families that fall through — informal workers, newly separated parents, people who distrust forms — are usually the ones already struggling. A payment that reaches everyone needs no gatekeeper.
options.t: 我会投给全民津贴。任何审核流程都会在边缘漏人，而漏掉的那些——打零工的、刚离婚的、不敢跟表格打交道的——往往本来就是最吃力的人。一笔发给所有人的钱不需要任何守门人。

options.t_en: I will vote for the housing vouchers. The same budget spent on everyone leaves the family paying half its income in rent with pocket change, and I would rather a smaller number of households get out of crisis than every household get a token amount. The test is worth the paperwork.
options.t: 我会投给住房券。同样一笔钱摊给所有人，那个房租吃掉一半收入的家庭只能分到零头；我宁愿让少一些家庭真正脱离危机，也不愿所有家庭都拿到一笔不痛不痒的钱。为这个目标，审核手续是值得的。

options.t_en: I will propose a hybrid: a smaller universal payment funded first, with the remainder concentrated as housing top-ups for the highest rent burdens, using tax records to pre-enroll families so almost no separate application is needed.
options.t: 我会提出一个混合方案：先保证一笔较小的全民津贴，剩余的钱集中用于房租负担最重家庭的住房补差，并直接调取税务记录为家庭自动登记，几乎不需要另行申请。

options.t_en: I can't really take a side here — I don't know enough about this to judge.
options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。

scene_en: Parliament is debating a package of tariffs and production subsidies to shield domestic solar panel factories from imports sold below estimated cost. The manufacturers warn that three plants employing 12,000 people will close within two years without protection, and that the country's panel supply should not depend on a single foreign production chain. Importers and installation companies counter that tariffs would raise panel prices for households and slow the national installation rate, and that subsidy races between governments mostly burn public money while production simply relocates. You sit on the committee that must recommend a position.
scene: 议会正在讨论一组关税与生产补贴方案，用以保护本国光伏组件工厂免受低于估算成本进口产品的冲击。厂商警告说，若无保护，三家共雇佣一万二千人的工厂将在两年内关闭，且本国组件供应不应系于单一的外国产业链。进口商与安装企业则反驳，关税会抬高家庭采购组件的价格、拖慢全国安装进度，而各国之间的补贴竞赛大多在烧公共财政，产业却只是换个地方生产。你是负责给出建议的委员会成员。

options.t_en: I will recommend the tariffs plus subsidies. Once the domestic plants and their trained workforce are gone, rebuilding them will cost far more than the price difference on panels, and a country that cannot make its own energy equipment negotiates every future contract from weakness.
options.t: 我会建议采用关税加补贴。国内工厂和熟练工人一旦流失，重建的代价将远超组件上的差价，而一个连能源设备都要依赖别国的国家，在未来的每一场谈判里都会处于下风。

options.t_en: I will recommend against the tariffs. Households pay for protection either at the register or through taxes, and history suggests the subsidized plants will lobby for renewal every few years. I would rather spend the same money directly on installation incentives that cut bills regardless of where panels come from.
options.t: 我会建议不加关税。保护的成本终究由家庭支付——要么在货架上，要么在税单里，而且经验表明受补贴的工厂每隔几年就会游说延期。我宁愿把同样的钱直接投进安装补贴，让电费账单下降，而不在乎组件产自哪里。

options.t_en: I will recommend skipping tariffs but funding time-limited support for domestic factory retooling and worker retraining, reviewed publicly every two years so the subsidy must show results to continue.
options.t: 我会建议不设关税，但为国内工厂的技术改造和工人转岗培训设立限期资金支持，每两年公开评估一次——补贴要想延续，就得拿得出成效。

options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I'd handle it some other way entirely.
options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。

scene_en: The port authority proposes a deep-water expansion onto a coastal wetland that hosts hundreds of thousands of migratory birds each year and is listed under an international conservation convention. The expansion is projected to create 3,000 direct jobs in a region where youth unemployment is high, and the authority offers to fund an artificial wetland in a neighbouring estuary as an offset. Ornithologists respond that no artificial site has yet been shown to replace this wetland's function for the bird populations that depend on it. The provincial cabinet must approve or reject the plan this quarter.
scene: 港务局提出在一片滨海湿地上进行深水港扩建，这片湿地每年承载数十万只候鸟，并被列入一项国际保护公约。扩建预计将在青年失业率偏高的地区直接创造三千个岗位，港务局还承诺出资在邻近河口建造一片人工湿地作为补偿。鸟类学家回应说，迄今没有任何人工湿地被证明能够替代这片湿地对依赖它的鸟类种群的功能。省内阁必须在本季度内批准或否决该方案。

options.t_en: I will approve the expansion with strict conditions: construction phased away from migration season, the offset wetland built and monitored before the first dredge, and an independent ecological audit with the power to halt works. Jobs in that region will not wait for a perfect answer.
options.t: 我会在严格条件下批准扩建：施工避开候鸟迁徙季、补偿湿地在第一次清淤前建成并接受监测、设立有权叫停工程的独立生态审计。那个地区的就业问题，等不来一个完美答案。

options.t_en: I will reject the plan. An offset is only a promise on paper until a bird population actually uses the new site, and the species that stop here cannot re-route once the mudflats are gone. Port capacity can grow elsewhere; a stopover site used for millennia cannot be rebuilt.
options.t: 我会否决该方案。在鸟类真的开始使用新地点之前，所谓补偿只是纸面承诺，而一旦滩涂消失，在此停歇的物种没有第二条路线可走。港口吞吐能力可以另找地方扩展，但使用了上千年的候鸟中转站无法重建。

options.t_en: I will support a smaller single-berth version on already-degraded parts of the site, with the untouched core wetland legally protected as a permanent reserve and the jobs estimate re-published honestly at the smaller scale.
options.t: 我会支持一个规模更小的单泊位版本，只占用场址内已经退化的部分，同时把未触动的核心湿地区以法律形式永久保护起来，并按缩小后的规模重新如实公布就业预期。

options.t_en: I'm genuinely indifferent — this barely affects my life either way.
options.t: 我确实无所谓，这事对生活影响不大。

scene_en: The national school board must decide the fate of the standardized exit examination taken by all eighteen-year-olds. A review found grade differences between schools have widened so much that transcripts are no longer comparable, and selective universities now weight the exam heavily. A proposal would abolish the exam and let schools certify students through coursework, projects and teacher assessments. Teachers' colleges support the change, saying one exam narrows teaching to test drills; university admissions officers warn they have no reliable way to compare applicants from 4,000 schools with different standards.
scene: 全国教育委员会必须决定年满十八岁学生统一参加的标准化结业考试的存废。一份评估发现，不同学校之间的分数差距已扩大到成绩单无法横向比较的程度，选拔型大学因此越来越倚重这门考试。一项提案主张废除该考试，改由各校通过课程作业、项目与教师评语为学生出具认证。师范院校支持这一改变，认为单一考试把教学压缩成了应试训练；大学招生部门则警告，面对四千所标准各异的学校，他们没有可靠的办法横向比较申请者。

options.t_en: I will keep the common exam. However imperfect, it is the one measure applied identically to a student from a wealthy district and one from a poor one; replacing it with school-based grades would make family background and school reputation weigh even more heavily.
options.t: 我会保留统一考试。它再不完美，也是唯一一把对富裕学区和贫困学区的学生同样使用的尺子；改用各校自评的成绩，反而会让家庭出身和学校名气在录取中占更大的分量。

options.t_en: I will abolish the exam. A single high-stakes test tells you who prepped well, not who can think, and it drags every classroom toward drilling. Schools certifying their own students with coursework and projects is how most of adult life already works.
options.t: 我会废除统一考试。一场定终身的高利害考试衡量的只是谁备考充分，而不是谁会思考，并且把所有课堂拖向刷题。由学校用课程作业和项目来认证学生，本来就更接近成年后真实世界的运作方式。

options.t_en: I will keep the exam but cut its weight to a passing threshold, letting coursework and a standardised project portfolio carry the selective decisions, with an external auditor sampling school grading each year.
options.t: 我会保留考试，但把它降为达标线，让课程成绩加一份标准化项目作品集来承担选拔功能，并由外部机构每年抽检各校的评分是否可靠。

options.t_en: I keep going back and forth on this; neither direction feels quite right to me.
options.t: 这题我反复摇摆，哪个方向都觉得不太对。

scene_en: A national resettlement program proposes relocating 300 refugee families over three years to your town of 40,000, where the school roll has fallen by a quarter and several apartment blocks stand empty. The council must vote on a welcome package: language classes, school places and housing allocation. Supporters say the families would fill empty classrooms and staff shortages in local care work. Opponents, including some long-time residents, say the town's medical clinic already has an eighteen-month waiting list and that the national government is placing families where housing is cheap, not where support exists.
scene: 全国安置计划提议在三年内向你所在的四万人小镇迁移三百户难民家庭。镇上学生人数已减少四分之一，多栋公寓楼空置。议会须就一份安置配套方案表决：语言课程、学校学位与住房分配。支持者表示，这些家庭能填满空置的教室并缓解本地护理行业的用工短缺；包括部分老居民在内的反对者则指出，镇上的诊所预约已排到十八个月之后，而且联邦政府把家庭安置到这里，看中的是房租便宜，而不是配套支持到位。

options.t_en: I will vote yes and argue we should ask for a larger share. The town's decline is a people shortage, and the national funds attached to each family — for teachers, interpreters, clinics — are the first new money our services have seen in a decade. Arrival planning can fix the waiting lists.
options.t: 我会投赞成票，并主张争取更大的份额。小镇这些年最直观的变化就是人越来越少，而随每个家庭一同拨付的经费——给教师、翻译、诊所的——是本地公共服务十年来见到的第一笔新钱。排队问题完全可以在安置规划里解决。

options.t_en: I will vote no for now. It is fair to ask that services be sized before arrivals, and the clinic waiting list is already eighteen months for the people who live here today. I will propose accepting families only after the national government funds a second doctor and the empty blocks are actually habitable.
options.t: 现阶段我会投反对票。在家庭抵达之前先把服务配套到位，这个要求并不过分——诊所的等候名单对现在的居民来说已经有十八个月。我会提议，等联邦政府出资聘到第二名医生、空置公寓真正具备入住条件之后，再接受安置。

options.t_en: I will propose a staged yes: half the families in year one, with the rest contingent on published metrics — clinic wait times, school capacity, housing readiness — reviewed openly each six months with residents.
options.t: 我会提议一个分阶段的赞成方案：第一年先接收一半家庭，其余名额取决于公开指标——诊所等候时间、学校容量、住房可用性——每六个月与居民共同评议一次。

options.t_en: It would depend on details this scenario doesn't give, so I can't commit to any of these.
options.t: 这取决于情景里没交代的细节，我没法锁定任何一项。

scene_en: The city council is considering a pilot network of acoustic sensors and camera analytics in two high-incident districts, designed to detect gunfire and automatically alert police. Recordings would be retained for 30 days and shared with a regional crime database. The residents' associations in both districts, whose members include many shift workers and parents, support the pilot. Civil liberties organizations object that the sensors also capture ordinary life — arguments, gatherings, who walks home late — and that once the database exists, its uses will expand. The council will decide after two public hearings.
scene: 市议会正在考虑在两个案发率偏高的街区试点部署声学传感器与摄像头分析网络，用于探测枪声并自动报警。录音录像将保存三十天，并接入区域犯罪数据库。这两个街区的居民协会成员中有大量轮班工人和带孩子的家长，他们对试点表示支持。公民自由组织则反对称，传感器同样会录下日常生活——争吵、聚会、深夜独行的人——而数据库一旦存在，用途必然扩张。议会将在两场听证会后做出决定。

options.t_en: I will back the pilot. The people asking for it are the ones who live with the sirens, and gunshot detection cuts response times in ways no app can. Thirty days of retention in two districts, judged by results, is a proportionate place to start.
options.t: 我会支持试点。要求安装的正是每天听着警笛生活的人，而枪声探测能把响应时间缩短到任何手机应用都做不到的程度。只在两个街区、只保留三十天、用效果说话——这是一个相称的起点。

options.t_en: I will oppose it. A system built to catch gunfire does not stop at gunfire; it records every conversation on the street, and the district's young men will bear the cost of that recording long after the pilot ends. Safety bought by putting whole neighbourhoods under permanent audio watch is not a trade I accept.
options.t: 我会反对。一套为捕捉枪声而建的系统不会止步于枪声，它录下的是街上的每一次交谈，而试点结束后，为这份长期录音买单的会是街区里的年轻人。用让整个社区处于永久监听之下来换取安全，这笔交易我不接受。

options.t_en: I will support a conditional pilot: an independent oversight board with resident seats, audio processed on-device so only detected alerts leave the sensor, retention capped at 72 hours unless flagged, and a public report before any expansion.
options.t: 我会支持附条件的试点：设立有居民席位的独立监督委员会，音频在设备端处理、只有被识别的警报才会传出传感器，未标记的记录最多保存七十二小时，扩展部署前必须先公布评估报告。

options.t_en: It's really none of my business — I'd let the people involved sort it out themselves.
options.t: 这说不上和我有关，让当事各方自己去定就好。

scene_en: With the vacancy rate in your city at one percent, the tenant union is campaigning for a rent cap tied to inflation across all existing rentals, with a board to approve exceptions. Landlord associations and developers respond that capped rents plus rising costs will push small landlords to sell and developers to shelve projects, shrinking supply further. A commissioned economic study recommends instead a package of zoning liberalization near transit lines, fast-track permits, and a ten-year public housing construction program. The council must choose a direction this month.
scene: 你所在城市的空置率只有百分之一，租客联盟正在推动一项把全部存量租赁房源租金涨幅与通胀挂钩的限租令，并设委员会审批例外情形。房东协会与开发商回应说，租金封顶叠加成本上升，会迫使小房东卖房、开发商搁置项目，让供给进一步萎缩。一项受委托的经济研究则建议改推另一揽子方案：放宽轨道沿线的分区管制、加快审批速度，并启动一项十年期公共住房建造计划。议会本月内必须定下方向。

options.t_en: I will support the rent cap. With one percent vacancy, tenants have zero bargaining power, and the market has already shown it will not discipline itself. Supply arguments describe a future that is years away; the family facing a 25 percent increase at renewal needs protection now.
options.t: 我会支持限租令。在空置率只有百分之一的市场里，租户毫无议价能力，而这个市场已经证明它不会自我约束。供给侧的说法描绘的是几年后的图景，可续约时面对租金上涨百分之二十五的家庭，需要的是当下的保护。

options.t_en: I will back the zoning and construction package. Rent caps freeze the market in place while doing nothing about the shortage underneath, and cities that tried them watched maintenance and new projects dry up within a decade. Building is slower, but it is the only thing that actually adds homes.
options.t: 我会支持放宽管制加建造计划的方案。限租令把市场冻在原地，却不解决底下的短缺问题，尝试过的城市大多在十年内看到维护投入和新项目一起枯竭。盖房虽然慢，但真正能增加住房供给的只有它。

options.t_en: I will propose both, at half strength: a cap on existing tenancies only, leaving new units exempt for fifteen years, alongside an immediate down payment on the public construction program.
options.t: 我会主张两者都做、各打对折：限租令只覆盖存量租约，新建房源十五年内豁免，以留住开发商的投资意愿；同时立即为公共住房计划拨付首期资金，让供给端的回应不必等上十年。

options.t_en: I'd abstain if I could — the way this is framed forces a stance I don't actually hold.
options.t: 可以弃权的话我就弃权，这题的问法有点替我表态的意思。

scene_en: The health ministry proposes mandatory front-of-pack labels that score packaged foods on nutrition and carbon footprint, displayed as a letter grade with color coding. Public health researchers cite trials showing the labels shift purchases toward higher-scored items. Small producers — the regional raw-milk cheese makers, the family olive presses — object that lab certification fees and a scoring formula biased toward industrial fortification would penalize traditional products and drive them off shelves. Supermarkets say they can implement any scheme within a year if it is mandatory for all, so costs are shared.
scene: 卫生部提议在包装食品正面强制标注营养与碳足迹评分，以带颜色的字母等级呈现。公共卫生研究者引用实验数据称，这类标签能促使消费者转向评分更高的商品。小型生产者——本地区的生乳奶酪坊、家族橄榄油作坊——反对称，认证收费和偏向工业化营养强化的评分公式会惩罚传统产品，把它们挤出货架。连锁超市则表示，只要对所有厂商一律强制，任何方案都能在一年内落地，成本也能分摊。

options.t_en: I will support the mandatory labels. Shoppers currently navigate packages engineered by marketing departments, and a single standardized grade on the front of every package is the cheapest way to level that field. The carbon score should stay — the food system's footprint is too large to leave off the label.
options.t: 我会支持强制标签。目前消费者面对的是由市场部门精心设计的包装，在每件商品正面给出一个统一的标准化等级，是拉平这种信息落差最省钱的方式。碳足迹评分也应该保留——食品体系的排放占比太大，不该从标签上省略。

options.t_en: I will oppose making it mandatory. A formula written once in an office will rank a centuries-old cheese below a fortified snack, and the certification costs will fall hardest on producers who can least carry them. Voluntary labels let the standard earn its adoption instead of legislating it.
options.t: 我会反对强制推行。一个坐在办公室里定下的公式，会把有数百年历史的奶酪排在营养强化零食之下，而认证费用对最无力承担的小生产者打击最重。自愿标签让这套标准靠自身说服力被市场接受，而不是靠立法强加。

options.t_en: I will support the labels for large producers, with an exemption and a simplified self-declaration for producers under a size threshold, so the family creamery is not filing the same paperwork as a multinational.
options.t: 我会支持对大型生产商强制标注，但对低于规模门槛的生产者给予豁免和简化的自我申报，让家庭作坊不必和跨国公司填同一套表格。

options.t_en: I don't hold a fixed view on this; my answer would probably change from one day to the next.
options.t: 我对这事没有固定立场，换个日子答案可能就不一样。

scene_en: A draft law would require social platforms above a user threshold to offer every user a chronological feed as the default, to permit third-party apps on equal terms, and to export a user's full data on request — with fines for non-compliance. User groups and independent developers support it, saying ranking algorithms decide what a billion people see and users should be able to choose simpler feeds and move their data. Platform representatives argue the ranking feed is their core product, that open interfaces create security and moderation risks they would absorb alone, and that product design decisions belong to the company and its users, not the legislature.
scene: 一项法律草案要求达到用户规模门槛的社交平台，把按时间排序的信息流设为默认选项，允许第三方应用在同等条件下接入，并应请求导出用户的全部数据，违者处以罚款。用户团体与独立开发者表示支持：排名算法决定了十亿人能看到什么，用户理应能选择更简单的信息流、能带走自己的数据。平台代表则辩称，排名信息流是他们的核心产品，开放的接口带来的安全与内容治理风险将由平台独自承担，而产品设计的决定权属于公司与其用户，不属于立法机关。

options.t_en: I will support the law. When one design choice shapes what hundreds of millions of people see each day, giving users a plain chronological option and the right to leave with their data is a fair rule for any company that size.
options.t: 我会支持这部法律。当一项设计决定影响着数亿人每天看到的内容时，给用户提供一个朴素的时间排序选项、并允许他们带着数据离开，对任何这个体量的公司都是合理的规则。

options.t_en: I will oppose the law. Regulators do not know which feed design will suit which user, and legislating one default replaces the market's feedback with a committee's guess. The export requirement I could accept; dictating product design I would not.
options.t: 我会反对这部法律。监管者并不了解哪种信息流适合哪类用户，用立法规定默认选项，等于用一个委员会的猜测取代市场的反馈。数据导出的要求我可以接受，但对产品设计本身下指令，我不赞成。

options.t_en: I will support only the data portability clause, with a standard export format, and leave feed design and third-party access to voluntary agreements between platforms and developers.
options.t: 我只支持数据可携带条款——规定一个标准化的导出格式即可；至于信息流设计和第三方接入，交给平台与开发者之间自愿达成的协议去解决。

options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I'd rather just skip it.
options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。

scene: 阿尔德街尽头有一座废弃加油站，场地在十年前清理过土壤后一直围栏空置。邻里协会已征集到签名，推动一个由居民自营的方案：高架菜畦、工具借用库和一片小游乐场，由会员家庭轮班维护，靠少量年费和周末义务劳动维持。市属房产部门另有一份承租报价——一家连锁便利店愿按市场价租下这块地，租金进入区级一般预算，并承诺安装照明、开设夜间柜台、提供十一个本地岗位。两份方案下月要在同一场议会表决中二选一，只能落地一个。
scene_en: At the end of Alder Street sits a disused filling station, fenced off since the soil was cleared a decade ago. The neighbourhood association has collected signatures for a resident-run scheme: raised vegetable beds, a tool library, a small playground, maintained by member households on a rota, funded by a modest annual fee and weekend work days. The city's property office has a competing offer — a convenience chain will lease the plot at market rate, with the rent going into the district's general budget, and promises lighting, a night counter and eleven local jobs. Both proposals need the same council vote next month, and only one can go ahead.

options.t_en: I will back the resident scheme. A plot that neighbours build and maintain themselves keeps the money and the decisions on the street, and a rota means the upkeep does not depend on a budget line that can be cut in a bad year.
options.t: 我会支持居民合作社的方案。一块由邻居自己建、自己维护的地，钱和决定都留在街上；轮班维护也意味着日常开销不挂在一条遇到坏年份就会被砍掉的预算科目上。

options.t_en: I would take the lease. Rent at market rate is revenue the district can spend on whatever it needs most, and eleven wage jobs plus lighting at night are concrete gains, while a members' garden serves only the households that can pay the fee and show up on work days.
options.t: 我会选择出租。按市场价收的租金是区里可以花在最要紧处的收入，十一个带薪岗位和夜间照明是看得见的收益；而会员制菜园只服务那些交得起年费、周末还能来干活的家庭。

options.t_en: I would split the plot: half leased to the chain, half kept for the garden, with the lease money paying for the garden's water and fencing.
options.t: 我会把这块地分成两半：一半租给连锁店，一半留给菜园，租金用来支付菜园的灌溉和围栏费用，两边的开支各自有着落，不必互相挤占。

options.t_en: Neither the council nor the association should settle this in a closed vote; I would put both offers on a street ballot with the rent figures and the maintenance costs printed, and let the residents within two blocks decide.
options.t: 这事不该由议会或协会在一次闭门表决里定下来。我会把两份报价放上街区投票，附上租金数额和维护成本，让住在两个街区以内的居民自己选。

options.t_en: Honestly, none of these speaks for me on this one — I would rather just skip it.
options.t: 说实话这几个说法都不代表我，这题我宁愿跳过。

scene: 连续三个周末在地区卫生局门外发生对峙之后，市里提出一项条例：在公共街道上超过五十人的集会须提前七天登记，只能在四个指定场地举行，未登记可处罚款。警方称这四个场地配有供水、医疗人员和分离的出入口，而上个月的人群管控几乎耗尽了他们的相关预算。一个抗议农村诊所经费削减的小团体组织者则认为，七天足够反对一方组织起反制活动、也足够让他们的议题从新闻里淡出；而被安排在离大楼三个街区的围栏里，抗议对它所针对的人而言等于不存在。
scene_en: After three weekends of confrontations outside the regional health office, the city proposes an ordinance: any gathering of more than fifty people on a public street must be registered seven days ahead, must use one of four designated sites, and may be fined for non-registration. The police say the four sites have water, medics and separated entrances, and that the last month cost them most of their crowd-control budget. Organisers of a small group protesting cuts to a rural clinic say seven days is enough time for a counter-campaign to be organised and for their issue to fall out of the news, and that a pen three blocks from the building makes the protest invisible to the people it targets.

options.t_en: I will support the ordinance. Four sites with water, medics and separate entrances is a workable arrangement for a city that has spent a month absorbing the cost of unmanaged crowds, and a seven-day notice period is short enough that no campaign has ever died waiting a week.
options.t: 我会支持这项条例。对一座已经花了一个月消化人群失控成本的城市来说，四个配供水、医疗人员和分离出入口的场地是可操作的安排；七天的通知期也短到不至于让哪场行动因为等这一周而消失。

options.t_en: I would vote it down. A protest's effect comes from being where the decision is made; moving it three blocks away and requiring a week's notice turns a right into a scheduling request, and the fine turns an unregistered gathering into a revenue line.
options.t: 我会投反对票。抗议的作用来自它发生在做决定的地方；挪到三个街区外、再加一周通知期，就把一项权利变成了排期申请，罚款则把未登记的集会变成一条收入科目。

options.t_en: I would keep the seven-day registration and drop the designated-site rule, so the city can plan medics and barriers while the gathering stays in sight of the building it is addressing.
options.t: 我会保留七天登记，去掉指定场地的规定：市里照样能提前安排医疗人员和隔离栏，而集会仍然待在它所针对的那栋楼看得见的地方。

options.t_en: I would set the threshold by risk rather than headcount — require notice only where a route blocks traffic or where opposing groups have clashed before, and leave a stationary gathering of sixty people on a wide pavement alone.
options.t: 我会按风险而不是按人数设门槛：只对封路路线、或对立团体此前发生过冲突的场合要求报备；六十个人在宽人行道上静立，就不去管它。

options.t_en: I do not feel personally involved in this issue; any of these outcomes would be fine with me.
options.t: 这事我没啥代入感，哪种结果我都能接受。

scene: 国家器官移植服务机构报告称，在人生最艰难的时刻被问及时，四成家庭拒绝捐献，等待名单已连续六年增长。议会正在审议一项法案，拟改为「推定同意」：每位成年人默认是捐献者，除非本人登记过反对；家属仍会被征询，但不再能否决已登记的意愿。移植外科医生与患者组织支持该法案，并援引一些国家在改革后捐献率上升三分之一的经验。缓和医疗医生与若干宗教团体反对，认为以沉默给出的同意不是同意，而在最糟糕的时刻要求悲痛的家属授权摘取器官，等于把他们变成守门人。
scene_en: The national transplant service reports that four in ten families refuse donation when asked at the worst moment of their lives, and that waiting lists have grown for six consecutive years. A bill before parliament would move to presumed consent: every adult is a donor unless they have recorded an objection, with families still consulted but no longer able to override a registered wish. Transplant surgeons and patient associations support it and point to countries where rates rose by a third after the change. Palliative care doctors and several faith communities object that consent given by silence is not consent, and that asking a grieving family to authorise retrieval turns them into gatekeepers at the worst possible hour.

options.t_en: I will vote for presumed consent. The default is the one part of this system that has never been tried, and a registry that lets anyone opt out at any hour records a person's own stated wish, which is a better guide than a family's guess made in the first hour of grief.
options.t: 我会投支持票。默认设定是这个体系里唯一还没试过的一环；一个允许任何人随时登记退出的名册，记录的是本人说过的意愿，比家属在悲痛最初一小时里的猜测更可靠。

options.t_en: I would oppose it. Silence in a country where most people have never seen the form is not a decision, and a system that reads absence as consent will collect organs from people who simply never got around to registering an objection.
options.t: 我会反对。在一个大多数人从没见过那份表格的国家，沉默不是决定；把「没登记」读成「同意」的制度，会从那些只是没来得及去登记反对的人身上取走器官。

options.t_en: I would support presumed consent only if the family's veto stays in place; the registry would then carry the intent, and the family would still hold the last word, which is the part that keeps the conversation humane.
options.t: 只有在保留家属否决权的前提下我才会支持推定同意：名册负责承载本人的意愿，最后一句话仍留给家属——让这场对话还像人与人之间的对话的，正是这一条。

options.t_en: I would replace presumed consent with mandated choice: every adult must answer the question at some routine transaction, a licence renewal or a tax filing, and no default is recorded until they do.
options.t: 我会用「强制选择」替代推定同意：每位成年人在某次日常事务中必须回答这个问题，比如换驾照或报税，在回答之前不记录任何默认值。

options.t_en: I cannot really take a side here — I do not know enough about this to judge.
options.t: 这题我站不了边，了解得不够，判断不了。

scene: 一家制造企业提供六个月的育儿假，但符合条件的父亲中只有五分之一休满一个月以上，其余人表示长期缺勤在考核时会被读作投入不足。劳动部起草了一项规则：其中四个月专属于第二照护人，不休即作废，费用由国家保险基金与雇主分担。妇女团体与劳动部称，在可比经济体中，这类制度是少数被观测到确实改变照护分工的措施之一。雇主联合会则表示，小企业无法在短期内承受四个月的岗位空缺；也有家长认为，一个家庭如何分配这几个月不该由国家来决定。
scene_en: A manufacturing company offers six months of parental leave, but only a fifth of eligible fathers take more than a month; the rest say a long absence is read as low commitment at review time. The labour ministry drafts a rule: four months of the leave are reserved to the second parent and are forfeited if unused, with the cost shared between the state insurance fund and the employer. Women's groups and the ministry say this is one of the few measures observed to shift the division of care in comparable economies. Employer federations say a small firm cannot absorb a four-month absence on short notice, and some parents say the state should not decide how a household divides its months.

options.t_en: I will support the reserved months. The reason fathers do not take leave is not preference but what a review committee reads into an absence; making the months non-transferable changes what the committee reads, and that is the part no awareness campaign has managed to change.
options.t: 我会支持这四个月的专属安排。父亲不休假的原因不是偏好，而是考核委员会会把缺勤读成什么；把月份设成不可转让，改的正是委员会的读法，而这恰恰是宣传运动一直没改动的部分。

options.t_en: I would oppose it. A household is better placed than a ministry to decide which parent steps back for a season, and a rule that voids the months if unused pushes a choice onto families that had already made a different one.
options.t: 我会反对。哪个家长暂时退出工作一段时间，家庭比一个部委更清楚；不休就作废的规则，是把一种选择强加给早已做出另一种安排的家庭。

options.t_en: I would support the rule together with a compensation scheme for firms under fifty staff, so the cost of the absence is pooled rather than landing on the payroll of the smallest employer in the chain.
options.t: 我会支持这条规则，同时要求为五十人以下的企业配套补偿机制，让缺勤的成本由共同池子分摊，而不是全落在这条供应链上规模最小的那家雇主的工资表里。

options.t_en: I would drop the forfeiture and pay a bonus to households where both parents take at least three months; the split is what matters, and a bonus reaches the same split without voiding anyone's leave.
options.t: 我会取消「不休作废」，改为给双方各休满三个月的家庭发一笔补贴：要的是分工这个结果，补贴同样能换来分工，又不必作废任何人的假期。

options.t_en: This feels like a false choice to me; if it actually came up, I would handle it some other way entirely.
options.t: 我觉得这题是个伪选择，真到那一步我会用别的方式处理。

scene: 卫生部提议建立一个全国统一的诊断影像库：公立医院拍摄的每一张影像须在四十八小时内上传，配唯一患者标识，用于训练与审计 AI 阅片工具。官员称，没有任何本国厂商能靠一家医院的数据训练出可靠模型，共享影像库可以让区级诊所借用教学医院的准确度。放射科医师协会与患者组织提出两点反对：这个影像库本身会成为一个攻击目标；而且从来没人问过患者——入院时签的同意书覆盖的是诊疗，不是训练一个商业产品。医院方面则表示，如果允许真正退出，留在库里的恰好是最没用的那批影像。
scene_en: The health ministry proposes a single national archive of diagnostic imaging: every scan taken in a public hospital, uploaded within 48 hours, tagged with a unique patient identifier, used to train and audit AI reading tools. Officials say no domestic vendor can build a reliable model from one hospital's data, and that a shared archive would let a district clinic borrow the accuracy of a teaching hospital. Radiologists' associations and patient groups raise two objections: the archive becomes a target, and patients were never asked, since the form signed at admission covers treatment rather than the training of a commercial product. Hospitals say a real opt-out would leave them holding exactly the scans that are least useful.

options.t_en: I would build the archive with upload as a condition of public funding. A model trained on one hospital's scanners does not travel well, and the patients who would benefit most sit in districts that will never generate enough scans of their own.
options.t: 我会把上传设为接受公共拨款的条件，据此建起这个影像库。只在一家医院的机器上训练出来的模型换个地方就不灵，而最可能受益的患者，恰恰在那些永远攒不出足够影像的区县。

options.t_en: I would require explicit consent for every scan, renewed when a patient changes hospitals. A form signed on the way into surgery cannot be read as agreement to train a product a vendor will later sell, and the size of the archive is not a reason to skip the question.
options.t: 我会要求每一张影像都取得明确同意，患者换医院时重新确认。进手术室路上签的那张表格，不能被读作同意去训练一个厂商日后要卖的产品；影像库要多大，都不是不问这一句的理由。

options.t_en: I would support the archive with identifiers stripped at the hospital and a genuine opt-out offered at the counter rather than buried in an admission packet; the model still gets its scale, and the patient keeps a switch.
options.t: 我会支持建库，但要求标识在医院端就剥离，并把退出选项在服务台当面提供，而不是塞进入院材料里。这样模型仍有足够的规模，患者手里也留着一个开关。
